一.zh: 我哋由最簡單嘅一個字開始：一。你睇吓佢個樣——就係一橫，由左去右，一劃就寫完，簡單到唔可以再簡單。佢讀做 jat1，意思就係「一」、「單獨一個」，好似「一個」（jat1 go3）同「一種」（jat1 zung2）咁。喺倉頡入面，一橫呢個形係擺喺 M 掣度，所以呢個字淨係取 M，一個掣就搞掂。記住喇：一橫就係 M，一劃、一個掣、一個字，好易記！

三.en: This character is 三, read saam1, and it simply means the number three. Look at its shape: three flat horizontal strokes stacked one above the other, drawn top to bottom. Each stroke is 一, which lives on the M key, so three of them give you M, M, M — the full code is MMM. Why does it split this way? 三 is a whole character (整體字) with no separate head and body, and for a shape like this Cangjie takes the head stroke, the second stroke, and the tail stroke — here all three just happen to be 一, so you press M three times. Easy hook: three lines, three taps of M.
三.zh: 呢個字係「三」，讀saam1，意思就係數字三，好簡單。你望下佢嘅樣：三條橫劃，一條疊住一條，由上到下排住。每一條橫劃都係「一」，喺鍵盤上面撳M（讀「一」），所以三條就係M、M、M，成個碼就係MMM。點解會咁拆呢？因為「三」係一個整體字，冇字首字身之分，遇到呢種情況倉頡就取頭、二、尾三劃——即係第一劃、第二劃同最尾一劃，啱啱好都係「一」，所以撳三下M就得。記住喇：三條線，撳三次M，橫平豎直，一目了然。

上.en: Today we meet the character 上, read soeng5 or soeng6, meaning "top, highest, or to go up" — you see it in words like 上面 (upstairs) and 上水 (Sheung Shui here in Hong Kong). Take a look at its shape: on top there's a vertical stroke with a dot, which is the 卜 piece, and underneath it rests a single flat line, the 一 piece. In Cangjie, 卜 lives on the Y key and 一 lives on the M key, so 上 is simply coded YM — just two codes. Why only two? Because 上 is a whole character (整體字) with a very simple build, so you don't break it down any further; you just take the leading 卜 and the closing 一, giving 卜一. Remember it this way: a dot standing up, a line lying flat — 卜一, YM — that's where the cat sleeps, right on top of the table.
上.zh: 今日我哋學「上」呢個字，佢讀作 soeng5 或者 soeng6，意思係「頂部、最高、向上」，好似上面、上水噉樣用。你望吓佢個樣：上面一個豎加一點，就係個「卜」形，下面墊住一橫，就係「一」。喺倉頡入面，「卜」對應 Y 鍵，「一」對應 M 鍵，所以「上」個碼就係 YM，啱啱兩碼。點解得兩碼咁少呢？因為「上」係一個結構好簡單嘅整體字，佢唔使拆到咁散，直接拎頭嘅「卜」同尾嘅「一」就夠，卜一。記住嘞：一點望上，一橫墊住，卜一 YM，貓咪就瞓喺枱上面喇。

下.en: Today we learn 下, read haa6, the very same 下 as in 上下 (up and down); it means under, below, the bottom, or moving downward. Look at its shape: a single flat stroke across the top, with a small piece hanging beneath it. This is a whole-character (整體字), meaning it doesn't break into many separate parts, so we take just the head and the tail. The head is that top stroke 一, typed with M, and the tail is the little ⺊ shape below it, typed with Y — together that gives you MY. Remember it this way: one stroke on top (M), a small hook underneath (Y), and one-above-one-below spells 下.
下.zh: 我哋今日學「下」呢個字，讀音係 haa6，就係「上下」嗰個「下」，解作下面、底部，或者向下嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅樣：上面係一橫，下面就掛住一點一豎嘅細部件。呢個字係一個「整體字」，佢唔會拆到好多份出嚟，所以我哋用最簡單嘅辦法——只取個頭同個尾兩碼。個頭係最頂嗰橫「一」，喺鍵盤打 M；個尾就係下面嗰個「⺊」形，喺鍵盤打 Y，合埋就係 MY。記住一個口訣：「一橫喺上（M），細鈎喺下（Y），一上一下就係『下』」。

不.en: Today we learn 不, read "bat1", meaning "no" or "not" — the negative word you hear in 不停 (non-stop) and 不過 (however). Look at its shape: one flat stroke across the top, and below it a form that spreads out like a splash. In Cangjie, 不 is a whole character, so we don't over-split it — we simply take two codes: the top stroke is 一, the key M, and the lower part we read as 火, the key F, giving the full code M F. Why split here? Because a whole character skips the usual 字首/字身 quota rules and is read straight down by shape: top stroke M, then 火 below as F. Memory hook: one bar pressing down on a fire — M then F — and you've got 不.
不.zh: 今日我哋學「不」呢個字，讀「bat1」，即係「唔」、「否定」嘅意思，好似「不停」、「不過」入面都用到佢。你望下佢個樣，上面一橫，下面一個好似撇捺分開嘅形狀。喺倉頡入面，「不」係一個整體字，唔使拆得太複雜，我哋淨係取兩個碼：上面嗰一橫就係「一」，鍵係M；下面嗰個部分我哋當佢係「火」，鍵係F，所以成個字打M F。點解係咁樣拆？因為整體字唔跟一般字首字身嘅規矩，而係直接由上到下順住取形，上一橫M、下面火F，簡簡單單兩碼就搞掂。記住喇：一橫壓住個火，M配F，就係「不」。

且.en: Today we learn 且, which has several readings, but the one you'll meet most is ce2 in words like 而且, meaning "moreover" or "in addition" — it links back to the previous clause to add another layer. Look at the character: it's really two written pieces, the ⺼ shape on top and through the middle, which you type with B, and one flat horizontal stroke 一 at the very bottom, which you type with M. Why only two codes? Because 且 is a single-body character — the whole thing counts as one unified block that we don't chop up further, so Cangjie's rule is to take just the head and the tail. That gives us head ⺼ as B and tail 一 as M, so the full code is BM. Remember it as running from B (⺼) down to M (一) — top piece, bottom piece, and you've got the 且 in 而且.
且.zh: 我哋今日學「且」呢個字，讀音有幾個，最常見係喺「而且」度讀 ce2，意思係「而且、並且」，用嚟接住上一句加多層意思。你望住個字，其實由兩橛砌成：上面同中間嗰嚿係「⺼」，喺鍵盤上打 B；最底一橫係「一」，打 M。點解淨係得兩碼咁少？因為「且」係一個連體字（整體字），成個字當一嚿睇，唔會拆到七零八落，倉頡規矩就係只取個頭同個尾兩碼，所以就係頭「⺼」B、尾「一」M，即係 BM。記住個口訣：由 B（⺼）行到 M（一），一頭一尾夾住，就係「而且」嘅「且」啦。

世.en: Today we learn the character 世, read sai3, meaning a generation, an era, or the world. Look at its shape: horizontal and vertical strokes woven together, yet Cangjie takes it apart in the simplest way, using only two codes. The first code is 匕 on the P key, which is the head, and the second is 廿 on the T key, which is the tail, so the full code is PT. Why only two codes? Because 世 is a whole-form character (整體字) that is not chopped into many pieces; for this kind of character Cangjie simply grabs the head and the tail, head P and tail T, and stops there. To remember it, think of the word 世界, world — press P then T, open and close, and the whole world appears on your screen.
世.zh: 今日我哋學「世」呢個字，讀音係 sai3，意思係世代、世界、一個時代。你望吓佢個樣，好似橫直交錯咁織埋一齊，其實倉頡拆佢好簡單，只係兩碼。第一碼係「匕」，喺 P 鍵，係佢個字首；第二碼係「廿」，喺 T 鍵，係佢個字尾，所以個碼就係 PT。點解得兩碼咁少呢？因為「世」係一個整體字，佢唔會硬拆成好多件，倉頡對呢類字有個特別做法，就係直接取個頭同個尾，頭 P 尾 T 就夠喇。記住佢嘅時候，你可以諗成「世界」呢個詞——PT 兩鍵，一開一合，成個世界就打出嚟喇。

並.en: Today we're learning 並, read "bing6" or "bing3", meaning "side by side" or "equal to", and it can also mean "and" or "moreover", as in 並且. Look closely: this is a single-body character, so instead of splitting it into a head part and a body part, we simply pick out its most important pieces from top to bottom. First take the 廿 across the top, which sits on the T key; next take the two little strokes 丷 in the middle, which are also T; and finally take the 八 at the bottom, which is C, giving us TTC. Because it counts as a single body, the rule tells us to grab the head, the second, and the tail — that's T, T, then C. Here's your hook: two T's stacked up with a C holding the base, standing 並 shoulder to shoulder in a neat row!
並.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「並」，讀「bing6」或者「bing3」，意思係「並排」、「相等」，又可以解「而且」、「並且」。你望下呢個字，佢係一個整體字，所以我哋唔會拆成字首同字身兩截，而係直接由頭到尾揀最重要嘅碼。首先揀頂上嘅「廿」，佢喺鍵盤上係 T；跟住揀中間嗰兩點「丷」，佢一樣係 T；最後揀底部嘅「八」，佢係 C，合埋就係 TTC。因為係整體字，規則就係取「頭、二、尾」三個部分，即係 T、T、C 三碼。記住呢個口訣：兩個 T 疊住，一個 C 托底，「並」肩企齊齊排一行！

串.en: Today we learn 串, read "cyun3," which means a string or skewer of things — think 串燒 (cyun3 siu1), food threaded onto a bamboo stick and grilled; it can also read "gwaan3," meaning relatives or to conspire. Look at its shape: it's simply two 中 stacked one on top of the other, one above and one below. Because this is an integral character, both the top 中 and the bottom 中 are taken as the same root, 中, which lives on the L key, so you type the top 中 as L, then the bottom 中 as L again, giving the whole code LL — just two taps. Here's your hook: two fish-ball skewers stacked up, L plus L makes 串!
串.zh: 今日我哋學「串」呢個字，讀「cyun3」，即係一串嘢嘅串，好似「串燒」（cyun3 siu1）咁，將食物穿喺竹籤上面燒；佢又可以讀「gwaan3」，解親戚或者串通。你望吓個字嘅樣，其實就係上下兩個「中」疊埋一齊，一個喺上，一個喺下。因為佢係一個整體字，上下兩個「中」都係取同一個字根「中」，個字根喺鍵盤上係 L 掣，所以你打上面嘅「中」係 L，再打下面嘅「中」又係 L，成個碼就係 LL，簡簡單單兩下。記住喇：兩串魚蛋疊起身，L 加 L 就係「串」！

主.en: Today's character is 主, read zyu2, meaning master, chief owner, or host — you'll meet it in 主要 (zyu2 jiu3, mainly) and 主義 (zyu2 ji6, ideology). Look at the shape: there's a single dot on top, and beneath it sits the whole character 土, earth, so it falls neatly into two pieces. The first piece is that top dot 丶, which lives on the Y key; the second is the 土 sitting underneath, which lives on the G key, giving you the full code YG in just two letters. Why only these two? Cangjie takes the leading piece as the head and what follows as the body, and here the dot 丶 is clearly the head while 土 is the body — the split is obvious, so nothing more needs breaking down. Remember it this way: a dot on top (Y) standing on solid earth (G) — the master stands upon the land.
主.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「主」，讀作 zyu2，解作主人、主宰嘅意思，好似「主要」zyu2 jiu3 同「主義」zyu2 ji6 都用到佢。你望吓個字：上面一點，下面一個「土」字，剛好可以拆成兩嚿。第一嚿係嗰一點「丶」，喺 Y 鍵；第二嚿係下面嗰個「土」字，喺 G 鍵，所以個碼就係 YG，簡簡單單兩碼就搞掂。點解淨係取呢兩嚿？因為倉頡拆字取頭一嚿做字首、後面做字身，「丶」擺頭，「土」墊底，兩嚿之間清清楚楚，唔使再細分。記住喇：一點喺頭 Y，一撇泥土 G 喺腳，主人企喺土地上。

之.en: Today we learn 之, read zi1. It's a very common classical word that links two phrases the way 嘅 does, and it can also mean "it/him/her" or "go to." Look at the shape: there's no clean top-and-bottom or left-and-right division you can grab, so 之 is treated as a whole character (整體字), and instead of splitting it we simply take codes in stroke order from head to tail. The first stroke is the dot on top, 丶, keyed with I; next comes the curving middle piece 乙, keyed with N; and last is the 人-like sweep at the bottom, keyed with O — giving you INO. As a memory hook, just read the strokes top to bottom as you write it: dot, 乙, 人 — I, N, O.
之.zh: 今日我哋學「之」呢個字，讀音係 zi1，佢係文言常見嘅字，可以做「嘅」咁樣連接前後兩個部分，又可以解「佢」或者「去」。你望住個字形，佢冇一個好清楚嘅字首同字身可以分開，係一個「整體字」，所以我哋唔會左右或者上下拆開，而係由頭到尾順住筆順逐筆取碼。第一筆係上面嗰點「丶」，撳 I（fifth 一橫嗰邊）；跟住係中間彎彎嘅「乙」，撳 N；最後係下面似「人」嘅一撇一捺，撳 O，合埋就係 INO。記住呢個字係整體字，你就由上到下讀出「點、乙、人」三筆，順住個字寫落嚟就啱嘞。

乜.en: Here's a character you use every single day in Cantonese: 乜, read mat1, the 乜 in 乜嘢 that means "what?" — the word you reach for when you ask someone what's going on. Look at its shape and you'll see it's built from just two pieces: first you write the little 匕 at the top, which lives on the P key, and then the curving hook 乙 that cradles it below, which lives on the N key, giving you the code PN. Why so short, only two codes? Because 乜 is a whole-character (整體字) — it isn't divided into a head and a body, so Cangjie just takes it straight through from start to finish, and the pieces it captures, 匕 P and 乙 N, are the whole thing. Remember it like this: draw the little 匕 P, then sweep the 乙 N underneath, and PN spells out the 乜 in 你講乜嘢呀?
乜.zh: 呢個「乜」字，你一定日日都見到、日日都講——就係廣東話「乜嘢」嗰個「乜」，讀 mat1，即係「咩」、「乜嘢」嘅意思，問人「乜嘢事？」嗰陣就用佢。你望住個字，佢係由兩件嘢砌成：先寫左上邊嘅「匕」，喺鍵盤上係 P 掣，然後寫個托底彎彎地嘅「乙」，喺鍵盤上係 N 掣，所以個碼就係 PN。點解淨係兩碼咁少？因為「乜」係一個整體字，佢冇分字首字身，倉頡有條規矩：成個字直接由頭到尾拆，最多都係咁多件，取到嘅就係全部——「匕」P、「乙」N，兩件齊，收工。記住佢好易：先撇個「匕」P，再兜個「乙」N，PN 兩下就打晒「你講乜嘢呀」嗰個「乜」。

九.en: Today's character is 「九」, read gau2, meaning the number nine. Look at its shape: first there's the 大 form made of a slanting stroke and a crossing line, then a curved hook that sweeps down like 弓. In Cangjie this character splits into just two codes — take 大 first by pressing K, then take 弓 by pressing N, giving you KN. Why so few codes? Because 九 is a whole character (整體字) that can't be cleanly divided into a head part and a body part, so Cangjie uses the head-tail rule, keeping only the first piece and the last piece: 大 and 弓. Remember it this way — the 九 in 九龍 (Kowloon) is a 大 bow (大弓), so imagine drawing a big bow to shoot across the harbour into 九龍城, and KN will stick.
九.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「九」，讀作 gau2，即係數字九嘅意思。你望下佢個形：先有一撇一橫嘅「大」形，跟住一個彎彎哋兜落嘅「弓」形。呢個字倉頡拆做兩碼，先取「大」字，撳 K 掣，再取「弓」字，撳 N 掣，所以個碼就係 KN。點解淨係得兩碼咁少呢？因為「九」係一個整體字，冇得清楚分成字首同字身，遇到呢種情況，倉頡就用「頭尾取碼」嘅辦法，淨係攞頭一件同尾一件，即係大同弓。記住喇：「九」龍嘅九，就係「大弓」兩碼——你去過九龍城，就當自己攞住一個大弓射過海去九龍，KN 就記得穩陣喇。

也.en: Today we're learning 也, which reads "jaa5." In classical Chinese it's a particle of strong affirmation, and in everyday sense it means "also" or "too" — like in 我也想去玩, meaning I also want to go play. Look at how 也 flows in a few curved strokes; Cangjie treats it as a simple character, so you just take the head and the tail. The head code is 七 on the P key, and the tail code is 木 on the D key, giving you the whole thing as PD. Remember it as just two keys — a hook at the front like 七 (P) and a finish like 木 (D), one at each end.
也.zh: 今日我哋學「也」呢個字，讀「jaa5」。喺古文入面佢係一個語氣詞，表示肯定或者「都、亦」嘅意思，好似「我也想去玩」就係話我都想去玩。你睇「也」個樣好似彎彎曲曲一筆過寫落嚟，其實倉頡就當佢係簡單字，只取頭尾兩碼。頭嗰碼係「七」，喺字母P度，尾嗰碼係「木」，喺字母D度，所以成個字打「PD」就搞掂。記住呢個字得兩粒掣，開頭一個彎鈎似「七」（P），收尾似「木」（D），一頭一尾好易記。

了.en: Today we're learning 了, a very common little character read liu5, working at the end of a sentence as a particle of completed action — that feeling of something being finished, as in 呢件事完了, meaning this matter is over and done with. Look at the shape of 了: it's a single flowing form that curves and then drops straight down. When Cangjie breaks it up, it takes the curved top part first as the head piece, which is 弓 on the N key, and then takes the hooked downward stroke at the bottom as the tail piece, which is 亅, also on the N key. Because 了 is a single-piece character, Cangjie's rule for such characters is to take at most a head and a tail — just two codes — so head 弓 plus tail 亅 gives you NN. Remember it this way: one character, two N's, head-bow and tail-hook, and 了 is done.
了.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「了」呢個字，佢好常用，讀作 liu5，喺句尾做完成嘅語氣助詞，好似「食咗飯喇」嗰種完結嘅感覺，例如「呢件事完了。」意思就係件事完咗，冇喇。你望住「了」呢個形，其實佢係一個彎彎曲曲、由上到下嘅單體字。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，先取上面彎起嗰部分做字首，就係「弓」，個鍵係 N；再取落尾嗰條帶鈎嘅豎筆做字尾，就係「亅」，個鍵一樣係 N。因為「了」係一個單體字，倉頡規定單體字最多只取頭尾兩碼，所以頭取弓、尾取亅，合埋就係 NN。記住喇：一個字兩隻 N，頭弓尾亅，「了」就打完了。

事.en: Today we meet 事, read si6, meaning an affair, a matter, or business — you see it in words like 故事 (gu3 si6, an old story) and 事件 (si6 gin2, an incident). Because this character is one tightly connected shape with no clean place to break it into a head and a body, Cangjie treats it as a whole-form character and simply takes head-second-third-tail codes straight down the form. So you follow the strokes and collect four pieces: the top 十 (J), the crossbar with its vertical stroke, then the two inner uprights, each read as 中 (L and L), and finally the hooked 弓 (N) wrapping it all, giving you JLLN. Remember it like this: one matter, 十 first, two 中 in the middle, a 弓 to close — J, L, L, N — and that's the 事 in 呢件事好難.
事.zh: 今日我哋學「事」呢個字，讀做 si6，意思係事情、事務，好似「故事」gu3 si6 或者「事件」si6 gin2 咁樣用。呢個字上下連成一體，冇一個好清楚嘅分割位，所以倉頡當佢係整體字，唔分字首字身，直接由外到內、由頭到尾順住個形攞碼。你就順住個筆順攞四個碼：先係頂上嗰一橫加豎交叉嘅「十」J，跟住中間兩條豎畫，每條都係「中」L、L，最後包住個鈎嘅「弓」N，合埋就係 JLLN。記住呢句口訣：一件事，先「十」後兩「中」，尾收一個「弓」，J、L、L、N，就係「呢件事好難」嗰個「事」喇。

二.en: Today's character is 二, read ji6, meaning "two" or "twice" — you'll see it in words like 第二 (dai6 ji6, second) and 二十 (ji6 sap6, twenty). Look at its shape: one horizontal stroke on top, one horizontal stroke below, two flat lines stacked together, and that's all there is to 二. Each of those strokes is the familiar 一, which lives on the M key, so the top stroke gives you one M and the bottom stroke gives you another M, making the code MM. The split falls this way because the two horizontal strokes are each a separate shape, and each one contributes a single code, taken in order from top to bottom — M, then M. Remember it like this: two lines, two taps of M, and MM is done.
二.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「二」，讀做 ji6，意思就係「兩個」或者「兩次」，好似「第二」（dai6 ji6）同「二十」（ji6 sap6）咁樣用。你望吓佢個樣：上面一橫，下面一橫，兩橫疊埋一齊，簡簡單單就係「二」。呢兩橫，每一橫都係我哋熟悉嘅「一」，而「一」喺鍵盤上係 M 鍵，所以上面嗰橫取一個 M，下面嗰橫再取一個 M，合埋就係 MM 兩碼。點解咁樣拆呢？因為上下兩橫各自係一件獨立嘅字形，每件取一碼，順住由上到下嘅次序打，就自然係 M 之後再 M。記住一個口訣：「二」就係兩條線，兩隻手指撳兩下 M，MM 就搞掂。

五.en: Today we learn 五, read ng5, which means the number five and can also be a surname. Look at its shape: there's one flat stroke on top, one flat stroke on the bottom, and a little crossed tangle squeezed in the middle. In Cangjie this is a "whole-shape" character — the pieces knot together so tightly that you can't cleanly split it into a head and a body, so we use a special rule: take the first, the second, and the last, and skip whatever sits in the middle. The top stroke is 一 M, the crossed middle piece is ⿻ D, and the closing stroke at the bottom is 一 M again, giving you MDM, with everything in the middle simply skipped. Remember it as a sandwich: a stroke, a cross, a stroke — M, D, M — top and bottom holding the middle, and you'll never mistype it.
五.zh: 今日我哋學「五」呢個字，讀做 ng5，即係數字五，都可以做姓氏用。你望吓佢個樣：上下各有一橫，中間夾住一舊交叉嘅嘢，睇落好似糾纏埋一齊。喺倉頡入面，佢係一個「整體字」——即係話成個字寫落好似黐埋一齊，冇辦法乾淨咁分開字首同字身，所以我哋用一條特別規矩：取頭二尾，跳過中間。第一橫係「一」M，中間果舊交叉嘅嘢係「⿻」D，最後尾嗰橫又係「一」M，所以拼埋就係 MDM，中間有幾多都唔理，直接跳過。你記住：一橫、一交叉、一橫，M、D、M，好似三文治咁上下夾住中間，就永遠唔會撳錯喇。

亞.en: Today we learn 亞, read aa3 in Cantonese. It means Asia — as in 亞洲 — and it also works as a prefix before names, like in 瑪利亞 for Mary. Look at its shape: a flat stroke on top and another on the bottom, wrapping around two vertical strokes in the middle, all neat and symmetrical. This is a whole-form character (整體字), which means we don't break it into a 字首 and 字身 — instead we just read straight through its structure from top to bottom, taking the head first: the top 一 is M, then the two verticals in the middle are each 中, giving L and L, and finally the bottom 一 is M again, so the full code is MLLM. Here's your memory hook: two flat strokes like the top and bottom of a box, two uprights standing inside — M-L-L-M, top down, easy!
亞.zh: 今日我哋學「亞」呢個字，粵音讀 aa3，指「亞洲」嘅亞，亦都可以做名字前面嘅字頭，好似「瑪利亞」咁。你望吓佢個樣，上下都係一橫，中間包住兩豎，形狀四四方方好對稱。呢個字係一個「整體字」，即係話佢唔會拆做字首同字身兩橛，而係直接由頭到尾順住個結構逐一取碼：先取最頂嗰橫「一」M，再取中間兩豎，兩個都係「中」L，最後取最底嗰橫「一」M，合埋就係 MLLM。你記住個口訣：一橫夾住兩豎、再封一橫，M-L-L-M，上下兩橫像匣門，中間兩豎企喺度，好易記！

交.en: Today's character is 交, read gaau1, and it carries a rich set of meanings — to mix, to intersect, to exchange or communicate, and also to deliver or hand something over, as in handing in your homework. Look at its shape: it's built from three pieces stacked top to bottom, starting with 亠 on the key Y, then 八 in the middle on the key C, and finally 乂 at the bottom on the key K. Because 交 is a whole character that can't be cleanly split into a lead part and a body, we use the whole-character method: take the head, the second piece, and the tail — head Y, second C, tail K — giving YCK. Here's your memory hook: just write it straight down from top to bottom, Y, C, K, and you've delivered the character in three steps.
交.zh: 今日學嘅字係「交」，讀 gaau1，意思好豐富，可以解作交錯、交往、交換，又或者係交嘢俾人，好似「交功課」咁。你望吓佢個樣，其實係由三嚿部件由上而下砌出嚟：最頂係「亠」，個鍵係 Y；跟住中間係「八」，個鍵係 C；最底係「乂」，個鍵係 K。「交」係一個整體字，冇辦法清楚分成字首同字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅取碼法，取頭一碼、第二碼同埋尾碼，即係頭 Y、二 C、尾 K，砌埋就係 YCK。記憶鉤：由頭到尾一路寫落去，Y、C、K三步就交到功課喇！

亦.en: Today we learn 亦, which reads jik6 and means "also" or "likewise" — you see it in 亦都 (jik6 dou1), meaning "also," and 亦可 (jik6 ho2), meaning "can too" or "might as well." Look at the character: it has no clean left-right or top-bottom seam, so we treat it as one whole shape (整體字) and don't force a 字首/字身 split. Whole shapes follow a special rule — you take the first, second, and third pieces, then the very last, and skip whatever sits in the middle. Following the writing order, that gives you 亠 (Y) on top, then 丨 (L), then 乙 (N), and finally 八 (C) at the end, spelling YLNC. Remember it as first-second-third-then-last, middle left out — just like in 佢亦都想去玩, "He also wants to go play."
亦.zh: 今日我哋學「亦」呢個字，佢讀作 jik6，意思係「都」、「同樣」，好似「亦都」（jik6 dou1）就係「都」嘅意思，「亦可」（jik6 ho2）就係「亦都可以」。你睇「亦」呢個字，佢冇一個清清楚楚嘅左右或者上下分界，所以我哋當佢係一個「整體字」，唔會硬生生咁劈開字首字身。整體字有條特別嘅取碼規則：取頭、二、三，再取最尾，中間嘅嘢就跳過唔理。所以我哋順住寫嘅次序，先取上面嗰點橫嘅「亠」（Y），跟住中間一豎「丨」（L），再嚟「乙」（N），最後補返尾嗰個「八」（C），合埋就係 YLNC。記住呢個口訣：頭二三尾、中間唔要——「佢亦都想去玩」，個「亦」就係咁砌出嚟。

京.en: Today we learn 京, read ging1, meaning a capital city — you'll see it in 北京 (Beijing) and 東京 (Tokyo). Look at the character and you'll notice it stacks three pieces top to bottom: 亠 on top, 口 in the middle, and 小 at the bottom. In Cangjie we first take 亠 as the head, which contributes just one code, Y; then the remaining body is coded by its first-and-last parts, 口 (R) and 小 (F), giving us the full code YRF. Remember it like this: a little hat 亠 (Y) sits above a mouth 口 (R) holding a small 小 (F) — that's your capital city.
京.zh: 今日我哋學「京」呢個字，讀做 ging1，即係首都、京城嘅意思，好似「北京」同「東京」都有佢。你望住個字，會見到佢由上而下疊起三嚿嘢：最頂係「亠」，中間係「口」，最底係「小」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，先睇上面嘅「亠」做字首，佢淨係取一碼 Y；跟住剩低嘅部分做字身，按頭尾原則取頭嘅「口」R 同尾嘅「小」F，所以整個字砌埋就係 YRF。記住：頭上一頂帽 Y，下面一個口 R 含住粒小 F，就係京城喇。

人.en: This time we're learning 人, read "jan4," which means man, people, mankind, or someone else. Take a look at its shape: one falling stroke to the left and one to the right, like a person standing with legs apart — it's one of the most basic and common characters you'll meet. In Cangjie, 人 is a whole-character (整體字), meaning it's already a complete form on its own, so you don't split it into a head piece and a body piece — it takes just a single key, O. Why can it be so short? Because Cangjie assigns many simple, low-stroke basic forms directly to one key, and 人 maps straight to the letter O. Remember it this way: see 人, one stroke left and one stroke right, and just press O — as clean as a person taking a single step.
人.zh: 我哋今次學嘅係「人」呢個字，讀「jan4」，即係人類、人群、其他人嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，一撇一捺，好似一個人張開對腳企喺度咁，係一個好基本又好常見嘅字。喺倉頡入面，「人」係一個「整體字」，即係話佢本身就係一個完整嘅字形，唔使再拆做字首同字身，所以佢只係得一碼，就係O鍵。點解可以咁簡單淨係打一個O呢？因為倉頡有個規則，好多筆畫少、結構簡單嘅基本字形都會直接對應一個鍵，「人」正正就係揸O呢個字母。記住喇：見到「人」，一撇一捺，一個O就搞掂，好似一個人淨係企咗一步咁乾脆。

今.en: The character 今 reads "gam1" and means now, today, or the present era — you meet it constantly, in words like 今日 (gam1 jat6, meaning nowadays or today) and 今年 (gam1 nin4, this year). Look at its shape: up top sits a little peaked roof, the piece 𠆢, and in Cangjie that head becomes your first key, O. Everything underneath is treated as the body, and for the body we take the first stroke and the last stroke — first is 戈 (I), last is 弓 (N) — giving you OIN all together. The reason the body contributes only those two codes is the first-last rule: once a character is divided into head and body, the body is capped, and taking just the opening and closing pieces neatly satisfies that quota without spelling out every stroke. Remember it this way: a 𠆢 roof on top (O), then from 戈 (I) down to 弓 (N) below — 𝐎𝐈𝐍 is 今.
今.zh: 今呢個字讀「gam1」，即係「而家、今日」嘅意思，係你日日都會見到嘅字，好似「今日」（gam1 jat6，指眼下呢個時候）同「今年」（gam1 nin4，指呢一年）咁。你睇佢個樣，上面有一個好似人字帽咁遮住嘅頂蓋，喺倉頡入面呢個 𠆢 就係字首，取碼 O。下面嗰嚿就係字身，我哋跟「頭尾」嘅規矩去取，頭嗰筆係戈 I，尾嗰筆係弓 N，所以合埋就係 OIN。點解字身淨係攞頭尾兩碼呢？因為一個字分咗字首同字身之後，字身最多都係攞三碼，而呢度用取頭尾嘅方法就啱啱好夠用，唔使成隻字逐筆咁拆。記住呢個口訣：頂上一個 𠆢 帽（O），底下由戈 I 到弓 N，𝐎𝐈𝐍 就係「今」。

仍.en: Today's character is 仍, read jing4, meaning "still" or "as ever" — the sense of something continuing unchanged, as in 仍然 (still) or 仍舊 (remaining the same); think of the sentence "He is still waiting for you here." Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, the familiar side form of a person, which lives on the O key. Everything on the right is the body 乃, and Cangjie breaks that into three pieces in writing order — the curving bow 弓 on N, a single throw-stroke of bamboo 竹 on H, and the corpse shape 尸 on S to finish. The head 亻 contributes just one code, O, while the body 乃 takes its full share of three codes, NHS, giving you ONHS all together. Remember it this way: a person stands on the left, still waiting, while 乃 is built on the right from bow, bamboo, and corpse.
仍.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「仍」，讀作 jing4，意思係「仍然」、「仍舊」，即係「依然」、「繼續咁樣」，好似「佢仍然喺度等你」入面咁，話畀你知件事到而家都未變。你睇下佢個形，左邊係企人邊亻，就係我哋熟悉嘅單人旁，佢喺鍵盤上面按 O。右邊淨低嘅係「乃」呢個字身，倉頡拆佢做三橛：先取彎彎嘅弓 N，再取一撇竹 H，最後收尾嗰筆屍字部 S。字首亻淨係取一個碼 O，字身「乃」就取足 NHS 三個碼，合埋就係 ONHS。記住：企人邊企喺左，右邊「乃」由弓、竹、尸三筆疊起，仍然咁企定定等你。

仔.en: Today we learn 仔, read "zai2" in Cantonese, often meaning a small thing or a child; for example 女仔 is a young lady, a girl. Look at it: on the left is the person radical 亻, and on the right sits 子, the character for child. We split it in two: the left 亻 is the head, which you press with O; the right 子 is the body, and instead of spelling out every stroke we take only its first and last shapes — 弓 first, pressed N, then 木 last, pressed D — giving us the full code OND. Why does 子 only give up its first and last? Because as the body it obeys the head-and-tail rule, taking at most two codes and skipping the middle strokes, keeping things short. Remember it this way: the little kid beside the person — a bow 弓 shooting into wood 木, so O, N, D.
仔.zh: 我哋今日學「仔」呢個字，喺廣東話讀「zai2」，好多時解細嘅嘢或者小朋友，例如「女仔」就係一個女孩子。你望下佢，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊就係一個「子」字。呢個字拆開有兩橛：左邊「亻」係字首，喺鍵盤度撳O；右邊「子」係字身，我哋唔可以逐筆拆晒，只取頭尾兩碼，頭係「弓」撳N，尾係「木」撳D，所以全碼就係OND。點解「子」淨係攞頭尾呢？因為佢已經係字身，而字身淨係最多攞頭同尾兩碼，中間嗰啲筆畫就唔理佢，咁樣先夠簡潔。記住個口訣：企人邊嘅仔，弓箭射中木——O、N、D。

他.en: Today we learn 他, read taa1, meaning 'other', 'another', or 'he/she/it' — you'll see it in 其他 kei4 taa1 ('the rest, others') and 其他人 kei4 taa1 jan4 ('other people'). Look at the character: on the left is the person radical 亻, and on the right is 也. Cangjie follows this left-right structure to split it. The 字首 on the left, 亻, gives just one code, O. The 字身 on the right is 也, and a 字身 takes at most two codes, so we take its head and its tail — the head 匕 is P and the tail 木 is D — giving OPD. Memory hook: one person 亻 standing there talking about 'the others', O-P-D, and you've got 他.
他.zh: 今日我哋學「他」呢個字，讀作 taa1，意思係「他」、「其他」、「別人」，好似「其他」kei4 taa1 或者「其他人」kei4 taa1 jan4 咁用。你望下呢個字，左邊係企人邊「亻」，右邊係「也」，倉頡就係跟住呢個左右結構嚟拆。左邊嘅字首「亻」係企人邊，佢淨係取一碼 O。右邊嘅字身係「也」，字身最多取兩碼，所以我哋取佢嘅頭同尾——頭係「匕」P，尾係「木」D，合埋就係 OPD。記住呢個字：一個人「亻」企喺度講「其他」嘅事，OPD，你就唔會拆錯喇。

仙.en: Today we learn 仙, read sin1, which originally means a Taoist immortal — a transcendent being who has attained the Way and lives forever — and in Cantonese it can even stand in for a tiny amount of money, as in "a single cent." Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is 山, the mountain — clearly a left-right structure. When Cangjie meets a left-right character, it splits from left to right: the head takes the left piece 亻, which sits on the O key, and the body takes the right piece 山, which sits on the U key. Each side gives just one code, so together they make OU — clean and short, with nothing extra. Here's your hook: a person (亻, O) climbs a mountain (山, U) to cultivate and becomes an immortal — OU!
仙.zh: 今日我哋學「仙」呢個字，讀做 sin1，本來係指道教入面得道嘅神仙、長生不老嘅仙人，喺廣東話入面仲可以借嚟講「一個仙」咁少嘅錢。你望吓佢嘅樣，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係一座山「山」，明顯係一個左右結構嘅字。倉頡遇到左右結構，就會由左至右拆開：字首取左邊嘅「亻」，攞 O 呢個鍵；字身取右邊嘅「山」，攞 U 呢個鍵。兩邊都各得一碼，加埋就係 OU，簡單利落，冇多餘嘅嘢。記住喇：一個人（亻，O）行到座山（山，U）度修煉，就變咗做神仙，OU！

代.en: Today we're learning 代, read doi6, which means to replace or substitute — think of 代表 (doi6 biu2), the person who stands in for others as a representative, or its other sense of a generation or era, as in 現代 (jin6 doi6), the present age we live in. Look at the character: on the left is the standing-person shape 亻, and on the right sits a lump that looks like 戈. To break it down, the 字首 is that left-side 亻, which you type with O; then the 字身 covers the right side, where from the 弋 form we take 戈 (I) and then the tail piece 匕 (P), giving you O, I, P in full. The 字身 is allowed to contribute more than one piece, so we grab the head 戈 first with I and then finish with the closing 匕 on P, fitting neatly into the two-or-three-code shape. Remember it this way: one standing person O holding up a spear 戈 (I) with a little dagger 匕 (P) — that's 代.
代.zh: 今日我哋學「代」呢個字，讀音係 doi6，意思係代替、替代——譬如「代表」（doi6 biu2），即係代人出面嗰個人；又或者係指世代、時代，好似「現代」（jin6 doi6），即係我哋而家身處嘅時代。你望住個字，左邊係一個企人邊亻，右邊嗰嚿睇落好似「戈」咁樣。拆碼嘅時候，字首係左邊嘅亻，按 O；跟住字身要拆右邊嗰嚿，我哋喺「弋」度取到「戈」嘅頭，按 I，再取埋個尾巴嘅匕，按 P，所以成個碼就係 O、I、P。留意個字身可以取多過一嚿，所以先取戈嘅 I，再補返個收尾嘅匕 P，就啱晒兩三碼嘅規矩。記住呢個口訣：企個人 O 頂住把戈 I 加一個匕 P，就係「代」。

令.en: Today we learn 令, which reads ling6 and means to command or order, and it also means 'to cause' or 'to make' — as in 令人開心, to make someone happy. Look at its shape: a pointed roof sitting on top, with a few strokes folded underneath. In Cangjie, 令 is a whole-form character (整體字), which means we don't split it into a head and a body — instead we sweep straight through and pull codes from start to finish: first the person-roof 𠆢 on the O key, then the halberd 戈 on the I key, then the bow 弓 on the N key, and finally one more halberd 戈 on the I key again, giving us OINI. Because it's a whole-form character, the rule is head code, second, third, plus the tail — that's O, I, N, I — so you never have to decide where a head ends and a body begins. Remember it this way: one pointed roof O, then 戈 I, 弓 N, 戈 I — 令 makes you happy, and it makes the code easy.
令.zh: 今日我哋學「令」呢個字，佢讀 ling6，意思係命令、下令，又可以解「使到、令到」，好似「令人開心」咁樣，意思就係使人開心。你望下佢個樣，上面一個尖尖嘅頭，下面幾筆疊埋落去。喺倉頡入面，「令」係一個整體字，即係話我哋唔會拆做字首字身兩截，而係一路由頭掃到尾攞碼：先攞最頂嗰個人字頭 𠆢，佢喺 O 鍵；跟住攞第二筆戈 戈，喺 I 鍵；再攞第三筆弓 弓，喺 N 鍵；最尾再攞多一個戈 戈，又係 I 鍵，合埋就係 OINI。因為佢係整體字，所以規矩係頭一碼、第二碼、第三碼加尾碼，即係 O、I、N、I，唔使諗點樣分邊度係首邊度係身。記住個口訣：一個尖頭 O，戈 I 弓 N 戈 I，「令」你一開心就記得晒。

以.en: Today's character is 以, read ji5, meaning "by means of, thereby, in order to" — you'll meet it everywhere, in words like 所以 so2 ji5 (hence) and 可以 ho2 ji5 (so-so, or "can"). Look at its shape: a cluster of strokes on the left and a clean 人 (person) on the right, and it doesn't cleanly break into a tidy front-and-back pair. Because of that, Cangjie treats 以 as a whole character (整體字), which means you take the head, the second piece, and the tail — three codes only. The head is 女 (V), the second piece is the little 戈 shape (I), and the tail is 人 (O), giving you exactly VIO. The whole-character rule spares you from wrestling with the fiddly middle strokes: just grab first, second, and last, and let your memory hook be "a woman (V) crosses a blade (I) and finally meets a person (O)" — V, I, O, and you'll type 以 right from now on.
以.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「以」，讀 ji5，意思係「用嚟」、「憑住」，好似「所以」so2 ji5、「可以」ho2 ji5 咁樣，係好常用嘅字。你睇吓佢個形，左邊有幾筆，右邊係一個「人」。呢個字唔容易乾淨咁拆開頭尾兩截，所以倉頡當佢係整體字，用頭、次、尾三碼嘅取碼方法：頭碼取「女」V，次碼取當中似「戈」嘅一筆 I，尾碼取最後嘅「人」O，砌埋就係 VIO。要記住整體字唔會分字首字身四碼，而係頭一個、第二個、同最尾一個字形，剛好幫你避開中間啲難處理嘅碎筆。記住個口訣：女行過一刀（戈），最後遇到一個人——V、I、O，「以後」以後就唔會拆錯喇！

仲.en: Today we're learning 仲, which reads zung6. Its root meaning is the middle brother in a family, and by extension a go-between or mediator, and it also works as a surname — but in spoken Cantonese you'll meet it constantly in words like 仲有 and 仲係, where it means "moreover" or "still." Look at the shape: it's two pieces side by side, with 亻 (the standing-person radical) on the left, typed with O, and 中 on the right, typed with L, giving you the full code OL. The split falls right down the middle because 亻 sits on the left as the head and 中 stands on the right as the body — one head, one body, exactly two codes, nothing more to take. Here's your hook: picture a person (亻 = O) standing in the middle (中 = L), and you've got 仲.
仲.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「仲」，讀音係 zung6，本義係排行中間嘅兄弟，又可以解作居中調停嘅人，亦都做姓氏用；不過喺廣東話口語入面，你會成日見到佢，好似「仲有」、「仲係」噉，解作「還」、「依然」嘅意思。你睇下呢個字，係左右兩件砌埋一齊嘅：左邊係「亻」，即係企人邊，喺個鍵盤度撳 O 字；右邊係「中」，撳 L 字，所以成個字碼就係 OL。點解要噉樣拆呢？因為「亻」企喺左邊做字首，「中」擺喺右邊做字身，一件頭一件身，剛剛好兩碼，唔使再取多。記住喇：一個人（亻＝O）企喺個「中」（L）間，就係「仲」。

件.en: Today we learn 件, read gin6, a measure word you use to count objects or matters — think of 呢件衫 (this piece of clothing) or 一件事 (one matter). Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right sits a 牛. When we split it, the head 亻 is taken straight as O; then the body 牛, being too full to take whole, follows the first-last rule and gives its head 竹 (H) and its tail 手 (Q), so the full code is OHQ. Remember it this way: one person 亻 holding the first and last (H, Q) makes a single 件 of something.
件.zh: 今日我哋學「件」呢個字，讀作 gin6，係量詞，好似講「呢件衫」、「一件事」咁樣用嚟數啲物件或者事情。你睇下佢個樣，左邊係企人邊「亻」，右邊係一個「牛」字，兩部分合埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「亻」直接攞佢，即係 O 掣；右邊嘅字身係「牛」，因為佢唔止得一兩碼，所以要用首尾兩碼嘅取碼法，攞頭嗰個「竹」H，再攞尾嗰個「手」Q，合埋就係 OHQ。記住喇：一個人「亻」，攞住頭同尾（H、Q），就儲成一「件」嘢。

任.en: Today's character is 任, read jam6 or jam4, meaning to appoint, to trust, to rely on, and also duty or office — you'll see it in 任何 (jam6 ho4, meaning any or whatever) and 任務 (jam6 mou6, meaning mission or task). Look at its shape: it's a left-right character, with the standing-person radical 亻 on the left and 壬 on the right. The left piece 亻 becomes the 字首, the head, and it takes the key O. The right piece 壬 is the 字身, the body, and when Cangjie breaks down a body it usually takes just the head and the tail, so from 壬 you take the head 竹 (H) and the tail 土 (G), giving you OHG all together. Here's your hook: a person (O) shoulders (HG) a duty — 任 is someone standing ready to bear the load.
任.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「任」，讀作 jam6 或者 jam4，意思係委任、任用、信任，又可以指責任同職務，好似「任何」（jam6 ho4，即係無論邊個）同「任務」（jam6 mou6，即係使命同職責）咁樣。你望下佢，係一個左右結構嘅字：左邊係企人邊亻，右邊係「壬」。左邊嘅亻我哋當作字首，佢對應個 O 掣。右邊嘅壬就係字身，倉頡分拆字身嘅時候，通常取頭同尾兩個部分，所以我哋喺壬入面攞個頭嘅竹（H），再攞個尾嘅土（G），合埋就係 OHG。記住呢個字嘅口訣：一個人（O）擔起（HG）一份責任，人企喺前面，扛住個壬——就係「任」。

份.en: Today we look at 「份」, read fan6 or fan2, meaning a portion or part, and also one's duty or share. Look at it: on the left is the standing-person radical 「亻」, and on the right sits the character 「分」. When we break it into code, 「亻」 is the 字首 and takes just one code, O; then 「分」 is the 字身, and instead of taking every stroke we take the first-two-and-last, which gives us 「八」C, then 「尸」S, then 「竹」H — spelling OCSH together. Why split the body this way? Because when a 字身 has more than two parts, Cangjie takes head, next, and tail — so 「八」 is the head, 「尸」 the next, 「竹」 the tail, and whatever sits between is skipped. Remember it as a person 「亻」 holding one 「份」 — 「this gift is yours」 — the person stands on the left while 八, 尸, 竹 line up on the right.
份.zh: 我哋今日睇「份」呢個字，讀 fan6 或者 fan2，意思係一部分、一份，又或者係本分、職責。你望下佢，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊就係「分」字。拆碼嘅時候，「亻」係字首，佢淨係取一碼 O；跟住嘅「分」係字身，我哋唔逐筆全取，而係取頭二尾，即係頭嗰個「八」C、然後「尸」S、最後「竹」H，合埋成 OCSH。點解字身係咁樣拆呢？因為字身唔止兩碼嗰陣，倉頡就取「頭、次、尾」三碼，「八」係頭、「尸」係次、「竹」係尾，中間嘅筆畫就跳過。記住一句：一個人「亻」拎一「份」禮物——「呢份禮物係你嘅」，人企喺左邊，八尸竹排喺右邊。

企.en: Today's character is 企, read kei2, and its most familiar sense in Cantonese is simply to stand — to stand somewhere, to stand to one side. Look at it: there's a 人 (person) sitting on top, and a 止 planted underneath, two pieces stacked together. Cangjie treats the top 人 as the 字首, a self-contained part that gives just one code, O; the bottom 止 is the 字身, and a 字身 takes head, second, and tail — three codes — so you take 卜 Y, then 中 L, then the final stroke 一 M. Put it all together and you get OYLM (人-卜-中-一). Memory hook: a person 人 standing on 止, OYLM — when you 返屋企, go home, that's where you stand.
企.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「企」，讀作 kei2，最熟悉嘅意思就係「企」——企喺度、企埋一邊嗰個企。你望下佢，上面係一個「人」，下面墊住一個「止」，兩件砌埋一齊。倉頡拆呢個字，上面嘅字首「人」係一個獨立部件，攞一碼就夠，寫個 O；下面嘅「止」做字身，字身要取頭、次、尾三碼，所以順住寫「卜」Y、「中」L、同埋最尾嗰橫「一」M。合埋就係 OYLM，人卜中一。記憶鉤：一個「人」企喺「止」上面，OYLM，你返屋企就企喺度啦。

似.en: Today we learn 似, read ci5, meaning to resemble or seem alike — as in 好似 (hou2 ci5, similar, alike) and 似乎 (ci5 fu4, it seems, as if). Look at the character: on the left is the person radical 亻, and on the right is the whole piece 以. When we split it, the left-side 亻 is the 字首, and a radical like this contributes just one code, O; then the right-side 以 is the 字身, from which we take the head and the tail, following the writing order to get ㄑ (V), 戈 (I), and 人 (O). Put together, the full code is O, V, I, O. Here's your memory hook: one person (亻, O) watching 以 will start to look just alike — 似.
似.zh: 我哋今日學「似」呢個字，讀做 ci5，意思係「相似、好像、似乎」，好似「好似」（hou2 ci5，即係差唔多、相像）同「似乎」（ci5 fu4，即係好像、彷彿）咁。你望下呢個字，左邊係「人」字旁「亻」，右邊係「以」字。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「亻」係字首，一個部件只取一碼，就係 O；跟住右邊嘅「以」做字身，字身要取頭同尾，我哋順住寫嘅次序攞到「ㄑ」（V）、「戈」（I）、同埋「人」（O）三碼，所以成個字砌埋就係 O、V、I、O。記住個口訣：一個人（亻，O）望住「以」，你就會覺得佢哋好「似」。

但.en: Today we learn 但, read daan6, meaning "but, however, yet" — the word you hear in 但係, "but." Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is 旦, a picture of a person pausing to say "however..." To key it, the head 亻 comes first and lives on O; then the body 旦, being a body, gives only its first and last pieces — the top 日 on A, and the bottom single stroke 一 on M. Typed in order that gives you O, A, M, so the full code is OAM. Here's your hook: a person (O) speaks up, and even as the sun (日, A) sinks to the horizon line (一, M), they keep saying "but..."
但.zh: 今日我哋學「但」呢個字，讀做 daan6，係「不過、然而」嘅意思，好似「但係」咁常用。你望下佢個形，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係「旦」，意思本來就係一個人企喺度講「不過⋯⋯」。拆碼嘅時候，字首係「亻」，佢喺鍵盤上面對應 O；跟住嘅字身係「旦」，因為佢係字身，我哋淨係取頭同尾兩個部件——頭係「日」對應 A，尾係最底嗰一橫「一」對應 M。所以成個字順住打落去就係 O、A、M，即係 OAM。記住喇：一個人（O）講咗一句話，太陽（日 A）落到地平線（一 M）——「但係」黃昏都要繼續講落去。

位.en: Look at this character: 位, read wai6 or wai2, meaning position, seat, status, or a post or rank. Notice it's built from a left part and a right part: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, which we call 人 (person), and you'll find it on the O key. The right side, 立, is the 字身 (body), and because a body only needs its head and tail codes, we don't spell it out stroke by stroke — instead we take its head 亠 on Y and its tail 廿 on T, skipping what sits in between. So the whole character types straight across as O, then Y, then T. Remember it this way: a person standing beside 立 has claimed a spot — a 位.
位.zh: 睇下呢個字：位，讀作 wai6 或者 wai2，意思係位置、座位、地位，又或者係崗位、職位。你留意到佢係左右兩部分砌成嘅，左邊嗰個企人邊亻，我哋叫做「人」字，喺鍵盤上面撳 O。右邊個「立」字就係字身，因為一個字身淨係要頭尾兩碼，所以我哋唔會將佢逐筆拆完，而係取佢個頭亠，撳 Y，再取佢個尾廿，撳 T，中間嘅筆畫就跳過。所以成個字順住打落去就係 O、Y、T。記住個口訣：一個人企喺立字旁邊，就佔咗一個位。

低.en: Today we learn 低, read "dai1", meaning low, or to lower, hang, and bow down. Look at it: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is 氐. When Cangjie splits this character, the left 亻 acts as the prefix and takes just one code, O; the right 氐 acts as the body and is taken by the first-second-last method, so we grab the head and tail of 氏 — that's 竹 H and 匕 P — then add the bottom stroke 一, which is M, giving the full code OHPM. Remember, the prefix gets only one code while the body takes first-second-last, and since 氐 is just 氏 with one extra stroke underneath, that final M is what supplies the bottom line. Memory hook: a person 亻 crouching down so low that they touch the ground line 一 — that's 低.
低.zh: 今日我哋學「低」呢個字，讀「dai1」，意思係低、低下，又或者係垂低、俯低身。你睇下佢，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係「氐」。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，左邊嘅「亻」做字首，只取一碼，就係 O；右邊嘅「氐」做字身，用「頭二尾」嘅方法嚟拆，先取「氏」呢個部分嘅頭同尾，即係竹 H 同匕 P，然之後補返最底嗰一橫「一」，即係 M，所以成個字砌埋就係 OHPM。記住喇，字首得一碼、字身取頭二尾嘅原則，而「氐」比「氏」多咗底下一橫，就係靠最後嗰個 M 補返出嚟。記憶鉤：一個人「亻」蹲到好低，低到貼住地下嗰一「橫」，就係「低」啦。

住.en: Today we learn 住, read zyu6, meaning to reside or live somewhere — the 住 in 我住喺香港, "I live in Hong Kong." Look at its shape: it's a left-right character, with the standing-person radical 亻 on the left and 主 on the right. In Cangjie we take the 字首 (the head part) first — that's 亻 on the O key — then we break down the 字身 on the right, 主, taking its head 卜 on the Y key and its tail 土 on the G key, giving us OYG. Why only head and tail on the right? Because a 字身 takes at most three codes, and here 主 splits neatly into just two pieces, 卜 above and 土 below, so taking head-then-tail covers it all. Memory hook: a person 亻 comes and settles down — plunk (卜) onto the earth (土) — that's where they live, 住.
住.zh: 今日我哋學「住」字，讀做 zyu6，意思係居住、住喺邊度嘅「住」，好似「我住喺香港」咁樣。你望下呢個字，佢係左右結構：左邊係企人邊「亻」，右邊係「主」。倉頡拆法係先攞左邊嘅字首「亻」，佢喺 O 鍵；再拆右邊嘅字身「主」，字身要取頭同尾，所以攞個頭「卜」，佢喺 Y 鍵，最後攞個尾「土」，佢喺 G 鍵，砌埋就係 OYG。點解右邊淨係攞頭尾兩碼呢？因為喺字首字身結構入面，字身最多取三碼，但「主」拆開就係「卜」加「土」兩件，所以順住頭尾攞晒就夠。記住呢個口訣：一個人「亻」蹲喺度，卜卜聲落到「土」上面住咗低，就係「住」。

何.en: Today we learn 何, read ho4, the word you meet in 任何 (jam6 ho4, meaning any or whatever) and 何時 (when); on its own it asks what, why, where, or how. Look at it: on the left stands the person radical 亻, and on the right sits 可. The 亻 takes the role of 字首 and gives us its key O; then the whole right side 可 becomes the 字身, and because a 字身 can be broken into first, second and last pieces, we read straight down through it — the top stroke 一 is M, the 弓 in the middle is N, and the 口 at the bottom is R. Put together that makes OMNR, four codes in all — just picture a person standing on the left while 可 lines up 一, 弓, 口 down its side, and you've got 何.
何.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「何」，讀 ho4，喺「任何」（jam6 ho4，即係無論邊個都得）或者「何時」（幾時）呢啲詞入面出現，本身係問「乜嘢、點解、邊度」嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係「可」字。企人邊「亻」做字首，取佢個鍵 O；跟住右邊嘅「可」做字身，字身可以拆到頭、二、尾三碼，所以我哋順住寫落去：頂上一橫「一」係 M，中間個「弓」係 N，最後個「口」係 R。合埋就係 OMNR 四碼——記住「亻」做人企喺左，右邊個「可」一橫一弓一口拉直落嚟，就係「何」喇。

作.en: Today we're learning 作, read zok3, meaning to make, to work, or to compose and write. Look at it closely: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right sits 乍 — together it gives the feeling of a person at work doing something. When we split it, the left-side head 亻 takes just one code, O, because a 字首 head is only allowed one code; then the right-side 乍 becomes the body, and a body gives its head and tail, so we take the head 竹 (H) and the tail 尸 (S), making the full code O, H, S. Here's your hook: a person (亻) holding bamboo (竹) sitting down (尸) is busy at 作, getting the work done.
作.zh: 今日我哋學「作」呢個字，讀 zok3，解做「製作」、「工作」或者「創作」寫作嘅意思。你望下佢，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係「乍」——成個字係「人喺度做嘢」嘅感覺。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「亻」淨係取一碼 O，因為字首規矩只攞一碼；跟住右邊嘅「乍」做字身，字身要取頭同尾，頭係「竹」H，尾係「尸」S，所以成個字拆做 O、H、S。你可以咁記：一個人（亻）攞住把竹（竹）坐低（尸），就係喺度「作」嘢喇！

你.en: Today we're learning 你, read nei5 — it's the second-person pronoun "you," the one you reach for whenever you're talking to someone, and you'll see it everywhere. Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, which you type with O; on the right the body 尔 is split into its head and tail, giving you 弓 typed N and 火 typed F, so the whole code is ONF. Why does it break there? Because 亻 as the 字首 (lead piece) is allowed just one code, and taking itself alone is enough; the following body 尔 has many strokes, so it follows the head-tail rule, keeping only the opening 弓 and the closing 火 and skipping the middle. Here's your memory hook: a person (O) stands before you, draws a bow (N), and out flies a spark of fire (F) — that's 你!
你.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「你」，讀作 nei5，就係「你我他」嗰個第二人稱代名詞，講緊對方嘅時候就用佢，你日日都會見到。你望下佢個樣，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，呢個部件喺鍵盤上打 O；右邊嘅「尔」字身就拆開頭尾兩粒，頭係「弓」打 N，尾係「火」打 F，所以成個字就係 ONF。點解要噉拆呢？因為「亻」做字首，只可以取一碼，取佢自己就夠；跟住嘅字身「尔」筆畫多，就跟「頭尾」規矩，只攞開頭嘅「弓」同埋收尾嘅「火」，中間唔理。記住喇：一個「人」（O）站喺你面前，張弓（N）一射，擦出火花（F），噉就係「你」！

佢.en: Today we learn a word you use every single day: 佢, read keoi5, the Cantonese pronoun for he, she, or it — one character covers all of them, no matter the gender or whether it's a thing. Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right sits 巨. The character splits into a head part and a body part: the head is that left-side person radical 亻, which you type with O. The body is the 巨 on the right, and Cangjie tells us to take its first and last pieces — both the boxy frame shape 匚 — so you press S twice, making the full code O, S, S. Remember it this way: a person (亻, O) standing before one box (匚, S) and closed off by another box (匚, S) — that's 佢.
佢.zh: 今日我哋學一個你日日都用嘅字：「佢」，讀音係 keoi5，即係廣東話入面嘅「他、她、牠」，唔理男定女定物，都用呢個字。你望下佢個樣，左邊係個企人邊「亻」，右邊係「巨」字。呢個字分做字首同字身兩橛：字首係左邊嘅企人邊「亻」，喺鍵盤上面撳 O。字身係右邊個「巨」字，倉頡教我哋取頭同尾兩碼，個「巨」字頭尾兩橛都係方框形嘅「匚」，所以連續撳兩次 S，全碼就係 O、S、S。記住喇：一個人（亻，O）企喺一個大方框（匚，S）前面，再一個方框（匚，S）收尾，佢就係「佢」。

佳.en: Today's character is 佳, read gaai1, meaning good, beautiful, or excellent — you meet it in 最佳 (zeoi3 gaai1, the very best) and 佳美 (gaai1 mei5, beautiful). Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, which lives on the O key, and on the right are two 土 pieces stacked up, each one taken on the G key. Because 亻is the one-code head, it gives just a single code, and then the two 土 on the right each contribute their own code, so reading straight across you get O, then G, then G — OGG. Picture one person (O) standing on two mounds of earth (G, G), steady and fine — that's 佳.
佳.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「佳」，讀音係 gaai1，意思係「好、美好、優秀」，好似「最佳」（zeoi3 gaai1，即係最好）同「佳美」（gaai1 mei5，美麗）咁樣。你望下佢個形，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，鍵係 O，右邊係兩個「土」疊埋一齊，每個「土」個鍵都係 G。因為「亻」做字首，一碼就夠，右邊兩個「土」就各自取一碼，所以順住寫落嚟就係 O、G、G，即係 OGG。你可以咁記：一個人（O）企喺兩堆泥土（G、G）上面，安穩又美好，就係「佳」。

使.en: Today we learn 使, which in Cantonese has three readings—si2, sai2, si3—and means to cause, to send someone on a mission, to order, or the person doing it: an envoy or ambassador. Look at its shape: on the left stands the person radical, and on the right sits a cluster of strokes packed together. When we split it, the head 字首 is that standing-person 亻, keyed O; then the whole right side becomes the body 字身, and since a body takes at most three codes, we grab its head, second and tail—head 十 is J, second 中 is L, tail 大 is K—giving OJLK. Why head, second and tail? Because when a body holds more than three pieces, Cangjie won't take every one; it keeps only the first, the second and the last, so the code stays short and clean. Hold onto this: person O, then 十J, 中L, 大K march in—and 唔使咁客氣, no need to be so polite, types itself out.
使.zh: 我哋今日學「使」字，粵語有三個讀音——si2、sai2、si3——意思係「令到、差遣、命令」，又或者指「使者、使節」呢啲人。你望吓佢個形：左邊係企人邊，右邊係一組筆畫砌埋一齊。拆字嘅時候，字首就係企人邊亻，鍵係O；跟住成個右邊做字身，字身最多取三碼，所以取頭、二、尾——頭係十J，第二係中L，尾係大K，砌成OJLK。點解係「頭、二、尾」呢？因為字身超過三個部件嘅時候，倉頡就唔會逐件取，而係揀頭一件、第二件同最後一件，咁樣先夠精簡。記住呢個口訣：企人O，之後十J、中L、大K跟住行，「唔使咁客氣」自然就打得出嚟。

來.en: Today we learn 來, read "loi4", meaning to come or approach — you see it in 未來 mei6 loi4, the future, and 從來 cung4 loi4, meaning always or ever. Look at the character: it's a whole, tangled shape, and Cangjie has a clever trick for this kind of character — ignore everything crammed in the middle and take codes only from the head and the tail. So we start with 木 at the top, which is D, then take the two little 人 at the bottom, each one O, skipping all the crossing strokes in between, giving us D, O, O. To remember it, picture a tree (D) with two people (O and O) walking out from underneath it, coming your way.
來.zh: 今日我哋學「來」字，讀「loi4」，即係「來到」、「過來」嘅意思，好似「未來」mei6 loi4 就係將來嘅日子，「從來」cung4 loi4 就係一路以嚟嘅意思。你望吓個字，佢係一個整體字，中間又交叉又複雜，倉頡對付呢種字有個聰明嘅辦法：唔理中間所有嘢，淨係喺頭同尾攞碼。所以我哋先攞最上面嘅「木」，係 D 鍵，跟住喺下面攞兩個「人」，都係 O 鍵，中間嗰啲橫豎全部跳過，砌成 D、O、O。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成一棵樹木（D）下面企咗兩個人（O、O）行過嚟，咁就記得晒喇！

例.en: Today's character is 例, read lai6, meaning a precedent or example — as in 條例, meaning regulations or an ordinance. Look at its shape: it's a left-right character, with the standing-person radical 亻 on the left and 列 on the right. The 亻 is the prefix and gives just one code, O; the 列 on the right is the body, and Cangjie tells us a body takes its head, next, and tail, so from 列 we grab the head stroke 一 as M, then 弓 as N, and finally the tail 弓 again as N — putting it together as OMNN. Here's your hook: picture a person standing beside two bow-shaped 弓 pieces, holding up an example for you to copy — that's 例.
例.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「例」，讀作 lai6，即係例子、先例嘅意思，好似「條例」咁樣就係規則、法例。你望下呢個字，佢係左右結構，左邊係企人邊「亻」，右邊係「列」。企人邊「亻」係字首，取一個碼 O；右邊「列」係字身，倉頡教我哋字身要取頭、次、尾三個碼，所以喺「列」入面攞頭嗰筆「一」M、跟住嘅「弓」N，最後又係一個「弓」N，加埋成個字就係 OMNN。記法好簡單：一個人企喺度舉起兩張「弓」形嘅紙做示範，呢個就係「例」子啦！

供.en: Today's character is 供, read gung1 or gung3, meaning to supply, to provide for, or to make an offering in worship. Look at its shape: it's narrow on the left and wider on the right, with the standing-person radical 亻 as the 字首 on the left and 共 as the 字身 on the right. The 字首 亻 is simple and gives just one code, so you press O. The 字身 共 is more than two pieces, so by the rule we take its head and tail — the head 廿 is T and the tail 八 is C — which together spell OTC. Remember it this way: one person (亻, O) takes twenty (廿, T) things and shares them among eight (八, C) — that's supplying, 供.
供.zh: 今日學嘅字係「供」，讀 gung1 或者 gung3，意思係供應、供給，又或者係拜神時嘅供奉。你望下佢，係一個左窄右闊嘅字：左邊個企人邊「亻」係字首，右邊個「共」係字身。字首「亻」好簡單，一碼就搞掂，撳 O 就得。跟住睇字身「共」，佢唔止兩碼咁少，所以我哋跟規矩取頭同尾——頭係「廿」，撳 T；尾係「八」，撳 C，合埋就係 OTC。你可以咁記：一個人（亻，O）拎住廿（T）樣嘢分俾八（C）個人，就係「供應」嘅供啦。

便.en: Today we meet 便, a character that reads bin6 in 方便 and pin4 in 便宜, meaning convenience, ease, or doing something the expedient way. Look at its shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right sits the character 更, and together they form 便. When we break it into Cangjie code, 便 splits left-and-right: the left 亻 is the head and gives its key O, while the right-side 更 is the body, and a body follows the head-second-last rule to take three codes — 一 (M), 中 (L), and 乂 (K) — giving us OMLK. The reason the body takes only three pieces is that once a character divides into head and body, the body can never spell out all its strokes; it is limited, so we choose the head, the second, and the last to stand in for the whole. Remember it this way: a person 亻 standing there looking for convenience — that O leads the way.
便.zh: 今日我哋學「便」呢個字，佢有幾個讀音——「方便」讀 bin6，「便宜」讀 pin4，意思係方便、容易、隨手就得。你望下佢個樣，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係「更」字，兩件夾埋就係「便」。拆碼嘅時候，「便」係一個左右結構嘅字，左邊「亻」做字首，取佢個鍵 O；右邊「更」做字身，字身照倉頡規矩取頭、二、尾三碼，所以攞「一」M、「中」L、同埋「乂」K，合埋成 OMLK。點解字身淨係取三個碼？因為當一個字分咗字首字身，字身最多都係取三碼，唔可以齊晒五件，所以先要揀頭、二、尾嚟代表。記住呢個字：一個人企喺度求方「便」，你就會諗起左邊個「亻」O 帶頭喇。

係.en: Today's character is 係, read hai6, a word you use constantly in Cantonese — in 即係 and 但係 — and it originally carries the sense of binding or being connected. Look at its shape: on the left stands the person radical 亻, and on the right is a cluster of strokes packed together. When we break it down, the 字首 (lead) is that left-side person radical 亻, which sits on key O; then the 字身 (body) is split into head, second, and tail, taking the head 丿 on H, the second piece ㄑ on V, and the tail 小 on F, giving the full code OHVF. Why does the body split this way? Because when a body has many strokes, Cangjie never spells out every one — it takes just the head, a middle representative, and the tail, so you type fast and remember easily. Hold the order in mind: the person (O) walks across (H), then a slash and a little 小 (V, F) — that's 係.
係.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「係」，讀作 hai6，喺廣東話入面用得好密，好似「即係」、「但係」咁，本身有牽連、關聯嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊就係一堆筆畫砌埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，字首就係左邊嗰個企人邊「亻」，佢個鍵係 O；接住嘅字身要拆做頭、二、尾三部分，先取個頭「丿」係 H，再取第二個「ㄑ」係 V，最後取個尾「小」係 F，所以成個碼就係 OHVF。點解字身係咁拆呢？因為當一個字身筆畫比較多嘅時候，倉頡唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取頭、取次、取尾三個代表碼，等你打得快又記得住。記住呢個順序：企人（O）行過去（H），一撇一小（V、F），就係「係」喇。

保.en: Today we learn 保, read bou2, meaning to protect, to safeguard, or to care for — as in 保護 (to protect) and 確保 (to ensure). Look at its structure: on the left is the person radical 亻, and on the right sits a 口 on top with a 木 below, and together they make 保. The 亻 on the left is the 字首, typed O; the right side is the 字身, and when Cangjie breaks a 字身 it takes head and tail — the 口 on top is the head R, and the 木 at the bottom is the tail D, giving you the full code O, R, D. Remember it as a person O keeping watch over a mouth R and a tree D — that's the 保 in 保重, to take care.
保.zh: 今日我哋學「保」呢個字，讀做 bou2，意思係保護、保衛、照顧，好似「保護」同埋「確保」咁。你望下佢個結構，左邊係人字邊亻，右邊上面係個口，下面係個木，砌埋一齊就係「保」。人字邊亻擺喺左邊，佢就係字首，撳 O；右邊嗰橛係字身，倉頡拆字身嘅時候，取頭同取尾，個口喺上面就係頭 R，個木喺下面就係尾 D，所以整個碼就係 O、R、D。記住呢個左右分家嘅拆法：一個人 O 喺度睇實住一個口 R 一棵木 D，就係「保重」嘅「保」。

信.en: Today we learn 信, read seon3, meaning to trust or believe, and it can also mean a letter you write — you'll see it in words like 相信 soeng1 seon3 (to trust) and 信仰 seon3 joeng5 (belief). Look at its structure: on the left is 亻, the standing-person radical, and on the right is the character 言. The 亻 is the 字首, drawn as a person leaning on the side, and you type it with O; a 字首 gives only one code, so it simply hands you O. The remaining 言 is the 字身, and Cangjie lets a 字身 take several positions, so we grab its head 卜 (Y), then the second stroke 一 (M), and finally the tail 口 (R), giving OYMR altogether. Remember it this way: a person (O) speaks words made of 卜, 一, 口 — and spoken words should always be trustworthy!
信.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「信」，讀作 seon3，解作相信、信任，亦可以指一封信件，好似「相信」soeng1 seon3、「信仰」seon3 joeng5 咁樣用。你望吓佢個結構：左邊係「亻」（單人邊），右邊係一個「言」字。「亻」係字首，佢就係人字企喺邊嘅樣，喺鍵盤上打 O，字首只取一碼，所以佢就簡簡單單畀你一個 O。剩返嘅「言」係字身，倉頡幫字身分配幾個位置，於是取佢個頭「卜」（打 Y）、跟住第二筆「一」（打 M），最後取個尾「口」（打 R），砌埋一齊就係 OYMR。你可以咁記：一個人（O）講咗一句卜、一、口嘅說話，講出嚟嘅嘢就要有信用啦！

修.zh: 今日我哋學「修」呢個字，讀音係 sau1，意思係修理、修讀、修養——好似「修訂」sau1 ding3、「修改」sau1 goi2 咁樣。你望住個字，佢由幾個部件砌成，我哋順住打字次序拆佢。最左邊嗰個「亻」係企人邊，取碼 O，跟住中間有一豎「丨」取 L。呢個「亻」係字首，字首只可以取兩碼，所以「亻」O 加「丨」L 之後就夠數，剩返嘅部分「攸」加「彡」全部歸入字身，字身用頭尾規則，取最頭嘅「人」O 同最尾嘅「竹」H，砌埋一齊就係 OLOH。記住個口訣：一個企人一豎，人字打頭、竹字收尾，修理就係咁修！

俾.en: Today's character is 俾, read "bei2," and in Cantonese it means to give or hand over — exactly the everyday word you'd use in a sentence like "give me the pen." Look at how it's built: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is the character 卑. When Cangjie breaks it up, the left side becomes the prefix, and since 亻 is the leaning-person form it takes just one code, O; then the right-hand 卑 becomes the body, and because a body of this size takes more than two codes, we grab its first, second, and last shapes in order — bamboo 竹 (H), bamboo 竹 again (H), and the final ten 十 (J). Put it all together and the full code is OHHJ, that is O, H, H, J. Here's your memory hook: a person 亻 stands there holding two stalks of bamboo (HH) and plants a little flag 十 (J) to hand it over to you — 俾 is all about giving something to someone.
俾.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「俾」，讀「bei2」，喺廣東話入面就係「畀、給」嘅意思，好似「你俾支筆我」咁樣，日日都會用到。你望吓佢嘅結構：左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係一個「卑」字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，先睇左邊做字首，企人邊「亻」係人字嘅側身寫法，取一碼 O 就夠；跟住右邊個「卑」字做字身，因為字身唔止兩筆，就要取頭、二、尾三碼，順住寫落去係竹「H」、竹「H」、再加最尾嗰個十「J」。所以合埋成個碼就係 OHHJ，即係 O、H、H、J。你可以咁記：一個人「亻」企喺度，親手拎住兩枝竹「HH」，再插支旗仔「J」送俾你——「俾」就係送嘢俾人嘅意思。

個.en: Today we learn 個, read "go3", a measure word — the piece you use when counting a single thing, as in 一個 (one) or 呢個 (this one). Look at how it's built: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is the character 固. In Cangjie, the head 字首 takes that left-side 亻, which lives on the O key; then the body 字身 is 固, and since a body may take at most three codes, we pull its head 囗 (on W), its second piece 十 (on J), and its tail 口 (on R), giving us OWJR. The reason we take only these three is the body's three-code quota — head, middle, tail stand in for the whole of 固. Picture a person 亻 holding a firm little box 固, and you've got 個.
個.zh: 我哋今日學「個」呢個字，讀「go3」，係量詞，好似「一個」、「呢個」咁樣，數單一件嘢就用佢。你望下佢嘅結構：左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊係一個「固」字。倉頡拆字，字首取左邊嘅「亻」，佢喺O鍵；跟住字身係「固」，字身最多取三碼，所以我哋取佢個頭「囗」（喺W鍵）、第二個部件「十」（喺J鍵），再取最後嘅「口」（喺R鍵），合埋就係OWJR。點解字身淨係取呢三部分？因為字身有三碼嘅限額，要取頭、次、尾嚟代表成個「固」。記住呢個字：一個「人」，揸住一個「固」定嘅盒仔，就係「個」。

們.en: Today we learn 們, read mun4, a character that marks a plural — you meet it in 他們 (taa1 mun4), meaning "they" or "them," and in 他們的 (taa1 mun4 dik1), meaning "their." Look at how it's built from two big parts: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, which you type with O, and on the right is the 門 (gate) shape. Cangjie limits a character to at most five codes, so when a body has many strokes we don't break it down stroke by stroke — instead we take just its first and last pieces. The body 門 gives its opening piece 日 (A) and its closing piece 弓 (N), skipping everything between, so the whole code is OAN. Picture a person (亻) standing at a gate — the gate opens and shuts, leaving only its head and tail, O-A-N, and you've typed 們.
們.zh: 今日我哋學「們」呢個字，讀音係 mun4，係一個表示複數嘅字，好似「他們」（taa1 mun4）就係指「佢哋」，「他們的」（taa1 mun4 dik1）就係「佢哋嘅」。你睇下佢分做兩大部分：左邊係企人邊「亻」，喺鍵盤上面打 O；右邊係一個「門」字。倉頡有個規矩，一個字最多拆五碼，所以當字身有好多筆畫嘅時候，就唔會逐筆咁拆晒，而係取「頭尾碼」——「門」字取佢起頭嘅「日」（A）同埋最尾嘅「弓」（N），中間嗰啲就省略咗。所以合埋就係 OAN。記住呢個口訣：一個人（亻）企喺門口，門一開一關，剩低頭同尾——O、A、N，「們」就打好喇。

候.en: Today we learn 候, read hau6, meaning to wait or expect, and also to greet or pay a visit. Look at it: on the left stands the person radical 亻, and on the right sits a body made of several stacked pieces. The 亻 on the left is the 字首, and a single-part 字首 gives just one code, so we take its key O first. The right-hand 字身 then follows the head-middle-tail rule: the head piece is 中, taking L; the second piece is 弓, taking N; and the tail piece is 大, taking K — together OLNK. Here's your hook: one person 亻 stands on the left while 中, 弓 and 大 line up on the right, all waiting — that waiting builds 候!
候.zh: 今日我哋學「候」字，讀做 hau6，解等候、期望，又可以係問候、拜候嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右邊就係一嚿由幾件砌埋一齊嘅字身。左邊嘅「亻」係字首，一個部件就夠一碼，所以我哋先取佢個 O。右邊嘅字身跟返頭、次、尾嘅規矩去揀：頭嗰件係「中」，取 L；跟住第二件係「弓」，取 N；最尾嗰件係「大」，取 K，合埋就係 OLNK。記住嘞：一個「亻」企喺左邊，右邊等緊「中弓大」三兄弟排隊，一齊等候，就砌成「候」喇！

值.en: Today we learn 值, read zik6, meaning price or worth — you meet it in 數值 (a numerical value) and 值得 (worth doing, worth the money). Look at its shape: on the left stands a person radical, and on the right sits the character 直. When we split it, the left-side 亻 becomes the head and takes the key O on your keyboard; then the body is read straight through, top to bottom, taking a first, second and last code — 十 (J) at the top, ⺼ (B) in the middle, and the single stroke 一 (M) at the bottom, giving OJBM. Why does the body get three codes? Because the head is just the lone 亻, everything else falls to the body, and a body may take up to three codes — first, second and last — which fits 十, ⺼ and 一 exactly. Remember it this way: a person (O) looking at 直, counting down 十, ⺼, 一 — that's OJBM for 值.
值.zh: 今日我哋學「值」呢個字，讀音係 zik6，意思係價值、值得，好似「數值」係數目嘅值、「值得」就係抵買抵做嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，左邊係一個企喺度嘅人字邊，右邊就係一個「直」。拆碼嗰陣，左邊嘅亻做字首，佢喺鍵盤上面攞 O 呢個掣；跟住個字身用直取法，順住個樣由頭到尾攞頭、次、尾三碼——先攞頂上嘅十（J），再攞中間嘅⺼（B），最後攞底部嗰橫一（M），砌埋一齊就係 OJBM。點解字身要攞三碼呢？因為字首得一件亻，剩低嘅畫都歸字身，而字身最多可以攞頭、次、尾三碼，啱啱夠位擺晒十、⺼、一。記住喇：一個人（O）望住個「直」，由上而下數十、⺼、一，OJBM 就係「值」。

做.en: Today we learn 做, read zou6, the everyday word for to do, to make, or to act. Look at how it's built from two big parts: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, which sits on the O key; on the right is the character-body 故, which itself breaks into three pieces. That body 故 gives up its head 十 on the J key, then its next piece 口 on the R key, and finally its tail 攵 on the K key. That's why the split falls this way — the 字首 亻 takes one code, O, and the 字身 故 follows the usual head-second-tail rule to give J, R, K, so the full code is OJRK. Remember it like this: a person (亻) sets out to do something about a 故 story — person plus 故 makes 做, as in 叫做 (to be called), 做咗 (to have done), and 你做緊乜嘢？ (What are you doing?).
做.zh: 今日我哋學「做」呢個字，讀音係 zou6，即係做嘢、做事、做人嗰個「做」，好常用。你望下佢由兩大部分砌成：左邊係企人邊「亻」，喺鍵盤上面撳O；右邊其實係「故」呢個字身，佢自己又拆做三舊——起頭嘅「十」撳J，中間嘅「口」撳R，最後埋尾嘅「攵」撳K。所以個拆法係字首「亻」取一碼O，字身「故」照倉頡規矩取頭、取次、取尾三碼，即係J、R、K，合埋就係OJRK。你可以咁記：一個人（亻）用心去做番啲「故」事，人加故，就係「做」啦。你平時會聽到「叫做」zou6、「做咗」zou6 zo2，又或者有人問你「你做緊乜嘢？」，全部都用到呢個字。

傳.en: Today's character is 傳, read "cyun4," meaning to summon, propagate, or transmit — you'll see it in 傳統 (customs handed down through generations) and 傳播 (to broadcast news far and wide). Look at the shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right sits 專. In Cangjie the 字首 is 亻, which gives you O on the keyboard; then the 字身 專 must be broken down further, and here we take its head 十 (J) and its tail two pieces 戈 and 戈 (the lower part being 寸), each of which is I, so the full code is O, J, I, I. Why only three codes from the body? Because a 字身 takes at most head-first plus tail-two, and 專 breaks neatly into head 十 (J) and tail 戈 (I), 戈 (I) — exactly three. Remember it like this: a person (亻 O) takes a bundle sealed with a ten (十 J) and, with two spears (戈, 戈 — II), transmits it onward — that's 傳.
傳.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「傳」，讀「cyun4」，即係傳達、傳遞嘅意思，例如「傳統」就係一代一代傳落嚟嘅習俗，「傳播」就係將消息散開去。你望下呢個字，左邊係一個企人邊亻，右邊係「專」。倉頡入面，字首取亻，喺鍵盤度打O；跟住個字身「專」就要拆開嚟取碼，我哋取佢個頭「十」，喺鍵盤度係J，再取尾部嘅兩個部分「戈」同「戈」（其實下面係個「寸」），兩個都係I，所以成個字係O、J、I、I。點解字身淨係取三碼呢？因為字身最多取到頭一尾二，「專」個頭係十J，尾就係戈I、戈I，啱啱夠三個碼。你可以咁樣記：一個人（亻O）將一疊十J字包住嘅嘢，用兩支戈II傳出去，就係「傳」喇。

價.en: Today we learn 價, read gaa3, meaning price or value. Look at its structure: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is the component 賈. When we split it, the head is that leftmost 亻, which gives O. Then comes the body 賈, and because it has many strokes we take head-second-tail: the head is the top 一 giving M, the second piece is the middle 囗 giving W, and the tail is the bottom 金 giving C, so the whole code reads OMWC. Remember it this way: a person 亻 names a price, and reading 賈 from top to bottom you get M, W, C — and out comes the price tag.
價.zh: 今日我哋學「價」字，讀作 gaa3，即係價錢、價值嘅意思。你望下佢個結構：左邊係企人邊「亻」，右邊係「賈」呢個部件。分拆嗰陣，字首就係最左邊嘅「亻」，攞佢個碼 O。跟住輪到字身「賈」，因為佢筆畫多，就用頭、次、尾三碼——頭係頂部嘅「一」攞 M，次係中間嗰個「囗」攞 W，尾就係底下嘅「金」攞 C，所以成個碼砌埋係 OMWC。記住呢個口訣：一個人「亻」去出價，望住個「賈」字由上到下數 M、W、C，價錢就出嚟喇。

元.en: Today we meet 元, read jyun4, a character with many meanings — first, origin, head — but in Hong Kong you'll see it most often meaning dollar, as in 美元, the US dollar. Look at its shape: two flat strokes stacked on top, and a pair of legs 儿 underneath. This is a single-body character that can't be cleanly split into a left and a right, so we use the head-second-tail method: the top stroke 一 is M, the second stroke 一 is M again, and the tail piece 儿 at the bottom is U, giving you MMU. Remember it like this: two horizontal M's resting on the little 儿 legs U — that's the 元 of 元朗 (Yuen Long) and the 元 of 十元 (ten dollars).
元.zh: 今日我哋學「元」字，讀 jyun4，意思好多，可以係「第一」、「開始」、「本源」，喺香港最常見嘅就係「銀紙」嘅意思，好似「美元」咁。你睇下佢個樣，上面兩橫，下面一個「儿」腳。呢個係整體字，冇得清清楚楚咁一分為二，所以我哋用「取頭二尾」嘅方法：頭一橫「一」係 M，第二橫「一」又係 M，最後個尾就係下面嘅「儿」，打 U，合埋就係 MMU。記住個口訣：兩條橫線 M、M 頂住一對「儿」腳 U，「元朗」個元、「十元」個元，就係咁砌出嚟。

先.en: Today we learn 先, read sin1, meaning "first, former, before" — the same 先 you see in 先生, Mr. Look at it: it has a stacked shape that almost looks like a little standing figure, but Cangjie doesn't break it piece by piece here, because 先 is a 整體字, a whole-unit character, where we take only the head, second, third and tail and skip the middle. So the typing order is: the head stroke 丿 (H), then 土 (G), then another stroke 丿 (H), and finally 凵 (U), giving you HGHU. The reason we grab just these four corners and leap over the middle is exactly the 整體字 rule — no full decomposition, just the representative codes at the outer edges. Remember it as "stroke, earth, stroke, valley," and like the sentence 你行先啦, you go first — it'll stick!
先.zh: 今日我哋學「先」呢個字，讀作 sin1，意思係「首先、之前」，好似「先生」嘅「先」咁。你望住佢，係一個上下有啲似人企喺度嘅形，但係倉頡唔會逐部分咁拆，因為佢係一個整體字，我哋淨係取頭、二、三同尾嘅位，中間跳過。所以打字順序係：頭一撇 丿（H），第二個係 土（G），第三個又係一撇 丿（H），最尾係 凵（U），合埋就係 HGHU。之所以要跳過中間、只取四個角位，正正就係整體字嘅規矩——唔逐塊拆，只揀最外圍嘅代表碼。記住口訣「撇、土、撇、凵」，你行先啦，就記得晒喇！

光.en: Today's character is 光, read gwong1, meaning light, brightness, or brilliance — you'll see it in 陽光 joeng4 gwong1, sunlight, and 光輝 gwong1 fai1, radiance or glory. Look at how it's built: at the top sit three little sparks that form ⺌, typed with F; beneath them lies a single flat stroke, 一, typed with M; and right at the bottom is an upward-open trough, 凵, typed with U. Why only these three pieces? Because 光 is a whole-shape character with no clean head-and-body split, so Cangjie uses its special rule: take the first, the second, the third, and the very last, skipping whatever sits in the middle. That gives us the head ⺌ (F), the next piece 一 (M), and the final 凵 (U), leaving the middle out — the code FMU. Picture it: three sparks resting on a flat line, then skip straight down to the little cup at the bottom, and you've got 光, FMU.
光.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「光」，讀作 gwong1，意思係光線、明亮、光輝，例如「陽光」joeng4 gwong1 就係太陽嘅光，「光輝」gwong1 fai1 就係燦爛耀眼嘅意思。你望下呢個字嘅結構：上面有三粒細嘢好似三支火花，就係「⺌」，喺鍵盤上打 F；跟住下面橫住一畫，就係「一」，打 M；最後底部有個開口向上嘅「凵」，打 U。點解淨係取呢三件呢？因為「光」係一個整體字，唔可以清楚咁分字首字身，遇到呢種情況倉頡有一條特別規則：取頭、次、三，再加最尾，中間全部跳過——所以我哋就攞頭嘅「⺌」F、第二嘅「一」M、同最尾嘅「凵」U，中間嗰啲就唔理喇，砌成 FMU。記住呢個畫面：三點火花喺一橫之上，跳過中間，直落到底部個凹槽，就係「光」FMU。試下講「間房好光。」，就記得住喇。

克.en: Today we learn 克, read hak1 or haak1. It can mean to overcome, it works as the weight unit "gram," and it shows up a lot in transliterations of foreign names, like 星巴克 (sing1 baa1 hak1, Starbucks) and 烏克蘭 (wu1 hak1 laan4, Ukraine). Look at its shape: a 十 sits up top, a 口 below it, then a short slash and a little upward-opening box at the bottom. In Cangjie, 克 is a whole-character (整體字), meaning it doesn't break cleanly into a head part and a body part, so instead we use the head-second-third-last method, walking through it in stroke order to pick four codes: first the top 十 is J, next the 口 is R, then the third piece, the slash 丿, is H, and finally the closing box 凵 is U, giving JRHU. Remember it as "十, 口, slash, box" scanned top to bottom — like counting five grams of candy one piece at a time.
克.zh: 今日我哋學「克」呢個字，讀音係 hak1 或者 haak1，佢可以解「克服」嘅意思，又可以做重量單位「克」，仲成日用嚟音譯外國名，好似「星巴克」（sing1 baa1 hak1）同「烏克蘭」（wu1 hak1 laan4）咁。你望吓佢個樣：上面一個「十」，下面一個「口」，再落嚟係一撇同一個開口向上嘅框。喺倉頡入面，「克」係一個「整體字」，即係佢唔會清清楚楚拆成字首同字身兩橛，所以我哋改用「頭、二、三、尾」嘅方法，順住筆順揀出四粒碼：先取起首嘅十係 J，跟住第二個口係 R，再取第三筆嘅一撇丿係 H，最後取埋尾嗰個凵係 U，砌埋就係 JRHU。記住呢句：「十、口、撇、凵」由上到下順住掃落嚟，就好似五克糖一粒一粒數清楚咁。

免.en: Today's character is 免, read min5, meaning to spare, to excuse from, or to evade — as in 免費 min5 fai3, meaning free of charge, and 避免 bei6 min5, meaning to avert or avoid something. This is a whole character, one that can't be neatly split into a head and a body, so we follow the Cangjie rule for whole characters: take the head, the second, the third, then the tail. Look first for the 弓 shape, which sits on the N key and comes first; next the 日 shape on the A key as the second piece; then the 竹 shape on the H key as the third; and finally the 山 shape on the U key to close it off. Put together head to tail, the full code is NAHU, four pieces in order. Remember it with the phrase — admission is free, 免 — bow, sun, bamboo, mountain, one piece after another.
免.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「免」，讀作 min5，意思係免除、豁免或者避開，好似「免費」min5 fai3 意思係唔使畀錢，「避免」bei6 min5 就係設法唔畀件事發生。呢個字係一個整體字，冇明確嘅字首同字身可以拆開，所以我哋要跟足倉頡拆整體字嘅規矩：取頭、取二、取三，再加尾。你先睇個「弓」字形，佢喺 N 掣，係第一件；跟住個「日」形喺 A 掣，係第二件；再嚟個「竹」形喺 H 掣，係第三件；最後個「山」形喺 U 掣，係收尾一件。所以成個碼由頭到尾就係 NAHU，四件砌埋一齊。記住喇，入場免費㗎，「免」就係弓、日、竹、山，一件跟一件砌落去。

入.en: Today's character is 入, read jap6, meaning "to enter, come in, or join" — you'll see it in 入面 jap6 min6 (inside) and 加入 gaa1 jap6 (to join or participate). Look at its shape: it's like two simple strokes leaning together, and it splits into just two pieces. The first piece is the whole 入 form itself, typed with the O key, and the second is the single left-falling stroke 丿, typed with the H key, so the full code is OH. The reason it breaks this way is simple: 入 divides into 入 and 丿, taking the overall entering-shape as O for the first code and finishing with that leftover stroke H — exactly two codes, no more, no less. Here's your hook: one O and one H, like someone stepping in through a doorway — OH, come on in!
入.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「入」，讀做 jap6，意思係「進入、加入」，好似你講「入面」jap6 min6 指裏面，或者「加入」gaa1 jap6 指參加、加入。你望下呢個字，好似一撇一捺搭埋，形態好簡單。倉頡拆佢做兩個部件：頭嗰個係「入」呢個字形本身，撳 O 呢個掣，然後尾嗰個係一撇「丿」，撳 H 呢個掣，所以成個碼就係 OH。點解會咁拆呢？因為「入」拆入同丿兩碼，先取整體嘅入形攞第一碼 O，再攞埋剩低嗰筆撇 H 收尾，唔多唔少啱啱兩碼。記住喇：一個 O 帶住一撇 H，就好似有人一步「入」門口咁——OH，入嚟坐啦！

內.en: Today we learn 內, read noi6, meaning "inside" or "interior" — you meet it in words like 內容 noi6 jung4 (content) and 內部 noi6 bou6 (interior). Look at the shape: there's an open frame 冂 facing down, wrapping a 入 tucked inside it — literally the picture of something "entering the frame." In Cangjie, the frame 冂 is the head, and its own code is XB, so at the first position it gives O, which you type first; then the 入 inside is the body, and since a body takes only its last part, 入's own code OH ends in B, so you type B next, making the full code OB. Remember the picture: a frame O wrapping an 入 that ends in B — that's 內 tucked inside!
內.zh: 今日我哋學「內」呢個字，佢讀 noi6，即係「入面、裏面」嘅意思，好似「內容」noi6 jung4 同「內部」noi6 bou6 都用得到。你望吓佢個樣：外面係個開口向下嘅框「冂」，包住裏面一個「入」字，正正就係「入到框裏面」嘅畫面。喺倉頡入面，個框「冂」係字首，佢自己嘅碼係 XB，喺頭一個位攞到 O，所以你先撳 O；跟住入面嘅「入」係字身，佢自己嘅碼係 OH，因為係字身淨係攞尾，尾位就係 B，所以你再撳 B，全碼就係 OB。記住個畫面：一個框 O 包住一個入到尾嘅 B，「內」就係咁入嚟！

全.en: Today we learn 全, read cyun4, meaning to keep something whole, intact, or complete. Look at its shape: on top sits a little roof-like piece 𠆢, and underneath stands the character 王 (king). When we split it for typing, the prefix 𠆢 comes first — that downward pair of strokes is keyed as O. Then we move to the body 王, and because it's a self-contained block, we don't peel off every stroke; instead we take its head and its tail — the head is the top stroke 一, which is M, and the tail is the 土 shape at the bottom, which is G — giving the full code OMG. So remember: a little roof 𠆢 perched on top of the king 王 makes 全, and three taps, OMG, types it out — think of 完全 or 全球, the whole world made complete.
全.zh: 今日我哋學「全」字，讀作 cyun4，意思係完整、保全、成個都齊。你望吓佢個樣：上面係一個好似人字帽咁嘅「𠆢」，下面坐住一個「王」字。拆碼嘅時候，字首取「𠆢」呢一撇一捺，喺鍵盤上係 O；跟住去到字身「王」，因為佢係一個獨立嘅塊面，我哋唔會逐橫逐豎咁攞，而係取佢個頭同個尾——頭係一橫「一」，係 M，尾係下面嘅「土」，係 G，所以成個碼砌埋就係 OMG。記住喇，人字帽戴喺王頭上，就係「全」，OMG 三下就打得出！你可以諗埋「完全」、「全球」，成個世界都齊晒。

兩.en: Today's character is 兩, read loeng5, meaning "two" or "a pair," the word you use in 兩個 (two items) or when counting ounces. Look at its shape: an outer frame enclosing two pieces that look like 入, packed tightly together — because it's so compact, Cangjie treats it as a whole-character, so instead of splitting it into a head and a body, we just take the pieces in writing order from top down and outside in. That's why we pull the top stroke 一 first as M, then the vertical 丨 as L, then the ⺼ as B, and finally 入 as the tail O, giving you MLBO. Here's your hook: 兩 hides a pair of 入 inside its frame — two things together, read loeng5.
兩.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「兩」，讀作 loeng5，即係「二」、「一對」嘅意思，好似「兩個」、「一兩」咁樣用。你望下呢個字，佢框住兩個似「入」嘅部件，成個字結構緊密，喺倉頡入面當作一個「整體字」處理，唔會分做字首字身兩截，而係順住寫嘅次序連續拆開。所以我哋由上而下、由外到內咁攞碼：先攞最頂嗰橫「一」（M），跟住攞裏面嗰一豎「丨」（L），再攞「⺼」（B），最後收尾攞「入」（O），合埋就係 MLBO。記住喇：「兩」框入面藏住一對「入」，你就記得佢係兩件嘢一齊，讀 loeng5。

八.en: Today we learn the character 八, read baat3, which means the number eight and can also mean 'all around, all sides' — think of the eight points of the compass. Look at its shape: one stroke sweeping down to the left, one stroke sweeping down to the right, like two legs spread apart. 八 is a whole shape (整體字) with just two strokes, so in Cangjie we don't break it into any complicated split — we simply take the two pieces in writing order: the left downstroke as 竹 H, then the right downstroke as 人 O, giving the code HO. Because it has so few strokes and already forms one complete shape, there's no 字首 and 字身 to separate — you just pick H then O straight across, left to right. Remember it this way: two strokes fanning apart, 竹人 HO — like two legs stepping out to either side.
八.zh: 今日我哋學「八」呢個字，讀做 baat3，即係數目字八，亦都可以解「四面八方」嘅「八」，帶住周圍、各個方向嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，左邊一撇、右邊一捺，好似兩隻腳撇開咁企喺度。「八」係一個整體字，成個字得兩筆咁簡單，喺倉頡入面我哋唔使拆得咁複雜，直接由頭到尾取兩個碼——先取一撇當做竹字 H，再取一捺當做人字 O，所以個碼就係 HO。因為佢筆畫咁少，本身已經係一個完整嘅形，唔會再分字首字身，你順住個字由左寫到右揀 H、O 就得。記住喇：「八」字兩撇一分開，竹人 HO 就係佢，好似兩隻腳一撇一捺分向兩邊。

公.en: Today we learn 公, read gung1, a character rich in meaning — it can mean fair or equitable, it can mean public, and it even names the rank of a duke. Look at its shape: on top sits the 八 hat, two strokes spreading open like something being split apart, and beneath it sits a small 厶. In Cangjie this character breaks cleanly into two pieces from top to bottom, so the top 八 gives you C and the bottom 厶 gives you I, making the full code CI. Why only two codes? Because 公 is a whole character that divides plainly into an upper and a lower part, and each part simply hands over one letter, with nothing extra to add. Remember it this way: the 八 hat opens wide at C, the 厶 closes it off at I — that's the 公 in 公園 (park) and 公司!
公.zh: 我哋今日學「公」呢個字，讀音係 gung1，意思好豐富，可以指「公平」，又可以指「公眾」嘅公，甚至係爵位裏面嘅「公爵」。你留意佢個樣：上面係「八」字頭，兩撇打開好似分開嘅樣，下面係一個「厶」。喺倉頡入面呢個字要拆做兩橛，上面嘅「八」攞 C 鍵，下面嘅「厶」攞 I 鍵，所以全碼就係 CI。點解淨係得兩個碼？因為「公」係一個由上到下清清楚楚分成兩橛嘅字，每一橛各攞一個字母就夠，唔使補。記住：八字頭 C 開嘴，厶字底 I 收尾，「公園」「公司」都係佢！

六.en: Today's character is 六, read luk6, meaning the number six — you'll spot it everywhere, like in 星期六 (Saturday) or 六十 (sixty). Look at the shape: on top there's a little lid made of a horizontal stroke with a dot above it, and underneath sit two strokes spreading apart. That top piece is 亠, which lives on the Y key, and the bottom piece is 八, which you find on C. So 六 splits neatly into the head 亠 (Y) and the body 八 (C), giving you the full code YC — just two keys. Here's your memory hook: a hat 亠 (Y) on top, two feet 八 (C) below, and that's how you count out six.
六.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「六」，讀做 luk6，即係數字六，好似「星期六」sing1 kei4 luk6 、又或者「六十」luk6 sap6 呢啲你日日都見到嘅詞。你望住個字，上面有一橫加一點嘅蓋頭，下面有兩撇分開企喺度。上面呢個部件叫做「亠」，喺鍵盤上面撳 Y；下面兩撇係「八」，撳 C。所以「六」拆做字首亠（Y）、字身八（C），成個碼就係 YC，簡簡單單兩個掣。記住個小口訣：頭戴亠帽（Y），腳踏八字（C），數到六就係咁樣拼出嚟。

共.en: Today's character is 共, read gung6, meaning "together, total, to share" — you see it in words like 共同 gung6 tung4 (joint, common) and 公共 gung1 gung6 (public). Look at its shape: on top sits 廿, which you type with the T key, and underneath is 八, which you type with C — so the whole code is just two letters, TC. Why only two codes? Because 共 is a whole-form character (整體字), and instead of taking three or four pieces like an ordinary character, a whole-form takes only its head and its tail: head 廿 gives T, tail 八 gives C. Here's your memory hook: 廿 up top, 八 holding it up below, two shapes standing together — that's 共, TC.
共.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「共」，讀做 gung6，意思係「一齊、總共、共享」，好似「共同」gung6 tung4 同「公共」gung1 gung6 咁樣用。你望下佢個樣，上面係「廿」，喺鍵盤上面撳 T；下面係「八」，撳 C——所以個碼就係 TC 兩個字母。點解得兩碼咁少呢？因為「共」係一個整體字，唔使好似普通字咁拆頭尾三四碼，整體字嘅取碼規矩係取頭一碼、尾一碼，即係頭「廿」T、尾「八」C。記住呢個口訣：上面「廿」載住，下面「八」撐住，兩個人一齊「共」，咪就係 TC 囉！

其.en: Today we learn 其, read kei4, which in written Chinese means "his, her, its, their" or "that" — you see it in 其他 kei4 taa1, meaning the rest or everyone else, and 其實 kei4 sat6, meaning "actually" or "in fact." Look at its shape: on top sits 廿, then two flat strokes 一 and 一 in the middle, and a pair of legs 八 resting underneath, all neatly stacked and symmetrical. This is a whole-shape character (整體字), meaning it can't be cleanly divided into a head part and a body part, so Cangjie uses its special rule for such characters: take the first, second, third, and last pieces. Reading top to bottom, that gives us 廿 which is T, then the second stroke 一 which is M, the third stroke 一 which is M again, and finally the bottom 八 which is C — spelling out TMMC. Just remember the top-to-bottom order 廿一一八, layer by layer, and you'll never scramble it.
其.zh: 我哋今日學「其」呢個字，佢讀作 kei4，喺書面語入面即係「佢嘅」、「嗰個」嘅意思，例如「其他」kei4 taa1 就係指其餘嘅人或物，「其實」kei4 sat6 就係「事實上」。你望吓佢個樣：上面係個「廿」，中間有兩橫「一」「一」，下面墊住個「八」字腳，成個字結構企理對稱。呢個字係一個整體字，即係話冇得清楚拆成字首同字身兩橛，遇到呢種情況，倉頡嘅規則就係取頭、二、三、尾四碼——所以我哋順住由上到下攞：頭嗰個「廿」係 T，跟住第二筆「一」係 M，第三筆「一」又係 M，最後個尾「八」係 C，砌埋一齊就係 TMMC。你記住「廿一一八」呢個由上落下嘅次序，好似逐層搭落去咁，就唔會撈亂喇。

具.en: Today we learn 具, read geoi6, meaning a tool or implement, as in 工具 gung1 geoi6 (tool) and 具有 geoi6 jau5 (to possess). Look at the shape: on top there's a form like ⺼, two horizontal strokes sit in the middle, and at the bottom it closes with 八, the two little legs. This is a whole-character, meaning it doesn't cleanly break into a head and a body, so we follow Cangjie's head-second-third-last rule: take the head ⺼ which is B, then the second stroke 一 as M, the third stroke 一 as M, and finally the closing 八 as C, skipping whatever sits in the middle. That gives you BMMC — just remember '⺼ holding two bars, with 八 as the feet' and it'll stick.
具.zh: 今日我哋學「具」呢個字，讀做 geoi6，意思係工具、器具，好似「工具」gung1 geoi6 同「具有」geoi6 jau5 咁樣用。你望住個字，上面好似個「⺼」字形，中間有橫畫，下面收尾係「八」字兩點。呢個係整體字，即係話唔會拆成清清楚楚嘅字首字身，我哋要跟倉頡「頭、二、三、尾」嘅取碼法：先攞頭一個⺼，就係 B；跟住攞第二劃一 M、第三劃一 M；最後攞尾嘅八 C，中間嗰啲就直接跳過唔理，所以成個碼係 BMMC。記住呢個口訣——「⺼載住兩橫，八字腳收尾」，你就唔會撈亂啦。

冇.en: Today we're learning the character 冇, read mou5, one of the most common words in spoken Cantonese, meaning "to not have" — it's the direct opposite of 有 ("to have"). Take a good look at its shape: it's like 有 with its two inner horizontal strokes emptied out, which fits its meaning nicely — there's simply nothing inside. When we break it down for typing, 冇 has only two parts: the head is the slanted-plus-horizontal 「ナ」 on the K key, and the tail is the enclosing 「冂」 on the B key, giving us the full code KB. Because the whole character is made of just these two pieces, we follow the writing order and take the head 「ナ」 then the tail 「冂」 — no further splitting needed, clean and simple. Remember it this way: 冇 is K plus B, a stroke dropping into an empty frame with nothing inside, just like when you say 我冇錢喇 — "I have no money."
冇.zh: 今日我哋學嘅呢個字係「冇」，讀作 mou5，係我哋廣東話最常用嘅字之一，解「無」、「沒有」嘅意思，同「有」啱啱相反。你望吓佢個樣，其實好似「有」少咗中間兩橫，變成空咗兩橫，好切合佢「乜都冇」嘅意思。拆碼嘅時候，「冇」只有兩個部分：字首係上面嘅一撇一橫「ナ」，喺 K 掣，字尾係下面包住嘅「冂」，喺 B 掣，所以全碼就係 KB。因為成個字只得兩件，我哋順住寫嘅次序取頭「ナ」、取尾「冂」，唔使再拆多啲，簡單直接。記住喇：「冇」就係 K 加 B，一撇一橫落個空框，框裏面乜都冇，好似你講「我冇錢喇」咁樣。

再.en: Today's character is 再, read zoi3, meaning "again" or "once more" — you'll meet it in words like 再見 (goodbye, see you again) and 再次 (once more). Look at how it's packed together in tight layers: there's no clean way to slice it into a separate head and body, so 再 counts as a whole-character. For whole-characters Cantonese Cangjie has a special rule — you skip the middle and take only three parts: head, second, and tail. So you grab the top stroke 一, which is M; then the middle horizontal-and-vertical shape 土, which is G; and finally the outer frame 冂 wrapping the bottom, which is B, letting the inner details in the middle drop away. Put those three together and you get MGB. Remember it as "top one M, body 土 G, frame B, and jump over the rest" — and you'll never have to say goodbye to this code.
再.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「再」，讀作 zoi3，即係「再一次」、「重複」嘅意思，好似「再見」、「再次」咁。你望住個字，佢層層疊埋一齊，好難清清楚楚咁劃開頭同身，所以佢係一個「整體字」。遇到整體字，倉頡有一條特別規矩：唔理中間，淨係取頭、次、尾三個部分。你先攞最頂嗰橫「一」，係 M；跟住攞中間嗰橫連豎砌成嘅「土」，係 G；最後攞包住下邊嗰個「冂」框，係 B，中間嘅細節就跳過，唔取。所以三碼合埋就係 MGB。記住呢個「跳過中間」嘅口訣：頭一 M、身土 G、尾框 B，再見就唔使煩喇。

冰.en: Today we meet 冰, read bing1 in Cantonese, meaning ice or ice-cold. Look at its shape: on the left sits 冫, the two-drop water radical, and on the right sits the full 水 for water — freeze the water and you get ice, an easy image to hold. When Cangjie breaks it apart, 冫 acts as the head and is small, so it takes just one code, I; then 水 acts as the body, and because a body is allowed more than one code, we take its first-and-last: 一 first (M), then 水 itself (E). Put together that gives you IME, head then body, in clean order. Remember it like this: two drops (I) plus a stroke (M) plus water (E) — ice is simply water frozen solid.
冰.zh: 今日我哋學「冰」呢個字，粵音讀 bing1，即係冰塊、凍冰冰嗰個意思。你望吓佢個結構：左邊係「冫」（兩點水），右邊係「水」字，一凍一水，好易記。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，「冫」做字首，佢只係得個小小嘅形，取碼 I；跟住「水」做字身，因為字身容許取多過一碼，所以要取佢個頭一同尾一，即係先取「一」（M），再取「水」本身（E）。合埋一齊就係 IME，順序頭尾清清楚楚。記住個口訣：兩點水（I）加一（M）加水（E），冰就係凍到結晶嘅水啦！

出.en: Today we're learning the character 出, which reads ceot1 and means to go out or to come out — as in 出街 (go out on the street) or 出現 (to appear). Look at the shape: it looks like two 凵 forms stacked one on top of the other, growing upward. In Cangjie, 出 is treated as an integral character (整體字), so instead of breaking it into many messy pieces, we simply take the head and the tail: first the top 凵, pressed as U, then the bottom 屮, also pressed as U, giving us the full code UU. Because it's an integral character, we skip whatever is in the middle and grab only those two endpoints — no need to overthink it. Memory hook: 出 is just two U's stacked up, so tap U twice and out it comes!
出.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「出」，讀音係 ceot1，意思係出去、出嚟，好似「出街」、「出現」噉。你望下呢個字，佢好似兩個「凵」形疊埋一齊，上下咁重疊起嚟。倉頡入面，「出」屬於整體字，即係話佢唔會拆到好散，我哋只需要取頭尾兩碼：先取上面嗰個「凵」，撳 U 掣，再取下面嗰個「屮」形，又係撳 U 掣，所以成個字就係 UU 兩碼。因為佢係整體字，我哋跳過中間嘅部分，淨係捉頭尾兩件，唔使諗太多。記住呢個口訣：「出」就係兩粒 U 疊起，撳兩下 U 就出到嚟！

分.en: Today's character is 分, read "fan1" or "fan6", meaning to divide or split, and it can also name a small unit of time, like a minute. Look at the shape: on top sits 八, two strokes fanning outward as if separating, and below it sits 刀, a knife — the whole picture is literally something being cut apart. When Cangjie breaks this down, the top 八 is the 字首 and gives C, while the bottom 刀 is the 字身; since the knife shape 刀 is written out as 尸 then 竹, you take 尸 = S and 竹 = H, giving the full code CSH. Here's your memory hook: the two strokes on top fan apart as 八 (C), and the knife slicing down below is 尸 (S) and 竹 (H) — one clean cut makes 分. Try it with 部分 (bou6 fan6, a part) and 分析 (fan1 sik1, to analyze), as in the sentence "We sit separately."
分.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「分」，讀「fan1」或者「fan6」，意思係「分開」、「分割」，又可以指時間嘅細單位，好似一分鐘咁。你望下呢個字，上面係一個「八」字，好似兩撇向外分開咁樣，落到下面係一把「刀」，一分為二，字形本身就已經講緊「分開」嘅意思。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，上面嘅「八」做字首，取碼C；下面嘅「刀」做字身，因為刀呢個部件嘅完整碼係「尸竹」，所以取「尸」S同「竹」H，合埋成為CSH。記住喇：上面兩撇分開係八C，下面一把刀切落去就係尸S竹H，一刀切開就係「分」。你可以諗下「部分」（bou6 fan6）同埋「分析」（fan1 sik1），造句嘅話就係「我哋分開坐。」

列.en: Today we meet 列, read lit6, which in a word like 系列 means a line or a whole series, and can mean to arrange in order or to classify. Look at how it splits into two sides: on the left is 歹, and on the right is 刂. In Cangjie, 歹 is the prefix (字首), and a prefix can only give up its first and last codes, so from 歹 we take the head 一 (M) and the tail 弓 (N); then 刂 is the body (字身), which gives 中 (L) and 弓 (N), so the whole code lines up as MNLN. Here's your memory hook: the left 歹 prefix hands over 一弓, the right 刂 body hands over 中弓, and just like people who 排成一列 — line up in a row — M-N-L-N follow one after another in order.
列.zh: 今日我哋學「列」呢個字，讀 lit6，喺「系列」入面就係一行、一連串嘅意思，可以解作排列、分類。你望吓佢分做兩邊：左邊係「歹」，右邊係「刂」。倉頡拆字嗰陣，「歹」做字首，字首只可以攞頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋喺「歹」度取頭嘅一（M）同尾嘅弓（N）；跟住「刂」做字身，字身攞中（L）同弓（N），連埋就係一弓中弓——MNLN。記住個口訣：左邊歹字首「一弓」，右邊刂字身「中弓」，你排隊嗰陣一個跟一個「排成一列」，M-N-L-N都係咁順住嚟。

初.en: Today we're learning 初, read co1, meaning "beginning" or "initial," as in 最初 (zeoi3 co1, "at first") and 初期 (co1 kei4, "primary phase"). Look at how it splits into two parts: on the left is 衤, and on the right is 刀 with a little stroke. That left-side 衤 is the head, and a head takes just one code, which is L; the 刀 on the right together with the stroke is the body, and a body takes first-last, so 刀 gives S as the first and the falling stroke 丿 gives H as the last, making LSH. Remember the rule that the head takes one code while the body takes first-last, and you'll see exactly why it's one L plus the two codes S and H. Memory hook: the cloth radical takes up a 刀 (knife) — that first cut is the very beginning!
初.zh: 我哋今日學「初」呢個字，讀做 co1，意思係「開始、最初」，好似「最初」（zeoi3 co1）同「初期」（co1 kei4）咁樣。你望下佢分兩橛：左邊係「衤」，右邊係「刀」加一撇。左邊嘅「衤」係字首，只取一碼，就係 L；右邊嘅「刀」連埋嗰撇係字身，字身要取頭尾兩碼——「刀」本身取 S 做頭，最後嗰撇「丿」取 H 做尾，所以合埋就係 LSH。記住字首得一碼、字身取頭尾嘅規矩，你就明點解係 L 一碼、S 同 H 兩碼咁分。記憶鉤：衣字旁一「刀」下去，就係「初」次動手嘅開始！
