別.en: Today we learn 別, read bit6, meaning to separate or other, and also do not — you'll meet it in 特別 dak6 bit6 (special) and 分別 fan1 bit6 (to distinguish). Look at its shape: on the left is 另, and on the right stands a knife 刂 — a knife cutting things apart, which fits the idea of separating so nicely. The character splits into two halves: 另 is the 字首 (lead) and 刂 is the 字身 (body), and each half is coded first-last. From 另 we take its first and last pieces — 口 which is R, then 尸 which is S; then from 刂 we take its first and last — 中 which is L, then 弓 which is N, giving the full code RSLN. Remember it as: a mouth 口 R, a corpse 尸 S, and a knife's 中 L and 弓 N — cut apart, and you get 別.
別.zh: 今日我哋學「別」呢個字,讀作 bit6,意思係「分開」、「另外」,又可以解「唔好」,好似「特別」dak6 bit6 同「分別」fan1 bit6 咁。你睇下佢個樣,左邊係「另」,右邊係一把刀「刂」,分開嗰把刀,難怪就有「分別」嘅意思。呢個字拆做兩橛:左邊「另」係字首,右邊「刂」係字身,兩橛都用頭尾法嚟拆。「另」個字首取頭尾——頭係「口」R,尾係「尸」S;跟住「刂」個字身都取頭尾——頭係「中」L,尾係「弓」N,所以成個碼就係 RSLN。記住啦:一個口 R、一個尸 S、加把刀嘅中 L 同弓 N,分開分開就係「別」。

利.en: Today we learn 利, read lei6, meaning gain, advantage or profit — you'll see it in 意大利 (ji3 daai6 lei6, Italy), and it also describes a knife being sharp. Look at 利: it's built from two side-by-side parts, 禾 on the left and 刂 on the right. Its full code is HDLN, and we split it into a head and a body. The head is the left-hand 禾, and since a head takes its first and last shapes, it gives ⺾ H at the top and 木 D at the bottom; the body is the right-hand 刂, which also takes first and last, giving 衤 L and 亅 N. The split falls this way because each side can supply at most two codes, so 禾 contributes H, D and 刂 contributes L, N, together making the four-code HDLN. Remember it like this: a stalk of grain with a knife beside it — grain brings profit, and the blade stays sharp.
利.zh: 我哋今日學「利」，讀作 lei6，意思係利益、好處，例如「意大利」（ji3 daai6 lei6，即係 Italy），又或者形容一把刀好鋒利。你望住「利」，佢係左右兩邊拼埋一齊：左邊係「禾」，右邊係「刂」。呢個字全碼係 HDLN，我哋分開字首同字身嚟拆——字首係左邊嘅「禾」，取頭尾兩碼，即係頂上面嘅「⺾」H，同埋尾嘅「木」D；字身係右邊嘅「刂」，都係取頭尾，得到「衤」L 同「亅」N。點解係咁分呢？因為字首同字身每邊都最多取兩碼，「禾」取H、D，「刂」取L、N，啱啱兩邊各兩碼合成四碼 HDLN。記住呢個口訣：一棵禾，旁邊擺把刀，禾生利益，刀就鋒利。

到.en: Today we learn 到, read "dou2" or "dou3", meaning to arrive or to reach a place — as in 見到 (gin3 dou2), to see, or 令到 (ling6 dou3), to cause someone to do something. Look at the character: on the left sits 至, and on the right stands 刂, the standing-knife radical, and we pull the code out piece by piece. The left 至 is the head, and Cangjie takes only its first and last shapes here — the horizontal 一 (M) and 土 (G); then the right 刂 is the body, giving 中 (L) and 弓 (N), so the whole code comes out as MGLN. The split falls this way because head and body each have their quota: 至 as the head keeps just its first and last strokes, and 刂 as the body supplies the final two codes, filling out four neatly. Remember it like this: 一土 from 至, then 中弓 from 刂 — and you've arrived home!
到.zh: 今日我哋學「到」呢個字，讀「dou2」或者「dou3」，意思係到達、去到某個地方，好似「見到」（gin3 dou2）就係睇見咗，「令到」（ling6 dou3）就係搞到、使到咁。你望下個字，左邊係「至」，右邊係「刂」（企刀邊），拆碼嘅時候就要一部份一部份咁攞出嚟。左邊嘅「至」係字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，頭係一橫「一」（M），尾係「土」（G）；右邊嘅「刂」係字身，取「中」（L）同埋「弓」（N），所以全碼砌埋就係 MGLN。點解係咁分呢？因為字首字身各自有配額，「至」做字首只攞頭尾，「刂」做字身補返後面兩碼，啱啱夠四碼。記住個口訣：一土（至）加中弓（刂），返到屋企喇！

制.en: Today we learn 制, read zai3, which means system, to establish, or to overpower — you'll see it in words like 控制 (hung3 zai3, to control) and 制度 (zai3 dou6, a system or institution). Look at the character and you'll notice it's built left-and-right: on the left, 牛 and 冂 are stacked together, and on the right stands the knife 刂. The left cluster is the 字首, and from it we take just the head and tail — the head is 竹 (H) and the tail is 月 (B), so the 字首 gives us HB. The right-hand 刂 is the 字身, and its own code is 中 (L) plus 弓 (N), that is LN. Join the 字首 and 字身 and you get HBLN. Remember it this way: the left 牛-冂 gives head-and-tail HB, the right knife gives LN, so 制 is HBLN.
制.zh: 今日我哋學「制」呢個字，讀作 zai3，佢有制度、建立、控制嘅意思，好似「控制」（hung3 zai3）同「制度」（zai3 dou6）咁樣。你望住個字，會見到佢係左右兩邊砌成嘅：左邊係牛同冂疊埋一齊，右邊係把刀「刂」。左邊呢一嚿係字首，我哋取佢嘅頭同尾——頭係竹（H），尾係月（B），所以字首就係 HB。右邊嘅「刂」係字身，佢自己嘅碼係中（L）加弓（N），即係 LN。將字首字身接埋，就砌成 HBLN 喇。記住呢個口訣：左邊牛冂取頭尾（HB），右邊一把刀 LN，制字就係 HBLN。

則.en: Today we learn 則, read zak1, meaning a rule or a principle — you'll meet it in words like 規則 kwai1 zak1 (regulation) and 原則 jyun4 zak1 (principle). Look at the shape: it splits into a left part 貝 and a right part 刂. In Cangjie, 貝 acts as the head, and instead of taking every stroke we take its first and last codes, giving 月 B and 金 C; the right-hand 刂 is the body, giving 中 L and 弓 N, so the full code is BCLN. The split falls this way because a left-right character lets the head and the body each take their own codes by the usual rules — 貝 yields 月金, 刂 yields 中弓, cleanly separated. Remember it like this: 貝 becomes 月金, 刂 becomes 中弓, and 則 is built.
則.zh: 今日我哋學「則」呢個字，讀做 zak1，意思係規則、法則，好似「規則」kwai1 zak1 同「原則」jyun4 zak1 都用到佢。你望住個字，佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係「貝」，右邊係「刂」。倉頡拆字，「貝」做字首，唔會逐筆咁攞，而係攞頭同尾兩碼，就係「月」B 同「金」C；右邊個「刂」做字身，攞「中」L 同「弓」N，合埋就係 BCLN。點解咁拆？因為左右結構嘅字，字首同字身各自照規矩取碼，貝取頭尾成月金，刂取中弓，唔會混埋一齊。記住喇：貝變月金，刂變中弓，一個「則」就砌好。

前.en: Today we learn 前, read cin4, meaning "in front" or "forward" — the same 前 you see in 以前 (formerly) and 之前 (before). Notice the two little strokes 丷 sitting on top: that's the head of the character, and you type it with T. The rest of the character is the body, and here we follow the head/second/tail rule — take the first piece ⺼ as B, then the second piece 衤 as L, and finally the tail, the little hook 亅, as N, giving you TBLN. Remember it like this: the two dots T lead the way, then B, L, N step forward one by one, just like the sentence 你行前少少 — walk a little forward!
前.zh: 今日我哋學「前」呢個字，讀做 cin4，即係「前面」、「向前」嘅意思，好似「以前」、「之前」咁樣講。你留意個字上面有兩點「丷」，我哋叫佢做字首，喺鍵盤上面撳 T。跟住落嚟就係字身部分，我哋按照「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼規矩，先攞第一個部件「⺼」係 B，再攞第二個「衤」係 L，最後攞尾嘅一鈎「亅」係 N，所以成個字砌埋就係 TBLN。記住喇：上面兩點 T 起頭，之後 B、L、N 一步步向前行，就好似個字叫你「行前少少」咁！

創.en: Today we learn 創, read cong3, meaning to establish or create, and it originally carries the sense of a knife cutting. Look at it: on the left sits 倉 (a granary), and on the right stands an upright knife, the 刂 shape. Cangjie takes the left as the head and the right as the body, but for a busy head like 倉 we don't spell the whole thing — we take only its outer top and bottom, which are 人 (O) and 口 (R); then the body 刂 gives 中 (L) and 弓 (N), so the full code is ORLN. The reason it splits so neatly into two plus two is that a complex head like this is capped at its first two codes, letting you skip the crowded middle, so 人口 is all you need up front. Remember it like this: a granary (人口) sliced open by a knife (中弓) is where something new gets created.
創.zh: 今日我哋學「創」呢個字，讀做 cong3，意思係開創、創造，本身重同刀切有關。你望下佢：左邊係一個「倉」，右邊係一把企起身嘅刀，即係「刂」。倉頡拆字係左邊做字首、右邊做字身，字首嘅「倉」我哋唔會全部拆晒，淨係取佢頭尾兩個外形，即係上面嘅人（O）同埋下面嘅口（R）；跟住字身嘅「刂」就取中（L）同弓（N），砌埋一齊就係 ORLN。點解字首得兩碼、字身得兩碼咁齊整呢？因為「倉」呢啲比較複雜嘅字首，倉頡最多只取頭兩個碼，將中間慳走，所以你只需記住人口就夠。你可以咁記：一間倉（人口），畀把刀（中弓）劃開，就開創咗新嘅嘢喇。

劃.en: Today we learn 劃, read waak6, meaning to divide, to mark off, or to lay down a boundary — think of drawing a dividing line. Look at it: it's a left-right character, with 畫 on the left and the standing-knife 刂 on the right. When Cangjie breaks it apart, the left head-part 畫 is a busy shape, so we take only its first and last codes: the head is 中 L and the tail is 一 M, giving LM; then the body 刂 on the right contributes two codes, its 中 L and its 弓 N. Type them in order and you get 中 L, 一 M, 中 L, 弓 N — LMLN. You'll meet this word in 計劃 and 規劃, as in "we need to plan the next step," so here's your hook: 畫's head-and-tail LM, then the knife's L-and-N, and 劃 is done.
劃.zh: 今日我哋學「劃」呢個字，讀做 waak6，意思係劃分、界定範圍，好似劃界綫、劃分地方咁。你望下佢，係一個左右結構嘅字，左邊係「畫」，右邊係企刀「刂」。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「畫」筆畫多，我哋淨係取頭尾兩碼：頭係中 L，尾係一 M，砌成 LM；跟住輪到右邊嘅字身「刂」，佢取中間同尾嘅兩碼，就係中 L 同弓 N。所以成個字順住打落去係中 L、一 M、中 L、弓 N，即係 LMLN。呢個字實用得好，例如「計劃」同「規劃」都會用到，好似「我哋要計劃下一步」咁講。記住個口訣：畫嘅頭尾配埋刀嘅中弓，LM 加 LN，就係劃嘞。

力.en: Today we learn the character 力, read lik6, which means power, capability, or influence — you see it in words like 能力 (nang4 lik6, ability) and 努力 (nou5 lik6, diligent). Look at 力: it's a whole-form character, meaning it doesn't break cleanly into a head part and a body part — it's one complete shape. Because it's a whole-form character, Cangjie's rule is to take just the head and the tail: the head is 大 on the K key, and the tail is 匚 on the S key, giving you the code KS. Remember it this way: to use force you plant yourself firmly like 大 (K) and then push with a bent arm like 匚 (S) — head and tail together make 力.
力.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「力」字，讀做 lik6，即係力量、能力、影響力嘅意思，好似「能力」（nang4 lik6）同「努力」（nou5 lik6）都用到佢。你望住「力」呢個字，佢係一個整體字——即係話佢冇明顯咁分開嘅字首同字身，係一個完整嘅形狀。因為係整體字，倉頡嘅取碼規則就係取頭同取尾兩個碼：頭係「大」，喺 K 鍵；尾係「匚」，喺 S 鍵，所以個碼就係 KS。你可以咁樣記：使力嘅時候要一大（K）扎穩，再屈起手臂（匚，S）發勁，一頭一尾就成個「力」字喇。

功.en: Today we learn 功, read gung1, meaning achievement, merit, or a good result — you see it in 成功 sing4 gung1, to succeed, and 功能 gung1 nang4, function or capability. Look at how it's built from two parts: on the left is 工, and on the right is 力. In Cangjie the head part takes at most two codes, so from the head 工 we take only its first and last shapes — 一 (M) at the top and 大 (K) at the bottom; then the body 力 gives its representative shape 尸 (S), making the full code M, K, S. Remember it this way: put in the effort (力, keyed as 尸/S) and you earn the merit that is 功.
功.zh: 今日我哋學「功」呢個字，讀作 gung1，意思係功勞、成就、好嘅成果，好似「成功」sing4 gung1 就係做成件事，「功能」gung1 nang4 就係一樣嘢做到嘅本領。你睇下佢由兩部分砌成：左邊係「工」，右邊係「力」。倉頡有個規矩，字首最多取兩碼，所以「工」呢個字首只取頭尾兩形——頭係「一」（M），尾係「大」（K）；至於字身「力」，就取佢個代表碼「尸」（S），所以成個字打 M、K、S。記住呢個口訣：出得力（尸／S），先至有功。

加.en: Today we learn 加, read gaa1, meaning to add to or to increase — the very same 加 in the sentence "one plus one equals two." Look at the shape: it splits cleanly into a left side and a right side, with 力 on the left and 口 on the right. In Cangjie the left 力 is the 字首, the leading part, so it gives us just one code, K; the right side is the 字身, the body, and it's built from two written pieces, 尸 and 口, which we take in writing order as S then R. Put them together and the full code is KSR. Here's your hook: on the left you put in some 力 (effort, K), and on the right a 尸 lies over a 口 (S, R) — effort added on!
加.zh: 我哋今日學「加」字，佢讀作 gaa1，意思係增添、加多，就好似「一加一等於二」入面嘅「加」咁。你望下呢個字，佢係左右兩邊分開嘅：左邊係「力」，右邊係「口」，中間仲夾住一劃。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊嘅「力」係字首，我哋淨係取佢一個碼，就係 K；右邊嗰嚿嘢係字身，佢由「尸」同「口」兩個部件砌成，所以順住寫落去取 S 同 R，合埋一齊就係 KSR。記住喇：左邊出力（K），右邊有個尸躺住張口（S、R），出力去加多啲！

助.en: Today we learn 助, read zo6, meaning to help, aid, or assist — you'll see it in words like 幫助 (assistance) and 資助 (to subsidize). Look at how it's built: on the left is 且, and on the right is 力, two pieces side by side. In Cangjie the left becomes the 字首 and the right becomes the 字身, and each side takes only its head and tail. From the 字首 且 we take head-tail: the head 月 keyed B and the tail 一 keyed M; from the 字身 力 we take head-tail: the head 大 keyed K and the tail 尸 keyed S, giving the full code BMKS. Memory hook: two pieces, each head and tail — 且 gives you 月一, 力 gives you 大尸, and you're done.
助.zh: 今日我哋學「助」呢個字，讀音係 zo6，意思係幫忙、援助，好似「幫助」同「資助」咁樣。你睇吓佢係左右兩件砌埋一齊：左邊係「且」，右邊係「力」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊做字首，右邊做字身，各自都取頭尾兩碼。字首「且」取頭尾——頭係「月」，鍵係 B，尾係「一」，鍵係 M；字身「力」都取頭尾——頭係「大」，鍵係 K，尾係「尸」，鍵係 S，所以全碼就係 BMKS。記住嘅方法係：兩件字，各取頭尾，左邊「且」變 月一，右邊「力」變 大尸，一手就搞掂。

動.en: Today's character is 動, read dung6, meaning to move or to happen, and as a noun it means movement or action — you'll see it in 動物 dung6 mat6 (animal) and 活動 wut6 dung6 (an event). Look at its shape: on the left sits 重, on the right sits 力, so this is a left–right character. In Cangjie the left 重 becomes the 字首, and a 字首 never gives all its strokes — it hands over only its head and its tail, which here are 竹 (H) and 土 (G); the right 力 becomes the 字身 and offers 大 (K) and 尸 (S). Put them together in order and you get HGKS. Memory hook: the heavy left gives head-竹 and tail-土, the strong right gives 大 and 尸, and 動 springs into action.
動.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「動」，讀做 dung6，意思係郁動、發生，又或者當名詞用嘅時候解「動作、活動」，好似「動物」dung6 mat6 同「活動」wut6 dung6 咁。你望吓佢，左邊係個「重」字，右邊係個「力」字，係一個左右分開嘅結構。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊「重」做字首，但字首唔會逐筆全取，只取頭同尾——頭係「竹」（H），尾係「土」（G 之後嘅那個，其實 G 就係「土」），所以字首取到「竹」H 同「土」G；右邊「力」做字身，取埋「大」K 同「尸」S。連埋一齊，全碼就係 HGKS。記住個口訣：左重取頭竹尾土，右力得大尸，一「動」就到手。

務.en: Today we learn 務, read mou6, meaning affairs, business, or a duty you must attend to — you'll meet it in 服務 (fuk6 mou6, to serve, service) and 任務 (jam6 mou6, a mission or assignment given to you). Look at the character: the left side is 矛 and the right side is the part built with 攵, so Cangjie splits it left-to-right into 字首 and 字身. The 字首 矛 gives only its head and tail — 弓 (N) and 竹 (H) — because a leading part is capped at two codes; then the 字身 gives its head 人 (O), a second piece 大 (K), and its tail 尸 (S), so the full code is NHOKS. That's the head-second-tail pattern a body part is allowed. Remember it as: draw the spear first (弓竹), then walk through 人, 大, 尸 — and think of the man who works hard at his duties.
務.zh: 今日我哋學「務」呢個字，讀作 mou6，意思係事務、任務，好似「服務」（fuk6 mou6，即係服侍人）同「任務」（jam6 mou6，即係派畀你要完成嘅工作）咁。你睇下呢個字，左邊係個「矛」，右邊係「攵」加落嚟嘅部分，倉頡就係跟住呢個左右結構嚟拆。字首「矛」淨係攞頭尾兩碼，即係頭一個「弓」（N）同尾一個「竹」（H）；到咗字身，就攞頭「人」（O）、第二個「大」（K）同埋尾「尸」（S），合埋就係 NHOKS。點解要咁樣拆？因為字首一律最多攞兩碼，所以「矛」得 NH 兩碼；跟住字身可以攞到三碼，頭、二、尾各攞一個。記住喇：先寫個矛（弓竹），再由人行到大再到尸，「佢好努力做事務」就係咁勤力做嘢㗎喇。

勝.en: Today's character is 「勝」, read 'sing3', meaning victory or to excel over someone — you see it in 「勝利」 sing3 lei6, meaning victory, and even in 「必勝客」 bit1 sing3 haak3, which is Pizza Hut. This character splits left and right: the left side is 「⺼」 (the flesh radical), coded B, and it acts as the 字首, the leading part. Because a 字首 only takes a single code, the left side gives us just that one B. The right side is the 字身, the body, which can supply up to three codes, so we take head, second, and tail — head is 「火」 F, second is 「手」 Q, and the tail is 「匚」 S. Put together you get BFQS; remember it as 'flesh on the left, fire and hand tucked together on the right, and you've got victory,' just like saying 「我哋今場勝咗喇。」 — we won this match!
勝.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「勝」，讀「sing3」，即係勝利、勝過人嘅意思，你睇「勝利」sing3 lei6 就係贏嘅意思，連「必勝客」bit1 sing3 haak3 都用到佢。呢個字左右兩邊分，左邊係「⺼」（肉字旁），倉頡碼係 B，佢做字首；因為做字首嘅時候淨係要一碼，所以左邊就淨係取 B 一個碼。右邊嗰大嚿就係字身，字身可以取到三碼，我哋分別攞頭、二、尾——頭係「火」F，第二個係「手」Q，最尾就係「匚」S。合埋一齊就係 BFQS，你可以記住「肉字旁邊，火手圍埋一齊，就係勝利」。就好似講「我哋今場勝咗喇。」，贏咗場波，開心！

勞.en: Today we learn 勞, read lou4, meaning labor or toil — the hard-working kind of effort, like the 勞 in 麥當勞 (McDonald's) or in 勞工, laborers. Look at its shape: across the top sit two identical fire pieces, 火 and 火, then a flat cover 冖 stretched beneath them, and at the very bottom stands 力, strength. When we split it, the 字首 top takes the two fires, F and F, plus that cover 冖 as B; the leftover 字身 is the lower 力, which gives its first and last codes, K and S — so the whole thing types as FFBKS. The split falls here because Cangjie first separates the character top from bottom, gathering the fires and the cover into the head while 力 stands alone as the body. Remember it this way: two fires burning above hard-working strength — that is the toil of 勞.
勞.zh: 今日我哋學「勞」呢個字，讀做 lou4，意思係勞動、辛苦做嘢，好似麥當勞嘅「勞」，又或者勞工、勞力咁用。你望吓佢個樣，上面有火同火兩個一樣嘅火，跟住一橫蓋住嘅冖，最底就係一個力字。拆碼嘅時候，字首要攞熒頭上邊嘅火火，即係 F 同 F，再加埋個冖 B；剩落嘅字身係下面個力，個力就取頭尾兩碼 K 同 S，所以成個字砌埋就係 FFBKS。點解字首要攞到火火冖三部分先過到落字身呢？因為倉頡係先分好上下兩截，上面熒頭嘅火火同冖歸字首，下底個力自己一份做字身。記住呢個字：兩團火燒到辛苦，先叫做勞。

包.en: Today we're learning 包, read baau1, which means to wrap, to pack, or a package — the same 包 you see in 麵包, bread. Look at its shape: there's a curved wrapper 勹 on the outside, and tucked inside it are 口 (a mouth-box) on top and 山 (mountain) below, three pieces nested together. Because 包 is a whole-form character with no clear head-and-body split, we use the whole-form rule: take the head, the second piece, and the tail. The head is that outer wrapper 勹 on P, the second piece is 口 on R, and the tail is 山 on U, giving you PRU. Remember it this way: one wrapper 勹 hugging a 口 and a 山, counted outside-in and top-to-bottom — P, R, U packs up 包!
包.zh: 我哋今日學「包」呢個字，讀作 baau1，意思係包裹、打包，好似「麵包」個「包」咁。你望下佢個形，外面有個彎彎哋嘅「勹」字包住，入面上邊係「口」字，下邊係「山」字，三嚿疊埋一齊。呢個字係一個整體字，冇分明顯嘅字首字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅拆法：取頭、取二、取尾。頭係外面嗰個「勹」，按 P；跟住第二嚿係「口」，按 R；最後取尾嗰嚿「山」，按 U，合埋就係 PRU。記住喇：一個「勹」包住「口」同「山」，由外到內、由上到下數，P、R、U 就砌成「包」！

化.en: Today we learn 化, read faa3 (sometimes faa1), meaning to change, to convert, or the English suffix -ize. Look at the shape: on the left is the standing-person radical 亻, and on the right is 匕 — a clear left-right structure. In Cangjie the split is simple: the leading part 亻 on the left gives O, and the body 匕 on the right gives P, so the whole character is just OP. Because the two sides divide so cleanly, the leading piece and the body each take one code, giving you a tidy two-letter answer with nothing extra. Here's your memory hook: 雪糕化咗喇 — the ice cream has melted; picture a person (亻) watching something slowly transform (匕), and think of the words 文化 (culture) and 變化 (change).
化.zh: 今日我哋學「化」呢個字，讀音係 faa3，有時讀 faa1，意思係「改變、變化」，好似英文嘅 -ize 咁樣。你望下呢個字，左手邊係一個企人邊「亻」，右手邊係「匕」，一睇就知係左右結構。倉頡拆碼好簡單，左邊嘅字首「亻」取 O，右邊嘅字身「匕」取 P，所以成個字就係 OP。因為呢個字左右分得好清楚，字首同字身各佔一部分，唔使拆多，就係咁乾淨俐落嘅兩碼。記住呢句：「雪糕化咗喇。」——一個人（亻）企喺度睇住雪糕慢慢變（匕），咁就係「化」喇，可以諗返「文化」同「變化」嚟幫記。

北.en: Look at this character: 北, read "bak1", meaning north — the northern direction, as in 北角 North Point or 北京 Beijing. It divides into two parts: a head on the left and a body on the right. The left part is itself broken into two pieces — the ⺊ shape on top gives L, and the flat 一 stroke beneath gives M, so the head contributes two codes, LM. The right part is 匕, and as the body it gives just one code, P. Why split it this way? Because Cangjie lets a head take at most two codes while the body usually takes its last code, so the left ⺊ and 一 fill up as LM and the right 匕 finishes with P, spelling LMP. Remember it like this: on the left you have "⺊ plus 一" (LM), and on the right the little 匕 (P) — 北, the way you face when you look north.
北.zh: 睇下呢個字：北，讀「bak1」，係方向嘅意思，指北方、北面，好似北角、北京噉。呢個字分開兩橛：左邊係字首，右邊係字身。左邊嗰橛我哋要拆做兩件——上面個⺊拆做 L，下面一橫係 M，所以字首連住取兩碼 LM；右邊嗰橛係一個 匕，佢就係字身，取 P 一碼。點解係噉分？因為倉頡規定，一個字分開字首同字身之後，字首最多取到兩碼，字身通常取尾碼，於是左邊嘅⺊同一就湊夠 LM，右邊嘅匕就係尾嘅 P，合埋就係 LMP。記住喇：左邊「⺊一」（LM），右邊一撇一豎嘅匕（P），北就係向北望嘅方向。

匯.en: Today we're learning 匯, read wui6, which means to gather or flow together — like rivers joining into one — and it also means to remit money, as when you go to the bank to send someone a payment. Look at its shape: there's a bracket opening to the right that wraps around what sits inside — that enclosing piece is 匚, and you type it with S. Tucked inside the bracket is 淮, whose own code is EOG, so we read that component through its first-second-last positions: first E, then O, and last G. Put it together and 匚 as the head gives S, while the inner 淮 contributes its first-second-last EOG, making the full code SEOG. Remember the frame: one 匚 embracing 淮, bracket first then body, S to open and EOG to close — that's 匯, the character for flowing together!
匯.zh: 今日我哋學「匯」呢個字，讀做 wui6，意思係匯集、匯合，好似河流匯埋一齊咁，亦都可以解匯款，即係去銀行匯錢過畀人。你望吓佢個樣，右邊同上邊有個開口向右嘅框框，將入面嘅嘢包住——呢個包框就係「匚」，喺鍵盤上面撳 S。框入面裝住嘅係「淮」，佢自己嘅碼係 EOG，所以我哋照住佢個順序拆頭、二、尾——先取 E，再取 O，最後取尾嘅 G。連埋一齊，「匚」做字首取 S，字身「淮」取頭二尾 EOG，全碼就係 SEOG。記住呢個框：一個「匚」框住「淮」，先框後身，S 開頭 EOG 收尾，就係匯合嘅「匯」喇！

區.en: Today we're learning 區, read keoi1, meaning an area, district, or region — you'll see it in words like 地區 (region) and 社區 (community). Look at its shape: there's a box open on the right side, and tucked inside it are three little mouth shapes. That outer box is 匚, which lives on the S key, and it's the head of the character; the three 口 boxes packed inside form the body, and each 口 sits on the R key. When Cangjie takes a body of many pieces it grabs the first, second, and last, but here there are exactly three 口, so we simply take all three. That gives us 匚 (S) followed by 口, 口, 口 (R, R, R), spelling SRRR. Memory hook: one open box holding three mouths in a row — press S, then tap R three times, and you've built 區!
區.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「區」，讀作 keoi1，即係地方、區域嘅意思，好似「地區」、「社區」咁。你望吓佢個樣：外面有個開口向右嘅框，框入面裝住三個「口」。呢個外框叫「匚」，喺個 S 掣度，佢係字首；框入面嘅三個「口」就一齊做字身，每個「口」都喺 R 掣。倉頡拆字身嗰陣，如果部件多過三個要取頭、次、尾，但呢度啱啱好三個「口」，所以三個都攞晒，於是全碼就係 匚（S）加三個口（R、R、R），砌埋成 SRRR。記住個口訣：一個匚，裝住三個口排排企，S 之後三下 R，就係「區」喇！

十.en: Today we're learning 十, read sap6, meaning the number ten, and by extension "complete" or "perfect," as in the idea of being wholly whole. Look at its shape: one horizontal stroke crossed by one vertical stroke, a plain little cross made from just two strokes. In Cangjie this character is itself a single key on the keyboard — it's a basic one-code character, so there's nothing to split apart; you simply press J once. Remember that J is this crossing shape 十, so whenever you meet 二十 (ji6 sap6, twenty) or 十二 (sap6 ji6, twelve), that ten inside is just one tap of J — try saying "I have ten dollars in change" and picture that quick, clean cross.
十.zh: 今日我哋學「十」呢個字，讀作 sap6，就係數字十嘅意思，亦都有「完整」、「圓滿」嘅引申意思，好似「十全十美」咁。你望下佢嘅樣：一橫加一豎交叉，簡簡單單兩筆，就砌成一個十字形。呢個字喺倉頡入面本身就係一個字母鍵，屬於基本嘅一碼字，所以你唔使拆，直接㩒一個 J 就得㗎喇。記住 J 就係「十」呢個交叉形，你以後見到「二十」（ji6 sap6）或者「十二」（sap6 ji6），入面嗰個十都係㩒 J 一下；試下讀「我有十蚊零錢」，感受下十字乾脆利落嘅一筆。

千.en: Look at this character: 千, read cin1 — most often it just means "a thousand," a number word, and by extension "many" or "very numerous," so 幾千 means several thousands. You can see it breaks into two parts: the slanting stroke 丿 across the top, which lives on the H key, and the 十 shape below it, which sits on the J key — giving the full code HJ. Why is it so short, only two codes? Because 千 is a whole-character (整體字) that doesn't split cleanly into a head and a body, and for these small, undivided shapes Cangjie is happy to take just the leading and trailing pieces: the stroke 丿 H plus 十 J, nothing more. Picture one slanting stroke sliding down onto a little cross — H then J, and you've typed the 千 in a thousand dollars.
千.zh: 睇下呢個字：千，讀 cin1，最常見嘅意思就係「一千」嘅千，數目字，好多、好大量嘅意思，講「幾千」就係幾多個一千。你會見到佢分兩部分：上面斜斜嘅一撇丿，喺 H 鍵，跟住下面一個十字，喺 J 鍵，所以成個字就係 HJ 兩碼。點解淨係得兩碼咁短？因為千係一個「整體字」，佢冇拆到字首字身分家，倉頡對呢類細細粒嘅整體字有個做法，最多取頭尾嗰兩個碼就夠，撇 H 加十 J，唔使再攞多。記住一個畫面：一撇斜斜劃落嚟，落到一個「十」字上面，H-J 兩下就打起千蚊嘅千啦。

升.en: Today's character is 升, read sing1, meaning to rise or to go up — you see it in words like 提升 (tai4 sing1, to promote or lift) and 上升 (soeng6 sing1, to ascend), all pointing upward. Look at its shape: there's a slanting stroke 丿 across the top, and underneath sits the 廿 shape. This 升 is a whole-character (整體字), so Cangjie doesn't break it into a head and a body — it just takes it as one piece with only two codes. You type the opening stroke 丿 first, which lives on the H key, then the 廿 shape below it on the T key, giving you HT. Picture 太陽升起嚟喇, the sun rising: stroke 丿 H leads, 廿 T follows, and two taps send it up.
升.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「升」，讀作 sing1，意思係上升、升起，好似「提升」（tai4 sing1）同「上升」（soeng6 sing1）咁，都係向上走嘅意思。你睇吓佢個樣，上面有一撇斜落嚟，下面就係一個「廿」字形。呢個「升」係一個整體字，唔會拆到好散，倉頡就當佢係一嚿嚟取碼，只需要兩個碼：先打起筆嗰一撇丿，佢喺 H 鍵，跟住打下面個「廿」字形，佢喺 T 鍵，合埋就係 HT。因為係整體字，我哋唔使揀字首字身，順住由上到下、由起筆開始寫嘅次序取碼就得。記住「太陽升起嚟喇」呢句，太陽向上升，撇 H 起頭、廿 T 收尾，兩下就打好。

半.en: Today we learn 半, read bun3, which simply means "half." Take a look at its shape: a single vertical stroke runs straight through top to bottom, with two dots split apart on the left and right — almost as if something has been cleanly cut into two. In Cangjie this is treated as a whole-shape character (整體字), which means we don't slowly break it stroke by stroke; instead we take just the first and last parts: the first is 火 on the F key, and the last is 手 on the Q key, giving the code FQ. Why split it this way? The whole-shape rule lets us skip the middle entirely and grab only the two representative shapes at the head and tail — quick and reliable. Here's your memory hook: 半 is 火 (F) plus 手 (Q), cut cleanly into two halves, so it's FQ.
半.zh: 今日我哋學「半」呢個字，讀做 bun3，就係「一半」嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣，中間一條直畫貫穿上下，兩點分開喺左右，好似真係將樣嘢劈開兩邊咁。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候當佢係一個整體字，即係唔會逐橫逐豎咁慢慢拆，而係淨係取頭同尾兩個部分：頭係「火」，喺 F 鍵；尾係「手」，喺 Q 鍵，所以碼就係 FQ。點解咁拆？因為整體字有個特別規矩，唔使取盡中間所有筆畫，只要取頭尾兩個代表形就夠，快而準。記住呢個口訣：「半」係火（F）加手（Q），劈開兩邊，一半一半，就係 FQ。

協.en: This character is 協, read hip3, and it means to be united or to cooperate — you meet it in 協調 hip3 tiu4 (to coordinate, to make things fit and harmonize) and 協議 hip3 ji5 (an agreement or pact that two sides have settled). Look at the left side first: it's 十, written as one horizontal stroke crossed by one vertical stroke, and on the keyboard it lives on J — that's your head piece. The right side is the lump 劦, and rather than break its three little 力 shapes apart one by one, Cangjie treats it as a single body and takes it by the first-middle-last rule: grab the first shape 大 on K, then the middle 尸 on S, then the last 尸 on S. Put it all together and you get 十J, 大K, 尸S, 尸S — the code JKSS. Remember it as a 十 leading the way, followed by three hands pulling together (大K 尸S 尸S) — that's exactly what cooperating looks like.
協.zh: 呢個字係「協」，讀 hip3，即係齊心合力、互相配合嘅意思，好似「協調」hip3 tiu4（大家夾埋一齊，配合得好）、「協議」hip3 ji5（雙方傾掂咗嘅共識）。你望吓，左邊有個「十」字，寫出嚟就係一橫一豎，佢喺鍵盤上面撳 J，呢個就係字首。右邊嗰嚿係「劦」，佢由三個「力」疊埋一齊組成，但拆碼嗰陣唔會逐個字咁拆，而係當佢係一嚿字身，用「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼法：先攞頭嗰個 大K，再攞第二個 尸S，最後攞尾嗰個 尸S。所以成個字合埋就係 十J、大K、尸S、尸S，即係 JKSS。你可以咁記：一個「十」字帶頭，後面三隻手齊心（大K 尸S 尸S）一齊出力，就係「協力」啦。

南.en: Today's character is 南, read naam4, meaning south — the direction where the sun sits at midday. Look at the whole shape: everything is packed together top-to-bottom into one solid block, with no clean seam where you could cut it into a lead part and a body part, so the ordinary head-and-tail split simply doesn't apply here. For a squeezed-together whole character like this, Cangjie uses a special rule: you take the head, second, third, and tail pieces — four codes in all — following the order you'd write them. So we start with the top horizontal 十 on the J key, then the enclosing 冂 on the B key, then the 廿 in the middle on the T key, and finally the closing 十 again on the J key, giving you JBTJ. Remember it as a little stack from top to bottom: a 十 on top, wrapping a 冂, a 廿 in the middle, and one more 十 to close — 十冂廿十, read straight down.
南.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「南」，讀做 naam4，即係方向入面嘅南方，太陽當中嗰邊。你望吓成個字，佢係一個上下夾埋、周身部件擠成一嚿嘅整體字，冇一個明顯嘅位可以斬開做字首字身，所以我哋唔可以用普通嘅「頭尾兩橛」拆法。遇到呢種黐成一嚿嘅整體字，倉頡有一條特別規矩：取頭、二、三、尾一共四個碼，於是我哋順住寫嘅次序，由最頂嗰橫「十」開始，佢喺 J 鍵，跟住係包住下面嘅「冂」，喺 B 鍵，再嚟中間嗰個「廿」，喺 T 鍵，最後收尾又係一個「十」喺 J 鍵，砌埋就係 JBTJ。記住嘅竅門就係：頂上一橫十，抱住一個冂，中間廿字，收尾再一橫十——十冂廿十，由上到下順住讀落嚟就啱。

卡.en: Today we meet 卡, read "kaa1" — the very "card" you use every day, whether a name card or a credit card, and it can also mean a calorie. Look at its shape: a 卜 sitting on top, a single horizontal stroke 一 across the middle, and another 卜 underneath, almost like a 上 and a 下 stacked together. In Cangjie, 卡 is a whole-form character (整體字), which means we do not break it into a head part and a body part; instead we treat the whole thing as one form and take the head, the second, and the last pieces. So we take the top 卜 as Y, the middle stroke 一 as M, and the bottom 卜 again as Y, giving us exactly YMY. To lock it in, just think "top 卜, one stroke, bottom 卜" — Y-M-Y flowing straight through, as smooth as swiping a card.
卡.zh: 我哋今日學「卡」呢個字，讀「kaa1」，就係你日日用嘅咭片、信用卡嗰個「卡」，亦都可以指卡路里嘅計量單位。你望吓佢個形：上面一個「卜」，中間一橫，下面又一個「卜」，好似把一個「上」字同「下」字疊埋一齊咁。喺倉頡入面，「卡」係一隻整體字，即係佢唔會拆做字首同字身兩橛，而係當成一個完整嘅形嚟拆碼，跟頭、二、尾嘅規則取碼，所以我哋取上面嘅「卜」係 Y、中間嘅一橫「一」係 M、最後下面嘅「卜」又係 Y，合埋就係 YMY。記住嘅時候，你可以諗成「上卜、一橫、下卜」，Y-M-Y 一氣呵成，好似打卡咁順手。

印.en: Today we learn 印, read jan3, meaning to print, to stamp, or a seal or chop — you meet it in words like 印度 jan3 dou6 (India) and 印象 jan3 zoeng6, an impression that stays in your mind. Look at the character: it splits into a left side and a right side, a head part and a body. Cangjie takes first-last from each half — from the head it grabs 竹 H and 勹 P, and from the body 卩 it grabs 尸 S and 中 L. That is why the full code reads HPSL: two codes for the head, two codes for the body, neat and balanced. Here is your hook: the left starts with 竹 H and 勹 P, the right seals it with 尸 S and 中 L — 我要印張相, one press and the stamp comes down.
印.zh: 今日我哋學「印」呢個字，讀作 jan3，即係印刷、蓋印、印章嘅意思，好似「印度」jan3 dou6 同「印象」jan3 zoeng6 都用到佢。你望住個字，佢係左右兩邊嘅結構：左邊係字首，右邊係字身。倉頡拆呢個字，字首取頭尾兩碼，就攞「竹」H 同「勹」P；字身係「卩」，一樣取頭尾，攞「尸」S 同「中」L。所以成個字順住打落去就係 HPSL，字首兩碼加字身兩碼，齊齊整整。記住喇：左手竹勹起頭，右手尸中收尾，「我要印張相」，一按落去個印就蓋咗上去。

即.en: Today's character is 即, read zik1, meaning promptly, right away, immediately — as in 你即刻返嚟啦, 'come back right away,' the sense of doing something without any delay. It splits into two sides: a head on the left and a body on the right. The left piece is 艮, but we don't spell it out fully — as a head it takes only its first and last parts, which are 日 (A) and 厶 (I), giving AI. The right piece is 卩, and as a body it likewise takes head and tail, which are 尸 (S) and 中 (L), giving SL. Put the four together and you get AISL — remember it as head-and-tail on the left, head-and-tail on the right, both sides trimmed cleanly to make 即, 'at once.'
即.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「即」，讀做 zik1，意思係即刻、馬上、立即，好似「你即刻返嚟啦」入面咁樣，表示唔使等，即時就做。呢個字分做左右兩邊：左邊係字首，右邊係字身。左邊嗰嚿係「艮」，我哋唔會成嚿咁拆晒，字首淨係取頭同尾兩碼——頭係「日」A，尾係「厶」I，所以左邊出 AI。右邊嗰嚿係「卩」，作為字身都係取頭同尾——頭係「尸」S，尾係「中」L，所以右邊出 SL。四碼砌埋一齊就係 AISL，你可以記住「日厶尸中」——左邊即刻取頭尾，右邊卩都取頭尾，一即到底就係「即」。

原.en: Today we look at 原, read jyun4, meaning source, origin, or beginning — you see it in 原因 (jyun4 jan1, the root cause of something) and 原來 (jyun4 loi4, originally or as it turns out). Look at its shape: there's a 厂 covering the top-left, and tucked underneath is a 白 sitting above a little 水 flourish. When we split it, the 字首 厂 comes first and gives M; then the whole 字身 takes head-second-tail, so 白 gives H and then A, and we finish with the small 水 shape at the bottom, F — spelling M, H, A, F. Remember it like this: the 厂 roof (M) shelters 白 broken into H and A, and one drop of water (F) trickles out the bottom — that's where the source begins.
原.zh: 我哋今日睇「原」呢個字，讀 jyun4，意思係源頭、起初、原本，好似「原因」（jyun4 jan1，即係事情嘅根源）同「原來」（jyun4 loi4，即係本來、起初）咁用。你望吓佢嘅結構：左上係一個「厂」字頭，取碼 M；入面包住一個「白」同一個「水」嘅樣。分拆嘅時候，字首係「厂」，先取 M；跟住落嚟成個字身要取頭、二、尾三碼，「白」拆到日字頭 H 同埋 A，最後就係下面嗰個小水 F，砌埋一齊就係 M、H、A、F。記住口訣：厂遮住頂（M），白拆做 H、A，尾尾流出一滴水 F，源頭就係咁嚟。

去.en: Today we learn 去, read heoi3, meaning to go away or leave — as in 我想去公園, "I want to go to the park." Look at the shape: on top sits 土 (the G key), and underneath is a curved form which is actually 戈 (the I key). To type it in Cangjie you take the first piece 土 (G) and the last piece 戈 (I), giving you the code GI. Why only two codes? Because 去 is a whole shape (整體字), and whole shapes aren't broken down into many parts — you simply grab the first and last pieces, 土 then 戈. Remember it as "earth on top, spear below — one GI and you're gone," and 去 will always come easily.
去.zh: 今日我哋學「去」字，讀heoi3，即係離開、走去邊度嘅意思，好似「我想去公園」咁樣。你望住個字，上面係個「土」，下面係一個彎彎哋嘅形，其實佢係「戈」。用倉頡拆，我哋取頭嘅土（G）同尾嘅戈（I），所以個碼係GI。點解淨係取兩個碼呢？因為「去」係一個整體字，整體字唔會拆到咁散，只需要取頭尾兩個部件——頭係土（G），尾係戈（I）——就夠喇。記住個口訣：「土上戈下，一去GI就到」，落樓梯落去（lok6 heoi3），一步土一步戈，就記得晒喇！

參.en: Today we learn the character 參, read "caam1" and also "sam1". It means to take part, to intervene, and it can also refer to ginseng, a kind of medicinal root. Look at the top of the character: you'll see three identical little pieces 厶 stacked in a row, each one the key I in Cangjie, written one after another, so you take I three times to get the first three codes of IIIH. Then at the bottom you notice three slanting strokes 丿, but instead of splitting each one out, we simply take the final 丿, which is the key H. Why split it this way? Because the three 厶 on top already fill the three-code quota for the leading part, so the leftover strokes below contribute just their last stroke 丿 for the final code, giving IIIH. Here's your memory hook: three 厶 piled on top, one final slash to close it off.
參.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「參」，讀「caam1」，又可以讀「sam1」，意思係參加、介入，另外仲可以指人參嗰種藥材。你望下呢個字，上面排住三個一樣嘅細部件「厶」，係倉頡碼嘅 I 鍵，一個一個順住寫落去，所以連續取三個 I，就係 IIIH 頭三個碼。到咗字嘅下半部，你會見到三撇斜落嚟，我哋唔會逐撇拆開，而係喺呢一堆撇入面淨係取最尾嗰一「丿」，就係 H 鍵。點解係咁分呢？因為上面三個「厶」已經夠晒三碼，剩落嘅撇筆就用尾筆「丿」補埋最後一碼，合埋就係 IIIH。記住呢個口訣：三粒厶疊上頭，一撇尾巴收尾，你就唔會撈亂。

又.en: Today's character is 又, read jau6, meaning "and, also, again, in addition" — the same 又 you'd use in "you're late again." When you look at this character, you'll see it's made of just two crossing strokes; it looks simple, but Cangjie still hunts for the shapes hidden inside it. The first stroke that sweeps down is treated as 弓, which lives on the N key, and the second falling stroke is treated as 大, which lives on the K key, so the whole character is typed NK. Why only these two codes? Because 又 is a simple form (單體字) with no head-and-body division, so you simply take the head and the tail — head N and tail K. Remember it this way: 又 = 弓 N + 大 K, two crossing strokes, and NK does the job.
又.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「又」，讀作 jau6，意思係「又、再、而且」，好似你會講「你又遲到喇」嗰個「又」咁。你望住呢個字嘅時候，會見到佢由兩筆交叉組成，睇落簡單，但係倉頡拆碼嘅時候都要搵到當中嘅字形。第一筆撇出嚟嘅形，倉頡當佢係「弓」，個掣係 N；跟住嘅一捺，倉頡當佢係「大」，個掣係 K，所以整個字打 NK。點解淨係取呢兩個碼呢？因為「又」係一個單體字，冇分字首同字身，所以我哋淨係要取「頭」同「尾」兩個字形，即係頭 N、尾 K。記住喇：「又」= 弓 N + 大 K，兩筆交叉，一撇一捺，NK 就搞掂。

及.en: Today we meet 及, read kap6, meaning to reach or extend up to something, and it also works as "and" — you'll see it in 以及 (ji5 kap6) and 涉及 (sip3 kap6). This character reads as one connected flowing stroke, so it's a whole character (整體字) that can't be cleanly split into a head part and a body part. Because of that, instead of chopping it into components we use the whole-character rule: take just the head, the second, and the tail — three codes. Look at it and you'll find the opening bend counts as 弓 (N), the slanting stroke as 竹 (H), and the final falling stroke at the end as 水 (E), giving you NHE. The memory hook: a whole character skips head-and-body and just grabs head-second-tail, so trace it top to bottom — 弓, 竹, 水, and that's NHE.
及.zh: 今日我哋學「及」呢個字，讀音係 kap6，意思係「達到、觸及」，亦都可以當「和、同」咁用，好似「以及」（ji5 kap6）同「涉及」（sip3 kap6）咁。呢個字睇落一筆過連埋一齊，係一個整體字，冇辦法好乾淨咁拆做字首同字身兩橛，所以我哋唔逐部件拆，而係跟整體字嘅取碼法，攞頭、二、尾三碼。你望住個字：起筆嗰下橫折鈎當「弓」（N），跟住嘅撇當「竹」（H），最後尾嗰下捺當「水」（E），所以三碼砌埋就係 NHE。記住嘅竅門：整體字唔使頭身，只揀「頭、二、尾」三個位——弓、竹、水，一路望落去就係 NHE。

友.en: Today we learn 友, read "jau5", meaning friend or companion. Look at its shape: on top sits ナ, a slanting stroke crossing a flat one, and underneath sits 又, a piece you already know well. To split it, the top ナ becomes the head and you press K, while the bottom 又 becomes the body and you press E, giving you the code KE. Why does it break this way? Cangjie reads top to bottom, and 友 is clearly two parts stacked vertically, so the upper part naturally takes the head slot and the lower part the body — one piece each, clean and simple. Here's your hook: that little ナ resting on 又 is your good friend — 佢係我嘅好朋友, he is my good friend.
友.zh: 今日我哋學「友」呢個字，讀「jau5」，即係朋友、友伴嘅意思。你望下佢個形，上面係一撇一橫嘅「ナ」，下面就係「又」呢個好熟悉嘅部件。拆字嘅時候，上邊嘅「ナ」做字首，撳 K；下邊嘅「又」做字身，撳 E，所以「友」嘅碼就係 KE。點解係咁分呢？因為倉頡係由上到下拆，「友」明顯係上下兩截疊埋，上面一截自然做字首，下面一截做字身，一人一個部件，乾淨企理。記住呢個口訣：一撇一橫搭住個「又」，就係你嘅好朋友——佢係我嘅好朋友。

反.en: Today we learn 反, read faan2, meaning to reverse, opposite, or contrary — you meet it in words like 相反 (soeng1 faan2, opposite) and 反映 (faan2 jing2, to reflect). Look at its shape: there's a sloping frame across the top-left that wraps around the piece inside, so we begin decoding from that outer frame. That frame is 厂, the head, typed with H; what's left inside — the short 又 made of a stroke and a sweep — is the body, typed with E, giving you HE. Why split here? Cangjie takes an enclosing frame like 厂 as the head first and the enclosed content as the body next, and one head plus one body makes a tidy two-key code. Memory hook: 厂 folds over 又 — flip it once and you get HE.
反.zh: 我哋今日學「反」呢個字，讀音係 faan2，意思係反轉、相反、對立，好似「相反」（soeng1 faan2）或者「反映」（faan2 jing2）咁樣用。你望吓佢個樣，係一個外框斜斜咁罩住入面嘅部件，所以拆嘅時候由左上角嗰個「厂」開始起手。呢個「厂」就係字首，撳 H 鍵；跟住入面淨低一撇一捺嘅「又」就係字身，撳 E 鍵，合埋就係 HE。點解會咁樣分呢？因為倉頡見到「厂」呢類包住嘅部件，會先攞外框做字首，再攞入面嘅內容做字身，一頭一身剛剛好兩碼。記住個口訣：厂罩住又，一反就成——HE。

取.en: Today we meet 取, read ceoi2, meaning to take, receive, or obtain — and also to select, as in 取錢 (withdraw money) or 取得 (to acquire). Look at the character: on the left sits 耳, and on the right sits 又, and those two blocks are all it's made of. In Cangjie the left 耳 is the head of the character, so we split it head-tail: its head 匚 is the key S, and its tail 十 is the key J; then the right 又 is the body, written as the shape 水 on the key E, giving the full code SJE. Why split 耳 head-tail rather than piece by piece? Because as the head block it's allowed at most two codes, so we take just its opening and closing shapes and leave room for the body. Remember it this way: 耳 listens (SJ), then 又 grabs (E) — hear it, then take it.
取.zh: 今日我哋學「取」字，讀作 ceoi2，意思係攞、拿取、得到，又或者揀選，好似「取錢」、「取得」咁樣。你望住個字，左邊係「耳」，右邊係「又」，成個字就係由呢兩橛砌出嚟。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊嘅「耳」係字首，我哋幫佢分頭尾——頭係「匚」，撳 S 掣，尾係「十」，撳 J 掣；跟住右邊嘅「又」係字身，佢個形係「水」，撳 E 掣，所以成個碼就係 SJE。點解「耳」要拆頭尾而唔係逐橛拆？因為佢做字首，字首最多只取兩碼，於是就用頭尾各取一個代表，留返個位畀字身。記住呢個口訣：「耳」聽（SJ），「又」攞（E），一聽就攞到手。

受.en: Today we learn 受, read sau6, meaning to receive or accept, and also to bear or stand something — as in 我受唔到咁熱, "I can't stand it being so hot." Look at how it stacks top to bottom in three pieces: at the top is 爫, the clawlike hand-shape, typed B; in the middle is 冖, the covering stroke, also typed B; and at the bottom is 又, typed E. 受 is a whole-form character, so Cangjie takes only the head, the second piece, and the tail — head 爫 (B), second 冖 (B), tail 又 (E) — and the middle is skipped, giving you exactly BBE. Picture one hand (爫) reaching down over a cover (冖) to pass something to another hand (又) waiting below to receive it — that's 受.
受.zh: 今日我哋學「受」呢個字，讀音係 sau6，意思係接收、接受，又可以解作承受、頂得住，好似「我受唔到咁熱。」咁樣。你留意「受」由上到下疊咗三嚿嘢：最頂係爫（就係「爪」字頭嗰隻手勢），打 B；中間有一橫蓋住嘅冖，都係打 B；最底係又，打 E。「受」係一隻整體字，倉頡取碼時只取頭、次、尾三部分——頭爫係 B，次冖係 B，尾又係 E，中間嗰啲筆畫就跳過唔取，所以成個碼就係 BBE。記住個畫面：一隻手（爫）由上面伸落嚟，隔住個蓋（冖），交畀下面另一隻手（又）接住，就係「受」啦。

口.en: Today's character is 口, read hau2, meaning mouth — the thing you eat and speak with — and by extension any opening, entrance, or gate, as in 人口 for the population living in a place, or 口岸 for a border port where trade passes through. Look at its shape: a simple square frame, empty in the middle, drawn like a mouth held open. In Cangjie, 口 is a complete single-piece character — it's one of the basic shapes itself, called 口, and it lives on the R key. Because it's a single piece, there's nothing to split apart, no 字首 or 字身 to find, so the whole code is just one letter, R, and you're done in a single tap. Remember it this way: the little frame is a mouth, and one press of R opens it right up.
口.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「口」，讀做 hau2，就係我哋講嘢食嘢嗰個嘴，亦都可以解做出入嘅開口位、入口或者門口，好似「人口」就係講一個地方住幾多人，「口岸」就係對外通商嘅關口。你睇下佢個樣：一個四四方方、中間空咗嘅框，簡單直接，就好似一張擘開晒嘅嘴咁。呢個字喺倉頡入面係一個完整嘅單體字，本身就係一個基本字形，叫做「口」，放喺鍵盤嘅 R 掣度。因為佢係單體字，唔使拆開，唔使搵字首字身，所以個碼就得一個 R，打一下就完成。記住呢個框框就係一張嘴，一個 R 打開個口，就係「口」喇。

古.en: Today's character is 「古」, read gu2, meaning old, ancient, or classic — you'll spot it in the word 「古代」, ancient times. Look at its shape: on top sits a 十, and beneath it rests a 口, making a clear top-bottom structure. Cangjie follows that top-to-bottom order when breaking it apart: the top 十 is the head and you press J, then the bottom 口 is the body and you press R, giving you JR — exactly two codes. In a top-bottom character, the head and the body each contribute the code for their own piece, so 十 and 口 each give one letter and nothing gets left out. Remember it like this: one 十 pressing down on one 口 makes 「古」, the old and ancient character you see in 「太古城」 and 「古代」.
古.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「古」，讀音係 gu2，意思係「古老、古代、經典」，你喺「古代」呢個詞入面就見到佢。你望下佢嘅樣，上面係一個「十」字，下面托住一個「口」字，係一個清清楚楚嘅上下結構。倉頡拆碼嘅時候就跟住呢個上下嘅次序：上面嘅「十」係字首，撳 J 鍵；下面嘅「口」係字身，撳 R 鍵，合埋就係 JR，啱啱兩碼。因為上下結構嘅字，字首同字身各取自己嗰部分嘅碼，所以「十」同「口」都各自貢獻一個字母，一個都唔會走漏。記住喇：一個「十」壓住一個「口」，就係古老嘅「古」，好似「太古城」同「古代」都用到佢。

另.en: Today we learn 另, read ling6, meaning "another" or "other" — like when you say 我要另一個, "I want another one." Look at its shape: it stacks in two levels, with 口 sitting on top and 力 underneath. The top 口 becomes the 字首 and gives us its key R; the bottom 力 becomes the 字身, and since 力 has its own code K then S, as a 字身 we take its first key K and its last key S, so the whole code for 另 comes out as R, K, S. Why split it this way? Because in a top-bottom character the top part is the 字首 and the bottom is the 字身, and the 字身 is taken by its head and tail — so 力 hands over K and S. Remember it like this: one 口 up high, one 力 down low, R-K-S, and you've got the 另 of 另外.
另.zh: 今日我哋學「另」呢個字，讀「ling6」，即係「另外」、「其他」嘅意思，好似你講「我要另一個」咁。你望吓佢個樣，係上下兩橛砌成嘅，上面係個「口」，下面係個「力」。上面嘅「口」做字首，我哋取佢個鍵R；下面嘅「力」做字身，因為「力」自己嘅碼係K同S，做字身就取佢個頭K同個尾S，所以合埋成「另」個碼就係R、K、S。點解係咁拆呢？因為上下結構嘅字，上面做字首、下面做字身，字身要取頭同尾兩碼，所以「力」就攞K同S。記住喇：一個「口」喺上，一個「力」喺下，R-K-S，就係「另」外一個嘅「另」。

只.en: Today's character is 只, read zi2, meaning "only, just, simply" — as in 我只係想瞓覺, "I only want to sleep," that feeling of just one thing and nothing more. Look at its shape: there's a 口 on top, and underneath two little strokes 丷, which is really a form of 八. In Cangjie the 字首 takes the top 口, sitting on the R key, and the 字身 takes that lower 八/丷 shape on the C key, giving you the full code RC. The 字身 gives only a single code here because it is just that one 八 shape — one code is enough, nothing more needs to be added. Remember it like this: one mouth R plus one 八 C, and "only" 只 appears — only two keys, fittingly.
只.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「只」，讀做 zi2，意思係「淨係、只不過」，好似「我只係想瞓覺」噉樣，表達「淨係要做一件嘢」嘅感覺。你望下呢個字嘅結構：上面係一個「口」，下面係兩點「丷」，即係「八」嘅變形。用倉頡拆，字首取上面嘅「口」，佢喺 R 鍵；字身就係下面嗰個「八」／「丷」形，佢喺 C 鍵，所以成個碼就係 RC。點解字身淨係取一碼呢？因為字身本身簡單，得一個「八」形，取一碼就夠曬，唔使再補。記住呢個口訣：一個「口」R 加一個「八」C，只此一家，「只」就打得出嚟喇。

叫.en: Today's character is 叫, read giu3, meaning to cry out, to hail or greet someone, or to be called by some name. Look at how it divides into two parts: on the left is the mouth 口, and on the right is a piece called 丩. The left part is the 字首, the mouth 口, and it takes just one code, R. The right side is the 字身, and since a 字身 takes at most two codes, we take its head and its tail — the opening bend ㄑ is V, and the closing vertical stroke 丨 is L. Put in order, that gives you R, V, L, spelled out as RVL. A little hook to remember it: a mouth (R) calls out, its cry curving (V) then falling straight down (L).
叫.zh: 你今日學嘅字係「叫」，讀 giu3，即係大聲呼喊、招呼人、或者叫做某個名嘅意思。你望下佢分做兩橛：左邊係個「口」字，右邊係一個叫做「丩」嘅部件。左邊嘅字首「口」好簡單，就係 R 一碼。到右邊嘅字身「丩」，倉頡規矩係字身最多取兩碼，於是就取頭同尾——起首嘅「ㄑ」係 V，收尾嘅一直筆「丨」係 L。所以「叫」順住次序砌落去，就係 R、V、L，即 RVL。你可以咁樣記：一個「口」（R）喺度大聲叫，尾音拉到又彎（V）又直（L）。

可.en: Today we learn 可, read ho2, meaning "may," "can," or "-able," as in the sentence "this thing can be done." Look at its shape: a flat stroke across the top, a curved hook on the right, and a mouth-shape sitting underneath. This is a whole character (整體字), so instead of neatly splitting it into a head part and a body part, we use the head-second-tail method — we pick the first piece, the second piece, and the last piece. Following the character down, the top stroke is 一, typed M; the curved hook counts as 弓, typed N; and the mouth at the bottom is 口, typed R, giving us MNR. Remember it as one-bow-mouth from top to bottom, and the order falls right into place.
可.zh: 今日我哋學「可」呢個字，讀音係 ho2，意思係「可以」、「能夠」，好似「呢件事可以做到」入面咁用。你望下佢個樣：上面一橫，右邊一個彎彎嘅鈎，下面一個口。呢個字係一個整體字，拆嘅時候唔係逐塊逐塊咁分頭尾，而係用「取頭二尾」嘅辦法，即係揀最頭嗰部分、第二部分同埋最尾嗰部分。所以我哋順住個字取三個碼：最頂嗰橫係「一」，打 M；跟住個彎鈎當作「弓」，打 N；最尾底下嗰個「口」，打 R；合埋就係 MNR。記住呢個小貼士：一橫、一弓、一口，由上到下順住寫落嚟，就啱曬個順序啦。

台.en: Today we learn 台, read toi4, meaning a platform or stage — it can also be a measure word or a respectful way to address someone. Take a look at its shape: there's a small 厶 sitting on top, resting on a 口 below, so it's clearly a top-bottom structure and we split it from top to bottom. The top piece 厶 is the 字首 and is typed with I, while the bottom piece 口 is the 字身 and is typed with R, giving you IR together. Because a top-bottom character takes its 字首 and 字身 each straight from their own shapes with no filler code needed, this one is clean and finishes in just two keys. Picture a little 厶 standing on a 口 stage to sing — I on top, R below — and you've got 台!
台.zh: 今日我哋學「台」呢個字，佢讀作 toi4，意思係平台、舞台，亦都可以做量詞或者尊稱人嘅用語。你望吓佢嘅樣：上面係一個細細哋嘅「厶」，下面托住一個「口」，明顯係上下結構，所以我哋由上至下拆。上面嘅「厶」就係字首，喺鍵盤上面取 I；下面嘅「口」就係字身，取 R，兩個夾埋就係 IR。因為上下結構嘅字，字首同字身各自照字形取碼，唔使補碼，所以呢個字乾淨俐落，兩碼收工。記住呢個畫面：一個小小嘅「厶」企喺一個「口」台上面唱歌，I 上 R 下，就係「台」喇！

史.en: Today's character is 史, read si2, meaning history, chronicle, or annals. Take a look at its shape — it's like a 口 with a stroke running through it, all fused into one connected body, what we call a single-body character. Because 史 is a single body, Cangjie doesn't chop it into many pieces; it takes just the head and the tail, two codes only: first the vertical 中 (L) running down the middle, then the crossing strokes 乂 (K) at the bottom, giving you LK. Remember it as 中 spearing straight down and 乂 crossing at the tail — L then K spells 史, as in 歷史, the study I like to read.
史.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「史」，讀作 si2，即係歷史、史書嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣，好似一個「口」加一劃穿過去，成隻字連埋一齊，係一個連體字。因為佢係連體字，倉頡就唔會拆到好碎，只取頭同尾兩碼：先寫中間直落嘅「中」（L），再寫下面撇捺交叉嘅「乂」（K），所以碼就係 LK。記住喇，一直「中」貫落去，再打隻「乂」交叉埋尾，L、K 兩下就寫得出「史」，好似「我鍾意讀歷史」咁。

司.en: Today we learn 司, read si1, meaning to take charge of, to manage, or an officer — the same 司 you see in 公司, a company. Look at its shape: an outer frame wrapping the top and right side, with a horizontal stroke and a mouth tucked inside. Because 司 is a whole character (整體字), we don't split it into a normal head and body of two codes each; instead we take the outer frame 尸 first, pressing S, then read the inside pieces — the horizontal 一 with M, and the mouth 口 with R — giving SMR. The memory hook is simple: frame before filling, so the 尸 leads with S and the hidden 一 and 口 follow as MR.
司.zh: 今日我哋學「司」呢個字，讀音係 si1，意思係掌管、管理，又或者指做官嘅人，好似「公司」嘅「司」咁。你望吓佢個樣：外面有個框住上面同右邊嘅形，入面藏住一橫同一個口。呢個「司」係一個整體字，所以我哋唔會好似普通字咁分字首字身各取兩碼，而係先取外框嘅 尸，撳 S，然後取入面嘅部件——先係一橫 一 撳 M，再係個口 口 撳 R，合埋就係 SMR。記住嘅竅門係：先框後心，外面個尸帶頭，入面藏住一同口，S 開場 MR 收尾。

各.zh: 今日我哋學「各」呢個字，讀作 gok3，意思係「每一個、各自」。你望下佢，係上下兩橛砌成嘅：上面係「夂」，個鍵係 H；跟住係「水」，個鍵係 E；最下面係「口」，個鍵係 R，所以成個碼就係 HER。點解會咁拆呢？因為上面嘅「夂」係字首，倉頡俾字首最多取兩碼，於是就攞「夂」H 同「水」E 兩碼；剩返下面嘅「口」就係字身，取 R 一碼。你睇「各種」、「雅各」呢啲詞，都係同一個「各」。記住嘅竅門：由上到下一路數落嚟，夂（H）、水（E）、口（R），三碼一氣呵成。

合.en: Today we learn 合, a character with two readings — it can read hap6, as in 合作 (to cooperate), or ho4, and it means to combine, unite, or gather together. Look at its shape: a pointed roof on top, a horizontal line beneath it, and a mouth 口 at the bottom, as if something is coming down from above and joining into one. When we split it, the pointed roof 𠆢 is the head, which you type with O; everything left below, the 一 and the 口, forms the body, and since a body made of several pieces takes at most its head and tail in Cangjie, we take the head 一 (M) and the tail 口 (R), giving the full code OMR. Picture it this way: a pointed lid O closing over a bar M and a mouth R — everything coming together into one, and that's 合.
合.zh: 今日我哋學「合」呢個字，佢有兩個讀音，可以讀 hap6，好似「合作」咁，又可以讀 ho4，意思係組合、結合、聚埋一齊。你留意佢個樣：上面一個尖尖嘅蓋，下面一橫，再下面一個口，好似有嘢從上面蓋落嚟、合埋一齊咁。拆碼嗰陣，上面嗰個蓋叫「𠆢」，佢係字首，撳 O；下面剩返嘅「一」加「口」就係字身，因為字身唔止一件嘢，倉頡規定最多取頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋取個頭「一」M，再取個尾「口」R，全碼就係 OMR。記住呢個畫面：一個尖蓋 O，蓋住一橫 M 同一個口 R，蓋落去、合埋一齊，就係「合」。

吉.en: Today we learn 吉, read gat1, meaning lucky or auspicious — a good-fortune character. Look at its shape: on top sits a 士, and beneath it sits a 口, one stacked neatly above the other. Cangjie splits from top to bottom, so the top 士 becomes the 字首 and gives G, while the bottom 口 becomes the 字身 and gives R, joining into GR — just two codes. Why so short? Because the character has only two clear parts, one head and one body, and each contributes a single representative code. Remember it this way: 士 on top is G, 口 at the bottom is R — top scholar, bottom mouth, a lucky pair.
吉.zh: 今日我哋學「吉」呢個字，讀音係 gat1，意思係吉祥、好運，好意頭嘅字。你望吓佢嘅樣，上面係一個「士」，下面係一個「口」，一個疊喺一個上面，結構好清楚。倉頡分字嘅時候，係由上至下拆嘅，所以上面嘅「士」做字首，取佢個碼 G；下面嘅「口」做字身，取佢個碼 R，合埋就係 GR，啱啱好兩個碼。點解淨係取兩個碼咁少呢？因為呢個字得兩橛，一橛字首、一橛字身，每橛各取一個代表碼就夠。記住一個口訣：士頭 G、口底 R，上士下口，好運吉祥。

同.en: Today's character is 同, read tung4, meaning "same" or "together with" — you'll meet it in 同埋 (tung4 maai4, "and, together") and 唔同 (m4 tung4, "different"). Look at its shape: there's an outer frame like an open box, 冂, and tucked inside it a single horizontal stroke and a mouth 口. The Cangjie code is BMR, and here's how it breaks down: the head piece is the frame 冂, which lives on the B key. Then the body inside follows Cangjie's head-and-tail rule, so we take its first stroke, 一 on M, and its last piece, 口 on R. Type them in order — B, M, R, frame first then what's inside, top to bottom — and just picture that box holding a line and a mouth, and 同 will always come out right.
同.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「同」，讀做 tung4，意思係「相同」、「一齊」，好似「同埋」（tung4 maai4，即係「和」）同「唔同」（m4 tung4，即係「不一樣」）咁樣。你望下個字嘅結構：外面有個好似框咁嘅「冂」，入面就藏住一橫同一個「口」。倉頡碼係 BMR，我哋一步步拆：字首係「冂」，佢喺 B 掣；跟住入面嘅字身要取，倉頡有「頭尾」嘅規矩，字身取頭取尾，所以先攞頭一筆「一」喺 M 掣，再攞最尾嘅「口」喺 R 掣。順住打就係 B、M、R，先框後入面，由上到下咁行，記住個框住橫同口嘅樣，「同」就唔會拆錯喇。

名.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「名」，讀 ming4，口語有時讀 meng2，意思係名字、名銜、名聲。你望下佢嘅結構：上面係「夕」，下面係「口」，一個上下疊埋一齊嘅字。上面嘅「夕」係字首，倉頡教我哋一個字首最多取頭尾兩碼，所以「夕」取頭「乛」（N 鍵）同尾「戈」（I 鍵）；下面嘅「口」係字身，整齊地取「口」（R 鍵）。咁樣砌埋就係 N、I、R，即係 NIR。記住喇：夕陽（NI）之下有一個口（R）叫緊你嘅名，就係「名」。

后.en: Today we meet 后, read hau6, which means queen or empress — think of 天后 tin1 hau6, the goddess Mat, Empress of Heaven — and in simplified writing it also stands in for 後, meaning behind or after. Take a good look at its shape: up top there's a short slanting stroke resting on a horizontal line, and underneath sits a mouth 口. This is a whole-character (整體字), meaning it doesn't break cleanly into a head part and a body part, so instead of splitting it we use the head-second-last method: we grab the very first piece, the slanting 丿 on key H, then the second piece, the horizontal 一 on key M, then we skip whatever's in the middle and jump straight to the last piece, the 口 on key R, giving HMR. Here's your memory hook: read 后 top to bottom and count first, second, last — 丿H, 一M, 口R — and let the middle quietly slip away.
后.zh: 今日我哋學「后」呢個字，讀作 hau6，本身解「皇后」、「女王」，好似「天后」tin1 hau6，即係海上守護神媽祖；而喺簡體字入面，佢又借嚟做「後」，解「後面」、「之後」。你望吓佢個樣：上面有一撇搭一橫，下面係一個「口」字。呢個字係一個「整體字」，即係佢唔容易一刀切開成字首同字身，所以我哋唔逐部件拆，而係用「取頭二尾」嘅辦法——揀最頭嘅一撇丿，就係 H；跟住第二個部件一橫一，就係 M；然後跳過中間，直接攞最尾嘅口 R，砌成 HMR。記住喇：「后」由上到下數，頭、二、尾——撇 H、橫 M、口 R，中間嗰啲統統跳過。

向.en: Today we learn 向, read hoeng3, meaning toward, a direction, or a trend — as in 方向 fong1 hoeng3 (direction) and 傾向 king1 hoeng3 (tendency). Look at the character: there's a single stroke 丿 across the top, and below it a frame wrapping around a mouth shape. In Cangjie the 字首 takes that top stroke 丿 first, which sits on H; then the 字身 below holds two pieces, 冂 and 口, and from the body we take the head and the tail, giving 冂 as B and 口 as R, so the whole code is HBR. Why take only first and last of the body rather than every piece? Because the 字身 has a limited quota — the head and tail codes are enough to identify it, so nothing in between is added. Your memory hook: a stroke 丿 H on top, then 冂 B framing the 口 R — walk forward with HBR.
向.zh: 今日我哋學「向」呢個字，讀音係 hoeng3，意思係方向、朝住某個方向，好似「方向」fong1 hoeng3 同「傾向」king1 hoeng3 咁。你望下個字，最頂有一撇 丿，接住下面係一個框住個口嘅樣。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，字首先取最頂嗰撇 丿，佢喺鍵盤上係 H；跟住落到字身，字身入面有 冂 同 口 兩件嘢，我哋取頭同尾，冂 係 B、口 係 R，所以成個碼砌埋就係 HBR。點解字身唔係逐件全取，而係取頭尾呢？因為字身有配額限制，取頭同尾兩碼就夠代表，所以中間唔使再拆。記住個口訣：一撇 H 起頭，冂 B 框住個口 R，向前行 HBR。

吓.en: Today we meet 吓, read haa2 or haa1. On its own it means to scare or frighten, but in Cantonese you'll see it far more often as a soft particle, as in 睇吓 (have a look) or 試吓 (give it a try), giving that easy 'just try it, just check' feeling. Look closely: on the left is 口, the mouth, and on the right is 下, meaning below. When you type it, the 字首 is 口 standing alone as a single code, R; then the 字身 is 下, and because it's a joined body we don't spell out every stroke — we take just its head and tail, the head being 一 as M and the tail being 卜 as Y. Put them together and you get R, M, Y. Here's your hook: a mouth 口 on the left doing the talking, and 下 giving you only its head and tail — open, close, and you've got 吓!
吓.zh: 今日我哋學「吓」呢個字，讀「haa2」或者「haa1」，本身有嚇親、恐嚇嘅意思，但喺廣東話入面你更加成日見到佢做語氣詞，好似「睇吓」、「試吓」咁，帶住「試一試、望一望」嘅輕鬆感覺。你望真啲個字：左邊係個「口」字，右邊係個「下」字。打嘅時候，字首「口」自己一個部件，取碼R；字身係「下」，因為佢係一個相連嘅字身，唔會逐筆拆盡，只取頭尾兩碼——頭係「一」M，尾係「卜」Y。合埋就係口一卜，即係R、M、Y。記住喇：左邊有個口喺度講嘢，右邊個「下」淨係要頭同尾，一開一合就係「吓」！

吞.en: Today's character is 吞, read tan1, meaning to swallow or gulp down, and by extension to absorb, annex, or engulf — it's the 吞 in 雲吞麵, wonton noodles. Look at how it's built: on top sits 夭, and underneath sits a 口 (mouth). When Cangjie breaks this apart, the head part and the body part are coded separately, and the head 夭 doesn't give all of itself — it follows the head-tail rule, taking only its first piece 禾 (H) and its last piece 大 (K). The body below is the whole 口 (R), so reading straight down you get 禾 大 口, which is HKR. Here's your memory hook: the 夭 up top hands over its head and tail, 禾 and 大, and then everything drops down into the 口 (mouth) — and that's how you swallow, 吞.
吞.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「吞」，讀作 tan1，意思係吞落肚、吞食，引申仲有吞併、吞沒嘅意思，好似「雲吞麵」個「吞」就係呢個字。你望吓佢嘅結構，上面係一個「夭」，下面係一個「口」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首同字身分開嚟取碼：字首係上面嘅「夭」，但係字首唔會成個攞晒，佢淨係取頭尾兩件——頭係「禾」（H），尾係「大」（K）；跟住字身就係下面成個「口」（R）。所以順住打落去就係禾大口，即係 HKR。記住個口訣：夭字頭取頭尾禾大，一啖吞落個口，就係「吞」喇。

吧.en: Today we learn 吧, read baa1, an emphatic final particle you drop at the end of a sentence to make a gentle suggestion or soften the tone, like in "let's go eat 吧." Look at the character: on the left sits a mouth 口, and on the right is 巴. The mouth 口 is the head of the character, and in Cangjie it is typed with R. The 巴 on the right is the body, and when Cangjie breaks down a body it does not take every stroke — it takes the first and last pieces, which here are 日 (A) and 山 (U), giving AU. Put it all together and you get RAU: the mouth R first, then the first-and-last of 巴, A then U. Remember it this way: a mouth on the left is calling out, 巴 gives you its head and tail, and out comes 吧.
吧.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「吧」，讀作 baa1，係一個語氣助詞，放喺句尾用嚟表達提議或者輕鬆嘅語氣，好似「去食飯吧」咁。你望下呢個字，左邊係一個口，右邊係一個「巴」。左邊嘅口就係字首，喺倉頡入面用 R 嚟打。右邊個「巴」就係字身，倉頡拆字身嘅時候唔會逐筆咁拆，而係取頭同取尾兩個碼——巴嘅頭係日 A，尾係山 U，所以合埋就係 A 加 U。成個字砌落嚟就係 RAU，先口 R，再巴嘅頭尾 AU。記住呢個口訣：一個口喺左邊叫你講嘢，右邊個巴取頭尾，講完就「吧」一聲喇。

呀.en: Today we learn 呀, read aa4, a word you hear constantly in Cantonese — sometimes as a fast, slurred way of saying ten, and often as a little particle that adds surprise or gentle emphasis, as in 係呀 (yes) or 點呀 (so? how about?). Look at its shape: on the left sits the 口 mouth radical, and on the right sits 牙, the tooth. Cangjie treats the 口 on the left as the 字首, the leading part, and a leading part gives just one code, so 口＝R. The 牙 on the right becomes the 字身, the body, and a body follows the head-2nd-last rule — take its first two pieces plus its very last piece — which gives 一＝M, ㄑ＝V, and the final falling stroke 丿＝H. Put it together and 呀 is RMVH; remember it as the mouth opening first (R), then the tooth biting down piece by piece (MVH).
呀.zh: 今日我哋學「呀」呢個字，讀作 aa4，喺廣東話入面好常見，有時當「十」嘅急讀，有時做語氣助詞，帶少少驚訝或者輕輕強調嘅意思，好似「係呀」、「點呀」咁。你望下佢個樣：左邊係個「口」字，右邊係個「牙」字。倉頡分字嘅時候，左邊嘅「口」做字首，只取一碼，就係 口＝R；右邊嘅「牙」做字身，跟「頭二尾一」嘅規矩，即係取頭嗰兩碼、再加最尾嗰一碼，於是取到 一＝M、ㄑ＝V，同埋最尾嗰一畫 丿＝H。合埋一齊，「呀」就係 RMVH。記住呢一句：口先開聲（R），跟住牙齒一啖一啖（MVH）咬落去，你自然就記得「呀」點打。

呢.en: Today we learn 呢, a word you say all day long, read ne1 or nei1 — Cantonese's most common particle and demonstrative, as in 呢個, meaning "this". Look at the character: on the left is the mouth radical 口, and on the right sits 尼. The 口 on the left is the 字首, so you press R; the 尼 on the right is the 字身, and a 字身 gives its head and tail, so from 尼 you take the head 尸 for S and the tail 匕 for P, spelling RSP. Why split here? Once 口 takes the 字首 slot, what remains, 尼, is one body part, and the head-tail rule keeps only 尸 at the top and 匕 at the bottom, dropping the middle. Remember it this way: a mouth on the left doing the talking, with 尸 and 匕 holding down the right — 口, 尸, 匕, RSP.
呢.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「呢」，你日日都講嘅一個字，讀 ne1 或者 nei1，係廣東話最常用嘅語氣同指示詞，好似「呢個」就係 this 嘅意思。你望下呢個字，左邊係個「口」字部，右邊係「尼」字。左邊個「口」係字首，我哋撳 R；右邊嘅「尼」就係字身，字身要取頭同尾兩個部件，所以喺「尼」入面取頭嘅「尸」撳 S，再取尾嘅「匕」撳 P，砌埋一齊就係 RSP。點解係咁拆？因為口部做咗字首之後，淨低嘅字身「尼」係一個獨立部件，跟住取頭尾嘅規矩，頭係尸尾係匕，中間唔使理。記住呢個字嘅口訣：一個口喺左邊講嘢，尸同匕喺右邊壓陣——口、尸、匕，RSP。

周.en: Today we meet 周, read zau1, which names the Zhou dynasty and also means circumference — the whole way around a circle. Look at its shape: there's an outer frame wrapping around, with pieces packed inside it. This is a 整體字, a whole-character, because it's too tightly bound to cut cleanly into a left/right or top/bottom split, so instead of forcing a 字首/字身 divide we use the whole-character rule: take the head, then the second piece, then the last, and simply skip whatever sits in the middle. That's why you type the outer frame 冂 first (the B key), then 土 inside the upper part (the G key), and finally 口 at the end (the R key), giving BGR. Remember it as frame, earth, mouth — B, G, R — one wrapper holding two pieces, middle ignored.
周.zh: 今日我哋學「周」呢個字，讀音係 zau1，佢可以指周朝，又或者指「周圍」嘅意思，即係四周一圈。你望吓佢個樣：外面有一個包住嘅框，入面塞咗好多嘢。呢個字係一個「整體字」，因為佢個結構好緊湊，冇一刀清脆嘅左右或者上下界線，所以我哋唔會硬分字首字身，而係用「整體字」嘅取碼法：先攞個頭、再攞第二件、最後攞個尾，中間嗰啲就直接跳過。所以你打嘅時候，先撳個外框冂（B 鍵），跟住撳裡面上半嘅土（G 鍵），最尾撳個口（R 鍵），砌出 BGR。記住口訣：外框冂、中間土、埋尾口，中間唔理，一框套三件就係「周」。

味.en: Today we learn 味, read mei6, meaning taste or smell — as in 好味 (hou2 mei6), meaning something is delicious, or 味道 (mei6 dou6), meaning the taste of something. Look at its structure: on the left is 口 (mouth), and on the right is 未 — fitting, since taste is something you experience with your mouth. When you break it up, the left-side 口 is the 字首, and a 字首 gives only one code, which is R; then the right-side 未 is the 字身, and a 字身 takes head and tail, so you grab 十 (J) at the top and 木 (D) at the bottom, skipping the middle. Put them together and you get 口十木, that is RJD. Remember it this way: a mouth on the left, and 未 giving only its head and tail — when the soup has flavour you open your mouth to praise it: 口十木, RJD.
味.zh: 今日我哋學「味」呢個字，讀做 mei6，即係味道、氣味嘅意思，好似「好味」（hou2 mei6）咁講一樣嘢好食，又或者「味道」（mei6 dou6）指嘢食嘅滋味。你望吓佢嘅結構，左邊係一個「口」字，右邊係一個「未」字，因為味道係用個口去感受嘅嘛。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「口」係字首，字首淨係取一碼，就係 R；跟住右邊嘅「未」做字身，字身要取頭尾兩碼，個頭係「十」（J），個尾係「木」（D），所以「未」淨係取 十木，唔會取中間。合埋一齊就係 口十木，即係 RJD。記住呢個字：一個口喺左邊，右邊個未取頭尾，湯一有味你就開口讚，口十木、RJD。

命.en: This character is 命, read ming6, the 命 in 生命 (life); it also means destiny or fate, and even a command or instruction. Look at its shape: a pointed roof 𠆢 sits on top, and underneath it hides a mouth 口 with a short horizontal stroke and a vertical hook. To type it we first take the head 𠆢, which is a face of the 人 (person) shape, so we press the person key O; then the whole body is broken down using head-second-tail, giving the first stroke 一 as M, the 口 as R, and the vertical hook 中 as L, so the full code is OMRL. Why does the head give only one code? Because a head takes at most two codes, and 𠆢 is a single unit that supplies just O, leaving everything below it to the body under the head-second-tail rule. Remember it this way: pointed person on top gives O, then M, R, L drop down beneath — as if someone under that roof is crying out 救命呀, 'Help, save my life!'
命.zh: 呢個字係「命」，讀 ming6，係「生命」嘅「命」，亦都解命運、天命，仲可以解命令、吩咐。你睇佢個樣：上面一個尖頂「𠆢」，下面藏住一個「口」同埋一劃、一豎。拆嘅時候，我哋先攞字首「𠆢」，佢係「人」嘅一種樣貌，所以打人字 O；跟住成個字身要拆，字身用頭、二、尾嘅取碼法，攞頭一劃「一」打 M，第二個係「口」打 R，最尾攞豎鈎「中」打 L，合埋就係 OMRL。點解字首淨係攞一個碼呢？因為字首最多只攞兩碼，而「𠆢」係一個整體，攞埋 O 就夠喇，跟住嘅嘢全部歸入字身按頭二尾嚟拆。記住個口訣：尖頂人字 O，下面 M、R、L 順住入，好似有人喺尖頂下面大叫「救命呀」！

咀.en: Today we'll learn 咀, read "zeoi2", a character you'll spot all over Hong Kong place names like 尖沙咀 (Tsim Sha Tsui) and 大角咀 (Tai Kok Tsui); on its own it means to suck or to chew. Notice it splits left and right: the left side is 口, which sits on the R key, and the right side is the body 且. Because Cangjie divides a character into a prefix and a body, the prefix 口 gives just its one code R, while the body 且 takes only its head and tail — the head 月 on B, and the bottom stroke 一 on M — so the full code is RBM. To lock it in, picture a mouth (口) chewing away, biting first (月) then swallowing down to that final line (一), and R, B, M will come easily.
咀.zh: 今日我哋學「咀」呢個字，讀「zeoi2」，喺香港嘅地名度成日見到，好似「尖沙咀」同「大角咀」咁，佢本身嘅意思係吮、咀嚼。你留意佢係左右兩邊嘅結構：左邊係個「口」字，喺鍵盤上面撳R；右邊嘅字身係「且」字。因為倉頡拆字要分字首同字身，個「口」做字首淨係取R一碼，而字身「且」就要取頭同尾兩碼——頭係「月」，撳B，尾係最底嗰橫「一」，撳M，所以連埋一齊就係RBM。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成「一個口喺度食嘢，先咬（月）後吞落一（一）條線」，咁就好易記住R、B、M三個字啦。

咁.en: Today we learn a very Cantonese little word: 咁, read gam3, the one in 咁多 (so much) and 冇咁 (not so much) — it means "like this" or "to such an extent." Look at its shape: on the left sits a mouth 口, and on the right sits 甘, so this is a left-right character, which tells you the 字首 is that left piece 口, and 口 lives on the R key. Then comes the 字身 on the right, 甘, and because it's the 字身 you don't take every stroke — you follow the head-and-tail rule, grabbing its opening piece 廿 (the T key) and its final stroke 一 (the M key). Put it all in typing order and you get R, T, M. The memory hook: mouth speaks first (R), then 甘 offers only its head 廿 and its tail 一, so "點解你咁開心？" types out cleanly every time.
咁.zh: 今日我哋學個好地道嘅廣東話字：咁，讀做 gam3，即係「咁樣」、「咁多」嗰個咁，形容到咁上下、去到某個程度嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣，左邊係個口字口，右邊係個甘字，係一個左右並排嘅結構，所以拆碼嘅時候，字首就攞左邊個口，個口喺鍵盤上面對應 R。跟住嚟到右邊嘅字身甘，因為佢係字身，唔會逐筆全部攞，而係跟「頭同尾」嘅規矩，先攞佢起首嗰個廿字（對應 T），再攞佢最後嗰橫一（對應 M），所以成隻字合埋就係 R、T、M。記住呢個口訣：口先講，甘就淨係要頭嘅廿同尾嘅一，咁樣你打「點解你咁開心？」就一定唔會撳錯。

和.en: Today we learn 和, read "wo4", meaning harmony, peace, or calm — like when you say two people are friendly and get along. Look at it: on the left is 禾 (grain), and on the right is 口 (mouth). Cangjie splits it neatly at that boundary: the left 禾 is the head, and because it's a fuller shape we don't spell out every stroke — we take just its first and last pieces, ⺮ (H) and 木 (D); then the right 口 (R) is the body, taking one code. Put together that gives HDR, exactly three codes. Remember it this way: a stalk of grain (⺮木) standing next to a mouth (口) speaking peaceful words — that's 和!
和.zh: 今日我哋學「和」呢個字，讀「wo4」，意思係和平、和諧、平靜，好似你成日講嘅「和氣」咁。你望吓佢，左邊係一個「禾」字，右邊係一個「口」字。倉頡就係咁樣拆嘅：左邊嘅「禾」做字首，佢係一個複雜嘅字，唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取頭尾兩個碼——頭係「⺮」（H），尾係「木」（D）；跟住右邊嘅「口」（R）做字身，取一個碼。所以成個字排出嚟就係 HDR，剛好三個碼。記住喇：禾苗（⺮木）旁邊有把口（口）喺度講和氣說話，咁就係「和」！

咖.en: Today's character is 咖, read gaa3 or kaa1, a phonetic-borrowing character you'll meet most often in the loanword 咖啡, coffee. Look at it: there's a 口 on the left and 加 on the right, a classic left-right structure. When you split it, the prefix is that left-hand 口, which gives R and takes just one code; then the body is 加 on the right, and because it stands as one whole part it follows the head-second-tail rule for a continuous body — head 大 is K, second 匚 is S, and the tail 口 is R, so the full code strings together as RKSR. Notice that both the prefix 口 and the body's tail 口 are R, bracketing the KS in the middle — picture sipping 咖啡 one mouthful (口) at a time, front and back, and RKSR will stick.
咖.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「咖」，讀「gaa3」或者「kaa1」，係一個借聲嘅字，最常見就係「咖啡」呢個外來詞。你望吓佢，左邊有個「口」，右邊係「加」，係典型嘅左右結構。拆碼嘅時候，字首係左邊個「口」，取R一個碼；跟住字身係右邊嘅「加」，因為佢自成一個部分，就照連續字身嘅規矩取頭、次、尾三碼——頭係「大」K，次係「匚」S，尾係最後嘅「口」R，所以全碼砌埋就係RKSR。你要記住，字首個「口」同字身尾嘅「口」都係R，一頭一尾夾住中間嘅KS，好似「我想飲杯咖啡」咁，一口一口咁飲落去就記得咯。

咗.en: Today we learn the character 咗, read "zo2". It's one of the most common Cantonese particles, sitting after a verb to show the action is finished — like in 食咗 (have eaten) or 去咗 (have gone). Take a look at its shape: on the left is a 口 (mouth), and on the right is the character 左, and together they form 咗. When Cangjie breaks it down, the 口 on the left is the 字首 (leading part), coded R; then the 左 on the right is the 字身 (body), and a body doesn't take every stroke — it takes only its head and tail. The head is ナ, typed as K, and the tail is 一, typed as M, so the full code is RKM. Here's your hook: a 口 opens it (R), and the 左 gives just its head and tail (K, M) — think 食咗飯, and you'll remember RKM.
咗.zh: 我哋今日學嘅係「咗」呢個字，讀「zo2」，係廣東話最常用嘅助詞之一，擺喺動詞後面表示動作已經做完，好似「食咗」、「去咗」噉。你望下佢個樣，左邊係一個「口」字，右邊係一個「左」字，砌埋一齊就係「咗」。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，個「口」係字首，取碼R；跟住個「左」係字身，字身唔會逐畫取晒，而係取頭尾——頭嗰部分係「ナ」，喺鍵盤上打K，尾嗰部分係「一」，打M，所以全碼就係 RKM。記住喇：左邊有把「口」開頭（R），右邊嘅「左」淨係取頭尾兩件（K、M），一講到食咗飯，你就記得個 RKM。

咩.en: Today we learn 咩, read me1 — one of the most Cantonese characters there is, a little question particle you hear in 「係咩?」(really?) and 「做咩?」(what's up?), and it originally meant the bleating of a sheep too. Look at it: on the left is 口, a mouth, and on the right is really the character 羊, a sheep — a mouth beside a sheep, which fits its meaning nicely. To code it, the left 口 becomes the head and you press R; the right 羊 becomes the body, but a body may contribute at most three codes, and since 羊 is a single self-contained shape, you take it head-and-tail — its top 廿 (T) and its bottom 手 (Q). So the whole thing is 口廿手, that is RTQ. Remember it like this: one mouth, one sheep, and from the sheep grab only its head and tail, 廿 and 手 — and that's how you'd type 你講咩話呀?
咩.zh: 今日我哋學「咩」呢個字，讀 me1，係我哋廣東話最貼身嘅一個字啦，做疑問語氣詞，好似「係咩？」「做咩？」咁，本來仲有羊叫嘅意思添。你望下佢：左邊係個「口」字，右邊其實係個「羊」字，一個口配一隻羊，好夾嘛。拆碼嘅時候，左邊個「口」做字首，敲 R；右邊個「羊」做字身，但係倉頡規定一個字身最多淨係取三碼，而「羊」係一個獨立部件，所以要用「頭尾」取法——取佢個頭同個尾，就係「廿」T 加「手」Q。所以成個字係 口廿手，即係 RTQ。記住呢句：一個口，一隻羊，羊淨係取頭尾廿同手，「你講咩話呀？」就係咁講出嚟。

咪.en: Today we learn 咪, a character with lots of uses in Cantonese: it can mean "don't," as in 咪郁我啲嘢 (don't touch my stuff), it can be the sound a cat makes, and it also appears in words like "meter." Look at the shape: on the left is the mouth radical 口, and on the right is 米, the character for rice. In Cangjie, the left 口 is the head, and a head normally gives up just one code, so we take only R from it; the right side 米 is the body, and a body takes its first and last pieces, which are 火 (F) at the top and 木 (D) at the bottom. Put them together and you get 口 R, 火 F, 木 D — the full code RFD. Here's your memory hook: a mouth R barking "don't!" comes first, and the rice 米, wrapping fire and wood, follows behind.
咪.zh: 今日我哋學「咪」呢個字，佢喺廣東話入面用途好廣：可以係「唔好」嘅意思，好似「咪郁我啲嘢」咁樣叫人唔好掂；又可以係貓叫聲，仲可以指「咪錶」個「咪」。你睇睇個字，左邊係一個「口」字部，右邊就係一個「米」字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊「口」係字首，字首通常淨係取一個碼，所以我哋只攞「口」嘅R；跟住右邊「米」係字身，字身要取頭尾，頭係「火」F、尾係「木」D，所以合埋就係口R、火F、木D，即係RFD。記住喇：一把口R叫你唔好郁，你可以諗「咪郁」嗰陣把口喺前面，米字包住火同木喺後面！

品.en: Today we learn 品, read ban2, meaning an article, a product, or a commodity — you see it in words like 作品 zok3 ban2, a work or opus, and 甜品 tim4 ban2, a dessert. Look at its shape: it's simply three 口 stacked together, one on top and two below, like a little pile of goods. Each 口 is the key R in Cangjie, so all you need to remember is that one familiar piece. Cangjie normally takes at most five codes and, when there are many pieces, it grabs the head, the second, and the tail — but 品 has exactly three 口, no more and no less, so you take all three and type RRR. Remember it this way: three mouths piled into a heap of goods, and you tap R, R, R in one breath!
品.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「品」，讀做 ban2，即係物品、產品嘅意思，好似「作品」zok3 ban2 或者「甜品」tim4 ban2 咁。你望下呢個字嘅樣，其實就係三個「口」砌埋一齊，一個喺上面、兩個喺下面，好似一堆貨物疊起咁。每一個「口」都係倉頡入面嘅 R 鍵，所以你只要記住「口」呢個部件就夠。倉頡拆碼有個規矩，就係一個字最多取五碼，如果部件太多，就要「取頭二尾」，即係取頭一個、第二個，同埋最尾一個；但「品」啱啱只有三個「口」，唔多唔少，所以三個都取齊，打 RRR。記住喇：三個口疊成一堆貨，R、R、R 一口氣打晒！

哋.en: Today we're learning 哋, read dei6, and you'll know it instantly — it's the 哋 in 我哋 (we) and 佢哋 (they), the Cantonese marker for plurals. Take a look: on the left sits a mouth, 口, and on the right is really the character 地. Cangjie reads left to right, so the left 口 becomes the head and gives you R. Then the right-hand 地 acts as the body, and for a body we take first-two-last, so we grab 土 as G, then the little 匕 as P, and finally 木 as D — giving the full code RGPD. Just remember the mouth leads on the left, and 地 unfolds neatly toward its last piece, and you won't mix them up.
哋.zh: 今日我哋學嘅呢個字係「哋」，讀做 dei6，你一定好熟——「我哋」、「佢哋」嘅「哋」，係廣東話用嚟表示複數嘅字。你望下佢，左邊係個口字，右邊其實係個「地」字。倉頡拆字係由左至右，所以先取左邊嘅口字首，個口就係 R 鍵。跟住輪到右邊個「地」，佢做字身，取頭二尾三碼：頭嗰個土係 G，第二個係個匕字 P，最尾個係木 D，合埋成 RGPD。記住個口喺左邊做頭，右邊個地慢慢拆落去尾，你就唔會撈亂喇。

員.en: Today we learn 員, read jyun4, meaning a member or staff person — one individual within an organisation. Look at its structure: a 口 sits on top and a 貝 sits underneath, stacked top over bottom. The top 口 is the head of the character, nice and simple — a single mouth shape, coded R. The bottom 貝 is the body, and on its own it codes as BUC, meaning we take its first, second, and last pieces: the first is 月 giving B, the second is 金 giving U, and the last is 八 giving C. Put it all together and the character is R, B, U, C. Picture it this way: a 口 standing at the front atop 貝, like a member leading the line — 口 R carrying 貝 BUC, so 員 is RBUC.
員.zh: 我哋今日學「員」字，讀作 jyun4，即係成員、職員嘅意思，一個組織入面嘅一分子。你望下佢嘅結構：上面一個「口」，下面一個「貝」，係上下相疊咁砌成。上面嘅「口」係字首，好簡單，一個口字，取 R。下面嘅「貝」就係字身，佢自己嘅碼係 BUC，即係取佢嘅頭、二、尾三個部件：頭係「月」取 B，第二個係「金」取 U，最尾係「八」取 C。所以成隻字合埋就係 R、B、U、C。記住呢個畫面：一個「口」坐喺「貝」上面，就好似一個成員企喺隊伍最前，口 R 帶住貝 BUC，「員」就係 RBUC。

哥.en: Today's character is 哥, read go1, and it means elder brother. Take a look and you'll see it's really two 可 shapes stacked one on top of the other. In Cangjie we start with the prefix, the upper 可, which is built from 一 and 口 — 一 gives its head M (a single flat stroke laid down), and 口 gives its tail R, so the prefix contributes M and R; then we drop to the body, the lower 可, made of 弓 which is N and 口 which is R, giving N and R. Put together that's MRNR: the prefix takes head and tail, and the body is spelled out with its two key pieces, a very typical way of handling a top-bottom character in Cangjie. Remember it through 哥哥, the affectionate nickname of the late singer Leslie Cheung — two 可 shapes climbing up, one flat stroke, two mouths and a bow, and MRNR sticks.
哥.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「哥」，讀做 go1，意思就係大佬、兄長。你望吓佢，其實係上下兩個「可」字疊埋一齊。倉頡拆字嘅時候，我哋先睇字首，即係上面嗰個「可」——佢由「一」同「口」砌成，「一」取頭係 M（一橫平放），「口」取尾係 R，所以字首係 M、R；跟住落到字身，即係下面嗰個「可」，佢由「弓」同「口」組成，「弓」係 N、「口」係 R，所以字身取 N、R。合埋就係 MRNR，字首取頭尾、字身照樣拆出關鍵兩碼，係倉頡好典型嘅上下結構做法。你可以諗吓「哥哥」——即係張國榮嘅暱稱，兩個「可」疊高高，一橫兩口再加一弓，MRNR 就記得實嗮。

唔.en: Today we're learning 唔, read m4, which is the most common negation word in Cantonese — you see it in phrases like 唔係 (m4 hai6, no/not) and 唔會 (m4 wui2, would not), as in 我唔想去 (I don't want to go). This character has a 口 on the left and 吾 on the right, and we split it between them. The left 口 is the 字首, coded on its own as R. The right side 吾 is the 字身, and for a 字身 Cangjie takes head, second, and tail — so from the 五 on top we take its opening 一 (M), then the middle 一 (M) of 五, and finally the 口 underneath (R). Put it all together and you get RMMR. Here's your memory hook: a mouth opens, two flat strokes sit between, and a mouth closes — R, M, M, R, two mouths hugging two lines.
唔.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「唔」字，讀 m4，係我哋廣東話最常用嘅否定詞，好似「唔係」（m4 hai6）、「唔會」（m4 wui2）咁，例如「我唔想去。」呢個字左邊係一個「口」，右邊係「吾」，我哋要分開嚟拆。左邊嘅「口」係字首，佢單獨取碼，就係 R。右邊嘅「吾」係字身，倉頡拆字身嘅時候係取頭、二、尾三部分，所以「吾」上面嘅「五」我哋淨係取佢頭一筆嘅「一」（M），再取「五」中間嗰筆「一」（M），最後取下面嘅「口」（R）。合埋一齊就係 RMMR。記住嘅竅門：一個口起頭，兩橫夾住，再一個口收尾——R、M、M、R，兩口夾兩橫。

商.en: Today we're learning 商, read soeng1, meaning commerce, business, or trade — you'll see it in words like 商場 soeng1 coeng4, a shopping mall, and 商業 soeng1 jip6, business. Look at the shape: up top there's a little hat, the piece 亠 on the Y key, and tucked under it sits 八 on C; below that comes the wrapping frame 冂 on B, and hiding right inside it is a mouth 口 on R. To break the code we split the character into a head and a body: the head is the upper 立 shape, and Cangjie takes its first and last pieces, 亠 (Y) then 八 (C), while the body below also gives its first and last, the outer frame 冂 (B) then the inner 口 (R), which is why the full code is YCBR. Keep that rhythm in mind — head first-and-last, body first-and-last — and picture a little hat covering a mouth (亠八冂口, Y-C-B-R), and 商 will stick with you every time you see a shop sign.
商.zh: 今日我哋學「商」字，讀做 soeng1，意思係商業、貿易、做生意，好似「商場」soeng1 coeng4 同「商業」soeng1 jip6 都用到佢。你望住個字，上面有一頂帽仔咁嘅「亠」，跟住裡面有個「八」，再落去係包圍住嘅「冂」，最入面藏住一個「口」。拆碼嘅時候，我哋將個字分做字首同字身：字首係上半嘅「立」形，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，頭係「亠」Y、尾係「八」C；字身就係下半，同樣取頭尾，頭係外框「冂」B、尾係入面嘅「口」R，所以整個字合埋就係 YCBR。記住字首字身各取頭尾呢個口訣，你就唔會亂晒——「亠八冂口」（Y、C、B、R），一頂帽罩住一個口，就係商店嘅「商」啦。

啊.en: Look at 啊, the little exclamatory particle we tag onto the end of a sentence, read "aa3" — the friendly trailing sound in "你好啊," Hello! The character splits left and right: the mouth 口 on the left is the 字首, and the 阿 on the right is the 字身. The 字首 is easy — the mouth 口 gives you R and that one code is done; for the 字身 阿, because it is itself a full-bodied character, Cangjie takes it head-second-tail, grabbing the head 乙 N, then the middle 中 L, then the tail mouth 口 R. Put together with the opening mouth, the full code is RNLR. Remember it as a mouth at each end — one 口 opening the sound at the front, one 口 closing it at the back, with 乙 and 中 sandwiched between.
啊.zh: 你睇下「啊」呢個字，佢係我哋講嘢成日尾巴帶住嘅語氣助詞，讀「aa3」，好似「你好啊」嗰個親切嘅尾音。整個字分做左右兩邊：左邊個口係字首，右邊個「阿」係字身。字首好簡單，個口 R 就攞咗佢，一碼搞掂；到咗字身「阿」，因為佢自己都係一個有頭有尾嘅字，倉頡就用頭二尾嘅方法拆佢，先攞頭嘅乙 N，跟住中間嘅中 L，最後個尾嘅口 R，所以個「阝」拆成 N、L，加埋尾嘅口，合埋成 RNLR。記住呢個口頭口尾嘅樣：一個口喺前面開聲，一個口喺後面收音，中間夾住乙同中，就係「啊」喇！

問.en: Today we learn 問, read man6, meaning to ask or to inquire — when you want to know something, you open your mouth and ask. Look at its structure: on the outside is a 門 gate frame that wraps around a 口 mouth sitting inside it. This is an enclosing whole-form character, so Cangjie takes it by head, second, and tail — the first, second, and last pieces — which gives you A (日), N (弓), and R (口), spelling ANR. Notice that the 門 frame supplies the head and second pieces as A (日) and N (弓), while the trapped 口 inside becomes R, the tail. Remember it as a gate — A, N — shutting a mouth R inside, so 問 is ANR.
問.zh: 今日我哋學「問」呢個字，讀 man6，即係「發問」、「查問」嘅意思，你想知道啲乜嘢，就開口問人。你望住佢嘅結構：外面係一個「門」框，將裏面嘅「口」包住咗。呢個字係一個包圍嘅整體字，倉頡拆碼嘅時候會用「頭、二、尾」嘅取法，即係取起首、第二，同埋最尾三個部件，所以你打嘅係 A（日）、N（弓）、R（口），合埋就係 ANR。留意「門」框係由 A（日）同 N（弓）呢兩個部件砌成頭同二，最後個 R（口）就係困喺入面嘅字身，做尾碼。記住個口訣：一道門 A、N，關住個 R 口喺入面，打 ANR 就係問。

啟.en: Today's character is 啟, read kai2, meaning "to open" or "to begin" — as in 啟業, opening for business. Look at how it's built: it's a left-right character, with 启 on the left and 攵 on the right. When Cangjie splits it, the left-hand head 启 isn't typed whole; instead we take its first and last shapes — since 启 has the code ISR, its first is H (the slanting stroke) and its last is R (the 口), giving us HR. The right-hand body 攵 is a familiar component whose own code is OK, and we take its first and last too, O and K, so the full character spells HROK. Remember it this way: hold the 口 R on the left, lean the OK 攵 on the right, and you've got 啟.
啟.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「啟」，讀作 kai2，即係「打開」或者「開始」嘅意思，好似「啟業」咁講就係開張做生意。你望下佢嘅結構，係左右兩邊：左邊係「启」，右邊係一個「攵」。倉頡拆字嗰陣，左邊嘅字首「启」唔會成隻打出嚟，而係取佢個「頭」同「尾」——「启」自己嘅碼係 ISR，所以頭係 H（斜），尾係 R（口），得出 HR；右邊嘅字身「攵」係一個常見部件，自己碼係 OK，同樣取頭尾 O 同 K，於是全字砌成 HROK。你記住：左邊揸住個「口」R，右邊靠住個 OK 嘅「攵」，就係「啟」喇。

啡.en: Today we meet 啡, the character you'll spot in the loanword 咖啡, read fe1. Look at its shape: there's a 口 mouth on the left and 非 on the right, so the whole character splits into a head and a body. The head is that left-side 口, keyed as R; then the 非 on the right becomes the body, and because a body can give at most three codes, we don't spell out every stroke — instead we take its head, its second piece, and its last piece. From 非 we take the vertical 丨 (L), then 一 (M), then 卜 (Y), three codes exactly, giving the full code RLMY. Here's your hook: a 口 mouth on the left is sipping something from the 非 on the right — your morning cup of coffee, 啡!
啡.zh: 今日我哋學「啡」呢個字，佢最常見喺「咖啡」呢個借字入面，讀 fe1。你望下佢嘅結構：左邊係一個「口」字，右邊係一個「非」字，成個字先拆做字首同字身兩橛。字首就係左邊嘅「口」，取碼 R；跟住輪到右邊嘅「非」做字身，而字身最多只可以取三碼，所以我哋唔會逐筆逐筆拆晒，而係取頭、取二、取尾——「非」嘅頭係一豎「丨」（L），第二個碼取「一」（M），最尾就取「卜」（Y），三碼啱啱好。所以成個字打 RLMY。記住呢個口訣：一個「口」講嘢，右邊「非」字要飲杯 coffee——你朝早飲杯咖啡，就係「啡」喇！

啦.en: Today we learn 啦, read "laa1" or "la1", the little particle you tack onto the end of a sentence to assert something or nudge someone along, as in 好啦 or 走啦. Look at it: on the left sits a 口 (mouth), and on the right is the character 拉 built up piece by piece. In Cangjie the head, 口, gives just one code, R; then the body 拉 must hand over three codes — its first piece 扌 is Q, the middle 卜 is Y, and the tail 廿 is T, giving you the full code RQYT. Why does the body split into Q, Y, T like that? Because when a body has several pieces it follows the first-middle-last rule and surrenders exactly three codes, not one for each part. Picture a mouth speaking up first (口), then a hand (扌) pulling the words along — say "走啦" and it sticks.
啦.zh: 今日我哋學「啦」呢個字，讀「laa1」或者「la1」，係我哋講嘢時尾嗰個語氣字，好似「好啦」、「走啦」咁，帶住肯定同催促嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係個「口」字，右邊就係一個「拉」字砌埋一齊。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，字首「口」取一個碼 R；跟住字身「拉」要交足三個碼，取頭「扌」係 Q、中間個「卜」係 Y、最尾「廿」係 T，所以成個字碼就係 RQYT。點解字身要 Q、Y、T 咁樣頭、次、尾咁取？因為字身唔止一件，就要跟「頭、中、尾」嘅規矩取三碼，唔可以個個都取。記住個口喺前面開聲，跟住一隻手（扌）拉住，講句「走啦」就得。

啲.en: Today we're learning 啲, read di1, a word you use all the time in Cantonese meaning 'a few' or 'a little bit,' as in 我想食多啲飯 — 'I want to eat a bit more rice.' Look at the shape: on the left is the mouth radical 口, and on the right is the whole 的 element. To break it down, the left 口 is the head, so we take 口, which lives on the R key. The right side 的 is the body, and Cangjie has a rule for a body that needs more than two codes: you take the first, the second, and the last piece — so from the right we take 竹 (H), then 日 (A), and finally 戈 (I) at the very end, giving RHAI. Here's your memory hook: one mouth on the left, then three strokes on the right — 竹, 日, 戈 — and you've spelled 啲.
啲.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「啲」，讀做 di1，係我哋廣東話成日用嘅字，意思係「一些、少少」，好似「我想食多啲飯」入面咁。你望下呢個字，左邊係個口字，右邊係「的」字。開始拆碼，左邊嘅口字係字首，我哋取「口」，個鍵係 R。右邊嘅「的」係字身，倉頡拆字身有個規矩：如果唔止兩碼，就要取頭、次、尾三個字碼，所以我哋喺右邊順序取「竹」（H）、「日」（A），再取最尾嘅「戈」（I），合埋就係 RHAI。記住呢個字嘅竅門：左邊一個口，右邊三筆竹、日、戈，一路寫落去就係「啲」啦。

喇.en: Today's character is 喇, which you'll recognise best as the sentence-final particle in Cantonese, as in 我食完飯喇。 (I've finished eating), read laa3, laa1 and so on. Notice it's a left-right character: on the left sits the 口 mouth radical, and on the right stands 剌. For the code the 字首 is that left-hand 口, giving R; then the 字身 剌 follows the head-2nd-tail rule, so you take its first piece, its second piece, and skip to its very last piece — 木 D, 中 L, and the final 弓 (the standing knife 刂) N. Put together that gives you exactly RDLN. Memory hook: one mouth R leads the way, then the three bits of 剌 (DLN) trail behind — 喇!
喇.zh: 今日學嘅字係「喇」，喺廣東話入面你最熟嘅就係做句尾嘅語氣助詞，好似「我食完飯喇。」咁樣，讀 laa3、laa1 等音。你留意佢係左右兩份：左邊係個「口」字部，右邊係個「剌」字。拆碼嘅時候，字首就係左邊嘅口，取 R；跟住嘅字身「剌」要跟「頭二尾」嘅規矩，即係取頭一碼、第二碼，再跳去取最尾一碼，所以喺剌入面攞到木 D、中 L，同埋最尾嗰個弓（即係企刀刂）N，合埋就係 RDLN。記住喇：一個口 R 帶住一嚿剌 DLN，講完飯就講「喇」！

喎.en: Today we learn 喎, read wo3, one of Cantonese's most expressive final particles — it marks reported speech, surprise, or contradiction, as in 係喎 (Oh, right!) or 冇喎. Look at its shape: on the left sits the familiar mouth radical 口, and on the right is the component 咼. Here's how Cangjie splits it: the left 口 is the one-code head, living on the R key, so it gives just R; then the right-hand 咼 acts as the body, and following the writing order we take its first ⺆ (B), its second ⺆ (B), and finally the 口 (R). Because a body only takes its first, second, and last codes, anything in the middle is simply skipped over — that's why we land on RBBR. Memory hook: one mouth on the left, and the 咼 on the right with its two little ⺆ frames wrapping a mouth, spilling out the sound 喎!
喎.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「喎」，讀作 wo3，係廣東話最傳神嘅語氣助詞之一，用嚟表示轉述、意外或者反駁，好似「係喎」、「冇喎」噉。你望下佢個形，左邊係熟悉嘅「口」部，右邊就係「咼」字。倉頡點拆呢？左邊個「口」做字首，佢係鍵盤 R 位，取一碼；跟住右邊嘅「咼」做字身，順住寫落去取頭一個「⺆」（B）、第二個「⺆」（B），最後係個「口」（R）——因為字身淨係取頭、二、尾三碼，所以中間嘅嘢就跳過唔取。合埋就係 RBBR。記法好簡單：一個口喺左，右邊嘅咼有兩個「⺆」夾住個口，講嘢一口口噉爆出「喎」！

喜.en: Today we learn 喜, read hei2, meaning to like, love or enjoy — a joyful thing, as in 喜悅 (joy) and 驚喜 (a pleasant surprise). Notice it stacks in two layers: on top sits a component called 壴, and underneath sits a 口, a mouth shape. The 壴 is the head, and a head takes at most three codes, so instead of picking it apart stroke by stroke we read its own code from front to back — 壴's own code is GRT, so we type 土 (G), 口 (R), then 廿 (T). What follows is the body, the lower 口, and the last piece of the body usually gives just one code, so we add one more 口 (R), making the full code GRTR. Remember the hook: one 壴 for the head-and-tail three codes, then one 口 to close — that's how joy is built.
喜.zh: 今日我哋學「喜」字，讀做 hei2，係歡喜、鍾意嘅意思，好似「喜悅」（歡樂）同「驚喜」咁樣。你留意佢係上下兩截砌成：上面係一個叫「壴」嘅組件，下面係一個「口」。個「壴」係字首，字首最多得三碼，所以我哋唔會逐筆逐筆拆佢，而係喺佢自己嘅碼度取頭尾——「壴」自己嘅碼係 GRT，頭尾加中間就係 GRT，所以順住打土（G）、口（R）、廿（T）。跟住落嚟嘅字身係下面個「口」，字身最尾嗰個組件通常淨取一碼，所以再打多一個口（R）就夠，全碼合埋就係 GRTR。記住個口訣：一個「壴」拆頭尾三碼，再落多一個口埋尾，開心就係咁砌出嚟。

單.en: Today's character is 單, read daan1, meaning single, individual, or only — as in 簡單 gaan2 daan1, meaning simple and not complicated, or 唔單止 m4 daan1 zi2, meaning not only. Look at the shape: two little squares up top, a horizontal line in the middle, and more strokes below — it looks busy and complicated, doesn't it? Cangjie handles it as a whole-character (整體字), taking head, second, third, and last: the two 口 (口=R, 口=R) first, then the 田 in the middle (田=W), and then it skips ahead and grabs the 十 at the very end (十=J), giving you RRWJ. The reason for the skip is that 單 is one tightly-knit unified shape that doesn't split cleanly into a top-part and a body, so Cangjie uses the head-2nd-3rd-last rule instead of pulling out every piece. Remember it this way: two 口, one 田, skip the middle and take the last 十 — and 單 appears, as in 呢張單好貴呀.
