單.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「單」，讀做 daan1，意思係單一、獨個、只得一個，好似「簡單」gaan2 daan1 咁，即係唔複雜；又或者「唔單止」m4 daan1 zi2，即係唔止咁。你望下個字，上面兩個細細嘅方形，中間一橫，下面再有嘢——係咪覺得筆畫好多好複雜？倉頡就係用「整體字」嘅辦法拆佢：頭、二、三、尾咁樣取，先取兩個口（口=R、口=R），再取中間嘅田（田=W），跟住跳過中間唔取，最後喺尾攞返個十（十=J），所以成個碼係 RRWJ。點解要跳呢？因為「單」係一個好整齊、成舊一齊嘅整體字，唔會一分為二做字首字身，倉頡對呢種字就用頭二三尾去取，唔會逐格全部拆晒。記住個口訣：兩個口、一個田，跳過中間攞尾十，「單」就打得出——「呢張單好貴呀。」

喺.en: Today we're learning 喺, read hai2 in Cantonese — this is the word you use to say where something is located, like 喺屋企 (at home) or 喺邊度 (where). Take a look: on the left there's a 口 mouth radical, and on the right sits the character 係. When we split it, the 口 (R) on the far left becomes the 字首, the leading part, because it stands alone on the left; then the 係 on the right becomes the 字身, the body. For the body we take head, second, and tail — that's 亻 (O) as the head, 竹 (H) as the second, and 火 (F) as the tail — giving us R-O-H-F, ROHF. Remember: one code for the head-part, then three for the body, four in all. A little hook: picture that 口 mouth asking you 喺唔喺 — 'are you here?'
喺.zh: 今日我哋學「喺」呢個字，粵音讀 hai2，係我哋廣東話講「喺邊度」、「喺屋企」嗰個「喺」，即係表示某樣嘢喺某個位置。你望下呢個字，左邊係一個「口」字部，右邊係「係」字。拆字嘅時候，左邊嘅「口（R）」做字首，因為佢喺最左邊；跟住右邊嘅「係」做字身，而字身要取頭、二、尾，即係「亻（O）」做頭、「竹（H）」做二、「火（F）」做尾，串埋一齊就係 ROHF。記住個口訣：字首淨係一個口，字身取頭二尾三碼，加埋啱啱四碼。你可以咁記：一個口「喺」度出聲，問你「喺唔喺呢度」呀！

嗰.en: Today we learn 嗰, read go2 — this is the Cantonese word for 'that', as in 嗰個 (that one) or 嗰啲 (those), pointing to something over there. Look at it: on the left sits a mouth 口, and on the right is the character 個, so the whole thing reads in a very colloquial, spoken way. The Cangjie split works like this: the head is the left-side 口, coded R; the body is the right-side 個, and because the body has several parts, we follow the head-then-last-two rule, taking the head 人 (O) and then its final two codes 囗 (W) and 口 (R), giving OWR. Put together the full code is R, O, W, R — that is ROWR. Remember it this way: a mouth 口 speaks first, then 個 folds in from both ends, and you have the word you use to point at 'that one' across the room.
嗰.zh: 今日我哋學「嗰」呢個字，讀 go2，係廣東話「嗰個」、「嗰啲」嘅「嗰」，即係指遠嗰邊嗰件嘢，英文嘅 that。你睇下佢，左邊係個口字，右邊係「個」字，成個字讀落好口語化。倉頡拆法係咁：字首係左邊嘅「口」，取碼 R；字身係右邊嘅「個」，因為字身唔止一個部件，就要跟「拆頭二尾」嘅規矩，取頭「人」O、再取埋尾嗰兩碼「囗」W同「口」R，砌埋一齊就係 OWR。所以成個字碼係 R、O、W、R，即 ROWR。記住喇：一個「口」開頭講嘢，跟住個「個」字兩頭夾埋，就係你指遠處嘅「嗰個」。

嘅.en: Today we're learning 嘅, read ge3, one of the most common words in spoken Cantonese, used to show possession — like 佢嘅, meaning belonging to him. Look at the shape: on the left is a 口, and on the right is 既, so this is a left-right structure. The left 口 is the 字首, and it's simple, taking just one code, R; the right 既 is the 字身, which takes head, second, and tail, three codes in all. The full code for 既 on its own is AIMVU, so from inside it we pick the head 日 as A, the second 厶 as I, and the tail 山 as U, skipping the middle pieces. Put it all together and the whole character is R, A, I, U — 口 R, 日 A, 厶 I, 山 U. Here's your memory hook: the left mouth 口 says one code, and the right 既 grabs its head and tail around the middle, so saying 佢嘅 will help you keep it in mind.
嘅.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「嘅」，讀作 ge3，係廣東話最常用嘅字之一，用嚟表示屬於，好似「佢嘅」意思係屬於佢咁。你望吓個字，左邊係一個「口」，右邊係「既」，係左右兩邊夾埋嘅結構。左邊嘅「口」係字首，佢好簡單，只取一碼 R；右邊嘅「既」係字身，要取頭、二、尾三碼，佢自己嘅完整碼係 AIMVU，所以我哋喺入面揀頭一個「日」係 A、第二個「厶」係 I、最尾嘅「山」係 U，中間嗰啲就跳過唔要。所以成個字砌埋就係 R、A、I、U，即係口 R、日 A、厶 I、山 U。記住呢個口訣：左邊「口」講嘢一碼，右邊「既」頭尾夾中間，講出「佢嘅」就記得晒喇。

嘉.en: Today we learn 嘉, read gaa1, meaning excellent, joyful, or auspicious — the very word in 嘉年華 gaa1 nin4 waa4, a carnival. Look at its shape: on the left sits 壴 and on the right sits 加, and Cangjie splits it along that left-right boundary. The head block 壴 takes its first and last pieces — 士 G at the top and 口 R at the bottom; the body 加 does the same, taking 廿 T first and 口 R last, so the full code comes together as GRTR. A neat way to remember it: 士 G then 口 R, then 廿 T then 口 R — both halves are first-and-last, and the warm little sentence 嘉嘉係我朋友, 'Ka-ka is my friend,' suits this joyful character perfectly.
嘉.zh: 今日我哋學「嘉」字，讀作 gaa1，意思係美好、歡樂、值得讚賞，好似「嘉年華」gaa1 nin4 waa4 咁樣嘅節慶。你望吓佢個結構，左邊係「壴」，右邊係「加」，倉頡就係按呢個左右兩份嚟拆。字首「壴」取頭尾兩碼，開頭係「士」G，收尾係「口」R；字身「加」都係取頭尾，開頭係「廿」T，收尾係「口」R，所以全碼砌埋就係 GRTR。記住一句：一士G一口R，再一廿T一口R，兩份都係「先頭後尾」，「嘉嘉係我朋友」呢句咁溫暖，正正配得起呢個「嘉」字。

嘢.en: Today we learn 嘢, read je5 — a genuine Cantonese colloquial character meaning "thing," the word you use every day in phrases like "buy things" or "eat something." Look at its structure: the mouth 口 sits on the left and 野 sits on the right, so the whole character splits left-and-right. The 字首 takes the left mouth 口, which is R; then the 字身 野 gets broken down, taking its head 田 with W, its second piece 土 with G, and its tail 乚 with N, giving you RWGN together. Why does the 字身 only give three codes? Because Cangjie limits a 字身 to at most head, one-to-two middle, and tail — three codes total — so 野 isn't written stroke by stroke but represented by just 田, 土, and 乚. Remember the mouth leads on the left, and the right runs from 田 down to 乚 — 嘢 is simply the "stuff" you talk about all day long.
嘢.zh: 今日我哋學「嘢」呢個字，讀做 je5，係地地道道嘅廣東話口語字，解作「東西」，好似「買嘢」、「食嘢」咁樣日日都用到。你望吓佢嘅結構：左邊係個「口」字，右邊係「野」字，成個字係左右分開嘅。所以字首取左邊嘅口，撳 R；跟住字身「野」就要拆開，取頭嘅田撳 W，第二個係土撳 G，最後尾嘅乚撳 N，合埋就係 RWGN。點解字身淨係取三碼呢？因為倉頡規定字身最多取頭、一至二、尾共三碼，所以「野」入面唔會逐筆拆晒，只揀田、土、乚呢三個代表。記住個口喺左邊帶頭，右邊由田開始一路寫到乚，「嘢」就係你日常講嘅嗰啲嘢喇。

噉.en: Today we learn 噉, read "gam2," a distinctly Cantonese character meaning "like this" or "in this way" — as in 噉你, "so, you..." Look at it: on the left is the mouth 口, and on the right sits 敢. When we take the code, the head is that left-side 口, keyed R. The body 敢 comes next, and because it is a body rather than a head it follows the first-second-last rule: first 一 (M), second 十 (J), last ナ (K), giving MJK. So the whole thing is RMJK — remember it as "a mouth opens up front, then 敢 gives its first, middle, and last," and you'll have it right just like this.
噉.zh: 今日我哋學「噉」，讀「gam2」，係地道嘅廣東話字，解「噉樣、咁樣」嘅意思，好似「噉你」就係「那你」噉解。你望吓佢，左邊係個「口」字，右邊係個「敢」字。取碼嘅時候，字首就係左邊個「口」，鍵係 R。到咗字身「敢」呢個部分，因為佢唔係字首，所以要跟「頭、次、尾」嘅規矩嚟拆：頭取「一」M，次取「十」J，尾取「ナ」K，合埋就係 MJK。所以成個字打 RMJK；你就記住「口喺前面開口，敢字取頭尾三粒」，噉樣做就啱喇。

嚟.en: This character is 嚟, read lai4, one of the most everyday words in our Cantonese — it means "to come, to arrive," as in 你快啲嚟啦, "come quickly." Look at its shape: on the left sits a 口 (mouth), and on the right is the piece 黎. In Cangjie we take the head first, so 口 gives us R; then the body 黎 has many strokes, so we follow the body rule of first-second-last, taking ⺮ as H, then the next 丿 also as H, and finally the tail 氺 as E. Put together that makes RHHE — remember it as a mouth (口) calling out, inviting someone to "come," with H, H, E carrying them right to you.
嚟.zh: 呢個字係「嚟」，讀 lai4，係我哋廣東話最常用嘅字之一，意思係「來、到」，好似「你快啲嚟啦」咁講。你望下佢個樣，左邊有個「口」字，右邊就係「黎」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，先攞字首個「口」，佢喺鍵盤上係 R；跟住個字身「黎」筆畫多，就照字身取碼嘅規矩攞頭二尾——即係頭嘅「⺮」係 H、跟住嘅「丿」都係 H，最後個尾「氺」係 E。所以四碼合埋就係 RHHE，你可以記住：一個「口」講嘢，招呼人「嚟」啦，H、H、E 三步就到你面前。

囍.en: Look at this character: 囍, read hei2, meaning "double happiness" — you see it everywhere at weddings and on red invitation cards, and it's simply two 喜 characters set side by side. Its Cangjie code is GRGRR, five parts in total. Start with the left 喜: its top is 土 (G) and its bottom is 口 (R), giving you GR; then the right 喜, being the body of the character, uses the head-second-tail method to give GRR — head 土 (G) and the second and last both 口 (R, R). So the whole thing builds up as GR plus GRR, which is GRGRR. Here's your hook: the left 喜 gives two, the right 喜 gives three, earth-and-mouth paired up again — that's the 囍 pasted on the door.
囍.zh: 睇下呢個字：囍，讀作 hei2，意思係「雙喜臨門」，成日喺婚禮、喜帖度見到，係兩個「喜」字並排砌埋一齊。你嘅倉頡碼係 GRGRR，齊齊有五個部分。先睇左邊嗰個「喜」：喜字上面係「土」（G），下面係「口」（R），拆做 GR 兩碼；跟住右邊嗰個「喜」，因為係字身，就用「取頭、次、尾」嘅方法，攞到 GRR——頭係「土」（G），次同尾係兩個「口」（R、R）。所以成隻字砌起嚟就係 GR 加 GRR，即係 GRGRR。記住喇：左喜攞兩碼，右喜攞三碼，土口一對又一對，門上貼個囍字就係咁嚟嘅。

囖.en: This character is 囖, read lo4, a Cantonese final particle you tack on to point out something so obvious it hardly needs saying — like in 係囖, meaning "yeah, obviously." Look at its shape: on the left is a mouth 口, and on the right is the busy character 羅, so the split follows this simple left-right structure. The left 口 is the head, and because it's a self-contained piece it gives just one code, R; then the whole right side 羅 becomes the body, and a body takes its first, second, and last shapes — so you pull the top ⺮ (H), the middle 田 (W), and the bottom 土 (G). Put them together and you get RHWG. Remember it like this: a mouth speaks 係囖, and the 羅 breaks down into ⺮, 田, 土 — obvious, right?
囖.zh: 呢個字係「囖」，讀 lo4，係廣東話嘅語氣助詞，用嚟指出啲明顯到唔使講嘅嘢，好似「係囖」咁，即係「梗係啦」嘅意思。你睇下佢個樣，左邊係一個口字，右邊係個好複雜嘅「羅」字，所以拆法就跟住左右結構嚟做。左邊個口 R 就係字首，佢係一件獨立部件，所以淨係取一碼 R；跟住右邊個「羅」就做字身，字身要取頭、次、尾三碼，於是攞頭嘅⺮ H、中間嘅田 W、同埋最底嘅土 G。合埋就係 RHWG。記住喇：「口講句係囖，羅字拆⺮田土」，講完就明晒。

四.en: Today's character is 四, read sei3, and it simply means the number four — you'll meet it everywhere, in words like 第四 (dai6 sei3, the fourth) or 四十 (sei3 sap6, forty). Look at its shape: there's a big square box 囗 on the outside, and tucked inside it sits a little 八 shape. In Cangjie, 四 is treated as a whole-character, meaning the outer box and its contents are taken together, so we start with the outer square 囗, which lives on the W key, and then reach inside for that 八 shape, which lives on the C key, giving us just WC, two codes exactly. Why so few? Because a whole-character doesn't get broken down piece by piece — the outer frame plus one code for what's inside is enough. Remember it this way: one W box enclosing one C 八 makes a neat, four-square 四.
四.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「四」，讀作 sei3，就係數字四嘅意思，好似「第四」dai6 sei3 或者「四十」sei3 sap6 咁樣，日日都會見到。你望吓佢個樣：外面有個大方框「囗」，入面裝住個「八」形嘅嘢。喺倉頡入面，呢個「四」係一個整體字，即係話個框同入面嘅嘢係一齊拆嘅，所以我哋先由外圍嘅方框「囗」開始，佢喺 W 鍵，再入去打入面嗰個「八」形，佢喺 C 鍵，合埋就係 WC，啱啱兩碼。點解淨係得兩碼咁少呢？因為整體字唔使一味咁拆碎，只要外圍加一個代表內裡嘅字碼就夠喇。你可以咁記：一個 W 框，圍住一個 C 「八」，四四方方就係「四」。

回.en: Today's character is 回, read wui4, meaning to return or turn back, and it can also work as a measure word for counting times or occasions. Look at its shape: it's a big square box with a small mouth sitting right inside it, like one ring wrapped around another. To take it apart we follow the outside-to-inside order: first you write the big outer frame 囗, which lives on the W key, and then the little inner 口, which lives on the R key, so the whole code is simply WR. Why does the split fall there? Because the outer 囗 is the head and the inner 口 is the body, and Cangjie always works from the outer shell inward toward the center. Remember it this way: box first, then fill the middle — W wraps R, and you've got 回. You'll meet it in words like 回應 (wui4 jing3, to respond) and 回想 (wui4 soeng2, to recall), as in "I'm going home now."
回.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「回」，讀做 wui4，意思係返轉頭、返嚟，又可以做量詞，好似講次數噉樣。你望下佢個樣，就係一個大框裡面包住一個細口，好似一個圈套住另一個圈。拆嘅時候，我哋跟由外到內嘅次序：先寫外面個大框囗，佢喺 W 鍵度；跟住寫入面細細個嘅口，佢喺 R 鍵度，所以成個碼就係 WR。點解要噉樣分呢？因為外框囗做字首，入面個口做字身，倉頡就係由外殼開始，一路寫入去中心。你記住：先框住，後填心，W 大框套 R 細口，就係「回」。你可以用喺「回應」（wui4 jing3，回覆嘅意思）同埋「回想」（wui4 soeng2，返轉頭去諗以前嘅事），例如「我而家回家。」

因.en: Today we learn 因, read jan1, the 因 in 原因 and 因為, meaning cause or reason, and also "because of." Look at the shape: a square frame with a 大 sitting inside it—this is an enclosing character, like a box wrapping around what's within. Cangjie has a firm rule here: for enclosing characters you take the outer frame first, then the contents, so the first code is the frame 囗 on the W key, and only then the inner 大 on the K key, giving you WK. Remember it the way you'd write it by hand: draw the box first (囗, W), then fill in the 大 inside (K)—that order spells 因.
因.zh: 我哋今日學「因」，讀做 jan1，即係「原因」、「因為」嘅「因」，解做原因、緣由，又可以解「因為」。你望下呢個字，係一個四四方方嘅框，入面裝住一個「大」字——呢種字叫做包圍字，好似有個盒子將入面嘅嘢圍住咁。倉頡拆字有規矩：包圍字要先寫外面個框，再寫入面嘅嘢，所以我哋第一個碼取外框「囗」，佢喺 W 掣；跟住先取入面嘅「大」，佢喺 K 掣，合埋就係 WK 兩碼。記住：好似寫字咁，一定係先畫個框（囗，W），再喺入面填個「大」（K），呢個順序就係「因」。

國.en: Today we learn 國, read gwok3, meaning a nation or country, as in 國家 gwok3 gaa1 (country) and 美國 mei5 gwok3 (the United States). Look at the character: the outermost part is a big square frame, which is 囗, typed with W on your keyboard. Because 囗 is an enclosing shape, Cangjie has a special rule for it: you take the outer frame first, then whatever sits inside, and only at the very end do you close off the frame's tail. So after the frame you take the inner 戈 (I), then 口 (R), and finally the bottom stroke 一 (M) that closes the box, giving WIRM. Picture the frame as a city wall around its people — you build the inside first and seal the floor last, so remember to save that closing stroke 一 (M) for the very end.
國.zh: 今日我哋學「國」字，讀作 gwok3，意思係國家、國度，好似「國家」gwok3 gaa1 同「美國」mei5 gwok3 呢啲詞咁。你望住個字，最外面係個四四方方嘅框，呢個就係「囗」，喺鍵盤上面撳 W。因為「囗」係一個包圍字，倉頡有一條特別規則：外框要拆開嚟取，先取外框頭，再取入面嘅嘢，最後先至補返外框嘅尾。所以個框入面先取「戈」（I），跟住「口」（R），最後補返框底嗰橫「一」（M），合埋就係 WIRM。記住嗰個框好似一堵城牆，圍住入面嘅百姓，寫完入面先封返個底，你就記得個尾要留返一橫 M 喇。

園.en: Today we learn 園, read jyun4, meaning a garden, a park, or an orchard — a place with plants and trees where people go to relax. Look at the shape: the whole character is wrapped inside a big square border. That border is called 囗, and on your keyboard it's W. Cangjie has a firm rule: when a character has an outer enclosure, you type the enclosure first, then take what's inside — so after W we deal with the 袁 that sits within the frame. Because the inside already counts as one grouped piece, we don't spell out all of 袁 stroke by stroke; instead we take head-second-tail, giving us 土 (G) at the top, 口 (R) in the middle, and 女 (V) at the bottom, which together spell WGRV. Picture it this way: first you build the fence (囗 = W), then inside it, from top to bottom, you plant 土, 口, and 女 — and there's your garden. Say 我哋去公園玩 (we go play at the park), and the 園 in 公園 is exactly this one.
園.zh: 今日我哋學「園」呢個字，讀作 jyun4，意思係花園、公園或者果園，即係種花種樹俾人休息嘅地方。你望吓，成個字外面圍住一個大框，呢個框叫「囗」，喺鍵盤上面打 W。倉頡有條規矩：外面有框嘅字，要先打框，然後再取框入面嘅嘢，所以我哋打完 W 之後，就處理框入面嗰個「袁」字。因為框入面已經算係一個部件，唔使成個袁字逐筆拆晒，我哋用「頭、次、尾」嘅方法取三個碼——最上面嘅「土」打 G，中間嘅「口」打 R，最底嘅「女」打 V，合埋就係 WGRV。記住呢個畫面：先圍好個圍欄（囗＝W），再喺入面由頭到尾種落土、口、女三樣嘢，一個花園就成形喇。你可以講「我哋去公園玩」，comment公園個「園」就係佢。

圖.en: Today's character is 圖, read tou4, meaning a diagram, chart, map or picture — you see it in words like 試圖 (si3 tou4, to attempt) and 圖書館 (tou4 syu1 gun2, library). Look at the shape: there's a big enclosure 囗, keyed W, wrapping everything inside — and with an enclosure, Cangjie always takes that outer frame first as the head, so your first code is 囗W. Now go inside the frame and take first-then-last of what's there: the top 口 keyed R, then 卜 keyed Y, and finally, because the enclosure is a fully closed frame, you add the closing 囗W again, giving you WRYW. Here's the memory hook: one big frame W opens it and one big frame W closes it, hugging 口R and 卜Y in between — like a picture book held shut by covers front and back.
圖.zh: 你今日要學嘅字係「圖」，讀做 tou4，意思係圖畫、地圖、圖表，好似「試圖」（si3 tou4）同「圖書館」（tou4 syu1 gun2）咁樣用。你望下呢個字，最外面有個大方框「囗」，讀 W，包住入面一堆嘢——呢種包圍結構，倉頡就係先取外框做字首，所以第一碼一定係囗W。跟住入到框裏面，就照「頭尾」規則揀，先取最頂嘅「口」R，再取下面嘅「卜」Y，最後因為外框係一個完整嘅包圍框，要補返個收口嘅「囗」W，於是成個碼就砌成 WRYW。你可以咁記：一個大框 W 開頭、一個大框 W 收尾，中間夾住「口 R 卜 Y」，就好似一本圖冊咁前後有硬封面包住。

團.en: Today's character is 團, read tyun4, meaning a sphere, a ball, a lump, or a group — you'll meet it in words like 團隊 (tyun4 deoi2, a team) and 團結 (tyun4 git3, to unite). Look at its shape: on the outside there's a square box, 囗, which sits on the W key; tucked inside that box is 專, and we break it into its strokes, taking 十 on J, then two 戈 shapes, each on I, so the full code comes out as WJII. Why does it split this way? Because 囗 is the enclosing 字首, so we take it first as the opening piece, and everything wrapped inside — the 專 — becomes the 字身, which we read out in order as 十 and then the two 戈, missing nothing. Picture a square wrapper (囗) hugging a bundle inside, with a 十 and a pair of 戈 戈 folded within, and you've got 團 — just like kneading round glutinous rice balls together into one wrapped lump.
團.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「團」，讀作 tyun4，本身解作圓球、一團嘢，或者一堆、一團體，好似「團隊」（tyun4 deoi2）同「團結」（tyun4 git3）咁樣用。你睇下佢個形，最外面有個四四方方嘅框，就係「囗」，佢喺鍵盤上面撳 W；框裏面藏住一個「專」字，我哋要拆佢入面嘅筆畫，先取「十」，撳 J，再取兩個「戈」，撳兩次 I，所以成個字打出嚟就係 WJII。點解要咁拆呢？因為「囗」係個包住成個字嘅字首，先取佢做開頭，跟住裏面被包住嘅「專」就係字身，字身順住取「十」同埋兩個「戈」，一個都唔漏。你可以記住：一個方框（囗）包住一團嘢，裏面「十」字加兩劃「戈戈」，就砌成呢個「團」——正如「我哋一齊搓湯圓團」咁，圓圓一團被包喺一齊。

土.en: Today's character is 土, read tou2, meaning soil, earth, or things made of earth. Look at its shape: a flat horizontal stroke on top, a vertical stroke pushing down through the middle, and a longer horizontal stroke at the bottom holding everything up — like a little mound of packed earth sitting on the ground. In Cangjie, 土 is a whole-form character (整體字), meaning the shape is already a complete, indivisible unit, so it takes just one code: 土G. Think of the words 土地 (tou2 dei6), meaning land, and 土瓜灣 (tou2 gwaa1 waan4), To Kwa Wan, a district in central Kowloon — both begin from this one heap of soil. Remember it this way: soil is one mound, one key, G — because a whole-form character can't be split any further.
土.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「土」，讀作 tou2，即係泥土、土地嘅意思，凡係用泥造嘅嘢都同佢有關。你留意佢個樣：一橫喺頂，中間一豎插落嚟，最底再拖一長橫托住，好似一堆泥堆喺地面咁。喺倉頡入面，「土」係一個整體字——即係話佢本身已經係一個完整嘅字形部件，唔使拆開，所以佢淨係得一碼，就係土G。你可以諗吓「土地」（tou2 dei6）同埋「土瓜灣」（tou2 gwaa1 waan4）呢個九龍中部嘅地方，個個都由呢一堆泥開始。記住呢句：泥土G一堆，一個掣就夠——因為佢係整體字，冇得再拆。

在.en: Today's character is 在, read zoi6, meaning "to be at" or "located in," the way it works in 存在 cyun4 zoi6 (to exist, existence) and 旨在 zi2 zoi6 (to aim to, be intended to); the sentence 我在屋企休息 simply says you rest at home. Look at the shape and you'll see it built from three pieces: first the top-left ナ, found on the K key; then the single vertical 丨 running through the middle, on the L key; and finally the 土 sitting underneath, on the G key. Why does it split this way? Because 在 is a whole-character (整體字) with no clean head-and-body division, so we use the head-second-tail rule — take the first piece, the second piece, and the last piece — giving ナ, 丨, 土, which types as KLG. Remember it like this: start with ナ at the top left, drive a stroke down the middle, then plant it firmly on 土, and you'll always know where you 在.
在.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「在」，讀做 zoi6，意思係「喺、位於」，好似「存在」cyun4 zoi6（存在、有）同「旨在」zi2 zoi6（目的在於）咁用，例句「我在屋企休息」就係話你喺屋企休息。你望住個字，佢係由三嚿嘢砌成：先係左上角嘅撇橫 ナ，喺 K 掣度搵到；跟住中間嗰一豎 丨，喺 L 掣；最後係下面嘅 土，喺 G 掣。點解會咁拆呢？因為「在」係一個整體字，冇明顯嘅字首字身可以分開，遇到呢種字我哋就用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法——即係取最頭一嚿、第二嚿、同最尾一嚿，所以係 ナ、丨、土，砌成 KLG。記住喇：由左上角嘅 ナ 起筆，穿條豎落中間，最後坐喺塊 土 上面，你就穩穩噉「在」度喇。

地.en: Today we learn 地, read dei6, meaning earth, soil, ground, and by extension a region or area. Look at how it's built: on the left sits 土 (earth), and on the right sits 也. In Cangjie, 土 is the head of the character, so it gives us G; then 也 is the body, and since a body takes at most its first and last shapes, we pull the head 匕 as P and the tail 乜 as D — put together, that's G, P, D. Here's your hook: lay down some earth 土 (G), plant a 也 beside it (P, D), and you've made the very ground 地 beneath your feet!
地.zh: 今日我哋學「地」呢個字，讀作 dei6，意思係大地、泥土、地面，又可以指地方、區域。你睇吓佢點樣砌成：左邊係「土」，右邊係「也」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，「土」係字首，取碼 G；跟住「也」係字身，一個字身最多取頭尾兩碼，所以我哋取佢個頭「匕」係 P，同埋佢個尾「乜」係 D，合埋就係 G、P、D。記住喇：泥「土」（G）鋪喺地上，加埋一個「也」字（P、D），就係我哋腳下嘅大「地」喇！

均.en: Today we learn 均, read gwan1, meaning equal, even, or fair, and it can also mean 'all' or 'also' — as in 平均 ping4 gwan1, meaning average. Look at its shape: on the left sits a 土, and on the right sits a 勻, so this is a left-right character and we split left first, then right. The left 土 serves as the head, and although a head may take up to two codes, 土 is simple enough to give just one code, G. The right side 勻 is the body: following the natural writing order we take the outer wrap 勹 as P, then the inner 厶 as I, and finally the bottom stroke 一 as M, giving us GPIM. Picture it this way: you divide the soil (土) so everyone gets an even, fair share (勻) — that balance is exactly 均.
均.zh: 今日我哋學「均」呢個字，讀作 gwan1，意思係平均、均勻、公平，亦可以解「全部、都」，好似「平均」ping4 gwan1 就係 average 咁解。你望吓佢嘅結構，左邊係一個「土」字，右邊係一個「勻」字，係一個左右分開嘅字，所以我哋要先拆左後拆右。左邊嘅「土」做字首，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，但佢本身簡單，淨係取一碼就係 G；右邊嘅「勻」做字身，我哋順住寫字嘅方向，先取外面嘅「勹」P，再取入面嘅「厶」I，最後取底部嗰一橫「一」M，合埋就係 GPIM。記住呢個字嘅畫面：把泥土（土）分到平平均均，個「勻」字包住一粒厶同一橫，公平公正，就係「均」喇。

坊.en: Today's character is 坊, read fong1, meaning a neighborhood or an urban subdivision of a city. Look at its shape: it splits left and right, with 土 (earth) sitting on the left and 方 on the right. When we break it into code, we take the radical 土 first, which lives on the G key; then we move to the body 方, and because it is one complete piece, Cangjie asks us to take its head, second and tail — the head 亠 is Y, the second part 竹 is H, and the tail 尸 is S, giving us GYHS in full. Why does 方 get pulled into three pieces? Because as the body of the character it is allowed up to three codes, so we sample its top, middle and bottom. Here's your hook: a patch of 土 earth with a 方 house on it — that's the 坊 where your neighbours live.
坊.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「坊」，讀 fong1，指街坊、鄰里，或者城市裏面嘅一個區域。你睇下佢個樣，係左右兩邊拼埋一齊：左邊係個「土」字，右邊係個「方」字。拆碼嘅時候，我哋先攞字首「土」，佢喺鍵盤上係 G；跟住輪到字身「方」，因為佢係一個完整嘅部件，我哋要照倉頡嘅規矩，取頭、二、尾三個碼——頭係「亠」揀 Y，第二個係「竹」揀 H，最後個尾係「尸」揀 S，所以全碼就係 GYHS。點解「方」要拆到三部分呢？因為佢做字身，字身最多可以取三碼，於是頭、身、尾都要照顧到。記住呢句：泥「土」上面一「方」屋，就係街坊嘅「坊」。

坑.en: This character is 坑, read haang1, meaning a pit, hole or trap dug into the ground — a shape you'll spot all over Hong Kong place names like Hang Hau and Tai Hang. Look at how it's built: on the left sits 土 (earth), and on the right sits the component 亢. The left 土 (G) is a complete head on its own, taking just one code, so we take it cleanly as a single letter. The right 亢 acts as the body, and a body can take up to three codes, so we use the head-second-tail method: the top 亠 (Y), then a slanting 丿 taken with 竹 (H), and finally the bottom 乙 (N), giving GYHN. Picture a patch of earth (土) with a big hole beside it — that's your 坑.
坑.zh: 呢個字係「坑」，讀 haang1，即係地上凹落去嘅窟窿、氹或者陷阱，喺香港地名裏面好常見，好似坑口同大坑。你睇下佢嘅結構：左邊係「土」，右邊係「亢」字。左邊嘅「土」（G）自己就係一個完整嘅字首，佔一碼，所以我哋乾淨淨咁淨係攞佢一個碼。右邊嘅「亢」做字身，字身最多攞三碼，我哋就用頭、二、尾嘅方法：頭係上面嘅「亠」（Y），中間攞一撇「丿」用竹（H），最尾係下面嘅「乙」（N），砌埋一齊就係 GYHN。記住呢個畫面：一撻泥土（土）邊有個大氹，掉隻卜、竹、乙落去填佢，就係「坑」喇。

型.en: Today we meet 型, read "jing4", meaning a pattern, model, or type — the sense of something made to a standard or a mold. Look at how it stacks: on top sits 刑, and underneath sits 土. The top part 刑 is the 字首, and because it holds more than one piece we don't spell it out fully — instead Cangjie takes just its head and its tail, the first stroke 一 (M) and the last stroke 弓 (N), giving the two codes MN. Then the 字身 below, 土, counts as one piece and contributes a single code G, so the whole character is MNG. Remember it this way: head 一 (M) and tail 弓 (N) shape the 刑 on top, and the block of earth 土 (G) sits beneath as the mold that forms the 型.
型.zh: 今日我哋學「型」呢個字，讀「jing4」，即係模樣、款式、類型，例如做嘢有標準、有模板嗰種意思。你望下佢，係上下結構：上面係「刑」，下面係「土」。上半部「刑」係字首，因為佢部件多過一個，我哋唔會逐件拆晒，而係用倉頡「頭尾」嘅取碼法——攞最頭嗰筆「一」（M鍵），再攞最尾嗰筆「弓」（N鍵），所以字首得兩碼 MN。落到字身「土」，佢自己只算一個部件，取一碼 G 就夠，全字合埋就係 MNG。記住呢個口訣：頭一（M）尾弓（N）打起個「刑」，下面墊塊「土」（G），塊土做模，就整出個「型」嚟喇。

埋.en: Today we learn 埋, read "maai4" in Cantonese, meaning to bury, to conceal, to hide something away under cover. Look closely and you'll see it's made of 土 on the left and 里 on the right joined together. In Cangjie, the head 土 stands as its own piece and gives just one code, G; then the body 里 follows the head-tail rule, taking its top piece 田 (W) and its bottom piece 土 (G), so the whole code reads G, W, G. Why does the body take only head and tail? Because a body piece with many strokes is represented by just its first and last codes, and the middle is dropped. Here's your hook: start with a lump of earth (土), then pile a field and another lump of earth (里) on top, and you've buried it — 埋; you'll meet it in 同埋 and 加埋, as in "你行埋嚟啦".
埋.zh: 今日我哋學「埋」呢個字，粵音讀「maai4」，意思係埋藏、掩蓋，好似「埋葬」咁樣藏起嚟。你望真啲，呢個字係左邊一個「土」，右邊一個「里」砌埋一齊嘅。倉頡拆法係，左邊嘅字首「土」係一個獨立部件，只取一碼 G；跟住右邊嘅字身「里」，我哋依照「頭尾碼」嘅規矩，取佢最上面嘅「田」W 同最下面嘅「土」G，所以整個字碼就係 G、W、G。點解字身淨係取頭尾？因為字身部件筆畫多，倉頡只取頭同尾兩碼嚟代表，中間嘅就略去。你可以咁記：一嚿泥土（土）先，再嚟一片田加一嚿土（里），泥泥田田就「埋」落去啦。你可以喺「同埋」同「加埋」度見到佢，例如「你行埋嚟啦」。

城.en: Today we learn 城, read sing4, the character in words like 城市 (city) — it means a walled city, a town, a municipality. Take a good look: it splits neatly into a left part 土 and a right part 成. The left 土 is the 字首, the leading part, and since a 字首 only needs one code we simply take it as G. The right side 成 is the 字身, the body, and a body takes its head, a middle piece, and its tail, so we write in order: the curved 戈 as the head, typed I; then the little ⺊ inside as the second piece, typed H; and the 尸 shape closing it off at the tail, typed S. Put the left and right together and the full code is GIHS — 土 (G), 戈 (I), ⺊ (H), 尸 (S). Memory hook: one lump of 土 on the left, then break 成 into 戈, ⺊, 尸, and your whole city is built — just like 城市 (sing4 si5) and 九龍城 (Kowloon City).
城.zh: 今日我哋學「城」呢個字，讀 sing4，就係「城市」、「城堡」嘅城，係一個地方、一座城嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係個「土」字，右邊係個「成」字，好清楚咁分做兩邊。左手邊嘅「土」係字首，一個部件夠晒，只取一碼 G；右邊嘅「成」就係字身，字身要取頭、次、尾三部分，所以我哋順住寫落去：頭嗰撇彎彎嘅係「戈」，撳 I，跟住入面個「⺊」係第二個部件，撳 H，最後個「尸」形收尾，撳 S。噉樣連埋左邊，成個碼就係 GIHS，即係土（G）、戈（I）、⺊（H）、尸（S）。記住喇：左邊一舊土，右邊「成」字拆成戈、⺊、尸三步，一座城市就砌好晒，好似「城市 sing4 si5」同「九龍城」噉。

埔.en: Today's character is 埔, read bou3, meaning a plain or a marketplace — it shows up in lots of place names, like 大埔 (Tai Po) here in Hong Kong. Look at how it is built from a left and a right side: on the left is 土, and on the right is 甫. In Cangjie the left-hand 土 is the 字首, which gives just one code, G; the right-hand 甫 is the 字身, from which you take the head 戈 (I), the second piece 十 (J), and the tail ⺼ (B) — three codes in all, so the full code is GIJB. Why does the 字首 only get one code? Because 土 is simple enough that one code captures it, leaving the remaining slots for the busier 字身 甫 to take its head, second, and tail. Remember it this way: 土 gives one G, and 甫 grabs three — IJB — so if you live in Tai Po you'll never mistype this one.
埔.zh: 今日學嘅字係「埔」，讀 bou3，意思係平地、市集，好多地名都用到佢，好似香港嘅「大埔」噉。你睇佢由左右兩橀砌成：左邊係「土」，右邊係「甫」。倉頡拆字，左邊嘅「土」係字首，一碼就取 G；右邊嘅「甫」係字身，取頭「戈」I、取二「十」J、取尾「⺼」B，合共三碼，所以全碼係 GIJB。點解字首淨係得一碼？因為字首本身結構簡單，一碼已經夠代表「土」，餘落嘅碼位就留畀較複雜嘅字身「甫」慢慢取頭、二、尾。記住喇：「土」一 G，「甫」搏三碼 IJB，你住喺大埔就唔怕串錯呢個字啦。

埗.en: Look at 埗, read "bou6" — it means the same as 埠, a wharf or dock, or a trading port, and you'll see it in many place names like Hong Kong's own Sham Shui Po (深水埗). The character breaks into a left-side head and a right-side body: the head is 土, which sits on the G key. The body is 步, but Cangjie doesn't spell out the whole of 步 — a body takes only head-second-tail, three codes at most, so from 步 you pull 卜 (Y), 中 (L) and 竹 (H). Put them together and you get GYLH, just "土, 卜, 中, 竹" in order. To remember it, picture a lump of earth 土 with half of 步 stacked beside it — that's the 埗 in Sham Shui Po.
埗.zh: 你睇下「埗」呢個字，讀「bou6」，同「埠」係一樣意思，指碼頭、渡口，又或者係做買賣嘅口岸，好多地名都用到佢，好似香港嘅「深水埗」。呢個字分做左邊嘅字首同右邊嘅字身：字首係「土」，你喺鍵盤搵字母 G。右邊嘅字身係「步」，但係倉頡唔會將成個「步」拆晒，字身淨係取頭、次、尾三碼，所以喺「步」度攞到「卜」（Y）、「中」（L）同「竹」（H）呢三件。合埋一齊就係 GYLH，你記住「土、卜、中、竹」四步就掂。你可以咁樣記：一撻泥「土」上面搭住半個「步」，就係深水埗嗰個埗喇。

基.en: Today we learn 基, read gei1, meaning foundation or base — like the groundwork you lay before putting up a building. Look at it: on top sits 其, and underneath sits 土. In Cangjie we split this into a 字首 (lead part) and a 字身 (body): the top 其 is the lead, and the bottom 土 is the body. Because 其 has many strokes, Cangjie's rule lets a lead part give only its head and tail — so instead of spelling it all out, we take the head 廿 (T) and the tail 八 (C); then the body 土 gives one code, 土 (G), making TCG. Remember it this way: head 廿, tail 八, planted on a lump of 土 earth — that's how you build a solid 基 foundation.
基.zh: 今日我哋學「基」呢個字，讀作 gei1，意思係地基、基礎，好似起樓打嗰個底咁。你望下佢，上面係「其」，下面係「土」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，我哋分做字首同字身兩部分：上面嘅「其」係字首，下面嘅「土」係字身。字首「其」筆畫多，倉頡有個規矩，一件字首最多只取頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取頭嘅「廿」(T)同尾嘅「八」(C)；跟住字身「土」(G) 取一碼，合埋就係 TCG。記住個口訣：頭廿尾八踩住一嚿泥土，就係打好個「基」礎喇。

堂.en: Today's character is 堂, read tong4, meaning a hall or large room, and also a government office — you'll meet it in words like 教堂 (gaau3 tong2, church) and 天堂 (tin1 tong4, heaven). Look at how it stacks vertically: the top block is the head of the character, and the bottom block is the body. The upper head has too many strokes to take whole, so Cangjie's rule is to take just its first and last pieces — the first is ⺌ (F) and the last is 冖 (B); then you drop into the body and do the same, taking its head 口 (R) and its tail 土 (G), giving you FBRG. As a memory hook, read it top to bottom as ⺌, 冖, 口, 土 — a little roof settling layer by layer onto solid ground, exactly what a grand hall should stand on.
堂.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「堂」，讀音係 tong4，意思係大廳、殿堂，又或者係官府嘅地方，好似「教堂」（gaau3 tong2）同「天堂」（tin1 tong4）都用到佢。你望吓成隻字，佢係上下堆疊起嚟嘅：上面一嚿係字首，下面一嚿係字身。字首嗰部分筆畫多，唔會全部取晒，倉頡規矩係取頭同尾兩碼——頭係「⺌」（F），尾係「冖」（B）；跟住落到字身，同樣取頭同尾——頭係「口」（R），尾係「土」（G），砌埋一齊就係 FBRG。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以由上到下讀成「⺌、冖、口、土」，好似一層層搭上去嘅屋頂同地基咁，難怪佢係一間「堂」啦。

報.en: Today we learn 報, read "bou3", meaning to report, tell, or announce — the same 報 in "I'm reading the newspaper." The character splits into a left side and a right side: 幸 acts as the head, and the right part forms the body. Because 幸 on the left is too busy to spell out fully, Cangjie takes only its first and last codes, 土 (G) and 十 (J); then the right-side body is read in order as 尸 (S), 中 (L), and 又 (E), giving the full code GJSLE. Remember it this way: the left 幸 hands you 土十, the right body hands you 尸中又 — five pieces, one report.
報.zh: 今日我哋學「報」呢個字，讀「bou3」，即係報告、通知嘅意思，好似你「睇緊份報紙」嗰個「報」。呢個字分做左右兩邊，左邊係「幸」字做字首，右邊做字身。左邊「幸」字太複雜，唔會逐筆拆晒，倉頡淨係取佢頭尾兩碼，就係「土」（G）同「十」（J）；跟住右邊字身順住寫落去，取「尸」（S）、「中」（L）同「又」（E），所以成個碼就係 GJSLE。記住喇：左邊「幸」交出土十，右邊字身交出尸中又，一報就到手。

場.en: Look at 場, read coeng4 — it means an open space or field, and also a market or marketplace, as in 廣場 (a public square or plaza) and 商場 (a shopping mall). This is a left-right character: the left side is the radical 土, meaning earth or soil, which sits on the G key. The right-hand body is 昜, and because it's too full to type whole, Cangjie uses its head-and-tail rule — you take the first piece 日 (A), then the last two pieces 一 (M) and 竹 (H), giving AMH for the body. Put it together and the full code is GAMH, that is 土, 日, 一, 竹. Here's your hook: earth underfoot on the left (G), then the body opening with 日 (A) and closing with 一 (M) and 竹 (H) — so 場 spreads out just like an open field.
場.zh: 睇下「場」呢個字，讀 coeng4，意思係一片開闊嘅空地、田場，又或者係做買賣嘅市場，好似「廣場」同「商場」咁。呢個字係左右結構，左邊係部首「土」，就係泥土嘅「土」，佢喺個鍵盤上面撳 G。右邊嘅字身係「昜」，佢唔可以成個一次過打晒，要跟倉頡「取頭同取尾」嘅規矩：頭一個碼取「日」A，然後取到尾嘅兩個碼「一」M 同「竹」H，所以字身係 AMH。合埋一齊，個碼就係 GAMH，即係土、日、一、竹。記住一句：「土地上面有個昜」，左邊踩住泥土 G，右邊由日 A 起頭、一 M 竹 H 收尾，你就唔會撈亂喇。

塘.en: Today we learn 塘, read tong4, meaning a pond, pool or embankment — you'll meet it in Hong Kong place names like Kwun Tong (觀塘) and Yau Tong (油塘). Look at the shape: on the left sits 土 (earth), and on the right sits 唐, so this is a left-right character. The Cangjie split is tidy: the prefix takes the left piece 土 as G, and then the body 唐 must be coded, but a body is allowed at most three keys, so we take its head, second and tail — the head 广 as I, the second piece 中 as L, and the tail 口 as R, giving GILR. Here's your hook: earth first, then 唐 wrapped from top to bottom — 土 广 中 口 — so next time you commute to Kwun Tong, think GILR!
塘.zh: 今日我哋學「塘」呢個字，讀 tong4，即係水塘、池塘嘅意思，好似觀塘、油塘呢啲香港地名都用得着。你望住個字，左邊係個「土」字，右邊就係「唐」，成個字係左右分開嘅結構。倉頡拆法好清楚：字首拎左邊個「土」，取 G；跟住字身係「唐」，倉頡規定字身最多取三碼，所以要取頭、次、尾——頭係上面個「广」取 I，次係中間個「中」取 L，尾係下面個「口」取 R，合埋就係 GILR。記住個口訣：土起頭，唐字頭尾夾住個中，就係「土廣中口」——你返工去觀塘嗰陣，就當自己喺打緊 GILR 啦！

境.en: Today we learn 境, read ging2, meaning a boundary or frontier, and also an area or region — you'll meet it in words like 環境 (waan4 ging2, environment) and 入境 (jap6 ging2, to enter a country). Look at its shape: on the left is the earth radical 土, and on the right is 竟, so it clearly splits into a left-right pair, with 土 as the head and 竟 as the body. Cangjie has a rule that when the head is itself a compound piece it gives only one code, so 土 contributes just its first stroke G; the body 竟 is a fuller cluster, so we take head, second, and last from it — 卜 as Y, 廿 as T, and 山 as U, which builds the full code GYTU. Here's your memory hook: lay the earth foundation with one G for 土, then read 竟 top to bottom — 卜 Y, 廿 T, 山 U.
境.zh: 今日我哋學「境」呢個字，讀做 ging2，意思係界限、邊界，又或者係一個地方、地域，好似「環境」（waan4 ging2）同「入境」（jap6 ging2）咁用。你望吓佢個形，左邊係「土」字旁，右邊係「竟」，好明顯係左右兩橛：左邊「土」做字首，右邊「竟」做字身。倉頡有個規矩，字首係複合字嘅時候淨係取一碼，所以「土」就只攞頭嗰個 G；跟住字身「竟」係一個複雜嘅組合，就照字身取頭、二、尾嘅方法拆，頭係「卜」Y，第二係「廿」T，尾係「山」U，合埋成 GYTU。記住一句：「土」打地基一碼 G，「竟」由上望到落——卜 Y、廿 T、山 U 就得喇。

增.en: Today we learn 增, read zang1, meaning to increase or add more. Look at it: on the left is 土 (earth), and on the right is 曾 stacked up. When we split it, the left-hand 土 becomes the head and takes one code, G; the right-hand 曾 becomes the body. That body is broken into three codes — first the little 丷 on top is C, then the enclosing 囗 is W, and finally the 日 at the bottom is A, giving GCWA in full. Why does the body get three codes? Because the head only claims one code, everything else goes to the body, and the body may take up to three codes — 曾 fills all three neatly. Remember it this way: pile more onto the earth and it grows, zang1, just like a salary that has increased!
增.zh: 我哋今日學「增」呢個字，讀做 zang1，即係增加、加多啲嘅意思。你望下佢：左邊係個「土」字，右邊係個「曾」字疊埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「土」做字首，取一碼 G；右邊嘅「曾」做字身。字身呢部分要拆三碼——先取個頭上邊嘅「丷」係 C，再取中間包住嘅「囗」係 W，最後取底部嘅「日」係 A，所以成個字係 GCWA。點解字身要拆到三碼咁多？因為字首淨係佔一碼，其餘就全部畀字身，字身最多可以取三碼，「曾」啱啱好夠三個部件填滿。記住喇：土地上面「增」多咗嘢，讀 zang1，就好似人工增加咗一樣！

墟.en: Today we learn 墟, read heoi1. It originally means a high mound or hilly, open countryside, and it can also mean wasteland or ruins; in Hong Kong you know it best from 大埔墟, Tai Po Market, and from 廢墟, meaning ruins. Look at its build: on the left sits 土, and on the right stands the complex character 虛. When you split it, the head 土 is a single simple part, so it gives just one code, G; the body 虛 is a complex shape, so you take its head-second-last pattern — the opening 卜 is Y, then 匕 is P, and the final stroke 一 is M. Read left to right, first part then body, and the whole thing comes out as GYPM. Here's your hook: plant 土 (G) first, then the body 虛 gives its head 卜 (Y), second 匕 (P), and last 一 (M) — heading off to the market fair.
墟.zh: 今日我哋學「墟」字，讀作 heoi1，本來意思係高高嘅土丘、山野之地，又或者荒廢咗嘅地方；喺香港你最熟嘅一定係「大埔墟」呢個地名，即係 Tai Po Market，仲有「廢墟」，就係頹垣敗瓦嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣：左邊係「土」，右邊係一個複雜嘅「虛」字。拆碼嘅時候，字首「土」得一件嘢，就取一碼 G；字身係「虛」，屬於複雜字形，所以要取頭、二、尾三碼——起首嗰個「卜」係 Y，接住嘅「匕」係 P，最尾嗰橫「一」係 M。順住由左至右、由頭到尾嘅次序砌埋，就係 GYPM 喇。記住個口訣：土（G）先企好，虛就頭卜（Y）、二匕（P）、尾一（M），去趁墟就係去到有嘢賣嘅地方。

士.en: Today we learn 士, read si6, meaning a scholar or a learned person — as in 人士 jan4 si6, folks — and it can also mean a soldier. Look at its shape: a longer horizontal line on top, a vertical stroke down the middle, and a shorter horizontal line at the bottom, almost like the character 十 with an extra line beneath it. This is a whole-form character (整體字) — it can't be cleanly split into a head and a body — so Cangjie uses its special rule: for a whole-form shape you take just the head and the tail. So we take the head 十, which is J, then the tail 一, which is M, giving us JM. Remember it this way: a 十 (J) sitting on a line 一 (M) is 士 — and it's right there in the 巴士 baa1 si2 bus you ride every day!
士.zh: 今日我哋學「士」呢個字，讀作 si6，意思係讀書人、有學問嘅人，好似「人士」jan4 si6 咁，亦都可以指軍人。你睇佢個樣：上面一橫長啲，中間一豎，下面一橫短啲，好似一個「十」字下面加多一橫。呢個字係一個整體字，冇得一分為二咁清楚拆開，所以倉頡有一條特別規矩：整體字取頭同尾兩碼就夠。所以我哋先攞個頭「十」，就係 J 鍵，再攞個尾「一」，就係 M 鍵，合埋就係 JM。記住喇：一個「十」J 加一橫 M，就係「士」——你日日搭嘅「巴士」baa1 si2 就有佢！

壹.en: Today we're learning 壹, read "jat1", the formal capital version of the number one — the kind you write on cheques and banknotes because 壹 is much harder to alter than the plain 一. Look at how tall it is, stacked from top to bottom, so we split it into a head and a body. The head takes the top piece 士G, and then for the body we use the first-middle-last method: first the 冖B, then the 一M in the middle, and finally the 廿T at the bottom, giving you GBMT. Even though it reads exactly like 一, it looks grand and official, as in "here it's written one dollar" — so remember it as scholar-on-top building down layer by layer: 士, 冖, 一, 廿.
壹.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「壹」，讀「jat1」，即係數目字「一」嘅大寫，喺寫銀碼嘅時候用，好似支票同鈔票咁，寫成「壹」就好難改動。你望下呢個字，佢係上下疊起嚟嘅一個高身字，所以要拆做字首同字身兩部分。字首取最頂嘅士G，落到字身部分，就要用「頭二尾」嘅方法：先取個頭嘅冖B，再取中間嘅一M，最後取個尾嘅廿T，砌埋一齊就係GBMT。記住呢個字讀嘅時候同「一」一樣，但寫法隆重好多，好似「呢度寫住壹蚊」咁莊重，你就記得士頭一冖一廿，一層層由上砌到落底。

壽.en: Today's character is 壽, read sau6, meaning old age or long life — literally how long a lifespan lasts. It's a dense, many-stroked character that can't be cleanly split into a head and a body, so it counts as a whole-form character: instead of forcing a division we simply take the head, the second, the third, and the tail pieces in order. Reading top to bottom, you start with 土 on the G key, then 弓 on the N key, then the single stroke 一 on the M key, and finally 戈 on the I key, giving you GNMI. Picture 壽司 (sushi) and 壽命 (life span) as you type, and remember the run 土-弓-一-戈 from head to tail — that flat 一 pressed in the middle is your anchor for wishing someone long life.
壽.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「壽」，讀做 sau6，意思係長壽、壽命，即係人可以活幾耐嘅意思。呢個字筆畫多、結構密，好難乾淨咁分開頭同身，所以佢屬於「整體字」，我哋唔勉強分割，而係順住由上到下、由外到內嘅次序，取頭、二、三、尾四粒碼。你順住寫落去：先係最上面嘅「土」，喺 G 鍵；跟住係「弓」，喺 N 鍵；再嚟係一橫「一」，喺 M 鍵；最後係「戈」，喺 I 鍵，合埋就係 GNMI。你想想「壽司」同「壽命」呢兩個詞，記住「土弓一戈」由頭數到尾——一橫壓喺中間，就係長命百歲嘅「壽」。

外.en: Today we learn 外, read "ngoi6" in Cantonese, meaning out, outside, or external as in something foreign. Look at it: the left side is 夕 and the right side is 卜, and Cangjie splits it exactly along that left-right divide. The head 夕 gives you its first two codes only — first 乙 on the N key, then 厶 on the I key — while the body 卜 supplies its own single code Y, so the whole word is NIY. Why does the head stop at two codes? Because in a left-right character the head is allowed at most two codes, leaving the rest for the body, so 夕 hands over just N and I. Picture the evening 夕 (N, I) sitting under a little 卜 pole (Y), and you step "outside" — that's 外, as in 之外 and 另外.
外.zh: 我哋今日學「外」呢個字，粵語讀「ngoi6」，解外面、外邊，又或者係「外國」嗰種外來嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係個「夕」字，右邊係個「卜」字，倉頡就係跟住呢個左右結構去拆。左邊嘅「夕」係字首，我哋淨係攞頭兩個碼，先攞「乙」，個鍵係 N，再攞「厶」，個鍵係 I；右邊嘅「卜」係字身，攞埋佢個碼 Y，合埋就係 NIY。點解字首得兩個碼咁多呢？因為分左右嘅字，字首最多都係取兩個碼，其餘留返畀字身，所以「夕」點都好都只攞 N、I 兩碼。記住一句：夕陽（N、I）之下有卜卦（Y），出到「外」面去，就記得「之外」同埋「另外」呢兩個詞喇。

多.en: Today's character is 多, read do1, meaning "much" or "many" — the same 多 you see in 好多 (a whole lot) and 好多人 (many people). Take a look at its shape: it's really just two 夕 stacked one on top of the other. Each 夕 gets split into two pieces — first the 夕 form itself, which sits on the N key, and then the little 丶 dot, which is the I key. So the top 夕 becomes 夕丶, giving NI, and the bottom 夕 does exactly the same thing, giving another NI, and the two together make the full code NINI. Here's your hook: one 夕 is NI, and since there are so many of them, you just say it twice — NINI, too many to say only once!
多.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「多」，讀做 do1，即係「多」嘅意思，好似「好多」、「好多人」噉。你望吓佢個樣，其實係兩個「夕」上下疊埋一齊。每一個「夕」都要拆做兩橛：先係「夕」呢個形，佢喺鍵盤上係 N 鍵，跟住個小小嘅「丶」（一點），係 I 鍵。上面個夕拆做夕丶，就係 NI；下面個夕又照樣拆做夕丶，又係 NI；兩橛合埋，成個字就係 NINI。記住喇：一個夕就係 NI，兩個夕疊高高，你打多次就得，NINI，多到要講兩次！

夜.en: Today we learn 夜, read je6, meaning night or darkness, as in 夜晚要早啲瞓 — at night you should sleep early. Look at the character: on top sits 亠, a dot over a stroke; then comes the standing-person radical 亻 on the left, the person shape 人 in the middle, and a little crossing shape 乂 tucked into the lower right. This is a whole-character (整體字), so instead of splitting it into a head-part and a body-part, we simply read its pieces straight through in order: head 亠 gives Y, second 亻 gives O, then 人 gives N, and the tail 乂 gives K, spelling YONK. Your hook: 亠 Y opens, 亻 O stands aside, 人 N holds the centre, and 乂 K closes the night.
夜.zh: 今日我哋學「夜」呢個字，讀 je6，即係夜晚、黑暗嘅意思，好似「夜晚要早啲瞓」入面咁用。你望住個字，頂上係一點加一橫嘅「亠」，落嚟先寫左邊嘅企人邊「亻」，再係中間嘅「人」，最後右下角有個交叉形嘅「乂」。呢個係一個整體字，所以我哋唔會分字首字身兩橛，而係由頭到尾順住嚟拆碼：頭先取「亠」Y，第二取「亻」O，跟住取「人」N，最尾取「乂」K，砌埋就係 YONK。記住喇：「亠 Y 開頭，亻 O 企埋一邊，人 N 站中間，乂 K 收尾」，夜晚就係咁一筆一畫由天光寫到天黑。

夠.en: Today we're learning 夠, read gau3 in Cantonese, meaning "enough" or "adequate" — the word behind 能夠 (to be able to) and 唔夠 (not enough). Look closely and you'll see it's the left part 多 joined to the right part 句, which Cangjie splits into a head and a body. The head is 多, made of two stacked 夕 shapes, so we take its first stroke 弓 (N) and its last stroke 乙 (N) — both land on N. The body is 句, from which we take the opening wrap 勹 (P) and the enclosed 口 (R), giving the full code NNPR. Memory hook: two N's to say "more than enough," then a little 勹 wrapping a 口 to seal the deal.
夠.zh: 今日我哋學「夠」呢個字，粵音讀 gau3，意思係「足夠、夠晒」，好似「唔夠使」、「能夠」咁樣用。你望真啲，成個字係左邊嘅「多」加右邊嘅「句」砌成，倉頡分成字首同字身兩橛。字首係「多」，佢由兩個「夕」疊住寫，筆畫多，所以取頭嗰筆「弓」（N 鍵）同尾嗰筆「乙」（N 鍵），兩個都撳 N；字身係「句」，取頭嗰件「勹」（P 鍵）同裏面嘅「口」（R 鍵）。合埋就係 NNPR。記住一個口訣：多得夠嗮，兩個 N 開頭，勹住個口就啱晒。

大.en: Today we'll learn a very common character: 大, read daai6, meaning big, wide, or great. Look at its shape — it's like a person standing with arms stretched wide open, one horizontal stroke across the top and a slanting stroke on each side below, giving a real feeling of largeness and openness. This character is a 整體字, a whole-character, which means its entire form is treated as one complete unit — you don't split it into a 字首 and a 字身 and you don't break it stroke by stroke. Because of the whole-character rule, there's no code quota to fill; the whole shape maps to a single key, and that key is K, so one press types the whole thing. Remember it like this: arms flung wide open, just one tap of K, and 大 is done.
大.zh: 今日我哋學一個好常見嘅字：大，讀作 daai6，即係大細嘅大，解「大、闊、多」嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，好似一個人張開雙手咁企喺度，中間一橫、下面一撇一捺，感覺真係好大好開揚。呢個字係一個「整體字」，意思係佢自己成個字就係一嚿完整嘅字形，唔使拆做字首同字身，所以我哋唔會逐筆拆佢，只需要㩒一個掣就得，就係 K。點解淨係一碼？因為整體字有個特別規則：唔使湊夠碼數，成個形對應一個碼就完，K 一個掣打晒。記住個口訣：張大雙手 K 一嘢，大字就係咁簡單。

天.en: Today we're learning 天, read tin1, meaning the sky or the heavens, like in the sentence 今日天氣好好, "the weather is great today." Look at its shape: there's a flat stroke 一 across the top, and underneath it sits the character 大, "big" — clean and easy to spot. When we type it, 天 is a whole character, so we simply read it top to bottom: the top stroke 一 gives us M, and the 大 below gives us K, making the full code MK. The reason we split it this way is that as a whole character there's no head-and-body division to worry about — we just follow the natural top-to-bottom order, stroke first (M), then 大 (K). Here's your memory hook: one line across the sky (M) resting on a big person (K) — look up, and it's MK.
天.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「天」，讀做 tin1，即係天空、上天嘅意思，好似「今日天氣好好」入面嘅「天」。你望下佢個樣：上面有一橫，下面就係一個「大」字，好易認。拆碼嘅時候，「天」係一個整體字，我哋由上到下順住嚟拆，上面嗰一橫係「一」，攞 M；下面個「大」字，攞 K，所以成個碼就係 MK。之所以咁拆，係因為「天」係整體字，唔使分字首字身，淨係跟住由上到下嘅次序，一橫先，大字後，就係 M、K。記住個口訣：天上有一橫（M），底下企個大人（K），一望上天就係 MK。

太.en: Today's character is 太, read taai3, meaning "too" or "very" — the extreme end of things, as in 今日太熱喇, "it's too hot today." Look at its shape: it's simply the character 大 ("big") with one extra dot tucked underneath. Because 太 is a single-body character, Cangjie doesn't chop it stroke by stroke — the rule is just take the head and the tail, with nothing in between. So the head is 大 on the K key, the tail is that little dot 丶 on the I key, and the full code is KI. Here's your memory hook: a big person 大 with one drop of sweat 丶 — too big, too much, too hot!
太.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「太」，讀做 taai3，意思係「太過」、「非常」，好似「今日太熱喇」入面咁，形容過頭嘅程度。你睇下佢嘅樣，其實就係一個「大」字，下面加多一點。呢個字係一個整體字，倉頡拆嘅時候唔會逐畫拆散，而係取頭同取尾兩橛就夠：頭係「大」，喺 K 鍵；尾係嗰一點「丶」，喺 I 鍵，中間乜都唔使理，所以碼就係 KI。記住呢個口訣——一個大人加一點汗，就係太熱嘅「太」喇！

奇.en: Today we meet 奇, read kei4, meaning strange, unusual, or uncanny. Look at it: a 大 sits on top, and beneath it rests a 可, stacked into two layers. When you split it, the head 大 gives just one code, which is K; then the body 可 is allowed up to three codes, so you take head-second-last from it, drawing 一 M, 弓 N, and 口 R, giving you KMNR altogether. Why does 可 split this way? Because 可 is treated as one whole unit here and isn't broken down further, so you simply read its first, second, and last shapes off its outline. Here's your hook: one big person (大 K) topped by a stroke, a bow, and a mouth — no wonder they look so 奇 strange!
奇.zh: 今日我哋學「奇」字，讀音係 kei4，意思係奇怪、罕見、唔尋常嘅嘢。你望吓佢，上面一個「大」字，下面墊住一個「可」字，兩層疊埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，字首「大」淨係取一個碼，就係 K；跟住落嚟嘅「可」係字身，因為字身可以取到三個碼，所以我哋用頭一二尾嘅方法，順住畫出「一」M、「弓」N、同埋「口」R，合埋就係 KMNR。點解「可」要咁拆呢？因為「可」係整體字，唔再繼續細分，所以直接由佢嘅字形取頭、二、尾三個位。記住喇：一個大人（大K），頭上頂住一橫一弓一口，樣衰到咁「奇」怪！

女.en: Today we're learning the character 女, read neoi5, which means woman or girl. Take a look at its shape: one flowing, crossing stroke that curves like a person kneeling gracefully — this picture stands for the feminine. The lovely thing about this character is that in Cangjie it's itself one of the basic shapes, the shape called 女, which lives on the V key. Because it's a complete single-piece character (整體字), there's nothing to split into a 字首 and a 字身, so you just press one key, V, and you're done — a single code. Remember it this way: see 女, tap V, no thinking required.
女.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「女」，讀作 neoi5，即係女人、女仔嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣，一筆彎彎曲曲咁交叉起嚟，好似一個人跪坐咁優雅嘅姿態，正正代表女性。呢個字有趣嘅地方，就係佢喺倉頡入面本身就係一個字母形——佢係「女」呢個字形，本身放喺鍵盤嘅 V 掣度。因為佢係一個完整嘅整體字，冇得再拆開做字首同字身，所以打嘅時候淨係撳一個掣 V 就得，一碼搞掂。記住喇：見到「女」，直接撳 V，簡單到唔使諗。

奶.en: Today we learn 奶, read "naai5", the word for milk — the same character you see in 牛奶 (cow's milk) and 奶茶 (milk tea). Look at it: on the left is a 女 (woman), and on the right is 乃, and together they make 奶. In Cangjie the head 女 on the left is treated as one whole piece, so it gives just a single code, the woman key V. Then the body 乃 on the right gets broken down by head-and-tail: first its head 弓N, then its last two pieces 竹H and 尸S, giving N-H-S — so the full code is VNHS. Remember it like this: a 女 woman V on the left, then unpack 乃 into 弓竹尸 on the right, and your milk tea is ready.
奶.zh: 今日我哋學「奶」呢個字，讀「naai5」，就係牛奶嘅「奶」，好似「牛奶」、「奶茶」度嗰個字咁。你望下佢，左邊係一個「女」字，右邊係一個「乃」字，合埋就係「奶」。喺倉頡入面，左邊嘅字首「女」係一個整體，只取一碼，就係女字鍵V。跟住右邊嘅字身「乃」，我哋要拆佢，取頭同尾——頭一碼係弓N，然後取埋最後兩碼竹H同尸S，所以「乃」拆出嚟就係 N、H、S。全個字連埋就係 VNHS。記住喇：左邊一個「女」人V，右邊「乃」字慢慢拆做弓竹尸，飲杯奶茶就記得晒。

好.en: Today we're learning 好, which reads "hou2" or "hou3" and means good, excellent, fine, or well — the word you reach for when you say something's just right. Look at its shape: on the left is 女 (woman) and on the right is 子 (child), the two placed side by side to make 好. In Cangjie, 女 is the 字首, and a 字首 only gives one code, so we take just 女, which is V. Then 子 is the 字身, and a 字身 gives its head and tail — here the head is 弓 (N) and the tail is 木 (D) — so the full code comes out as VND. Remember it this way: a woman plus a child equals "good," V-N-D, and saying it aloud will lock it in.
好.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「好」呢個字，讀「hou2」或者「hou3」，意思係好、優秀、妥當，好似你講「好好呀」咁。你望下佢嘅結構，左邊係一個「女」字，右邊係一個「子」字，一女一子放埋一齊，就係「好」喇。倉頡分字嘅時候，「女」係字首，字首淨係取一碼，所以我哋只攞「女」呢個 V。跟住「子」係字身，字身要取頭同尾，「子」呢個字拆出嚟頭係「弓」N、尾係「木」D，所以整個字嘅碼就係 VND。記住喇：一個女、一個仔，湊埋就係「好」，V-N-D，讀嗰下你就記得晒。

如.en: Today's character is 如, read jyu4, meaning "if" or "like, as" — you'll see it in words like 例如, which means "for example." Look at the shape: it splits cleanly into two sides, with 女 on the left and 口 on the right, both pieces you already know. In Cangjie, the left 女 is the 字首 and takes the key V, while the right 口 is the 字身 and takes the key R, so the whole character is simply VR. Because this is a clear left-right character, the 字首 and 字身 each get exactly one piece and one code each, so there's nothing to trim or squeeze. Remember it like this: a woman (女) with an open mouth (口) — V then R, and you're done.
如.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「如」，讀做 jyu4，意思係「如果」、「好似」，比如「例如」就係「舉個例子」咁解。你望下呢個字，左右兩邊分開得好清楚：左邊係「女」，右邊係「口」，兩件都係你熟悉嘅部件。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「女」做字首，撳 V 鍵；右邊嘅「口」做字身，撳 R 鍵，一件取一碼，所以成個字就係 VR。因為呢個字係清楚嘅左右結構，字首同字身各佔一件、各取一碼，唔使諗點樣分割。記住嘅方法好簡單：一個「女」子開口講嘢，就係「如」，V 加 R，兩下就打完。

始.en: Today's character is 始, read ci2, meaning to begin or to start — you see it in words like 開始 (hoi1 ci2, to begin) and 原始 (jyun4 ci2, original or primitive). Look at how it's built: it splits left and right, with 女 on the left and 台 on the right. The left 女 is the 字首, and since it's a single complete piece it just gives one code, V. The right 台 is the 字身, and a 字身 takes at most its head and its tail, so from 台 we grab the head 厶 (I) and the tail 口 (R), skipping whatever sits between. Put together that gives you VIR — picture a woman (V) picking up a spear 戈 (I) and opening her mouth 口 (R) to say 'let's begin!'
始.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「始」，讀作 ci2，意思係開始、起頭，好似「開始」（hoi1 ci2）同「原始」（jyun4 ci2）咁。你望下呢個字，佢係左右兩邊砌成嘅：左邊係「女」，右邊係「台」。左邊「女」係字首，佢自己一個部件就足夠，所以淨係取一碼 V。右邊「台」做字身，字身最多取頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋喺「台」入面攞個頭「戈」（I）同埋個尾「口」（R），中間跳過。噉合埋就係 VIR。記住呢個口訣：一個女仔（V）用戈（I）開口（R）講「開始」，噉就唔會撳錯喇！

姐.en: Today we learn 姐, read "ze2", meaning an elder sister and also a way to address a woman, as in 小姐, a young lady or Ms. Look at how it stands in two parts side by side: on the left is the piece 女, which you type with V, and on the right is 且, which looks like a little stack. Cangjie does not spell out every line of a body piece — instead it takes just the first and last, so from 且 you take its head ⺼ (B) and its final bottom stroke 一 (M). That is why the head 女 gives only one code V, while the body 且 gives two, the first-last pair B and M, making the full code VBM. Remember it like this: the girl 女 stands on the left as V, and 且 on the right is squeezed from top B to bottom M — together they build the 姐 in 家姐.
姐.zh: 我哋今日學「姐」呢個字，讀「ze2」，即係家姐、姊姊，又或者用嚟稱呼女士，好似「小姐」噉。你望下佢係左右兩橛：左邊係「女」呢個部件，喺鍵盤上面撳 V。右邊係「且」，睇落好似一疊嘢，但係倉頡拆碼唔會逐橛拆晒，而係取佢嘅頭同尾——頭係「⺼」，撳 B；尾係最底嗰一橫「一」，撳 M。所以字首「女」淨係畀一個碼 V，字身「且」就取頭尾兩碼 B、M，合埋就係 VBM。記住：「女」仔企喺左邊 V，右邊「且」就頭 B 尾 M 咁夾埋，就砌成「家姐」個「姐」喇。

委.en: Today we learn 委, read wai2 or wai1, meaning to appoint or commission — sending someone to take on a duty, as in 委員, a committee member. Look at its shape: on top sits 禾, the grain plant, and underneath sits 女, woman, stacked neatly in two layers. In Cangjie we first take the head 禾, which is written from two pieces: the opening slant is 竹, key H, and below it is 木, key D, so the head gives us HD; then comes the body 女, key V, making the whole code HDV. Why does 禾 give only two codes? Because as the head of the character it can take at most two, and 竹 plus 木 fill that quota exactly, so there is nothing more to grab. Here's your memory hook: picture grain (竹木) growing over a woman's head, and you commission her to work — H, D, V, top to bottom, builds the whole thing.
委.zh: 今日我哋學「委」呢個字，讀音係wai2或者wai1，意思係委派、委任，好似「委員」咁樣派人去做嘢。你望下佢嘅結構，上面係個「禾」字，下面係個「女」字，兩層清清楚楚咁疊住。倉頡拆法係先攞字首「禾」，佢由兩件砌成：起筆嗰撇係「竹」，撳H鍵，跟住下面就係「木」，撳D鍵，所以字首取咗HD兩碼；之後就到字身「女」，撳V鍵，全個字就係HDV。點解「禾」只取頭尾兩碼呢？因為佢做字首，最多都係取兩碼，「竹」同「木」啱啱好夠數，唔使再理中間。記住嘅竅門：禾苗（竹木）長喺個女仔頭頂，委派佢去做嘢，H、D、V順住由上而下就砌得成。

威.en: Today we're learning 威, read "wai1", meaning pomp, power, or an impressive, commanding presence — like saying someone is really impressive. Look at its shape: on the outside there's a 戈 spear-frame wrapping around, and tucked inside sits a 女 woman. This is a whole-shape character that can't be cleanly split into a head and a body, so we use the whole-shape rule — take the first, second, third, and last pieces, and skip whatever's in the middle. Going in order, you take 戈 (the I key), then 竹 (the H key), then 一 (the M key), and finally 女 (the V key), skipping the middle strokes, which gives you IHMV. Here's your hook: a bold 戈 spear holding up the whole scene with a 女 tucked inside — four keys, and you've captured all that power.
威.zh: 我哋今日學「威」呢個字，讀「wai1」，係威風、威力、有氣勢嘅意思，好似講一個人好威、好神氣噉。你望吓佢個樣：外面係一個「戈」字框住，中間夾住一個「女」字。呢個字係整體字，拆唔開成清楚嘅字首字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅法則——取頭、二、三同埋尾，中間就跳過唔理。順住嚟：先取「戈」（I 鍵），再取「竹」（H 鍵），跟住「一」（M 鍵），最尾取「女」（V 鍵），中間嘅筆畫就略去，所以個碼係 IHMV。記住喇：一個「戈」字撐起個場面，中間收埋個「女」字，四粒就夠威。

媽.en: Today we're learning 媽, the word for mother or mama, and although it can read maa1, maa2, maa4 or maa5, the everyday one is the maa1 you hear in 媽媽. Look at it and you'll see a woman radical 女 sitting on the left and a horse 馬 filling the right side. In Cangjie the head 女 is taken first — that's the V key — and then the body 馬 follows. Because 馬 is a big, busy shape we don't spell out every piece; instead we take head-second-last, grabbing 尸 (S), 手 (Q) and 火 (F), which together give you VSQF. So picture it simply: a woman (V) beside a horse (SQF) is your mother — 媽媽 cooks rice for me.
媽.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「媽」，即係媽媽嘅媽，讀音有 maa1、maa2、maa4、maa5 幾種，最常見就係叫「媽媽」嗰個 maa1。你望吓佢，左邊係一個女字部，右邊就係一隻馬。倉頡分字嘅時候，先取字首「女」，佢喺鍵盤上係 V；跟住個字身係「馬」，馬係一個複雜字，唔可以逐筆全取，所以要用「取頭二尾」嘅辦法，即係捉住頭一碼加埋最後兩碼，得出 尸（S）、手（Q）、火（F），合埋成 VSQF。所以你記住：一個女人（V）陪住一隻馬（SQF），就係「媽」——媽媽煮飯畀我食。

子.en: Today we're learning the character 子, read zi2, which means a child or offspring, and can also mean a seed or fruit, as in words like 句子 (a sentence) and 日子 (a day or the days of your life). Look at it: the whole thing flows as one connected shape, so it's hard to cleanly split into a separate head and body — that's why Cangjie treats it as a whole-form character (整體字) and simply takes the head and the tail. The head is that curving hook you see across the top, which we take as 弓 on the N key; the tail is the long final horizontal stroke sweeping across, which we take as 木 on the D key, giving you N then D — ND. As your memory hook, just remember that for a whole-form character you skip the middle entirely: head 弓 N, tail 木 D, and 子 is done.
子.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「子」，讀做 zi2，本身解「小朋友、仔女」，又可以指「種子」或者用喺「句子」、「日子」呢啲詞入面。你望住呢個字，成個係一體流暢寫落嚟，好難清清楚楚咁分開頭同身，所以倉頡就當佢係「整體字」，只取頭同尾兩碼。頭碼係你睇到頂上面嗰個轉彎嘅形，我哋當佢係「弓」，撳鍵盤上嘅 N；尾碼係最尾一橫兜落嚟嗰筆，我哋當佢係「木」，撳鍵盤上嘅 D，合埋就係 ND。記住一個口訣：整體字唔使諗中間，淨係「頭弓 N、尾木 D」，就成個「子」啦。

字.en: Today we learn the character 字 itself, read zi6, meaning a letter, a character, or a word — how fitting. Look at its shape: on top sits the roof-like cover 宀, and beneath it sits 子, the piece for child. When you type it, 宀 acts as the head and lives on the J key, so you press that first. Then 子 acts as the body, and a body doesn't always give just one code — here it gives its head-and-tail: the head 乛 on N and the tail 子 on D, making the full code J, N, D. The split falls this way because 子, standing as the body, isn't skipped as one whole unit but is coded by its first and last strokes. Remember it like this: roof J, then 子 gives head-tail N and D — 呢個字好難寫, but it's not hard to type.
字.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字，就係「字」本身，讀做 zi6，意思係文字、字母、詞語，好貼切啦。你望吓佢嘅結構：上面有個寶蓋頭「宀」，下面有個「子」。打字嘅時候，「宀」做字首，佢對應鍵盤上嘅 J，你先撳佢。跟住落嚟嘅「子」做字身，字身唔止取一個碼，而係取頭尾兩碼：頭係「乛」對應 N，尾係「子」對應 D，所以成隻字嘅碼就係 J、N、D。點解「子」要拆頭尾呢？因為佢做字身嗰陣，唔係當一整個部件咁跳過，而係按「頭一筆、尾一筆」嘅規矩取碼。記住個口訣：寶蓋頭 J，子字頭尾 N、D，「呢個字好難寫」，但唔難打。

存.en: Today we learn 存, read cyun4, which means to exist, to survive, or to keep something safe, as in 存在 cyun4 zoi6, 'to exist,' and 生存 sang1 cyun4, 'survival.' Look at the character: on the upper left sits 才, and tucked into the lower right sits 子. Cangjie takes the head and tail of the first part, 字首 才 — the head is ナ (K) and the tail is 中 (L) — then the head and tail of the body, 字身 子 — the head is 弓 (N) and the tail is 木 (D). The split falls this way because when one 字首 meets one 字身, each contributes just its head and tail, so 才 gives KL and 子 gives ND, joining into KLND. Remember it like this: write 才 first (KL), then 子 (ND), as in 我存咗啲錢 — I put some money away safely.
存.zh: 今日我哋學「存」呢個字，讀音係 cyun4，意思係存在、生存、保存，好似「存在」cyun4 zoi6，又或者「生存」sang1 cyun4 咁樣用。呢個字睇落好似兩橛拼埋一齊：左邊上面係「才」，右下係「子」。倉頡拆呢個字，先攞字首「才」嘅頭尾——頭係「ナ」（K），尾係「中」（L）；跟住攞字身「子」嘅頭尾——頭係「弓」（N），尾係「木」（D）。點解要咁樣拆呢？因為一個字首、一個字身都係各自取頭尾兩碼，所以「才」畀 KL、「子」畀 ND，合埋就係 KLND。記住喇：先寫「才」（KL）再寫「子」（ND），好似「我存咗啲錢」咁，把嘢好好保存起身。

學.en: Today's character is 學, read hok6, meaning learning, study, or school — you'll meet it everywhere, as in 學校 (hok6 haau6, school) and 學生 (hok6 saang1, student). It's a top-bottom character: the big top piece is called 𦥯, and as the 字首 it hands over just its head and tail — head 竹 H and tail 月 B. The bottom piece is 子, which serves as the 字身 and also gives head and tail; since 子's own code is ND, that's head 弓 N and tail 木 D, taken together. Put it all in typing order and you get H, B, 弓 N, 木 D — HBND. Picture it this way: a cap on top (HB) and a little child (子 = ND) studying underneath — that's 學!
學.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「學」，讀作 hok6，即係學習、讀書、學校嘅意思，好似「學校」（hok6 haau6）同「學生」（hok6 saang1）咁常見。呢個字係上下結構，上半部係一大嚿叫做𦥯，佢做字首，倉頡淨係取佢嘅頭同尾兩碼——頭係「竹」H，尾係「月」B；下面嘅「子」做字身，同樣取頭尾兩碼，「子」自己嘅碼係 ND，頭係「弓」N、尾係「木」D，兩個位一齊攞落嚟。所以成個字砌埋就係 H、B、弓 N、木 D，即 HBND。你可以咁記：頂上一頂帽（HB），底下一個細路仔（子＝ND）勤力讀書，就係「學」喇！

安.en: Today we learn 安, read on1, meaning peaceful, tranquil, or quiet — it's the 安 in the word 安全, safety. Look at how it's built: on top sits the 宀 roof radical, like the roof of a house spread over everything below, and underneath is 女, woman. Cangjie splits it in the most natural way — the top 宀 is the character head, so we take J, and the bottom 女 is the character body, so we take V, giving you JV. The split falls there because the character has a clear top-and-bottom layout: the head takes the upper piece and the body takes the lower piece, one code each, nothing fussy about it. Picture it this way: a roof (J) sheltering a woman (V) — a home with someone safely inside is 安.
安.zh: 今日我哋學「安」字，讀作 on1，意思係平安、安寧、安靜，好似你講「安全」嗰個「安」。你望吓佢嘅結構：上面係一個「宀」字頭，好似一間屋嘅屋頂，罩住下面；下面係一個「女」字。倉頡拆佢就好順理成章：上面嘅「宀」係字首，我哋取 J；下面嘅「女」係字身，我哋取 V，合埋就係 JV。點解係咁分？因為呢個字有清清楚楚嘅上下兩截，字首取上面嗰嚿、字身取下面嗰嚿，各取一碼，一啲都唔複雜。記住個畫面：屋頂（J）遮住一個女仔（V），一間屋有人喺度，就係「安」。

完.en: Today we learn 完, read jyun4, meaning to complete, to finish, or whole — as in 完全 (jyun4 cyun4, completely) and 完成 (jyun4 sing4, to accomplish). Look at its shape: a roof 宀 sitting on top of 元, so it splits into a 字首 on top and a 字身 below. The roof 宀 is the 字首, typed J; the 元 underneath becomes the 字身, and we read its own first, second, and last pieces — the opening stroke 一 is M, the second stroke 一 is M, and the closing 山 shape is U. Put it together and you get J, M, M, U, that is JMMU. Remember it this way: one roof J covering two flat strokes and a 山 tail, MMU — 我做完功課喇, all finished!
完.zh: 今日我哋學「完」呢個字，讀 jyun4，意思係完成、完結、完整，好似「完全」（jyun4 cyun4）同「完成」（jyun4 sing4）咁用。你望下佢個樣，係一個「宀」冚喺「元」上面，所以要分做字首同字身兩橛。上面個蓋頭「宀」做字首，撳 J；下面個「元」就做字身，要拆佢自己嘅頭、二、尾——起筆一橫「一」係 M，第二筆又一橫「一」係 M，最後個「山」形收尾係 U。合埋就係 J、M、M、U，即係 JMMU。記住喇：一個蓋頭 J 冚住兩橫加一個山尾 MMU，「我做完功課喇」就係完晒嘞！

官.en: Today we're learning 官, read gun1 — the word for an official or public servant, someone who holds a government post. Look at its shape: right at the top sits a roof cover 宀, which you type with J; underneath it, the rest of the pieces stack together. Cangjie has a firm rule that the 字首, the leading part, may only give one code, so 宀 takes its single J and we move on to the 字身, the body. The body isn't taken whole either — we use the head-second-last method, grabbing the first piece, the second piece, and the very last piece, which here gives us 口 (R), then 丨 — that's the 中 shape, typed L — and finally the last 口 (R), spelling out JRLR. Here's your hook: one roof shelters two mouths with an upright stroke between them, the official seated high in his office presiding over all beneath him — that's 官.
官.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「官」字，讀作 gun1，即係官員、做官嗰個「官」，泛指政府裏面嘅公職人員。你睇下佢個樣：最上面係一個寶蓋頭「宀」，喺鍵盤上面打 J；下面就係一堆組件疊埋。倉頡拆字有規矩，字首只可以取一碼，所以「宀」自己佔咗個 J，跟住落到字身。字身唔可以無限咁取，要用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法，即係取開頭、第二個、同最尾嘅組件，所以我哋喺下面攞到口（R）、丨（呢個係「中」字，打 L）、再加最尾一個口（R），合埋就係 JRLR。記住喇：一個寶蓋頭遮住兩個口夾住一豎，官老爺高高在上，坐鎮衙門，就係「官」。

定.en: Today we learn 定, read ding6 — the 定 in 決定 (to decide) and 一定 (surely, definitely) — and it means to decide, settle, or fix something firmly. Look at its shape: the roof piece 宀 sits on top, with 疋 tucked underneath. In Cangjie the top 宀 is the 字首 (leading part) and gives us J; the bottom 疋 is the 字身 (body part), and because a body part takes head, second, and tail, we pick its head 一 = M, then its second piece 卜 = Y, then its tail 人 = O, giving JMYO. Your memory hook: under the roof, one dot decides a person — J, M, Y, O — 定.
定.zh: 我哋今日學「定」字，讀 ding6，即係「決定」、「一定」嗰個「定」，意思係決定、安定、固定落嚟。你望吓佢個樣：上面係個寶蓋頭「宀」，下面托住個「疋」字。喺倉頡入面，上面嘅「宀」做字首，取 J；下面嘅「疋」做字身，因為字身要取頭、次、尾三部分，所以我哋先取個頭「一」＝M，再取第二個部分「卜」＝Y，最後取個尾「人」＝O，合埋就係 JMYO。記住個口訣：宝蓋頭住咗，下面一卜人，人一決定咗「你決定咗未呀？」。

室.en: This character is 室, read sat1, and it means a room or a home — the kind of space like a classroom or a bedroom. Look up at its roof first: that curved top is 宀, the piece Chinese uses to signal a house or shelter, and you'll find it on the J key. What sits under the roof is 至, and Cangjie doesn't spell out every stroke of it — instead it follows the 'first two, last one' rule for the body, taking the opening horizontal stroke 一 on M, then 戈 on I, and finally 土 on G, giving you the full code JMIG. That's why the split puts the roof 宀 first and then breaks the lower 至 into just three of its pieces. Remember it this way: a roof (J) up top, with 至 tucked neatly inside the house, and you've built 室.
室.zh: 呢個字係「室」，讀sat1，解房間、屋企，好似課室、睡房嗰啲空間。你抬頭望吓佢嘅頭頂，係個屋簷「宀」，就係中文入面代表「屋」嘅部件，喺鍵盤上面撳J。跟住落嚟嘅字身係「至」，倉頡取碼嘅時候唔會逐筆拆晒，而係跟「頭二尾一」嘅規矩，抽佢起首兩個部件同最尾一個：起首係一橫「一」撳M，再嚟係「戈」撳I，最後「土」撳G，四個部件合埋就係JMIG。所以個順序係頂上個屋簷行先，之後先至輪到下面嘅「至」拆做一、戈、土。記住：屋簷（J）之下，有個「至」字乖乖坐喺屋入面，就係一間「室」喇。

宮.en: Today we learn 宮, read gung1, meaning a palace or imperial dwelling — the grand hall where an emperor lives. Look at its shape: a roof cover 宀 sits on top, and underneath is 呂, so it reads like a great hall crowned with a roof. When we split it, the head is that roof cover 宀 on top, which lives on the J key. Then we move to the body 呂; because it is a piece built from more than two parts, we take first, middle, and last — the first mouth 口 R, then the middle stroke 丿 H, then the last mouth 口 R, giving JRHR. Remember it this way: one roof J, and inside two mouths with a little stroke wedged between them makes 宮 — once you have visited the palace at 故宮, you will never forget this grand hall.
宮.zh: 今日我哋學「宮」字，讀作 gung1，意思係宮殿、皇宮，即係帝王住嘅地方。你望吓佢嘅樣：上面有個寶蓋頭「宀」，下面坐住個「呂」字，就好似一座有屋頂嘅大殿咁。拆碼嘅時候，字首就係頂上嘅寶蓋頭「宀」，佢喺鍵盤上係 J。跟住落到字身「呂」，因為佢係一個由多過兩橛砌成嘅部分，所以我哋要取頭、中、尾三部分——先取最頭嘅口 R，再取中間嗰筆丿 H，最後取埋尾嘅口 R，合埋成 JRHR。記住喇：一間屋 J，入面兩個口中間夾住一劃，就係「宮」，你去過故宮嘅話一定唔會唔記得呢座大殿。

宴.en: Today's character is 宴, read jin3, meaning to hold a feast or throw a banquet — think of 宴會 jin3 wui6, a proper dinner party, or the grander 宴會廳 jin3 wui5 teng1, the banqueting hall where such feasts are laid out. Look at the shape: there's a roof piece 宀 sitting on top, sheltering everything below it, and that roof is the character-head, keyed as J. Once the head is taken, the whole bottom block becomes the character-body, and a body is split by the head-tail rule, so from that lower block we take its first piece 日, keyed as A, and its last piece 女, keyed as V, skipping whatever sits between them. Put it together and 宴 is J, A, V. Picture it this way: under one roof, a woman lays out a feast beneath the sun — we're off to a wedding banquet.
宴.zh: 今日學嘅字係「宴」，讀做 jin3，意思係設宴、擺酒請人食飯，好似「宴會」jin3 wui6 咁，即係盛大嘅飯局；再大啲嘅場合就有「宴會廳」jin3 wui5 teng1，即係擺酒宴賓客嘅大廳。你睇下個字嘅結構：上面有個寶蓋頭「宀」，遮住下面兩件嘢，呢個「宀」係個字首，key 係 J。個字首拆完之後，就輪到下面嗰嚿做字身。字身要跟頭尾原則嚟拆，所以喺下面嗰嚿裏面，我哋取最頭嘅「日」，key 係 A，再取最尾嘅「女」，key 係 V，中間嘅部分就唔使理，於是整個字砌埋就係 J、A、V。記住個畫面：一個屋頂「宀」之下，日頭底下有個女子擺開一席酒——我哋去飲喜宴啦。

家.en: Today we learn 家, read "gaa1", meaning a house or home, the place where you live, and also a family. Look at its shape: there's a roof on top, and underneath it a pig is kept — so 家 is a place with a roof overhead and food cooking, your home. When we break it up, the roof-radical 宀 on top is the 字首, typed with J; the 豕 below is the 字身, and because a 字身 gives at most three codes, we take head-second-tail — the head 一 (M), the second piece 匚 (S), and the tail 人 (O) — skipping the middle piece, which builds JMSO. Practise it with 而家 (ji4 gaa1, "right now") and 國家 (gwok3 gaa1, "country"). Remember the hook: under the roof lives a pig, and that makes a family (J, M, S, O).
家.zh: 我哋今日學「家」呢個字，讀「gaa1」，即係屋企、住嘅地方，又指一個家庭。你睇下佢嘅樣：上面有個屋頂，下面住住一隻豬——所以「家」就係有瓦遮頭、有煮食嘅地方喇。拆碼嗰陣，上面個寶蓋頭「宀」係字首，撳 J；下面個「豕」係字身，因為字身最多得三碼，要用「取頭二尾」嘅辦法，所以攞頭「一」M、第二個「匚」S、同埋尾「人」O，中間嗰截就跳過唔要，砌埋一齊就係 JMSO。你可以用「而家 ji4 gaa1」（即係「而家幾點」嗰個而家）同「國家 gwok3 gaa1」嚟練習。記住個口訣：屋頂之下養住豬，就係一家人喇（J、M、S、O）。

容.en: Today we learn 容, read jung4, meaning looks, appearance, or form — the same 容 you see in 內容 noi6 jung4, "content," the stuff held inside. Look at the top: it's the roof 宀, which we take as J, and that whole roof is the character head. What sits below is the body 谷, and because Cangjie lets a body give at most three parts, we pick its head, middle, and tail — 八 as C, then 人 as O, then 口 as R at the bottom. String them together and you get exactly JCOR: roof first, then the head, middle, and tail of 谷. Picture a house 宀 sheltering a valley 谷 underneath — a roof with room to contain everything, which is just what 容 means.
容.zh: 我哋今日學「容」呢個字，讀做 jung4，意思係樣貌、樣子、形態，好似「內容」noi6 jung4 嗰種「入面裝住嘅嘢」嘅感覺。你望住個字，最上面係個屋簷「宀」，喺倉頡入面攞 J，成個頭就係佢；跟住落嚟嘅係「谷」呢個字身，倉頡教我哋一個字身最多拆三橛，所以要揀頭、揀次、揀尾——頭係「八」攞 C，中間攞「人」O，最後個尾攞「口」R。咁樣夾埋就係 JCOR，屋頂先，谷字頭中尾在後，次序好清楚。記住呢個畫面：一間屋「宀」，入面裝住個「谷」，屋簷之下容納晒所有嘢，容量就係咁大。

富.en: Today's character is 富, read fu3, meaning abundant, ample, or wealthy — you'll meet it in words like 豐富 (fung1 fu3), to be rich and plentiful, and 財富 (coi4 fu3), property or wealth. Look at its shape: there's a roof radical 宀 on top, and the piece 畐 underneath. The top forms the 字首 and you take 宀 on the J key; the bottom 畐 is the 字身, and since we can't take every stroke, we grab head, second, and tail — head 一 on M, then 口 on R, and finally the tail 田 on W. Put it all together and the code is JMRW: first the roof of the 字首, then the 一, 口, and 田 of the 字身. Remember it this way — under one roof (宀) sits a mouth guarding a field (畐), and a household with land and food is a wealthy one.
富.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「富」，讀做 fu3，意思係豐盛、富有，好似「豐富」（fung1 fu3）同「財富」（coi4 fu3）咁樣。你望吓佢個樣：上面有個寶蓋頭「宀」，下面就係「畐」呢個部件。上面嘅字首取「宀」，個鍵係 J；下面嘅字身係「畐」，我哋唔可以逐筆全部取，只能夠取頭、次、尾三個部分——頭係「一」（M），跟住係「口」（R），最尾就取個「田」（W）。所以成個碼砌埋就係 JMRW，即係先寫字首嘅宀，再寫字身嘅一、口、田。你可以咁記：一間屋（宀）入面，有一個口人守住一塊田（畐），有田有食就係富有喇。

實.en: Today we learn 實, read sat6, meaning real, true, solid, or honest. Look at how it's built: on top sits a roof 宀, which is the 字首 — press J. Everything under the roof is the 字身, and Cangjie tells us to pick three parts from it: first the head 田, press W, then the middle 十, press J, and finally the tail 八, press C, giving the full code JWJC. Why does the split fall this way? Because the 字首 takes at most two codes but 宀 is a single piece, so it fills only the first key J; then the 字身 takes up to three codes, chosen in head-middle-tail order as W, J, C. Here's your memory hook: under the roof 宀 (J), tuck away a field 田 (W), a ten 十 (J), and a little 八 (C) — four keys, real and solid. Practise with 其實 and 現實, as in "You will definitely win."
實.zh: 今日我哋學「實」呢個字，讀做 sat6，意思係真實、實在、實淨。你望吓佢嘅結構：最上面戴住一個屋頂「宀」，呢個就係字首，撳 J。屋頂底下嘅部分就係字身，我哋要照倉頡嘅取碼規矩挑三個部分——先取頭「田」，撳 W，再取中間嘅「十」，撳 J，最後取尾「八」，撳 C，所以成個字係 JWJC。點解要咁樣拆呢？因為倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，但「宀」得一個部分，就淨係佔咗頭一碼 J；跟住字身最多取三碼，就順住頭、中、尾嘅次序揀出 W、J、C。記住嘅竅門係：屋頂宀 J 之下，收埋一格田 W、一個十 J、一撇八 C，實實在在四碼收工。你可以用「其實」同「現實」呢兩個詞嚟練吓手，例如「你實會贏㗎。」

寫.en: Today we learn 寫, read se2, which means to write, to draw, or to compose — you see it in 寫作 se2 zok3, meaning to write or compose, and in 縮寫 suk1 se2, meaning an abbreviation. Look at the shape: a roof 宀 sits on top, and underneath it a tangle of tiny strokes crowds in, packed and busy. To type it, the head is the roof 宀 on the J key, and then the body is so complicated that Cangjie uses the head-and-tail trick: after the head, we skip the messy middle with the X 難 (difficulty) key, and finish with the four-dot fire 灬 on the F key, giving the full code JHXF. Here's your memory hook: when a body is too crowded to pick apart, X jumps over the middle — 寫 is a lot to write, so let the difficulty key carry the load.
寫.zh: 今日我哋學「寫」呢個字，讀作 se2，係書寫、繪畫、作文嘅意思，好似「寫作」se2 zok3 就係寫文，「縮寫」suk1 se2 就係簡略嘅寫法。你望下呢個字，上面有個寶蓋頭「宀」，下面塞咗好多零碎嘅筆畫，睇落非常擠迫。拆碼嘅時候，字首先取寶蓋頭「宀」，佢喺 J 鍵；跟住個字身好複雜，中間嗰堆筆畫太亂太多，倉頡就用「頭尾取碼」嘅辦法，取頭之後跳中間用難鍵 X 頂住，再取最尾嘅四點火「灬」，佢喺 F 鍵，所以整個碼就係 JHXF。記住喇：見到字身塞得又密又亂，就用 X 難鍵幫你「跳過中間」，「寫」字咁多嘢寫，正好用個難字鍵扛住佢。

寶.en: Today's character is 「寶」, read bou2, meaning a treasure or jewel, and by extension anything precious or rare — as in 寶貴 bou2 gwai3, meaning valuable or to treasure. Look at its shape: there's a roof radical 宀 sitting on top, with a whole pile of things tucked underneath, exactly like a precious item locked away safe inside a house. The 字首 here is that roof 宀 on the J key; then we tackle the 字身, and because it's crowded, Cangjie's rule is to take the head, the tail, and one representative piece in between — so from the body we grab the head 一 (M), the second piece 山 (U), and the tail 八 (C), skipping the cluttered middle, giving us JMUC. Here's your hook: under the roof (J) hides one (M) mountain (U) that splits open (C) to reveal treasure — just like your son is your treasure!
寶.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「寶」，讀作 bou2，解作珍貴嘅寶物、寶石，又可以形容珍貴、罕有嘅嘢，好似「寶貴」bou2 gwai3 咁。你望下佢個樣：上面有個寶蓋頭「宀」，下面塞咗好多嘢入去，正正就係一件收埋喺屋入面嘅寶貝。呢個字嘅字首就係最頂嘅「宀」，喺 J 鍵度；跟住落嚟就要拆字身，倉頡嘅規矩係字身太複雜嘅時候要取頭、取尾、再加中間有代表性嘅一部分，所以我哋喺字身度取頭「一」（M）、第二件「山」（U）、同尾「八」（C），中間嗰嚿就跳過唔要，砌成 JMUC。記住呢個口訣：屋簷（J）之下藏住一（M）座山（U），山下分（C）出寶藏，你屋企個仔就係你嘅寶貝！

將.en: This character is 將, read "zoeng1", meaning "will" or "going to", the sense of the future — as in "我將啲書放好", where it carries the feeling of something about to be done; it can also be read "zoeng3" as in "general". Look at it: the left side is 爿 and the right side is a cluster of stacked pieces, so it divides into a head and a body. Cangjie gives the head 爿 two codes, ㄑ (V) and 一 (M); then the body on the right is too complex to take stroke by stroke, so it uses the head/second/tail method, taking ⺼ (B), 木 (D) and 寸 (I). Put together the whole thing is VMBDI — two codes for the head plus three for the body, five in all. Remember it this way: on the left, 爿 draws a ㄑ and a stroke, and on the right, top to bottom, grab head and tail — ⺼, 木, 寸 — and 將 appears.
將.zh: 呢個字係「將」，讀「zoeng1」，即係「將會」、「將來」嘅意思，好似「我將啲書放好」咁樣，帶住「就快要做」嘅語氣；佢又可以讀「zoeng3」，做「將軍」嘅將。你睇佢左邊係「爿」，右邊係一堆疊埋一齊嘅部件，所以要分做字首同字身兩截。倉頡幫呢個字左邊嘅字首「爿」揀咗兩碼，就係「ㄑ」（V）同「一」（M）；跟住右邊嘅字身太複雜，唔可以逐筆取，就用「頭、次、尾」三碼嘅辦法，取「⺼」（B）、「木」（D）同埋「寸」（I）。所以成個字砌埋就係 VMBDI，字首兩碼加字身三碼，總共五碼。記住個口訣：左邊「爿」畫個ㄑ加一橫，右邊由上到下捉頭捉尾——⺼、木、寸，「將」就出嚟喇。

專.en: Today's character is 專, read zyun1, meaning to monopolize or take sole possession, the same 專 you see in 專門店 (zyun1 mun4 dim3, a specialty or exclusive store) and 專家 (zyun1 gaa1, an expert). Look at the shape: it stacks into two parts, a head on top and the body 寸 sitting underneath. Cangjie usually caps a character at four codes, so both the head and the body have to be trimmed to their first and last pieces — the head gives 十 (J) first and 厶 (I) last, making JI, while the body 寸 gives 木 (D) first and the tiny dot 丶 (I) last, making DI. Put them together and you get the full code JIDI. To remember it, think of both halves following the same first-and-last habit — JI on top, DI below — just like the sentence 佢好專心做功課, where being 專心 means giving something your undivided, first-to-last attention.
專.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「專」，讀作 zyun1，意思係專一、獨佔，好似「專門店」（zyun1 mun4 dim3，即係只賣某種嘢嘅商店）同「專家」（zyun1 gaa1，即係某方面好叻嘅人）咁。你望住呢個字，佢分做上下兩截：上面一截係字首，下面「寸」係字身。倉頡有個規矩，一個字通常拆到最多四碼，所以字首同字身都要取捨——字首上面嗰截筆畫多，我哋淨係取頭尾兩個碼，頭係「十」（J），尾係「厶」（I），砌成 JI；字身「寸」都係取頭尾，頭係「木」（D），尾係果一點「丶」（I），砌成 DI。合埋就係 JIDI 四碼。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗住上下兩截都係「取頭尾」——上截 JI、下截 DI，一句「佢好專心做功課」，專心就係一心一意，砌碼都要一頭一尾咁專心至得。

對.en: Today we learn 對, read deoi3, meaning "correct, right," and also "facing, opposed." Look at its shape: the left part is the head and the right part is the body. For the head, you pull out two pieces — first 廿, which sits on the T key, then 土, on the G key. Cangjie limits the head to at most two codes, so once you've taken 廿土 (TG) the head is done and you don't break it down further. The body on the right is 寸, which splits into 木 (the D key) and 戈 (the I key), giving you the full code TGDI. Remember it this way: 廿土 stand on the left, 寸 breaks into 木戈 on the right — and 對 is exactly right! Think of 對於 (deoi3 jyu1) and 絕對 (zyut6 deoi3), and the code will come back to you.
對.zh: 今日我哋學「對」呢個字，讀作 deoi3，意思係「正確、啱」，又可以解「面對、相對」。你睇下佢嘅結構，左邊係字首，右邊係字身。字首嗰邊，你要拆出兩個部件：先係「廿」，喺鍵盤上係 T 鍵，跟住係「土」，係 G 鍵。倉頡有個規矩，字首最多取兩碼，所以字首取到「廿土」（TG）就夠數，唔會再拆落去。至於右邊嘅字身係「寸」，佢拆做「木」（D 鍵）同「戈」（I 鍵），所以全碼就係 TGDI。記住個口訣：廿土在左，寸邊木戈，「對」就啱晒！你可以諗下「對於」（deoi3 jyu1）同「絕對」（zyut6 deoi3），寫嘅時候就自然記得。

導.en: Today we learn 導, read dou6, meaning to guide, lead, direct or conduct — think of a tour guide leading people around. Look at it closely: it's really a 道 wrapping around a 寸 tucked underneath. When Cangjie breaks it apart, the 字首 (the 道 part) is a busy shape, so it gives up only its head and tail — head 卜 (Y) and tail 山 (U); then the 字身 (the 寸 part) also takes just head and tail — head 木 (D) and tail 戈 (I), so the full code is YUDI. Remember, once a character splits into a 字首 and a 字身, each side politely offers only its head and tail rather than every stroke — picture 道 laying out the road (YU) while 寸 stays close every inch of the way to the finish (DI).
導.zh: 我哋今日學「導」，讀音係 dou6，意思係引導、帶領、指導，例如做導遊帶人遊覽。你望吓佢，其實係一個「道」字包住個「寸」字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，字首「道」係一個複雜嘅字，所以淨係取頭尾兩碼——頭係「卜」（Y），尾係「山」（U）；跟住字身「寸」都係取頭尾兩碼——頭係「木」（D），尾係「戈」（I），所以全碼就係 YUDI。記住喇，一個字拆做字首同字身兩橛，各自都乖乖咁取頭尾，唔會全部筆畫都拆晒——你可以諗成「道路引路，寸步不離」，YU 帶你上路，DI 帶你到終點。

小.en: Today we learn 小, read siu2, meaning small, tiny, or insignificant. Look at its shape: a standing hook down the middle with a single dot on each side, like something small scattered out. This is a whole character (整體字) — it doesn't cleanly break into a 字首 part and a 字身 part, so Cangjie takes just two codes for it. The first code captures that central hook, treated as 弓, which lives on the N key; the second captures the two dots, treated as 金, which lives on the C key, giving you NC. Here's your hook: one hook and two dots, 弓 N then 金 C, and you've got the little 小 — the same one you see in 小朋友 (siu2 pang4 jau5, child) and 小學 (siu2 hok6, primary school), as in 呢隻貓好小, this cat is very small.
小.zh: 我哋今日學「小」字，讀做 siu2，即係細細粒、唔大嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣：中間一條企鈎，兩邊各一點，好似一樣好細嘅嘢周圍散開咁。呢個字係一個「整體字」，冇得清清楚楚分做字首同字身兩橛，所以倉頡淨係取兩碼就夠。第一碼取中間嗰條鈎，我哋當佢係「弓」，喺鍵盤上係 N；第二碼取兩點，當佢係「金」，喺鍵盤上係 C，合埋就係 NC。記住喇：一鈎兩點，弓 N 金 C，就係細細粒嘅「小」。你可以喺「小朋友」（siu2 pang4 jau5）同「小學」（siu2 hok6）度見到佢，好似「呢隻貓好小」咁用。

少.en: Today's character is 少, read siu2 or siu3, meaning "few, less, inadequate" — you see it in 少少, meaning a little bit, and in 至少, meaning at least. Look at the shape: on top sits a 小, and beneath it hangs a single falling stroke, so the whole thing reads like 小 with one extra slash added. In Cangjie, 少 is treated as a whole character (整體字), which means we don't chop it into many small pieces — instead we take just the head and the tail, two codes only. The head is 小 on the F key, and the tail is that lone falling stroke 丿 on the H key, giving you FH; the whole-character rule keeps it to first-and-last, dropping anything in the middle for a clean, distinctive code. Remember it this way: write the 小 first (F), then sweep down the final stroke (H) — just a little, and 少 is done.
少.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「少」，讀作 siu2 或者 siu3，意思係「少、唔多、不足夠」，好似「少少」係一點點，「至少」就係最起碼咁多。你望下呢個字：上面係一個「小」字，下面加咗一撇，成個字睇起嚟就係「小」再多一劃咁。喺倉頡入面，「少」係一個整體字，我哋唔會逐部件拆到好散，而係取頭同尾兩碼——頭係「小」，喺 F 鍵，尾係嗰一撇「丿」，喺 H 鍵，所以個碼就係 FH。點解淨係取兩碼呢？因為整體字有個規矩，就係只取首尾兩個部分，中間唔理，咁樣夠簡潔又夠獨特。記住喇：先寫個「小」（F），再掃低最後嗰撇（H），少少兩下就打起「少」喇。

尖.en: Today we're learning 尖, read zim1, meaning sharp or pointed — like the tip of a pencil or a needle. Take a good look at its shape, because it tells the whole story: on top sits 小 (small), and underneath sits 大 (big), so something wide at the bottom narrows up to a fine point, and that pointedness is exactly what the character means. In Cangjie, 尖 is treated as a whole shape, so instead of breaking it into many little bits, we simply take the first and last pieces: the top 小, typed with F, and the bottom 大, typed with K. That gives you the tidy code FK, just two keys. Remember it this way: small on top, big below — a shape that tapers to a sharp point is 尖.
尖.zh: 今日我哋學「尖」呢個字，讀做 zim1，意思係尖銳、尖端，好似支筆或者針嘅頂端咁尖。你望下佢個樣，其實好有意思：上面係「小」，下面係「大」——小嘅喺上，大嘅喺下，就好似一件嘢由闊變窄、收成一個尖點咁樣，個意思自然就出嚟喇。喺倉頡入面，「尖」係一個整體字，唔會拆成好多細件，我哋淨係取頭尾兩個部分，即係開頭嘅「小」（F）同結尾嘅「大」（K），所以個碼就係 FK 兩個掣。你可以記住：頂尖係小，底部係大——上小下大，就係「尖」。

尚.en: Today we learn 尚, read soeng6, meaning "still, yet, rather" — you'll see it in 高尚 gou1 soeng6, meaning affluent and refined, or 時尚 si4 soeng6, meaning chic and fashionable. Look at the shape: it's a whole form (整體字), which means instead of chopping it up in fine detail, we simply take the first, middle, and last pieces and skip whatever sits in between. The first piece is the little top dots ⺌ on the F key, then the enclosing frame 冂 on the B key, and finally the mouth 口 at the bottom on the R key, giving you FBR. Because it's a whole form, you don't have to count every stroke — you just grab the head, the middle, and the tail. Remember it top to bottom: ⺌F, then 冂B, then 口R, reading straight down the character.
尚.zh: 今日我哋學「尚」呢個字，讀作 soeng6，佢有「仍然、還」嘅意思，好似「高尚」gou1 soeng6 咁解富有雅致，又或者「時尚」si4 soeng6 解時髦入時。你望住個字，佢係一個整體字，即係話唔會拆得太仔細，而係取頭、中、尾三個部件跳過中間嘅。第一筆係頂上嘅小點「⺌」，喺 F 鍵；跟住係中間包住嘅框「冂」，喺 B 鍵；最後係下面嗰個「口」，喺 R 鍵，砌埋一齊就係 FBR。因為佢係整體字，我哋只需要記住頭中尾三粒，中間夾住嘅部分就唔理佢，所以你唔使數盡每一筆——記住「⺌F 冂B 口R」，由上而下一望到底就得㗎喇。

就.en: Today's character is 就, read zau6, a very common word meaning "just" or "simply," and it can also mean to come, to go to, or to approach — as in 我食完就走, "I'll leave right after eating." The character splits into a left side and a right side: the head is 京 and the body is 尤. For the head 京 we don't take every piece, only the first and the last — the top 亠 (Y) and the 小 (F) beneath it, giving the head's two codes YF. The body 尤 then takes head, second, and last: 戈 (I), 大 (K), and 山 (U), so the whole code reads YFIKU. Remember it this way: the capital 京 gives you first-and-last, while 尤 gives you head-second-last, and together they build 就.
就.zh: 今日學嘅字係「就」，讀音zau6，係好常用嘅字，意思係「就係」、「即刻」，又可以解「去到」、「接近」，好似「我食完就走」咁樣。呢個字分做左右兩橛：字首係「京」，字身係「尤」。「京」呢個部分我哋唔會全部拆晒，只係拆頭同尾——最頂嘅「亠」（Y），再加下面嘅「小」（F），呢個就係字首要嘅頭尾兩碼YF。至於字身「尤」，就要拆頭、二、尾三碼：先係「戈」（I），再係「大」（K），最後係「山」（U），砌埋成YFIKU。記住喇：京城取頭尾，尤字取頭二尾，「就」字就係咁砌成。

尼.en: Today's character is 尼, read nei4, which originally means a Buddhist nun — a woman who has left home for religious life — though you'll often see it used to transliterate foreign sounds, as in 印尼 (short for Indonesia) or 尼斯 (the French city Nice). Look at how it's built: the shape that wraps across the top and down the left is 尸, which sits on the S key, and the small piece tucked into the lower right is 匕, which is on the P key. Why does it split this way? Because 尼 is a 尸-radical character, so we take the radical 尸 as the head first (S), and whatever remains — here just 匕 — becomes the body (P), giving you the full code SP. Picture the nunnery in the sentence 呢間係尼姑庵: the 尸 roof up top with 匕 hiding beneath it, S then P, and the nun appears.
尼.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「尼」，讀做 nei4，本來解作尼姑，即係女嘅出家人，好多時亦都攞嚟做外文音譯，好似「印尼」（印度尼西亞嘅簡稱）同埋「尼斯」（法國嗰個城市 Nice）。你留意吓個字嘅結構：上面同左邊圍住嘅係一個「尸」字，喺鍵盤上打 S；入面右下角嗰粒係「匕」，喺鍵盤上打 P。點解要咁樣拆呢？因為「尼」係一個尸部字，我哋就先取個部首「尸」做字首（S），跟住將剩低嘅「匕」做字身（P），所以成個碼就係 SP。記住呢句「呢間係尼姑庵」，你就會諗起「尸」字頭下面藏住個「匕」，S 先 P 後，尼姑就出嚟喇。

局.en: Today we learn 局, read "guk6", meaning a government bureau or office — as in 教育局, the Education Bureau, or 當局, the authorities — and it can also mean a situation or circumstance. Look at the shape: there's a 尸 on top that wraps around the pieces underneath. In Cangjie we split it like this: the top 尸 is the 字首, which lives on the S key; then the inner 勹口 forms the 字身, and from a 字身 we take only its first and last pieces, so 勹 gives S and the 口 at the bottom gives R. That's why the full code is S, S, R and not every stroke inside — once a character has a clear head piece, the body contributes at most its opening and closing shapes. Remember it as 尸 on top plus the 勹口 inside, three taps SSR, and you've typed the 局 in "I go to the post office to send a letter".
局.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「局」，讀「guk6」，即係政府嘅部門或者辦事處，好似「教育局」同「當局」咁；「局」都可以解作局面、情勢。你望下呢個字，上面係一個「尸」字，包住下面嘅嘢。倉頡拆法係咁：字首取最上面嘅「尸」，佢喺個鍵盤上係S鍵；跟住入面嘅「勹口」就係字身，我哋取字身頭同尾兩個碼，先攞「勹」畀個S碼，再攞底下嘅「口」畀R碼，所以成個字砌埋就係S、S、R。點解字身淨係取頭尾兩碼呢？因為當一個字有明顯嘅字首之後，字身最多都係取頭同尾，唔會逐件全取，所以「勹口」淨係得S同R兩碼。記住呢個「尸」頭配「勹口」尾，SSR三下，就砌到「我去郵政局寄信」個「局」喇。

居.en: Today we're learning 居, read geoi1, which means to live or dwell — as in 鄰居 (leon4 geoi1), the neighbor who lives next to you, or 居民 (geoi1 man4), the residents who live in a place. Look at the shape: there's a 尸 draped over the top and left, wrapping around a 古 tucked inside. When Cangjie breaks this apart, 尸 is the 字首, the leading part, and a single piece like this gives just one code, S; then the 古 inside is the 字身, the body, and a body is allowed to take its first and last pieces — so we grab the head 十 (J) and the tail 口 (R), skipping whatever sits between. Put them in order and you get 尸 (S), 十 (J), 口 (R), which is SJR. Here's your memory hook: one 尸 drapes over one 古, so start with S, then finish with a 十 and a 口 — S, J, R.
居.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「居」，讀作 geoi1，意思係居住、生活嘅意思，好似「鄰居」（leon4 geoi1）就係住喺你隔籬嘅人，「居民」（geoi1 man4）就係住喺一個地方嘅人。你睇下呢個字嘅結構：外面係一個「尸」字披住，包住入面一個「古」字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，「尸」係字首，一個部件淨係取一碼，就係 S；而入面嘅「古」係字身，字身可以取到頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋取佢個頭「十」（J）同個尾「口」（R），中間嗰啲就跳過唔取。合埋一齊就係 尸（S）、十（J）、口（R），即係 SJR。記住喇：一個「尸」披住一個「古」，S 開頭，尾尾就係一「十」一「口」，你就記得晒喇！
