屋.en: Today we meet 屋, read uk1, meaning a house, a room, or a home — a place that gives you shelter. Look at its shape: on top sits the piece 尸, and underneath is the character 至. When Cangjie breaks it apart, the head 尸 contributes just its one key, S; then we turn to the body 至, and because a body can't hand over every stroke, we follow the 'first two, last one' rule — taking the opening pieces 一 (M) and 厶 (I), then the final piece 土 (G), giving the full code SMIG. The split falls this way because 尸 is the head and 至 is the body, and a body only gives part of itself rather than every code. Remember it like this: a 尸 roof shelters a 至 — that's where your home (屋企) lives.
屋.zh: 今日我哋學個「屋」字，讀做 uk1，即係房屋、屋企嘅意思，係遮風擋雨嘅地方。你望下佢嘅結構：上面係一個「尸」字頭，下面就係一個「至」字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，字首個「尸」淨係取佢一碼，就係 S；跟住落嚟拆字身個「至」，唔可以逐碼全取，要跟「頭二尾一」嘅規矩，即係取頭兩碼「一」M 同「厶」I，再取最尾一碼「土」G，所以全碼就係 SMIG。點解字身要咁樣減碼呢？因為佢係字身，唔係字首，取碼有配額，唔會成個字全取。記住個口訣：尸頭遮住一個「至」，屋企就喺呢個「至」裏面。

展.en: Today's character is 展, read zin2, and it means to open, to unfold, to stretch or extend — you hear it in 發展 (faat3 zin2), development or growth, and in 展示 (zin2 si6), to display or show something to people. Look at the whole shape: the big frame across the top is 尸, and because it sits as the prefix it gives us the first key, S. What's left underneath is the body of the character, and in Cangjie a body takes at most two codes — its head and its tail — so we take the head 廿, which is T, and the tail 女, which is V, giving us STV in all. Remember the order this way: 尸 caps the top, then 廿 leads and 女 closes the bottom — S, T, V, unfolding one piece at a time.
展.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「展」，讀做 zin2，意思係打開、展開、伸展，好似「發展」faat3 zin2 咁講進步同成長，又或者「展示」zin2 si6 咁講擺出嚟畀人睇。你望吓成個字，最外面上邊嗰個大大嘅框係「尸」，佢做字首，所以第一個碼就取「尸」嘅 S。跟住落嚟嘅係下面嗰嚿字身，倉頡取字身嘅時候最多取頭尾兩碼，所以我哋取佢個頭「廿」嘅 T，再取佢個尾「女」嘅 V，合埋就係 STV。記住個順序：先有「尸」蓋住上面，下面再由「廿」帶頭、「女」收尾——尸、廿、女，S、T、V，一步一步展開。

層.en: This character is 層, read cang4 — the very same sound as 曾 — and it means a story, a layer, a floor or a stratum, like the third floor of a building. Look at its shape: the 尸 sits across the top like a roof, sheltering the 曾 tucked underneath. In Cangjie the 尸 is the 字首 (the leading part) and gives us S, while the 曾 below is the 字身 (the body); a 字身 is coded by its head, its second piece and its tail, so from 曾 we take 八 as C, 囗 as W and 日 as A, giving the full code SCWA. Remember it this way: one 尸 roof S covering a 曾 that breaks into C, W, A — and under that roof, the floors stack up neatly.
層.zh: 呢個字係「層」，讀音同「曾」一樣，讀 cang4，意思係樓層、層次，即係一層一層咁疊上去嘅意思，好似大廈嘅三層樓噉。你望下佢個樣，上面係個「尸」字頭，包住下面嘅「曾」。倉頡拆呢個字，字首就係「尸」，取佢個鍵 S；跟住嘅「曾」係字身，字身取碼取頭、二、尾，所以由「曾」入面順住拆出「八」C、「囗」W、同埋「日」A，合埋就係 SCWA。記住喇：一個「尸」字頭 S，罩住一個「曾」拆成 C、W、A，你就記得三層樓喺呢個字入面疊得整整齊齊。

屬.en: Today we learn 屬, read suk6, the word you see in 金屬 meaning "metal" — its core sense is class, category, or type, and it also means "to belong to," as in falling under a certain group. Look at the shape: the outer 尸 hangs over the top and left like a bent ruler, while a cluster of pieces is packed inside. Because this is an enclosing structure, the outer 尸 (S) acts as the prefix and gives just one code; the stuff tucked inside is the body, and for the body you take first-second-last — the first 卜 (Y), the second 卜 (Y), and the final 戈 (I) — building SYYI. Picture one 尸 sheltering two little 卜 dots and one sweeping 戈, and you'll always know which category 屬 belongs to.
屬.zh: 今日我哋學「屬」字，讀作 suk6，喺「金屬」呢個詞入面就係「金屬」嘅意思，指類別、種類，又可以解作「屬於」——即係歸入邊一類、係邊個嘅。你望吓個字，外邊有個「尸」，好似一把橫住嘅尺咁罩住上面同左邊，入面就塞住一堆嘢。呢個係包圍結構，所以外邊嘅「尸」（S）做字首，只取一碼；跟住入面就係字身，字身要取頭二尾，即係頭「卜」（Y）、第二個「卜」（Y）、最尾嘅「戈」（I），砌埋成 SYYI。你記住：一個尸罩住，入面兩粒卜再加一撇戈，「屬於」邊一類就一目了然啦。

屯.en: Today we're learning the character 屯, read "tyun4", meaning a village or hamlet, a camp or a garrison station — and for someone in Hong Kong the most familiar sight of it is surely the district name Tuen Mun, 屯門. Look closely at this character: it's all tangled into a single knot, a horizontal stroke and a vertical hook curling together, with no clean place to slice it into left-right or top-bottom halves. Because of that, Cangjie treats 屯 as one whole shape, a 整體字, and instead of breaking it into every part we simply take the first and last pieces: the first is 匕 on the P key, and the last is 山 on the U key. Put them together and the whole code is just PU, two keys and done. Remember it this way — the 屯 of Tuen Mun grabs its head and tail, 匕 (P) leading to 山 (U), giving you PU.
屯.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「屯」，讀「tyun4」，意思係村莊、營寨、駐守嘅地方，香港人最熟悉嘅一定係屯門呢個地名喇。你望吓呢個字，成個緊緊纏埋一齊，寫落去似一橫加上一豎再彎起，好難拆成清清楚楚嘅左右或者上下兩橛，所以倉頡當佢係一個「整體字」。遇到整體字，我哋唔會逐部件拆到散晒，而係淨係取「頭尾」兩碼：頭係「匕」，個鍵係 P；尾係「山」，個鍵係 U，砌埋就係 PU，齊活。記住喇——屯門嘅屯，一頭一尾，匕（P）帶住山（U），就係 PU。

山.en: Look at this character: 山, read "saan1", meaning mountain, hill, or peak — a shape every Hongkonger knows well. Notice its form: a tall stroke standing in the middle with a point rising on each side, just like the outline of a mountain ridge seen from afar. In Cangjie, 山 is itself a complete radical, so there is nothing to break apart — it is coded with a single key, U, and that lone U is the whole code. Because it is one self-contained radical, there is no question of splitting it into a lead part and a body; when you see the whole 山, you simply press U. Remember it this way: one mountain, one U, as clear as a single glance at Lantau Island or Ma On Shan on the horizon.
山.zh: 睇下呢個字：山，讀「saan1」，意思就係山、山峰、山丘，係香港人最熟悉唔過嘅一個字啦。你留意佢個樣：中間一豎企起身，兩邊各有一個角，就好似遠處望過去嘅山嶺輪廓咁，形神俱備。喺倉頡入面，山本身就係一個完整嘅字根，唔使拆開，一碼就搞掂，佢對應嘅鍵就係 U，所以整個字嘅碼就係 U 一個掣。因為佢係一個獨立字根，唔存在字首字身嘅拆分問題，你見到成個山就直接㩒 U 好啦。記住：一座山，一個 U，簡單到似遠望大嶼山、馬鞍山嗰陣嘅一眼清晰。

岸.en: Today's character is 岸, read ngon6, meaning the land at the edge of a river or sea — the shore or coast, as in 海岸 (seacoast) and 口岸 (a trading port). Look at it: sitting on top is 山, the mountain shape, which is your head piece — press U. Underneath sits the body, built from three pieces: 厂, a cliff-like top shape, pressed with M; then a single horizontal 一, also M; and finally 十, pressed with J. Put together, the full code is UMMJ. The body splits this way because when a body has several pieces, Cangjie doesn't take every one — it takes the head piece plus the last two, the head-second-last rule, so 厂, 一, 十 give exactly MMJ. Picture a mountain (山) resting on the rocky shore while the water runs past its foot.
岸.zh: 今日學嘅字係「岸」，讀做 ngon6，即係江河海邊嘅陸地，好似「海岸」、「口岸」入面嘅意思。你望下佢，上面坐住一座「山」，係佢嘅字首，你要㩒 U。下面係字身，由三件砌埋一齊：「厂」係一個廠字頭形，㩒 M；跟住一橫「一」，同樣㩒 M；最後係「十」，㩒 J。整個字嘅碼就係 UMMJ。點解字身要咁樣拆呢？因為字身唔止一件嘢嘅時候，我哋唔會逐件全部取碼，而係取頭一件同埋尾二件——即係「頭、二、尾」，所以字身喺「厂、一、十」三件度剛好取晒 MMJ。記住個畫面：一座「山」壓喺岸邊嘅石頭上面，水就喺山腳流過。

島.en: Today we learn the character 島, read dou2, which means an island — a piece of land in the middle of the sea. Look at its shape: it's like a bird resting above a mountain, and that's exactly how its pieces come together. In Cangjie, 島 is a whole-character (整體字), meaning it can't be cleanly divided into a head part and a body part, so we use the whole-character method: head, second, third, and tail. Following that rule we take, in order, 竹 (H), 日 (A), 卜 (Y), and 山 (U), giving us HAYU. You'll meet this character in 半島, which in Hong Kong usually means the Peninsula Hotel in Tsimshatsui, and in 島嶼, meaning islands — so remember: a bird (竹日卜) perched on a mountain (山) is an island!
島.zh: 今日我哋學「島」呢個字，讀音係 dou2，即係海中間嘅一塊陸地。你望下佢個樣，上面好似隻雀鳥停喺一座山之上，其實佢就係由呢啲部件砌成。喺倉頡入面，「島」係一個整體字，即係話佢唔可以清清楚楚咁分做字首同字身兩截，所以我哋要用整體字嘅取碼方法——頭、二、三、尾。順住呢個規則，我哋順序取：竹（H）、日（A）、卜（Y）、山（U），砌埋一齊就係 HAYU。記住呢個字唔止見喺地圖，「半島」就係尖沙咀嗰間半島酒店，而「島嶼」就係一串島嘅意思。記個口訣：竹日卜山，一隻鳥停喺山頂就係「島」！

嶺.en: Today we're learning 嶺, read ling5, meaning a mountain ridge or peak — you'll spot it in place names like 粉嶺 (Fanling) up in the northern New Territories. Look at the shape and you'll see it stacks top over bottom: the 山 sits on top, and 領 sits underneath. That top 山 is a standalone piece, and as the 字首 it contributes just one code, U. The 領 below is the 字身, and though its own full code is OIMBC, a 字身 doesn't hand over everything — instead you take its head, second, and tail, which are 人 (O), 戈 (I), and 金 (C), so the whole character comes together as UOIC. Here's your memory hook: one mountain, 山, leading 人-戈-金 up the ridge to see the view — U, O, I, C.
嶺.zh: 我哋今日學「嶺」呢個字，讀音係 ling5，即係山脊、山頂嘅意思，好似「粉嶺」呢個新界北嘅地方就用到佢。你望住個字，會見到佢係上下結構：頂部係個「山」，下面就係「領」。頭嗰個「山」係一個獨立部件，取碼淨係要一碼，就係 U。跟住落嚟嘅「領」係字身，佢自己嘅完整碼係 OIMBC，但做字身嗰陣唔會全部攞晒，而係按規矩取佢嘅頭、二同尾——頭係「人」O，第二個係「戈」I，最尾係「金」C，所以合埋成個字就係 UOIC。記住呢個口訣：一座山，領住人、戈、金上山嶺睇景，你就唔會撈亂喇！

川.en: Today we learn 川, read "cyun1," which means a stream or river, the flow of water — it's the same 川 you see in 四川, Sichuan. Take a look at its shape: it's simply three upright vertical strokes standing side by side, like three currents of water flowing downward together. Each of those three strokes is 中(丨), which lives on the L key, so you just press L three times, LLL, to type 川. Why can we take the code so straightforwardly, stroke by stroke? Because 川 is a whole-form character — there's no splitting into 字首 and 字身; you just read it from start to finish, and every one of the three strokes is 丨. Remember it this way: three flowing streams, three L's — 川 is LLL.
川.zh: 今日我哋學「川」呢個字，讀「cyun1」，意思係河流、水流嘅意思，你成日見到嘅「四川」個「川」就係佢。你望吓佢個樣，其實就係三條企直嘅豎筆並埋一齊，好似三道水流順住流落嚟咁。呢三筆每一筆都係中(丨)，喺鍵盤上面就係 L 呢個掣，所以你只要打三次 L，即係 LLL，就打得出「川」喇。點解可以咁簡單順住取碼呢？因為「川」係一個整體字，唔使拆字首字身，直接由頭到尾順住三筆逐筆取碼就得，每筆都係丨。記住喇：三道水流，三個 L，川就係 LLL。

州.en: Today we're learning 州, read "zau1," meaning an administrative division or state — you see it in place names like 潮州 (Chaozhou) and 加州 (California). Look at the character: it's really a run of strokes lined up side by side, and Cangjie treats it as a whole-character (整體字). Because it's a whole-character, there's no splitting into a head and a body — you simply take four strokes in writing order from start to finish: first a dot 丶 (I), then a vertical 丨 (L), then another dot 丶 (I), and finally another vertical 丨 (L), giving I L I L. The reason the code works this way is that a whole-character can't be broken apart, so the rule is to take the strokes in the order you write them, and here the four dots-and-verticals fill the code neatly. Here's your memory hook: two pairs of "dot plus vertical," tapping I L I L straight across.
州.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「州」字，讀「zau1」，即係行政區劃嘅單位，好似潮州、加州咁。你望下呢個字，其實係由幾筆順住排開嘅結構，倉頡就當佢係一個整體字。因為佢係整體字，我哋唔使分字首字身，直接由頭到尾攞四個筆形就得：先係一點丶（I），再一豎丨（L），跟住又一點丶（I），最後又一豎丨（L），砌埋就係 I L I L。點解要咁攞？因為整體字冇得再拆開，倉頡規定順住寫嘅次序取碼，一點一豎一點一豎剛好四個，齊晒。記憶竅門好簡單：兩對「點加豎」，一路 I L I L 咁跳落去就得喇。

工.en: Today's character is 「工」, read gung1, meaning labor or work, and also a worker or laborer. Look at its shape: a flat stroke on top, a single vertical stroke straight down the middle, and another flat stroke at the bottom — a simple picture of a tool. To type it we follow three pieces in order: the top stroke 一 is on key M, the middle vertical 丨 is on key L, and the bottom stroke 一 is on key M again, giving you the full code MLM. Why does it break up this way? Because 「工」 is a whole-form character with no head-and-body split, so we simply follow the Cangjie rule and take the head M, the second piece L, and the tail M — three codes and you're done. Remember it as flat, upright, flat, M-L-M, like a worker driving a post down with a bar clamped top and bottom.
工.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「工」，讀gung1，意思係勞工、工作，或者做嘢嘅工人。你望吓佢個樣：上面一橫，中間一豎直落，下面又一橫，好似一件工具嘅簡單樣。拆碼嘅時候，我哋跟住三個部件嚟打：頭嗰橫係一，鍵係M；中間嗰豎係丨，鍵係L；尾嗰橫又係一，鍵仲係M，所以成個碼就係MLM。點解係咁拆呢？因為「工」係一個整體字，冇分字首字身嘅界線，我哋就照倉頡嘅取碼規矩攞頭M、二L、尾M，一共三碼就搞掂。記住個口訣：一橫、一豎、一橫，M-L-M，就好似工人一鎚落去，上下夾實中間嘅一條柱咁。

己.en: Today's character is 己, read gei2, meaning "self" or "oneself" — the very word in 自己. Look at the shape: it's a single-body character, one connected unit that you can't neatly break into a left-right or top-bottom pair of solid pieces. For a single-body character like this, Cangjie takes only the head and the tail, ignoring whatever sits in between. So the first code is the upper piece written as 尸, keyed S, and the second is the lower hooked piece written as 山, keyed U — together SU. Remember it this way: a 尸 sitting over a 山, S at the head and U at the tail, and that's your own 己.
己.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「己」，讀音係 gei2，意思係「自己」、「本身」，好似「自己」呢個詞噉。你望住個字，佢係一個獨體字，冇辦法分做左右或者上下兩嚿實實在在嘅部件。遇到呢種獨體字，倉頡嘅做法就係「拆頭尾」，即係只取最頭同最尾兩個形，中間唔理。所以第一個碼係字形上半個「尸」，鍵係 S；第二個碼係字形下半嗰個好似「山」嘅彎鈎，鍵係 U，合埋就係 SU。記住喇：一個「尸」壓住一個「山」，S 頭 U 尾，就係你自己嘅「己」。

已.en: Today's character is 已, read ji5, meaning 'already', 'finished' or 'stop' — as in the sentence 我已經食完飯, 'I have already finished eating'. Look at its shape: it's a single-body character with no clear left-right or top-bottom division, so we split it into a head piece and a tail piece and take one shape from each. The head is 尸, typed with S, and the closing hook and curve at the bottom are read as the shape 山, typed with U, so the full code for 已 is simply SU. Remember it this way: 尸 opens, 山 closes — S then U — and you've 'already' got it!
已.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「已」，讀作 ji5，意思係「已經」、「完成」、「停止」，好似「我已經食完飯」入面咁用。你望吓呢個字，佢係一個獨體字，冇明顯分開嘅左右或者上下兩橛，所以我哋用拆頭尾嘅方法，先攞開頭嘅形，再攞埋尾嘅形。開頭嗰橛係「尸」，撳 S 鍵；跟住個尾收埋嘅一勾一彎，就當作「山」，撳 U 鍵，所以「已」嘅全碼就係 SU。記住喇：「尸」字起頭、「山」字收尾，S 頭 U 尾，「已經」學咗喇！

巴.en: Today's character is 巴, read baa1, which originally means to greatly desire or anxiously hope for something, though you'll know it best from the loanword 巴士, the bus you ride every day. Look at 巴: it's a connected form, one shape whose parts all run into each other without a clean break, and for cases like this Cangjie has a simple rule — take the head and take the tail. The head is 日, typed with the key A, and the tail is that upward-opening 凵 shape at the bottom, typed with the key U. That gives you the whole code, A then U, and the reason you take only two pieces is that a connected form isn't broken down bit by bit — just the head and the tail are enough. Memory hook: to catch the 巴 bus, the sun (日) sits on top and the little basin (凵) holds it below, so A U and you're on board.
巴.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「巴」，讀做 baa1，本義係熱切咁想要、渴望嘅意思，不過你最熟嘅一定係「巴士」呢個外來詞——就係你日日搭嘅嗰架車。你望下「巴」呢個字，佢係一個連體字，成個黐埋一齊、拆唔開清晰嘅部件，遇到呢種情況倉頡就有個辦法：取頭同取尾。個頭係「日」，撳 A 呢個鍵；個尾係下面嗰個開口向上嘅「凵」字形，撳 U 呢個鍵。所以「巴」嘅編碼就係 A、U 兩個字母，簡簡單單。之所以淨係要頭同尾，係因為連體字唔會逐嚿拆晒，只需要頭尾兩個位就夠。記住喇：搭「巴」士，日頭出門口，凵字兜住底，A U 兩下就搞掂。

市.en: Today's character is 市, read si5, and it means a market or fair, and by extension a city or town — you'll see it in words like 城市 sing4 si5, "city," and 街市 gaai1 si5, the wet market where you buy groceries. Look at the shape: there's a little lid 亠 on top, and below it sits the cloth radical 巾. In Cangjie this is a whole character (整體字), which means we don't chop 巾 into a tangle of separate head and body pieces — we simply read down the form in order. So we take the top 亠 first, which lives on the Y key, then from 巾 we grab just its head and tail, giving L then the final B — put together that's Y, L, B. Picture it this way: a little hat on top (亠 Y) with a cloth 巾 hanging beneath, and you catch it by the head and the tail — that's 市.
市.zh: 你今日學嘅字係「市」，讀作 si5，指市場、市集，又可以指城市、市鎮，好似「城市」sing4 si5 同「街市」gaai1 si5 咁。你睇下呢個字，上面頂住一個「亠」，落面就係一個「巾」字。喺倉頡入面，我哋叫佢做整體字，即係話唔會將個「巾」拆到分頭分身咁複雜，而係順住個形一路取落去。所以先取最頂嘅「亠」，佢喺 Y 掣度；跟住個「巾」我哋只取頭尾兩碼，個頭係「L」，最尾就係「B」，合埋一齊就得出 Y、L、B。記住一個畫面：頭上一頂帽仔（亠 Y），下面掛住一塊布巾（巾），一頭一尾捉住就係「市」喇。

布.en: Today's character is 布, read bou3, meaning cotton cloth, textiles, or linen — the same 布 you see in 宣布, to declare. Look at the whole shape: on top there's a slanting cover made of a short stroke and a horizontal, and underneath sits the piece 巾, cloth. Cangjie takes the head ナ first, pressing K; then it moves to the body, the 巾 below, and because 巾 is a full component you can't just grab half of it — instead you take its first and last strokes, the central 中 as L and 月 as B, giving you K L B. Here's your hook: a slanting cover draped over a hanging cloth — K opens, L in the middle, B closes — and that's your piece of 布.
布.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「布」，讀 bou3，即係棉布、布料、麻布嗰種「布」，宣布嘅「布」都係佢。你望吓成個字，上面有一撇一橫嘅斜蓋，下面就係一個「巾」字。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，先取字首嗰個ナ，撳 K；跟住落到字身，就係下面個「巾」，因為佢係一個完整嘅部件，唔可以只取一半，所以要「取頭尾」——頭取中間嗰一豎「中」撳 L，尾取「月」撳 B，合埋就係 KLB。記住嘅竅門：一撇蓋住一條巾，K 起頭、L 中、B 收尾，掛喺度就係一塊布喇。

希.en: Today we learn 希, read hei1, which means to hope or expect — as in 我希望聽日晴天, "I hope tomorrow is sunny." Look at its shape: up top there's a little cross-stroke 乂 followed by 一撇一橫 forming ナ, and beneath them sits the cloth character 巾 with an upright piercing through the middle. To split it we divide the character into a head and a body: the top is the head, and a head takes at most two codes, so we grab 乂 (K) and ナ (K) — exactly two codes filled. What remains below, 巾, is the body, and a body gives its first and last pieces, 丨 (L) and 巾 (B), so the full code is KKLB. Memory hook: two crosses stacked on top (KK), then one upright threading the cloth below (LB), and you've got the 希 of 希望.
希.zh: 今日我哋學「希」呢個字，讀做 hei1，喺「希望」入面就係盼望、期待嘅意思，例如「我希望聽日晴天」。你睇吓佢個樣，上面有個像交叉嘅乂，跟住一撇一橫嘅ナ，下邊就係一個巾字，中間一豎穿落嚟。拆碼嘅時候，我哋將個字分做字首同字身：上部係字首，字首最多取兩碼，所以取乂（K）同ナ（K），啱啱兩碼；淨返下邊個巾就係字身，字身取頭同尾兩碼，即係丨（L）同巾（B），合埋就係 KKLB。記住個口訣：上面兩個交叉重疊（KK），下面一豎串起條巾（LB），咁樣「希」就係希望嘅希喇。

師.en: Today's character 師 reads si1 and means a teacher or master, and it can also mean troops or a multitude. Look at how it splits into a left side and a right side: the left is the 字首 (lead), the right is the 字身 (body). A 字首 can contribute at most two codes, so from the left piece you take only its head and tail — the head is the bamboo shape ⺮ (H) and the tail is the mouth shape 口 (R), while the vertical stroke in the middle is skipped. Then the right piece 帀 acts as the 字身, which allows up to three codes, so you take head, second, and tail: the head 一 (M), the second stroke 中 (L), and the flesh-moon shape ⺼ (B), giving you HRMLB in full. Your memory hook: bamboo-and-mouth catch the two ends on the left, then read the right side top to bottom as one-middle-moon — try it on 老師 (teacher) and 咖啡師 (barista) and it'll stick.
師.zh: 今日學嘅「師」字讀 si1，即係老師、師傅嘅意思，亦都可以解軍隊、群眾。你睇下佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係字首，右邊係字身。倉頡拆字有個規矩，字首最多取兩碼，所以左邊呢一嚿只攞頭同尾——頭係竹形嘅⺮（H），尾係口形嘅口（R），中間嗰豎就跳過唔取。跟住右邊個「帀」做字身，字身最多攞三碼，就取頭、二、尾：頭係一（M），第二係中間嗰豎中（L），最尾係月肉形嘅⺼（B），合埋成 HRMLB。記住呢個口訣：左邊竹口一頭一尾，右邊一中月從上數到底，例如「老師」、「咖啡師」，你就唔會拆錯喇。

席.en: Today's character is 席, read "zik6", meaning a seat, a mat, or a banquet — think of 主席 as the person in the head seat, the chairperson, and 出席 as showing up to attend. Look at its shape: on top is 广, the sheltering roof, which is the I key; tucked inside is 廿, the T key; below that comes a single vertical stroke 丨, the L key; and right at the bottom sits 巾, the B key. Because 席 is an integrated character with many strokes, Cangjie doesn't break every piece apart — instead it uses the head-second-third-tail rule, taking only the first, second, third and very last pieces while skipping whatever sits in the middle, giving us 广, 廿, 丨, 巾, which spells ITLB. Here's your memory hook: under the 广 canopy, grab the head, the second, the third and the trailing 巾, and let the middle go — that's how you weave a 席.
席.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「席」，讀「zik6」，即係坐嘅蓆、座位，又或者係宴會嘅意思，好似「主席」就係坐首位嗰個人，「出席」就係去到場。你望吓佢個樣，上面係「广」字頭，係 I 掣，包住下面嘅嘢；入面有個「廿」，係 T 掣，再落嚟有一豎「丨」，係 L 掣，最底就係「巾」字，係 B 掣。因為「席」係一個整體字，筆畫太多，倉頡唔會逐件拆晒，而係用「頭二三尾」嘅方法，只取頭嗰件、第二件、第三件同埋最尾嗰件，中間嘅就跳過唔要，所以就係 广、廿、丨、巾，砌埋一齊就係 ITLB。記住呢個口訣：广字帳篷之下，攞頭、二、三同埋個尾巾，中間唔理佢，就砌得成一張「席」喇。

帶.en: Today we learn 帶, read "daai3", the belt or strap you wear, and it can also mean a zone or band of land. Look at its shape: crowded pieces up top with a cloth 巾 hanging below — a busy, complicated character. This is a whole-character split, so we don't divide it into head and body; instead we follow the head-2nd-3rd-last rule. We take the head 卄 as K, the second piece 匕 as P, the third piece 冖 as B, then skip over the middle and grab the last two — 巾 as L and 冂 as B — giving the full code KPBLB. Why skip the middle? Cangjie allows only five keys, so for a dense whole character it keeps the first three and the final two. Remember the line "remember to bring an umbrella" — the umbrella cloth 巾 sits under the crowded top: KPBLB.
帶.zh: 今日我哋學「帶」呢個字，讀「daai3」，即係腰帶、皮帶嗰條帶，又可以解作一區地帶。你望吓佢個樣，上面密密麻麻、下面有把巾咁,係一個結構複雜嘅字。呢個字係整體字，唔會分開字首字身,而係跟「頭二三尾」嘅規矩嚟拆：先取頭嘅「卄」係 K,再取第二嘅「匕」係 P,第三嘅「冖」係 B,跟住跳過中間唔理，直接拎最後嘅兩件——「巾」係 L、「冂」係 B,所以全碼係 KPBLB。點解要跳中間?因為整體字太多筆畫,倉頡只准你取五碼,唯有頭三加尾二咁揀。記住呢句：出街「記得帶把遮呀」,帶字上頭一堆、下底把遮巾，KPBLB。

常.en: Today we learn 常, read soeng4, meaning common, normal, frequent or regular — you meet it in 通常 tung1 soeng4 (usually) and 非常 fei1 soeng4 (very, extraordinary). Look at its shape: on top sits a flat little crown ⺌ over a covering stroke 冖, and below there's a mouth 口 holding up a 巾 cloth. When Cangjie splits it, the top forms the 字首 ⺌冖 and gives just two codes — ⺌ is F and 冖 is B; then the lower part 口巾 is the 字身, which takes at most three codes, so we take its head 口 as R, its second piece 中 as L, and its tail ⺼ as B, giving the full FBRLB. Remember it like this: a hat on top (⺌冖 = FB) and an open mouth holding a cloth below (口中尾 = RLB), just as in the sentence 我常常去公園 — I often go to the park.
常.zh: 今日我哋學「常」呢個字，讀作 soeng4，意思係「經常、平常、普通」，好似「通常」tung1 soeng4（平時、一般）同「非常」fei1 soeng4（好、極之）咁常見。你望吓佢個樣，上面係一個平頭嘅「⺌」，跟住一橫遮住嘅「冖」，下面就係一個「口」再托住一個「巾」字。倉頡分家嘅時候，上半嘅字首「⺌冖」取兩碼，⺌撳 F、冖撳 B；跟住落到字身「口巾」，字身最多取三碼，於是取頭「口」係 R、取次「中」係 L、取尾「⺼」係 B，合埋就係 FBRLB。記法係：上面戴帽（⺌冖＝FB），下面開口托住條巾（口中尾＝RLB），一句「我常常去公園」就記住佢。

幫.en: Today we meet 幫, read bong1, meaning to help or assist — as in 你可唔可以幫我？, one of the most everyday words you'll ever type. The character sits in two stacked halves: 封 on top and 帛 on the bottom, so Cangjie treats it as a top-and-bottom build, taking 封 as the head and 帛 as the body. For the head 封 we don't spell out everything — we take just its first and last pieces, the opening 土 (G) and the closing 戈 (I). Then the body 帛 gives its pieces in order: 竹 (H), 日 (A), and finally the flesh radical ⺼ (B) at the bottom. Reading top to bottom, head then body, you get GIHAB — just remember the little chain 土-戈-竹-日-⺼ and the whole character clicks into place.
幫.zh: 今日我哋學「幫」呢個字，讀做 bong1，意思係幫忙、幫助，好似「你可唔可以幫我？」咁樣，係我哋日常最常講嘅字之一。呢個字上下兩截：上邊係「封」，下邊係「帛」，倉頡揸佢做上下結構，上邊做字首、下邊做字身。字首「封」我哋唔會全部拆晒，只取頭同尾——起首個「土」（G），再取埋最尾個「戈」（I）；跟住落到字身「帛」，就照順序取「竹」（H）、「日」（A），最後個肉字底「⺼」（B）。所以成個碼由上到下、由首到身砌出嚟就係 GIHAB，記住「土戈竹日肉」呢五粒，個字就成形喇。

平.en: Today we learn 平, read ping4, and sometimes peng4, meaning flat, level, or even — and also the 平 of peace. In everyday Cantonese it's often used to say something is cheap, as in the example sentence 呢件衫好平, this shirt is very cheap. This is a whole-shape character (整體字): it can't be cleanly split into a head part and a body part, so we use the whole-shape rule of taking the first, the second, and the last piece — three codes in total. Reading the shape from top to bottom and left to right, the top horizontal is 一 on the M key, the 火 shape in the middle is on the F key, and the final 十 shape is on the J key, giving you M, F, J. Picture it as memory hook: one flat line pressing down on a fire, with a cross-post 十 driven through it — everything settling down nice and level.
平.zh: 我哋今日學「平」呢個字，佢讀作 ping4，有時亦讀 peng4，意思係平坦、平均，又或者係和平嘅「平」。喺廣東話口語入面，「平」仲成日用嚟講價錢平宜，好似例句「呢件衫好平」噉樣。呢個字係一個整體字，冇辦法清清楚楚噉分做字首同字身兩橛，所以我哋用倉頡「整體字」嘅取碼法：取頭、二，再取尾，總共三個碼。你望住個字由上到下、由左到右噉睇，最頂嗰橫係「一」，佢喺 M 鍵；跟住中間嗰個「火」形，喺 F 鍵；最尾嗰豎連橫嘅「十」形，喺 J 鍵，砌埋一齊就係 M、F、J。記住個口訣：一橫壓住把火，插一支十字杆，成塊嘢就平平穩穩噉擺喺度。

年.en: Today we're learning 年, read nin4, the word for a year, an age, or the new year — just like in 今年好開心, meaning this year is very happy. Look at the character: it's a stack of crossing horizontal strokes with no clean left-right seam, so there's no natural way to split it into separate parts — that makes it a whole character, an 整體字. For whole characters Cangjie uses a special shortcut: instead of breaking it into many pieces, you take just the head and the tail, two codes in total. Here the head piece is 人 on the O key and the tail piece is 手 on the Q key, so the code is simply OQ. Remember it this way: one person (人, O) reaches out a hand (手, Q) to mark the passing of a year.
年.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「年」字，讀做 nin4，就係年份、年紀、新年嗰個「年」，好似「今年好開心」入面咁用。你望住呢個字，佢嘅筆畫係一橫一橫咁交織埋一齊，睇落好似冇辦法清楚拆開左右兩邊，呢種就叫做整體字。遇到整體字，倉頡有一條特別規則：唔使逐部分拆，而係取頭同尾兩碼就夠。所以「年」字嘅頭係「人」，喺 O 鍵；尾係「手」，喺 Q 鍵，砌埋一齊就係 OQ 兩碼。記住喇：一個「人」行咗一「手」路過咗一「年」，人 O 手 Q，就係「年」。

幸.en: The character we're learning today is 幸, read hang6 — the 幸 in 幸運 (luck) and 幸福 (well-being), carrying the sense of good fortune. Look at how it stacks up: on top sits 土 (G), then comes 廿 (T), and at the very bottom is 十 (J), giving you the full code GTJ. This is a whole-shape character, packed so tightly that there's no clean way to split it into a head and a body, so we use the first-two-and-last method — we take the first two pieces plus the final piece and simply skip whatever sits in the middle, which is how we land on 土, 廿 and 十. Remember it like this: fortune starts from the 土 (earth), passes through 廿 years of effort, and ends 十 (ten) out of ten perfect, layer stacked upon layer.
幸.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「幸」，讀作 hang6，即係「幸運」、「幸福」嗰個「幸」，帶住好運同福氣嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅結構：頂上係「土」（G），跟住係「廿」（T），最底係「十」（J），砌埋一齊就係 GTJ。呢個字係一個整體字，堆疊得好密，冇辦法乾淨俐落咁分開字首字身，所以我哋用嘅係「取頭二尾」嘅辦法——攞開頭兩個部件加最尾一個部件，中間嗰啲就跳過唔理，於是就得出「土」、「廿」、「十」三個碼。你可以咁記：幸福係由「土」地開始，經過「廿」年辛勞，最後「十」全十美，一步一步疊起嚟。

幾.en: Today we're learning 幾, read "gei2", a word you use every single day in Cantonese — 幾多 for how much, 幾個 for how many, 幾歲 for how old. Look at the character: it's packed tight with little pieces, so crowded that you can't cleanly separate a head from a body, which is exactly why it counts as a whole character (整體字). For a whole character we don't force a head-body split; instead we take the first, second, third, and last pieces, four in all: first the 女 on the left, which is the V key; then the 戈 up top, the I key; next the 竹 in the middle, the H key; and finally another 戈 at the end, again the I key — giving you VIHI. Remember the order 女, 戈, 竹, 戈 — one girl counting how many spears there are, that's 幾.
幾.zh: 今日我哋學「幾」呢個字，讀「gei2」，係你日日都用到嘅字——問「幾多」、「幾個」、「幾歲」，全部都靠佢。你望下呢個字，佢由好多細件砌埋一齊，密密麻麻，好難清清楚楚咁分開頭同身，所以佢係一個「整體字」。遇到整體字，我哋唔強分字首字身，而係直接取頭、二、三、尾四個部件：先係左邊嘅「女」，係 V 掣；跟住上面嘅「戈」，係 I 掣；再嚟係中間嘅「竹」，係 H 掣；最後又係一個「戈」，同樣係 I 掣，所以整個碼就係 VIHI。記住呢個順序「女、戈、竹、戈」——一個女仔搵到幾多枝戈，就係「幾」。

店.en: Today's character is 店, read dim3, meaning a shop or store — you meet it in words like 酒店 (hotel) and 專門店 (specialty store). Look at its shape: a 广 canopy on the top-left wrapping around 占 tucked underneath. When Cangjie splits it, 广 is the 字首 and gives just one code, the shed-shape 广 keyed as I; then 占 is the 字身, and because it has more than one part, you take its head-and-tail, so the head 卜 gives Y and the tail 口 gives R, spelling IYR. Remember it this way: one canopy I sheltering the 卜 (Y) and the 口 (R) beneath makes your 店.
店.zh: 今日學嘅字係「店」，讀 dim3，即係舖頭、商店嘅意思，好似「酒店」、「專門店」咁。你望吓佢個樣，左邊個「广」字頭包住右下角一個「占」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，「广」係字首，喺屋簷部件度取一碼，就係 I；跟住「占」係字身，因為佢唔止一件，所以取頭尾兩碼，頭係「卜」揀 Y，尾係「口」揀 R，合埋就係 IYR。記住喇：一個屋簷 I 遮住底下嘅卜 Y 同口 R，就係間「店」。

府.en: Today we learn 府, read fu2 in Cantonese, meaning a prefecture or government — you meet it in 政府 (zing3 fu2, government) and in 廣府人 (gwong2 fu2 jan4, the Cantonese people). Look at its shape: an outer 广 canopy on top and left, covering an inner 付, and you write it from the outside inward. Because 广 is the outer 字首, we take just its one code I (广); the inner 付 becomes the 字身, and a 字身 may give up to three codes, so we take its head 人 (O), then its second piece 木 (D), then its tail piece 戈 (I) — together IODI. Here's your hook: write the roof I first, then sweep left to right through 付's 人, 木, 戈 — one canopy sheltering one 付, and the government office is built.
府.zh: 今日我哋學「府」呢個字，粵音讀 fu2，解「官府、政府」嘅意思，好似「政府」（zing3 fu2）就係管治嘅機構，而「廣府人」（gwong2 fu2 jan4）就係我哋廣東人啦。你望吓佢個樣，係外面一個「广」字頭罩住入面嘅「付」，寫嘅時候由外去入。因為「广」係外框做字首，我哋淨係取佢個碼 I（廣）；入面嘅「付」做字身，字身可以取到三碼，於是取頭嗰個「人」（O），跟住第二個「木」（D），最後取尾嗰個「戈」（I），合埋就係 IODI。記住喇：先寫外簷 I，再由左到右執「付」入面嘅人、木、戈，一個屋簷罩住一個付，官府就砌好晒喇。

度.en: Today we learn 度, read "dou6" — the 度 in "thirty degrees," the word for measuring temperature or angles, and it also reads "dok6" meaning to measure or consider. Look at the whole character: there's a 广 roof shape sheltering the parts underneath. In Cangjie, the head 广 comes first and it lives on the I key, then we handle the body below. The body isn't spelled stroke by stroke; instead we take first-and-last — the top piece 廿 (T) and the bottom piece 水 (E), skipping whatever sits in between. Put it together and the code is exactly ITE (广廿水), just three keys. Remember it as "roof up top, 廿 first and 水 last" and you'll never split it wrong.
度.zh: 今日我哋學「度」呢個字，讀「dou6」，好似「三十度」嘅度，係量度溫度、角度嗰個「度」，亦都可以讀「dok6」，解作量度、考慮。你望住成個字，佢係一個「广」字頭包住下面嘅嘢。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首「广」就係 I，之後係字身部分；字身入面唔係逐筆拆晒，而係用「拆頭尾」嘅方法——先攞頭「廿」T，再攞尾「水」E，中間嘅嘢就唔理。所以成個碼砌埋就係 ITE（广廿水），三個碼就搞掂。記住個口訣：「广字頭，廿頭水尾」，就唔會拆錯喇。

座.en: Today we learn 座, which reads "zo6" and means a seat or a base or stand, as in 座位 (a seat) or 座地 (floor-standing). Look at its shape: there is a 广 canopy up top leaning over the whole character 坐 underneath, giving you that steady, settled-down feeling of something resting in place. To break it into code, you first take the radical 广 as your 字首, which lives on the I key; then you handle the body 坐, which is itself built from two 人 and one 土, so following the writing order you take the first 人 (O), then the second 人 (O), and finally the tail piece 土 (G). The split falls this way because 广 is the outer radical taken first, while the whole 坐 is the 字身 read top to bottom, head to tail, piece by piece — put together that gives you exactly IOOG. Here is your memory hook: under one sloping roof 广, two little people 人 sit down on a patch of earth 土, and that is how a whole "seat" comes to rest.
座.zh: 今日我哋學「座」呢個字，佢讀「zo6」，解作座位、底座嘅意思，好似「座位」或者「座地」咁樣。你望下佢個樣，上面有個「广」字頭，斜斜咁罩住下面成個「坐」字，好有一種穩陣、坐落嚟嘅感覺。拆碼嘅時候，我哋先攞字首「广」，佢喺 I 掣度；跟住就處理字身嗰個「坐」——「坐」自己係由兩個「人」加一個「土」砌成，所以順住寫嘅次序，先取頭一個「人」（O），再取第二個「人」（O），最尾攞底下嘅「土」（G）。點解係咁分呢？因為「广」係外圍嘅字首要先取，而「坐」成個係字身，就跟返佢由上到下、由頭到尾嘅筆順逐件攞落去，所以合埋就係 IOOG。記住嘅竅門好簡單：一間屋簷「广」，底下坐住兩個人企喺塊「土」上面，一座樓咪就係咁起出嚟囉。

庭.en: Today's character is 庭, read ting4, meaning a courtyard, a backyard, or a spacious hall — you meet it in words like 家庭 (gaa1 ting4, family) and 法庭 (faat3 ting4, tribunal). Look at its shape: an outer 广 canopy leans over the inner 廷, its opening stroke sweeping like a slanted roof-eave over everything below. When we split it, 广 is the head and takes just one code, I; then the inner 廷 acts as the body, and since a body may take up to three codes we take its first, middle, and last pieces — first the 乙, which is N, then the 大 in the middle, which is K, and finally the 土 at the bottom, which is G. Put them together and you get INKG, one head code plus three body codes, filling the quota exactly. Remember it this way: the 广 eave (I) shelters a 廷 built from 乙 (N), 大 (K), and 土 (G) — a household tucked under the roof.
庭.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「庭」，讀 ting4，指庭院、後院，又或者係寬闊嘅廳堂，好似「家庭」（gaa1 ting4）同「法庭」（faat3 ting4）咁樣用。你睇下佢個樣，外面有個「广」字頭包住入面嘅「廷」，起筆嘅時候一撇搭一橫，好似個屋簷斜斜咁遮住下面嘅嘢。拆碼嘅時候，「广」係字首，只取一碼，就係 I；跟住入面嘅「廷」做字身，因為字身最多取三碼，所以我哋取頭、次、尾三個部件——先係頭嗰個「乙」，係 N，再係中間嘅「大」，係 K，最後尾嗰個「土」，係 G。合埋一齊就係 INKG，一碼字首加三碼字身，啱啱好夠。記住個口訣：屋簷「广」（I）遮住，入面乙（N）大（K）土（G）三件砌成廷，家庭喺屋簷底下。

康.en: Today's character is 康, read hong1, meaning peaceful and quiet, and also happy and healthy — you meet it in words like 健康 (gin6 hong1, health) and 康城 (hong1 sing4, the French city Cannes). Look first at the outer frame: the sloping roof wrapping the top and left is the 广 head, which sits on the I key like a little house sheltering everything below. For the body inside, we don't spell out every stroke; instead we take its head and its tail — first 中, which is L, then the closing piece 水, which is E — so the whole character builds as ILE. Why only head and tail? Because the body has too many strokes to take piece by piece, and Cangjie's rule tells us to grab just the leading and trailing shapes in cases like this. Remember it this way: under a sloping roof (广 I), a center pole (中 L) with water flowing (水 E) — a calm, healthy home.
康.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「康」，讀作 hong1，解作安寧、平靜，亦有健康、快樂嘅意思，好似「健康」（gin6 hong1）同「康城」（hong1 sing4，即係法國嗰個 Cannes）咁。你先睇個外框：上邊同左邊圍住嘅係「广」字頭，喺鍵盤上係 I，佢好似一間有斜頂嘅屋咁遮住下面。跟住入面嘅字身，我哋唔會逐畫拆晒，而係取頭尾兩件——先取「中」，佢係 L，再取結尾嗰個「水」，佢係 E，於是整個字砌成 ILE。點解淨係取頭尾？因為字身部分太多筆畫，倉頡規則叫我哋喺呢啲情況取頭同取尾兩個碼就夠，唔使全部逐件數。記住嘅方法：一間有斜頂嘅屋（广 I）裏面，中間（中 L）流住水（水 E），住得又靜又安康。

廈.en: Today we learn 廈, read haa6, meaning a big building or a mansion. Look at it: there is a 广 roof sheltering a 夏 inside, just like a grand structure standing tall. When we split it, the outer 字首 广 takes I, and then the inner 字身 夏 is broken into head and tail: the top stroke 一 takes M, the middle piece 凵 takes U, and the trailing 夂 at the bottom takes E, giving the full code IMUE. Why does 夏 split this way? Because it is not a whole-unit character, so it follows Cangjie's head-second-tail rule — first the head 一, then the second piece 凵, and finally the tail 夂. Remember it like this: a 夏 (summer) tucked under a 广 roof — that is how a great building 廈 is raised.
廈.zh: 我哋今日學「廈」呢個字，讀做 haa6，即係大樓、大廈嘅意思。你望下佢，係一個「广」字頭罩住入面嘅「夏」，就好似一座宏偉嘅建築物咁。拆字嘅時候，最外面嘅字首「广」取 I，跟住入面嘅字身「夏」就要分頭、尾嚟拆：頭一橫「一」取 M，然後中間嘅「凵」取 U，最尾拖落嚟嘅「夂」取 E，所以成個碼就係 IMUE。點解字身「夏」要咁拆呢？因為佢唔係一個整體字，要照倉頡「頭、次、尾」嘅規矩取碼，所以先攞頭嘅一，再攞第二個部件凵，最後攞落腳嘅夂。記住呢個口訣：广裏面藏住一個夏天（夏），大廈就係咁起成嘅。

廚.en: Today we meet 廚, read cyu4, meaning the place where you cook — the kitchen. Look at its shape: there's a 广 canopy on the outside wrapping a big chunk underneath, and that 广 is the head, which you type with I. Because 广 sits in the upper-left corner sheltering the whole body, it naturally becomes the head, leaving 尌 as the body. A body can give at most three codes, so 尌 uses the head-then-second-then-last method: take the opening 土 (G), then the next piece 廿 (T), then jump to the tail 戈 (I), giving GTI. Read straight through, the whole character is IGTI. Here's your hook: one 广 roof (I) shelters the 土廿戈 (GTI) cooking inside — that's your 廚 kitchen.
廚.zh: 今日我哋學「廚」呢個字，讀 cyu4，就係煮嘢食嘅地方——廚房。你睇吓佢個樣，外面有個「广」字頭包住下面一大嚿嘢，呢個「广」字頭就係字首，喺鍵盤上面撳 I。因為「广」擺喺左上角包住成個字身，佢自然做字首,淨低嘅「尌」就係字身。字身通常最多只可以拆三粒碼，所以「尌」用「拆頭二尾」嘅方法：攞開頭嘅「土」G、跟住第二嘅「廿」T，最後跳去尾嘅「戈」I，砌埋就係 GTI。成隻字順住打就係 IGTI。記住喇：一個「广」字簷（I）遮住入面煮飯嘅土廿戈（GTI），呢間就係「廚」房。

廣.en: Today we learn 廣, read gwong2, meaning broad or widespread — it's the 廣 in 廣東話, the word for Cantonese itself. Look at the whole shape: on the outside there's a wide roof-like frame 广, opening up to shelter what sits inside, and this outer piece is keyed as I. Tucked underneath it is a full 黃. When Cangjie splits a character where one piece shelters another, we take the outer 字首 first and then the inner 字身, so 广 comes first as I. The inner 黃 is the 字身, and a 字身 normally gives its head, a middle, and its tail: the head 廿 keyed T, one more 一 keyed M, and the tail 金 keyed C — giving the full code ITMC. Remember it as "the roof 广 covers a 黃, and the 黃 gives 廿, 一, 金," and you'll never mis-split it again.
廣.zh: 今日我哋學「廣」呢個字，讀做 gwong2，意思係闊、廣泛，好似你成日講嘅「廣東話」個「廣」。你望吓成個字，外面有個廠仔頭「广」，攤開嚟遮住入面嘅嘢，呢個部件叫 I；入面收埋咗一個「黃」字。倉頡拆呢啲有蓋嘅字，會先取外面嘅字首，再取入面嘅字身，所以我哋先攞外「广」做字首，得個碼 I。跟住入面個「黃」係字身，字身通常攞頭、次、尾三部分：頭係「廿」做 T，中間攞多個「一」做 M，最後攞埋個尾「金」做 C。所以成個字砌埋就係 ITMC——記住一句：「广蓋住個黃，黃頭廿、中一、尾金」，你就唔會再拆錯喇。

廳.en: This character is 廳, read teng1, meaning a hall or the big central room of a home. Look at its shape: everything sits underneath a 广 roof, and that 广 is the head of the character, which you type with I. What follows is a busy body, and Cangjie has a firm rule here — the body can contribute at most three codes, so instead of spelling out every stroke we take only the head, the next piece, and the tail. The head of the body is 尸 on S, the next piece is 土 on G, and the tail is 匕 on P, giving you the full code ISGP. Remember it as one leaning roof, 广 on I, sheltering S, then G, then P inside — like stepping into a grand hall room by room.
廳.zh: 呢個字係「廳」，讀 teng1，即係大堂或者屋企正中間嗰間大房。你睇下佢個樣，成個字都擺喺一個「广」字部下面，呢個「广」就係字首，喺鍵盤上面撳 I。跟住落嚟嘅字身好複雜，倉頡有個規矩：字身最多只可以取三碼，所以我哋唔會逐筆逐筆全部拆晒，而係取「頭、次、尾」——先取頭嗰個「尸」係 S，再取第二件「土」係 G，最後取尾嗰件「匕」係 P，合埋就係 ISGP。記住呢個順序：一撇「广」遮住頭頂，入面由 S 排到 G 再到 P，就好似你行入間大廳，一層一層咁見到。

建.en: Today's character is 建, read gin3, meaning to build, establish, or found — you see it in words like 建立 (gin3 laap6, to establish or set up) and 建議 (gin3 ji5, to propose or suggest). Look at the shape: on the right sits the 廴 base, like a long stretching road carrying the piece above it, and in Cangjie we take that road first by grabbing just its head, 乛, which lives on the N key. Once N is down, what's left on top is 聿, and that becomes the 字身 — the body — which follows the head-second-tail rule: its head is ナ on K, its second piece is 中 on L, and its tail is 手 on Q, giving you the full code NKLQ. The reason 廴 goes first is that it's the enclosing radical wrapping under everything, so Cangjie's rule takes that supporting stroke N before breaking down the body inside. Remember it this way: lay the road (N) first, then stand up the 聿 by its head, middle and tail (K, L, Q) — road laid, 聿 raised, and you have 建 built up!
建.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「建」，讀做 gin3，即係英文 build、establish 嘅意思，好似「建立」（gin3 laap6，即係建設起嚟）同「建議」（gin3 ji5，即係提出意見）咁樣用。你望吓成個字，右邊有個「廴」字底，好似一條長長嘅路托住上面嗰嚿嘢；喺倉頡入面，呢個「廴」我哋要先攞佢個頭，就係「乛」，個鍵係 N。攞完 N 之後，剩返上面嘅「聿」就係字身，字身要跟「頭二尾」嘅取碼規則：個頭係「ナ」，個鍵 K；跟住個第二個係「中」，個鍵 L；最後個尾係「手」，個鍵 Q，所以成個字砌埋就係 NKLQ。點解「廴」要行先呢？因為佢係包住成個字嘅部首偏旁，倉頡規矩就係先寫外面托底嗰個 N，再拆入面嘅字身。記住喇：一條路（N）行先，路上面立起「聿」嘅頭二尾（K、L、Q），路修好、聿立好，就係「建」立起嚟啦！

式.en: Today's character is 式, read sik1, the same 式 in 款式 (style) and 方式 (way, method); it means style, system, formula, or rule, as in 形式 (jing4 sik1, format or type). Look at its build: the top-left is 弋 as the head, wrapping around a 工 that serves as the body. When we split it, the head 弋 gives only 戈 (I), and then the body 工 takes its head and tail — 心 (P) and 一 (M) — because a body of this kind supplies its first and last pieces, giving us IPM in all. Remember it this way: 戈 (I) leads, then the head-and-tail of 工, which are 心 (P) and 一 (M) — and you've typed a character full of style.
式.zh: 我哋今日學嘅呢個字係「式」，讀做 sik1，即係「款式」、「方式」嗰個式，解作樣式、制度、公式或者規則，好似「形式」（jing4 sik1）咁樣講。你望下佢嘅結構，左上邊有個「弋」做字首，入面藏住一個「工」做字身。拆碼嘅時候，字首個「弋」只取到「戈」（I），跟住輪到字身個「工」，因為字身要取頭同尾，所以就攞「工」嘅頭「心」（P）加尾「一」（M），砌埋一齊就係 IPM。記住喇：戈（I）先行，跟住工字頭尾嘅心（P）同一（M），咁樣就砌出一個好有「款式」嘅字啦。

引.en: Today we learn the character 引, read jan5, meaning to pull, to draw out, to attract — as in 吸引 (kap1 jan5), to catch someone's attention, like drawing their eyes toward you. Look at its shape: on the left sits 弓, a bow, and on the right stands a single vertical stroke. Cangjie splits this one cleanly down the middle: the left 弓 takes the key N, and the right vertical stroke 丨 takes the key L, giving you NL. The reason it's only two codes is that 引 divides plainly into left and right, each side being one clear, complete piece — one piece, one code, with nothing more to break down. To remember it, picture a bow (N) drawn taut against a single arrow-shaft (L): pull and release, and you've got 引.
引.zh: 今日我哋學「引」呢個字，讀作 jan5，意思係拉、抽出、吸引，好似「吸引」（kap1 jan5）咁樣，將人哋嘅注意力拉埋嚟。你望下佢嘅樣，左邊係一個「弓」字，右邊就企咗一豎。倉頡拆呢個字好簡單直接，左邊嘅「弓」取碼 N，右邊嗰條直豎「丨」取碼 L，所以成個字就係 NL。點解淨係兩碼咁少呢？因為「引」左右分明，兩邊各自係一件清清楚楚嘅部件，一件一碼，唔使再拆落去。記住嘅時候，你可以諗成一張「弓」（N）拉緊咗一條箭「丨」（L），一拉一射，就係「引」喇。

張.en: Today we learn 張, read "zoeng1" in Cantonese, meaning to stretch or extend — like drawing a bow open — and it also works as a measure word for flat things, as in 一張紙 (a sheet of paper) or 一張枱 (a table). Look at its shape: on the left sits 弓, and on the right sits 長, and together they make 張. When Cangjie splits it, the 字首 (head part) is the left-hand 弓, which gives just one code, N; the 字身 (body part) is the right-hand 長, and because the body may take more than one code, we pull head-second-tail from it — 尸 S, 一 M, and 女 V — so the full code reads NSMV. Why does the head give only one code? A 字首 may take at most two codes, but 弓 is a single root, so all it can offer is that one N. Remember it this way: draw the bow 弓 (N) and let it fly toward the long 長 (SMV) — one pull and release, and you have 張.
張.zh: 今日我哋學「張」呢個字，粵音讀「zoeng1」，本意係拉開、伸展，好似拉弓咁；佢又可以做量詞，數平嘅嘢，例如一張紙、一張枱。你睇下佢個樣，左邊係個「弓」字，右邊係「長」，兩部份合埋就係「張」。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，字首係左邊嘅「弓」，取一個碼N，就係咁多；字身係右邊嘅「長」，因為字身可以攞多過一個碼，所以要拆頭、二、尾——即係「尸」S、「一」M、同埋「女」V，加埋成個碼就係NSMV。點解字首得一個碼？因為倉頡規定字首最多兩碼，而「弓」只有一個字根，攞晒都係得N一個。你可以咁記：拉「弓」（N）射向長長嘅「長」（SMV），一拉一放就係「張」。

強.en: Today we learn 強, read koeng4, meaning strong, powerful, full of energy. Look at it: on the left is the 弓 (bow) piece, and on the right sits 虽 — that's how we split it. The head 弓 gives us N, and then the body 虽 comes next; because that body needs more than two codes, we take head-second-tail from it, which is 戈 as I, 中 as L, and another 戈 as I, giving ILI. Put it together and the full code is NILI — N, I, L, I. Here's your hook: a bow (N) shooting clean through a bug (ILI) — that takes real strength, so it's 強.
強.zh: 今日我哋學「強」呢個字，讀koeng4，即係強壯、強大嘅意思，形容一樣嘢有力量、夠猛。你望下佢，左邊係一個「弓」字，右邊係「虽」，我哋就係咁樣拆佢。字首取「弓」，撳N；字身就係「虽」，因為佢唔止兩個碼位，所以要取頭、二、尾三個碼——「戈」係I、「中」係L、最後再一個「戈」係I，合埋就係ILI。全個字連埋就係NILI，即係N、I、L、I。記住個口訣：一張弓（N）射穿個虫（ILI），力量就係咁強，寫「強大」、「強調」都用得着。

形.en: Today we learn 形, read jing4, meaning form, shape, or appearance — you meet it in words like 形式 (jing4 sik1, format or type) and 形成 (jing4 sing4, to take shape). Look at the character: the left side is 幵 and the right side is three little slanting strokes 彡, so we split it as a left head and a right body. For the head 幵 Cangjie doesn't spell out every stroke — it takes only the first and last piece, the top 一 which sits on the M key, and 廿 which sits on the T key, giving MT. Then the body 彡 is just three repeated 丿 strokes, and each 丿 lives on the H key, so that's HHH, and the whole character joins up as MTHHH. Remember it this way: the left 幵 gives you one-then-廿 (MT), and the right side is a neat trio of H's — say 呢個係圓形 and picture the circle taking shape.
形.zh: 今日我哋學「形」字，讀 jing4，即係形狀、樣貌嘅意思，好似「形式」（jing4 sik1，即格式）同「形成」（jing4 sing4，即慢慢成形）咁用。你望下呢個字，左邊係「幵」，右邊係三條斜斜嘅撇「彡」，我哋就照呢個左右結構分做字首同字身。字首「幵」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，倉頡淨係取頭尾兩碼——頭係一橫「一」，個掣係 M，尾係「廿」，個掣係 T，所以字首係 MT。跟住字身「彡」係三條撇，每條撇都係「丿」，個掣係 H，砌埋就 HHH，全個字合起嚟就係 MTHHH。記住個口訣：左邊幵取一同廿（MT），右邊三撇連環三個 H，「呢個係圓形」你就唔會再串錯喇。

彩.en: Today we learn 彩, read coi2, meaning hue or bright, variegated colors — as in 彩虹 (coi2 hung4), the rainbow arching across the sky. Look at the shape: on the left sits 采, and on the right are three little slanting strokes forming 彡, and Cangjie splits the character right there between them. The 字首 is 采, taken by the head-and-tail method: first the top piece 爫 on the B key, then the bottom piece 木 on the D key, giving you B and D. The 字身 is 彡, which is simply three 丿 strokes, and each one is the H key, so you tap H, H, H in a row. Put it together and you get BDHHH — remember it as 'head-and-tail BD for 采, then three strokes lined up as three H's,' and you'll type this lucky character right every time.
彩.zh: 今日我哋學「彩」呢個字，讀coi2，係色彩、繽紛顏色嘅意思，好似「彩虹」（coi2 hung4）就係天上嗰道七彩嘅光。你望下呢個字，左邊係「采」，右邊係三撇「彡」，倉頡就跟住咁樣分開嚟拆。字首係「采」，我哋用頭尾嘅取碼方法，先攞上面嘅爫（B鍵），再攞下面嘅木（D鍵），就得到B、D兩碼。跟住字身係「彡」，佢由三條斜撇組成，每一撇都係丿（H鍵），所以連續打三個H，H、H、H。合埋一齊就係BDHHH，你記住「采字頭尾BD，三撇齊齊排三個H」，就好彩（hou2 coi2）一次過打得啱喇。

影.en: Today we learn 影, read "jing2" — it means shadow, reflection, or the 影 in taking a photograph. Look at it and you'll see it breaks into two big parts: the left side is 景, and the right side is 彡, three little slanting strokes. In Cangjie we handle the head 景 first — because it's a complete unit, we take just its head and tail, the top 日 (A) and the bottom 火 (F), giving AF for the head; then the body 彡 is made of three sweeping 丿 strokes, and each 丿 is H, so three of them give HHH. Put together, that's the full five-code AFHHH. Remember it this way: the sun's fire shines down and throws out three slanting rays of shadow — that's 影.
影.zh: 今日我哋學「影」呢個字，讀「jing2」，即係影子、倒影，又或者影相嘅「影」。你望住佢，會發現分成左右兩大嚿：左邊係「景」，右邊係三撇「彡」。倉頡拆嘅時候，先處理字首「景」——因為佢係一個完整嘅部件，我哋取頭尾兩碼，頭係上面嘅「日」（A），尾係下面嘅「火」（F），所以字首係AF；跟住字身「彡」由三筆撇組成，每一撇都係「丿」（H），三撇就取HHH。合埋一齊就係AFHHH，五碼齊全。你可以咁樣記：日頭嘅火照落嚟，投出三道斜斜嘅影，就係「影」。

律.en: Today we learn 律, read leot6, meaning a statute, a principle, a regulation — the 律 in 法律, law. Look at how it splits into left and right: on the left is 彳, and on the right is 聿. The 彳 on the left is the 字首, so Cangjie takes its head and tail, H and O, giving HO; the 聿 on the right is the 字身, which also takes head and tail — the head 中 is L and the tail 手 is Q — so the full code is HOLQ. The thing to hold onto is that once the character breaks into left and right, both the 字首 and the 字身 keep taking their own head-and-tail: HO on the left, LQ on the right, joining smoothly. Memory hook: a person (O) walking a path (彳) with a hand (Q) holding the middle (L) rule — that's 律!
律.zh: 今日我哋學「律」呢個字，讀做 leot6，意思係法規、法則，好似「法律」嘅「律」咁。你睇佢分左右兩邊：左邊係「彳」，右邊係「聿」。左邊嘅「彳」係字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，即係頭 H、尾 O，砌成 HO；右邊嘅「聿」係字身，字身都係取頭尾，頭係「中」L、尾係「手」Q，於是全碼就係 HOLQ。你要記住嘅係，左右結構分開嗰刻，字首同字身各自照樣攞頭尾——左邊 HO，右邊 LQ，合埋自然順暢。記憶鈎：一個人（O）行喺路（彳）上，手（Q）中（L）揸住規矩，就係「律」喇！

後.en: Today's character is 後, read hau6, meaning behind or rear in space, after in time, and also descendants. Look at it: on the left is the double-person radical 彳, and on the right sits a cluster of small pieces stacked together. When we split it, 彳 is the head and gives only one code, H; the whole right side then becomes the body, and since a body may take up to three codes plus a tail, we follow the head-two-three-tail rule and read 𠆢 as O, ㄠ as V, 戈 as I, and finally the tail 夂 as E, giving HOVIE. Here's your hook: a little person (彳) walks behind, and the three pieces trail all the way to the last one, 夂 — first eat, then afterward go play, always coming after.
後.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「後」，讀音係 hau6，即係「後面」、「之後」嘅意思，可以指位置喺後便，或者時間上發生喺之後，甚至指子孫後代。你睇下呢個字，左邊係一個雙人旁「彳」，右邊係一組零件砌埋一齊。拆字嘅時候，「彳」係字首，淨係取佢一個碼，就係 H；跟住成個右半邊當作字身，因為字身可以取到三碼加一個尾碼，所以我哋按「頭、二、三、尾」嘅規矩，順住攞入面嘅「𠆢」係 O、「ㄠ」係 V、「戈」係 I，最後個尾係「夂」E，合埋就係 HOVIE。記法係咁：一個人（彳）行喺後面，跟住三個零件一路排到最尾嘅「夂」，「食飯之後去玩」，行完先至到「後」。

得.en: Today we learn 得, read "dak1", meaning to obtain or get — as in 得到 (dak1 dou3), to receive something. Look at its shape: on the left is 彳, and on the right is a stack of strokes. In Cangjie this character splits left and right first: the head is the left-side 彳, which gives just one code — H; then the entire right side becomes the body, and a body may take head, second, third, and tail — four codes. So reading down the right side we take 日 O, the upper stroke 一 A, the lower stroke 一 M, and finally 戈 I, giving HOAMI. Why this split? Because in a left-right character the head takes only one code and the body takes head-two-three-tail, exactly four slots for 日一一戈. Remember it this way: the walking 彳 H steps first on the left, then top to bottom on the right you gather 日一一戈 — walk far enough and you'll get (得) there!
得.zh: 我哋今日學「得」呢個字，讀「dak1」，意思係得到、獲得，好似「得到」（dak1 dou3）咁樣，攞到一樣嘢。你望下佢個樣，左邊係「彳」，右邊係一堆疊埋嘅筆畫。倉頡入面，呢個字先分左右：字首係左邊嘅「彳」，佢淨係俾一個碼——H；跟住成個右邊當做字身，字身可以取頭、二、三、尾四個碼，所以我哋順住寫落去，攞「日」O、上面一橫「一」A、下面一橫「一」M、最後個「戈」I，合埋就係 HOAMI。點解係咁分？因為左右結構嘅字，字首只取一碼，字身取頭二三尾，啱啱夠四個位裝落「日一一戈」四件嘢。記住喇：左邊行人企 H 行先，右邊由上到下攞「日一一戈」，行路（彳）行得到（得）啦！

從.en: Today we meet 從, read cung4, meaning "from," "since," or "by way of" — you see it in 從來 cung4 loi4, "always, ever, at all," and 自從 zi6 cung4, "ever since." Look at its shape: on the left is the double-person radical 彳, and on the right sits a cluster of repeated person-shapes. Cangjie splits it head-then-body: the left 彳 is the 字首, and from it we take only its head 竹 (H); then the whole right side is the 字身, which gives four 人 in a row, O, O, O, O, to fill out the code. That makes the full code HOOOO — one 竹 leading a line of four 人. Memory hook: one 竹 walks in front and four people follow behind, marching along "from" here to there.
從.zh: 今日我哋學「從」呢個字，佢讀 cung4，意思係「從……開始」、「自從」或者「由邊度嚟」嘅意思，好似「從來」cung4 loi4 就係「一向、至今」，「自從」zi6 cung4 就係「由某個時候開始」。你望吓佢個樣，左邊係雙人旁「彳」，右邊有一堆重疊嘅人形。倉頡拆呢個字，係先取字首再取字身：左邊嘅「彳」係字首，我哋淨係攞佢個頭「竹」H；跟住右邊成嚿係字身，一連取四個「人」O、O、O、O，湊夠碼數。所以成個碼就係 HOOOO，一個竹帶住四個人。記住佢嘅口訣：一個彳頭「竹」行頭，後面四個人排成隊——「從細到大」都係一班人跟住行，就記得晒喇！

循.en: Today we learn 循, read ceon4, meaning to follow, obey, or comply — as in 循環 ceon4 waan4 (recycle) and 依循 ji1 ceon4 (to follow, to comply). Look at it: on the left is 彳, and on the right sits a 盾, so the character splits into a 字首 (left) and a 字身 (right). The 字首 彳 gives head-tail, which is 彳 (H) and 人 (O), making HO. The right-side 盾 is the 字身 and takes head, middle, and tail — head 竹 (H), middle 十 (J), tail 凵 (U) — so the whole thing is HOHJU. Memory hook: the little walking 彳 steps out first (HO), then the shield gives its head, waist, and foot (HJU) — put them side by side and you've followed the path to 循.
循.zh: 今日我哋學「循」呢個字，讀 ceon4，意思係跟隨、遵照，好似「循環」ceon4 waan4（循環再用）同「依循」ji1 ceon4（跟從、遵從）咁。你望住佢，左邊係「彳」，右邊係一個「盾」字，所以要分做字首同字身兩橛。左邊嘅「彳」係字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，即係「彳」（H）同「人」（O），砌成 HO。右邊嘅「盾」係字身，取頭、二、尾三碼：頭係「竹」（H），中間係「十」（J），尾係「凵」（U），砌埋一齊就係 HOHJU。記住個口訣：左邊行人先行過（HO），右邊盾牌頭腰尾（HJU），左右夾埋就係「循」。

德.en: Today we learn 德, read dak1, meaning ethics, morality, or virtue — the moral character a person carries, as in the sentence 佢好有道德, "He is very moral." Look at the whole character: it splits left and right, with the double-person radical 彳 on the left and the big block 𢛳 on the right. In Cangjie the left 彳 is the 字首, and its own code is 竹人 HO, so we begin by typing 竹 (H) and 人 (O). The right side 𢛳 is the 字身, and because it is a complex piece we don't spell every stroke — instead we take head, second, and tail: the head 十 (J), the second 田 (W), and the tail 心 (P), giving JWP. Put it all together in order and you get 竹人十田心, HOJWP. Here's your memory hook: the double-person HO leads, and virtue's 心 (P) sits right at the very bottom — a moral heart planted firmly at the end.
德.zh: 今日我哋學「德」字，讀音係 dak1，解作品德、道德，即係做人嘅倫理修養，好似「佢好有道德」呢句咁。你望吓成個字，左右分開嘅，左邊係雙人旁「彳」，右邊係一大嚿嘅「𢛳」。倉頡分字嘅時候，左邊嘅「彳」做字首，佢自己嘅碼係竹人 HO，所以我哋一開始就打竹（H）同人（O）。右邊嘅「𢛳」做字身，因為佢係一個複雜嘅部件，我哋唔會逐筆打晒，而係取頭、二、尾三個碼：頭係十（J），第二個係田（W），最尾係心（P），砌埋一齊就係 JWP。所以全字順住打落去就係竹人十田心 HOJWP。記住喇：左邊雙人 HO 帶頭，右邊由「十田心」由上到下收尾，有品德嘅人，個心（P）都擺喺最後最底，穩穩陣陣。

心.en: Today we learn 心, read sam1, the very word you use for heart, mind, and feelings. Look at its shape: a gentle curved bottom with three little dots above, like a small heart with a heartbeat. In Cangjie, 心 is a whole-unit character (整體字) — its form is already complete on its own, so you don't split it into a head and a body; it simply maps to one key, P. Because it stands as a single unit, there's no first-part or last-part division at all — the entire character is just P, one keystroke. Remember it this way: whenever you feel 心, put a P right on your heart, and you'll type words like 中心 and 開心 in a snap, as in 我好開心, "I am very happy"!
心.zh: 今日我哋學個「心」字，讀做 sam1，就係我哋成日講嘅心臟、心思、心靈嗰個「心」。你望吓佢個樣，一個彎彎嘅底加三點，好似一粒跳緊嘅心咁得意。喺倉頡入面，「心」係一個整體字，即係佢本身就已經係一個完整嘅字形，唔使再拆開，所以佢直接對應一個字母碼 P，打一個 P 就得㗎喇。因為佢係單體字，唔會出現字首字身分家嘅情況，全個字就係 P 一碼咁簡單。記住喇：見到「心」，心口一個 P，一諗就打得出，好似「中心」、「開心」都用得上，例如「我好開心」！

必.en: Today we're learning 必, read bit1, meaning "surely, certainly, must" — as in "你必須早啲瞓" (you must sleep earlier), the sense of something unavoidable that simply has to happen. Look at the character and you'll spot what looks like a 心 (heart) in the middle, with a slanting stroke cutting across it — an unusual little shape. In Cangjie we don't break it into lots of tiny pieces, because 必 is treated as a whole character, taking only the head and tail: the head is 心 (P) and the tail is 丿 (H), giving you the code PH. Why only two codes? Because a whole character never grabs all its parts — the head and tail alone stand in for the whole thing. Remember it this way: 心 P to begin, a single slash H to finish, and PH types 必.
必.zh: 今日我哋學「必」呢個字，讀 bit1，意思係「一定、必然」，好似「你必須早啲瞓」入面咁，表示無得避、一定要做嘅意思。你望住個字，會見到中間好似有個「心」字咁，再有一撇斜斜咁劃過去，個結構其實幾特別。用倉頡打嘅時候，我哋唔會逐筆逐筆拆到好散，因為「必」當作一個整體字嚟處理，只取頭同尾兩碼：頭係「心」P，尾係「丿」H，所以成個碼就係 PH。點解淨係取兩碼咁少呢？因為整體字唔會攞齊晒所有部件，只需要頭尾兩個代表就夠喇。記住喇：「心」P 起頭，一撇 H 收尾，PH 兩下就打得「必」出嚟。

快.en: Today we learn 快, read faai3 in Cantonese, meaning quick, fast, or speedy — as in 快餐 faai3 caan1, a fast meal, and even Hong Kong's fast-food chain 大快活 daai6 faai3 wut6. Look at its left-right shape: on the left is the heart radical 忄, and on the right is 夬. When Cangjie splits it, the left side 忄 is the 字首 and gives just one code, P, while the right side 夬 becomes the 字身, from which you take the head and the tail. The head of 夬 is ⺕ = D and the tail is 乂 = K, so the whole character is P, D, K. The 字身 stops at two codes here because a body takes at most three, and 夬 (whose own code is DK) is short enough that head D and tail K cover it — picture a heart beating fast: 忄(P), ⺕(D), 乂(K), and off you rush!
快.zh: 今日我哋學「快」字，粵音讀 faai3，即係快速、迅速嘅意思，好似「快餐」faai3 caan1 咁，就係快嘅餐；香港嘅「大快活」daai6 faai3 wut6 亦都係一間快餐店。你睇吓佢係左右結構，左邊係個「豎心邊」忄，右邊係個「夬」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊嘅字首忄淨係取一個碼 P，右邊嘅夬就做字身，要取頭同尾——頭係個「⺕」取 D，尾係個「乂」取 K，所以整個字係 PDK。點解字身淨係取頭尾兩碼呢？因為一個普通嘅字身最多取三碼，但夬呢個部件（佢自己嘅碼係 DK）拆落去只得幾筆，所以取頭 D、尾 K 就夠。記住個心跳得快嘅畫面：忄(P)、⺕(D)、乂(K)，心一急就想快啲走喇！

思.en: Today we learn 思, read si1 or si3, meaning to think, to consider, to ponder — using your mind to turn something over, and sometimes serving as a final particle at the end of a sentence. Look at its shape: it's a top-bottom structure, with 田 (a field) sitting on top and 心 (the heart) resting underneath, which pictures thinking done with the heart and mind. Cangjie breaks it simply, following that top-to-bottom order: the prefix 田 is on the W key, and the body 心 is on the P key, giving you the full code WP. Why only two codes? Because in a top-bottom structure the prefix takes just one code and the body takes just one code — 田 gives one, 心 gives one, adding up to exactly two. Remember it as 'field over heart, WP is how you ponder.'
思.zh: 今日我哋學「思」呢個字，讀 si1 或者 si3，意思係思考、思量，即係用個腦去諗嘢，有時亦都做句尾嘅語氣字。你望下佢，係上下結構：上面係一個「田」字，下面係一個「心」字，一望就知道係「用心去諗」嘅意思。倉頡拆佢好簡單，就係跟返上下嘅次序：字首係田，喺鍵盤嘅 W；字身係心，喺鍵盤嘅 P，所以全碼就係 WP。點解只係兩碼咁少呢？因為上下結構嘅字，字首同字身各自淨係取一碼，田一碼、心一碼，加埋剛剛好兩碼。記住「田心相疊，WP 諗嘢」，用心去思考，就係「思」。

性.en: Today we learn 性, read sing3, meaning nature, character, or sex — you meet it in words like 女性 (neoi5 sing3, a woman by gender) and 男性 (naam4 sing3, a man by gender). Look at its shape: on the left sits the upright heart radical 忄, the piece for feelings and disposition, which you type with P; on the right stands 生, the character for life or growing. When Cangjie splits this character, the left 忄 becomes the 字首 and takes just one code, P, while the right 生 becomes the 字身, and a 字身 may give at most three codes. So from 生 we take its head 竹 (H), then the second piece 手 (Q), and finally the tail 一 (M), giving us PHQM. Remember it this way: a single heart 忄 (P) joined to living, growing 生 (竹 H, 手 Q, 一 M) is how your true nature comes to be.
性.zh: 我哋今日學個「性」字，讀作 sing3，意思係本性、性格、性別，好似「女性」（neoi5 sing3）同「男性」（naam4 sing3）咁樣用嚟分男女。你望吓佢嘅結構，左邊係個豎心邊「忄」，就係心情、感受嗰個部件，喺倉頡度撳 P；右邊係個「生」字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊嘅「忄」做字首，淨係取一碼 P，跟住右邊嘅「生」做字身，字身最多取三碼，所以我哋喺「生」度攞頭嘅「竹」（H）、第二個「手」（Q），同埋尾嘅「一」（M），合埋就係 PHQM。記住喇：一顆心「忄」（P），配上生長嘅「生」（竹 H、手 Q、一 M），你嘅本「性」就係咁生成嘅。

悅.en: Today we learn 悅, read jyut6, meaning pleased or joyful, as in 喜悅 (joy). Look at it: on the left is the heart radical 忄, which tells you it's about feelings and pleasure, and in Cangjie it takes the code P. On the right sits the body 兌; since a character usually gives one code to the left head and up to three to the body, we read 兌 from top to bottom, taking 八 (C), then 口 (R), then the legs 儿 (U), giving PCRU. So the whole code is head 忄 P plus the body's head C, middle R, and tail U — exactly four codes. Remember it this way: a little heart (忄P) sees 兌 and lights up with delight — that's 悅!
悅.zh: 今日我哋學「悅」呢個字，讀 jyut6，意思係開心、愉快，好似「喜悅」咁。你望下佢，左邊係個豎心邊「忄」，代表心情，所以同開心有關；佢喺倉頡入面攞碼 P。右邊係「兌」呢個字身，倉頡通常字首取一碼、字身取到三碼，所以「兌」我哋順住寫落去，先取頭「八」（C），再取中間「口」（R），最後取埋腳「儿」（U），砌成 PCRU。整個字就係字首忄 P 加字身兌嘅頭 C、二 R、尾 U，剛剛好四碼。記住喇：一顆心（忄P）見到「兌」就笑咗，咁就係喜「悅」啦！

情.en: Today's character is 情, read cing4, the word for feeling, sentiment, or emotion. Notice it divides into a left and a right side: on the left is the upright heart radical 忄, which links to the heart and to feelings, and in Cangjie it gives just one code, P, because as a leading radical (字首) it is limited to a single code. The right side is 青, which serves as the body (字身) and is allowed up to three codes, so we take its head 扌 as Q, the middle stroke 一 as M, and the tail ⺼ as B. Put together that gives PQMB. Memory hook: one heart P, then 青's head, middle, and tail — 扌、一、⺼ — and your feelings are spelled out.
情.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「情」，讀 cing4，即係感情、情緒、心情嗰個「情」。你睇佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係豎心邊「忄」，代表同心、同感受有關，喺倉頡入面淨係取一個碼 P，因為佢係一個做字首嘅偏旁，通常只得一碼。右邊係「青」字，佢做字身，可以取到三個碼，所以我哋分別攞頭「扌」係 Q、中間嗰橫「一」係 M、尾嗰個「⺼」係 B。合埋一齊就係 PQMB。記住口訣：豎心一個 P，右邊青字頭扌、中一、尾⺼，情懷就寫好嘞。

想.en: Today's character is「想」, read soeng2, meaning to think, to consider, or to plan — as in「我想食杯麵」, expressing a wish inside your heart. Notice its structure is two layers stacked: on top sits「相」and below it sits a「心」. The「相」acts as the 字首, and since a 字首 takes at most its first and last codes, we grab the first piece「木」(D) and the last piece「目」(U), skipping the middle; then the「心」below is the 字身, and being a single part it simply gives「心」(P). Put those three together and you get D, U, P. Remember it like this: what you plan, you fix with your「木」-and「目」-eye, then keep it in your「心」(P) — that's「想」!
想.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「想」，讀soeng2，意思係諗嘢、思考、打算，好似「我想食杯麵」入面表達心裏面嘅願望噉。你望吓佢嘅結構，其實係上下兩層：上面係「相」，下面係一個「心」。「相」呢個部分做字首，倉頡規定字首最多取頭同尾兩碼，所以佢頭取「木」（D），尾取「目」（U），中間唔理；跟住下面嘅「心」做字身，得返一個部件就直接取「心」（P）。三個部件砌埋一齊，就係D、U、P三碼。記住喇：一件事諗到你要用「木」眼「目」睇實嗮，再放喺「心」（P）裏面，就係「想」！

意.en: Today's character is 意, read ji3, meaning a thought, an idea, or an opinion — you'll meet it in words like 鍾意 (to like) and 意思 (meaning), and in the sentence 我明白你嘅意思, it's the thought in someone's mind that you understand. Look at the shape: it stacks top over bottom, with 音 sitting above and 心 resting below. Cangjie splits into a 字首 and a 字身: the 字首 is the top piece 音, which is a compound, so instead of every stroke it gives head-second-tail — that's 卜 Y, 廿 T, and the final 日 A, making YTA. The 字身 is the bottom 心, and as the trailing part it contributes just one code, 心 P, so the whole thing comes together as YTAP. Remember it this way: 音 up top gives YTA, 心 down below gives P — top-sound, bottom-heart, and you've got 意.
意.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「意」，讀作 ji3，解作念頭、意思或者諗法，好似「鍾意」、「意思」呢啲字都會用到，「我明白你嘅意思」講嘅就係心裡面嗰個念頭。你望下呢個字，係上下疊埋嘅結構：上面係「音」，下面係「心」。倉頡拆碼分字首同字身，字首係上面嗰個「音」，佢係複合體，唔可以攞晒每一筆，就攞頭、二、尾三碼，即係「卜」Y、「廿」T、同尾嗰個「日」A，合埋就係 YTA；字身係下面嗰個「心」，屬於字身最後一部分，淨係攞一碼 P。所以四碼砌埋就係 YTAP。記住個口訣：「音」攞頭二尾 YTA，「心」一碼 P，上音下心，就係「意」喇。

愛.en: Today's character is 愛, read oi3, meaning love or to be fond of something, as in 親愛 (can1 oi3, dear) and 愛上 (oi3 soeng5, to fall in love with). It looks crowded, with lots of strokes stacked together, but that's exactly why it's a whole-shape character: Cangjie has a special rule for characters too tangled to split cleanly, where you take only the head, second, third, and very last pieces and skip whatever sits in the middle. So working from top to bottom, you take 爫 (B) at the head, then 冖 (B), then 心 (P) lower down, and finally 又 (E) at the very end, ignoring the middle, which gives you BBPE. Try writing 我好愛我媽媽, 'I love my mum very much,' and you'll feel the weight of this busy character. Remember it this way: 愛 is so full there's no room for the middle, so we keep only the head, second, third, and tail — 爫 冖 心 又.
愛.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「愛」，讀做 oi3，即係愛、鍾意嘅意思，好似「親愛」（can1 oi3）同「愛上」（oi3 soeng5）咁樣用。呢個字睇落好複雜，堆咗好多嘢喺一齊，但係佢係一個「整體字」，倉頡有一條特別規則專門處理呢種筆畫太多、拆唔清楚嘅字：只取頭、第二、第三同最尾四個部分，中間嗰啲通通跳過。所以我哋順住由上到下攞：頭係「爫」（B），跟住係「冖」（B），再嚟係下面嗰個「心」（P），最尾係「又」（E），中間嘅部分就唔理佢，砌埋一齊就係 BBPE。你試吓寫「我好愛我媽媽」，就會感覺到呢個字嘅份量。記住喇：愛太滿，中間唔夠位擺，所以我哋只留住頭、二、三同尾——爫冖心又。

感.en: Today we meet 感, read gam2 — the feel of 感覺 (feeling) and 感情 (emotion), meaning to feel, to perceive, to sense. Look at it: on top sits 咸, and underneath rests a single 心 (heart), and that heart at the bottom is exactly the clue that this character is about what you feel inside. In Cangjie the top part 咸 acts as the head, but we don't spell out its every stroke — we take just the leading slash 戈 on key I and the 口 inside it on key R; then the 心 below acts as the body, taken as the whole 心 shape on key P, giving you IRP. Why does 咸 hand over only 戈 and 口? Because as the head it may give at most two codes, so we take the leading piece and one representative piece and stop there. Here's your hook: a heart that feels — 戈 (I) and 口 (R) up top, one 心 (P) at the bottom.
感.zh: 今日我哋學「感」呢個字，讀音係 gam2，即係「感覺」、「感情」嗰個感，解作感受、感知，係一個好有情感嘅字。你望吓佢，上面係「咸」，下面係一粒「心」，個心字擺喺底部，正正就係話呢個字同心裏面嘅感受有關。喺倉頡入面，上面嘅「咸」做字首，我哋唔會將佢每一筆都拆出嚟，而係取佢頭嗰撇「戈」，鍵係 I，再取入面嗰個「口」，鍵係 R；跟住落到下面嘅「心」做字身，取「心」呢個形，鍵係 P，所以成個字就係 IRP。點解「咸」淨係取「戈口」兩嚿呢？因為佢係做字首，字首最多取兩碼，取到頭同代表性嗰兩部分就夠，唔使貪多。記住個口訣：心裏面有感覺，先有戈口喺頭，一粒心喺尾，戈（I）口（R）心（P）。

慈.en: Today we learn 慈, read ci4, meaning kind, charitable, or benevolent — it describes someone with a warm, loving heart. Look at the character: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath there's a busy stack of strokes that looks complicated, but the coding follows a clear rule. In Cangjie the head 艹 gives just one code, T; then the lower body is taken by the head-second-last method, so we pick 女 as V, 戈 as I, and 心 as P, skipping whatever sits in the middle. Put in typing order that gives you T, V, I, P — the full code TVIP. Here's your memory hook: the grass hat T comes first, then the three VIP guests walk in, and the crowd in the middle just gets skipped.
慈.zh: 今日我哋學「慈」字，讀做 ci4，意思係慈愛、慈祥，形容人心地善良、有愛心。你望住呢個字，上面係個草花頭「艹」，下面就層層疊起唔少嘢，睇落好似好複雜，但拆碼其實有規律。倉頡係咁樣分嘅：上面嘅字首「艹」淨取一個碼，就係 T；下面嘅字身部分照住「頭、二、尾」嘅口訣去取，即係「女」V、「戈」I、「心」P，中間嗰啲筆畫就跳過唔理。所以成個字順住打落去就係 T、V、I、P，即 TVIP。記住一句：草花頭 T 一開頭，跟住 VIP 三個貴賓入場，中間人自動跳過，你就即刻打得出「慈」喇。

應.en: Today we learn 應, read "jing1" or "jing3", meaning "should" or "ought to" — the very word you'd use in a sentence like "you should sleep earlier." This is a semi-enclosing character built with the ⿸ pattern: 䧹 wraps around on the outside as the head, and 心 sits inside as the body. For the head we don't spell out every stroke — instead we take its first and last pieces: since 䧹's own full code is IOOG, its first is 戈 (I) and its last is 土 (G), giving us IG. Then the body 心 follows, and since a body usually gives just one code, we simply take P. Put the three together — 戈, 土, 心 — and you get IGP. Remember it this way: the outer 䧹 gives you first-last 戈土, the inner 心 adds a single P, and that's how 應 comes together.
應.zh: 今日我哋學「應」呢個字，讀「jing1」或者「jing3」，意思係「應該」、「應當」，好似你同人講「你應該早啲瞓」嘅時候用嘅嗰個字。呢個字係半包圍結構，用「⿸」嘅方式，外面係「䧹」呢個字首，入面係「心」呢個字身。字首嘅部分我哋唔會逐筆拆到晒，而係取佢個「頭」同個「尾」：「䧹」自己嘅完整碼係 IOOG，所以頭係戈（I），尾係土（G），合埋就係 IG。跟住輪到字身「心」，一個字身通常只取一碼，所以我哋淨係攞佢個碼 P。三個拼埋就係戈土心，即係 IGP。記住個口訣：外面「䧹」取頭尾戈土，入面「心」淨係一個 P，「應該」就係咁應運而生。

成.en: Today we learn 成, read "sing4" or "seng4", meaning completed, finished, or accomplished, as in 成功 (to succeed). Look at its structure: it's a whole character (整體字), meaning it doesn't split cleanly into a left-right or top-bottom pair, so instead we use the special head-second-tail rule, taking only the first shape, the second shape, and the very last shape. The first is 戈 on the I key, then the second is 竹 on the H key, and the last is 尸 on the S key, which together spell IHS. Memory hook: a spear (戈) holds a stroke of bamboo (竹), with a tail (尸) trailing behind — that's how you finish 成.
成.zh: 今日我哋學「成」呢個字，讀「sing4」或者「seng4」，意思係完成、做好、成就，好似「成功」咁。你望下佢個結構，其實佢係一個整體字——即係話佢唔容易乾淨俐落噉分做左右或者上下兩橛，所以就要用「頭、二、尾」呢個特別規則，即係只揀第一嚿、第二嚿、同最尾一嚿嘅字形碼。第一嚿係「戈」，喺 I 掣；跟住第二嚿係「竹」，喺 H 掣；最後一嚿係「尸」，喺 S 掣，砌埋一齊就係 IHS。記憶鉤：一支「戈」揸住一撇「竹」，尾巴拖住個「尸」，成功打出「成」！

我.en: Today we learn a character you'll use every single day: 我, read ngo5, meaning "I", "me", or "we". This shape is hard to split cleanly at a glance, so Cangjie treats it as a whole-character and codes it with the head-second-tail rule — you take only the very first shape, the second shape, and the very last shape, ignoring whatever sits in the middle. First comes the slanting stroke 丿 on the H key, then the hand shape 手 on Q, and finally the spear shape 戈 on I, giving you HQI. Picture yourself gripping a spear (I) and sweeping your hand (Q) with a stroke (H) to defend yourself — head, hand, and spear spell 我.
我.zh: 今日我哋學一個你日日都要用嘅字：我，讀ngo5，即係「我」自己嘅意思，可以係「我」、「我哋」。呢個字唔容易一眼睇出點樣拆開，所以倉頡當佢係一個整體字，用「頭、二、尾」呢個規則嚟取碼——即係只取最頭一個、第二個同最尾一個字形，中間嘅唔理。先取一撇丿，佢喺Q鍵嘅隔籬，係H鍵；再取個手字，係Q鍵；最後取個戈字，係I鍵，砌埋一齊就係HQI。你可以記住：我攞住把戈（I），用手（Q）撇（H）出嚟保護自己，呢個「頭手尾戈」就係「我」。

或.en: Today we learn 或, read waak6, meaning "or" — think of choosing, like tea or coffee? Look at its shape: it's really a 戈 wrapping around the pieces inside, so the whole thing is framed by that enclosing structure. Because of that wrap, we don't chop it into many bits; instead we take head, second, and tail from the whole shape: 戈 is I, 口 is R, and 一 is M, giving IRM. Since 戈 encloses the rest, the character counts as one unit and we grab first, then second, then last — 戈口一 in order — which is exactly right. Memory hook: 戈 wraps it, take head-second-tail, read waak6, and type IRM.
或.zh: 今日我哋學「或」呢個字，讀音係 waak6，就係「或者」嘅意思，好似你揀啦：飲茶或者咖啡？睇吓佢個形，其實係一個「戈」字包住裏面啲嘢，所以整個字嘅框架都圍住成個結構。輸入嘅時候我哋唔會拆到好碎，而係喺呢個包住嘅整體度取頭、二、尾三個碼：戈係 I，口係 R，一係 M，砌埋就係 IRM。因為「戈」包住其餘部分，成個字當作一嚿嚟取碼，先頭、再第二、最後尾，順住 戈口一 就啱晒。記住呢個口訣：戈包住、頭二尾，讀 waak6，砌出嚟就係 IRM。

戰.en: Today we're learning 戰, read zin3, meaning war, fighting or battle — you'll see it in words like 戰爭 zin3 zang1 (war) and 挑戰 tiu1 zin3 (to challenge). Look at how it's built: on the left is 單, and on the right is 戈. In Cangjie, 單 is the head of this character and 戈 is the body. Because the head 單 is a busy, crowded shape, a head is only allowed to give up two codes, so we take its first piece 口 R and its last piece 十 J; then the body 戈 contributes just one code, itself, I, giving us RJI. Here's your hook: grab the outer edges of 單 (口 R, 十 J), then add the spear 戈 I, and the battle is set.
戰.zh: 今日我哋學「戰」字，讀作 zin3，即係打仗、戰爭嘅意思，好似「戰爭」zin3 zang1 或者「挑戰」tiu1 zin3 咁樣用。你睇吓佢個結構，左邊係「單」，右邊係「戈」。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，左邊「單」係字首，右邊「戈」係字身。字首「單」個樣好複雜，倉頡只准字首取到頭尾兩碼，所以我哋喺「單」度攞頭嗰個口 R 同尾嗰個十 J；跟住字身「戈」淨係取一碼，就係戈本身 I，合埋就係 RJI。記住喇：頭尾夾住個「單」（口 R、十 J），最後補一撇「戈」I，一場「戰」就打起嚟喇。

戶.en: look at this character: 戶, read wu6. It originally means a door — one leaf of a door — and from there it grew to mean a family or household. Notice the short slanting stroke at the very top: when we type it, we treat that as the 竹 shape on key H, while the part left underneath is a 尸 shape on key S. 戶 is a whole character (整體字), meaning it doesn't break cleanly into a head-part and a body-part, so we follow the whole-character rule: take just the first and last shapes, head 竹 H and tail 尸 S, giving HS. Remember it this way — a little slash of 竹 H on top, a 尸 S below, and that's how the door swings open.
戶.zh: 睇下呢個字：戶，讀作 wu6，本來意思係「門」，例如一扇門，後來就引申做「家庭」、「住戶」嘅意思。你留意佢頂上有一撇短短嘅斜筆，寫嘅時候我哋當佢做竹字形，個鍵係 H；而下面剩返嘅部分係一個尸字形，個鍵係 S。戶係一個整體字，佢唔會拆成清楚嘅字首同字身兩截，所以我哋跟整體字嘅取碼法：淨係攞頭同尾兩個形，頭係竹 H，尾係尸 S，合埋就係 HS。記住個口訣——頂上一撇竹 H，下面一個尸 S，門戶就係咁開嘅。

房.en: Today we learn 房, read "fong2", meaning a room in a home — the same 房 you see in 廚房 (kitchen) and 間房 (to partition a room). Look at its shape: it's a half-enclosing frame, with a canopy over the top-left wrapping the piece inside, and you write the top and left side first. Cangjie splits it into a 字首 and a 字身: the 字首 is 戶, whose own code is IS, and here we take its head and tail — the dot 丶 which is H, and the 尸 which is S; the 字身 is 方, whose own code is YHS, and here we take its head 亠 (Y), its 竹 (H), and its tail 尸 (S). Written out in order that gives you HSYHS. Memory hook: 戶 gives a dot then 尸, 方 gives 亠, 竹, 尸 — one house, a dot at the door, hiding a 方 inside.
房.zh: 今日我哋學「房」字，讀「fong2」，即係屋企入面嘅一間房，好似「廚房」嘅廚房、「間房」嘅房咁。你睇佢個外形，係一個半包圍嘅結構，左上角罩住入面嘅嘢，寫嘅時候上面同左邊先落筆。倉頡拆佢做字首同字身兩橛：字首係「戶」，佢自己嘅碼係 IS，喺呢度取頭尾兩個碼——頭嗰點「丶」係 H，尾嗰個「尸」係 S；字身係「方」，佢自己嘅碼係 YHS，喺呢度取頭嘅「亠」係 Y、中間嘅「竹」係 H、尾嘅「尸」係 S。所以成個碼順住寫落去就係 HSYHS。記住呢個口訣：戶頭尾點尸，方就亠竹尸——一間房，門口一點，入面藏住個方。

所.en: This character is 所, read so2, and it means a place or location — you meet it all the time in words like 所以 so2 ji5 (hence) and 所有 so2 jau5 (every). Look at how it divides down the middle into a left part and a right part: the left is the head 戶, the right is the body 斤. Because 戶 has that ⺁ on top, you take first-and-last: the first piece is ⺁ (H) and the last is the 尸 beneath it (S), so the head gives you just HS. The body 斤 gets the fuller three-code treatment of head-second-last: the head 丿 (H), the second 一 (M), and the last, that central stroke 中 (L), spelling HML. Put it together and you get HSHML — think of a doorway (戶) opening onto the place where you live, and the split stays clear in your mind.
所.zh: 呢個字係「所」，讀so2，解作地方、場所，好似「所以」so2 ji5同「所有」so2 jau5咁常用。你睇佢分做左右兩邊，左邊係字首「戶」，右邊係字身「斤」。因為「戶」上面有個⺁，你就要用取頭尾嘅方法：頭係⺁（H），尾係下面嘅尸（S），所以字首得HS兩碼。到右邊字身「斤」呢，字身可以攞到三碼，用取頭、次、尾：頭係丿（H），次係一（M），尾係中間嗰豎「中」（L），砌埋就係HML。成個字合埋就係HSHML，記住口訣「戶頭尾、斤頭次尾」，一個門戶開喺你住嘅所在，就唔會撈亂喇！

手.en: Today we learn 手, read sau2, which simply means "hand" — the hands on your body. Look at its shape: a small stroke on top, three horizontal lines in the middle, and a hook sweeping through them, and the whole thing looks like an open palm, which makes it easy to picture. In Cangjie, 手 is itself a radical, so it doesn't get broken into smaller pieces; you just press one key, Q, and the entire code is that single letter Q. Why only one code? Because when a character is already a complete radical on its own, Cangjie takes its own key directly and never splits it further. Here's your memory hook: see an open hand, and reach out your own hand to tap Q — one letter and you're done!
手.zh: 今日我哋學「手」呢個字，讀作 sau2，就係你身體嗰兩隻手嘅意思。你望住佢個樣：頂上一撇，中間三橫，穿過去嗰一勾，成個字寫落去就係一隻手掌張開嘅樣，好易記。喺倉頡入面，「手」本身就係一個字根，佢唔使拆開，所以你只需要撳一個掣 Q 就搞掂，全碼就係 Q 一個字母。點解淨係一碼呢？因為佢係整體字根，倉頡入面凡係本身已經係字根嘅字，就直接取佢自己嘅碼，唔會再拆細。記住喇：見到一隻手張開，你就伸隻手去撳個 Q 掣，一個字母就搞掂！

扒.en: Today's character is 扒, read paa2, as in 牛扒 (beefsteak), and it means to scratch, dig up, crawl, or crouch. Look at it: it's made of two side-by-side pieces — on the left the hand radical 扌, and on the right 八. In Cangjie the left piece 扌 is the head, which you type as Q, and the right piece 八 is the body, which you type as C, so the whole code is simply QC. The split falls here because the character clearly divides into a left and a right part, and Cangjie reads left-to-right, taking the head 扌 (Q) first and then the body 八 (C). To remember it, picture one hand 扌 (Q) reaching in to grab 八 (C) — that's 扒, the same character you'll see when you order your 牛扒 tonight.
扒.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「扒」，讀做 paa2，好似「牛扒」嗰個扒，意思有抓、挖、爬、蹲嘅意思。你望下佢，係左右兩橛砌埋一齊：左邊係提手旁「扌」，右邊係「八」。用倉頡拆嘅時候，字首就係左邊嘅「扌」，我哋喺鍵盤㩒 Q；字身就係右邊嘅「八」，㩒 C，兩個夾埋就係 QC。點解咁拆呢？因為呢個字明顯分咗左右兩部分，倉頡會由左至右、由外至內咁攞，先攞晒左邊字首嘅碼，再攞字身，所以係 Q 之後跟住 C。記住嘅時候可以咁諗：一隻手「扌」（Q）抓住「八」（C），就係扒——你今晚食「牛扒」嗰陣就記得起佢喇。

打.en: Today's character is 打, read daa2, meaning to strike, hit, or beat — you see it in words like 打波 (play ball) and 打開 (to open). Look at its shape: it's a left-right build, with the hand radical 扌 on the left and the character 丁 on the right. The left 扌 is the 字首 (leading part), and because it's a complete, mature piece it takes just one code, Q. The right 丁 serves as the 字身 (body), and since a body of more than one piece takes head and tail, we grab its head 一 (M) and its tail 亅 (N), giving M then N. Put it all together and the code is Q, M, N. Here's your hook: a hand (Q) picks up a nail with a hook (M, N) and hammers it down — that's 打, to hit.
打.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「打」，讀daa2，即係打擊、拍打、攻打嘅意思，好似「打波」、「打開」都用到佢。你望下佢嘅樣，係左右兩邊夾埋成一個字：左邊係手字旁「扌」，右邊係一個「丁」字。左邊個「扌」係字首，佢係一個成熟嘅部件，得一碼，就係Q。右邊嘅「丁」做字身，因為部件多過一碼嘅時候要取頭尾兩碼，所以攞頭「一」（M）同埋尾「亅」（N），連埋成M、N。合起嚟就係Q、M、N三碼。記住呢個口訣：手（Q）拎起一（M）支釘鈎（N），一手就打落去，「打」就係咁砌出嚟。

批.en: Today we learn 批, read pai1, meaning to comment, to criticize, and also to sell wholesale. Take a look at it: on the left is the hand radical 扌, and on the right is the character 比 — two parts joined together. When you break it into code, the head on the left, 扌, gives you Q; the body on the right is 比, which is made of two 匕 pieces, and since Cangjie takes only the first and last of a body, you grab the first 匕 as P and the last 匕 again as P, so the full code comes out QPP. Even though 比 looks like it has several strokes, the body rule keeps only its head and tail and ignores the middle, which is why the code stays short. Here's your memory hook: one hand (Q) pressing down on two little 匕 shapes (PP) makes 批 — and I just ate a piece of apple pie!
批.zh: 今日我哋學「批」字，讀音係 pai1，意思係批評、批准，亦都可以指批發嘅意思。你望下佢，左邊係個提手旁「扌」，右邊係「比」字，兩橛拼埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「扌」取碼 Q；右邊嘅字身係「比」，佢由兩個「匕」組成，倉頡對字身用「頭尾」規則，即係取頭嘅「匕」係 P，再取尾嘅「匕」又係 P，所以砌埋一齊全碼就係 QPP。呢個「比」字面上有幾筆，但係取碼淨係揀頭同尾，中間唔理，所以你唔會見到成串長碼。記住呢個口訣：一隻手（Q）撳住兩粒「匕」（PP），就係「批」，我食咗一件蘋果批啦！

技.en: Today we learn 技, read gei6, meaning skill, ability, or ingenuity — the same 技 in 技術 (technique) and 科技 (technology). Look at it: on the left is the hand radical 扌, and on the right is 支. When you break it into codes, the 字首 (leading part) 扌 is a familiar radical that sits on Q, and as a single radical it takes just one code — no further splitting. The 字身 (body) 支 is then split head-and-tail: the head 十 is J and the tail 又 is E, so the whole character comes out as QJE. Remember it this way: one hand (Q) practices with 十 (J) and 又 (E) until skill is mastered.
技.zh: 今日我哋學「技」呢個字，讀作 gei6，即係本領、技能嘅意思，好似「技術」、「科技」嗰個「技」。你望下佢，左邊係提手旁「扌」，右邊係「支」。拆碼嘅時候，字首「扌」係一個好熟嘅部件，喺鍵盤上係 Q，佢一個部首得一碼，唔使再拆。跟住嘅字身「支」拆頭尾：頭係「十」，喺 J，尾係「又」，喺 E，所以成隻字砌埋就係 QJE。記住個口訣：一隻手（Q）用十（J）字又（E）練，就練成一身好技術。

投.en: Today's character is 投, read tau4, meaning to throw, cast, or invest — think of pitching a ball or investing money. Look at how it divides into two sides: the left is 扌, the raised-hand radical, which you press with Q. Because 扌 is a mature radical serving as the head, it contributes just one code, so the head is simply Q. The right side, 殳, serves as the body and takes three codes — first, second, and last: the opening 丿 on H, the second stroke 乙 on N, and the final 又 on E, giving you QHNE. The split falls here because the one-code head already fills its slot, leaving the remaining slots for the body's first-second-last selection. Remember it this way: one hand (扌) gives a mighty toss (殳), and the ball is thrown — QHNE.
投.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「投」，讀 tau4，意思係「掟、擲、投放」，好似投球、投資噉樣。你望下佢分兩邊：左邊係「扌」，即係提手邊，佢喺鍵盤上面撳 Q；佢做字首，而扌係一個成熟嘅部首，做字首淨係取一碼，所以就係 Q 一個。右邊嘅「殳」做字身，你要取頭、次、尾三個碼——頭係「丿」撳 H，第二個係「乙」撳 N，最尾嘅係「又」撳 E，合埋就係 QHNE。點解殳要取三碼呢？因為左邊字首已經佔咗一位，剩落嘅位就畀字身填，字身取頭、次、尾就啱夠。記住喇：一隻手（扌）用力一掟（殳），個波就投出去，QHNE。

拉.en: Today we learn 拉, read laai1 (also laa1), meaning to pull, drag or stretch — think of pulling a door open. Look at the character: on the left is the hand radical 扌, a shape you already know well, and in Cangjie you press Q for it. On the right sits 立, which as the 字身 gets split into head and tail: the head 亠 gives you Y, and the tail 廿 gives you T. So after the 字首 扌 (Q), the body 立 contributes its head 亠 (Y) and tail 廿 (T), spelling out QYT in full. Here's your hook: one hand (Q) doing the work is exactly what 拉 means — like 拉麵, pulled noodles, where a good tug stretches the dough long.
拉.zh: 我哋今日學「拉」字，讀 laai1（又讀 laa1），意思係拉、拖、扯，好似你想拉開一道門噉。你睇睇個字，左邊係提手旁「扌」，呢個係好熟嘅部首，喺倉頡度我哋撳 Q。右邊係個「立」字，佢係一個要拆頭尾嘅字身：頭係「亠」，撳 Y；尾係「廿」，撳 T。所以字首「扌」（Q）之後，字身「立」取頭「亠」（Y）尾「廿」（T），合埋就係 QYT。記住喇：一隻手（Q）用力，就係去「拉」嘢，好似「拉麵」噉一扯就長咗。

括.en: Today we learn 括, which reads kut3 and means to include, to embrace, to enclose — as in 包括 (to comprise) and 概括 (to summarize). Look at it: on the left is the hand radical 扌, and on the right is the character 舌 (tongue). When typing, the radical 扌 comes first as the head, and it lives on the Q key; the body 舌 is not a whole-unit character, so it splits into head, second and tail — the head 竹 is H, the second piece 十 is J, and the tail 口 is R, giving you QHJR. Here's the hook: a hand cradling a tongue — one hand, one tongue, and it wraps everyone in, just like 包括埋你哋 means you are all included too.
括.zh: 今日我哋學「括」呢個字，讀做 kut3，意思係包含、包住、囊括入面，好似「包括」同「概括」噉。你望下佢，左邊係個提手旁扌，右邊係個「舌」字。輸入嗰陣，字首取左邊嘅扌，佢喺個 Q 鍵度；跟住個「舌」係字身，因為佢唔係整體字，所以要拆頭、二、尾三部分——頭係竹 H，第二係十 J，尾係口 R，砌埋一齊就係 QHJR。記住個口訣：提手抱住條舌頭，一手一舌就包晒你哋喇。

持.en: Today we learn 持, read ci4, meaning to hold, to support, or to keep — as in 支持 (zi1 ci4, to support) and 保持 (bou2 ci4, to maintain), both about keeping a grip on something. Look at the character: it splits left and right, with the hand radical 扌 on the left and 寺 on the right. In Cangjie, the radical 扌 becomes the head and is taken as Q; then the body 寺 follows the head-second-tail rule, giving 土 at G for the head, 木 at D for the second piece, and 戈 at I for the tail — so the full code is QGDI. Why doesn't 寺 spell out every stroke? Because the body is capped at three keys, so we take only the head, second, and tail as its representatives. Remember it this way: a hand (扌) holds firm at the temple (寺), and Q-G-D-I are the four points your hand grips.
持.zh: 今日我哋學「持」呢個字，讀作 ci4，意思係「握住、支撐、保持」，好似「支持」（zi1 ci4）同「保持」（bou2 ci4）咁樣，講緊守住某樣嘢唔放。你望下個字，佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係手部嘅「扌」，右邊係「寺」。倉頡拆碼時，字首取左邊嘅「扌」，喺 Q 位；跟住字身「寺」按倉頡「取頭、取次、取尾」嘅規矩拆——頭係「土」喺 G，第二個係「木」喺 D，尾嗰個係「戈」喺 I，所以整個字碼就係 QGDI。點解「寺」唔全部拆晒？因為字身最多取三碼，所以只揀頭、次、尾三個代表碼。記住喇：一隻手（扌）喺寺廟（寺）度堅持撐住，Q-G-D-I 就係你手裏握實嘅四個位。

指.en: Today we learn 指, read zi2, the same 指 as in 手指 (finger). It means a finger or toe, and also to point out, indicate or instruct — like using your finger to show something to someone. Look at its shape: the left side is a compressed form of 'hand', and the right side is the character 旨. In Cangjie the hand radical on the left is written 扌 on the Q key, and because it is a radical form used as the head, the head takes just that one code; the 旨 on the right is the body, and a body takes its head and tail, giving 匕 on the P key and 日 on the A key, so the full code is QPA. Here's your hook: one hand (Q) pointing at a target (PA) — that's exactly what 指 does, it points!
指.zh: 今日我哋學「指」呢個字，讀音係 zi2，同「手指」個「指」一樣，可以解手指、腳趾，又可以解「指出」、「指示」，即係用手指住嘢畀人睇。你望吓佢個樣：左邊係個「手」嘅變形，右邊係個「旨」字。喺倉頡入面，左邊嗰個提手旁我哋叫做「扌」，佢喺 Q 掣，係一個部首形，所以字首淨係取佢一碼；跟住右邊個「旨」係字身，字身要取頭同尾，頭係「匕」喺 P 掣，尾係「日」喺 A 掣，合埋就係 QPA。記住呢個手勢：一隻手（Q）指住一個目標（PA），咪就係「指」出方向囉！

排.en: Today we learn 排, read paai4, meaning a row, a rank, or a line — think of people lined up one after another. Look at how it's built from a left part and a right part: on the left is the hand radical 扌, and on the right is the shape 非. The 扌 is the 字首 (the leading part), and it takes just one code, Q. The right-hand 非 becomes the 字身 (the body), and a body can take up to three codes — head, middle, and tail — so we follow its shape and pick 中 = L for the head, 一 = M for the middle, and 卜 = Y for the tail. Put it together and you get Q, L, M, Y, that is QLMY: remember the 字首 gives only one code while the 字身 is allowed three. A little hook: one hand (扌) gathers everyone into a line, so you 安排 things and everyone 排隊 to go in.
排.zh: 今日我哋學「排」呢個字，讀做 paai4，解「一行、一列、排名」嘅意思，好似排隊咁樣一個接一個排成一行。你望吓佢係左右兩邊拼埋嘅：左邊係提手旁「扌」，右邊係「非」字。「扌」做字首，喺鍵盤度攞 Q；右邊嘅「非」就做字身，字身可以攞頭、身、尾三個碼，所以我哋順住個形去攞——先攞頭「中」係 L，再攞中間嘅「一」係 M，最尾攞「卜」係 Y。合埋就係 Q、L、M、Y，即係 QLMY。記住個字首淨係攞一個碼，字身先至可以攞到三個，所以「非」呢邊要拆到 L、M、Y 三橛。你可以咁記：一隻手（扌）將啲人扶埋一行，於是「安排」好晒去「排隊」。

接.en: Today we learn 接, read "zip3", a word with several linked meanings: to receive, to continue, to catch, to connect. Look at its shape — on the left is 扌 the hand radical, and on the right sits 妾. The left 扌 is the 字首, and you type it with Q; the right 妾 is the 字身. When a 字身 needs breaking down, we take its head, middle, and tail, so from 妾 we grab the head 卜 (Y), the middle 廿 (T), and the tail 女 (V). Put it together and you get QYTV — left first then right, the 字首 leading, and the 字身 giving head, middle, tail. Memory hook: a hand (扌) reaching out to catch — that's 接.
接.zh: 今日我哋學「接」呢個字，讀「zip3」，佢有好多意思：接收、接續、接住、連接。你睇下佢個結構——左邊係「扌」（提手旁），右邊係「妾」字。左邊嘅「扌」做字首，撳個掣係 Q；右邊個「妾」就係字身。字身要拆嘅時候要跟頭、身、尾嘅原則，所以我哋喺右邊「妾」度取頭「卜」（撳 Y）、中間「廿」（撳 T）、最尾「女」（撳 V）。合埋一齊就係 QYTV，先左後右，字首行先，字身跟住取頭中尾。記住呢個字：一隻手（扌）去接住個「妾」，就係「接」啦！

推.en: The character 推 reads teoi1 and means to push or push forward, like when you push a door open. Look at it: on the left sits a hand — the 扌 radical, which you type with Q. On the right is 隹, a piece too complex to spell stroke by stroke, so Cangjie takes just its head and tail: the head is 亻 (人), typed O, and the tail is the 土 at the bottom, typed G. That's why the 字首 扌 gives Q and the 字身 隹 contributes only head and tail O and G, giving you QOG. Picture it this way: a hand (Q) pushing a person (O) standing on the earth (G) — that's 推, and you'll meet it in words like 推動 (teoi1 dung6) and 推廣 (teoi1 gwong2).
推.zh: 「推」讀作 teoi1，意思係用力向前推、推動，好似你推開一度門噉。你望吓佢，左邊係一隻手 —— 就係「扌」，個提手邊，喺鍵盤上面撳 Q。右邊係「隹」，呢個部件本身好複雜，倉頡唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取佢嘅頭同尾兩部分：頭係「亻」（人），撳 O，尾係下面嗰個「土」，撳 G。所以「推」嘅字首扌取 Q，字身隹就取頭尾 O 同 G，合埋就係 QOG。你可以噉樣記：一隻手（Q）推住一個人（O）企喺土地（G）度，就係「推」喇。你亦都學到「推動」（teoi1 dung6）同「推廣」（teoi1 gwong2）呢兩個詞。

提.en: Today we learn 提, read "tai4", meaning to hold or lift something in your hand, as in 提供 (to provide) and 提出 (to bring up). Look at it: on the left is the hand radical 扌, and on the right sits 是, so the whole thing points to an action done with the hand.
