When we split it, the prefix 扌 on the left gives just one code, Q; the body 是 on the right takes three codes — head, second and tail — which are 日 A, 一 M, and 人 O. Why one code for the prefix but three for the body? Because in a left-right character the prefix yields and gives only one code, letting the body take more, and read in order that spells QAMO. Remember it this way: one hand Q lifting up 是 (AMO).
提.zh: 今日我哋學「提」呢個字，讀「tai4」，意思係用手拿起、舉起，好似「提供」、「提出」咁樣。你望下佢，左邊係手部嘅「扌」，右邊係「是」，一睇就知同用手嘅動作有關。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「扌」淨係取一碼，就係Q；右邊嘅字身「是」就要取頭、二、尾三碼——頭係「日」A，第二個碼係「一」M，尾係「人」O。點解字首得一碼、字身取三碼呢？因為喺左右結構入面，字首讓位只取一碼，字身先攞得多，順序砌埋就係QAMO。記住一句：一隻手Q，提起個「是」（AMO）。

搵.en: Today we learn 搵, a word you hear every day in Cantonese, read wan2 — it's the 搵 in 搵嘢 and 搵人, meaning to look for or search. Look at its shape: on the left is the hand radical 扌, and on the right is 昷, so you can already tell it's about doing something with your hands. When we split it, because 搵 is a left-right character, the left 扌 becomes the 字首 (lead) and takes just one code, Q; the right side 昷 becomes the 字身 (body), and for the body we take head, second, and tail — the head 囗 gives W, the second piece 人 inside gives O, and the tail 廿 at the bottom gives T, so the whole code is QWOT. Here's your hook: one hand (Q) reaching into a box (W) to find the person (O) and 廿 (T) inside — whatever you're searching for is right there in the box!
搵.zh: 今日我哋學「搵」呢個字，喺廣東話入面日日都用到，讀做 wan2，就係「搵嘢」、「搵人」嗰個「搵」，即係搜尋、揾嘢嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，左邊係提手旁「扌」，右邊係「昷」，一睇就知同用手嘅動作有關。拆碼嘅時候，因為「搵」係左右兩橛，左邊個「扌」就係字首，只取一碼 Q；右邊個「昷」就係字身，字身要拆頭、次、尾，頭係「囗」打 W，次係入面嘅「人」打 O，尾係下面嘅「廿」打 T，所以成個字砌埋就係 QWOT。記住個口訣：一隻手（Q）去搵一個框（W）入面嘅人（O）同廿（T），你要搵嘅嘢就喺框裏面！

據.en: Today's character is 據, read geoi3, meaning to occupy or take possession of, and also a base or foundation you rely on. Look at how it divides left and right: on the left is the hand radical 扌, which gives Q on your keyboard and serves as the head of the character. The right side is 豦, the body, and because it is crowded with strokes we don't spell every piece — instead we take head, second, and tail: the head 卜 is Y, the second piece 心 is P, and the tail 人 is O, giving QYPO. Why only three pieces from the body? Cangjie caps a body at three codes, so we pick the head, second, and last shapes to stand in for all of 豦. Picture a hand 扌 laying hold of 豦 — that's taking possession — 扌卜心人, QYPO. You'll meet it in 根據 and 數據, as in "根據天氣去着衫" — dress according to the weather.
據.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「據」，讀做 geoi3，意思係佔據、佔有，亦都可以解做根基、依據。你望下呢個字，佢分成左右兩邊：左邊係提手旁「扌」，喺倉頡入面攞 Q，呢個就係字首。右邊係「豦」，作為字身，因為右邊筆畫多，我哋唔會逐粒拆晒，而係用「取頭、次、尾」嘅辦法，只揀三粒代表：頭係「卜」Y，次係「心」P，尾係「人」O，砌埋就係 QYPO。點解字身淨係取三粒？因為倉頡規定字身最多取三碼，所以要挑頭、二、尾三個位嚟代表成個「豦」。記住：一隻手「扌」按住「豦」，就係佔據——扌卜心人，QYPO。你可以講「根據」同「數據」，好似「根據天氣去着衫」噉。

攞.en: Today we learn 攞, read lo2, a very common word in Cantonese that means to take, to fetch, to grab, as in 攞嚟 or 攞走. Look at it: on the left is the 扌 hand radical, and on the right is the character 羅, so the whole thing pictures using your hand to take something. When we break it down, the left 扌 acts as the head and gives just one code, Q; the right side 羅 is the body, and since a body takes at most three codes we use the head-second-last method — head 田 is W, second 中 is L, and last 土 is G, giving us QWLG. Here's your memory hook: one hand (扌 Q) reaches into the field (田 W) and takes (中 L) a lump of earth (土 G) — picture the grabbing and the code sticks.
攞.zh: 今日我哋學「攞」呢個字，讀做 lo2，喺廣東話入面好常用，好似「攞嚟」、「攞走」咁，即係拎、取嘅意思。你望下佢，左邊係個「扌」（提手旁），右邊係個「羅」字，一睇就知係用手去攞嘢。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「扌」做字首，只取一碼 Q；右邊「羅」做字身，字身最多取三碼，所以用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法，取頭「田」係 W，取第二個「中」係 L，最後取尾「土」係 G，合埋就係 QWLG。記住呢個口訣：一隻手（扌 Q）去田（W）中（L）攞塊土（G），去攞嘢嘅畫面就記得晒喇。

支.zh: 今日我哋學「支」呢個字，讀音係 zi1，意思好豐富：可以解作支持、支援，又可以解作「一支筆」嘅量詞。你望吓佢嘅結構，上面係一個「十」字，下面係一個「又」字，一上一下清清楚楚咁疊住。用倉頡拆嘅時候，我哋照住由上到下嘅次序：上邊嘅「十」做字首，取碼 J；下邊嘅「又」做字身，取碼 E，所以全碼就係 JE。點解要咁樣分呢？因為上邊嘅「十」自然做咗字首，下邊剩低嘅「又」就做字身，一首一身各佔一格，乾淨俐落。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗住：「十」字撐喺上面，「又」手托喺下面，就好似有人支持你噉。

收.en: Today we're learning 收, read sau1, which means to gather, to collect, or to harvest — as in 收集 sau1 zaap6, to bring things together, or 收到 sau1 dou2, to receive. Look at the character: there's a cluster of strokes on the left and the 攵 component on the right. Cangjie splits it into a head and a body: the left side is the head, giving two codes — ㄑ is V and 丨 is L; the 攵 on the right is the body, also giving two codes — 人 is O and 乂 is K, so the full code is VLOK. As a memory hook, picture the left 'ㄑ丨' cupping the harvest and the right 'human 人 with a cross 乂' pulling it all in.
收.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「收」，讀作 sau1，意思係收集、聚攏，或者收成，好似「收集」sau1 zaap6 嘅意思就係將啲嘢聚埋一齊，而「收到」sau1 dou2 就係接收到。你望下呢個字，左邊係一組筆畫，右邊係個「攵」部。倉頡拆呢個字要分字首同字身：左邊做字首，取兩碼——ㄑ係 V、丨係 L；右邊個攵做字身，也取兩碼——人係 O、乂係 K，所以全碼係 VLOK。記法好簡單：左邊「ㄑ丨」把嘢圍埋，右邊「人乂」一敲，就係將收成收埋一齊喇。

改.en: Today's character is 改, read goi2, meaning to change, to alter, or to improve. Look at it: the left side is 己, and the right side is 攵, the 'tap/strike' piece — together they carry the sense of making an alteration. When you split it for coding, the left 己 becomes the head, and Cangjie doesn't take it whole but breaks it into 尸 (the S key) and 山 (the U key); the right 攵 becomes the body, broken into 人 (the O key) and 乂 (the K key). Each part contributes its own codes from its own side, so joined together you get 尸山人乂, which is SUOK. Here's your hook: the left 己 opens with 尸山, the right 攵 finishes with 人乂 — one strike and it's changed. Practise it with words like 改變 (goi2 bin3) and 改善 (goi2 sin6), or the sentence 我想改個名, 'I want to change the name.'
改.zh: 你今日學嘅字係「改」，讀 goi2，意思係改變、修改、改善。你望下佢：左邊係「己」，右邊係代表打嘅「攵」，合埋就係「作出改動」嘅意思。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「己」做字首，倉頡唔係取成個「己」，而係拆成「尸」（S 鍵）同「山」（U 鍵）兩件；右邊嘅「攵」做字身，拆成「人」（O 鍵）同「乂」（K 鍵）。字首同字身各自取自己嗰邊嘅碼，所以合埋就係尸山人乂，即係 SUOK。記住喇：左邊「己」開頭（尸山），右邊「攵」收尾（人乂），一改就成。你可以講「我想改個名」，或者用「改變」（goi2 bin3）同「改善」（goi2 sin6）呢啲詞去記。

放.en: Today we're learning 放, which reads fong3 and means to put, to release, to set free. The character splits into two parts: the 字首 on the left is 方, and the 字身 on the right is 攵. Rather than typing every stroke, 方 gives up just its head-tail: the head 亠 on the Y key and the tail 尸 on the S key; then 攵 does the same, offering its head 人 on the O key and its tail ナ on the K key. Put those four together and you get YSOK, exactly in that order. Think of it this way — 方 sets the book down first (亠, 尸), then 攵 gives it a gentle release (人, ナ), and you've put it wherever you like.
放.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「放」，讀作 fong3，意思係放低、釋放、放開。呢個字分做兩部分：左邊嘅字首係「方」，右邊嘅字身係「攵」。字首「方」唔係逐筆全取，而係取佢嘅頭尾兩碼——頭係「亠」（Y鍵），尾係「尸」（S鍵）；字身「攵」都係一樣，取頭尾——頭係「人」（O鍵），尾係「ナ」（K鍵）。所以四碼合埋就係 YSOK，你可以記住：「方」開頭放低本書（亠尸），「攵」跟手輕輕一按（人ナ），你想放喺邊就放喺邊。

政.en: Today's character is 政, read zing3, meaning government or political affairs. Look at how it's built from left and right: on the left sits 正, and on the right sits 攵. When Cangjie breaks it down, the 字首 (lead part) 正 gives only its head and tail, which are 一 (M) and 一 (M) — so you press M twice; then the 字身 (body part) 攵 also gives its head and tail, 人 (O) and 大 (K), forming MMOK. Why only head and tail on each side? Because in a left-right character each part gets a limited quota and can't be typed stroke by stroke, so each side contributes just two representative codes. Remember it this way: two 一 strokes (MM) prop up 正, then 攵's head-and-tail 人-大 (OK) finish the job — proper, upright government.
政.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「政」，讀作 zing3，即係政府、政治嘅意思。你望吓佢係左右兩邊拼埋——左邊係「正」，右邊係「攵」。倉頡拆呢個字嗰陣，字首「正」淨係取頭尾兩碼，就係頭「一」（M）同尾「一」（M），所以你連撳兩個 M；字身「攵」都係取頭尾，就係頭「人」（O）同尾「大」（K），砌埋成 MMOK。點解要咁樣淨取頭尾呢？因為左右結構嘅字，字首同字身各自都有配額限制，唔可以逐筆全取，於是每邊只挑頭同尾兩個代表碼。記住喇：兩個一（MM）撐住「正」，再一個「攵」嘅頭尾人大（OK），就係「政」——正正經經去做政治。

故.en: Today we're learning 故, read gu3, which means ancient or old, and can also mean a reason or cause; you'll see it in 故事 (gu3 si6, old practice) and the everyday 故仔 (gu2 zai2, a story). Look at the character and you'll notice it splits into two sides: on the left is 古, on the right is 攵. In Cangjie the left side becomes the head and the right side becomes the body, and each side gets coded on its own. The head 古 is a multi-stroke part, so it takes just its first and last pieces — 十 (J) first, 口 (R) last, giving JR — while the body 攵 likewise takes first and last, 人 (O) then 乂 (K), giving OK. Put them together and you have JROK; remember it as 十-口-人-乂, like an old story passed from mouth to mouth among people!
故.zh: 今日我哋學「故」呢個字，讀音係 gu3，意思係古老、舊時，又可以解「原因」，好似「故事」（gu3 si6）或者口語嘅「故仔」（gu2 zai2），即係一段故事咁。你望住個字，佢分成左右兩邊：左邊係「古」，右邊係「攵」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊做字首，右邊做字身，兩者都要分開取碼。字首「古」係一個由多筆組成嘅部件，所以取頭尾兩碼——頭係「十」（J），尾係「口」（R），就係 JR；字身「攵」都係取頭尾——頭係「人」（O），尾係「乂」（K），就係 OK。四碼合埋就係 JROK，你可以記住「十口人乂」，好似講「一段古仔由人口一個傳一個」咁去記！

效.en: Today we're learning 效, read haau6, meaning result, effect, or effectiveness. Take a look at its shape: the left side is 交, and the right side is 攵, the tapping-radical. This character breaks into a head and a body: the head on the left is 交, from which we take its first and last pieces — the top 亠 (Y) and the bottom 乂 (K), giving YK; the body on the right is 攵, and we likewise take its first and last pieces — 人 (O) and 乂 (K), giving OK. Why does it split this way? Because in a left-right character the head and body each take at most two codes, so 交 gives its first-last and 攵 gives its first-last, landing exactly on four codes: Y, K, O, K. Here's your memory hook — both parts are held together by their heads and tails, and both tails happen to be 乂 (K), so K appears twice in "YK-OK," giving it a nice rhythm. Try saying 呢隻藥好有效, and think of the words 有效 and 效果.
效.zh: 今日我哋學「效」呢個字，讀作 haau6，意思係效果、成效。你睇下佢個樣，左邊係「交」，右邊係「攵」（反文旁）。呢個字分做字首同字身兩部分：左邊嘅字首「交」，我哋取佢嘅頭尾兩碼，頭係「亠」（Y），尾係「乂」（K），所以係 YK；右邊嘅字身「攵」，同樣取頭尾，頭係「人」（O），尾係「乂」（K），得出 OK。合埋成個字就係 Y、K、O、K。點解係咁樣拆呢？因為左右結構嘅字，字首同字身各自都最多取兩碼，所以「交」取頭尾、「攵」都取頭尾，啱啱夠四碼。記憶竅門：兩個部件都係「頭尾夾住」，而且兩邊個尾都係「乂」（K），所以尾兩個字母 K 出咗兩次——「YK-OK」，讀落好似有節奏咁！你可以講「呢隻藥好有效」，或者諗下「有效」同「效果」呢兩個詞。

教.en: Today we learn 教, read gaau3, meaning to teach or a class, as in 教育 (gaau3 juk6, education) and 宗教 (zung1 gaau3, religion). Look at it: it divides cleanly left and right, the left side being the 字首 and the right 攵 being the 字身. From the left 字首 we take head and tail — the head 十 (J) and the tail 木 (D); from the right 字身 we again take head and tail — the head 人 (O) and the tail 乂 (K), so the full code is JDOK. Why here? Because for a left-right character Cangjie treats one side as head-part and the other as body-part, and each side gives just its head and tail rather than everything. Remember it as left 十木, right 人乂 — the teacher teaches me to read, JDOK.
教.zh: 今日我哋學「教」呢個字，讀 gaau3，即係教導、上堂嘅意思，好似「教育」（gaau3 juk6）同「宗教」（zung1 gaau3）咁。你望下佢，左右兩邊分得好清楚：左邊係字首，右邊個「攵」係字身。左邊字首，我哋取頭同尾——頭係「十」（J），尾係「木」（D）；右邊字身都係取頭同尾——頭係「人」（O），尾係「乂」（K），所以成個碼砌埋就係 JDOK。點解要咁分？因為倉頡對左右結構嘅字，係一邊當字首、一邊當字身，各自都係頭尾兩碼咁取，唔會亂咁攞。記住喇：左邊「十木」，右邊「人乂」，老師教我讀書，就係 JDOK。

敦.en: Today's character is 敦, which reads deon1, the same syllable you meet in Hong Kong place names like 彌敦道 (Nathan Road) and 佐敦 (Jordan); on its own it means honest, sincere, and warmly esteeming. Look at the shape: it's built from two side-by-side halves, with 享 on the left and 攵 on the right. When Cangjie splits it, the head 享 gives only its first and last codes, Y and D, so you type Y then D; the body 攵 likewise gives its first and last, O and K, so you add O then K, making the full code YDOK. As a memory hook, picture the name 佐敦: the left 享 hands you its first-last YD, the right 攵 hands you its first-last OK, and reading left to right keeps the whole thing in order.
敦.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「敦」，讀音同「敦」（deon1）一樣，喺「彌敦道」同「佐敦」呢啲香港地名度成日見到，本身意思係敦厚、誠懇。你望下呢個字，佢係左右兩邊夾埋嘅結構——左邊係「享」，右邊係「攵」。倉頡拆字嗰陣，字首「享」淨係取頭尾兩碼，即係頭嘅 Y 同尾嘅 D，所以打 Y、D；字身「攵」都係取頭尾，頭係 O、尾係 K，所以再打 O、K，合埋就係 YDOK。要記住呢個字，你可以諗住「佐敦」嘅『敦』——左邊個『享』取頭尾 YD，右邊個『攵』取頭尾 OK，順住左右嚟就記得晒喇。

整.en: Today we learn 整, read zing2, which means orderly, neat, or tidy, and can also mean whole or entire. Notice that 整 is a top-and-bottom character: the top part is 敕 and the bottom part is 正. When Cangjie breaks this apart, the top 敕 acts as the head of the character, so we take only its first and last shapes, giving 木 (D) and 大 (K); then the bottom 正 is the body, so we take head-second-tail, giving 一 (M), 卜 (Y), and 一 (M) — the full code being DKMYM. The reason the top yields just two codes is that as the head it gets a smaller quota, while the body below is allowed up to three codes to spell out the rest of the character. Remember it as 木 and 大 stacked on top, with 一 卜 一 tidily lined up below — everything neatly in its place, just like when you 整咗個蛋糕, you made a whole cake.
整.zh: 今日我哋學「整」呢個字，讀音係 zing2，意思係整齊、整潔，又或者係「整個」嘅意思，即係完整、全部。你留意到「整」係一個上下結構嘅字：上面係「敕」，下面係「正」。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，因為個字係分開兩大部分，上面嗰個字首「敕」我哋取頭同尾，即係木（D）同大（K）；下面嗰個字身「正」就取頭、二、尾三碼，即係一（M）、卜（Y）、一（M），所以全碼就係 DKMYM。點解上面淨係取兩碼呢？因為佢係字首，一般只取頭尾，而下面做字身就可以取到三碼，先至夠拼出成個字。記住呢個口訣：木大喺上、一卜一喺下，你整齊咁砌返出嚟就係「整」，好似你整咗個蛋糕（我整咗個蛋糕）咁完整。

數.en: Today we learn 數, read sou3, whose core meaning is "number" or "figure" — the 數 in 數據, "data." It can also read sou2 meaning "to count," as in our sentence "I can count to ten." This is a left-right character: 婁 on the left and 攵 on the right, and its Cangjie code is four keys, LVOK. The left 婁 acts as the 字首, and a 字首 takes only its first and last codes, so from 婁's own full code LWLV we keep the first L (口) and the last V (女), giving us L, V. The right 攵 is the 字身, which also takes head and tail; since 攵's own code is just OK, its first and last are simply O (人) and K, completing all four. Remember it this way: 婁 hugging 攵 — pluck the head and tail L, V from the left, carry O, K straight over from the right, and count off exactly four.
數.zh: 今日我哋學「數」呢個字，佢讀 sou3，最基本嘅意思就係「數目、數字」，好似「數據」嘅「數」咁，亦都可以讀 sou2 解「數（一數）」，就好似例句「我識數到十。」咁樣。呢個字係左右結構，左邊係「婁」，右邊係「攵」，倉頡碼一共四鍵：LVOK。左邊個「婁」做字首，字首只取頭尾兩碼，所以我哋喺「婁」自己嘅碼 LWLV 入面，攞第一個 L（口）同最後一個 V（女），得出 L、V。右邊個「攵」做字身，字身同樣取頭尾，「攵」自己嘅碼係 OK，一頭一尾就係 O（人）同 K，啱啱好齊晒。你可以咁記：一個「婁」抱住個「攵」，左邊淨係摘頭尾 L、V，右邊 O、K 直接搬過嚟，數一數啱啱四碼。

文.en: Today we learn 文, read man4, meaning literature, culture, and writing itself. Look at its shape: on top there's a dot over a horizontal line, which is the piece 亠 — press Y for it; underneath is a crossing stroke, a slash and a sweep forming 乂 — press K for that. So 文 breaks into just two codes, the top 亠 (Y) and the bottom 乂 (K), giving you YK, clean and short with nothing extra. Why only these two pieces? Reading top to bottom, the character is plainly two parts stacked together, so there's no need to split it any further. Remember it like this: a little cap on top (亠 Y) and a cross below (乂 K) — YK spells 文, as in 英文 (jing1 man2, English) or 文化 (man4 faa3, culture), or in the sentence 我鍾意學中文, I like learning Chinese.
文.zh: 今日我哋學「文」呢個字，佢讀 man4，係「文學」、「文化」、「寫文」嘅意思，講嘅就係文字同文化本身。你留意佢個樣：上面一點加一橫，就係「亠」呢個部件，喺鍵盤上面撳 Y；下面交叉嗰一撇一捺，就係「乂」，撳 K。所以「文」淨係拆做兩碼——上面嘅亠（Y）同下面嘅乂（K），合埋就係 YK，好簡單，冇多餘嘢。點解就咁兩橛？因為由上到下睇，個字本身就係清清楚楚兩件嘢疊起，唔使再拆多。記住：頭頂一頂帽仔（亠 Y），下面一個交叉（乂 K），YK 就係「文」。你可以講「英文」jing1 man2、「文化」man4 faa3，又或者好似「我鍾意學中文」咁樣用佢。

料.en: Today's character is 料, read liu2 or liu6, meaning to consider or conjecture, and also materials or ingredients — you meet it in everyday words like 資料 (data, information) and 料理 (to handle, or cuisine). Look at the shape: on the left sits 米, and on the right sits 斗, a clean left-right structure. The left 米 acts as the 字首, so Cangjie takes its first and last pieces — 火 F to open and 木 D to close; the right 斗 is the 字身, and it too gives first and last — 卜 Y and 十 J. Read straight across in order, that's 火 F, 木 D, 卜 Y, 十 J, giving you FDYJ. To remember it, picture a bowl of ingredients: 米 rice on the left, 斗 measure on the right — the raw materials, measured out in exactly four keys.
料.zh: 今日學嘅字係「料」，讀作 liu2 或者 liu6，可以解「估計、料想」，又可以解「材料、原料」，好似「資料」同「料理」呢啲詞咁常見。你望下個字，左邊係「米」，右邊係「斗」，係一個清清楚楚嘅左右結構。左邊「米」做字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼——起筆嘅火 F，同收尾嘅木 D；右邊「斗」做字身，同樣取頭尾——卜 Y 同十 J，所以成個字順住次序打出嚟就係火 F、木 D、卜 Y、十 J，即係 FDYJ。記住呢個字嘅時候，你就諗成一碗有米又有斗嘅材料——左米右斗，剛好四碼，煮嘢食嘅材料就係咁樣砌返出嚟嘅。

斯.en: Today we learn 斯, read si1, which can mean "this" or "thus," and it also shows up in transliterated foreign names — for example 俄羅斯 (ngo4 lo4 si1) means Russia. The character has 其 on the left and 斤 on the right, so Cangjie splits it into a head part and a body part. The head is 其 on the left, and because it's a busy shape you take its first and last pieces only — the 廿 (T) at the top and the 八 (C) at the bottom. The body is 斤 on the right, and there you take head, second, and tail: 竹 (H), 一 (M), and 中 (L), giving you TCHML altogether. Remember it as 其 keeping just its ends 廿八, and 斤 spelling out 竹一中 — as neat and orderly as someone who, in the example, does everything 斯文, gently and politely.
斯.zh: 今日我哋學「斯」呢個字，讀音係 si1，佢可以解「呢個、如此」，亦都係好多外文名嘅譯音字，好似「俄羅斯」（ngo4 lo4 si1）就係俄國嘅意思。呢個字左邊係「其」，右邊係「斤」，倉頡拆碼要分字首同字身兩部分。字首係左邊嘅「其」，因為佢筆畫多過兩碼，所以用頭尾法，取頭嘅廿（T）同尾嘅八（C）；字身係右邊嘅「斤」，取頭嘅竹（H）、第二嘅一（M）、同埋尾嘅中（L），合埋就係 TCHML。記住：其字剩頭尾「廿八」，斤字「竹一中」，你就唔會亂——就好似佢做嘢咁「斯文」，一步步整齊咁排好。

新.en: Today we learn 新, read san1, meaning new, recent, or fresh — like the 新 in "a new shirt." Look at it: it splits left and right, with 親 on the left and 斤 on the right. The left 親 is the 字首, and a 字首 takes only head and tail — here the head 亠 (Y) and the tail 木 (D). The right 斤 is the 字身, and a 字身 may take head, second, and tail — so we get 竹 (H), 一 (M), and 中 (L), giving the full code YDHML. Remember it this way: what's close and親 to you brings a fresh 斤 start — that's why you see 新 in Hong Kong names like 新界 and 新蒲崗.
新.zh: 我哋今日學「新」呢個字，讀 san1，意思係新、最近、新鮮，好似「新衫」個「新」咁。你望下佢，左右兩邊：左邊係「親」，右邊係「斤」。左邊「親」係字首，字首取頭尾兩碼，頭係「亠」（Y），尾係「木」（D）；右邊「斤」係字身，字身可以取頭、次、尾三碼，所以攞到「竹」（H）、「一」（M）同「中」（L）。合埋就係 YDHML。你可以記住：親近有新意，一個新字由「親」同「斤」拼成，就好似「新界」、「新蒲崗」呢啲香港地方名咁熟口熟面。

方.en: Wait, let me redo this properly.
方.zh: 我哋今日學嘅係「方」字，讀做 fong1，佢嘅意思係四四方方嘅形狀，一個正方形或者長方形，又可以解做地方、地區，好似「地方」（dei6 fong1）同「方法」（fong1 faat3）咁。你望住個字，佢係一個整體字，唔會拆開頭尾兩截，而係一路順住寫落去、順住拆碼。所以我哋由上到下取三個部分：最頭係「亠」，撳 Y；跟住係中間嗰個「竹」形，撳 H；最尾包住嘅係「尸」，撳 S，合埋就係 YHS。記住一句：亠頭、竹身、尸尾，由上寫到落嚟，「方」字就係 Y、H、S。

於.en: Today we learn 於, read "jyu1", meaning "in, at, on" — you'll meet it constantly in writing, in words like 由於 (due to) and 關於 (concerning). Look at it: on the left is the 方 radical, and on the right sits a separate body. Cangjie has a firm quota — any 字首 or 字身 gives at most its head and tail — so we don't spell 方 stroke by stroke; we take just its head 卜 (Y) and its tail 尸 (S). Then the right-hand body follows the same head-tail rule, giving 人 (O) as head and 卜 (Y) as tail, so the whole code is YSOY. Remember it as "方 gives 卜尸, the right gives 人卜" — head and tail on each side, and 於 is built.
於.zh: 今日我哋學「於」呢個字，讀「jyu1」，係「喺、在」嘅意思，好似「由於」、「關於」咁樣用，好多書面語都見到佢。你望下佢，左邊係「方」字旁，右邊係另一嚿。倉頡有個規矩：一個字首或者字身，最多只可以取頭同尾兩碼，所以左邊嘅「方」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，淨係取頭尾兩碼——頭係卜（Y），尾係尸（S）；跟住右邊嘅字身都係取頭尾，頭係人（O），尾係卜（Y），合埋就係 YSOY。記住個口訣：「方字取卜尸，右邊取人卜」，一頭一尾，兩邊都齊，「於」就砌好喇。

施.en: Today we learn 施, read si1, meaning to grant, to give, or to carry out — you see it in 實施 sat6 si1 (to implement) and 設施 cit3 si1 (facilities). The character splits into two sides: the left is the 方 prefix, and the right is the 也 body. A prefix in Cangjie takes at most two codes, so from the left we take only first and last — 卜 (Y) at the head and 尸 (S) at the tail. The body can take more, up to three codes, so from the right we take first, second, and last — 人 (O), then 匕 (P), then 木 (D). Put them together and you get YSOPD; remember it as left gives 卜尸, right gives 人匕木, and the whole thing falls right into place.
施.zh: 今日我哋學「施」呢個字，讀作 si1，意思係施予、給予、施行，好似「實施」sat6 si1（實行、推行）同「設施」cit3 si1（設備）咁樣。呢個字分兩邊嚟拆：左邊係「方」字首，右邊係「也」字身。左邊嗰個字首唔會逐筆拆晒，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，所以只取頭尾兩件——頭係「卜」（Y），尾係「尸」（S）。右邊嘅字身可以取多啲，最多三碼，所以取頭、二、尾三件——頭係「人」（O），第二件係「匕」（P），尾係「木」（D）。連埋一齊就係 YSOPD。記住呢個口訣：左邊方字首得頭尾卜尸，右邊也字身得頭二尾人匕木，你就好易記得住喇。

旅.en: Today we learn 旅, read leoi5 — the 旅 of 旅行 and 旅遊, meaning a trip or a journey, the idea of setting off somewhere far. Look at it: the left side is the 方 radical, and the right side is a cluster of loose strokes, almost like someone carrying luggage on their back. We split it into a head and a body: the head is the left-side 方, and Cangjie takes its first and last codes, giving 卜 (Y) and 尸 (S); the body is the right-hand cluster, from which we take head, second, and tail — 人 (O), 竹 (H), and 女 (V). That builds the full code YSOHV, and if you remember the rule that a head gives at most two codes while a body gives head-second-tail, you won't get lost. Memory hook: 方 leads you out the door, and three little travelers follow behind to make the journey.
旅.zh: 今日我哋學「旅」字，讀作 leoi5，即係旅行、旅遊嘅「旅」，講嘅係出門去遠方嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係「方」字部，右邊係一堆散開嘅筆畫，睇落好似有人揹住行李咁。呢個字要拆做字首同字身兩橛：字首係左邊嘅「方」，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，即係「卜」（Y）同「尸」（S）；字身係右邊嗰一堆，取頭、二、尾三碼，順住寫就係「人」（O）、「竹」（H）、「女」（V）。所以成個碼就係 YSOHV，記住字首最多兩碼、字身取頭二尾嘅規矩，就唔會亂。可以咁記：「方」字帶你上路，後面跟住三個人一齊去旅行。

日.en: Today we're learning 日, read "jat6", which means the sun, and by extension a day or the daytime. Look at its shape: a neat rectangular frame with one horizontal stroke through the middle, like the sun sitting up in the sky. In Cangjie, 日 is itself one of the radical keys, and it lives on the A key, so you don't break it apart at all — you just press A once and the whole character comes out, a single code. Because it's one of the most basic building blocks, you'll see it inside many other characters, so it's worth locking in early. Remember it this way: one A, one sun — and words like 今日 (today) and 成日 (always) all start from this same A.
日.zh: 我哋今日學嘅係「日」字，讀「jat6」，即係太陽，又可以解一日、白天。你睇下佢個樣：一個四四方方嘅框，中間有一橫，好似太陽掛喺天上咁。喺倉頡入面，「日」本身就係一個獨立嘅字母，佢排喺鍵盤嘅 A 掣度，所以你唔使拆佢，直接㩒一個 A 就打得出成個字，得一碼咁簡單。因為佢係最基本嘅字根之一，好多字都會用到佢做部件，所以你要記實佢。記住：一個 A，一個太陽，「今日」、「成日」都係用呢個 A 開頭。

早.zh: 今日我哋學個「早」字，讀 zou2，意思係「早」、「清晨」，好似「朝早」呢個詞噉樣。你望吓佢個樣：上面係一個四四方方嘅「日」，下面托住一個「十」字。喺倉頡入面，我哋由上到下、由頭到尾噉睇：先取字首「日」，佢喺 A 鍵；再取字身「十」，佢喺 J 鍵，所以個碼就係 AJ。點解會噉樣拆？因為「日」係字首、「十」係字身，簡簡單單兩部分，唔使諗咁多。記住個口訣：太陽（日）一出，再插一「十」，就係一朝清「早」喇！

旺.en: Look at this character: 旺, read "wong6," meaning to prosper, to flourish, business booming. Notice it splits into two sides — the left is 日 and the right is 王. The left 日 is simple; it's the head, and since a head takes just one code, its key is A. The right 王 is the body, and when Cangjie breaks down a body made of one connected part, it takes head and tail — the head of 王 is the horizontal stroke 一, keyed M, and its tail is 土, keyed G. Put together the whole thing is A, M, G, spelled out as AMG. Here's your hook: the sun (日) shining on the king (王) makes business boom — AMG.
旺.zh: 睇下呢個字：旺，讀「wong6」，意思係興旺、旺盛、生意好。你留意到佢分做兩邊：左邊係個「日」，右邊係「王」。左邊個「日」好簡單，佢就係字首，一個字取佢，個鍵係 A。右邊個「王」係字身，倉頡拆字身嘅時候，如果係一個獨立部件，就取頭同尾兩碼——「王」嘅頭係一橫「一」，個鍵係 M；佢嘅尾係「土」，個鍵係 G。所以成個字砌埋就係 A、M、G，讀出嚟就係 AMG。記住個口訣：日光照住個王，就生意興旺，AMG。

昌.en: Today we learn 昌, read coeng1, meaning the bright light of the sun, and by extension good, proper, and flourishing — as in 興昌, prosperity. Take a good look at its shape: it's simply two 日 characters stacked, one sitting on top and one below. This is a top-bottom character, so Cangjie splits it that way: the upper 日 is the head, coded A, and the lower 日 is the body, also coded A, giving you the full code A, A (AA). Because each half is a single clean piece, one code each fills the quota neatly, with no need for any extra or final key. Remember it like this: two suns stacked, one above the other — AA — and business will be booming!
昌.zh: 今日我哋學「昌」字，讀作 coeng1，意思係陽光燦爛，引申為好、正當、興旺，好似「興昌」咁樣。你望一望佢個樣，其實就係兩個「日」字疊埋一齊，一個喺上面、一個喺下面。呢個係上下結構嘅字，倉頡拆碼嘅時候，上面嘅「日」係字首，取碼 A；下面嘅「日」係字身，同樣取碼 A，所以全碼就係 A、A（AA）。因為上下各得一件，一件一碼，剛啱夠位，唔使再取簡碼或者尾碼。記住喇：兩個太陽疊起，一上一下，AA 就係「昌」，好興旺！

明.en: Today's character is 明, read ming4, meaning bright, light, or clear, as in 明白 (to understand) and 證明 (proof). Take a look at its shape: it's a classic left-right character, with 日 (the sun) on the left and 月 (the moon) on the right — put the two brightest things in the sky side by side and of course you get brightness. Because it splits neatly into a left part and a right part, Cangjie simply reads it left to right: 日 gives you A, and 月 gives you B, so the whole code is just AB. Picture the sun and moon standing shoulder to shoulder — A then B — and 明 will always shine clear in your memory.
明.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「明」，讀做 ming4，意思係光亮、清楚，好似「明白」、「證明」咁用。你望吓呢個字，佢係一個典型嘅左右兩體字：左邊係「日」，右邊係「月」，太陽同月亮擺埋一齊，兩樣最光嘅嘢加起嚟，自然就係「明亮」啦。因為佢係左右分開嘅結構，倉頡就順住由左至右嘅次序拆：左邊嘅「日」取 A，右邊嘅「月」取 B，所以成個字嘅碼就係 AB。記住呢個畫面就得喇——日頭同月光並排，A 配 B，一亮就明。

易.en: Today we learn 易, a character with two readings, ji6 and jik6, meaning either "to change" or "easy." Look at its shape: the top is 日, the sun, and the bottom is 勿. When we split it, the head is 日, and a head only needs one code here—日=A. Then we take the body 勿, and since a Cangjie body caps out at three codes using the "first, second, last" rule, we pull 心=P, 竹=H, and the final 竹=H from 勿, giving us APHH altogether. Remember it this way: under the sun (日), things change easily—so 易 is both "change" and "easy," and it's easy to recall!
易.zh: 今日我哋學「易」呢個字，佢有兩個讀音，一個係 ji6，一個係 jik6，可以解作「改變」，又可以解作「容易」。你望下佢個樣，上面係一個「日」字，下面係一個「勿」字。拆碼嘅時候，字首係「日」，我哋取佢一個碼——日=A。跟住落嚟就係字身「勿」，倉頡取碼有個「頭二尾一」嘅規矩，字身最多取三個碼，所以我哋喺「勿」度取頭一二同尾——分別係心=P、竹=H、同埋尾嘅竹=H，砌埋就係 APHH。記住呢個字：太陽（日）之下嘅嘢好易變，所以「易」既係變，又係易，好易記！

星.en: Today we learn 星, read sing1 or seng1, meaning a star, a planet, or any point of light in the sky. Look at the character and you'll see it splits top and bottom: on top is 日, and below it is 生. The top 日 is the head, so you type 日=A. The bottom 生 is the body, and instead of spelling out every stroke we take its head, second, and tail parts — the head 竹=H, the second piece 手=Q, and the tail 一=M — giving you AHQM. Why only three parts from the body? Because a body takes at most its head, next, and tail pieces, so 生 hands us H, Q, and M. To remember it, picture a 日 sun above, giving birth (生) to a bright dot of light — sun-born light is a star.
星.zh: 我哋今日學「星」字，讀作 sing1 或者 seng1，意思係天上嘅星星、行星，任何一點發光嘅光點都可以叫做星。你望住個字，佢係上下兩截：上面係「日」，下面係「生」。上面嘅「日」擺喺字首，取「日」＝A；下面嘅「生」係字身，我哋唔會逐筆逐筆咁拆，而係取佢嘅頭、二、尾三個碼——頭係「竹」＝H，第二個係「手」＝Q，尾係「一」＝M，合埋就係 AHQM。點解字身淨係取三個碼呢？因為字身最多都係取頭、次、尾三部分，所以「生」就取 H、Q、M 三粒。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成一個「日」頭光光，落面生出一粒星，日生一星，就係 星。

是.en: Today we learn 是, read si6, meaning "yes, correct, to be," and it can also work as a demonstrative like "this" or "that." Look at its shape: on top sits 日, and below it sits 疋. In Cangjie the top 日 is taken as the head, giving A. The lower 疋 is the body, and since a body takes at most three codes, we use the first-second-last rule: grab the leading 一 (M), then the middle 卜 (Y), then the final 人 (O), which strings together as AMYO. Here is your memory hook: sun on top, then one-divination-person below, and 是 is complete. Try typing 於是 and 是但 to make it stick.
是.zh: 今日我哋學「是」，讀作 si6，意思係「係、對、正確」，亦都可以做指示代詞，好似「這、那」咁。你望下佢嘅結構：上面係一個「日」字，下面係一個「疋」字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，上面嘅「日」做字首，取碼 A。下面嘅「疋」係字身，字身最多取三碼，所以我哋用「頭、二、尾」嘅法則：先取最頭嘅「一」M，再取中間嘅「卜」Y，最後取尾嘅「人」O，合埋就係 AMYO。記住一句：日頭一卜人，「是」就砌好晒喇。你可以試下打「於是」同「是但」，加深印象。

時.en: Today we're learning 時, read si4, meaning time, season, an era or a period. Take a look at it: on the left sits a 日 (sun), and on the right sits 寺 (temple), and together they make 時. In Cangjie we first take the head 日, whose key is A, and then we split the body 寺; because 寺 is a busy body piece we can't type every stroke, so by the rule we take head, second, and last — that gives us 土 (G), then 木 (D), then 戈 (I), spelling GDI. Put it all together and the full code is AGDI. You use this character every day in words like 時候 (a moment, a period) and 時間 (time), as in "Now is dinner time." Here's your hook: sun on the left, temple on the right telling the time — A then GDI makes 時.
時.zh: 今日我哋學「時」呢個字，讀 si4，即係時間、時候、年代嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係一個「日」，右邊係一個「寺」，兩邊夾埋就係「時」。喺倉頡入面，我哋先取字首「日」，佢嘅鍵係 A；跟住就要拆右邊嘅字身「寺」，因為佢係一個複雜嘅字身，唔可以取齊晒每一筆，所以按規矩取「頭、二、尾」——頭係「土」G，接住「木」D，最尾係「戈」I，砌埋就係 GDI。合埋成個字就係 AGDI 呢四個鍵。你平時講「時候」、「時間」都用呢個字，好似「依家係食飯時間」咁。記住呢句：日頭之下，寺廟報時（土木戈），A—GDI 就係「時」。

晒.en: Today we learn 晒, read saai3, meaning to dry in the sun or expose something to sunlight; in Cantonese it's also constantly used to mean "all, completely," as in 返晒 or 多謝晒 (thank you very much). Look at the character: on the left is 日, the sun, and on the right is 西. When you break it into codes, you first take the left piece 日, which sits on the A key. Then comes the body 西, and here's the rule — a body takes at most three codes, so you take its head, middle, and tail: 一 on the M key, 金 on the C key, and 田 on the W key, giving you AMCW. Here's your memory hook: the sun (日) is beating down on the west (西) side — when the sun leans west it shines its hottest, so you'll remember 晒 saai3.
晒.zh: 今日我哋學「晒」，讀 saai3，意思係曬太陽、放喺陽光下面晾乾嘅意思，喺廣東話入面仲成日用嚟表示「全部、晒晒」，好似「返晒」、「多謝晒」噉樣。你睇睇個字，左邊係一個「日」，右邊係一個「西」字。拆碼嘅時候，先取字首「日」，佢喺 A 鍵；跟住輪到字身「西」，倉頡有個規矩，字身最多取三碼，於是就取佢嘅頭、身、尾三部分——頭係「一」喺 M 鍵，中間當做「金」喺 C 鍵，尾係「田」喺 W 鍵。所以成個字砌埋一齊就係 AMCW。記住個小貼士：太陽（日）曬住個「西」邊，日頭西斜嘅時候最曬，噉就記得晒 saai3 喇。

晚.en: Today we learn 晚, read maan5, meaning night or evening — the time after the sky turns dark, as in 夜晚 (night) and 今晚 (tonight). Look at how it's built: on the left sits a 日, and on the right sits 免, two pieces standing side by side. When we take the code, the head is easy — it's that left-hand 日, which lives on the A key. The right-hand 免 becomes the body, and here Cangjie has a rule: a body takes at most three codes, so instead of spelling out every stroke we grab its first, middle and last pieces — the first is 弓 N, the middle is a single stroke 一 A, and the last is the 儿 at the bottom, taken here as 山 U. Put it together and you get ANAU; just remember one 日 to open, then 免 read head-middle-tail in three steps, and 晚 is done.
晚.zh: 我哋今日學「晚」呢個字，讀做 maan5，就係夜晚、天黑之後嘅時間，好似「夜晚」同「今晚」噉樣。你望下佢嘅結構，左邊係一個「日」，右邊係「免」字，左右並排砌成一個字。拆碼嗰陣，字首好簡單，就係左邊個「日」，佢喺鍵盤上面係 A。到咗右邊個「免」做字身，倉頡有個規矩：一個字身最多拆三碼，所以我哋唔會逐筆逐筆拆晒，而係取佢嘅頭、二、同尾三個部分——頭係「弓」N，中間係一橫「一」A，最尾係下面隻「儿」，佢喺呢度當「山」U嚟拆。噉樣砌埋一齊就係 ANAU，你記住：一個「日」開頭，跟住「免」字頭中尾三步，晚就砌好喇。「今晚食乜嘢呀？」

普.en: Today we're learning 普, read pou2, meaning universal, general, or widespread — you meet it in words like 普通 (pou2 tung1, ordinary or common) and 普遍 (pou2 pin3, widespread and general). Look at its shape: it stacks in two layers, with the 並 form sitting on top and a 日 resting underneath. In Cangjie the top part takes at most two codes, so the 並 across the top breaks into 廿 (the T key) plus 八 (the C key), giving you TC; then the bottom 日 stands on its own as one piece, coded A, so the whole character comes out as TCA. Here's your memory hook: the top 並 hands you TC, the bottom 日 hands you A, and together they build 普.
普.zh: 今日我哋學「普」呢個字，讀音係 pou2，意思係「普遍、廣泛、通行」，好似「普通」（pou2 tung1，即係平平無奇、大眾化）同埋「普遍」（pou2 pin3，即係到處都係）咁樣用。你望下佢個樣，上下兩層咁疊住：上邊係「並」字形，下邊坐住一個「日」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，上邊一份最多取兩碼，所以「並」呢一橫排嘅結構就拆做「廿」（T鍵）加「八」（C鍵），合埋就係 TC；跟住落到下邊，「日」係一個獨立部件，取字碼 A，於是全個字砌成 TCA。記住呢個口訣：上面「並」畀你 TC，下面「日」畀你 A，加埋就係「普」。

景.en: Today we learn 景, read ging2, meaning scenery or a view, and also conditions or circumstances. Look at how it's built: on top sits 日 (the sun), and underneath is the character 京, together painting a scene lit by the sun. When you split it, the top 日 is the 字首 and takes just one code, A; the bottom 京 is the 字身, and instead of typing every stroke you take its head and tail — the 亠 (Y) up top, plus the 口 (R) and 火 (F) below — giving you the full code AYRF. The reason the 字身 comes out this way is the head-and-tail quota: 京 gets condensed into three representative codes rather than the whole thing. Remember it as: sun on top gives A, then the 京 body hands you 亠, 口, 火 — and you've got the 景 in 背景 and 美景.
景.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「景」，讀作 ging2，解作風景、景色，又可以指景況、情形。你睇下佢嘅結構：上面係一個「日」，下面係一個「京」字，合埋就係「日」照住嘅景象。拆碼嗰陣，上面嘅「日」係字首，只取一碼，就係 A；下面嘅「京」係字身，我哋唔會逐筆全取，而係取頭同尾，即係頭嗰個「亠」（Y），加埋下面嘅「口」（R）同「火」（F），所以成個字碼就係 AYRF。點解字身係咁樣取？因為字身要遵守「頭二尾」嘅取碼規則，將「京」濃縮成三個代表碼。記住個口訣：日頭一碼，京身取亠口火，你就打得出「背景」同「美景」嘅「景」喇。

更.en: Today's character is 更, read gang3 or gaang1, meaning "more, still further" — as in "today is even colder than yesterday," it stacks one degree on top of another. If you look at the whole shape, you'll see it doesn't break cleanly into a head part and a body part, so we treat it as a whole-form character (整體字) and simply read its pieces in order from top to inside to bottom. The whole-form rule takes four codes — head, second, third, tail — and here that gives you the top stroke 一 as M, then 中 as L, then the 田 tucked inside as W, and finally the 大 closing the bottom as K, spelling MLWK. The reason there are exactly these four is that whole-form characters ignore the head/body quotas and just walk the shape from first to last. Remember it as M-starts-the-line, L-runs-through-the-middle, W-hides-the-field, K-catches-the-bottom: MLWK.
更.zh: 我哋今日學嘅係「更」字，讀 gang3 或者 gaang1，意思係「更加、進一步」，好似「今日比琴日更凍」咁樣，用嚟表示「多啲、深一層」。你望吓成個字，其實好難乾淨俐落咁劈開字首字身，所以我哋當佢係一個整體字，唔硬性分頭同身，而係由外到內、由頭到尾順住取碼。整體字嘅取碼方法係「頭、二、三、尾」四碼，喺「更」度就係：最頂嗰橫「一」係 M，跟住中間嗰豎連住嘅「中」係 L，再入面嘅「田」係 W，最後包住底嘅「大」係 K，合埋就係 MLWK。點解係呢四粒？因為整體字唔理字首字身嘅限額，就係順住字形攞頭、第二、第三同最尾嘅碼。記住個口訣：一橫（M）起、中（L）接、田（W）藏、大（K）收，MLWK 四步就搞掂。

書.en: Today we learn 書, read syu1, meaning a book, a letter, or a written document. Look at it: the strokes stack tightly from top to bottom, so there's no clean place to split a head from a body — that makes it a whole-character (整體字). For a whole-character we don't divide into 字首 and 字身; instead we take head, second, and tail: first the top piece ⺕ (L), then the next piece 土 (G), and finally the bottom piece 日 (A), skipping whatever sits in the middle, giving us LGA. Think of it like a thick stack of books — you grab the top and the bottom and let the middle go: ⺕L, 土G, 日A. Next time you say "我鍾意睇書" (I like reading books), that book is simply LGA.
書.zh: 今日我哋學「書」呢個字，讀作 syu1，即係書本、書信、文件嘅意思。你望下佢，成個字由上到下疊得密密實實，好難清楚咁切開頭同身，所以佢係一個「整體字」。遇到整體字，我哋唔分字首字身，而係跟「頭、二、三、尾」嘅方法取碼：先攞最頂嗰筆⺕（L），再攞第二嚿土（G），最後攞埋尾嗰嚿日（A），中間嗰啲就直接跳過，所以最終碼就係 LGA。你可以記住：書堆到成疊，我哋淨係捉頭捉尾——⺕L、土G、日A。你平時話「我鍾意睇書」，打嘅就係呢個 LGA。

曾.en: Today we learn 曾, a character that means "already" or "formerly" and works as a marker of the past; it reads "cang4", and in names it can read "zang1", as in 曾蔭權, Sir Donald Tsang. Look carefully at how it stacks up: at the very top sits the shape 八, typed with C; in the middle there is 田, typed with W; and at the bottom rests 日, typed with A. You might wonder why we skip the strokes in the middle — that is because 曾 is a whole-character (整體字), a shape treated as one connected block, and for such characters Cangjie has a special rule: take the head, take the second, take the tail, and simply skip the middle. That gives us the code CWA, so remember it top to bottom: head 八 C, second 田 W, tail 日 A, jump over the middle, and you have written the 曾 of 曾經.
曾.zh: 今日我哋學「曾」呢個字，佢有「曾經」、「以前」嘅意思，係表示過去嘅一個記號，讀「cang4」，喺人名度亦可以讀「zang1」，好似「曾蔭權」噉。你細心望吓佢嘅結構：最頂係「八」字形，喺鍵盤上打C；跟住中間有個「田」，打W；最底就係「日」字，打A。你可能會問，中間明明仲有筆畫，點解淨係揀呢三橛呢？因為「曾」係一個成個連埋一齊嘅整體字，倉頡對呢種字有特別規矩：取頭、取次、取尾，中間嗰段就跳過唔理，所以碼就係C、W、A。記住喇：由頭到尾，八C田W日A，中間跳過，你就打得出「曾經」個「曾」喇。

最.en: Today we learn 最, read zeoi3, meaning "most" or "to the greatest degree" — you'll meet it in words like 最好 (best) and 最後 (final, in the end). Look at the character: on top sits 曰, and below sits 取, which itself breaks into 尸, then 十, then 又. In Cangjie we first take the 字首 (the head) 曰, coded A; then we handle the 字身 (the body) 取, and because a body of several pieces is split by head-second-tail, we take its head 尸 as S, its second piece 十 as J, and its tail 又 as E, giving us ASJE. Here's your memory hook: 曰 caps 取 — A leads, then 尸-十-又 close it out (S-J-E), spelling the "most" in 我最鍾意你.
最.zh: 今日我哋學「最」字，讀做 zeoi3，意思係「最」、最極、程度去到頂，好似「最好」、「最後」咁樣。你望住個字，上面係一個「曰」，下面係一個「取」——「取」本身又拆得開，係「耳」邊嘅「尸」加「十」再加「又」。倉頡入面，我哋先攞字首「曰」，取碼 A，之後再入字身「取」：字身唔係成件成件咁攞，而係攞頭、二、尾三碼，所以攞頭嘅「尸」係 S，第二個「十」係 J，最尾嘅「又」係 E，合埋就係 ASJE。你記住個口訣：「曰」頂住「取」，A 起頭，尸十又收尾——最鍾意你嘅嗰個「最」，就係 ASJE。

會.en: Today we learn 會, read wui5, wui6, wui2, or wui3, meaning to assemble or meet, a meeting, or an organization — like in 都會 (dou1 wui6), a big city or metropolis. Look at its shape from top to bottom: there's the pointed roof 𠆢, which sits on the O key; then a single horizontal stroke 一, the M key; tucked in the middle is 田, the W key; and at the bottom sits 日, the A key — so the full code is OMWA. Why does it split this way? Because 會 is a whole character (整體字), too dense and layered to cleanly divide into a head and a body, so Cangjie uses the head-second-third-tail rule, taking the head 𠆢, then 一, then 田, then the tail 日, skipping right over the crowded middle for a tidy four codes. Remember it like this: pointed roof, one line, a 田 hiding a 日 inside — four parts gathering together, just like a meeting.
會.zh: 今日我哋學「會」呢個字，粵拼讀 wui5、wui6、wui2 或者 wui3，意思係聚集、開會，又或者係一個團體、一個組織，好似「都會」（dou1 wui6）就係大城市噉解。你望吓佢個樣：上面有個尖尖嘅頂 𠆢，就係 O 鍵；跟住一橫 一，係 M 鍵；中間夾住個 田 字，係 W 鍵；最底係個 日 字，係 A 鍵，所以成個碼就係 OMWA。點解會噉拆呢？因為「會」係一個整體字，筆畫多又疊得密，冇辦法乾淨俐落噉分頭同身，倉頡就用「頭二三尾」嘅辦法，取頭 𠆢、第二 一、第三 田、最尾 日，正正跳過中間嗰啲多餘部分，一共四碼。記住喇：尖頂一橫、田裏藏日，四位齊集就係「開會」嘅「會」。

月.en: Look at this character: 月, read "jyut6," which means the moon in the sky, and it also means "month," the way a year has twelve of them. Notice its shape: an outer frame with two short horizontal strokes inside, curving like a slice of moonlight cradling something. In Cangjie, 月 is itself a complete radical, and it has its very own key — the B key — so when you type this character you simply press B once, with no splitting at all. Why so simple? Because 月 isn't built from smaller pieces; it is one basic radical on its own, so a single key covers the whole thing. Remember it this way: see 月, press one B, as direct as looking up at night and spotting the moon straight away.
月.zh: 睇下呢個字：月，讀「jyut6」，意思係天上嘅月亮，亦都可以指「月份」，好似一年有十二個月咁。你留意佢個樣：外面一個框，入面兩橫，成個形好似一彎抱住嘢嘅月光。喺倉頡入面，月本身就係一個完整嘅字根，佢有一個專屬嘅鍵，就係 B 鍵，所以你打呢個字嘅時候，淨係㩒一個 B 就得㗎喇，唔使拆開。點解咁簡單呢？因為月唔係由更細嘅部件砌成，佢自己就係一個基本字根，一個鍵包晒。記住喇：見到月，一個 B 搞掂，就好似夜晚抬頭一望就見到一個月光咁直接。

有.en: Today we learn 有, read "jau5", which means to have, to own, or to exist — the word you use in phrases like "I have" or "is there any". Look at how it's built: on top sits the shape ナ, a slanting stroke crossed by a horizontal one, and underneath sits 月, which here is really the flesh radical ⺼. In Cangjie the head of the character, ナ, is typed as K, and the body, ⺼, is typed as B, so the whole character is simply KB — just two keys. The split falls here because Cangjie reads top to bottom: it takes the head ナ (K) first, then the body ⺼ (B) after, one piece each, neatly done. Remember it this way: one hand ナ holding a piece of meat ⺼ means you "have" something in hand — K then B. Try typing 我有好多書 and you'll put it to use.
有.zh: 今日我哋學「有」呢個字，讀「jau5」，即係「擁有」、「存在」嘅意思，好似「我有」、「有冇」咁樣用。你望吓佢嘅結構：上面係一撇加一橫嘅「ナ」形，下面係「月」（其實係肉字旁「⺼」）。用倉頡拆嘅時候，字首就係「ナ」，喺鍵盤上打K；字身就係「月」，打B，所以成個字嘅碼就係 KB，簡簡單單兩個掣。點解係咁拆呢？因為倉頡係由上到下、由外到內咁睇，先取字首「ナ」（K），再取字身「月」（B），一頭一尾兩個部分啱啱好。記住喇：一隻手「ナ」揸住一嚿「月」肉，你就「有」嘢喺手，K配B。試吓打「我有好多書」，你就會用到佢。

朋.en: Today's character is 「朋」, read pang4, meaning friend or companion. Look at it closely: it's simply two identical 「⺼」 shapes standing side by side, one on the left and one on the right. In Cangjie this 「⺼」 shape lives on the B key, so two of them give you B and B, spelled out as BB. Why is it just two codes? Because Cangjie splits a character into a prefix (字首) and a body (字身); in a left-right character the prefix takes one code and the body takes one code, so the left ⺼ gives B and the right ⺼ gives B, and you're done. Remember it this way: two good friends standing shoulder to shoulder, each holding a B — BB spells 「朋」.
朋.zh: 今日學嘅字係「朋」，讀作 pang4，即係朋友、伙伴嘅意思。你望下佢，其實係兩個一模一樣嘅「⺼」並排排喺一齊，左邊一個，右邊一個。呢個「⺼」形喺倉頡度係 B 鍵，所以左右兩個⺼，就係 B 同 B，全碼寫作 BB。點解只係兩碼咁簡單呢？因為倉頡分字首同字身，左右結構嘅字，字首取一碼、字身取一碼，你嘅左邊⺼做字首取 B，右邊⺼做字身取 B，啱啱兩碼收工。記住喇：兩個好朋友並排企埋一齊，一人一個 B，BB 就係「朋」。

服.en: Today's character is 服, read fuk6, meaning clothes, or to wear and to dress; you'll meet it in words like 服務 (fuk6 mou6, to serve) and 說服 (seoi3 fuk6, to persuade). Look at the shape: it sits in two halves side by side, with a ⺼ (B) on the left and the block 𠬝 on the right. Because Cangjie splits a character into 字首 and 字身, the left-hand ⺼ is the 字首 and gets only one code, so it contributes just B. The right-hand 𠬝 is the 字身, and a 字身 takes head, second, and tail — here the head is 尸 (S), the second is 中 (L), and the tail is 水 (E). Put them in order and you get BSLE: first the 字首 ⺼=B, then the 字身 pieces 尸=S, 中=L, 水=E — think of a slab of ⺼ dressed up with 尸中水, and you've got 服.
服.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「服」，讀做 fuk6，解衫、衣服，又或者係著衫、穿戴嘅意思，好似「服務」（fuk6 mou6）同「說服」（seoi3 fuk6）都用到佢。你望下呢個字，左右兩邊砌埋一齊：左邊係一個⺼（B），右邊就係𠬝呢一嚿。因為倉頡分字首字身，左邊嘅⺼做字首，只可以取一碼，所以淨係得個 B；而右邊嘅𠬝做字身，就要取頭、二、尾三碼——頭係尸（S），第二係中（L），尾係水（E）。合埋一齊就係 BSLE，即係先寫左邊字首嗰個 ⺼=B，再由右邊字身順住攞 尸=S、中=L、水=E。記住呢句：一片⺼掛住尸中水，著上身就係「服」。

朗.en: Today we learn 朗, read "long5", meaning clear, bright, or distinct — the sort of brightness you see on a cloudless day. Look at how it splits into two sides: on the left is 良, and on the right is the flesh radical ⺼. In Cangjie you start with the left side as the 字首 (head), but a 字首 may contribute at most its first and last shapes, so 良 gives only its head 厶 (I) and its tail 丶 (also I), skipping everything in between — that's why you press I twice. Then the 字身 (body) on the right, ⺼, contributes a single B, giving the full code IIB. Memory hook: 良 keeps just its two ends as I, I, then you stick on a slice of flesh B — that's the 朗 in Yuen Long (元朗).
朗.zh: 我哋今日學「朗」呢個字，讀「long5」，意思係光亮、清晰，好似晴天冇雲咁明朗。你睇佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係「良」，右邊係個肉字部「⺼」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，先由左邊嘅字首「良」入手，但字首最多只可以取頭同尾兩碼，所以「良」淨係取頭「厶」（I 碼）同埋尾「丶」（都係 I 碼），中間嘅筆畫就唔理啦，於是打出兩個 I。跟住到右邊嘅字身「⺼」，取一個 B 碼，合埋就係 IIB。記住呢個口訣：良只留頭尾兩個 I，再貼一塊肉 B，元朗嘅朗就係咁砌出嚟。

望.en: Today's character is 望, read mong6, meaning to look at, to look forward, to hope or expect — the feeling in a word like 希望 (hei1 mong6), a hope or a wish, of gazing forward with expectation. The character stacks in two layers: the top is 亡月, and the bottom is 王. From the top layer you first take the little 亠 at the head, which sits on the Y key, then the 月-shape piece ⺼, which is the B key, giving you YB for the whole top. The bottom 王 is one solid body, so by the usual rule you take just its head and tail — the head 竹 is H and the tail 土 is G — and everything joins into YBHG. Remember it this way: lift your head (亠) to look at the moon (⺼), with a king (王) standing below, and you'll be full of hope every time you see 望.
望.zh: 今日學嘅字係「望」，讀mong6，意思係「望向遠處、盼望、期望」，好似「希望」（hei1 mong6）咁，帶住一種向前睇、有所期待嘅感覺。呢個字上下兩截咁擺，上邊係「亡月」，下邊係「王」。上邊嗰截你要先攞頭上嗰粒「亠」，佢係Y掣，跟住攞下面嘅「⺼」，佢係B掣，所以上邊就係YB兩碼；下邊嘅「王」係一整塊字身，照倉頡取碼規則攞頭尾兩碼，頭係「竹」H，尾係「土」G，於是砌埋成YBHG。記法係咁：抬起個頭（亠）望向月亮（⺼），底下企住個王（王），一望就充滿希望喇。

朝.en: Today we learn 朝, a character with two readings: read ziu1 it means "dynasty," and read ciu4 it means "morning," as in 今朝 (this morning). Look at it: the left side is a busy tangle of strokes, but the right side is clearly a 月 (moon). Cangjie treats the left as the head and the 月 on the right as the body; the head takes its first and last shapes, and both the top and bottom of that left part read as 十, giving you two 十 = J, J, while the body 月 = B contributes just one code, so the whole thing is JJB. Here's your hook: two 十 hooks on the left, one 月 on the right — at 朝 (morning) the moon fades as the sun rises.
朝.zh: 今日我哋學「朝」字，佢有兩個讀音：讀 ziu1 嘅時候解「朝代」，讀 ciu4 嘅時候解「朝早、早晨」，好似「今朝」咁樣。你望下呢個字，左邊係一堆好複雜嘅筆畫，右邊清清楚楚係一個「月」字。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，左邊當做字首，右邊個「月」字當做字身；字首要取頭同尾，左邊個複雜部分頭尾都係「十」字形，所以拆出兩個十＝J、J，而字身「月」＝B 只取一碼，砌埋一齊就係 JJB。記住喇：左邊頭尾兩個「十」，右邊一個「月」，朝早見到月同太陽交替，就係「朝」。

期.en: Today we learn 期, read kei4, as in 時期 and 期間 — it means a period of time, a date, or a time limit. Look at its shape: 其 sits on the left and 月 on the right, so it's clearly a left-right character, which means we split it into a head and a body. The head 其 is a busy shape, and since Cangjie lets a head give at most two codes, we take its first and last pieces: the top 廿 gives T, and the bottom 八 gives C. Then the body is the 月 on the right — written here as the flesh radical ⺼ — which gives B, so the whole character is TCB. Remember it this way: 廿 (T) and 八 (C) framing a 月 (B) spell out the 期 in 期待放假, the holiday you're looking forward to.
期.zh: 今日我哋學「期」呢個字，讀 kei4，好似「時期」、「期間」入面咁，意思係一段時間或者限期。你望下佢嘅結構，左邊係「其」，右邊係「月」，一睇就知係一個左右分開嘅字，所以要拆做字首同字身。字首「其」係一個複雜嘅字形，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，於是我哋用取頭尾嘅方法，攞佢最上面嘅「廿」係 T，再攞佢最底嘅「八」係 C。跟住字身係右邊嘅「月」，喺呢度寫成肉字邊「⺼」，取碼係 B，所以成個字砌埋一齊就係 TCB。記住呢個字口訣：廿（T）、八（C）夾住一個月（B），就係你「好期待放假」嗰個「期」喇。

木.en: Look at this character: 木, read muk6 — it's the 木 in 樹木, and it means a tree, or wood and lumber. See its shape: a vertical stroke down the middle, a flat stroke across the top, and two strokes slanting down to the left and right below, just like a tree trunk with its branches spreading out. This one is beautifully simple, because 木 is itself one of the basic radicals in Cangjie, so there's nothing to split apart — you just press the single key D, and the whole code is D. To remember it, picture that D as the shape of a leafy tree standing on its own, one press and the tree is planted.
木.zh: 睇下呢個字：木，讀 muk6，即係「樹木」嘅木，可以指一棵樹，又可以指木材、木頭。你望住佢個形：中間一豎，上面一橫，下面向左右斜出兩筆，好似一棵樹嘅樹幹同枝椏咁伸開。呢個字特別簡單，因為木本身就已經係倉頡入面嘅一個字根，唔使再拆開，所以你只要撳一個掣 D 就得，成個字碼就係 D。記住呢個「D」字，你可以聯想到樹木要「地」上生長，一個掣就種到一棵樹落嚟。

未.en: Today we learn 未, read mei6, meaning "not yet" — as in something that hasn't happened so far. Look at its shape: it's like a tree 木 with an extra horizontal stroke crossing near the top, the whole thing stacked from top to bottom. Cangjie breaks it very simply because it's a whole character (整體字), so we just take the pieces from top down: the top part is 十 on key J, and the bottom part is 木 on key D, giving you the full code JD, just two codes. Why only two? Because a whole character isn't chopped into fine detail — you simply read the codes in top-to-bottom order without forcing in extra keys. Remember it this way: a tree 木 with a 十 sitting on its head, still growing but 'not yet' finished — that's JD.
未.zh: 今日我哋學「未」呢個字，讀 mei6，即係「仲未」、「未曾」嘅意思，代表一件事情重未發生。你望吓佢個樣，好似一棵樹「木」上面加多一橫，成個字上下咁樣疊落嚟。倉頡拆呢個字好簡單，因為佢係一個整體字，我哋淨係要由上至下攞：上面嗰部分係「十」，鍵 J，下面嗰部分係「木」，鍵 D，所以成個碼就係 JD，兩碼搞掂。點解只係兩碼咁少呢？就係因為整體字唔使拆到咁細，跟返由上落下嘅次序取碼就得，唔會硬要湊夠更多碼。記住呢個字嘅樣：一棵「木」頭頂多咗個「十」字，仲『未』長高，就係 JD。

本.en: Today we learn 本, read bun2, meaning root, origin, source, or basis — you see it in 日本 for Japan and 根本 for something fundamental. Look at the shape: it's really the character 木 (tree) with one extra horizontal stroke drawn at the bottom, like the root of the tree reaching into the ground, which is exactly why it carries the meaning of origin. Because 本 is a whole character — 木 with a single bottom stroke added — we don't chop it into many pieces; we just take the code in writing order, starting with 木, which sits on the D key, and then the bottom stroke 一, which sits on the M key, giving us DM. Here's your memory hook: a tree 木 with a root line drawn underneath, D then M, and that's 本.
本.zh: 今日我哋學「本」呢個字，讀作 bun2，意思係根、源頭、基礎，好似「日本」呢個國名，或者「根本」講嘅根基咁。你望下佢個形，其實就係一棵「木」字，然後喺個底部橫多一畫，好似樹木埋落地嘅根一樣，所以先至有「根源」嘅意思。因為「本」係一個整體字，木字下面加多一橫，我哋唔會拆到好碎，只要順住寫嘅次序取碼就得——先取「木」，佢喺 D 鍵，再取底部嗰一橫「一」，佢喺 M 鍵，合埋就係 DM 兩碼。記住個口訣：一棵木，落到底畫一橫定根，D、M，就係「本」。

村.en: Today's character is 村, read cyun1, meaning a village or hamlet — it's the 村 in 屋村, the word for a housing estate. Look at the shape: it splits neatly into a left half and a right half, with a tree 木 on the left and 寸 on the right. The left 木 acts as the 字首 (the lead part), and a lead part normally gives up just one code, so it contributes a single D; the right 寸 is the 字身 (the body part), and a body part is allowed a first-and-last pair, so from 寸 we take its head 木 as D and its tail 戈 as I, giving us D, D, I. Why does the left side only get one code? Because the lead part is deliberately kept short so the body part can carry more detail. Remember it like this: one tree D on the left, then 寸 broken into head-tree D and tail-戈 I — a tree standing beside a little village.
村.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「村」，讀 cyun1，即係鄉村、村莊嘅意思，你住喺「屋村」嘅「村」就係佢。你望一望：呢個字左右兩邊拆開，左邊係一棵「木」，右邊係一個「寸」。左邊嘅「木」做字首，我哋淨係取佢一個字母 D；右邊嘅「寸」做字身，字身可以取到頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋喺「寸」入面先取頭嘅「木」D，再取尾嘅「戈」I，合埋成 DDI。點解左邊淨取一碼？因為做字首嘅部件一般只取一碼，個字嘅重點碼數留番畀字身，字身先可以取多啲。記住個心法：左邊一棵木（D），右邊一個寸拆做頭木尾戈（D I），三粒 D、D、I，一棵樹旁邊有條村。

東.en: Today we learn the character 東, read dung1, meaning east or eastward — the direction where, as the sentence says, the sun rises in the east. Take a good look at its shape: it reads almost like a single tree standing tall, hard to slice cleanly into a front and a body. In Cangjie, 東 is treated as a whole character (整體字), so instead of chopping it into many little bits, we simply pick out two representative pieces from within it: first 木 on the D key, then 田 on the W key, giving the code DW. A nice memory hook: picture the tree 木 growing over a field 田 in the east, and just tap those two keys, D then W.
東.zh: 今日我哋學「東」呢個字，讀做 dung1，即係東方、東邊嘅意思，好似「太陽喺東邊出」噉樣。你留心睇下佢個形，成個字好似一棵樹嘅樣，好難好整齊噉分兩截。喺倉頡入面，「東」係一個整體字，我哋唔會夾硬將佢拆到零零碎碎，而係喺入面揀出兩個代表性嘅部件嚟砌：先係「木」，喺 D 鍵，再係「田」，喺 W 鍵，所以個碼就係 DW。你可以記住：一棵樹「木」下面種住一塊「田」，東邊嘅太陽就喺呢度升起，DW 兩下就打得晒。

林.en: Today we learn 林, read lam4, meaning a forest or grove, and it's also a surname. Look at its shape: one 木 (tree) on the left, and another 木 on the right — two trees standing side by side, which is exactly how you picture a small forest. This is a left-right character, so Cangjie reads it from left to right: the left 木 is the head, giving D, and the right 木 is the body, giving D again. Because both pieces are the identical 木, the whole character is simply DD — you just press the same key twice. Here's your hook: two trees together make a forest, so 林 is 木 plus 木, DD. Think of the words 森林 (sam1 lam4) and 山林 (saan1 lam4), as in 'There are many forests on the mountain.'
林.zh: 今日我哋學「林」呢個字，讀做 lam4，意思係樹林、森林，都可以做姓氏。你望下佢嘅樣：左邊一棵「木」，右邊又一棵「木」，兩棵樹企埋一齊，好自然噉就係一片樹林嘞。呢個字係左右結構，倉頡從左至右噉拆：左邊個「木」係字首，取碼 D；右邊個「木」係字身，又取碼 D。因為兩個部件一模一樣，都係「木」，所以成個字就係 DD，你只需要撳兩下同一個掣就得。記住呢個口訣：兩棵木企埋，就係一片林——DD 兩下木。你可以諗下「森林」（sam1 lam4）同「山林」（saan1 lam4），例如「山上有好多樹林。」

果.en: Today we learn 果, read "gwo2", the fruit in words like 水果 and 生果 — it means fruit or fruit-crop, and it can also mean an outcome or result. Take a good look at its shape: on top sits a 田 (field), and underneath it holds up a 木 (tree), rather like fruit hanging on a tree, a very picture-like character. To take the code we read top to bottom: first grab the top 田, which lives on the W key, then the bottom 木, which lives on the D key, so the full code for 果 is simply W, D. Why only two parts? Because 果 is a whole character with a clean top-and-bottom build, so after the field comes the tree and there is nothing more to split. Just remember: field on top, tree below, fruit hanging in the branches — and it sticks in your mind at once.
果.zh: 今日我哋學「果」呢個字，讀「gwo2」，就好似「生果」、「水果」嘅果，意思係果實、果子，又可以解「結果」嗰種結局。你留心睇吓佢嘅樣子：上面係一個「田」字，下面托住一個「木」字，好似樹木上面掛住果實咁，畫面感十足。拆碼嗰陣，我哋由上到下、由外到內咁行，先攞上面嘅「田」，佢喺 W 鍵；再攞下面嘅「木」，佢喺 D 鍵，所以「果」嘅完整碼就係 W、D。點解淨係兩碼？因為「果」係一個整體字，結構清清楚楚係上下兩件砌埋一齊，田字之後緊接住木字，唔使再拆得更細。記住呢句：田上木下，果實掛喺樹頭，一睇就記得晒喇！

查.en: Today's character is 查, read caa4, meaning to investigate or look something up — as in "I look up information online." Take a look at its shape: on top sits a 木 (tree), and underneath is a horizontal stroke, a 日, and another horizontal stroke stacked together. Cangjie splits it into a head and a body: the head 木 is coded just once as D, while the body below — which reads like 旦 — takes its first-and-last pieces, 日 as A and the bottom stroke 一 as M, giving you the full code DAM. Why does the head get only one code? In a top-bottom character, Cangjie usually gives the head fewer codes and lets the body carry more, so that together they add up to enough codes to pin down the whole character. Picture a tree (木 D) pressing down on a rising sun (日 A) resting on the ground (一 M), and DAM will stick.
查.zh: 今日學嘅字係「查」，讀 caa4，即係調查、查閱嘅意思，好似「我上網查資料」噉樣。你望吓佢個樣：上面係一個「木」字，下面就係一橫加個「日」再加一橫，成個字上下疊起。倉頡拆字有規矩：字首同字身分開取碼，字首「木」淨係取一碼 D；而下面嘅「旦」係字身，取首尾兩碼——「日」取 A，最底嗰一橫「一」取 M，所以成個碼就係 DAM。點解字首得一碼？因為喺上下結構入面，倉頡通常畀字首少啲碼、字身多啲碼，噉樣先夠三四碼識別到成隻字。記住呢個字嘅樣：一棵樹（木 D）下面壓住一個日出天光嘅「旦」（A 加尾嗰橫 M），你就記得「查」係 DAM 喇。

校.en: Today we learn 校, which reads haau6 in a word like 學校, the place where you go to study, and can also read gaau3, meaning a field officer in the army. Look at how it's built from a left and a right side: on the left is the wood radical 木, which gives one code D; on the right is 交, and that's the 字身. Because 木 is the 字首, and a 字首 takes at most one code, it contributes just the head code D; then the 字身 交 follows the three-code rule for a body part, taking head, second, and tail — the head 亠 is Y, the second piece 父 is C, and the tail 乂 is K, giving you DYCK all together. Remember it this way: one tree (D) stands beside a crossroads, and walking past it brings you to school.
校.zh: 今日我哋學「校」呢個字，佢讀 haau6，喺「學校」度就係讀書嘅地方，另外都可以讀 gaau3，指軍隊入面嘅校官。你望下佢由左右兩邊砌成：左邊係木字部「木」，取一碼 D；右邊係個「交」字，就係字身喇。木字係字首，字首最多都係取一碼，所以淨係攞 D 呢個頭碼；跟住字身「交」就照字身嘅規矩，取頭、次、尾三碼——頭係「亠」取 Y，第二個係「父」取 C，最尾係「乂」取 K，砌埋一齊就係 DYCK。記住：一棵木（D）撐住個交叉路口，你行過去就返到學校啦。

根.en: Today we learn 根, read gan1, which means the root of a tree, and by extension a foundation or the basis of something. Look at how it's built: on the left sits 木 (tree), and on the right sits 艮, so the character naturally splits into these two parts. The left-hand 木 is the 字首, and a 字首 only ever gives one code, so we take just 木 on the D key. The right-hand 艮 is the 字身, and a 字身 is read by head-and-tail, so we take its head 日 on A and its tail 女 on V, giving us DAV. Remember it this way: one tree (D) hides a sun (A) and a woman (V) beneath it — roots buried deep, just like these three pieces lined up in order.
根.zh: 今日我哋學「根」字，讀作 gan1，就係樹木嘅根，引申做「根本」、「基礎」嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅結構：左邊係「木」，右邊係「艮」，所以呢個字分做兩部分。左邊嘅「木」係字首，字首只可以取一碼，所以我哋淨係攞「木」，個鍵係 D。右邊嘅「艮」係字身，字身要取頭同尾，個頭係「日」（鍵 A），個尾就係「女」（鍵 V），加埋就係 DAV。記住喇：一棵木（D），底下藏住日（A）同女（V）——樹根深藏喺泥土入面，就好似呢三個部件咁順序砌埋一齊。

格.en: Today's character is 格, read gaak3, meaning pattern, standard, or style — as when you say something has real class or form. Look at it: on the left sits a 木 tree, and on the right is the character 各, a classic left-right build. The left 木 (D) is a standalone piece serving as the 字首, and a 字首 gives only one code, so we simply take D. The right side, 各, acts as the 字身, so we take its head, a middle piece, and its tail: the head 夂 (H), then the second piece 水 (E), and finally the tail 口 (R), which strings together into DHER. Remember it this way — tree D beside 各, and 各 breaks into 夂 (H), 水 (E), 口 (R); even a teacup can have real 格!
格.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「格」，讀做 gaak3，解作款式、規格、格調，好似講一件嘢好有「格」咁。你望吓佢，左邊係一棵「木」，右邊係「各」字，係一個典型嘅左右結構。左邊嘅「木」（D）本身係一個獨立部件，做字首只取一碼，所以我哋淨係打一個 D。右邊嘅「各」做字身，就要拆開嚟拿頭、身、尾三粒碼：頭係「夂」（H），跟住取第二個部件「水」（E），最後取埋尾嘅「口」（R），砌埋一齊就係 DHER。你記住呢個口訣：木（D）配各，各字自己拆成夂（H）、水（E）、口（R），一件杯都可以好有「格」！

案.zh: 今日學嘅字係「案」，讀作 on3，意思係桌案、几案，亦都可以指法律上嘅案件，好似「答案」（daap3 on3）同「個案」（go3 on3）咁。你望吓成個字，其實係上下兩部分砌成：上邊係「安」，下邊係一個「木」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首要交足碼，所以上邊嘅「安」拆做兩碼——先取上面嘅「宀」形，寫做十（J），再取下面嘅「女」（V）；至於下邊嘅「木」就係一個完整部件，取D。所以成個碼就係 JVD，順住由上到下、由外到內咁一路砌落嚟。記住喇：一個「安」字坐喺一塊「木」板上面，就係一張案枱嘞！

條.en: Today's character is 「條」, read tiu4. It can mean a clause or condition — as in a rule or a term — and it can also count long, thin things, like one fish. Look at it: on the left sits the 字首 「攸」, and on the right the 字身 「木」. In Cangjie a 字首 and 字身 each get their own quota, so from 「攸」 we take the head, middle and tail — first the 亻 on top (key O), then the two pieces standing side by side in the middle, 丨 (key L) and 夂 (key O) — giving three codes; then the 字身 「木」 contributes just one code, D. Put together that spells OLOD. Memory hook: picture a person (亻) holding a wooden pole (木), and hanging between them, one long strip — OLOD.
條.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「條」，讀作 tiu4，佢可以解作「條例」嘅條文、條件，又可以指一條長長嘅嘢，好似一條魚咁。你望吓佢，左邊係「攸」呢個字首，右邊「木」係字身。倉頡拆字時，字首同字身各有配額：字首「攸」我哋取頭尾同中間，先寫最頂嘅亻（O 鍵），再落到中間並列嘅丨（L 鍵）同夂（O 鍵），三粒碼交足字首嘅份；跟住字身「木」淨係取一碼 D，所以全碼就係 OLOD。記住呢個字：一個人（亻）撐住條魚竿（木），中間夾住嘅就係一條，OLOD。

業.en: Today's character is 業, read jip6, meaning profession, business, or trade — you meet it in everyday words like 商業 (soeng1 jip6, business or commerce) and 專業 (zyun1 jip6, a specialized field). Take a good look: it's a busy, stacked shape, with a 廿-like row across the top, some strokes crowded in the middle, and a solid 木 (tree) holding up the bottom. Because 業 is a whole-body character, Cangjie doesn't chop out every piece — instead it takes just four: the head, the second, the third, and the tail, skipping whatever sits in the middle. So you type head 廿 = T, second 金 = C, third 廿 = T, and tail 木 = D, giving you TCTD, and the crowded middle is simply left out. Remember it as a stack — 廿 on top, 金 pressed in, 廿 again, and 木 at the foot — and TCTD will come straight to mind.
業.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「業」，讀作 jip6，即係職業、生意、行業嘅意思，好似「商業」（soeng1 jip6）同「專業」（zyun1 jip6）咁常見。你望下呢個字，佢筆畫好多，頭嗰橫排似「廿」字形，中間有筆畫夾住，最落底就係一個「木」字托住成個字。「業」係一個整體字，倉頡拆碼嘅時候唔會逐格拆晒，而係取頭、次、三、尾四個部分：頭嗰個廿係 T，第二個金係 C，第三個又係一個廿係 T，最尾個木係 D，所以成個碼就係 TCTD，中間嘅部分就跳過唔理。呢個「取頭尾、跳中間」係整體字嘅慣常做法，唔使你數盡每一筆。記住呢個口訣：廿頂住、金夾住、廿再一層、木托底，TCTD 就係「業」。

極.en: Today we learn 極, read gik6, which means extreme, the utmost, the furthest point — as in 極度 gik6 dou6, extremely, or 極之 gik6 zi1, exceedingly or immensely. Look at the character: on the left stands a tree, 木, and on the right sits the shape 亟, and Cangjie splits it right down that line. The left 木 is the head, and a head is given only one code, so it contributes just D. Everything else falls to the right side as the body 亟, which takes its opening 一 as M, then 水 as E, and finally the closing 一 as M again, giving you the full code DMEM. The reason the left yields only one code is simply that as the head it gets a single-code quota, and the remaining codes are all left for the body to fill. Remember it this way: 木 D, 一 M, 水 E, 一 M — a tree planted on the left while the right reaches all the way to the extreme.
極.zh: 我哋今日學「極」呢個字，讀 gik6，意思係到咗盡頭、最盡、最頂點，好似「極度」gik6 dou6 話極其厲害，又或者「極之」gik6 zi1 講到非常之高。你睇個字，左邊係一棵樹「木」，右邊係「亟」，倉頡就係咁樣拆：左邊嘅「木」係字首，只取一碼 D。而右邊嘅「亟」做字身，取頭「一」M、跟住「水」E、最後個尾又係「一」M，所以成個碼砌埋就係 DMEM。點解左邊淨係得一碼？因為佢係字首，字首取碼有限額，一個木字取一碼就夠，餘落嘅碼就全部畀返右邊個字身去補足。記住個口訣：木 D 一 M 水 E 一 M，樹木立喺左邊，右邊一路取到盡頭，就係「極」。

榮.en: Today we learn 榮, read wing4, meaning glory or honor, and by extension to flourish or prosper — think of plants growing lush and thriving. Look at its shape: two little fires stacked on top, a cover in the middle, and a tree holding everything up at the bottom. When you split it, the 字首 takes the first two pieces, which are those two 火 fires, so you press F and F; then the 字身 takes its head and its tail, the head being the small cover 冖 on key B and the tail being the 木 tree at the very bottom on key D, giving you the full code FFBD. Here's your hook: two fires F F blaze up top, a cap B shelters the tree D — and that's why he 'feels very proud'!
榮.zh: 今日我哋學「榮」字，讀 wing4，意思係光榮、榮譽，又可以指興旺繁盛，好似草木茂盛咁。你睇下佢個樣，上面兩粒火重疊住，中間一個蓋，下面托住棵樹咁。拆碼嘅時候，字首要攞頭兩個部件，就係嗰兩粒火，兩個都撳 F、F；跟住輪到字身，字身要取頭同尾，頭係嗰個寶蓋仔「冖」，撳 B，尾就係最底嘅「木」，撳 D，所以成個碼係 FFBD。記住喇：兩把火 F F 燒到頂，一頂帽 B 遮住棵樹 D，你就會覺得「好光榮」啦！

構.en: Today we learn 構, which reads kau3 or gau3 and means a frame, a building, or a structure. Look at it: on the left is the wood radical 木, and on the right sits a stack of strokes piled together. When we break it into code, the left-hand 字首 木 (D) takes just one code; then the 字身 on the right follows the head-and-last rule, taking from top to bottom 廿 (T), 廿 (T), and the closing 冂 (B), giving us the full code DTTB. Here's your memory hook: a piece of wood (D) holds up two 廿 shapes (T, T), and the 冂 (B) frames it all in — just like building an actual structure.
構.zh: 今日我哋學「構」呢個字，讀音係 kau3 或者 gau3，意思係架構、建築物、結構。你睇睇佢，左邊係一個「木」字部，右邊就係一堆疊埋一齊嘅筆畫。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「木」（D）只需要取一碼；跟住入面就係字身，字身按照「取頭二尾」嘅原則，順住由上到下取「廿」（T）、「廿」（T）同埋最尾嘅「冂」（B），所以成個碼就係 DTTB。記住呢個字嘅竅門：一嚿木（D）撐住兩個廿字（T、T），最後用個「冂」（B）框起佢，就好似真係搭起一個結構咁。

樂.en: Today's character is 樂, and it carries several readings: read lok6 it means happy or joyful, and read ngok6 it means music, as in 音樂. Take a good look at its shape — two tangled thread-like bundles sit up top with a small stroke pinched between them, and a 木 (a tree) props everything up from below, making the whole thing look crowded. Because it's a whole-shape character that can't be cleanly split into left-right or top-bottom halves, Cangjie uses the take-head-two-tail method, picking just three pieces: first the 女 (V) at the head, then the 戈 (I) as the second piece, and finally the 木 (D) at the very bottom, while the messy middle is simply skipped, giving you VID. Remember it as 女-戈-木 — tangles above, a tree below, holding up a character that is both happy and full of music.
樂.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「樂」，佢有幾個讀音：讀 lok6 解開心、快樂；讀 ngok6 就係音樂嘅意思，好似「音樂」咁。你望吓佢個樣，上面兩團似絞絲嘅嘢，中間夾住一橫，下面托住一個「木」，成隻字睇落密密麻麻。呢個係整體字，冇辦法整整齊齊分做左右或者上下兩橛，所以倉頡就用「取頭二尾」嘅方法，只揀三個部件：先取頭嗰個「女」（V），再取第二個「戈」（I），最後取底部嘅「木」（D），中間嗰截就跳過唔理，砌成 VID。記住口訣「女戈木」——上面糾纏、下面一棵樹，掛住個開心又動聽嘅「樂」。

樓.en: Today we learn 樓, read "lau4," meaning a building of two or more stories — the same 樓 in 閣樓, an attic or loft. Look at its shape: on the left is the narrow 木 (tree, wood), and on the right sits the bulkier 婁, so the whole character reads like a tall wooden structure. When we break it up, the 木 on the left is the 字首 and gives just one code, D; the 婁 on the right is the 字身, and because it's complex we take head-second-tail, three codes — 中 (L) at the head, then 田 (W) in the middle, and 女 (V) at the tail, giving DLWV. The split falls this way because the 字首 contributes only one code while the 字身 fills out the rest with head, second, and tail, so the character gets enough codes to stand apart. Remember it like this: 木 stands guard on the left, while 中, 田, and 女 stack up floor by floor on the right to make a building.
樓.zh: 今日我哋學「樓」呢個字，讀「lau4」，即係有兩層或者以上嘅建築物，好似「閣樓」嘅樓咁。你望吓佢個形，左邊窄窄哋係「木」，右邊肥肥哋係「婁」，一睇就知係一間木構嘅高樓。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「木」係字首，取一碼，就係 D；右邊嘅「婁」係字身，佢比較複雜，所以按頭、次、尾嘅方法揀三碼——頭係「中」L，跟住係中間嘅「田」W，最後係下面嘅「女」V，合埋成 DLWV。點解字身要咁揀呢？因為字首淨係取一碼，字身就補足到頭二尾三碼，等成個字有足夠嘅碼去分辨。記住個口訣：木站喺左邊守門口，右邊由中、田、女一層層疊上去，就係一座樓。

標.en: This character 標 reads biu1, and it means a mark, a label, a sign, or a standard — as in 目標 (muk6 biu1), the target you aim for, or 標準 (biu1 zeon2), a standard or norm you measure things against. Look at it: on the left sits the wood radical 木, and on the right stands the character 票. When Cangjie breaks it down, the head 木 is simple and gives just one code, D. The body 票 is not a standalone whole-character piece, so it follows the ordinary body rule of head-second-tail: the top 一 gives M, the middle 田 gives W, and the bottom 火 gives F, which together make MWF. So the whole thing types in order as D, M, W, F — just picture a tree 木 planted on the left holding a ticket 票 on the right, and the code will come back to you.
標.zh: 呢個字「標」讀做 biu1，意思係記號、標記、標籤，又或者係標準嘅意思，好似「目標」（muk6 biu1）就係要追嘅目標，「標準」（biu1 zeon2）就係一把量度嘅尺度。你望吓佢，左邊係一個「木」字部，右邊係一個「票」字。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，字首「木」好簡單，淨係取一個 D。到咗字身「票」嗰邊，佢唔係一個獨立部件，所以要照普通字身嘅規矩：取頭、取次、再取尾，即係頂上面嘅「一」取 M，中間嘅「田」取 W，最底嘅「火」取 F，合埋就係 MWF。所以成個字順住打落去就係 D、M、W、F —— 記住「一棵木企喺左邊，右邊有塊票」，你就唔會撈亂喇。

模.en: Today we learn 模, read mou4, the character in 模型 (model) and 模範 (role model); it means a pattern, a standard, or to copy and imitate. Look at it: on the left a small 木 tree, and on the right a big block that is actually the character 莫. We split it into a head and a body: the head is the left-hand 木, keyed D; the body is 莫, and because a body may take more than two codes we grab its first-middle-last shapes — the grass-top 艹 T on top, the 日 A in the middle, and the 大 K at the bottom, giving DTAK. Why three codes for 莫? Because as the body it gets room for a first, middle, and last piece, not just two. Remember it this way: a tree beside a big block, grass over a sun over a 大 — 木草日大, DTAK.
模.zh: 今日我哋學「模」呢個字，讀 mou4，即係模型、模範嗰個「模」，意思係樣板、標準，又或者係照住嚟做、模仿。你望下佢，左邊一棵「木」，右邊一大嚿嘢，其實係「莫」字。呢個字要拆做字首同字身兩橛：字首係最左邊嘅「木」，撳 D；跟住嘅字身係「莫」，字身可以取多過兩碼，所以我哋用頭、中、尾三碼取形，頭係頂上嘅「艹」T，中間係「日」A，最尾係下面嘅「大」K，合埋就係 DTAK。點解「莫」要咁樣拆呢？因為佢做字身，唔止得兩碼位，倉頡就准你取首、次、尾三個碼嚟夠位。記住呢句：一棵木旁邊，草頭遮住日頭，落到一個大字底，木草日大 DTAK。

樣.en: This character is 樣, read joeng6 or joeng2, and it means shape, form, pattern or style — like in 你今日個樣好靚, 'you look pretty today.' Look at it: there's a 木 on the left and 羕 on the right, so straight away you can tell it's a left-right character. The prefix 木 on the left is easy — it's the tree shape, and it gives you the key D. The body 羕 on the right has a lot of strokes, and by Cangjie's rule that a body takes at most three codes, you can't grab every piece, so you take head, second and tail: the head 廿 gives T, the second piece 土 gives G, and the tail 水 gives E. Put the four together and you get DTGE. Remember it as 木, 廿, 土, 水 — a tree drawing out a pattern.
樣.zh: 呢個字係「樣」，讀joeng6或者joeng2，講嘅係樣式、樣子、形狀嘅意思，好似「你今日個樣好靚」咁樣。你望下佢，左邊係一棵「木」，右邊係「羕」，一睇就知係左右兩份嘅字。左邊嘅字首「木」好簡單，就係木字，取佢個鍵D。右邊嘅字身「羕」筆畫多，按倉頡「一個字身最多取三碼」嘅規矩，唔可以逐粒逐粒攞晒，所以要揀頭、二、尾三個位：頭係「廿」取T，第二係「土」取G，最後個尾係「水」取E。所以四碼合埋就係DTGE。記住個口訣：木、廿、土、水——一棵樹畫個樣板出嚟。

樹.en: Today we're learning 樹, read syu6, which means a tree or a plant, and can also mean to establish or set up. Look at its structure: on the left is the wood radical 木, which in Cangjie takes the code D, and this serves as the head of the whole character. The body on the right is actually made of several stacked pieces, and rather than typing every single one, we follow the head-second-tail rule for the body: the head 士 gives G, the second piece 廿 gives T, and the tail 戈 gives I, so altogether the code is DGTI. Why does it split this way? Because when a body has many parts, Cangjie caps it at three codes, so you take the first, the next, and the last, skipping whatever sits in the middle. Here's your memory hook: one piece of wood (D) stands on the left, while 士 (G), 廿 (T), and 戈 (I) prop up the right — together they grow into a tall tree, just like in 棵樹好高大, and you'll remember DGTI.
樹.zh: 今日我哋學「樹」呢個字，讀作 syu6，意思係樹木、植物，亦都可以解作「建立、設立」。你睇下佢嘅結構，左邊係一個「木」字旁，喺倉頡入面「木」取碼 D，佢就係整個字嘅字首。右邊嘅字身其實有幾個部件疊埋，我哋唔會逐粒逐粒全部拆晒，而係跟「頭、次、尾」嘅取碼原則：頭部係「士」取 G，中間取「廿」T，最後取尾部「戈」I，合埋就係 DGTI。點解要咁樣揀？因為字身部件多，倉頡規定字身最多取三碼，所以要取首、取次、再取尾，中間唔重要嘅就跳過。記住呢句：一棵「木」（D）企喺左邊，右邊由士（G）、廿（T）、戈（I）撐起，就砌成一棵大樹喇！好似「棵樹好高大」咁，你就記得住 DGTI。

橋.en: Today we learn 橋, read kiu4 — it's the bridge you walk across every day, and it can also mean a beam or crosspiece. Look at the character: on the left is 木 (wood), on the right is 喬, so it clearly splits into a left part and a right part. The left 木 is the 字首, giving us 木 (D); the right 喬 is the 字身, and by the Cangjie rule for a body we take head, second, and tail — the head 竹 (H), the second 大 (K), and the bottom piece ⺼ (B), which builds the full code DHKB. Why only three codes on the right? Because a 字身 takes at most three, so we grab the first, next, and last shape and skip whatever sits in the middle. Memory hook: a bridge built of wood — 木 (D), then 竹 (H) 大 (K) ⺼ (B) — and you'll cross it without stumbling.
橋.zh: 今日我哋學「橋」呢個字，讀做 kiu4，就係我哋每日行過嘅橋，又可以指樑或者橫木。你望吓個字，左邊有個「木」，右邊係一個「喬」，好明顯係左右兩橛。左邊嘅木字係字首，取「木」（D）；右邊嘅喬係字身，我哋照倉頡嘅規矩取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係「竹」（H），二係「大」（K），尾就係最底嗰個「⺼」（B），砌埋一齊就係 DHKB。點解右邊得三碼呢？因為字身最多取三碼，所以取頭一、次一、尾一就夠，中間嗰啲跳過。記住呢句：木邊架起一條橋——木（D），竹（H）大（K）⺼（B），你行過條橋就唔會撞板喇。

機.en: Today we learn 機, read gei1, which basically means a machine or mechanism, as in 機會 gei1 wui6 for opportunity or chance, and 機構 gei1 gau3 for an organization or institution. Look at its shape: on the left sits a 木 tree, and on the right a cluster of pieces packed together. Cangjie takes the prefix first, and the left-hand 木 is that prefix, giving D. Then comes the body, and the body follows the head-second-tail rule — first code, second code, last code — so reading the right side in order you take the head 女 V, then the second piece 戈 I, then the tail piece 戈 I again, which spells out DVII. Here's your memory hook: a tree on the left (木 D) and a woman (女 V) holding two spears (戈 I, 戈 I) — 木, 女, 戈, 戈 builds the machine.
機.zh: 今日我哋學「機」呢個字，讀音係 gei1，本義係機器、機械，好似「機會」gei1 wui6 咁指時機、機遇，又或者「機構」gei1 gau3 咁指組織、機關。你望吓佢個結構，左邊係一個「木」，右邊係一堆組件砌埋一齊。倉頡拆字先睇字首：左邊嘅「木」係字首，取碼 D。跟住輪到字身，字身嘅取碼規矩係「頭、二、尾」——即係頭一個碼、第二個碼、最尾一個碼，所以右邊順住寫落去，頭係「女」V，第二個係「戈」I，最尾又係一個「戈」I，加埋就係 DVII。記住呢個字：左邊一棵樹（木 D），右邊一個女仔（女 V）擰住兩支戈（I、I）——木、女、戈、戈，就砌成部機器喇。

檔.en: Today we learn 檔, read dong3 or dong2, which originally means a shelf or crosspiece and now often means a market stall, like the 熟食檔 (cooked food stall) you'd see in a wet market. Notice it splits left and right: the left side is the 木 radical, which we take as the head, keying D. The right side is the whole character 當 acting as the body, and a body takes head, second, and tail — three pieces — so working through 當 top to bottom you take the 「⺌」 on top first as the head, key F, then the 「⺼」 as the second, key B, and finally the 「田」 at the bottom as the tail, key W. Together that gives DFBW; because the left-side head only gets one code slot it takes just D, while the right-side body fills out the full head-second-tail of three. Remember it this way: wood beside a 當, and 木・⺌・⺼・田 spells D F B W.
檔.zh: 今日我哋學「檔」呢個字，讀 dong3 或者 dong2，本來係架、橫木嘅意思，好似「檔口」咁指擺賣嘅攤位，你去街市見到嘅「熟食檔」就係用呢個字。你留意佢係左右分開嘅：左邊係個「木」字部首，我哋取佢做字首，撳 D。右邊係成個「當」字做字身，字身要取頭、二、尾三個部分，所以喺個「當」入面順住撳落去——最上面嗰個「⺌」係頭，撳 F，接住個「⺼」係第二個，撳 B，最尾嗰個「田」係尾，撳 W。合埋一齊就係 DFBW；因為左邊字首淨係得一個碼位，唯有取一個 D，右邊字身就攞足頭二尾三碼補夠。記住口訣：木字旁邊擺住個「當」，木、⺌、⺼、田，D F B W。

權.zh: 今日我哋學「權」字，粵音讀 kyun4，意思係權力、權利、權威呢啲同「話事」有關嘅概念。你望下佢嘅結構，左邊係一個「木」字部，右邊係一個好複雜嘅「雚」。倉頡拆法係咁：字首取左邊嘅木＝D；至於右邊嘅字身「雚」，佢係一個複雜體，唔可以逐格拆晒，所以照複雜字身嘅取碼規矩——取頭、取次、取尾三碼，即係頭嗰個艹＝T、跟住第二個口＝R、最後尾嗰個土＝G，合埋成 DTRG。記住呢個畫面：一棵木（D）撐住一堆草（T）、一個口（R）、一撮泥土（G），你就記得「權」喇。

次.en: Today's character is 次, read ci3, meaning order or sequence, and also "next" — as in 一次, meaning "once" or "one time." Look at it: on the left is the little two-drop ice radical 冫, and on the right sits the character 欠. Cangjie splits it exactly there — the left part 冫 is the head and gives I, then the body 欠 on the right, being the body, is unpacked by the head-second-tail rule, taking its head 一 as M, its second piece 乙 as N, and its tail 人 as O, spelling IMNO. The reason 欠 gets three codes is that it's the body, and a body may draw head, second, and tail, unlike a head which only takes two. Remember the little ice drops leading (I), then 一, 乙, 人 following behind — say 呢次我贏咗, "this time I won," and it sticks.
次.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「次」，讀 ci3，意思係次序、下一個，好似「一次」咁講一遍嘅意思。你望吓佢：左邊係細細粒嘅冰點「冫」，右邊係一個「欠」字。倉頡就係咁分：左邊嘅字首冫取 I；跟住輪到右邊嘅字身「欠」，因為佢係字身，我哋照「頭、次、尾」規矩去拆，取頭嘅一取 M、第二個乙取 N、最尾嘅人取 O，砌埋成 IMNO。點解「欠」要拆咁多件呢？因為佢係字身，字身可以取到頭、次、尾三碼，唔似字首咁淨係取兩碼。記住個口訣：兩點水行先（I），然後一（M）、乙（N）、人（O）跟尾，「呢次我贏咗」你就記得晒喇。

止.en: Today we learn 止, read "zi2", meaning to stop, to halt, or to prohibit — as in the word 禁止, to forbid. Look at it: it sits like a foot planted firmly on the ground, refusing to move, which is exactly the feeling of stopping. This is a whole-shape character (整體字), meaning the whole thing is one solid form with no clean split into a leading part and a body, so we use the whole-shape rule: take the first, the second, and the last piece. Those are 卜 on the Y key, 中 on the L key, and 一 on the M key, giving you YLM. Remember it like a person standing still on the ground, unmoving — 卜, 中, 一, planted and stopped.
止.zh: 今日我哋學「止」呢個字，讀「zi2」，意思係停止、制止，好似「禁止」入面咁。你望住佢，成個字睇落好似一隻腳踏喺地上企定咗咁，唔郁，正正就係「停」嘅感覺。呢個係一個整體字，即係話成個字本身係一塊完整嘅形，冇一個清楚嘅字首同字身可以分開，所以我哋用整體字嘅取碼方法：攞頭、二、尾三個部分。首先係「卜」，喺 Y 鍵；跟住係「中」，喺 L 鍵；最後係「一」，喺 M 鍵，合埋就係 YLM。記住佢就好啦：一個人企喺地上唔郁，卜、中、一，停低唔行。

正.en: Today we learn 正, read zing3, and also zeng3 as in the sentence 呢個蛋糕好正 — this cake is really great. It means right, proper, correct — a very positive character, and if you look at it you'll see a flat stroke on top and another on the bottom, framing the middle, standing perfectly upright. 正 is a whole character (整體字), so we don't split it into head and body — we simply read off four pieces from top to bottom. The top stroke is 一, key M; above it sits 卜, key Y; the middle piece is 中, key L; and the bottom stroke is again 一, key M once more. That gives you MYLM, with M at both ends and Y then L held in between — nicely symmetrical and easy to remember. Picture 一卜中一 stacked upright and standing straight, and you've got 正.
正.zh: 今日我哋學「正」呢個字，佢讀 zing3，又可以讀 zeng3（好似「呢個蛋糕好正」咁），意思係「正確」、「端正」，好正面嘅一個字。你望住佢，其實可以睇到頂同底都有一橫，中間夾住啲筆畫，就好似企得筆直咁。「正」係一個整體字，唔使分字首字身，我哋直接由頭到尾拆出四個部件：頭嗰橫係一，撳 M；跟住上面嗰筆係卜，撳 Y；中間係中，撳 L；最尾又係一橫一，再撳一次 M。所以成個碼就係 MYLM，兩頭都係 M、中間夾住 Y 同 L，好對稱好易記。記住佢就好似「一卜中一」由上企到落，端端正正咁排好，就係「正」喇。

此.en: Today we learn 此, read ci2, meaning "this" or "these", and also "thus" or "in this case". Look at it: on the left is 止 and on the right is 匕, and that is exactly how Cangjie splits it. The left piece 止 is a long shape, so we take only its head and tail — first the 卜 up top on the Y key, then the flat 一 below on the M key, giving YM for the left. Then comes the right piece, the 匕 body, which contributes its final code, one 匕 on the P key, so the whole character is YMP. Here is your hook: the left 止 gives head-tail YM, the right 匕 closes with P, and YMP spells 此.
此.zh: 今日我哋學「此」字，讀作 ci2，意思係「呢個」、「呢啲」，又或者係「因此」嘅意思。你望吓佢：左邊係個「止」字，右邊係個「匕」字，倉頡就係咁樣拆嘅。左邊嘅「止」字比較長，我哋淨係取佢嘅頭同尾——先係頂上嗰個「卜」，撳 Y 鍵，再係下面嗰橫「一」，撳 M 鍵，所以左邊得出 YM。跟住輪到右邊嘅「匕」，佢做字身，取尾碼一個「匕」，撳 P 鍵，全個字就砌成 YMP。記住喇：左邊個「止」取頭尾卜一（YM），右邊個匕（P）收尾，YMP 就係「此」。

步.en: Today we learn 步, read bou6, which means a step or pace, and also to walk or stroll — think of putting one foot in front of the other. This character stacks its parts top to bottom without a clean head-and-body break, so we treat it as an 整體字, an integrated character, and instead of splitting into 字首 and 字身 we just take four codes in writing order: head, second, third, tail. Reading down the shape, the little dot on top is 卜 on the Y key, then the vertical stroke through the middle is 中 on the L key, then the horizontal line is 一 on the M key, and the final sweeping strokes at the bottom are 竹 on the H key, giving you YLMH. Remember it as a walk taken step by step from top to bottom: 卜, 中, 一, 竹, and you've arrived!
步.zh: 今日我哋學「步」呢個字，讀做 bou6，就好似行路一步一步噉，意思係腳步、步伐，又或者慢慢行、散步。呢個字上下疊埋一齊，好難好清楚噉分頭尾兩橛，所以我哋當佢係「整體字」，唔硬拆做字首字身，而係順住寫嘅次序拆頭、二、三、尾四碼。你由上到下睇：最頂係一點「卜」，喺 Y 鍵；跟住係中間豎過去嘅「中」，喺 L 鍵；再落嚟一橫「一」，喺 M 鍵；最尾收筆嗰撇捺就係「竹」，喺 H 鍵，合埋就係 YLMH。記住喇：一步一步由上行到落，卜、中、一、竹，行完就到！

歷.en: Today we meet 歷, read lik6, meaning history or the past, and also to take place or to experience — as in 經歷 ging1 lik6, to go through something. Look at its shape: the sweeping 厂 M wraps around the top and left, holding a busy cluster inside. Cangjie splits this into a 字首 and a 字身: the 字首 is 厂, which takes head and tail, giving M for 厂 and then D for 木, since two 木 shapes sit beneath the cover and one stands in as the tail code. The 字身 is 止 at the bottom, which takes head, second, and tail — Y for 卜, L for 中, and M for 一 — so the whole code is MDYLM. Remember it as 厂 opening with M-D, then 止 finishing with 卜-中-一, the very 歷 in 我好鍾意讀歷史, I really like studying history.
歷.zh: 今日我哋學「歷」呢個字，讀做 lik6，意思係「歷史」、「過去」，又可以解「發生、經歷」，好似「經歷」ging1 lik6 咁。你望下佢個樣，上面同左邊係一撇一橫嘅「厂」M，包住入面一大舊嘢。倉頡拆呢個字分做字首同字身兩部分：字首係「厂」，取頭尾兩碼，就係 M（厂）加 D（木），因為厂下面藏住兩個「木」，取代表嘅木做尾碼；跟住字身係下面嘅「止」，取頭、二、尾三碼，就係 Y（卜）、L（中）、M（一），砌埋成 MDYLM。記住個口訣：厂頭木尾，止就卜中一，讀「我好鍾意讀歷史」嗰個歷，就係佢喇。

死.en: Today we're learning 死, read sei2, which means to die or to be dead — you'll see it in everyday words like 死咗 (sei2 zo2), meaning dead, and 死亡 (sei2 mong4), meaning death. Look at this character: it's a whole-character shape, one tight unit that you can't neatly split into left-and-right or top-and-bottom parts, so we use the special method Cangjie reserves for such characters — take the head, the second piece, and the very last piece, skipping whatever sits in the middle. The head is the flat horizontal stroke 一, which is M; the second piece is 乙, which is N; and the final piece is 匕, which is P, giving you MNP. So remember it as head-one, second-乙, last-匕, ignoring the middle entirely — that's how 隻魚死咗喇 (the fish has died) gets its 死.
死.zh: 我哋今日學個「死」字，讀 sei2，就係死亡、無咗生命嘅意思，好似「死咗」（sei2 zo2）或者「死亡」（sei2 mong4）都用到佢。你望住呢個字，佢係一個整體字，成個字結構連埋一齊，唔可以清楚咁分做左右或者上下，所以我哋用倉頡專門對付整體字嘅辦法：取頭、取第二個、再取最尾，跳過中間唔理。頭嗰筆係一橫「一」，撳 M；跟住第二個部件係「乙」，撳 N；最尾嗰個部件係「匕」，撳 P，合埋就係 MNP。記住呢個口訣：頭一、二乙、尾匕，中間乜都唔理，「隻魚死咗喇」就係咁樣「死」出嚟嘅。

段.en: Today's character is 段, read dyun6, meaning a section, a stretch, or a piece of something — in 地段 dei6 dyun6 it means a plot or district, and in 一段 jat1 dyun6 it's the classifier for a stretch of road or a phase of a relationship. The character splits left and right: the left part is the head (字首) and the 殳 on the right is the body (字身). A head can give at most two codes, so on the left we take only its first and last shapes, 竹 (H) and 十 (J); then the 殳 body gives its first-second-last, written as 竹 (H), 乙 (N), and 又 (E). Put together in typing order that's HJHNE. Picture it like this: 竹十 opens the road on the left, and 殳 closes it with 竹乙又 on the right, laying down one long 段 — 呢段路好長。
段.zh: 今日學嘅字係「段」，讀做 dyun6，意思係一截、一部分，好似「地段」dei6 dyun6 就係一塊土地，「一段」jat1 dyun6 就係用嚟數一節路或者一段關係嘅量詞。呢個字分做左右兩邊：左邊係字首，右邊個「殳」係字身。字首唔會拆得太碎，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，所以我哋喺左邊只攞頭同尾，就係竹（H）同十（J）；跟住右邊嘅字身「殳」就取頭二尾，寫成竹（H）、乙（N）、又（E）。合埋順住打就係 HJHNE。記住呢個畫面：左邊竹十開路，右邊「殳」由竹乙又收尾，就砌成一「段」路喇——「呢段路好長。」

母.en: Today we learn 母, read mou5, meaning mother, a female elder, or simply female. Look closely at this shape: it's all woven together into a single tangled block, so there's no clean way to split it into a left and a right, or a top and a bottom — that makes it a whole-form character (整體字). Because of that, instead of the usual first-part-plus-body split, we take three pieces in the special order head, second, and last. The head piece is 囗, which is the W key; the second piece is 卜, which is the Y key; and the last piece is the dot 丶, which is the I key — together giving you WYI. The reason we use head-second-last here, rather than pulling out a 字首 and a 字身, is precisely that the strokes are all intertwined and can't be cleanly separated. To remember it, picture Mum (W) carrying a shoulder-pole (Y) and dropping a little dot (I) — WYI; you'll meet 母 in words like 母語 (native language) and 字母 (letter of the alphabet), as in 我好愛我嘅母親, "I love my mother very much."
母.zh: 今日我哋學「母」字，讀做 mou5，即係媽媽、母親，又可以指女性長輩或者雌性嘅意思。你望吓呢個字，佢係一個交纏埋一齊嘅整體字，冇辦法好清楚咁分成左右或者上下兩橛，所以我哋唔按普通拆法，而係用「整體字」嘅取碼規則：頭、第二、同埋尾三個部分。第一個部分係「囗」，喺鍵盤上面撳 W；第二個部分係「卜」，撳 Y；最後一個部分係「丶」，撳 I，合埋就係 WYI。因為佢係一個糾纏成一體嘅字，唔可以硬拆成字首字身，所以先至用呢種頭二尾嘅方法。記住嘅時候，你可以諗成媽媽（W）擔住個擔挑（Y）行路，仲跌咗一點（I）落嚟，WYI 就記得住喇！你可以喺「母語」、「字母」呢啲詞見到佢，好似「我好愛我嘅母親」咁樣。

每.en: Today we learn 每, read mui5, meaning "every" or "each." Look at the character: on top there's a little pointed cap shape, below it sits a neat square 田 (field), and at the very end there are a couple of dots. In Cangjie we call out four pieces in order: the cap is 𠆢, which is O; the field is 田, which is W; then comes 卜, which is Y; and the final dot is 丶, which is I — giving you OWYI. Why does it break down so completely? Because 每 is a 整體字, a whole-body character that isn't split into head and body; instead you simply read straight through, taking up to four pieces from start to finish — head O, second W, third Y, tail I — and here they land exactly at four. Remember it this way: a little cap sitting over a field, finished off with a dot, OWYI in one smooth breath.
每.zh: 今日我哋學「每」字，讀做 mui5，意思係「每一個」、「每次」嘅每。你望住個字，上面有個好似人字帽咁嘅部件，跟住下面係一個方方正正嘅「田」，最尾仲有兩點。喺倉頡入面，我哋要嗌出四個部件：頭嗰個帽形係「𠆢」，撳 O；第二個係「田」，撳 W；第三個係「卜」，撳 Y；最尾嗰一點係「丶」，撳 I，所以個碼就係 OWYI。點解要拆到咁齊全？因為「每」係一個整體字，整體字唔使分字首字身，而係由頭到尾順住嗌到最多四個部件——頭 O、二 W、三 Y、尾 I，啱啱四個，剛好夠數。記住呢個口訣：帽仔戴喺田上面，尾巴一點收尾，OWYI 一氣呵成。

比.en: Today we're learning 比, read "bei2", which means to compare or to liken — the word you use when you set two things side by side, like saying one is taller than the other. Look at its shape: it's really just two identical 匕 pieces standing next to each other, one on the left and one on the right. In Cangjie the piece 匕 is typed with the key P, so this character is simply two P's, and the whole code is PP. Why does it break this way? Because 比 is a whole character (整體字) with no head-and-body division — it's made of two matching 匕 pieces, and each 匕 gives one code P, so together they make PP. Here's your hook: two 匕 side by side comparing heights, a matching pair PP is 比.
比.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「比」，讀「bei2」，意思係比較、對比，好似「你高過我」入面嘅「過」咁，係將兩樣嘢擺埋一齊比。你睇吓佢個樣，其實係兩個一模一樣嘅「匕」字並排企埋一齊，一左一右。喺倉頡入面，「匕」呢個部件係打 P 鍵，所以呢個字就係兩個 P，成個碼就係 PP。點解係咁分呢？因為「比」係一個整體字，冇字首字身之分，佢就係由兩件相同嘅「匕」砌成，每件各取一碼 P，兩件加埋就係 PP。記住喇：兩個匕並排比高低，PP 一對就係「比」。

民.en: Today we learn 民, read man4, meaning the people, citizens, or common folk — as in 人民 and 市民. When you look at it, the strokes flow together as one connected shape that's hard to cleanly split apart, so 民 counts as an integral character (整體字). For integral characters, Cangjie uses a special shortcut: instead of breaking it fully, you take just three codes — the first, the second, and the last. So you take the opening 口 as R, then the second stroke ㇗ as V, and finally the ㇂ at the end as P, giving you RVP. Remember it this way: one 口 to start, two curving strokes to finish, first-second-last, and 民 appears.
民.zh: 今日我哋學「民」呢個字，讀作 man4，即係「人民」、「市民」嘅意思，指老百姓、公民。你望住佢，成個字係一筆過連埋，好難清清楚楚咁劈開，所以佢屬於「整體字」。遇到整體字，倉頡有個特別嘅取碼方法：唔使拆到齊全，只取頭、二、尾三個碼就夠。所以「民」上面取起首個「口」，係 R 鍵，跟住取第二筆「㇗」，係 V 鍵，最後取尾嘅「㇂」，係 P 鍵，砌埋一齊就係 RVP。記住呢個口訣：一個「口」開頭，兩條彎筆收尾，頭二尾三碼，「民」就出到嚟喇。
