氣.en: Today we're learning 氣, read hei3 — it means air, gas or vapor, and it can also mean spirit or energy. Take a look at its shape: up top is a short slanting stroke 𠂉, then a curving hook 乙, and tucked in the middle is 米, which itself holds two familiar pieces, 火 (fire) and 木 (wood). This is a whole-form character — a tight, single-unit shape that doesn't split cleanly into a head and body — so instead of counting every part we follow the head-second-third-last rule for its code: the head 𠂉 is O, the second piece 乙 is N, the third piece 火 is F, and the tail piece 木 is D, while the leftover strokes in the middle are simply skipped, giving ONFD. Here's your memory hook: 氣 hides 火 (F) and 木 (D) inside it, so picture steam rising as fire burns wood — a hot puff of vapor that makes ONFD easy to remember.
氣.zh: 今日我哋學「氣」呢個字，讀作 hei3，即係空氣、氣體嗰個氣，亦都可以解精神、氣勢。你望下佢個形狀：上面係一撇短短嘅「𠂉」，跟住一劃彎彎嘅「乙」，中間夾住嘅係「米」，而「米」入面就有「火」同「木」呢兩件熟悉嘅嘢。呢個字係整體字，一個結構好緊密、拆唔開字首字身嘅字，所以我哋唔逐部分數，而係跟「頭、二、三、尾」嘅規矩取碼：頭係「𠂉」（O），第二件係「乙」（N），第三件係「火」（F），最後尾係「木」（D），中間其餘嘅筆畫就跳過唔理，砌成 ONFD。記住喇：「氣」入面收埋咗「火」（F）同「木」（D），你想像蒸氣係火燒緊木頭時冒出嚟嘅一團熱氣，咁就好易記得住喇！

水.en: Today we're learning 水, read seoi2 — it's the water you drink every day, and it can also mean liquid, lotion, or juice. Look at its shape: a vertical stroke down the middle with strokes branching off to the left and right, like water flowing and spreading apart. The lovely thing about this character is that 水 is itself a radical — a complete, self-contained shape — so there's nothing to break apart, and it's simply a single code, E. Because it stands whole on its own, there's no splitting into a lead part and a body part to worry about. Here's your hook: water matters, and one tap of E gives it to you — as in the Hong Kong place names 深水埗 and 上水, or in the sentence 我想飲杯水, 'I want to drink a glass of water.'
水.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「水」，讀作 seoi2，就係我哋日日都要飲嘅水，亦都可以指液體、乳液或者果汁。你望下佢個樣，中間一條直畫，左右兩邊各有筆畫伸出去，好似水流散開咁。呢個字最方便嘅地方，就係佢本身已經係一個部首，係一個完整嘅「整體字」，所以唔使拆開，直接就係單碼 E。因為佢係一個字就打起，冇字首字身之分，你唔會為佢煩惱點樣分割。記住呢個口訣：水好緊要，一撳 E 就有——例如「深水埗」同「上水」呢啲香港地名，「我想飲杯水」都用到佢。

永.zh: 今日我哋學「永」字，讀做 wing5，即係長長久久、永遠、恆久嘅意思，好似「永遠」（wing5 jyun5）同「永恆」（wing5 hang4）咁。你望下呢個字，佢上面有一點，中間好似個弓咁彎，下面又有水嘅影子——其實佢係一個「整體字」，冇辦法清楚拆成字首同字身兩橛。遇到整體字，我哋唔理頭尾點分，直接取頭、二、尾三碼：頭係一點「丶」，打 I；第二個字形係「弓」，打 N；最尾係「水」，打 E，合埋就係 INE。記憶鈎子：一點水滴（I）順住個弓（N）流成長流嘅水（E），水流永不停息，就係「永」。

求.en: Today's character is 求, read kau4, meaning to seek, to request, or to beseech — as in the sentence 我求你幫下我, "I beg you to help me," carrying a real note of pleading. When you look at it, the strokes seem tangled together, and it's hard to cleanly cut it into a head part and a body part, so Cangjie treats it as a whole-shape character. A whole-shape character isn't split into two halves; instead you follow the "head, second, third, last" method, picking at most four codes from across the whole shape and skipping the middle. That's why 求 takes 戈 (I), 十 (J), and 水 (E) — just three codes forming IJE — and you'll notice the middle piece is passed over precisely because whole-shape characters keep only head, second, third, and last. Remember it this way: 戈 on top, 十 at the waist, 水 at the tail, and leap right over the middle — that's 求.
求.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「求」，讀做 kau4，意思係尋求、要求、懇求，好似「我求你幫下我」咁樣，帶住一份誠懇嘅祈求。你望住呢個字，會覺得筆畫好似糾纏喺一齊，好難清楚咁切成字首同字身，呢種情況倉頡就當佢做整體字。整體字唔使分頭尾兩橛，而係跟「頭、二、三、尾」嘅辦法，喺整個字揀最多四個碼，跳過中間唔取，所以「求」就取戈（I）、十（J）、水（E），啱啱三個碼砌成 IJE。你留意到中間嗰嚿係跳過咗嘅，正正因為佢係整體字，只揀頭二三尾。記住呢個口訣：戈頂、十腰、水尾，中間一躍而過，就係「求」喇。

江.en: Today's character is 江, read gong1, meaning a large river — like the Yangzi — and it also works as a surname. Look at it: on the left is the three-drop water radical 氵, and on the right sits the piece 工. In Cangjie the head is that water radical 氵, which gives you E, and the body is 工, but you don't spell 工 out fully — you take only its tail stroke, the flat line 一, which gives M, so the whole character is simply EM. Why just the tail of 工? Because a body usually contributes at most a head-and-tail pair, and here only the final stroke is needed to represent 工, so the horizontal 一 (M) is enough. Remember it this way: water (E) flows past, and the flat line at the end (M) is 工 — together they make a river.
江.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「江」，讀 gong1，意思係大河，好似長江咁，亦都可以做姓氏。你望吓佢，左邊係三點水氵，右邊係個「工」字。喺倉頡入面，字首係三點水氵，取 E；字身係個「工」，但「工」唔係逐筆拆晒，而係取佢個尾嘅一橫一，取 M，所以成個字就係 EM 兩碼咁簡單。點解淨係取「工」個尾一橫呢？因為字身通常最多取到頭同尾兩碼，而「工」呢個位置只需要取到最後嗰筆代表就夠，所以留低一橫 M 就得。記住喇：有水（E）流過就成一條江，最尾拉平一橫（M）就係「工」。

決.en: Today we learn 決, read kyut3, meaning to decide, determine, or judge — you'll see it in words like 決定 kyut3 ding6 (to make up your mind) and 解決 gaai2 kyut3 (to solve a problem). Look at the character: on the left is the three-drops-of-water 氵, our familiar E key, serving as the head; on the right sits 夬 as the body. Because the body has many strokes, Cangjie takes only its head and tail: the head is 木 D and the tail is 大 K, giving you EDK all together. Remember it this way: water E leads, then the right side 夬 gives you head 木 and tail 大 — that's the 決 in 我決定聽日去 (I decided to go tomorrow).
決.zh: 今日我哋學「決」，讀作 kyut3，意思係決定、判斷，好似「決定」kyut3 ding6（拿定主意）同「解決」gaai2 kyut3（解決問題）咁樣用。你望吓個字，左邊係三點水「氵」，就係我哋熟悉嘅 E 鍵，做咗字首；右邊嘅「夬」就係字身。因為個字身筆畫多，倉頡取形時會取頭尾兩碼，所以「夬」嘅頭係「木」D，尾係「大」K，合埋就係 EDK。記住喇：三點水 E 開頭，右邊夬字取頭「木」尾「大」，寫落去就係「我決定聽日去」嘅決。

沒.en: Today we're learning 沒, read mut6, which means "not" or "have not," as in 沒有 (mut6 jau5), meaning to not have or to not exist; it can also mean to sink or drown, as in 淹沒 (jim1 mut6). Look at the character and you'll see it breaks into three pieces. The left side is the three-drops-of-water radical 氵, and that's the prefix, which gives you E. Then comes the body, and since a prefix only contributes one code, the body takes its head and its tail: the head is 乙, giving N, and the tail is 又, giving E again. Put them together and you get E, N, E — the code ENE. Here's your memory hook: water (E) floats an 乙 (N) and a 又 (E), and the three water drops sink down, so 沒 goes under.
沒.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「沒」，讀作 mut6，係「無」、「沒有」嘅意思，好似「沒有」（mut6 jau5）咁解作唔存在、冇；亦都可以解作沉落水，好似「淹沒」（jim1 mut6）咁。你望下呢個字，佢分成三橛。第一橛係左邊嘅三點水「氵」，呢個係字首，取 E 呢個掣。跟住就係字身，字首淨係取一個碼，字身就要取頭同尾：字身嘅頭係「乙」，取 N；字身嘅尾係「又」，又係取返 E。所以成個字砌埋就係 E、N、E，即係 ENE。記住呢個口訣：水（E）漂住一個乙（N）同一個又（E），三點水沉入水，「沒」入水底。

沙.en: Today's character is 沙, read saa1, meaning the sand or gravel you find at the beach, or a gritty, granulated texture. Look at its shape: on the left there are the three water dots 氵, and on the right sits the character 少, so you can already sense it's water-related — sand always turns up by the water. When you break it down, the head is that left-side water radical 氵, which lives on the E key; then the body is the right-side 少, and Cangjie doesn't spell out every stroke of it but takes just the first and last pieces — 小 first, which is F, and the closing slant 丿, which is H — giving you EFH. Say it like a little story: water (E) with a small (F) grain of sand slanting (H) away, and remember that both Tsim Sha Tsui 尖沙咀 and Sha Tin 沙田 use this very character, so next time you see a beach full of sand, think EFH.
沙.zh: 你今日要學嘅字係「沙」，讀作 saa1，即係海邊嗰啲一粒粒嘅沙，又或者形容嘢好幼、好粗糙咁「沙沙聲」。你望下佢個形，左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係一個「少」字，一睇就知同水有關——沙成日喺水邊出現嘛。拆碼嘅時候，字首取左邊嘅三點水「氵」，佢喺 E 鍵；跟住字身係右邊個「少」，倉頡唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取頭尾兩碼，即係頭嗰個「小」F，加上尾嗰筆撇「丿」H，合埋就係 EFH。記住呢個口訣：水（E）邊有粒小（F）沙撇（H）過去，尖沙咀同沙田都係用呢個字，你行過海邊見到成地沙，就記得 EFH 喇。

河.en: Today we learn 河, read ho4, meaning a river or stream — as in 大河 (daai6 ho4), a large river, or 西灣河 (sai1 waan1 ho2), the town of Sai Wan Ho on Hong Kong Island. Look at the character: on the left is the three-drops-of-water radical 氵, and on the right sits 可, so straight away you know it has something to do with water. When we split it, the head 氵 is taken as a whole and gives just one code, E; then the body 可 is broken up using the head-second-last rule, taking 一 (M), 乙 (N) and the final 口 (R), which builds the full code EMNR. Here's your memory hook: water (E) flows past 可, spelled M, N, R — the three water drops leading you right down to the riverbank, just like walking by the river together.
河.zh: 今日我哋學「河」呢個字，讀作 ho4，即係河流、江河嘅意思，好似「大河」（daai6 ho4）或者港島嘅「西灣河」（sai1 waan1 ho2）咁。你望住個字，左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係「可」，一睇就知同水有關。拆碼嘅時候，字首「氵」係整體字，只取一碼 E；跟住字身「可」就要拆開嚟取——依照頭、二、尾嘅規矩，取起首嘅「一」M、中間嘅「乙」N，同埋最尾嘅「口」R，所以成個字係 EMNR。記住呢個口訣：水（E）流過「可」以（M、N、R），三點水帶你行埋去河邊，就好似「我哋喺河邊行」咁自然。

油.en: The character 油 reads jau4, and it means oil, grease, or fat — the very oil you pour into the wok, or even the oil in paint. Look at its shape: on the left sit the three water dots 氵, and on the right stands 由, so from the start you can tell it has something to do with liquid. In Cangjie the left-side water radical 氵 is the head, coded E; the right-side 由 is the body, and because it is not treated as a whole-piece character it must be split first-and-last — the first piece is the central vertical 丨, coded L, and the last piece is the 田 box, coded W, giving you E, L, W together. Remember it this way: water E, then 由's head L and its tail W — three keys flowing left to right, just like oil flowing into the pan.
油.zh: 「油」讀 jau4，就係我哋炒菜嗰啲油、食油、甚至係油漆嘅油。你望下佢個樣，左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係「由」，一睇就估到同液體有關。倉頡點拆呢？左邊三點水「氵」係字首，取碼 E；右邊「由」就係字身，字身唔係整體字，所以要拆頭尾兩碼——頭係中間嗰豎「丨」，取碼 L，尾就係個「田」字，取碼 W，合埋成 ELW。記住喇：水（E）由（L 頭）田（W 尾），三筆連住讀落嚟，就係我哋落鑊嘅「油」。

治.en: Today's character is 治, read zi6, meaning to govern or regulate — you see it in 政治 zing3 zi6 (politics). Look at the character: on the left is the three-drops-of-water 氵, which you press with E; on the right sits the piece 台. Here's the key point — we don't spell out every stroke of that right-hand 台. Instead the body takes just its first and last shapes: the top 厶 gives I, and the bottom 口 gives R. So the 氵 head gives E, the 台 body gives first-last IR, and together that makes EIR. Memory hook: water 氵E flows on the left, and on the right the 台 opens with I and closes with R — easy as ordering a 三文治 sandwich.
治.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「治」，讀作 zi6，意思係管治、治理，好似「政治」zing3 zi6（政治）咁樣。你望住個字，左邊係三點水氵，喺鍵盤上面撳 E；右邊係「台」字。留意喇，右邊個「台」我哋唔會逐筆逐筆拆晒，字身取頭尾就夠：頭部係個厶，撳 I，尾部係個口，撳 R。所以字首氵取 E，字身「台」取頭尾 IR，合埋就係 EIR。記住喇：水氵E 喺左邊流，右邊個台 I 頭 R 尾，讀落好似食「三文治」saam1 man4 zi6 咁易記。

況.en: Today we learn 況, read fong3, meaning a condition or situation — the state of things, as in 情況好轉喇 (the situation is getting better). Look at the character: on the left is the three-drops-of-water 氵, typed E, and that's our head piece. The right side is the body 兄, but a body can only take three codes at most, so Cangjie uses the first-and-last shortcut: we take the head 口 R, then a middle 丿 H, then jump to the last shape 山 U, giving R, H, U. So the whole thing types in order as E, R, H, U — remember it as water beside a younger brother (兄), and you'll always have the right situation in hand.
況.zh: 今日我哋學「況」字，讀音係 fong3，解「情況、狀況」，即係事物嘅狀態，好似「情況好轉喇。」咁樣講。你望下呢個字，左邊係三點水氵，喺鍵盤打 E，佢就係我哋嘅字首。右邊嘅「兄」係字身，但係一個字身最多只可以拆三碼，所以我哋用倉頡嘅「取頭兩碼、跳去尾碼」規則：頭係口 R，中間取一個 丿 H，最後跳到尾嘅山 U，合埋就係 R、H、U。所以成個字順住打就係 E、R、H、U，記住口訣「水兄成況」，水加個兄弟，情況自然講得通。

法.en: Today we learn 法, read faat3, meaning law, rule, or regulation, and it also gives us words like 方法 (method) and 法律 (law). Look at the character: on the left is the three-drop water radical 氵, and on the right sits the character 去, and together they build 法. When Cangjie splits this, the head is the left-side water 氵 on the E key, and because it is the head it takes just one code; the body is the right-side 去, which we break into its pieces, giving 土 on the G key and 厶 on the I key, so the full code is EGI. Remember it this way: water 氵 drips down first, then 去 opens up into 土 and 厶, and a law takes shape.
法.zh: 今日我哋學「法」字，讀 faat3，即係法律、規矩嘅意思，好似「方法」同「法律」呢啲詞都用到佢。你望下個字，左邊係三點水氵，右邊係一個「去」字，成個字就係咁樣砌出嚟嘅。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，字首係左邊嘅三點水氵，喺 E 掣度，佢係字首所以淨係取一碼；跟住字身就係右邊個「去」字，我哋要拆佢入面嘅部件，取出土（G 掣）同埋厶（I 掣），所以成個碼就係 EGI。記住喇：先有水氵滴落嚟，再有一撇「去」拆成土同厶，一條法律就成形。

注.en: The character we're learning today is 注, read zyu3, meaning to concentrate or focus — as in 注意, to direct your attention onto one thing. Look at its shape: on the left is the three-drops-of-water form 氵, and on the right is 主; the water clue makes sense, because 注 originally meant to pour or pour in. When we split it, the head 氵 on the left takes just one code, E — nice and simple; then the body 主 needs its head and its tail, so we first take its topmost dot 丶, which is Y, and then its bottom part 王, which is G. Put together that gives E, Y, G — the Cangjie code EYG for 注. Here's your memory hook: water E leads, then a dot Y and a king 王 as G, and you've written the 注 of paying at·tention.
注.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「注」，讀做 zyu3，意思係集中、專注，好似「注意」咁樣，叫你將心神放喺一件事上面。你望下佢嘅樣：左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係「主」，一睇就知同水有關，因為「注」原本係倒水、灌注嘅意思。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅字首「氵」淨係取一碼 E，好簡單；跟住輪到字身「主」，字身要取頭同尾，所以先取佢個頭嗰點「丶」，係 Y，再取佢個尾「王」，係 G。合埋就係 E、Y、G，即係「注」嘅倉頡碼 EYG。記住呢個口訣：水點 E 起頭，一點 Y 加隻王 G，就寫成專「注」嘅注喇。

泰.en: Today we learn 泰, read taai3, meaning great, exalted, or secure and at peace — you see it in 泰國 (Thailand) and 安泰 (safe and healthy). Look at the top of the character: it grows out of the shape 手 (hand), so the head simply takes 手, which sits on the Q key. Then the body splits into two written pieces — the crossing shape 乂 on the K key, and the water-like 氺 underneath on the E key. Because the head takes 手 and the body hands over both 乂 and 氺, the full code is exactly QKE, no more and no less. Remember it like this: one hand (Q) makes a cross (K) and pours out water (E) — stay peaceful and 泰!
泰.zh: 今日我哋學「泰」呢個字，讀音係 taai3，意思係盛大、安穩，好似「泰國」（Thailand）同「安泰」（平安健康）咁樣用。你留意住成個字嘅上半部，其實係由「手」字變化出嚟嘅頭，所以字首就直接取「手」，喺鍵盤上係 Q。跟住落嚟落半身要拆開嚟睇：一個交叉形嘅「乂」，喺鍵盤上係 K，最後係底下嗰個似水嘅「氺」，喺鍵盤上係 E。所以「泰」嘅字首取手，字身就交足「乂」同「氺」兩件，砌埋一齊就係 QKE。記住呢個口訣：一隻手（Q）打交叉（K），再淋落水（E），泰泰平安！

洋.en:
}
Today we learn 洋, read joeng4, meaning ocean or sea, as in 海洋, and it can also mean foreign or western. Look at its shape: on the left are the three water dots 氵, and on the right stands a sheep 羊, and together they picture a vast, boundless body of water. This character splits into a head and a body: the head is the left-side 氵, which takes the key E; the body is the right-side 羊, and because it has more than three strokes we don't break it piece by piece but take its first and last shapes instead — the first is 廿 giving T, the last is 手 giving Q, so the whole code is ETQ. Remember it this way: first a drop of water E, then on a patch of grass T you spot a sheep Q, and that builds the character 洋.
洋.zh: 今日我哋學「洋」字，讀做 joeng4，解海洋，好似「海洋」呢個詞噉，亦都可以解外國嘅、西洋嘅意思。你望吓佢個形，左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係一隻羊「羊」，合埋就係無邊無際嘅大水。呢個字分做字首同字身兩橛：字首係左邊嘅「氵」，取佢個鍵 E；字身係右邊嘅「羊」，因為佢筆畫多過三畫，所以唔係逐件拆，而係用頭尾兩件——頭係「廿」取 T，尾係「手」取 Q，合埋就係 ETQ。你記住喇，先有一滴水 E，再喺一片草地 T 上面見到一隻羊 Q，就砌成成個「洋」字啦。

洪.en: Today we're learning 洪, read hung4, meaning vast or immense — and also a flood, like a great sweep of water spilling over everything. Notice it breaks into two parts: the water radical 氵 on the left, and 共 on the right. The head 氵 is one you already know well, and it lives on E. For the body 共, Cangjie has a rule that a body takes at most its first and last pieces, so we don't spell out everything in the middle — instead we grab the top 廿 on T and the bottom 金 on C, skipping what sits between. Put together that gives E, T, C — a tidy three-key code. Here's your hook: the three water dots (E) start the flood, and then 共 hands you its first and last (T, C), and out pours the 洪 water!
洪.zh: 今日我哋學「洪」呢個字，讀做 hung4，係「浩大」、「洪水」嘅意思，好似一片大水咁泛濫開嚟。你留意佢分做兩截：左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係「共」。左邊嘅字首「氵」好熟悉喇，佢喺 E 度。到右邊嘅「共」呢個字身，倉頡有個規矩，字身最多都係取頭尾兩碼，所以我哋唔會逐部分拆晒，而係取佢個頭「廿」喺 T，再取佢個尾「金」喺 C，中間嘅嘢就跳過。咁樣夾埋就係 E、T、C，讀落去啱啱好三碼。記住喇：三點水一泛就成洪水，水（E）打頭，之後「共」字頭尾一夾（T、C），洪水就嚟喇！

洲.en: Today we're learning 洲, read "zau1" in Cantonese, meaning a continent, island, or islet — it's the 洲 in 歐洲 (Europe) and 亞洲 (Asia), and it's also the 洲 in Hong Kong's own 長洲, Cheung Chau. Look at its shape: on the left is the three-drops-of-water radical 氵, and on the right is 州, so you can tell at a glance it's about water — an 洲 is land sitting in the middle of water. When we break it down, the 字首 (leading part) 氵 is simple and takes just one code, the key E; then the 字身 (body) 州 is the complex part, so we use the head-then-last-two rule, taking the head piece 戈 (I) plus the final two strokes 丨 (L) and 丨 (L), giving us EILL. Remember it like this: water beside a 州, a 戈 hugging two verticals — E-I-L-L spells 洲.
洲.zh: 今日我哋學「洲」呢個字，粵音讀「zau1」，意思係大陸、島嶼，好似「歐洲」、「亞洲」嗰個洲一樣，而香港嘅「長洲」都用呢個字。你睇吓佢個樣，左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係個「州」字，一睇就知同水有關，因為洲就係水中間嘅陸地。拆碼嘅時候，字首「氵」好簡單，只取一碼，就係鍵盤上嘅 E；跟住字身「州」係複雜嘅部分，要用「取頭二尾」嘅規則，所以取頭嗰個「戈」（I），再取埋尾二筆「丨」（L）同「丨」（L），合埋就係 EILL。記住呢個口訣：水邊一個州，戈字夾兩豎，E-I-L-L 就係「洲」。

活.en: Today we learn 活, read "wut6" as in 生活, meaning to live, to exist, or to be lively. Look at it: on the left sits the three-drop water 氵, and on the right stands 舌 ("tongue"), so the whole character is water plus tongue built side by side. To type it, the 字首 is the left-hand water 氵, coded E; then the right-hand 舌 is the 字身, and since a 字身 may take head, second, and tail codes, 舌 gives its head 竹 (H), its second piece 十 (J), and its tail 口 (R), spelling EHJR. Why split it this way? Because as the body it takes at most three codes, so we pick one part from the head, one from the middle, and one from the tail rather than every stroke. Remember it like this: water (E) flowing over a tongue — 竹, 十, 口 — and you have the 活 of 生活.
活.zh: 今日我哋學「活」呢個字，讀「wut6」，好似「生活」嘅「活」，即係生存、有生命、有活力嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係三點水氵，右邊係「舌」字，成個字就係水加舌咁砌出嚟。拆碼嘅時候，字首係左邊嘅三點水氵，取碼E；跟住右邊嘅「舌」係字身，字身可以攞頭、二、尾三碼，所以「舌」就攞頭嘅竹H、中間嘅十J、同埋尾嘅口R，合埋就係EHJR。點解「舌」要咁拆呢？因為佢做字身，最多攞三碼，於是頭、次、尾各取一個部件，唔會攞齊全部。記住個口訣：水（E）流過條舌頭，竹（H）、十（J）、口（R），生活嘅活就係咁嚟。

派.en: Today we learn 派, read paai3, meaning a school of thought, a sect, or a branch — the same 派 in a phrase like 建制派. Look at the character: on the left is the three-drop water radical 氵, which you type with E, since 氵 always maps to E. The piece on the right is 𠂢, and it serves as the body of the character; when Cangjie breaks down a body it follows the take-the-head, take-the-next, take-the-tail rule, so we work down through it in order — first the topmost rising stroke of 𠂢 gives H, then the slanting 丿 inside gives H again, and finally the closing ㄣ at the bottom gives V, so the right side yields H, H, V. Put together, the whole code is EHHV. Remember it like this: water on the left is E, and 𠂢 on the right runs from top to tail as H, H, V — that spells 派.
派.zh: 今日我哋學「派」呢個字，讀 paai3，指一個流派、宗派或者派別，好似「建制派」嗰個「派」咁。你望住個字，左邊係三點水氵，喺鍵盤上面撳 E，因為氵一貫都係取 E。右邊嗰嚿係「𠂢」，佢做字身，倉頡拆字身嗰時要跟「取頭、取次、取尾」嘅規矩，所以我哋順住上落次序，頭先取𠂢最上面嘅一橫（其實係㇀嗰個形），係 H；跟住再取𠂢入面嘅一撇丿，又係 H；最後取埋下面收尾嘅ㄣ，係 V，於是右邊就得出 H、H、V 三個碼。合埋成個字就係 EHHV。你可以記住：左邊三點水去撳 E，右邊「𠂢」由頭撇到尾，H、H、V 順住一路落，就係「派」。

流.en: Today's character is 流, read lau4, meaning to flow, to circulate, or to drift, and it can also mean a class or trend as in 流行. Look at its shape: on the left sits the three-drops-of-water radical 氵, and on the right sits one block of pieces. When Cangjie splits it, 氵 becomes the 字首, and since it's a complete recognisable radical it contributes just one code, E; the right side is the 字身, which follows the head-middle-tail rule, so you take the head 卜 (Y), the second piece 戈 (I), and the tail 山 (U). Put together that gives you the full code EYIU, with the 字身 filling its allowance of three codes exactly through 卜, 戈, and 山. To remember it, picture water (氵) flowing downhill until it reaches the mountain (山) at the very end, and that final U will stick.
流.zh: 你今日學嘅字係「流」，讀作 lau4，即係水流動、流通、飄流嘅意思，亦都可以指「流行」呢類詞。你睇睇個字：左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊即係一嚿嘢。倉頡拆字嘅時候，「氵」做字首，佢係一個成形嘅部首，淨係取一碼 E；右邊做字身，就要跟「頭、次、尾」嘅規矩拆，頭係「卜」（Y），中間第二嚿係「戈」（I），最尾一嚿係「山」（U），所以成個碼砌埋就係 EYIU。字身可以取三碼，啱啱好卜、戈、山三嚿嘟住個位。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成：水（氵）向下流，一路流到落個山（山）度，就記得結尾嗰個 U 喇。

海.en: Today we learn 海, read hoi2, meaning the sea or ocean. Look at its shape: on the left is the three-drop water radical 氵, and on the right is the character 每. When we split it, the left side 氵 becomes the head and gives us E, nice and clean. The tricky part is the body 每 on the right: Cangjie takes at most three codes from a body, so we use the first-second-last rule — from inside 每 we pick the first piece 人 (O), the next piece 田 (W), and the last piece 卜 (Y), which makes exactly three. Put it all together and you get EOWY. Think of words like 海洋 (ocean) and 上海 (Shanghai), and remember 海 this way: water (E) flowing past a person, a field, and a divining stick brings you to the sea.
海.zh: 今日我哋學「海」呢個字，讀做 hoi2，就係大海、海洋嘅意思。你望下佢個樣：左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係「每」字。分割嘅時候，左邊個「氵」做字首，取碼 E，好清楚。難就難喺右邊個「每」字身：倉頡對一個字身最多取三碼，所以我哋用「頭、次、尾」嘅方法——喺「每」入面揀最頭嘅「人」（O）、跟住嘅「田」（W）、最後嘅「卜」（Y），三粒就啱。合埋一齊就係 EOWY。你諗下「海洋」同「上海」呢啲詞，記住個海字：水（E）流過人、田、卜，就到咗大海嘞。

消.en: Today we're learning 消, read siu1, meaning to vanish, melt away, or gradually disappear — as in 消失 (siu1 sat1, disappearance) and 消費 (siu1 fai3, consumption). Look at it: on the left is the three-drops-of-water 氵, and on the right is 肖, making a left-right structure. The left 氵 is the prefix, typed with E, and as a simple prefix it gives just one code and nothing more. The right side 肖 is the body, and a compound part like this isn't spelled out in full — Cangjie takes only its first and last pieces, the little dots ⺌ on top typed with F, and the flesh-moon ⺼ underneath typed with B. So the whole character comes together as E, F, B — picture the ice cream melting away (E), leaving just the little top marks (F) sitting over the flesh below (B).
消.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「消」，讀作 siu1，意思係消失、融化、慢慢冇咗，好似「消失」（siu1 sat1）同「消費」（siu1 fai3）咁。你望吓佢，左邊係三點水氵，右邊係「肖」，一個左右結構嘅字。左邊嘅三點水氵係字首，喺鍵盤上撳 E，佢係一個簡單嘅字首，得一碼就夠。右邊「肖」係字身，一個複合嘅部件唔會全部拆晒，倉頡淨係取頭同尾兩碼：頭係上面嘅小點形⺌，撳 F，尾係下面嘅肉月⺼，撳 B。所以成個字砌埋就係 E、F、B。記住喇：水氹啲雪糕都融化消失（E）咗，剩返上邊嘅小點（F）同底下嘅肉（B）。

涌.en: Today we meet 涌, read cung1, meaning water that surges or bubbles up, gushing skyward like a spring; you'll spot it all over Hong Kong place names, such as 葵涌 kwai4 cung1 (Kwai Chung) and 鰂魚涌 zak1 jyu4 cung1. Look at the character: on the left is the three-drops water radical, and on the right sits the piece 甬. In Cangjie the water 氵 on the left becomes the head and gives E; the 甬 on the right becomes the body, and because it's a fairly full piece, it's taken by the head-second-tail rule to yield three codes — the head 弓 N, the second 戈 I, and the tail 月 B, making NIB. So typed in order the whole thing is E, N, I, B. Here's your hook: water (E) on the left, and 甬 broken into 弓-戈-月 (NIB) — a splash of water and it surges into 涌.
涌.zh: 今日我哋學「涌」字，讀作 cung1，意思係水湧上嚟、噴出嚟，好似泉水咁向上冒；喺香港啲地名度你成日見到佢，好似「葵涌」kwai4 cung1 同「鰂魚涌」zak1 jyu4 cung1。你望吓個字，左邊係三點水，右邊係「甬」呢個部件。倉頡拆嘅時候，左邊嘅氵做字首，攞 E；右邊嘅甬做字身，因為佢係一個相對複雜嘅部件，就用「取頭、二、尾」嘅辦法拆出三碼——頭係弓 N，第二個係戈 I，尾係月 B，合埋 NIB。所以成個字順住打就係 E、N、I、B。記住呢個口訣：水（E）喺左，甬字拆做弓戈月（NIB），水一湧就係「涌」。

深.en: Today we learn 深, read sam1, meaning deep, depth, or by extension deeply felt and extreme. Look at its shape: on the left is the three-drop water radical 氵, telling you it relates to water, and on the right sits a right-hand block built from three small pieces. In Cangjie the 字首 氵 gives just one code, the key E; then the 字身 uses the head-2nd-last rule, so instead of taking every piece we grab only the head 冖 (B), the second piece 八 (C), and the final piece 木 (D). That gives us EBCD, and the reason we skip along like this is simply that when a 字身 has more than three pieces we pick the three most representative ones by head, second, and last. Here's your memory hook: water (E) with a cover (B) over the splitting 八 (C) above a tree 木 (D) — dig down deep, and you've got 深.
深.zh: 我哋今日學「深」呢個字，讀作 sam1，意思係「深」、「深度」，又可以引申做「深刻」、「非常」。你望吓佢個樣，左邊係三點水嘅氵，即係同水有關；右邊嗰嚿其實由三個部件砌成。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首氵淨係取一碼，個鍵係 E；跟住輪到字身，字身要用「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼法，所以我哋唔會逐粒攞晒，只係揀開頭第一個冖（B）、第二個八（C），最後結尾嗰個木（D）。咁樣併埋就係 EBCD，因為字身部件多過三個，就用呢種「頭二尾」嘅方法揀出最有代表性嘅三粒。記住個口訣：水（E）冚住（B）八字（C）棵木（D），越挖越深，就係「深」喇！

清.en: Today we learn 清, read cing1, meaning clear, pure, or clean — as in 好清, describing something wonderfully transparent. Look at its shape: on the left are three water drops, and on the right sits 青. Start with the left piece, 氵, the three-drops-of-water radical, which lives on the E key. Then the body on the right is 青, and because it's the 字身 we don't spell it out fully — we take just its head, second, and tail pieces: the head 手 is Q, the second piece 一 is M, and the tail ⺼ is B. Typed in order that gives you EQMB. Here's your hook: pour three drops of water onto 青 and it turns clear.
清.zh: 我哋今日學「清」呢個字，讀 cing1，即係清澈、乾淨嘅意思，好似「好清」形容啲嘢好透明咁。你望下佢個樣，左邊有三點水，右邊係「青」。先睇左邊嗰個部件「氵」，即係三點水，喺鍵盤度撳 E。跟住右邊嘅字身係「青」，因為佢係字身，唔使成個字咁樣拆晒，我哋淨係取佢嘅頭、第二同埋尾三個部件——「青」個頭係「手」撳 Q，第二個部件係「一」撳 M，最尾係「⺼」撳 B。所以順住打落去就係 EQMB。記住個口訣：三點水沖住一個青，水就變清喇。

港.en: Today's character is 港, read gong2, meaning a port or harbour — it's the 港 in 香港, Hong Kong. The first thing your eye catches is the three water dots 氵 on the left, and that piece is typed with E, the head of many water-related characters. What's left on the right is the body, and Cangjie has a rule here: the body takes at most three codes, so we pick head, second, and tail — the head is 廿 on top, typed T, then the middle piece 金, typed C, and finally the bottom shape 凵, typed U, giving you ETCU altogether. To lock it in, think 'water (E) makes a harbour, then 廿 (T), 金 (C), 凵 (U) read from top down to the bottom' and the order comes naturally.
港.zh: 今日要學嘅字係「港」，讀音係 gong2，意思係海港、碼頭，同「香港」嘅「港」就係呢個字。你一眼睇落去就會見到左邊有三點水氵，呢個部件喺鍵盤上面撳 E，係好多同水有關嘅字嘅字首。餘落嘅右邊就係字身，倉頡拆碼有個規矩：字身最多取三碼，所以我哋要揀頭、二、尾三個部件——頭係上面嘅廿，撳 T，接住取中間嘅金，撳 C，最後取底部個凵形，撳 U，合埋就係 ETCU。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗住「有水（E）先有港，廿（T）金（C）凵（U）由上落到底」，咁就順住次序記到嘞。

湖.en: Look at this character: 湖, read wu4, meaning a lake — a wide body of water, as in 天鵝湖 tin1 ngo4 wu4, Swan Lake, or in place names like Hunan and Hubei. See how the left side is the three-drops-of-water 氵 and the right side is the character 胡 — one glance tells you it's tied to water. The left 氵 is the prefix, and as a single prefix piece it gives just one code, E. The right 胡 is the body, so it follows the first-second-last rule: first is 十 as J, second is 口 as R, and last is the ⺼ underneath as B, spelling out EJRB together. Picture a lake of water (氵) soaking the character 胡 beside it — four keys, EJRB, and the lake's beauty is right before you.
湖.zh: 睇下呢個字：湖，讀 wu4，意思係湖泊、大片嘅水，例如「天鵝湖」tin1 ngo4 wu4，又或者用嚟講湖南、湖北呢啲地方。你望落去，左邊係三點水氵，右邊係個「胡」字，一睇就知同水有關。左邊嘅氵係字首，佢一個部件只取一碼，就係 E，好簡單。右邊「胡」係字身，要跟頭、次、尾嘅規矩拆：頭係十揀 J，次係口揀 R，尾係下面嗰個⺼揀 B，砌埋一齊就係 EJRB。記住個畫面：一潭湖水（氵）浸住個「胡」字，四碼 EJRB，湖光山色就喺你眼前。

湘.en: Today we learn 湘, read soeng1, an old name for Hunan. Look at the character: on the left sits the three-drop water radical 氵, and on the right is the whole 相. The water radical 氵 lives on the E key, and it acts as the head of the character, taking just one code. The body is 相, and from it we take three codes: first 木 on D, then the flesh piece ⺼ on B, and finally 山 on U — so head gives one code and body gives three, spelling EDBU. Remember it this way: water (E) flowing past a tree (D), flesh (B) and a mountain (U) builds 湘.
湘.zh: 我哋今日學「湘」，讀作 soeng1，係湖南嘅別稱。你望住個字，左邊有三點水 氵，右邊係「相」字。三點水 氵喺鍵盤上取 E，佢做字首，只佔一碼。跟住個字身就係「相」，我哋喺呢個部分取三碼：先取頭木 D，再取中間嘅 ⺼ 取 B，最後取尾嘅山 U，所以字首得一碼、字身取三碼，合埋就係 EDBU。記住呢個訣竅：水（E）流過樹木（D）、肉（B）同山（U），就砌成「湘」喇。

湯.en: Today we learn 湯, most often read tong1, meaning hot water or soup — the kind of fish soup or clear broth you'd drink. Look at its shape: on the left are the three water dots, and on the right sits the piece 昜. That left-hand water radical is written 氵 and it acts as the 字首, the leading part, which you press with E. The right-hand 昜 is the 字身, the body, and following the Cangjie rule it gives up three codes — its head, middle, and tail: the head is 日 on A, the middle stroke 一 on M, and the final falling stroke 丿 on H. Why split here? Because the 字首 only ever contributes one code (氵 = E), while the 字身 is allowed three, so the right side hands over A, M, and H in full, spelling EAMH. Memory hook: water dots plus 日一丿 — a bowl of fish soup you won't forget.
湯.zh: 今日我哋學「湯」呢個字，最常讀 tong1，指熱水、湯水，好似你飲嘅魚湯、清湯咁。你睇下佢個樣：左邊有三點水，右邊係「昜」字。左邊三點水寫出嚟就係「氵」，佢係字首，喺鍵盤上面撳 E。右邊嘅「昜」係字身，我哋照倉頡取碼規矩取頭、中、尾三部分：頭係「日」撳 A，中間嗰橫「一」撳 M，最尾嗰撇「丿」撳 H。點解要咁拆？因為字首淨係取一個碼（氵＝E），字身就取到三個碼，所以右邊由頭到尾攞晒 A、M、H，合埋就係 EAMH。記住喇：三點水加「日一丿」，飲碗魚湯就記得晒。

源.en: Today we learn 源, read jyun4, meaning a spring or a source — the head of a stream — as in 資源 (zi1 jyun4) and 來源 (loi4 jyun4). Look at it: the left side is the three-drops-of-water 氵, which sits on the E key, and the right side is the body 原. Cangjie has a rule here: the radical 氵 gives just one code, E, and then the body 原 must supply the rest, so we take its head 厂 (M), then the 日 inside 白 (H), dropping the middle strokes, and finally the water piece at the bottom written as 小 (F) — giving EMHF. Remember it this way: three drops of water plus 原 is where the water begins to flow.
源.zh: 今日我哋學「源」呢個字，讀做 jyun4，即係泉水、源頭嘅意思，好似「資源」（zi1 jyun4）同「來源」（loi4 jyun4）咁樣。你睇佢左邊係三點水氵，喺鍵盤上面撳 E；右邊個「原」就係字身。倉頡拆字有規矩：字首氵只取一碼 E，跟住個字身「原」要交足碼，所以取頭嗰個厂（M），再取白字裏面嘅日（H），中間嗰啲筆畫就慳咗唔要，最後取底部個水，寫做小（F），合埋就係 EMHF。記住：三點水加原本個「原」，源頭嘅水就係咁流出嚟。

滿.en: Today we learn 滿, read mun5, meaning to fill or to be full and satisfied — you'll see it in 充滿 (cung1 mun5), meaning full of or brimming with, and in 滿足 (mun5 zuk1), meaning to satisfy or to feel content. Look at the character: on the left is the three-drops-of-water shape 氵, keyed E, and it acts as the head, telling you this word has to do with water; everything on the right is the body. That right-hand body looks crowded, and Cangjie has a rule for exactly this — when a body is complex, you take head-two-and-tail, meaning its first two pieces plus its very last one, so moving through it you pick up 廿 (T) and 中 (L), then skip straight to the final 月 (B), giving the full code ETLB. Hold that picture in mind: water (E) poured across compartments (廿, T) in the middle (中, L) of the moon-shape (月, B), each compartment brimming to the top — just like 個杯裝滿咗水, the cup filled right up with water.
滿.zh: 今日我哋學「滿」呢個字，讀做 mun5，意思係「填滿、充滿、滿足」，例如「充滿」cung1 mun5 就係好多、周圍都係嘅意思，而「滿足」mun5 zuk1 就係心滿意足、需要都被滿足咗嘅意思。你望下呢個字，左邊係三點水「氵」，倉頡碼係 E，佢就做字首，代表同水有關；右邊嗰嚿就係字身。呢個字身睇落好複雜，但係倉頡有規矩：右邊字身太複雜嘅時候，就取「頭二尾」，即係頭嗰兩個部件加埋最尾一個，所以我哋順住寫落去，攞到「廿」T、「中」L，再跳到最尾嘅「月」B，砌埋一齊個碼就係 ETLB。記住呢個畫面就得喇：水（E）淋落去一格一格（廿 T）中間（中 L）嘅月（B），一格一格都裝到滿曬——「個杯裝滿咗水」，杯就係咁樣滿起嚟嘅。

漁.en: Today we learn 漁, read jyu4, which means to fish or to catch fish, and can also be a surname. Look at its shape: on the left is the three-drops-of-water 氵, and on the right sits a whole 魚 (fish) — put water beside the fish and you get the idea of catching fish in the water. To split it, the head piece is 氵, which you press with E; then the body is the complex character 魚, and here we skip its middle and take only head-second-tail — the head 弓 is N, the second piece 田 is W, and the tail four-dots-of-fire 灬 is F, giving the full code E, N, W, F. Why skip the middle? Because when a body is this busy, Cangjie's rule is not to grab everything but to take three codes — head, second, and tail — so the code stays a tidy length. Remember it this way: a fish with water beside it is 漁, and you type ENWF, like a fishing boat pulling its catch up out of the sea.
漁.zh: 今日我哋學「漁」呢個字，讀 jyu4，意思係捕魚、打魚，同埋可以做姓氏。你望吓佢個樣，左邊係三點水氵，右邊就係一條「魚」，加埋水就講緊喺水入面捉魚喇。拆碼嘅時候，字首係三點水氵，喺鍵盤上面撳 E；跟住字身係「魚」呢個複雜嘅字，我哋要跳過中間嗰嚿，淨係取頭、二、尾三部分——頭係弓 N，第二係田 W，尾係四點火灬 F，所以成個碼就係 E、N、W、F。點解要咁跳呢？因為字身太複雜，倉頡有個規矩，就係唔攞晒中間所有嘢，而係取頭二尾三碼，等個編碼唔會太長。你記住：有水嘅「魚」就係「漁」，撳 ENWF，好似一條漁船帶住魚出水咁。

潮.en: Today's character is 潮, read ciu4. It originally means tide or the ebb and flow of water, and it also means moist or damp; in Cantonese it can even describe something as fashionable or 'trendy'. Notice it has two big parts: the three-drops-of-water 氵 on the left, and 朝 on the right. The 氵 is the head of the character, and because it's a self-contained piece it takes just one code, E. The 朝 on the right serves as the body, and a body gets broken down by first-second-last: the opening 十 is J, the second 十 is also J, and the final ⺼ is B, so the whole thing builds up to EJJB. Remember the hook: water (E) washing over two 十 crosses (J, J) and a chunk of 月-flesh (B) — when the tide comes in, it's EJJB.
潮.zh: 今日學嘅字係「潮」，讀 ciu4，本義係潮水、潮汐，亦有潮濕、濕漉漉嘅意思，喺廣東話仲可以形容嘢好時尚，好「潮」。你睇佢由兩大部分組成：左邊係三點水「氵」，右邊係「朝」。左邊嘅「氵」係字首，佢係一個獨立部件，淨係取一碼，就係 E。右邊個「朝」做字身，字身要拆碼，我哋取頭、二、尾——即係開頭嘅「十」係 J，第二個「十」又係 J，最後嘅「⺼」係 B，所以成隻字砌埋就係 EJJB。記住個口訣：水（E）浸住兩支「十」（J、J）同埋一嚿「⺼」（B），潮水一嚟就 EJJB。

澳.en: Today's character is 「澳」, read ou3, meaning an inlet or bay, a dock, or the bank of water — you'll meet it in place names like 澳門 (Macau) and 澳洲 (Australia). It has a left–right structure, so the three-drop water radical 氵 on the left is written first and becomes the 字首, keyed as E. Everything on the right forms the 字身, but Cangjie lets a body take at most three codes, so we use the head-second-tail rule: take the head 竹 (H), then the second piece ⺼ (B), then the tail 大 (K), giving EHBK all together. To remember it, picture water's edge (氵) holding bamboo (H), flesh (⺼) and something big (大) — four pieces stacked into the bay-character 澳.
澳.zh: 今日學嘅字係「澳」，讀 ou3，解作海灣、船塢或者岸邊，你喺「澳門」同「澳洲」呢啲字入面都會見到佢。呢個字係左右結構，左邊嘅三點水要先寫，佢就係字首，鍵係 E。剩低右邊嘅一大嚿當做字身，倉頡最多只能取三個碼，所以我哋用「頭、二、尾」嘅辦法：取個頭嘅竹（H），跟住取中間嘅⺼（B），最後取個尾嘅大（K），合埋就係 EHBK。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成水邊（氵）有竹（H）、有肉（⺼）、又有大（大），四嚿砌埋一齊就係海灣嘅「澳」喇。

濟.en: Look at this character: 濟, read "zai3", meaning to help or relieve, and also to ferry or cross a river. On its left sits the three-drops-of-water 氵, which you already know well — it lives on the E key. On the right is 齊, a piece with far too many strokes to spell out fully, so Cangjie takes only its top 亠, found on the Y key, and then reaches for the X difficult key to stand in for the messy tail — remember that X is not a real shape but a special code used when the end of a character is too tangled to break down. Put together, the three codes are E, Y and X. Memory hook: water helps a person across, take the little roof Y, and let X carry the hard part that follows.
濟.zh: 睇下呢個字：濟，讀「zai3」，係幫助、救濟嘅意思，亦都有渡水、過河嘅意思。佢左邊係三點水氵，你已經好熟啦，喺鍵盤上面攞E。右邊係「齊」字，呢個部分筆畫太多、太複雜，倉頡拆碼唔會逐筆咁拆晒，所以先攞佢個頭「亠」，喺Y鍵，然後就用X難鍵去代替最尾嗰啲複雜筆畫——記住X唔係一個真正嘅形，而係遇到太難拆嘅尾部時嘅特別代碼。咁樣三碼合埋就係E、Y、X。記憶鉤：三點水濟人一把（Y），剩返嘅太難就交畀X頂住。

灣.en: Today's character is 灣, read waan1, meaning a bay, cove, or bend in a stream — the same 灣 you see in Hong Kong place names like 荃灣 (Tsuen Wan) and 灣仔 (Wan Chai). Look at it: on the left is the three-drop water radical 氵, and on the right sits a big, crowded body. In Cangjie we first take the left head, 氵, which lives on the E key. Because the right-hand body is so busy, we don't spell out every stroke — instead we use the first-second-last rule, taking just three pieces: the first 女 on V, the second 火 on F, and the very last 弓 on N, giving you EVFN. To remember it, picture a girl by the water lighting a fire and drawing a bow — reading left to right, top to bottom, the shape falls right into place as EVFN.
灣.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「灣」，讀 waan1，即係海灣、河灣嗰個意思，好似荃灣、灣仔咁，都係香港人日日都見到嘅地名。你望下佢，左邊係三點水氵，右邊就係一嚿好複雜嘅字身。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，先取左邊字首氵，佢喺鍵盤上面係 E 呢個掣。右邊嗰嚿字身好大，所以我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係用「頭二尾」嘅方法，只取頭兩個同最尾一個部件：頭一個係女 V，第二個係火 F，最尾一個係弓 N，加埋就係 EVFN。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成「水邊有個女仔生火拉弓」，順住由左去右、由上落下，就自然砌出 EVFN 喇。

火.en: Today's character is 火, read fo2, meaning fire or flame, and by extension burning or even flaring up in anger. Take a good look at its shape: a vertical stroke in the middle with a dot on each side, then two strokes trailing below, so the whole thing looks like a flame flickering upward. In Cangjie this is a whole-shape character (整體字), meaning it stands as one complete form and isn't broken into separate pieces, so you simply press the single key F and the entire code is just F. Because it's treated as a whole, there's no splitting into a head and body — one flame, one key, all in a single stroke of the finger. Remember it like this: one 火, one F, quick and clean.
火.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「火」，讀作 fo2，意思就係火焰、燃燒，有時亦引申做發脾氣、火滾嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣，就好似一團火噴出嚟：中間一竪，兩邊各有一點，下面再拖住兩劃，成個字睇落就係火苗跳動嘅形態。呢個字喺倉頡入面係一個「整體字」，即係話佢本身就係一個獨立嘅字形，唔使拆開一嚿嚿，所以你淨係要撳一個 F 掣就得，成個碼就係 F。因為佢係整體字，我哋唔會再分字首字身，就好似一團火係一個整體咁，一個 F 一撳到底。記住：一團「火」，一個 F，簡單直接。

為.en: Today we learn 為, read "wai4" or "wai6", meaning to do, to handle, or to become — as in 因為 jan1 wai6 (due to) and 成為 sing4 wai4 (to become). This character is dense and busy, so Cangjie treats it as a whole character (整體字): instead of splitting it cleanly into head and body, it simply takes the head, second, third, and tail shapes from across the whole thing and skips the crowded middle. Reading it in order, it opens with the dot-and-hook 戈 (I), then 大 (K), then 弓 (N), and finally the four dots of fire 灬 written as 火 (F), giving you IKNF. So don't be scared of a busy character — Cangjie grabs the head, two inner keys, and the tail, letting the messy centre drop away: 戈 大 弓 火, and you're happy for someone.
為.zh: 今日我哋學「為」呢個字，讀「wai4」或者「wai6」，意思係「做、處理、成為」，好似「因為」jan1 wai6同「成為」sing4 wai4咁。呢個字筆畫又多又密，睇落好複雜，所以倉頡當佢係一個「整體字」嚟拆，唔會逐部分咁分頭尾，而係喺成隻字度直接揀「頭、二、三、尾」四個碼，中間嘅嘢就跳過唔理。我哋順住個字睇：開頭係一點「戈」（I），跟住寫「大」（K），再嚟係「弓」（N），最後底下四點火「灬」寫成「火」（F），砌埋就係 IKNF。記住喇，見到咁密嘅字唔使驚，倉頡只攞頭尾同中間兩個關鍵，跳過雜亂嘅中段，「為你開心」由頭到尾就係戈大弓火。

烏.en: en, read wu1, means a crow or raven — that black bird — and by extension it also means black or dark. Look at the whole shape: this is a 整體字, a whole character that doesn't cleanly break into a head-piece and a body-piece, so instead we pick codes by head, second, third, and tail. The head is the 竹 shape (the little downstroke-and-tick), typed with H; the second piece is 口, typed with R; the third piece is 卜, typed with Y; and the tail is those four dots 灬 at the bottom, which stand for 火 fire, typed with F — giving you the full code HRYF. Remember the rhythm "head, second, third, tail," and you'll never forget those four little fire-dots underneath.
烏.zh: 今日我哋學「烏」呢個字，讀作 wu1，意思係烏鴉嗰種黑色嘅雀仔，亦都可以解「黑」、「暗」。你望吓成個字，佢係一個整體字，冇辦法乾脆咁分做字首同字身兩橛，所以我哋要用取碼嘅辦法：頭、二、三、尾咁揀。首先係頭嗰筆，一撇一橫嘅「竹」形取 H；跟住第二個部分係「口」形取 R；再嚟第三個係「卜」形取 Y；最後個尾巴，就係底下四點「灬」，代表火，取 F，所以成個碼就係 HRYF。記住呢個口訣「頭二三尾」，你就唔會漏咗底下嗰四點火啦。

烤.en: Today we learn 烤, read haau1, meaning to bake, roast, or toast — the very word in 燒烤 (barbecue) and 烤雞 (roast chicken). Look at it: on the left sits the fire radical 火, and on the right is 考, so the whole character is naturally about cooking with fire. It splits into a head and a body: the head is 火 on the left, which as a head takes just one code, F; the body is 考 on the right, from which we take head, second, and last — 十 J, ナ K, and 丂 S — giving the full code FJKS. The reason 火 gives only one code is the head quota: sitting as the head, it is trimmed down to its single first piece F. Remember it this way: fire F leads off, then 考 follows with 十J ナK 丂S — the exact strokes when 我哋一齊烤肉 (we barbecue meat together).
烤.zh: 今日我哋學「烤」呢個字，讀作 haau1，即係燒、焗、烘嘅意思，好似「燒烤」同「烤雞」咁。你望吓佢，左邊係個「火」字部，右邊係個「考」字，一睇就知同用火整嘢食有關。呢個字分成字首同字身兩橛：字首係左邊嘅「火」，佢淨係取一碼 F；字身係右邊個「考」，就要拆頭二尾，即係頭一碼「十」J、第二碼「ナ」K，再加尾碼「丂」S，砌埋一齊就係 FJKS。點解「火」淨係取一碼呢？因為佢做字首，配額少啲，所以只揀第一個碼 F 就夠。記住個口訣：火 F 起頭，考字 十J ナK 丂S 收尾，「我哋一齊烤肉」就是咁樣打出嚟。

無.en: Today we're learning 無, read mou4, meaning "no, not, lacking, having none" — you'll see it in 無論 (mou4 leon6, meaning no matter what or regardless) and 無限 (mou4 haan6, meaning infinity). Take a look at this character: it's dense and busy, with a whole cluster of strokes in the middle that don't split cleanly into a head part and a body part. Because of that, Cangjie treats 無 as a whole character (整體字), and for whole characters you don't code the middle at all — you just grab three points: the head 人 (O), the second piece 廿 (T), and the tail, which is the four fire-dots 灬 that count as 火 (F), giving you OTF. Here's your memory hook: head 人, then 廿, then the four dots of fire at the bottom — skip everything in between, and 無 is simply OTF.
無.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「無」字，讀作 mou4，意思係「冇、沒有、缺乏」，好似「無論」（mou4 leon6，即係唔理點樣都好）同「無限」（mou4 haan6，即係無窮無盡）咁用。你望吓呢個字，佢筆畫多、結構密，好難清清楚楚咁分出字首同字身，所以倉頡就當佢做一個「整體字」嚟拆。整體字唔使理中間嗰堆嘢，淨係取三個位：字頭「人」（O）、第二碼「廿」（T），同埋字尾嗰四點火「灬」，正正就係「火」（F），中間全部跳過，所以碼就係 OTF。記住呢個口訣：頭「人」、二「廿」、尾底四點火，中間一律唔理，「無」就係 OTF。

然.en: Today we learn 然, read jin4, meaning something like "so, certainly" — you'll meet it in words like 然後 (then, afterwards) and 雖然 (although). Look at its shape: on the left sits 「⺼」, the flesh radical, which you type with B; on the top right is 「大」, a big person, typed K; and the four dots underneath are 「灬」, the fire base, typed F. Cangjie always reads the head first and then the body, so the standalone 「⺼」 on the left becomes the head and gives B, while everything on the right forms the body, taken top to bottom as 「大」 K then 「灬」 F — the full code is BKF. Remember it like this: a piece of flesh (B) presses down on a big (K) figure, with four little flames (F) burning below — that's 然.
然.zh: 今日我哋學「然」呢個字，讀 jin4，本身有「係咁樣、當然」嘅意思，喺「然後」、「雖然」呢啲詞都會見到。你望吓佢嘅結構：左邊係「⺼」（肉字旁嘅寫法），喺鍵盤上打 B；右上邊係一個「大」字，打 K；下面嗰四點就係「灬」（火字底），打 F。倉頡拆字先睇字首、再睇字身，所以左邊獨立嘅「⺼」做字首取 B，剩返嘅右半邊做字身，順住由上到下取「大」K 加「灬」F，全個碼就係 BKF。記住喇：一嚿肉（B）壓住一個大（K）人，下面燒緊四點火（F），咁就係「然」啦。

煲.en: Today we learn 煲, read bou1, which means to heat or to boil something in a saucepan, like when you 煲湯 make soup. Look at the shape: it's really the character 保 sitting on top, with a 火 (fire) tucked underneath. In Cangjie the top part 保 is the head, so we take its head and tail — first 火 (F), then 田 (W); then the bottom 火 is the tail of the body, and instead of the whole fire we take the reduced form it becomes, ⺼ (B), giving us the full code FWB. Picture it: fire on top (F), a field squeezed in the middle (W), and the flesh-moon beneath (B) — a pot of piping-hot soup, as fragrant as a bowl of 煲仔飯!
煲.zh: 今日我哋學「煲」字，讀做 bou1，即係用個煲嚟煮嘢、滾水或者煲湯嘅意思。你望下呢個字，其實係「保」字放上面，下面墊住一個「火」字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，上面嘅「保」係一個字首，我哋用取頭尾嘅方法，先攞個「火」（F），再攞埋個「田」（W）；跟住下面嘅「火」係字身嘅尾，唔會再攞成個火，而係取佢化出嚟嘅「⺼」（B），所以成個碼就係火田月，即係 FWB。記住個畫面：頭頂有火（F），中間夾住個田（W），底下再襯個月肉（B），一煲熱辣辣嘅湯就出嚟啦，好似「煲仔飯」咁香！

燒.en: Look at 燒, read siu1 — it means to burn, roast, or bake, the word you'd use for cooking something over fire. The character splits into a left and a right side: on the left is 火, typed with F, and on the right is the component 堯. Since 火 sits as the 字首 (the leading part), it gives only one code, so it contributes just F. The right side 堯 is the 字身 (the body), and a body can take up to three codes using the head-second-tail rule: the head is 土 (G), the second is again 土 (G), and the tail is the 凵 shape at the bottom (U), giving you the full FGGU. Remember it this way: fire burns 堯 — first F for fire, then two G's for the stacked 土 土, and finally U for the little 凵 cradling the bottom.
燒.zh: 你睇下「燒」呢個字，讀做 siu1，意思係燒、烤、烘，好似燒嘢食嗰陣咁。呢個字分做左右兩邊：左邊係「火」，喺鍵盤上打 F；右邊係一個「堯」字。左邊嘅「火」係字首，一個字首淨係取一碼，所以就得個 F。右邊嘅「堯」做字身，字身可以取三碼，我哋用「頭、次、尾」嘅法則去拆，頭係「土」（G），次又係「土」（G），尾係下面嗰個「凵」（U），合埋就係 FGGU。記住個口訣：火燒堯，先火 F，再兩土 GG，最後一個凵 U 兜住底。

營.en: Today we learn 營, read jing4, meaning an encampment or barracks, and also to manage or run something — you'll see it in 西營盤 sai1 jing4 pun4, the town Sai Ying Pun, and in 營養 jing4 joeng5, nutrition. Take a good look at its shape: two 火 sit across the top, then a 冖 cover, and beneath it two 口 mouths stacked up. When we split it, the two 火 on top form the prefix and both are taken, so you type 火 F then 火 F. Then we move to the lower body, which is 呂 with a 冖 lid, and here we take head-two-tail: the 冖 B first, then the two 口 as R and R. Put it together and you get FFBRR — 火火冖口口 — so remember it as two flames on top, a lid covering the two mouths below, and it all flows out in one go.
營.zh: 今日我哋學「營」呢個字，讀做 jing4，意思係軍營、營盤，又可以解做經營、管理，好似「西營盤」sai1 jing4 pun4 呢個地方，又或者「營養」jing4 joeng5 咁。你望吓佢個樣，上邊有兩粒火，中間夾住個冖，下底再有兩個口，砌埋一齊就係「營」喇。拆字嘅時候，上邊兩粒火做字首，兩粒都要取，所以先打火 F，再打火 F；跟住落到下身，係「呂」字上面加個冖，我哋取頭二尾，即係先取個冖 B，再取兩個口 R、R。連埋一齊就係 FFBRR，火火冖口口。記住個口訣：兩團火喺頂，冖遮住底下兩個口，火火冖口口，一氣呵成就記得住喇！

爭.en: Today we learn 爭, read zang1, meaning to dispute, fight, contend or strive — the word in 戰爭 (zin3 zang1, war) and in 爭議 (zang1 ji5, a controversy people argue back and forth over). Look at how it stacks up: at the top is a downward-clawing hand 爫, which is the key B; in the middle sits 尸, the key S; and holding up the bottom is 木, the key D. 爭 is a whole character — it doesn't break cleanly into a head part and a body part — so the rule is to take the head, the second piece, and the tail: grab the first B, the second S, then skip whatever is in the middle and jump straight to the last D, giving you BSD. Picture it as a claw B up top, a body S in the middle, and 木 D bracing the bottom — three sides all scrapping over it, and that's 爭, BSD.
爭.zh: 今日我哋學「爭」呢個字，佢讀 zang1，意思係爭奪、爭鬥、爭取，好似「戰爭」（zin3 zang1）打仗，或者「爭議」（zang1 ji5）大家你一言我一語爭論嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅結構：最頂係一隻向下抓嘅爪「爫」，喺鍵盤上係 B；中間係「尸」，係 S；最底拖住一劃嘅係「木」，係 D。「爭」係一個整體字，冇明顯拆到字首字身，所以規則要你「取頭、取二、取尾」——即係揀最頭嘅 B、第二個 S，再跳過中間唔理，直接跳到最尾嘅 D，砌成 BSD。你可以咁記：一隻爪 B 喺上面抓住，屍 S 喺中間，木 D 喺下面撐住，三方爭嚟爭去，就係「爭」BSD。

爾.en: Today we learn 爾, read ji5, an elegant old word that can mean "you" and also works as a sentence particle, and in modern Chinese it lends its sound to names and loanwords like 貝爾 (Bell) and 華爾茲 (waltz). The character is dense and tightly packed, with all its strokes crammed together, so it is a classic whole-shape character that can't be cleanly split into a head and a body — instead we use the special rule: take the first, second, third and last pieces, skipping whatever sits in the middle. Following the writing order, the top flat stroke 一 is M, then the little 小 is F, then the enclosing 冂 is B, and finally the crossing 乂 is K, giving you MFBK while the middle clutter is simply ignored. Here's your hook: when a shape is this crowded, grab "一 (M), 小 (F), 冂 (B), 乂 (K)" — first, second, third, last, and let the middle go.
爾.zh: 今日我哋學「爾」呢個字，讀做 ji5，係一個古雅嘅字，可以解「你」，又可以做語氣詞，好似「貝爾」（Bell）同「華爾茲」（waltz）咁做譯音字。呢個字筆畫多又密，冚唪唥揸埋一堆，係一個典型嘅整體字，冇辦法清楚咁分開字首同字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅特別拆法：取頭二三尾，跳過中間。你順住寫嘅次序睇落去，頭嗰筆平橫係「一」F記住係 M，接住嘅「小」係 F，再嚟個包住嘅「冂」係 B，最尾嗰個交叉「乂」係 K，中間堆嘢就唔理，砌埋就係 MFBK。記住呢句口訣：字太密就「一（M）小（F）冂（B）乂（K）」——頭二三尾，中間唔使睇，就啱晒喇。

片.en: Today we learn 片, read pin3 as in 一片, a slice, and sometimes pin2 as in 影片, a video clip that you watch every day. The word means a thin piece, a slice, a strip, like something cut off in one flat sliver. This character is a whole-character (整體字), one that doesn't break neatly into a head and a body, so instead of the usual split we simply take its shapes in writing order, one after another. You take the first 中 (L), then a second 中 (L), then the horizontal stroke 一 (M) in the middle, and finally a last 中 (L), giving you the full code LLML. Remember it as slicing bread in four strokes, straight down the line: 中, 中, 一, 中 — that's 片!
片.zh: 今日我哋學「片」呢個字，讀作 pin3，好似「一片」；有時亦都讀 pin2，好似「影片」，即係我哋日日睇嘅短片。「片」解作一薄薄嘅嘢，一塊、一條，好似切出嚟嘅一小片。呢個字係一個整體字，冇辦法好清楚咁分開字首同字身，所以我哋唔按普通嘅分法，而係一筆一筆咁順住寫落去攞碼——先攞頭嘅一個中（L），再攞第二個中（L），跟住攞中間嗰一橫，即係一（M），最後再攞尾嗰個中（L）。所以全個碼就係 LLML，四個部件順住次序咁行落去。記住喇：食一片麵包，順住四筆數，中、中、一、中，就係「片」！

牛.en: Today we're learning 牛, read ngau4 — it's the cow, the ox, the bull, the same 牛 you'd find in cow's milk. Take a good look at its shape: one horizontal stroke crossed by an upright, with two little strokes leaning out at the top like a cow poking its horns up. In Cangjie the first code is 竹 on the H key, and the second is 手 on the Q key, so the whole thing is just HQ, two codes. Why so short? Because 牛 is a whole character (整體字) — you don't break it into a head and a body; you simply follow its stroke order straight through and take the last two pieces, 竹手, and that's enough. Remember it this way: the cow lifts its head with 竹手 (H, Q), just two keys, as easy as saying 牛奶 or 牛頭角.
牛.zh: 今日我哋學「牛」呢隻字，讀做 ngau4，即係田裏面嗰隻牛，可以指公牛、母牛，牛奶嘅牛就係佢。你睇下佢個樣：一橫一豎，上邊仲斜出兩隻角，好似隻牛探個頭出嚟咁。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，第一碼係「竹」，個掣喺 H，第二碼係「手」，個掣喺 Q，全碼就係 HQ 兩碼。點解淨係兩碼咁短呢？因為「牛」係一隻整體字，成隻字唔使分字首字身，直接由頭到尾順住個筆順取碼，取到最尾兩碼「竹手」就夠喇。記住喇：牛探個頭「竹手」（H、Q），兩碼就過，好似你叫得出「牛奶」、「牛頭角」咁順口。

物.en: Today we learn 物, read mat6, meaning a thing, an object, or a living creature — you'll see it in words like 動物 (dung6 mat6, animal) and 生物 (sang1 mat6, organism). Look at how it's built: it's a left-right character, with 牛 on the left and 勿 on the right. The left 牛 is the 字首, and Cangjie takes only its first two codes, ⺧ (H) and 手 (Q). The right 勿 is the 字身, so we take first-second-last — 勹 (P), 丿 (H), and the final 丿 (H) — which is exactly 勿's own code PHH. Put it together and you get HQPHH; remember it as "two strokes of the ox, three of 勿" — H, Q, P, H, H — and 我鍾意小動物, I like small animals, will flow right off your keyboard.
物.zh: 今日我哋學「物」呢個字，讀作 mat6，即係東西、物件、生物嘅意思，好似「動物」（dung6 mat6）同「生物」（sang1 mat6）咁樣用。你望下佢嘅結構，係左右兩邊：左邊係「牛」，右邊係「勿」。左邊嘅「牛」係字首，倉頡淨係取佢頭兩碼，就係「⺧」（H）同「手」（Q）；右邊嘅「勿」係字身，按頭、二、尾嘅規矩取三碼，即係「勹」（P）、「丿」（H）同尾嘅「丿」（H），所以「勿」自己嘅碼就係 PHH。合埋一齊就係 HQPHH，記住呢個口訣：牛頭兩碼、勿身三撇，H、Q、P、H、H，「我鍾意小動物」你就寫得出啦！

特.en: Today we're learning 特, read dak6, meaning special, unique, or distinguished — as in 今日有特價, "there's a special price today." Look at its structure: on the left is the "cow" radical, which when written on the side takes the form 牜, and on the right sits 寺, a temple. Cangjie splits this into a head and a body — the head is the left-side 牜, and because it's the head it takes its first and last shapes: ⺧ is H and 手 is Q. The body is the right-side 寺, which takes head, second, and tail — 土 is G, 木 is D, and 寸 is I — giving you the full code HQGDI. Remember it this way: the little cow (HQ) walks into the temple (GDI), and that special moment builds the character 特.
特.zh: 今日我哋學「特」呢個字，讀作 dak6，即係特別、獨特嘅意思，好似「今日有特價」咁樣講。你望下佢個結構：左邊係一隻「牛」字部首，寫嘅時候變成「牜」形，右邊係「寺」字。倉頡拆碼分字首同字身兩部分——字首係左邊嘅「牜」，因為佢係字首要取多啲，所以取頭尾兩碼，即「⺧」係 H、「手」係 Q；字身係右邊嘅「寺」，取頭、次、尾三碼，就係「土」G、「木」D、同埋「寸」I。合埋一齊就係 HQGDI 五碼。記住個口訣：牛仔（HQ）行入寺廟（GDI），特別嘅一日就係咁砌成。

獨.en: Today's character is 獨, read duk6, meaning alone, single, or solitary — the feeling of being by yourself, standing on your own. Look at it: on the left sits 犭, the dog radical, and on the right sits 蜀, so the whole character splits into a head part and a body part. The head is the left 犭, which is a joined-up single piece, so we take just its first and last shapes — the first is 疒, key K, and the last is 竹, key H. The body is the right-hand 蜀, and a body can give up to three codes — head, second, and tail — so we take 田 (W) for the head, 中 (L) for the second, and 戈 (I) for the tail, giving the full code KHWLI. Here's your memory hook: dog on the left is K-H, and 蜀 on the right is W-L-I — one lone dog standing all by itself, just like 獨立 (duk6 laap6, to stand independent) or 獨特 (duk6 dak6, unique).
獨.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「獨」，讀作 duk6，即係「單獨」、「獨自」嘅意思，一個人、唔靠人嘅感覺。你望下佢，左邊係「犭」，即係反犬旁，右邊係「蜀」，成隻字分做字首同字身兩部分。字首係左邊嘅「犭」，佢係一件連筆嘅部件，所以我哋取頭尾兩碼——頭係「疒」，撳 K；尾係「撇竹」，撳 H。字身係右邊嘅「蜀」，字身可以取頭、二、尾三碼，所以頭取「田」撳 W，第二碼取「中」撳 L，最尾取「戈」撳 I，合埋成 KHWLI 五碼。記住呢個口訣：左邊反犬 KH，右邊蜀字 W-L-I，一隻獨自企喺度嘅字就砌好喇。你可以諗下「獨立」（duk6 laap6，自己企得穩）同「獨特」（duk6 dak6，與眾不同）呢兩個詞去記佢。

獲.en: Today's character is 獲, read wok6, meaning to obtain, get, or seize — you'll meet it in words like 獲得 (wok6 dak1, to obtain) and 獲取 (wok6 ceoi2, to acquire). Look at its build: on the left sits the dog radical 犭, and on the right stands the larger body 蒦, so we take the head first. The head 犭 gives K. The body then follows the first-second-last rule for three codes: the first piece is the upper grass-like shape ⺿ at H, the second is the grass top 艹 at T, and even though the bird 隹 stands in the middle, the body only has room for three codes so 隹 keeps just one, O. The final tail is 又 at E, giving the full code KHTOE. Memory hook: dog on the left (K), grass over grass (HT), one little bird (O), and a hand to grab it (E) — that's how you seize 獲.
獲.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「獲」，讀作 wok6，意思係得到、獲取，例如「獲得」（wok6 dak1，得到）同埋「獲取」（wok6 ceoi2，取得）。你望吓佢嘅結構：左邊係反犬旁犭，右邊係一個較大嘅字身蒦，所以拆碼時字首取犬旁犭，撳 K。字身部分要取頭、二、尾三碼——頭係草花頭上面嗰個⺿，撳 H；第二個係草花頭艹，撳 T；至於中間嗰隻鳥仔隹雖然企喺度，但因為字身淨係得三個位，隹只取到一碼 O；最後尾係又，撳 E，所以全碼係 KHTOE。記住呢個口訣：狗仔企左邊（K），跟住頭草二草（HT），一隻雀仔（O），最後一隻手（E）。

王.en: Today we learn 王, read wong4, meaning king or ruler, and also a very common surname — you'll see it in words like 國王 (gwok3 wong4), a king, and 王子 (wong4 zi2), a prince. Look at 王: it's a solid, self-contained block made of three horizontal strokes crossed by one vertical, standing firm on the page. Because it's a 整體字, a single-body character that can't really be pulled apart, Cangjie just takes the head and the tail: the opening stroke 一 lives on M, and the base piece 土 lives on G, giving you MG. The middle horizontal stroke gets skipped entirely — that's the head-and-tail rule for these one-piece characters. Memory hook: read from the top 一 (M) straight down to the earth 土 (G), and let the middle stroke sleep through it.
王.zh: 今日我哋學「王」字，讀作 wong4，即係國王、君主嘅意思，亦都係好常見嘅姓氏，好似「國王」（gwok3 wong4）同「王子」（wong4 zi2）呢啲詞。你望住「王」字，佢係三橫加一豎砌成嘅一個完整方塊，好結實咁企喺度。呢個係「整體字」，即係一個唔可以真正拆散嘅單體字，所以倉頡就只取頭尾兩個碼：起首嗰橫係「一」，喺 M 鍵，最尾埋腳嗰部分係「土」，喺 G 鍵，中間嗰橫就直接跳過唔取，所以整個碼就係 MG。記法好簡單：由頭一橫（M）望到落腳嘅土（G），中間嗰橫瞓覺唔理佢！

班.en: This character is 「班」, read baan1, meaning a class, a group, or a squad. Look at its shape: it's three pieces side by side — a 王 on the left, a single dot in the middle, and another 王 on the right, like two jade halves split by a blade. Cangjie takes the left 王 by its first and last, M (一) and G (土); the middle stroke is just I (點); then the right 王 takes its first and last as L (中) and G (土), giving the full code M, G, I, L, G. You might wonder why the same 王 becomes MG on the left but LG on the right — that's because the right 王 sits in the body position, where its opening key shifts to L while the tail G stays. Remember it as two 王 hugging a dot: MG—I—LG, and 班 is built.
班.zh: 呢個字係「班」，讀 baan1，即係班級、一班人嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅樣，其實係三橛砌埋一齊：左邊一個王、中間一點、右邊又一個王，好似兩塊玉夾住把刀噉分開。倉頡拆呢個字，左邊個王取頭尾 M（一）同 G（土），中間嗰一點取 I（點），右邊個王再取頭尾 L（中）同 G（土），所以全碼係 M、G、I、L、G。點解同一個王，左邊拆到 MG，右邊卻拆到 LG 呢？因為右邊個王喺字身位置，佢個尾雖然都係取，但頭改咗做 L，呢個係倉頡對字身部件嘅取碼安排。記住呢個口訣：兩個王中間夾住一點，MG—I—LG，班就砌好喇。

現.en: Today we learn 現, read jin6, meaning to appear or become visible — the character you meet in words like 發現 (to discover) and 出現 (to show up), the sense of something coming into sight. Look at it: on the left sits 王 and on the right sits 見, a clean left-right pairing, so the left is the 字首 and the right is the 字身. The left 王 breaks into 一 (M) and 土 (G), giving the 字首 MG in full. The right side 見 has its own complete code BUHU, but because it sits as the 字身 it takes only head-second-tail, three codes, so from BUHU we pull the head 月 (B), the second 山 (U), and the last 山 (U) to make BUU. Typed in order the whole character is M, G, B, U, U — think of it as 王 on the left who just discovered a pair of eyes: MG plus BUU gives you 現.
現.zh: 今日我哋學「現」呢個字，讀作 jin6，意思係「出現、顯現」，好似「發現」同「出現」咁樣用，個樣本嚟嘅嘢畀你睇到、變得明顯。你望吓個字，左邊係「王」，右邊係「見」，係一個左右並排嘅結構，所以左邊做字首、右邊做字身。左邊嘅「王」拆做一（M）同土（G），兩碼合埋就係字首 MG。右邊嘅「見」自己嘅完整碼係 BUHU，但佢企喺字身位，字身要取頭、二、尾三碼，所以喺 BUHU 入面攞頭嘅月（B）、第二嘅山（U）、同最尾嘅山（U），砌成 BUU。全個字順住打就係 M、G、B、U、U。記住喇：王喺左邊發現咗一隻眼睛，MG 加 BUU，就係「現」。

球.en: Today we learn 球, read "kau4", meaning a ball, a sphere, a globe — the same 球 you see in 地球 (dei6 kau4, the earth) and 全球 (cyun4 kau4, worldwide). Look at its shape: 王 sits on the left and 求 sits on the right, a clean left-right build. For typing we take the 王 radical first as the 字首, and since it's one component we take only the head and tail of its own code MG — that gives 王 M plus 一 G. Then the 字身 is 求, whose own code is IJE, and a 字身 takes head-second-tail, so we read across 戈 I, 十 J, 水 E. Put it together and you get MGIJE, two codes for the head and three for the body, exactly five; picture a king on the left reaching out to grab a ball on the right — a kid in the park chasing that球.
球.zh: 我哋今日學「球」呢個字，讀「kau4」，意思係波、圓球，好似「地球」（dei6 kau4，我哋住嘅地球）同「全球」（cyun4 kau4，全世界）咁樣。你望吓佢個樣：左邊係「王」，右邊係「求」，係典型嘅左右結構。倉頡入碼要先攞字首「王」，因為佢係一個部件，我哋淨係取佢自己碼MG嘅頭同尾，即係「王」M加「一」G；跟住到字身「求」，佢自己碼係IJE，字身取頭二尾，所以順住攞「戈」I、「十」J、「水」E。合埋就係MGIJE，一個字首兩碼，一個字身三碼，啱啱好五碼。記住個畫面：一個王喺左邊，右手求緊一個球——「細路喺公園踢球」，你就唔會忘記。

理.en: Today we learn 理, read lei5, meaning reason or logic, and also to manage or handle — as in 理解 (lei5 gaai2, to comprehend) and 處理 (cyu2 lei5, to deal with something). Look at it: on the left is the 王 radical, and on the right is 里. In Cangjie, both the head part and the body part are taken by their first and last shapes, so we don't write every stroke. From the 王 head we take just the top and bottom — the flat stroke 一 (M) and 土 (G); from the 里 body we again take first and last — 田 (W) and 土 (G) — giving MGWG. Here's your memory hook: 王 gives 一土, 里 gives 田土, and the character 理 comes together in a nice, logical order.
理.zh: 今日我哋學「理」呢個字，讀作 lei5，解「道理、邏輯」，又可以解「管理、處理」，例如「理解」（lei5 gaai2，明白）同「處理」（cyu2 lei5，去搞掂一件事）。你望下佢，左邊係「王」字旁，右邊係「里」字。倉頡拆字，字首同字身都係取頭尾兩碼，所以左邊嘅「王」我哋唔會逐筆打晒，只取頭尾——頭係一橫（一=M），尾係一土（土=G）；右邊嘅「里」都係取頭尾——頭係田（田=W），尾係土（土=G），合埋就係 MGWG。記住呢個口訣：王頭尾一土，里頭尾田土，「理」就好有條理噉砌返出嚟喇！

瑞.en: Today's character is 瑞, read seoi6, meaning a felicitous omen — something auspicious. You'll meet it in country names like 瑞典 (seoi6 din2, Sweden) and 瑞士 (seoi6 si6, Switzerland). Look at the shape: on the left sits the 王 radical, and on the right stands 耑, so Cangjie splits it along that clear left-right divide. The left 王 acts as the head, and a head takes just its first and last pieces — here 一 (M) at the top and 土 (G) below — while the right 耑 is the body and gives all of its parts: 山 (U), then 一 (M), then ⺼ (B). Put them together and you get MGUMB — to remember it, picture the king (王) on the left offering his first and last, and 耑 on the right handing over everything it has.
瑞.zh: 今日學嘅字係「瑞」，讀作 seoi6，意思係吉祥嘅預兆、好兆頭，好似「瑞典」（seoi6 din2，即係 Sweden）同「瑞士」（seoi6 si6，即係 Switzerland）呢啲國名都用到佢。你望吓個字，左邊係「王」字旁，右邊係「耑」字，倉頡就順住呢個左右結構嚟拆。左邊嘅「王」做字首，字首取頭尾兩碼：頭係一橫「一」（M），尾係下面嘅「土」（G）；右邊嘅「耑」做字身，逐部分拎晒出嚟，就係頂上嘅「山」（U）、中間嘅一橫「一」（M），同最底嘅「⺼」（B）。所以成個字砌埋就係 MGUMB。記住個口訣：王邊一土，耑身山一月，左取頭尾右取全，「瑞」字自然砌得出。

環.en: Today we learn 環, read waan4, which originally means a jade ring or bracelet and by extension any ring or circle. Look at how it divides into left and right: the left side is the 王 radical serving as the 字首 (head part), and the whole right side is the 字身 (body part). We don't spell out every stroke of 王 — a 字首 takes at most two codes, so we grab its head 一 (M) and its tail 土 (G); then on the right body we take the head 田 (W), the middle 中 (L), and the tail 女 (V), giving MGWLV. That head-middle-tail pattern on the right is exactly the 字身 rule, which allows more than two pieces by taking first, second, and last. Memory hook: 王 gives one-and-earth on the left, then 田-中-女 on the right — picture yourself heading to 中環 (Central) for a meal and these five keys come right back to you!
環.zh: 今日我哋學「環」呢個字，讀 waan4，本來係指玉造嘅環或者手鈪，引申做「圈」、「圓環」嘅意思。你睇佢分做左右兩橛：左邊係「王」字旁做字首，右邊嗰大橛係字身。字首「王」我哋唔會逐劃咁拆，倉頡規定字首至多取兩碼，所以我哋取佢個頭「一」（M）同埋個尾「土」（G）；跟住右邊字身，取個頭「田」（W）、中間一「中」（L）、最後個尾「女」（V），合埋就係 MGWLV。呢個「頭一尾一、中間夾」嘅取法，正正係字身可以攞多過兩碼、取頭、取次、取尾嘅規矩。記住個口訣：王邊一土，右邊田中女——你去中環食飯嗰陣，就會諗返起呢五個碼喇！

甜.en: Today we're learning 甜, read "tim4," which means sweet or sweetness — the taste of sugar. Look at it: the left side is 舌 (tongue) and the right side is 甘, so you can already sense this character is about taste. It splits into left and right: the left 舌 is the head, and rather than typing the whole thing, we take its first and last codes, 竹=H plus 口=R, giving HR; the right 甘 is the body, and it likewise takes its head 廿=T and tail 一=M, so putting it all together gives HRTM. Here's your memory hook: the tongue on the left gives HR, the 甘 on the right gives TM, and your tongue tastes something sweet — "this cake is very sweet" — and you'll remember 甜.
甜.zh: 今日我哋學「甜」呢個字，讀「tim4」，即係甜、甜味嘅意思，好似食糖嗰種味道。你望吓佢，左邊係「舌」，右邊係「甘」，一睇就知同味覺有關。呢個字分左右兩邊：左邊嘅「舌」係字首，我哋唔會成個字打晒，而係取頭尾兩碼，「竹」=H加「口」=R，即係HR；右邊嘅「甘」係字身，同樣取頭「廿」=T同尾「一」=M，所以最後拼埋就係HRTM。記法好簡單：左邊條舌取HR，右邊個甘取TM，舌頭嚐到甜——「呢個蛋糕好甜」，你就會記得「甜」喇。

生.en: Today we learn 生, read "saang1" or "sang1", meaning life, living, or birth, as in 生活 (sang1 wut6, to live one's daily life) and 發生 (faat3 sang1, for something to happen). Look at how it's built from three pieces: it opens with a downward slash 丿, which is H on your keyboard; the middle is 手 (hand), which is Q; and the very bottom is a single flat stroke 一, which is M — so the whole code is HQM. Why only these three? Because 生 is a whole-character shape with no clean head-and-body split, and in that case we take the head, the second, and the last piece — the opening 丿, then 手, then the final 一 — skipping whatever sits in the middle. Here's your hook: life (生) sprouts from a slash (H), a hand (Q) holds it up in the middle, and it settles onto one line of ground (M) — head, second, last, that's HQM.
生.zh: 今日我哋學「生」呢個字，讀「saang1」或者「sang1」，即係生命、生活、出生嘅意思，好似「生活」（sang1 wut6，即係過日子）同「發生」（faat3 sang1，即係一件事情出現）咁樣。你望吓佢由三嚿嘢砌成：起首係一撇丿，喺鍵盤上係 H；中間位置係手 Q；最尾係一橫一，就係 M，所以全個碼係 HQM。點解淨係取呢三嚿呢？因為「生」係一個整體字，冇明顯嘅字首字身分界，遇到呢種情況我哋就取頭、二、尾——即係最頭嘅丿、第二嘅手、同最尾嘅一，中間嗰啲筆畫直接跳過唔理。記住呢個口訣：生命由一撇（H）發芽，中間有隻手（Q）扶住，落地生根喺一橫（M）之上，頭二尾一齊就係 HQM。

產.en: Today's character is 產, read caan2, meaning to give birth, bring forth, or produce, as in 產生 (caan2 sang1, to arise or come into being) and 產品 (caan2 ban2, goods or merchandise). Look at the shape: on top sits a little lid made of a horizontal stroke with a dot, which is 亠 — press Y for that. Below it is the body of the character, the 字身, which we break apart into four codes taken from its head, second, third, and tail. Writing top to bottom, that gives 丿 pressed H, another 丿 pressed H, then 手 pressed Q, and finally 一 pressed M, so the full code comes out as YHHQM. The reason for this split is the Cangjie rule that the 字首 gets only one code — 亠 takes the single Y — after which the 字身 is allowed its head-2nd-3rd-tail set of four. Remember it as: one lid Y, two slants H and H, one hand Q, one line M, and 產 is built.
產.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「產」，讀作 caan2，意思係生產、出產，好似「產生」（caan2 sang1，即係出現、發生）同「產品」（caan2 ban2，即係貨物）咁。你睇睇個字，上面有一橫加一點嘅頂蓋，就係亠，喺鍵盤上面撳 Y；跟住下半部就係字身，我哋要拆佢出嚟。字身部分要取頭、二、三、尾四碼，順住寫落去就係丿撳 H、再一個丿撳 H、然後手撳 Q，最後一橫一撇收尾嘅一撳 M，所以成個字碼就係 YHHQM。點解要咁拆呢？因為倉頡規矩係字首淨係取一碼，亠佔咗個 Y，跟住字身部分先至可以取到頭二三尾四碼。記住個口訣：一頂 Y、兩撇 H H、一隻手 Q、一橫 M，「產」就砌得成喇。

用.en: Today we learn 用, read jung6, meaning to use, employ, apply, or operate — you meet it constantly in words like 使用 sai2 jung6, to make use of, and 用嚟 jung6 lai4, to use as. Look at the shape: it resembles the 月 form with an extra stroke inside, but it's really a 整體字, a whole shape whose pieces can't be cleanly separated. For characters like this, Cangjie uses a special rule: instead of breaking it into every part, you take just the first and last shapes — 月 (B) at the start and 手 (Q) at the end — giving the code BQ. That final hooked stroke is exactly the 手 form, which is why it closes the code. Remember it as a 月 frame cradling a 手 hand, and you always 用 a hand to write: B opens, Q closes.
用.zh: 今日我哋學「用」呢個字，讀作 jung6，意思係使用、應用、運作，好似「使用」sai2 jung6、「用嚟」jung6 lai4 咁樣，日日都會見到。你望住個字，會覺得佢好似一個「月」字入面加咗一撇，其實佢係一個難以清楚分開部件嘅「整體字」。遇到呢種字，倉頡有個特別規矩：唔逐部件拆，而係取頭同尾兩個碼——頭係「月」（B），尾係「手」（Q），所以個碼就係 BQ。點解係「手」呢？因為個字最尾嗰筆勾出嚟嘅形，正正就係「手」呢個字形。記住：一個「月」框住一隻「手」，寫字要「用」筆，B 開 Q 收，就係「用」喇。

田.en: Today's character is 田, read tin4, meaning a field or cultivated farmland. Look at its shape: a square frame on the outside with a cross of one horizontal and one vertical stroke inside, exactly like a plot of land divided into four sections — very easy to picture. In Cangjie, 田 is a whole-character shape (整體字): the entire form is itself a ready-made root, so you don't break it apart, and the single code W stands for all of 田. Why just one code? Because a whole-character shape is already a complete root — you take it for itself, with no need to split it into a lead part and a body. Remember it this way: when you see 田, that neat little four-square field, just press W.
田.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「田」，讀做 tin4，即係耕種嘅田地、農田嘅意思。你望下佢個形：外面一個四方框，入面有一橫一豎交叉，好似一塊分咗四格嘅田咁，畫面感十足。喺倉頡入面，「田」係一個整體字，成個形就係一個現成嘅字根，所以你唔使拆佢，一碼 W 就代表咗成個「田」。點解淨係取一碼呢？因為整體字有個特別規則：佢本身已經係一個完整字根，取自己就夠，唔使再分字首字身。記住喇：見到「田」，一格四四方方嘅田地，直接㩒 W 就得。

由.en: Today we're learning 由, read jau4, which means a cause or reason, and can also mean "from" or "starting from" — as in 由你話事, meaning it's entirely up to you to decide. Take a look at its shape: there's a single vertical stroke 丨 running straight down through the character 田 in the middle. That vertical 丨 is the first piece of the code, typed with the L key; then the whole 田 shape underneath and around it is the second piece, typed with the W key, giving you the full code LW in just two keys. Why only two? Because 由 is an integral character (整體字) — it doesn't break cleanly into a head and a body, so Cangjie handles it with a special rule that takes only the head and the tail: head 丨 (L) and tail 田 (W). Just remember one vertical stroke spearing through 田, L for the top and W for the tail, and 由 is done.
由.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「由」，讀音係 jau4，意思係原因、因由，又可以解「從……開始」，好似「由你話事」咁，即係一切都由你決定。你望吓佢個樣，其實好簡單：中間有一豎「丨」由上而下貫穿咗個「田」字。呢個「丨」就係字碼嘅第一個部件，喺鍵盤上取 L 掣；跟住落嚟成個「田」形係第二個部件，取 W 掣，所以成個碼就係 LW，兩碼收工。點解淨係得兩碼呢？因為「由」屬於「整體字」——佢冇明顯嘅字首字身之分，唔會拆到好散，倉頡對呢類字有個特別辦法，就係只取「頭」同「尾」兩碼，頭係「丨」（L），尾係「田」（W）。你只要記住：一豎「插住」個田，L 頭 W 尾，「由」就出到嚟喇。

申.en: Today we learn 申, read san1, which means to state or report something to a superior; it can also mean to extend, and it is the ninth of the earthly branches. Look at its shape: in the middle sits a 田 (field), and a single vertical stroke pierces straight through it from top to bottom, as if a pole runs right through. This is an 'integrated' character (整體字) that can't be cleanly cut into a head part and a body part, so instead we take the head, second, and tail pieces: the top vertical 丨 is L, the central 田 is W, and the bottom vertical 丨 is L again, giving you LWL. Memory hook: one long pole 丨 skewers a 田 and pokes out the bottom as 丨 — L, field, L, a stick straight through the field, and that's 申.
申.zh: 今日我哋學「申」呢個字，讀 san1，意思係向上級報告、陳述，又可以解「伸展」，佢仲係地支入面第九位。你望吓佢個樣：中間係一個「田」字，上下各有一豎穿過去，好似有嘢貫穿咁。呢個字係一個「整體字」，冇辦法乾淨俐落噉分做字首同字身兩橛，所以我哋改用「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼法，即係揀最頭、第二、同最尾三個部件——上面嗰一豎「丨」係 L，中間個「田」係 W，最底再嗰一豎「丨」又係 L，砌埋一齊就係 LWL。記憶鉤：一支長棍「丨」穿過一塊「田」再露出「丨」，L 田 L，上下都係豎，中間包住田，就係「申」。

男.en: Today we're learning 男, read naam4, which means male or a man, and can also mean son or serve as a surname. Look at its shape: on top sits a 田 (a field), and underneath sits 力 (strength), stacked one above the other. In Cangjie the top 田 is the prefix, a whole square block that gives just one code, W; then we move down to the body 力, which Cangjie does not take as a single whole piece but splits into its head and tail — the head 大 keyed K and the tail 尸 keyed S — so the body contributes two codes. Put together that gives 田 W, 大 K, 尸 S, which is WKS. Here's your hook: a man is the one putting his strength (力) to work in the field (田) — field on top, strength below, and 男 is born.
男.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「男」，讀作 naam4，意思係男性、男人，亦可以指兒子或者用作姓氏。你望下佢嘅樣：上邊係一個「田」字，下邊係一個「力」字，上下疊住一齊。喺倉頡入面，上邊嘅「田」係字首，佢係一個整體嘅方塊，只取一碼 W；跟住落到字身嘅「力」，倉頡唔會當佢係一個整碼，而係將佢拆開成頭尾兩件——頭係「大」K，尾係「尸」S，所以字身取兩碼。合埋就係田 W、大 K、尸 S，即係 WKS。記住一個畫面：田裏面出力嘅係男人，田上出力，男仔就係咁樣拆出嚟。

畀.en: Today we learn 畀, read "bei2" (sometimes bei3), meaning "to give" — as in "give me a pen," one of those everyday Cantonese words you'll type all the time. Look at its shape: on top sits a 田 (field), and below it there's one horizontal stroke and one vertical stroke. In Cangjie the 田 is typed W, the horizontal 一 is typed M, and the vertical 丨 is typed L, so together they make WML. Why just these three? Because 畀 is a whole character (整體字) — it isn't split into a head and body, so you simply read it straight through from start to finish: head W, second M, tail L, and three codes are exactly enough. Remember it this way: a field (W) rests on top, propped up by a horizontal (M) and a vertical (L) — three taps and 畀 is given to you.
畀.zh: 今日我哋學「畀」呢個字，讀「bei2」（有時讀 bei3），意思係「畀」、「給予」，好似「畀支筆我」咁樣，係廣東話日常成日用到嘅字。你望下佢嘅結構：上面係一個「田」字，跟住下面有一橫同埋一豎。喺倉頡入面，呢個「田」我哋撳 W，接住嗰橫「一」撳 M，最尾嗰豎「丨」撳 L，砌埋一齊就係 WML。點解淨係取呢三個碼呢？因為「畀」係一個整體字，整體字唔分字首字身，係由頭到尾順住攞——頭 W、第二個 M、最尾 L，啱啱三碼就夠。記住嘞：一嚿「田」坐喺上面，落嚟一橫一豎撐住佢，W、M、L 三步就打好「畀」畀你。

界.en: Today's character is 界, read gaai3, meaning a boundary or limit, or a domain — think of 新界 (san1 gaai3), the New Territories here in Hong Kong, or 世界 (sai3 gaai3), the whole wide world. Look at how it's built: on top sits 田, which is the field shape on key W, and underneath is 介. To type 界, the head takes 田 as W; then the body 介 follows the first-two-last rule, giving its first piece 人 as O, and its final two strokes 中 and 中, both on L, so the full code is WOLL. Why does 介 break into two L's? Because those little downward strokes in 介 are treated as the 中 shape in Cangjie, and since the body allows three codes here, you take the leading 人 plus the last two 中's — a neat fit. Remember it this way: a field (田) resting on 介, with a pair of little strokes below the person, together they map out the whole 世界.
界.zh: 你今日學嘅字係「界」，讀做 gaai3，意思係界線、範圍，又或者一個領域，好似「新界」（san1 gaai3）就係香港嗰一區，而「世界」（sai3 gaai3）就係我哋成個天地。你望吓佢嘅結構：上面係一個「田」字，就係田字碼 W；下面係「介」字。倉頡入呢個「界」，字首取「田」嘅 W；跟住個字身係「介」，我哋照頭二尾嘅規矩，取頭一個「人」O，再取最尾兩筆「中」同「中」，兩個都係 L，所以成個碼就係 WOLL。點解「介」下面會拆出兩個 L 呢？因為「介」中間同兩邊嗰啲短豎，喺倉頡入面就係當「中」字形處理，字身取三碼，於是頭一個「人」加尾兩個「中」，啱啱好。記住喇：一塊「田」坐喺一個「介」上面，人字之下兩支豎，就砌出成個「世界」。

留.zh: 今日我哋學「留」字，讀作 lau4，意思係停留、留低、保留，好似「留意」（要小心、留神）同埋口語嘅「留低」（唔走、留喺度）。你望下呢個字，上面係個「卯」形，下面係一個四四方方嘅「田」字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，上面呢部分做字首，我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取佢嘅頭同尾兩撇——即係兩個「丿」，都撳 H 掣，所以係 H H；跟住下面個「田」做字身，撳 W。連埋一齊就係 HHW 三個碼。記住個口訣：兩撇喺頂 H、H，一塊田喺底 W，你要留低嘅嘢，好似擺喺塊田上面咁。

當.en: Today we're learning 當, read dong1 or dong3, meaning to bear or undertake something, and also "just when" — you'll meet it in 當中 (in the middle, among) and 當我 (when I…). Take a look at the character: it stacks four pieces top to bottom, starting with the three-dot ⺌ up top, then a ⼌ cover 冖, then a mouth 口, and finally the field 田 at the bottom. In Cangjie we split it into a head and a body, where the head is that top ⺌ giving F, and everything below is the body. The body follows the head-second-last rule, taking three codes: 冖 B, 口 R, and the final 田 W — so all together it reads FBRW. To remember it, read down the tower: three dots (F), a cover (B), a mouth (R), and a field (W) — FBRW, stacked in the order your eye travels.
當.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「當」字，讀作 dong1 或者 dong3，解作承擔、擔當，又或者「就在」嘅意思，好似「當中」（喺中間）或者「當我」（當我……嘅時候）咁用。你望下呢個字，佢由上到下疊咗四層：最頂係三點嘅⺌，跟住係一個冖蓋頭，再下面係一個口，最底就係田字。倉頡分做字首同字身，字首係最頂嘅⺌，攞佢一個碼 F；跟住嘅一大嚿就係字身，字身照規矩攞「頭、二、尾」三個碼，即係冖 B、口 R、同埋最尾嘅田 W，合埋一齊就係 FBRW。記憶方法：由頭到腳讀落嚟，三點戴帽（⺌B），口食田（RW），你「當」佢一嚿嚿疊上去就記得晒。

療.en: Today's character is 療, read liu4, meaning to be healed or to recover — you'll meet it in words like 醫療 ji1 liu4, meaning medical, and 治療 zi6 liu4, to treat an illness. Look at the whole shape: on the left is the sickness radical 疒, which on the keyboard is K, a form you'll see again and again in characters about illness and health. The right-hand piece 尞 is the body, and because a body with many strokes isn't spelled out fully, we use the head-second-last rule: take its head 大, which is K, then its last two parts 金 as C and 火 as F, giving KCF. Put the head K in front of the body's KCF and the full code is KKCF. Here's your hook: the sickness roof K covers 尞, and 尞 gives its head, second, and tail KCF — treatment at the hospital that brings you back to health.
療.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「療」，讀作 liu4，意思係醫好、康復，好似「醫療」ji1 liu4 同「治療」zi6 liu4 呢啲詞都用到佢。你望吓成個字，左邊係一個病字部「疒」，呢個部件喺倉頡就係 K，一撇一點加兩點，係好多同病痛有關嘅字嘅招牌。右邊個「尞」就係字身，因為字身筆畫多，我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係用「取頭二尾」嘅辦法：取佢個頭「大」係 K，再取埋尾嗰兩個部件「金」C 同「火」F，所以字身就係 KCF。合埋字首字尾，成個「療」就係 KKCF。記住喇：病字部 K 罩住個尞，尞取頭二尾 KCF，喺醫院做治療就會康復。

發.en: Today we meet 發, read faat3, which means to issue, dispatch, or send out; you'll see it in 發現 (faat3 jin6, to notice or discover) and 發展 (faat3 zin2, development or growth). Look at how it's built from five pieces: on top is 癶 (N), then inside there's ⺆ (O), followed by 弓 (N), then 几 (H), and finally 又 (E), so the full code is NONHE. Why does it split this way? 發 is an integral character with no clean head-and-body division, and for such characters we take head-two-three-tail — the first, second, and third codes, then skip the middle to grab the very last one — giving 癶⺆弓几又. Remember it like this: 癶 leads off, 又 closes it, and you hop over the middle, and you'll type 發 with ease.
發.zh: 今日我哋學「發」呢個字，佢讀作 faat3，喺「發現」（faat3 jin6，即係察覺到、留意到）同「發展」（faat3 zin2，即係成長、擴展）呢啲詞入面都見到，意思係發出、送出。你望下呢個字，佢由五嚿嘢砌成：上面係「癶」（N），跟住入面有個「⺆」（O），再有個「弓」（N），然後係「几」（H），最尾係一個「又」（E），所以全碼就係 NONHE。點解要咁樣拆呢？因為「發」係一個整體字，冇明顯嘅字首字身之分，遇到呢類字我哋就用頭二三尾取碼，即係取頭一碼、第二碼、第三碼，再跳過中間直接取最尾嗰碼，湊夠癶⺆弓几又五碼。記住呢句口訣：癶起頭、又收尾，中間跳一跳，你就打得出「發」喇。

白.en: Today's character is 白, read baak6, meaning white — and by extension pure, clean, and bright. Take a look at its shape: there's a single throw-stroke 丿 sitting on top, and underneath it is the familiar 日 (sun) shape. This is a whole-character, so you only need two codes: first the throw-stroke 丿 on top, which lives on the H key, then the 日 below it, which is on the A key — giving you HA. Because it's treated as a whole unit, you don't break it into many little pieces; you simply follow the top-to-bottom order, stroke H plus 日 A, and you're done. Here's your memory hook: a stroke pressing down on the sun (日) covers its glare and turns it white — H then A gives you 白, the character you'll spot in words like 明白 and 白色.
白.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「白」，讀做 baak6，即係白色嘅白，代表純潔、乾淨、光亮嘅意思。你望吓佢個樣：上面有一撇 丿，下面就係一個「日」字。呢個字係一個整體字，只需要打兩個碼——先打上面嗰撇 丿，佢喺 H 鍵；再打下面嘅 日，佢喺 A 鍵，所以成個字就係 HA。因為佢係整體字，我哋唔使拆到好碎，只要順住由上到下嘅次序，撇 H 加日 A 就搞掂。記住個口訣：一撇壓住個太陽（日），太陽被撇遮住咗光就變白——H 加 A 就係「白」。你可以喺「明白」同「白色」呢啲詞入面搵到佢。

百.en: Today we learn 百, read baak3, meaning one hundred, and by extension 'many' or 'numerous'. Look at its shape: a single horizontal stroke 一 sits on top, with 日 underneath. This character is a 整體字, a whole shape — it reads as one connected unit rather than splitting neatly into two halves, so instead of taking every piece we use the first-and-last rule, coding only the very top and the very bottom. The top is 一 on the M key, and the bottom is 日 on the A key, giving you MA, just two codes. Remember it like this: one stroke plus 日 makes one hundred — handy for words like 一百 (one hundred) and 百萬 (million), as in 'This book has a hundred pages.'
百.zh: 今日我哋學「百」呢個字，讀作 baak3，即係一百嘅意思，亦都可以引申做「好多、眾多」。你望下佢嘅樣：上面有一橫「一」，下面就係「日」字。呢個字係一個「整體字」，即係話佢連成一體、唔容易清清楚楚咁一分為二，所以我哋唔逐格拆，而係採用「頭尾取碼」嘅辦法——只取最頭同最尾嘅部分。頭係「一」，喺 M 鍵；尾係「日」，喺 A 鍵，所以「百」就係 MA 兩碼。記住呢個字嘅辦法好簡單：一橫一日，就砌成一百，例如「一百」同「百萬」，一句「呢本書有一百頁」就用得着喇。

的.en: Today we learn a character you see constantly: 的, read dik1, the little possessive and adjectival particle, as in 好的, a good one. Look at it — on the left sits 白 and on the right sits 勺, and Cangjie splits it left to right along that natural seam. The left part, 白, is the 字首, so it gives head 丿 (H) and tail 日 (A); the right part, 勺, is the 字身, giving head 勹 (P) and tail 丶 (I), which is why the code reads HAPI in full. A quick hook: 白 with a 日 inside, then 勺 wrapping a single dot — H A P I — and you can spell both 目的, a goal, and 的確, indeed.
的.zh: 今日我哋學一個你日日都會見到嘅字：「的」，讀作 dik1，係最常見嘅助詞，用嚟表示「屬於」或者接喺形容詞後面，好似「好的」咁。你望下佢，左邊係「白」，右邊係「勺」，倉頡就係按呢兩個部件由左去右咁拆。字首「白」屬於複合形，取頭「丿」（H鍵）同尾「日」（A鍵）；字身「勺」都係取頭取尾，先攞外面嗰個「勹」（P鍵），再攞入面嗰點「丶」（I鍵）——所以合埋就係 HAPI 呢四碼。記住一個小口訣：白日包住一點，H A P I，「目的」同「的確」都靠佢。

皇.en: Today we learn 皇, read wong4, meaning royal or imperial — a ruler, an emperor or empress. Look at the whole shape and you'll see it stacks into two parts: the top is 白 and the bottom is 王. Cangjie caps a code at a handful of keys, so in a top-bottom character the top part gives its pieces first and the bottom finishes it off — from 白 you take 竹 (H) then 日 (A), and from 王 you take 一 (M) then 土 (G), spelling HAMG. Here's your hook: white on top, king below — the emperor wears a white face over a kingly body, and the two halves click together as 皇.
皇.zh: 今日我哋學「皇」字，讀做 wong4，即係君主、帝王嘅意思，好似皇帝、皇后咁。你望吓成個字，其實係上下兩橛砌埋一齊：上面係個「白」字，下面係個「王」字。倉頡拆字有規矩，一個字最多得五碼，所以上下結構通常上面取兩碼、下面取埋尾，於是上面「白」字取頭同尾——先係「竹」（H），跟住「日」（A）；下面「王」字亦都取頭同尾——「一」（M）同「土」（G）。合埋就係 HAMG。你記住個口訣：白喺上、王喺下，皇者白面王身，一個字咁樣就砌起。

盛.en: Today we learn 盛, read either "sing6" or "sing4," meaning abundant or flourishing, and also "to contain" or "to fill" — like a bowl heaped full to the brim. Look at the shape: on top sits 成, and underneath is the vessel radical 皿, so the whole character pictures something filled up inside a container. When you break it down, 成 is the head and, by Cangjie's rule, it gives three codes taken from its front and end: 戈 (I), 尸 (S), and 月 (B); then 皿 is the body, and since a body contributes only its final piece, it gives just 廿 (T), making the full code ISBT. Why does 成 take as many as three codes? Because as the head it gets the head's quota of two-from-the-front plus one-from-the-end, three in total, so the whole character stays within the four-code limit once the body is added. Remember it this way: 成 piled onto a 皿 vessel, filled to overflowing — that's 盛.
盛.zh: 今日我哋學「盛」字，讀「sing6」或者「sing4」，意思係豐盛、興旺，又可以解「裝載」、「盛滿」，好似成碗飯堆到滿瀉噉。你睇下呢個字，上面係「成」，下面係個「皿」字底，成個字就係喺器皿入面裝到滿滿嘅畫面。拆碼嘅時候，「成」係字首，倉頡取頭同尾兩粒共三碼：戈（I）、尸（S）、月（B）；跟住「皿」係字身，因為字身淨係取最後一粒，所以只揀個廿（T），全碼就係 ISBT。點解「成」要拆到三碼咁多？因為佢做字首，倉頡俾字首取頭兩尾一，總共三碼嘅額度，等成個字加埋字身唔會超過四碼。記住個口訣：「成」字堆滿一個皿，滿到「盛」。

監.en: Today we learn 監, read gaam1 or gaam3, meaning to supervise, control, or direct — you'll see it in 監管 gaam1 gun2, to oversee, and 監督 gaam1 duk1, to supervise. This character breaks into four pieces: first the 匚 at the top left, whose key is S; then 戈, whose key is I; next the flesh radical ⺼, whose key is B; and finally the dish shape 皿 at the bottom, whose key is T, giving the full code SIBT. Why split it this way? Because 監 is a densely packed whole-character with no clean head-and-body division, so Cangjie doesn't cut it in two — instead it reads straight through from start to finish, taking head 匚, then 戈, then ⺼, and last 皿, for four codes total. Remember it like this: start at the top-left 匚 and follow the character down — 匚, 戈, ⺼, 皿 — like a teacher standing above and watching the whole class in one sweeping glance.
監.zh: 今日我哋學「監」呢個字，讀 gaam1 或者 gaam3，意思係監視、管理、督導，好似「監管」gaam1 gun2 同「監督」gaam1 duk1 咁樣。呢個字拆做四嚿：先係左上角個「匚」，佢個鍵係 S；跟住係「戈」，個鍵係 I；再落嚟係月肉旁「⺼」，個鍵係 B；最後係底部個「皿」，個鍵係 T，所以成個碼就係 SIBT。點解要咁樣拆呢？因為「監」係一個結構複雜、冇明顯字首字身之分嘅整體字，倉頡遇到呢種字就唔會分兩截，而係從頭到尾順住取碼，取頭「匚」、二「戈」、三「⺼」、尾「皿」共四碼。記住喇：由左上角個匚開始，順住個字寫落去——匚、戈、⺼、皿，好似老師由高處監住成班學生咁，一眼睇晒。

目.en: This character is 目, read muk6, and it originally means an eye; it also extends to mean to look or see, and to a division, item, or topic. Look at its shape — it stands upright like an eye seen end-on, a neat rectangle with lines across the middle, easy to picture. When Cangjie breaks it down, because 目 is a single-body character with no obvious left-right or top-bottom parts, we follow the head-and-tail rule: we take the head 目 as B, then the tail 山 as U, giving BU. Remember it this way — one eye, BU, and you can just look and see the answer.
目.zh: 呢個字係「目」，讀muk6，本義係眼睛，亦都可以解「睇」，同埋引申做「項目」、「題目」嘅意思。你望住佢個形，就好似一隻直立嘅眼，中間有橫紋，四四方方好易記。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，因為「目」係一個獨體字，冇明顯嘅左右或者上下部件，所以我哋跟拆頭尾嘅規則：先取字頭「目」B，再取字尾「山」U，合埋就係BU。記住喇，一隻眼BU，望一望就見到答案。

直.en: Today we learn the character 直, read zik6, meaning straight, erect or vertical. Look at it: it's a compact, whole character that doesn't break into a neat left-right or top-bottom pair, so we use the whole-character method and take four pieces — the head, second, third, and last. First comes 十 at the top, on the key J; then the 月-shaped ⺼ inside, on B; and finally two horizontal 一 strokes, both living on M, so you press M twice in a row. Why split it this way? Because 直 is a whole character, we don't carve it into a big front and back part — instead we read head-second-third-last straight through, giving JBMM. Remember it as 十, 月, 一, 一: one straight stroke standing over a moon, resting on two flat lines beneath.
直.zh: 今日我哋學「直」呢個字，讀音係 zik6，意思係「直」，好似筆直、垂直咁樣。你望住佢，會發現佢係一個好完整、拆唔開得太散嘅字，所以我哋用整體字嘅方法嚟拆——取頭、二、三、尾四個部件。首先係頂上嘅「十」，喺鍵盤 J 度；跟住入面上半嘅「⺼」（月字形），喺 B 度；然後就係兩橫「一」同「一」，兩個都喺 M 度，所以你要連續㩒兩次 M。點解要咁樣拆呢？因為「直」係一個整體字，佢唔會拆成頭尾兩大截，而係直接由外到內、由上到下取頭二三尾四個位，所以碼就係 JBMM。記住喇：十、月、一一，「一枝直筆撐住個月光，底下再墊兩條橫」。

相.en: Today we learn 相, read soeng1, meaning "mutual" or "each other" — you see it in 相信 soeng1 seon3, to trust, and 相關 soeng1 gwaan1, to be related. Look at the character: there's a 木 (tree) on the left and a 目 (eye) on the right, sitting side by side. In Cangjie, the left-hand 木 is the 字首 and simply gives D. The right-hand 目 is the 字身, but we don't spell out every stroke — instead we take its head and tail: the top piece ⺼ gives B, and the bottom piece 山 gives U. The reason for this split is that the 字首 gets just one code and the 字身 takes at most three, so a tall shape like 目 is captured by grabbing its top and bottom pieces, giving us D, B, U together. Memory hook: the tree (木) looks at the eye (目), and the eye's head and tail frame its middle — tree beside eye, side by side, is 相.
相.zh: 今日我哋學「相」呢個字，讀 soeng1，解「互相、彼此」嘅意思，好似「相信」soeng1 seon3 就係信任，「相關」soeng1 gwaan1 就係有關聯。你望吓個字，左邊係一棵「木」，右邊係一個「目」字，兩部分並排。喺倉頡入面，左邊嘅木做字首，直接取 D。右邊嘅目係字身，但係我哋唔會逐劃拆晒佢，而係取頭同尾兩個部分：頭係⺼，取 B；尾係山，取 U。之所以咁拆，係因為字首只可以出一碼、字身頂多出三碼，而目呢類直長嘅字形就用「取頭尾」嘅辦法，抽起最頂同最底嘅碼件，所以合埋就係 D、B、U。記住呢個口訣：木望住目，目嘅頭尾夾住個中間，木目相對就係「相」。

真.en: Today we learn 真, read zan1, meaning real, genuine, or true — the kind of "real" in something authentic and honest.
