Look at the character: it's a tightly stacked shape with no clean way to separate a head-part from a body-part, so it counts as a 整體字, and we simply take pieces from top to bottom in stroke order. The top is 十, which is J; below it sits the little hook ⺈, which is B; then the middle horizontal stroke 一, which is M; and at the bottom is 八, which is C — giving us JBMC. Because it's a whole-character type, we ignore the usual head-and-body quota and just pull the head J, the second B, the third M, and the tail C in order. Remember it top to bottom: ten (J), hook (B), line (M), eight (C) — that's the truly "real" way to type 真!
真.zh: 我哋今日學「真」字，讀作 zan1，意思係真實、真正、貨真價實嗰種真。你望住呢個字，佢上下疊得密密麻麻，係一個「整體字」，冇得清楚咁分字首字身，所以我哋直接由上到下、順住筆順逐嚿拆。最頂係「十」，撳 J；跟住係「⺈」呢個小勾，撳 B；再落嚟係中間一橫「一」，撳 M；最後底部係「八」，撳 C，合埋就係 JBMC。因為佢係整體字，我哋唔理字首字身嘅四碼限制，只需要順住筆順取頭 J、二 B、三 M、尾 C 就得。記住個口訣：由頭到尾——十（J）、勾（B）、橫（M）、八（C），呢個先至係真嘅拆法！

睇.en: Today we learn 睇, read as tai2, which means to look at or watch something with your eyes — as in 睇電視 (watch TV) or 睇書 (read a book). Look at it: on the left sits 目, the eye radical, and on the right sits 弟 (younger brother), the two joined side by side. The left part is the 字首, so we take just its head and tail: B (目) and U (山), since a busy 字首 like this fills its quota with two codes. The right part 弟 is the 字身, and following Cangjie's head-second-tail rule we take three codes — C (丷), N (弓) and H (竹) — giving us BUCNH in all. Memory hook: use your 目 (eye) to look at your little brother 弟, and eyes-on-brother spells 睇!
睇.zh: 今日我哋學「睇」，讀音係 tai2，即係用眼睛去看嘅意思，好似「睇電視」、「睇書」咁。你望吓佢，左邊係一個「目」字，代表眼睛，右邊係「弟」字，兩件砌埋一齊。左邊嘅字首「目」我哋取頭尾兩碼，就係 B（目）同 U（山），因為呢個字首本身複雜，取到兩碼就夠。右邊嘅字身「弟」就照倉頡「頭二尾」嘅規矩，取頭、第二同尾三碼，分別係 C（丷）、N（弓）、H（竹），所以合埋成 BUCNH。記住呢句：用「目」去睇個細佬（弟），眼睛望住弟弟，就係「睇」喇！

知.en: Today's character is 「知」, read "zi1", meaning to know, to perceive, to understand — as in 「知道」 (to know) and the everyday spoken 「唔知」 (don't know). Look at the shape: on the left is 「矢」 and on the right is 「口」, and Cangjie splits it in exactly that order. The 「矢」 part is the 字首 (leading part), and a 字首 takes first-and-last, so from it we grab the first piece 人 (O) and the last piece 大 (K); then the right-side 「口」 (R) is the 字身, and a 字身 takes just one code, so 「口」 stands alone. Put together that's 人, 大, 口 — OKR. Memory hook: an arrow 「矢」 aiming at a mouth 「口」 to speak, and that's how you come to 「know」.
知.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「知」，讀「zi1」，即係知道、明白嘅意思，例如「知道」同埋口語成日講嘅「唔知」。你睇下呢個字，左邊係「矢」，右邊係「口」，倉頡就係按呢個順序拆。「矢」呢個部分做字首，字首要取頭尾兩碼，所以我哋喺佢入面攞頭嗰個「人」（O）同尾嗰個「大」（K）；跟住右邊個「口」（R）做字身，字身淨係取一碼，所以「口」就自己一個。合埋就係人、大、口，即係 OKR。記憶鈎：一支箭「矢」瞄準個「口」講嘢，你就會「知」道佢想講乜。

石.en: Today we learn 石, read sek6, meaning stone, rock, or mineral. Look at its shape: on top sits a slanted 厂, like an overhanging cliff, and tucked beneath it is a square 口, a little box. The Cangjie split is simple because 石 is treated as a whole character, so we just take the head and the tail, two codes only — the head 厂 is M and the tail 口 is R, giving you MR, clean and quick with nothing extra to worry about. Picture 鑽石山, Diamond Hill in northern Kowloon, or the sentence "there is a big rock by the road," to fix the shape in mind. Memory hook: the little cliff 厂 M leans over the mouth 口 R, and a stone appears right in front of you.
石.zh: 今日我哋學「石」呢個字，讀作 sek6，就係石頭、岩石、礦物嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅樣：上面係一個斜斜嘅「厂」字頭，好似一塊突出嚟嘅崖石，下面就攞住一個四四方方嘅「口」。倉頡拆佢好簡單，因為「石」係一個整體字，我哋直接取頭同尾兩碼——頭係「厂」M，尾係「口」R，所以碼就係 MR，乾淨俐落，唔使多諗。你可以諗吓「鑽石山」呢個九龍北面嘅地方，或者一句「路邊有塊大石」，記住呢塊石頭嘅樣。記憶鈎：崖仔「厂」M 遮住個「口」R，一塊石頭喺你面前。

研.en: Today we meet 研, read "jin4", which originally means to grind or rub — like grinding an inkstick — and by extension means to study or do research. Look at how it splits into two side-by-side parts: 石 on the left and 开 on the right. Cangjie doesn't spell out every stroke; instead it takes the first and last piece of each part. The 石 head gives its first-last pair 一 (M) and 口 (R), and the 开 body gives its first-last pair 一 (M) and 廿 (T). Read in typing order that's 一 (M), 口 (R), 一 (M), 廿 (T), or MRMT. Remember it this way: 石 hands you 一 and 口, 开 hands you 一 and 廿 — first-last from each side, and 研 is yours.
研.zh: 今日我哋學「研」呢個字，讀「jin4」，本義係磨、擦，好似研墨咁；引申開就係研究、鑽研嘅意思。你望下佢係左右兩橛：左邊係「石」，右邊係「开」。倉頡拆呢個字，唔會逐筆逐畫咁齊全咁拆，而係每一橛都取頭尾兩碼。左邊「石」做字首，取頭尾就係一（M）同口（R）；右邊「开」做字身，取頭尾就係一（M）同廿（T）。所以順住打落去就係一（M）、口（R）、一（M）、廿（T），即係 MRMT。記住呢個口訣：「石」畀你一同口，「开」畀你一同廿，兩橛各取頭尾，研究就記得住喇。

確.en: Today we'll learn 確, read kok3, meaning sure, certain, real or true — the character you use in words like 確定 and 正確. Look at it: on the left is 石 and on the right is 隺, and that's exactly where we split the head from the body. The head 石 is a 整體字, so Cangjie takes only its head and tail — 一 and 口 — giving MR; then the body 隺 is coded head-second-tail, so we take ⺈ as O, then 月 as B, and finally 土 as G, coming together as MROBG. The head being a whole-form character means it gives just two codes for its head and tail, while the body gives three for head, second and tail — that's why the full code runs to five letters. To remember it: the right side wears a little ⺈ hat over 月 and 土, and you can be sure — 確 — you'll keep it in mind.
確.zh: 今日我哋學「確」呢個字，讀作 kok3，意思係確實、肯定、真確嘅意思，好似「確定」、「正確」咁樣用。你望吓佢，左邊係個「石」字，右邊係「隺」，我哋就係咁樣分字首字身。字首「石」係一個整體字，倉頡取碼嗰陣淨係攞頭同尾，即係「一」同「口」，所以打 MR；跟住字身「隺」就照頭、二、尾嘅方法取三碼，頭係個「⺈」揀 O，中間攞「月」B，最尾「土」揀 G，合埋成 MROBG。字首整體字只取頭尾兩碼，字身就攞返頭二尾三碼，呢個就係點解成個碼係五個字母嘅原因。記住個口訣：右邊有個「⺈」頭戴住「月」同「土」，你「確」實記得住！

碼.en: Today we learn 碼, read maa5, meaning a number or numeral — the 碼 in words like 數碼 (digital, figures) and 電話號碼 (phone number). Notice it splits left and right: on the left is 石 (stone), and on the right is 馬 (horse). The left part is the head, and Cangjie takes its first and last pieces — 石 as M, then 口 as R. The right part is the body, and as a body it takes three codes: head, second, and tail — 尸 as S, 手 as Q, and the four-dot fire 灬 as tail F. So two codes from the head plus three from the body give you the full code MRSQF. Remember it this way: a chunk of stone (M, R) sitting in front of a horse (S, Q, F) builds your 'number'.
碼.zh: 今日我哋學「碼」呢個字，讀做 maa5，即係數目、號碼嗰個「碼」，好似「數碼」、「電話號碼」咁用。你留意佢係左右兩橢：左邊係個「石」字，右邊係隻「馬」字。左邊嘅字首「石」，倉頡取頭尾兩碼——先取個「石」M，再取個「口」R；右邊嘅字身「馬」就取頭、二、尾三碼——「尸」S、「手」Q，最後個尾係四點火「灬」F。所以字首兩碼加字身三碼，成個字就係 MRSQF。記住喇：一嚿石（M、R）擺喺隻馬（S、Q、F）前面，數碼就係咁樣砌出嚟。

磡.en: Today's character is 磡, read ham3, meaning a cliff, ledge, or a bank of steps — the one you'll know best in Hong Kong is 紅磡, read hung4 ham3, Hung Hom in Kowloon. The character splits left and right: 石 on the left is the head, and 甚 on the right is the body. A head is allowed only two codes, so 石 breaks into 一 (M) and 口 (R), giving MR; the body then follows the head-second-tail rule, pulling 廿 (T), 女 (V), and the final 匚 (S) from 甚 to make TVS, so the whole code is MRTVS. To remember it, picture a slab of 石 stone forming 甚 such a cliff — 磡.
磡.zh: 今日學嘅字係「磡」，讀作 ham3，意思係崖、堤岸或者石級，你喺香港最熟嘅一定係「紅磡」呢個地名，讀 hung4 ham3。呢個字左右分開，左邊嘅「石」係字首，右邊嘅「甚」係字身。字首只可以取兩碼，所以「石」拆成「一」（M）同「口」（R），得出 MR；字身就跟頭一尾嘅取碼法，喺「甚」入面攞到「廿」（T）、「女」（V）同結尾嘅「匚」（S），砌埋成 TVS，全個字就係 MRTVS。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗住一塊「石」邊，配上「甚」麼樣嘅山崖，就記得住「磡」喇。

示.en: Today we learn the character 示, read si6, meaning to show, to display, or to demonstrate for someone. Look at its shape: two horizontal strokes stacked on top, sitting above a 小 underneath. This is a whole character, so we don't split it into a big head-and-body pair — we simply take each written piece in writing order: first the top stroke 一, which is the key M; then the second top stroke 一, again M; and finally the lower 小, which is the key F, giving you the full code MMF. Remember it as two 一 on top and one 小 below — two M's holding up an F, and that's 示 showing itself to you.
示.zh: 我哋今日學「示」呢個字，讀做 si6，意思係展示、顯示、示範畀人睇。你望下佢個樣：上面有兩橫，下面托住一個「小」字。呢個字係一個整體字，我哋唔會將佢拆成字首同字身兩大嚿，而係順住寫嘅次序逐嚿攞碼——先攞上面第一橫，就係「一」，鍵係 M；跟住攞上面第二橫，又係一個「一」，一樣係 M；最後攞下面嗰個「小」，鍵係 F，所以成個碼就係 MMF。記住兩橫喺上、一小喺下，兩個 M 頂住一個 F，就係「示」畀你睇嘅樣。

社.en: Today's character is 社, read "se5" or "se6" in Cantonese. It originally meant the god of the soil and the altars where people worshipped that god, and it later grew to mean a group of families or a society — you see it in words like 社會 (se5 wui2), community, and 社區 (se5 keoi1), neighborhood. Look at its shape: 礻 sits on the left and 土 on the right, so this is a left-right character where the left part is the head and the right part is the body. The head 礻 is not typed stroke by stroke; instead we take its first and last codes, and since 礻 has the code IF, that first-last gives us 戈 (I) and 火 (F), so the head contributes IF. The body 土 needs only one code, and that single code is 土 (G), so joining them we get 戈, 火, 土, which is IFG. Memory hook: 戈-火 (IF) greet you on the left, then a scoop of 土 (G) closes it off, and 社 is built.
社.zh: 今日學嘅字係「社」，粵音讀「se5」或者「se6」，本來指土地神同拜土神嘅祭壇，引申到今日就係一羣人、一個社團、公司嘅意思，好似「社會」（se5 wui2）同「社區」（se5 keoi1）咁。你望吓佢個樣，左邊係「礻」，右邊係「土」，係一個左右分開嘅字，所以左邊做字首、右邊做字身。左邊嘅「礻」係字首，倉頡拆佢嘅時候唔會逐筆全取，而係取頭尾兩碼，「礻」自己嘅碼係 IF，頭碼係戈（I），尾碼係火（F），所以字首就攞到 IF。右邊嘅「土」係字身，字身通常只需要交少少碼，「土」淨係取一個碼 G 就夠。合埋一齊就係戈、火、土，即係 IFG。記住個口訣：左邊戈火（IF）打招呼，右邊一撮土（G）收尾，「社」就砌好啦。

神.en: Today we look at 神, read san4, meaning spirit, god, or supernatural being — it appears in words like 精神 (zing1 san4, spirit or mind) and 神聖 (san4 sing3, divine or sacred). Look at its shape: on the left is the 礻 radical, and on the right is 申, so Cangjie splits it left-to-right. The left 礻 is the head, and for this kind of shape Cangjie takes its first and last parts, giving 广 (the I key) and 火 (the F key). The right 申 is the body, and a body can yield up to three codes, so we take its first, second, and last: 中 (the L key), 田 (the W key), and 丨 (the L key). Put together that's IFLWL — remember 广火 on the left leaning against 中田丨 on the right, and the spirit stands before you.
神.zh: 我哋今日睇「神」呢個字，讀 san4，意思係神靈、神明、超自然嘅存在，好似「精神」（zing1 san4）同「神聖」（san4 sing3）都用到佢。你望吓佢個形，左邊係個「礻」部（示字旁），右邊係個「申」字，倉頡就跟住左右分開拆。左邊個「礻」做字首，倉頡教我哋喺呢種形狀度取頭尾，所以攞「广」（I 鍵）同「火」（F 鍵）兩個碼；右邊個「申」做字身，字身可以取到三個碼，於是取頭、二、尾——「中」（L 鍵）、「田」（W 鍵）、「丨」（L 鍵）。合埋就係 IFLWL，你記住左邊「广火」搭右邊「中田丨」，一個神就企喺你面前喇。

祥.en: Today's character is 祥, read coeng4, meaning good luck, a good omen, or happiness — you'll see it in words like 吉祥 (gat1 coeng4, lucky) and 發祥 (faat3 coeng4, to give rise to something good). Look at its two halves: the 礻 radical on the left and 羊 on the right, and Cangjie splits it right down that line into head and body. For the head 礻 we take first and last as usual: the top 广 (key I) and the bottom 火 (key F); for the body 羊 we again take first and last: 廿 (key T) and 手 (key Q), giving the full code IFTQ. The split falls here because a left-right character first gives up the head's first-last pieces, then the body's first-last pieces — two codes each, neat and clear. Remember it as 礻 = 广火 (IF) and 羊 = 廿手 (TQ), and the sentence 祝你吉祥, wishing you good luck, will lock it in.
祥.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「祥」，讀作 coeng4，意思係吉利、好兆頭、幸福，好似「吉祥」（gat1 coeng4，好運）同「發祥」（faat3 coeng4，發源、興起好嘅嘢）咁。你睇吓佢左邊係「礻」，右邊係「羊」，倉頡就係咁樣分成字首同字身兩橛。字首係「礻」，我哋照頭尾嘅規矩，取頭「广」（打 I）同尾「火」（打 F）；字身係「羊」，一樣取頭尾，取頭「廿」（打 T）同尾「手」（打 Q），合埋就係 IFTQ。點解咁分呢？因為左右結構嘅字，先攞晒左邊個字首嘅頭尾，再攞右邊字身嘅頭尾，各取兩碼、清清楚楚。記住一句：礻攞「广火」（IF），羊攞「廿手」（TQ），一句「祝你吉祥」就記得晒喇！

福.en: Look at this character: 福, read fuk1, meaning happiness or good fortune — a truly auspicious word. It splits left and right: the head on the left is the 示 radical, and the body on the right is 畐. For the head 示 we don't spell out every stroke; instead we take first and last — the opening dot 丶 is I and the closing 火 is F, giving just IF for the head. The body 畐 then takes its head 一 as M, its second piece 口 as R, and its tail 田 as W, so everything joins into IFMRW. Remember it like this: the 示 radical of worship carries blessings, and 畐 stacks a stroke on top, a mouth in the middle, and a field below — build it piece by piece and you have 福.
福.zh: 睇下呢個字：福，讀 fuk1，即係幸福、福氣嘅意思，係一個好有好意頭嘅字。佢分做左右兩橛：左邊嘅字首係「示」字部，右邊嘅字身係「畐」。字首「示」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取頭尾——頭一點「丶」係 I，尾嘅「火」係 F，所以字首得 IF 兩碼；字身「畐」就取頭「一」M、第二個「口」R、同埋尾「田」W，砌埋成 IFMRW。你可以咁記：拜神個「示」字帶住福氣，畐字上面一橫、中間一個口、下面一塊田，一步步就寫出福。

私.en: Today we learn 私, read si1, meaning private or personal — as in privacy, the things that belong to you alone and you don't want shared. Look at it: on the left is 禾, and on the right is 厶. In Cangjie, 禾 is the head, and a head takes at most two codes, so we take its top and its bottom: the top is the bamboo-like shape ⺮, which is H, and the bottom is 木, which is D. Then 厶 is the body, a single simple piece, so it gives just one code, I, making the full code HDI. Remember it this way: the head and tail of 禾 (⺮ and 木) plus the little 厶 to keep your secrets — H, D, I.
私.zh: 今日我哋學「私」字，讀音係 si1，解作私人、私隱嗰個「私」，即係屬於自己、唔想俾人知嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係「禾」，右邊係「厶」。倉頡入面呢個「禾」係字首，一個字首最多取兩碼，所以我哋喺佢身上揀個頭同個尾：頭係竹頭形嘅⺮，撳 H；尾係木字底，撳 D。跟住「厶」係字身，得一件嘢，就淨係取佢自己一碼 I，合埋成 HDI。記住個口訣：禾嘅頭尾（⺮木）加個厶尾，私隱要收埋，就係 H、D、I。

科.en: Today's character is 科, read fo1, meaning a section or department, and by extension science — as in 科學, science itself. Look at it: 禾 stands on the left and 斗 sits on the right, so it clearly divides into a head part and a body part. The head 禾 takes its first and last shapes: the first is 竹 on the H key, and the last is 木 on the D key, giving you HD. The body 斗 also takes first and last: the first is 卜 on the Y key and the last is 十 on the J key, giving you YJ — so the whole thing reads HDYJ. Picture a stalk of grain (HD) beside a measuring dipper (YJ), together measuring out knowledge, and 科 will stay with you.
科.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「科」，讀作 fo1，即係「部門」或者「科學」嘅意思，好似「科學」呢個詞噉樣。你望吓佢，左邊係「禾」，右邊係「斗」，一望就知係一個左右分開嘅字，所以要拆成字首同字身兩部分。字首「禾」要取頭尾兩碼：頭係「竹」，個鍵係 H，尾係「木」，個鍵係 D，合埋就係 HD；字身「斗」都係取頭尾，頭係「卜」，個鍵係 Y，尾係「十」，個鍵係 J，合埋就係 YJ。成個字順住打落去就係 HDYJ，你可以記住：禾苗（HD）旁邊擺住個量米嘅斗（YJ），一齊組成量度知識嘅「科」。

移.en: Today we learn 移, read ji4, meaning to shift or move about — as in 移動 ji4 dung6 (to move) and 移民 ji4 man4 (to migrate). Look at its shape: on the left is 禾, and on the right two 夕 stacked one above the other. For splitting, the head is the left 禾, a complete piece on its own, so we take its first and last codes — the opening 禾 H and the closing 木 D — giving the head HD. The body is the two 夕 on the right, and since a body may yield up to three codes, we take head-second-last: the first 夕 N, the little dot 丶 I inside, and the final 夕 N, spelling NIN — so the whole code is HDNIN. Remember it this way: one stalk of grain 禾 (HD) with two 夕 (NIN) beside it, and everything gets moved along.
移.zh: 今日我哋學「移」呢個字，讀 ji4，意思係搬動、移位，好似「移動」ji4 dung6、「移民」ji4 man4 咁。你望下佢個樣，左邊係「禾」，右邊係兩個「夕」上下疊埋。拆字嘅時候，字首係左邊嘅「禾」，因為佢係一個完整部件，我哋取佢嘅頭尾兩碼，即係頭嗰筆「禾」H 同尾嗰筆「木」D，所以字首係 HD。跟住嘅字身係右邊兩個「夕」，字身可以取到三碼，所以我哋用頭二尾嘅取碼法，第一個「夕」N、佢入面嗰點「丶」I、再加最尾嗰個「夕」N，砌埋就係 NIN，全字碼係 HDNIN。記住呢個字：一棵「禾」HD，加兩個「夕」NIN 喺右邊，就係搬嚟搬去嘅「移」啦。

程.en: Today we're learning 程, read cing4, meaning a journey or itinerary, and also a schedule or a course of study — you'll meet it in words like 過程 (a process) and 課程 (an academic course). Look at it: it splits left and right, with 禾 on the left and 呈 on the right. The left 禾 is the 字首, and the rule is that a 字首 only ever gives its head and tail, so from 禾's own code HD we take the head 木 H and the tail 木 D. The right 呈 is the 字身, which is allowed up to three codes taken as head, middle and tail, so from 呈's own code RHG we take the head 口 R, the middle 丿 H, and the tail 土 G. Put them together and you get HDRHG — remember it as 禾's two woods (HD) leading, then 呈's mouth-slash-earth (RHG) following behind.
程.zh: 我哋今日學嘅係「程」呢個字，讀作 cing4，解作旅程、行程，又可以指日程或者課程，好似「過程」同「課程」呢兩個詞咁。你望下佢，係左右兩橛砌成嘅：左邊係「禾」，右邊係「呈」。左邊嘅「禾」係一個字首，按倉頡取碼規矩，字首淨係攞頭尾兩碼，「禾」自己嘅碼係 HD，頭係木 H、尾係木 D，所以左邊就出咗木 H、木 D 兩碼。右邊嘅「呈」係字身，字身可以攞三碼，取頭、二、尾，「呈」自己嘅碼係 RHG，於是取頭係口 R、第二係丿 H、尾係土 G。合埋一齊就係 HDRHG。記住個口訣：禾攞頭尾木木（HD），呈攞頭二尾口丿土（RHG），拼成「程」。

種.en: Today we learn 種, which reads either zung2 or zung3, and it means a seed, a kind or breed, or the verb to plant — like when you say 呢種花好靚, this kind of flower is pretty. Look at it: on the left is the grain radical 禾, and on the right is the character 重, so we split it into a 字首 and a 字身. The 字首 禾 is a standalone piece, so we follow the usual rule and take just its head and tail — the first code 竹 (H) and the last code 木 (D). The 字身 重 is a taller piece, so we take three codes from it: the head 丿 (H), then 十 (J), and finally the tail 土 (G), giving us HDHJG all together. Remember it as 禾 gives head-and-tail, and 重 marches top to bottom in three pieces — keep that order and you won't muddle them.
種.zh: 今日我哋學「種」呢個字，佢讀「zung2」或者「zung3」，意思係種子、品種，又或者係動詞「去種植」，好似你講「呢種花好靚」嗰個「種」咁。你望吓佢，左邊係個禾木旁「禾」，右邊係個「重」字，所以我哋分做字首同字身兩橛。字首「禾」係一個獨立部件，我哋照倉頡取碼規矩取頭同尾兩碼，即係頭一碼竹（H）、尾一碼木（D）。至於字身「重」呢個部件比較長，我哋一連取三碼——頭係一撇丿（H）、中間係個十（J）、最尾係個土（G），砌埋一齊就係 HDHJG。記住個口訣：「禾竹木、重丿十土」，禾字旁定咗頭尾，重字順住由上到落攞晒三橛，你就唔會撈亂喇。

稱.en: Today we learn 稱, read "cing1" or "cing3", meaning to call, to name, or a title — the way you address or name a person or thing. Notice it splits into left and right: the left is the 字首 禾, and the right is the 字身 爯. Because 禾 is a whole-shape character (整體字), Cangjie takes only its first and last codes, giving 竹 (H) and 木 (D); the 字身 爯 is more built-up, so it takes head, second, and tail — the head 爫 (B), then 土 (G), and the tail 冂 (B), for the full code HDBGB. Remember it like this: a stalk of grain (HD) with a hand 爫 above cradling earth inside a frame — that's the 稱 in "to call someone by name."
稱.zh: 今日我哋學「稱」呢個字，佢讀「cing1」或者「cing3」，意思係叫、稱呼、名號，好似大家點樣叫一個人或者一件嘢咁。你留意佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係字首「禾」，右邊係字身「爯」。字首「禾」係一個整體字，倉頡淨係取頭尾兩碼，所以攞竹（H）同木（D）；跟住字身「爯」比較複雜，就要取頭、次、尾三碼，個頭係爫（B），中間係土（G），最尾係冂（B），合埋就係 HDBGB。你可以記住：一棵禾（HD）之上，有隻手爫捧住土同一個框，就係「稱呼」個「稱」。

究.en: Today we're learning 究, read gau3, meaning to examine, investigate, or look deeply into something. Look at it: the top is the 穴 head, and underneath sits 九. In Cangjie, both the head part and the body part take codes, so from the 穴 head we take its first and last shapes — the roof 宀 (J) and the 八 (C) below it; then from the 九 body we again take first and last, giving 大 (K) and 乙 (N), so the whole thing is JCKN. Picture a hole (穴) at the top with 九 tucked underneath — when you investigate something, you dig right down to the bottom!
究.zh: 今日我哋學「究」呢個字，讀音係 gau3，意思係研究、探究、深入去查一件事。你望下佢，上面係個「穴」字頭，下面係個「九」字。倉頡入面，字首同字身各自都要取碼，個穴字頭我哋取頭尾兩碼，就係最頂嘅寶蓋「宀」（J）加下面嘅「八」（C）；字身「九」都係取頭尾，得出「大」（K）同「乙」（N），所以成個字拼埋就係 JCKN。記住上面係個窿（穴），下面藏住個「九」，你研究乜嘢都要挖到底先得㗎！

空.en: This character is 空, read hung1, meaning empty, hollow, bare or deserted — the same 空 in 天空 tin1 hung1, the sky, and 空間 hung1 gaan1, dimensions or space. Look at it: the top part is 穴 and the bottom part is 工. When Cangjie splits it, the top 穴 is the head, and since a head takes at most three codes, first-last is enough here, so we take the first piece 宀 (J) and the last piece 八 (C); the bottom 工 is the body, and a body contributes just one code, so we take 一 (M). Put them together and you get JCM — J, C, M, and to remember it, picture a roof with a little 八 moustache and one flat stroke closing the bottom, leaving nothing but empty space inside.
空.zh: 呢個字係「空」，讀做 hung1，意思係空、無嘢、空曠，好似「天空」tin1 hung1 個天，又或者「空間」hung1 gaan1 咁樣講一個範圍。你望落去，成個字上面係「穴」，下面係「工」。倉頡拆呢個字嗰陣，上面嘅「穴」係字首，字首最多取三碼，但取頭尾就夠，所以攞頭嘅宀（J）同尾嘅八（C）；下面嘅「工」係字身，字身淨係補一碼，就淨攞一（M）。所以連埋一齊就係 JCM——J、C、M，記住：一個「穴」開頭嘅屋頂加把八字鬚，下面一橫收尾，格仔入面就空空如也。

立.en: Today we learn 立, read laap6, meaning to stand, to establish, or to set up. Look at the shape: there is a 亠 sitting on top, and the rest of the body beneath it. 立 is a whole-form character (整體字), so instead of chopping it into many pieces front and back, we simply take two codes — the head piece 亠, which lives on the Y key, and the tail, which we take as T. That gives you the full code Y then T. Here is your memory hook: put on the little 亠 hat (Y), then plant your feet firmly with a T — and you're standing tall!
立.zh: 今日我哋學「立」呢個字，讀作 laap6，即係「企立」、「建立」嘅意思，代表站立、樹立、設立。你望住佢：上面有個「亠」，下面就係成個字身。「立」係一個整體字，唔會好似普通字咁前後拆好多件，所以我哋只取兩碼——頭嗰件係「亠」，喺鍵盤上係 Y；尾嗰件我哋取 T。所以整個「立」就係 Y、T 兩個碼。記住呢個口訣：頭戴一頂「亠」帽子（Y），企定定咁 T 一 T，你就企得住喇！

站.en: Today's character is 站, read "zaam6", meaning to stand up, or a station or stand. Look at how it divides into a left part 立 and a right part 占. The left piece 立 is the head, and rather than taking every stroke we take its head and tail: the head 卜 sits on Y, and the tail 廿 sits on T. Then we jump to the right body 占, again taking head and tail — the top is another 卜 on Y, and the bottom is 口 on R — so the whole code comes together as YTYR. Remember it this way: 立 stands up on the left (Y, T) while 占 holds its spot on the right (Y, R), and you're standing firm at the station.
站.zh: 我哋今日學「站」呢個字，讀「zaam6」，即係企起身、又或者車站嘅「站」。你睇下佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係「立」，右邊係「占」。「立」呢個字首，我哋唔會逐筆取，而係取頭尾——頭係「卜」，喺Y鍵，尾係「廿」，喺T鍵。跳去右邊嘅「占」做字身，同樣取頭尾——上面又係一個「卜」，即Y，下面係「口」，喺R鍵，所以成個碼砌埋就係YTYR。記住喇：左邊立起身（Y、T），右邊占住個位（Y、R），你就企穩喺個車站度喇。

第.en: Today's character is 第, read dai6, and it's the word you use to put things in order — 第一 dai6 jat1 means first or foremost, and 第二 dai6 ji6 means second or next. Look at its shape: a bamboo cap ⺮ sits on top, and underneath is the character 弟 (younger brother). We split it into a 字首 and a 字身: the 字首 is the bamboo top ⺮, which gives H — nice and easy. The 字身 is the 弟 underneath, and because a 字身 can only take head, second, and tail codes rather than every stroke, we pick 弟's head 弓 (N), its second piece 中 (L), and its tail 丿 (H), giving the full code HNLH. Here's your hook: bamboo caps the brother, with H at both the head and the tail — the two ends fenced in by bamboo, and 弓 pulling 中 in the middle.
第.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「第」，讀做 dai6，佢係用嚟排次序嘅字，好似「第一」dai6 jat1 就係最頭、最緊要嗰個，「第二」dai6 ji6 就係跟住嗰個。你睇個字嘅樣，上面頂住一個竹字頭⺮，下面就係個「弟」字。呢個字要拆做字首同字身兩橛：字首就係最頂嗰個⺮，取H，好易記；字身就係下面個「弟」，佢喺倉頡入面唔會攞晒成個形，只可以攞頭、次、尾三碼，所以我哋喺「弟」度攞頭嗰筆弓（N）、第二筆中（L）、同最尾嗰筆丿（H）。合埋一齊就係 HNLH，即係竹弓中竹。記住喇：竹頭壓住個弟，頭尾都係H，一頭一尾竹夾住，中間弓拉住個中，就係排第幾嘅「第」。

等.en: Today's character is 「等」, read dang2, which can mean rank or grade, but also means to wait, and shows up in phrases meaning "and so forth." Look at its structure: on top sits the bamboo radical 「⺮」, and underneath is the character 「寺」. The bamboo top is the 字首, and it gives just one code, H. The bottom 「寺」 is the 字身, and since a 字身 takes at most three codes, we grab its head, its next piece, and its tail—the head 「土」 is G, the next piece 「寸」 is D, and the tail hook 「戈」 is I, giving us HGDI all together. Notice how the division is clean: one code for the bamboo top above, and three codes (head, middle, tail) for the 寺 below, making exactly four. To remember it, picture bamboo (H) growing over a temple 寺 where you wait—等等, wait a minute for me!
等.zh: 今日學嘅字係「等」，讀 dang2，可以解作等級、階級，又可以解作「等候」，仲可以表示「等等」咁多樣嘢。你望下佢嘅結構：上面係竹花頭「⺮」，下面係一個「寺」字。竹花頭做字首，我哋淨係取一個碼，就係 H。下面嘅「寺」做字身，因為字身最多取三個碼，所以我哋取頭、次、尾——頭係「土」取 G，次係「寸」入面嗰個「寸」取 D，尾就係最後嗰筆勾「戈」取 I，合埋成 HGDI。你要記住：字首同字身分工好清楚，上面竹花頭一碼，下面寺字頭中尾三碼，就啱啱四碼。想記住佢，你可以諗成「竹（H）下面有座寺，等下你」——等等，等我一陣！

策.en: Today we learn 策, read caak3, which means a scheme or a plan — as in 政策 (zing3 caak3, policy) and 策略 (caak3 loek6, strategy) — and it can also mean to whip or to urge on. Look at its shape: on top sits the bamboo radical ⺮, and underneath is the character 朿. In Cangjie we take the top first as the 字首, which is ⺮ on the H key, and then we break down the body 朿 below it. Since the body is not a single whole-form character, the rule is that a 字身 keeps at most its head and its tail, so from 朿 we take the head 木 (D) and the tail ⺆ (B), skipping whatever is in the middle, giving us HDB. Remember it this way: a bamboo cane (H) strikes the wood (D) inside its frame (B) — one whip, one plan.
策.zh: 今日我哋學「策」呢個字，讀音係 caak3，意思係計謀、計劃，好似「政策」（zing3 caak3）同「策略」（caak3 loek6）咁，亦都可以解作用鞭去抽打或者督促。你望下佢個樣，上面係竹花頭⺮，下面係一個「朿」字。喺倉頡入面，我哋先取字首⺮，佢喺 H 鍵，然後就要拆下面嘅字身「朿」。因為字身唔係整體字，倉頡有規矩：字身最多都係取頭同取尾兩碼，所以我哋喺「朿」入面取頭嘅木 D，再取尾嘅⺆ B，中間嗰部分就略去唔理，砌埋一齊就係 HDB。記住呢個字：竹枝（H）打落木頭（D）圍住框（B），一鞭一個計策。

算.en: Today we learn 算, read syun3, meaning to count, calculate or plan — you see it in 就算, colloquial for 'even if', and in 演算法, the word for algorithm. Look at its build: the very top is the bamboo radical ⺮ on the H key, which acts as the head and gives just one code; the whole lower portion is then treated as one block that we take by head and tail. The head of that lower part is 目 on the B key, and the tail gives us the last two pieces, 凵 on the U key and 廾 on the T key, so everything joins into HBUT. That's the ⺮-top-one-code rule plus head-second-tail below. Remember it like this: bamboo opens the door with one code, then 目 凵 廾 line up underneath — and you can count on it!
算.zh: 今日我哋學「算」呢個字，讀作 syun3，意思係計算、盤算，好似「就算」係口語「即使」嘅意思，「演算法」就係英文 algorithm。你睇下佢嘅結構：最頂係竹字頭 ⺮，喺 H 鍵，呢個係字首，只取一碼；下面剩返嘅部分係一個整體，我哋用取頭、取尾嘅方法拆佢，頭一碼取 目，喺 B 鍵，跟住取到尾嗰兩碼係 凵（U 鍵）同 廾（T 鍵）。所以合埋就係 HBUT，⺮頭一碼、下面頭二尾三碼咁樣夾埋。記住一句：竹頭一碼開路，下面「目凵廾」順住寫落去，就算得掂喇！

管.en: Today we learn 管, read gun2, which originally means a pipe or tube — think of a water pipe or windpipe — and by extension it also means woodwind music and the idea of managing or overseeing. Look at its shape: on top sits the bamboo radical ⺮, and beneath it stands the character 官, a neat picture of a bamboo lid over an official's seat. When we break it into code, ⺮ is the 字首 and takes its key H; then the lower part 官 is the 字身, and a 字身 is read by head, middle, and tail, so we take the head 宀 as J, the middle 口 as R, and the tail 口 as R again, giving HJRR. The split falls here because 字首 and 字身 each get their own quota — the bamboo top ⺮ claims just one code, and the rest of the codes go to 官 filled in by head, middle, and tail. Remember it this way: bamboo H on top, then 官 as 宀 J and two mouths RR — the bamboo pipe that plays the music.
管.zh: 今日我哋學「管」呢個字，讀作 gun2，本來係指竹造嘅管、通嘅管，好似水管、氣管噉，亦都可以指管樂或者管理嘅意思。你望下佢個樣，上面係竹字頭「⺮」，坐喺一個「官」字之上，畫面就好清楚。拆碼嗰陣，「⺮」做字首，攞佢個鍵 H；跟住下面「官」係字身，字身分三份就攞頭、中、尾，官嘅頭係寶蓋「宀」攞 J，中間一個「口」攞 R，最後結尾又一個「口」再攞 R，所以成個字係 HJRR。點解咁樣分？因為字首同字身各有配額，字首「⺮」淨係攞一碼，剩低嘅碼就全部畀字身「官」用頭中尾嚟填。記住喇：竹頭 H，跟住官字宀 J、兩個口 RR，就係管樂嗰枝竹管喇。

節.en: Today's character is 節, read zit3, which originally means the joint of a bamboo stalk and by extension a knot, a section, or a festival — you'll see it in words like 節目 (zit3 muk6, events) and 音節 (jam1 zit3, syllable), and it even names the hexagram ䷻. Look at the shape: on top sits the bamboo radical ⺮, and underneath is 即. The bamboo top ⺮ is a 字首, a leading part, so here it contributes just a single code, H, and then the body 即 takes over. That body is coded head-second-tail: 日 gives A, 戈 gives I, and 中 gives L, so stringing them together the full code is HAIL. Remember it this way: one H from the bamboo hat, then walk down 即 as A, I, L — like counting down the days as 聖誕節就快到喇, Christmas is coming soon.
節.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「節」，讀做 zit3，本義係竹嘅關節，引申做「節日」、「音節」嘅節，例如「節目」（zit3 muk6）同「音節」（jam1 zit3），仲可以代表卦象 ䷻。你睇下個字，頂上係竹字頭「⺮」，下面係「即」。竹字頭「⺮」本身係一個字首，喺倉頡入面淨係取一個碼 H，之後就輪到字身「即」出場。字身「即」要拆頭、二、尾三個碼，頭係「日」揀 A，中間揀「戈」個 I，最尾就係「中」揀 L，四個碼砌埋一齊就係 HAIL。記住喇：竹字頭一個 H 起頭，跟住「即」慢慢數 A、I、L，「聖誕節就快到喇」，一路數落去就啱晒。

築.en: Today we learn 築, read zuk1, meaning to build or erect — as in 建築 gin3 zuk1, architecture. Look at its shape: the bamboo top ⺮ sits above a body made of stacked strokes. Cangjie splits head from body and codes them separately, so the head ⺮ gives just its one letter H, while the body takes three codes using the head-second-last rule — from the body you pick 一 (M), 弓 (N), and 木 (D), giving the full code HMND. Why only three from the body? Because when a character divides into head and body, the body is capped at three codes, chosen as first, second, and last to capture it without typing every stroke. Remember the hook: bamboo on top pressing down 一 (M), 弓 (N), 木 (D) — HMND builds the building.
築.zh: 今日我哋學「築」呢個字，讀作 zuk1，解建造、興建，例如「建築」gin3 zuk1 就係 architecture。你望下佢個樣，最頂係竹字頭⺮，跟住下面係一啲筆畫砌埋一齊嘅字身。倉頡拆字有個規矩：字首同字身分開取碼，字首⺮取一個 H，字身就取頭、二、尾三碼——字身入面你揀到 一（M）、弓（N）、木（D）三件，所以合埋成 HMND。點解字身淨係取三碼？因為當一個字有字首字身之分，字身最多取三碼，用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法揀出代表性嘅部件，唔使將所有筆畫都打晒。記住個口訣：竹頭壓住一（M）、弓（N）、木（D），HMND 就砌起一座建築物喇。

簡.en: Today we learn 簡, read gaan2, meaning simple or succinct, and it can also mean a letter. Look at its shape: on top sits the bamboo radical ⺮, and underneath is the character 間 — it's a top-and-bottom build. In Cangjie we first take the head piece, bamboo ⺮, which lives on the H key; then the body is 間, but a body may contribute at most three codes, so instead of spelling all of it we take the head, the second piece, and the tail — the 日 A inside, a middle piece, and the closing 日 A, giving ANA. Put them together and the full code is HANA. Memory hook: pop the bamboo hat on, then let 間 give you head-second-tail — simple indeed!
簡.zh: 今日我哋學「簡」呢個字，讀音係 gaan2，意思係簡單、簡潔，都可以解作書信。你望吓佢嘅樣，上面有個竹字頭⺮，下面就係「間」字，成個字係上下結構。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，先攞字首竹字頭⺮，佢喺 H 鍵；跟住落嚟嘅字身係「間」，字身唔可以攞成四碼咁多，最多得三碼，所以要取頭、二、尾——「間」入面第一個係門字外框裏面嘅日 A，中間再拆多一部分，最尾又收到日 A，變成 ANA。所以成個碼就係 HANA。記住喇：竹頭一戴，下面「間」字取頭二尾，好簡單！

米.en: Today we learn 米, read mai5, the plain uncooked rice you eat every single day. Look at its shape: a cross in the middle with two dots on top and two below, like grains of rice scattering apart. This is a whole character, so it doesn't split into a complicated head and body — Cangjie just takes two codes: first 火 on the F key, then 木 on the D key, giving you FD. Why only two codes? Because as a whole character 米 isn't broken into 字首 and 字身 quotas; Cangjie simply picks its opening and closing shapes, 火 (F) and 木 (D), and that's enough. Remember it this way: to cook a bowl of rice you need fire (F) and wood (D) — just two taps, FD.
米.zh: 今日我哋學「米」呢個字，讀做 mai5，就係我哋日日食嘅白米、生米。你睇下佢個樣，中間一個十字，上下四點分開，睇落好似穀粒散開咁。呢個字係一個整體字，唔使拆得好複雜，倉頡淨係要打兩碼：先係「火」，喺 F 鍵，跟住係「木」，喺 D 鍵，所以成個碼就係 FD。點解得兩碼咁少呢？因為「米」係整體字，唔會硬拆成字首字身，倉頡只取頭同尾兩個字形代表佢，火（F）加木（D）就夠。記住喇：一碗白米，火煮木燒，FD 兩下就有得食。

粉.en: Today we learn 粉, read fan2, meaning powder — face powder, or the plaster you smear on a wall. Look at it: on the left sits 米, and on the right sits 分, the two clamped together. When Cangjie breaks this apart, the left head 米 gives its first and last codes, 火 (F) and 木 (D); then the right body 分 gives first-two-and-last, which are 金 (C), 尸 (S), and 竹 (H), building the full code 火木金尸竹 (FDCSH). Why does the head get only two while the body gets three? Because for a left-right character Cangjie caps the head at two codes and hands the remaining slots to the body, so 米 steps aside and 分 takes more. Memory hook: when you order 炒粉, think 火 burning 木, then 金尸竹 — that's 粉!
粉.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「粉」，讀做 fan2，即係粉末、化妝用嘅香粉，又或者係批牆嘅灰粉。你望下佢，左邊係「米」，右邊係「分」，兩邊夾埋一齊。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，左邊字首「米」取頭尾兩個碼，就係火（F）同木（D）；然後右邊字身「分」取頭二尾三個碼，就係金（C）、尸（S）同竹（H），砌埋一齊變成 火木金尸竹（FDCSH）。點解字首得兩碼、字身有三碼呢？因為倉頡規定分開嘅左右結構，字首最多取兩碼、剩返嘅碼數就留畀字身，所以「米」讓位，「分」就攞多啲。記住喇：食「炒粉」嗰陣諗返「火燒木、金尸竹」，火木金尸竹就係「粉」！

粥.en: Today we meet 粥, read zuk1 — it's the bowl of congee you eat in the morning. Look at its shape: a left-middle-right character, with a 弓 on the left, a 米 in the middle, and another 弓 on the right. Cangjie takes the left 弓 as the 字首, giving N, and everything else becomes the 字身, which is allowed up to three codes taken as head, second, and tail — so the head is the middle 米 (F), the second is the 木 hidden inside the 米 (D), and the tail is the right 弓 (N), spelling NFDN. The reason we stop at three is the fixed quota: one code for the 字首 and at most three for the 字身, and 米, 木, 弓 fill that exactly. Remember it as two bows hugging a rice: N at both ends, with F and D snug in the middle.
粥.zh: 今日我哋學「粥」呢個字，讀 zuk1，就係我哋朝早成日食嗰碗粥、congee。你望吓佢個樣，係一個左中右嘅結構：左邊一個弓，中間一個米字，右邊又係一個弓。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，左邊嗰個弓做字首，取 N，剩返嘅部分就係字身，字身要取頭、次、尾三碼——頭係中間嘅米 F，次係藏喺米入面嘅木 D，尾係右邊嘅弓 N，所以全碼就係 NFDN。點解字身淨係取三碼呢？因為倉頡有規矩，字首取一碼、字身最多取三碼，於是米、木、弓三件啱啱夠數。記住個口訣：兩隻弓夾住一個米，一頭一尾都係 N（弓），中間先係 F（米）D（木）。

粵.en: Today we learn a character that should feel close to your heart: 粵, read jyut6. It's the short name for the Guangdong and Guangxi region, and it's the 粵 in 粵語 — Cantonese, the very language you speak every day. Look at its shape: it wears a little cap on top, packs a few parts in the middle, and finishes inside a frame at the bottom, so it looks crowded, but we'll pick it apart piece by piece. This is a whole-character (整體字), meaning it can't be cleanly split into a head and a body, so instead of going left-right or top-bottom we follow the head-to-tail rule, taking parts from the top straight down through the shape. Working down the character you take the cap-like 竹 (H), then 田 (W), then the single stroke 一 (M), then 女 (V), and finally the 尸 (S) that closes it off at the bottom, giving you HWMVS. Here's the hook: just count from the top down to the tail — 竹田一女, with 尸 sitting underneath to finish, and 粵 is done.
粵.zh: 今日我哋學一個對你嚟講好親切嘅字：粵，讀作 jyut6，就係「廣東」同「廣西」嘅簡稱，亦係「粵語」——即係你日日講嘅廣東話——嗰個粵。你睇吓佢個樣，上面戴住個帽咁，中間夾住幾件嘢，落到底又有個框，密密麻麻好似好複雜，但係我哋一件件慢慢拆。呢個字係一個整體字，冇辦法清清楚楚分開字首同字身，所以我哋唔按左右上下嚟拆，而係跟返「頭、二、三、尾」嘅規矩，由頂到底順住個形逐件揀出嚟。順住寫落去，你先攞個帽形嘅竹（H），跟住個田（W），再嚟一橫嘅一（M），然後個女（V），最後補返落底嘅尸（S），砌埋一齊就係 HWMVS。記法好簡單：由個頭一路數到個尾，竹田一女——尸墊底收尾，粵字就成形。

精.en: Today we learn 精, read "zing1", meaning essence or spirit — as in "He does things very smartly", it carries the sense of being sharp and refined. Look at the character: on the left is 米, on the right is 青, a clear left-right structure, so we split it into a head part and a body part. The left 米 is the head, and Cangjie takes its first and last shapes — 火 (F) at the head and 木 (D) at the tail; the right 青 is the body, giving 手 (Q), then 一 (M), and finally the ⺼ (B) at the bottom, so the full code is FDQMB. Remember it this way: 米 gives head-and-tail 火 木, 青 gives 手 一 ⺼ — five keys building the essence of 精.
精.zh: 今日我哋學「精」呢個字，讀「zing1」，係精華、精神嘅意思，好似「佢做嘢好精明」咁樣，代表醒目、精細。你望吓個字，左邊係「米」，右邊係「青」，係一個左右分開嘅結構，所以我哋要拆做字首同字身兩部分。左邊嘅「米」做字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，頭係火（F），尾係木（D）；右邊嘅「青」做字身，順住寫落嚟取手（Q）、一（M），最後係下面嗰個⺼（B），所以全碼就係 FDQMB。記住個口訣：米字頭尾火木，青字手一⺼，五碼砌成精華一個字。

糖.en: Today we learn 糖, read "tong4", meaning sugar, candy, and sweets — exactly the kind of thing you enjoy eating. Look at it: on the left sits 米 (rice), and on the right sits 唐, making a clear left-right structure. The left piece 米 is the head, and Cangjie takes its first and last shapes, 火F and 木D; the right piece 唐 is the body, and being a bigger piece it takes head-second-last, which gives 广I, ⺕L, and 口R. Put them all in order and you get 火F, 木D, 广I, ⺕L, 口R — that is FDILR. Here's your hook: think of rice (米) turning into sweetness, and the 唐 dynasty handing you candy, fire-wood-shelter-broom-mouth, sweet to the very end.
糖.zh: 我哋今日學「糖」呢個字，讀「tong4」，就係你食嘅糖同埋糖果嘅意思。你望下佢，左邊係「米」，右邊係「唐」，係一個左右結構嘅字。左邊嘅「米」做字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，就係火F同木D；右邊嘅「唐」做字身，取頭、二、尾三碼，順住嚟就係广I、⺕L、口R。所以成個字砌埋就係火F、木D、广I、⺕L、口R，即係 FDILR。記住喇：食糖之前，先要有「米」煮糖水，右邊個「唐」朝代出糖果，火木广⺕口，甜到入心。

系.en: Today we learn 系, read hai6, meaning a system, a series, or a link — that idea of connection, as in 佢讀中文系, "He studies in the Chinese department." This is a whole-character (整體字), a shape you can't cleanly split into a head and a body, so we take it by the four-part rule: head, second, third, and last. Reading it down the character, the top is a single stroke 丿, which is H; next comes the little 一 hook shape ㄑ, which is V; then 戈, which is I; and finally, sitting at the bottom, 火, which is F. That gives you the full code HVIF — just remember it top to bottom as "stroke, hook, 戈, fire," and you'll type it in the right order every time.
系.zh: 今日我哋學個「系」字，讀做 hai6，意思係系統、系列、聯繫嗰種連接嘅意思，好似「佢讀中文系」入面嘅「系」咁。呢個字係一個整體字，冇辦法清楚咁分開字首同字身，所以我哋要用整體字嘅取碼法：取頭、二、三、尾四個部分。你順住個字睇落去，最上面係一撇「丿」，撳 H；跟住係一個「ㄑ」形，撳 V；再嚟係「戈」，撳 I；最尾落到底係「火」，撳 F。所以成個碼就係 HVIF，記住「一撇拉起，ㄑ勾戈鉤，火腳收尾」，順住由上到下嘅次序就唔會撳錯喇。

紀.en: Today we learn 紀, which reads gei2 or gei3 and means a record, an annal, or a historical account — as in 世紀 (sai3 gei2), a century, or 紀律, kept discipline. Look at it: it's built from a left part and a right part. The left is the 糸 radical, and in Cangjie 糸 is always taken as two codes, 女 (V) and 火 (F) — that pairing is fixed for this silk-thread piece. The right part is the body 己, and because it's the second part it only gives its head and tail: 尸 (S) at the top and 山 (U) at the bottom. Put them together and you get 女火尸山, VFSU. Memory hook: spin the silk thread (VF), then record your own self 己 — that's how you keep a 紀.
紀.zh: 今日我哋學「紀」字，佢讀 gei2 或者 gei3，意思係記錄、年代嘅記述，好似「世紀」（sai3 gei2）就係一百年，又或者「紀律」嘅記載。你望吓佢，係左右兩部分砌成。左邊嘅字首係「糸」，倉頡拆做兩個碼：「女」（V）同「火」（F）；記住「糸」呢個絲線部首,喺倉頡入面一律取VF呢兩碼，係固定嘅拆法。右邊嘅字身係「己」，因為佢已經係第二個部分，只可以取頭同尾，所以頭取「尸」（S）、尾取「山」（U）。合埋就係女火尸山，VFSU。記憶鉤子：織好一條絲線（VF），寫低自己（己）嘅一段紀錄，就係「紀」喇。

約.en: Today's character is 約, read joek3, meaning a treaty, agreement, or covenant — you see it in words like 大約 (daai6 joek3, meaning "about") and 紐約 (nau2 joek3, New York). Look at it: on the left is the silk radical 糸, and on the right is 勺. The left piece 糸 acts as the 字首, and rather than spelling out every stroke we take just its head and tail: the head 巜 gives V, and the tail portion of 糸 gives F, so the left is VF. The right piece 勺 is the 字身, and it too gives head and tail: the wrapping 勹 gives P and the little dot 丶 inside gives I, so the right is PI. Put the two-code 字首 and two-code 字身 together and you get VFPI — remember it as "silk head-tail, then wrap-plus-dot."
約.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「約」，讀「joek3」，意思係約定、契約，好似「大約」（daai6 joek3，大概咁多）同「紐約」（nau2 joek3，New York）都用到佢。你望吓佢，左邊係個絞絲邊「糸」，右邊係個「勺」字。左邊嘅「糸」做字首，我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，只係取頭尾兩碼：頭係「ㄑ」，撳 V，尾係「糸」剩低嗰部分，撳 F，所以左邊得 VF。跟住右邊嘅「勺」做字身，同樣取頭尾兩碼：頭係包住嘅「勹」，撳 P，尾係入邊嗰點「丶」，撳 I，於是右邊係 PI。左字首兩碼加右字身兩碼，合埋就係 VFPI；記住個口訣「絲頭尾，勺包點」，就好易記住呢個字。

紅.en: Today's character is 「紅」, read hung4, meaning red or vermillion, and it can also describe a face flushing or blushing. Notice how it sits as a left-and-right pair: on the left is the 「糸」 silk radical, and on the right is 「工」. When Cangjie breaks it down, 「糸」 acts as the 字首 (lead) and is a connected shape, so we take just its first and last pieces, 女 (V) and 火 (F); the right side 「工」 is the 字身 (body), and as a single part it gives only one code, 一 (M), making the whole thing VFM. Remember that the lead and the body each have their own quota — first-last for the lead, one code for the body — and together they add up to three. Picture a girl (女) lighting a fire (火) until her face glows red like a single line (一), and VFM will stick with you.
紅.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「紅」，讀 hung4，即係紅色嘅紅，仲可以指面紅、發紅。你睇佢係左右兩邊夾埋：左邊係個「糸」部，右邊係「工」字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，「糸」做字首，屬於連筆嘅部件，我哋取頭尾兩碼，就係「女」（V）同「火」（F）；右邊「工」做字身，一個部件只需要取一碼，就係「一」（M），所以整個字砌埋就係 VFM。要留意，字首同字身各有取碼嘅名額，字首取頭尾、字身取一碼，咁樣先湊夠三碼。記住一個畫面：一個女仔（女）點著火（火），面紅得好似一條紅線（一），咁就記得「紅」係 VFM 喇。

級.en: today we learn 級, read kap1, meaning level, rank, or grade, as in 超級 (ciu1 kap1, super-) and 高級 (gou1 kap1, high grade). The character splits into a left part and a right part. The 字首 on the left is the 糸 radical, taken as head-tail: its head is 女 (V) and its tail is 火 (F). The 字身 on the right is 及, taken as head-second-tail: head 弓 (N), second 竹 (H), and tail 又 (E). Put together you type VFNHE — two codes for the 字首 and three for the 字身, exactly filling the quota for a left-right character. Memory hook: 女-火 leads (糸), then 弓-竹-又 finishes off (及), and you've got 級.
級.zh: 我哋今日學「級」字，讀作 kap1，意思係等級、級別，好似「超級」（ciu1 kap1）同「高級」（gou1 kap1）咁樣用。呢個字左邊係「糸」部，右邊係「及」，我哋分開嚟拆。字首係「糸」，係一個獨立部件，取頭尾兩碼——頭係「女」（V），尾係「火」（F）；字身係「及」，取頭、二、尾三碼——頭係「弓」（N），第二碼係「竹」（H），尾係「又」（E）。所以合埋就係 VFNHE，字首兩碼加字身三碼，啱啱好符合左右結構嘅拆碼配額。記住口訣：女火（糸）行先，跟住弓竹又（及）收尾，就係「級」喇。

素.en: This character is 素, read sou3. It originally meant white raw silk, and from there it grew to mean plain or simple, and also vegetarian (eating meat-free). Look at how it stacks in two layers: the top is 主, from which we don't take every stroke but instead grab the head and tail — 手 (Q) and 一 (M); the bottom is 糸, and as the body it takes head-second-tail, giving 女 (V), 戈 (I), 火 (F). Why does 主 give only two codes? Because as the character-head it is capped at two, so head-first tail-last is enough, while 糸 as the character-body is allowed three, so head, second, and tail combine into VIF. Put it together and you get QMVIF — memory hook: the top opens with 手一 (QM) and the bottom closes plainly with 女戈火 (VIF).
素.zh: 呢個字係「素」，讀作 sou3，本來指白色嘅生絲，引申做樸素、平素，仲有食素（食齋）嘅意思。你睇佢分做上下兩截：上邊嗰截係「主」，我哋唔會逐筆咁攞，而係取頭尾兩碼——手（Q）同一（M）；下邊嗰截係「糸」，字身取碼取頭、二、尾，即係女（V）、戈（I）、火（F）。點解「主」淨係俾兩碼？因為佢係字首，字首最多只可以取兩碼，所以攞頭一尾一就夠；而「糸」做字身，可以取到三碼，於是頭二尾湊成 VIF。合埋一齊就係 QMVIF。記住呢個口訣：「主」開頭兩下手一（QM），「糸」收尾女戈火（VIF）——素素淨淨，五碼齊全。

細.en: Today we learn 細, read sai3, meaning fine, tiny, or slender — you hear it in 細個 (sai3 go3), meaning young or little, and 細路 (sai3 lou6), the everyday word for kids. Look at how it splits into a left part and a right part: the left 糸 is the head, and it gives just its first code, 女 V. The right 田 is the body, and because a body is written out with more than one piece, we take its first-and-last codes — 田 begins with 火 F and ends with 田 itself W, giving F then W. Put the three together and you get 女 V, 火 F, 田 W, that is VFW — remember it as a fine thread 糸 sitting beside a field 田, small and neat, spelling 細.
細.zh: 今日我哋學「細」字，讀作 sai3，即係細小、幼細嘅意思，好似「細個」（sai3 go3）解細細個嗰陣時，又或者「細路」（sai3 lou6）解細路仔、細蚊仔。你睇下佢分做左右兩橛：左邊個「糸」係字首，取佢頭一個碼女V；右邊個「田」係字身，因為字身唔止一件，所以要取頭尾兩碼——「田」寫出嚟頭係火F、尾係田本身W，合埋就係火F、田W。三個碼砌埋一齊，就係女V、火F、田W，即係 VFW。記住個口訣：左邊糸開頭女V，右邊田字頭尾火田，一件細細嘅絲加塊田，就係「細」。

組.en: Today we learn 組, read "zou2", meaning a class, a group, or a department — as in "we are one group of people". The character splits into two parts left and right: the 字首 is 糸 and the 字身 is 且. For 糸 we don't spell out every stroke; we just take head and tail, which are 糸 (V) and 幺 (F). For the 字身 且 on the right, we do the same head-tail trick, taking ⺼ (B) at the head and 一 (M) at the tail, so the whole thing comes together as VFBM. Remember it this way: VF lifts up the silk 糸 on the left, and the right side 且 runs from its head 月 down to its tail 一 — you'll meet this often in words like 組織 and 組成.
組.zh: 今日我哋學「組」呢個字，讀「zou2」，即係組別、小組、部門嘅意思，好似「我哋一組人」咁。呢個字分做左右兩部分：字首係「糸」，字身係「且」。「糸」呢個部件我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，只取頭尾兩碼，就係頭嘅「糸」V同尾嘅「幺」F。至於右邊嘅字身「且」，同樣係取頭尾，頭係「月」B，尾係「一」M，所以成個字砌埋就係 VFBM。記住：左邊 VF 抽起條「糸」，右邊「且」由頭「月」到尾「一」，「組織」、「組成」呢啲詞你就會成日見到嘞。

結.en: Today we learn 結, read git3, meaning to knot, to tie, to join or connect — you see it in words like 結果 git3 gwo2 (a result) and 結婚 git3 fan1 (to get married). Look at how it's built left and right: the left side is the 字首 糸, the silk radical, and the right side is the 字身 吉. Cangjie has a rule that a 字首 and a 字身 each give at most a head-and-tail pair of codes, so the 字首 糸 takes only its head V and tail F, and the 字身 吉 gives its head 士 G and tail 口 R rather than being fully spelled out. Put them together and you get VFGR — head-tail meeting head-tail, neat and balanced. Here's your memory hook: a thread of silk (V, F) ties a knot on the character 吉 (G, R), and that knot is 結.
結.zh: 今日我哋學「結」呢個字，讀音係 git3，意思係打結、綁埋、連接，好似「結果」git3 gwo2、「結婚」git3 fan1 都用到佢。你望下佢係左右兩邊砌成：左邊係字首「糸」（絞絲邊），右邊係字身「吉」。倉頡有個規矩，一個字首同一個字身，最多都係各取頭尾兩碼，所以字首「糸」淨係取頭同尾——頭係 V，尾係 F；而字身「吉」我哋唔會成個拆散，只係攞佢嘅頭「士」G 同尾「口」R。合埋就係 VFGR，頭尾配頭尾，齊齊整整。記住個口訣：一條絲線 V、F 打咗個「吉」G、R 嘅結，就係「結」喇。

統.en: Today's character is 統, read tung2, meaning to govern, to command or control, and also to unite or connect together. Notice it splits left and right: the 糸 on the left is the head, and 充 on the right is the body. Cangjie gives this a clean rhythm — the head takes only its first and last shapes, so 糸 gives you its head ㇛ (V) and its tail 火 (F); then the body takes head, second, and tail, so 充 gives you head 卜 (Y), second 戈 (I), and tail 山 (U), building VFYIU together. Why two codes for the head but three for the body? Because in a left-right character the head is limited to its first-and-last pair, while the body is allowed the fuller head-second-tail set, and here everything lines up perfectly. Remember it as 糸 first-last (VF) then 充 head-second-tail (YIU), and you'll type 統 in one smooth run — try it in 系統 and 傳統, as in 呢個系統好易用.
統.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「統」，讀作 tung2，意思係管治、統領，又或者係統一、貫通。你望吓佢係左右分開嘅：左邊個「糸」係字首，右邊個「充」係字身。倉頡拆呢個字有個好清晰嘅節奏——字首取頭尾兩碼，於是「糸」就攞佢個頭㇛ㄑ（V）同埋佢個尾火（F）；跟住字身就取頭、二、尾三碼，「充」就攞頭卜（Y）、第二戈（I）同埋個尾山（U），合埋成 VFYIU。點解字首得兩碼、字身有三碼呢？因為倉頡規定左右結構嘅字首最多取頭尾兩碼，而字身就可以取到頭、次、尾三碼，咁樣就啱啱好齊晒。記住呢句：糸頭尾（VF）、充頭二尾（YIU），你就一次過打得晒「統」。你可以睇吓「系統」同「傳統」，好易上手，例如「呢個系統好易用。」

經.en: Today we're learning 經, read ging1, which can mean a classic text and can also mean to pass through or go by. Look at the character: on the left sits the 糸 silk radical, and on the right is a separate part, so Cangjie splits it into these two halves. The left 糸 is the head, and we take its first and last shapes, 女 (V) and 火 (F); then on the right body we take head-second-last, giving 一 (M), 女 (V), and 一 (M). Put it all together and you get VFMVM — notice the two 女 (V) keys and two 一 (M) keys framing the middle, almost mirror-like. Remember the sentence 我已經食咗飯 — you've already (ji5 ging1) mastered it!
經.zh: 今日我哋學「經」呢個字，讀做 ging1，可以解做經典嘅書，又可以解「經過」，即係穿過、通過嘅意思。你睇個字，左邊係「糸」字部，右邊係另一部分，倉頡就要分開兩邊嚟拆。左邊嘅「糸」係字首，倉頡取佢嘅頭同尾，即係「女」（V）同「火」（F）；跟住去到右邊字身，取頭、二、尾三碼，就係「一」（M）、「女」（V）、「一」（M）。所以成個碼砌埋一齊就係 VFMVM，你留意有兩個「女」（V）同兩個「一」（M）夾住中間，好似左右對稱噉。記住呢句「我已經食咗飯」，你已經（ji5 ging1）學識喇！

維.en: Today we learn 維, read wai4, meaning to maintain, to keep, or to safeguard something — as in 維持乾淨, keeping things clean. Look at it: 糸 sits on the left and 隹 on the right, two halves standing side by side. When Cangjie breaks it up, the head 糸 gives only its head and tail — the head is 女 (V) and the tail is 火 (F), so the head part is VF; then the body 隹 also takes head and tail, with 人 (O) as its head and 土 (G) as its tail, giving OG. Read straight through, the full code is VFOG, one piece from 糸 and one from 隹, each contributing head and tail neatly. Remember it as V-F then O-G — left 糸, right 隹, working together to maintain.
維.zh: 我哋今日學「維」，讀 wai4，意思係維持、保住、保護一樣嘢，好似「維持乾淨」個「維」。你望吓佢，左邊係「糸」，右邊係「隹」，左右兩橛砌埋一齊。倉頡拆嘅時候，字首個「糸」淨係取頭尾兩碼——頭係「女」（V），尾係「火」（F），所以字首係 VF；跟住字身個「隹」都係取頭尾，頭係「人」（O），尾係「土」（G），砌埋就係 OG。全碼順住讀落嚟就係 VFOG，一橛「糸」一橛「隹」，各取頭尾，好整齊。記住喇：「女火．人土」（VF．OG），左糸右隹一齊維持住。

網.en: Today we learn 網, read mong5, meaning a net or web — the same 網 in 網絡 (the Internet) and 網上 (online). Look at the character: on the left sits the 糸 silk radical, and on the right is 罔, and the two halves lock together. Cangjie splits it into head and body: the head 糸 gives its first-and-last codes as 女 and 火, that is V then F; the body 罔 then contributes three codes — its top frame ⺆ is B, the 廿 inside is T, and its final piece is another 女, V — giving the full code VFBTV. The body takes three codes rather than two because it is itself a full top-to-bottom structure, and Cangjie lets a body spell out head, middle, and tail to describe it clearly. Here's your hook: two 女 stand at the front and the back, wrapping the middle tight like a net closed at both ends — type VFBTV and it holds.
網.zh: 今日我哋學「網」呢個字，讀做 mong5，即係網、蜘蛛網，又或者係我哋成日講嘅「上網」嗰個網絡。你望下呢個字，左邊係「糸」字部，右邊係「罔」，兩橛砌埋一齊。倉頡分字首同字身：字首「糸」取頭尾兩碼，就係「女」火，即 V 同 F；跟住字身「罔」係複雜字，取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係外框「⺆」B，中間「廿」T，最尾又係一個「女」V，所以成個字砌出嚟就係 VFBTV。點解字身要拆到三橛咁多？因為淨係字身呢橛都已經係一個有頭有尾嘅完整結構，倉頡容許佢取多過兩碼去交代清楚。記住個訣竅：兩個「女」一頭一尾包住中間，就好似一張網頭尾都收緊咁，你打 VFBTV 就穩陣。

緊.en: Today we learn 緊, read gan2 — the very word you'd use in "holding it too tight," meaning tense, tight, taut, or firm and secure. Notice it stacks in two halves: 臤 sits on top and 糸 (the silk radical) sits below. The top 臤 acts as the 字首, so Cangjie takes just its first and last pieces — 臣 (S) and 又 (E); the bottom 糸 acts as the 字身, which is allowed three codes taken as first, second, and last — 女 (V), 幺 (I), and 火 (F) — giving you SEVIF all together. Why two from the top but three from the bottom? Because the 字首 and 字身 have separate quotas — the leading part yields at most two codes, while the body part may give up to three. Remember it this way: 臣又 up top, 女幺火 down below, just like the sentence 你揸得太緊喇 — you're holding it too tight.
緊.zh: 今日我哋學「緊」呢個字，讀做 gan2，就好似你講「揸得太緊」嗰個緊，意思係緊、實、繃緊，或者穩陣、緊固。你留意佢係上下兩截：上面係「臤」，下面係「糸」（絞絲底）。上半嘅「臤」做字首，倉頡取頭同尾兩碼，就係開頭嘅「臣」（S）同結尾嘅「又」（E）；下半嘅「糸」做字身，取頭、二同尾三碼，順住寫落去就係「女」（V）、「幺」（I）、「火」（F），所以成個字砌埋就係 SEVIF。點解上面淨係取兩碼而下面取三碼？因為字首同字身各有配額——字首最多攞兩碼，字身先至可以攞到三碼。記住口訣：臣又喺上，女幺火喺下，「你揸得太緊喇」就唔會唔記得。

線.en: Today's character is 線, read sin3, meaning a thread, line or wire, and by extension a clue. Look at how it's built: the left side is the silk radical 糸, and the right side is 泉 (spring). In Cangjie the left-hand 糸 acts as the 字首 and is allowed only two codes, so we take its head and tail — 女 (V) and 火 (F); the right-hand 泉 is the 字身 and takes three codes, head-second-tail — 竹 (H), 日 (A) and 水 (E), giving the full code VFHAE. Here's your memory hook: two from the front, three from the back — 女火 pulls the thread, and 竹日水 follows the line right to the end.
線.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「線」，讀作 sin3，即係線、繩、電線，又或者引申做「線索」嘅意思。你睇下，佢左邊係「糸」呢個絞絲部，右邊係「泉」字。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，左邊嘅「糸」做字首，只可以取頭尾兩碼——頭係「女」（V），尾係「火」（F）；右邊嘅「泉」做字身，取頭、二、尾三碼——頭係「竹」（H），第二碼係「日」（A），尾係「水」（E），合埋就係 VFHAE。記住呢個口訣：字首兩碼、字身三碼，「女火」牽起條「竹日水」嘅線，就唔會拆錯喇。

編.en: Today we learn 編, read pin1, meaning to knit, to weave, to arrange, or to compile. Look at it: it's a left-right character, with the silk radical 糸 on the left and 扁 on the right. In Cangjie the left 糸 isn't typed whole—it gives just two codes, 女 (V) and 火 (F); then the body 扁 follows the usual head-second-tail rule, giving 竹 (H), 尸 (S), and ⺆ (B). Put together, the full code is VFHSB. Remember it this way: whenever you see that silk-thread side 糸, it always begins with VF, and you finish off by picking apart 扁—weaving the character together piece by piece, just like editing a story.
編.zh: 今日我哋學「編」呢個字，讀作 pin1，即係編織、編排、編輯嘅意思。你望下佢，係左右兩橋：左邊係「糸」字旁，右邊係「扁」。倉頡拆字，左邊「糸」呢個部件唔係成個打晒，而係取頭尾兩碼——「女」（V）同「火」（F）；右邊嘅字身「扁」就照字首取頭、次取二、尾取尾嘅規矩，攞「竹」（H）、「尸」（S）同埋「⺆」（B）。所以成個編碼就係 VFHSB。記住喇：織布嗰個「糸」邊，永遠都係 VF 起手，之後再拆右邊嘅「扁」——編一個故事都係咁一步步編出嚟嘅。

總.en: Today we're learning 總, read zung2, meaning to collect or, more often, overall and altogether — as in 總站 (zung2 zaam6, a terminus) and 總統 (zung2 tung2, the president of a country). The character has 糸 on the left and 悤 on the right; for the silk radical 糸 on the left, Cangjie takes just the head and tail, which give you 女 (V) and 火 (F), so the left part is V F. The body 悤 on the right then takes its head, second and tail pieces: the head is 竹 (H), inside there are two 田 shapes so we take one 田 (W), and the tail at the bottom is 心 (P), together making VFHWP. Remember it this way: 女 and 火 open the road on the left, then 竹, 田 and 心 stack up on the right to form 總!
總.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「總」，讀作 zung2，意思係聚集、統括，好似「總站」（zung2 zaam6，即係總車站）同「總統」（zung2 tung2，一國之首）咁。呢個字左邊係「糸」部，右邊係「悤」；左邊嘅絞絲部，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，就係女（V）同火（F），所以字首係 V F。右邊嘅字身「悤」就要取頭、次同尾三部分：頭係竹（H），中間有兩個田字，所以取一個田（W），尾部係下面嘅心（P），合埋成 VFHWP。記住呢個字：左邊女火開路，右邊由竹田心疊起，變成一個「總」！

織.en: Today we learn 織, read zik1, which means to weave or knit, and by extension to organize or unite, as in 組織 (organization) and 交織 (to interweave). The character breaks into a left and a right part: the head on the left is 糸, and Cangjie takes just its first and last shapes, 女 V and 火 F; the body on the right is 戠, which as a body is allowed three codes, so we take first-middle-last, 卜 Y, 戈 I, and 日 A, giving the full code VFYIA. Notice how the quotas work — the head 糸 gives only two codes while the body 戠 gets its full three, which adds up neatly to five. To fix it in mind, picture Grandma knitting a sweater: her left hand holds the thread 糸 (V F) while her right hand stitches out 戠 (Y I A) one loop at a time.
織.zh: 今日我哋學「織」呢個字，讀做 zik1，意思係編織、織冷衫，亦可以引申做組織、聯合，好似「組織」同「交織」噉。呢個字分成左右兩橛，左邊嘅字首係「糸」，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，即係女 V 同火 F；右邊嘅字身係「戠」，因為佢係字身可以取到三碼，所以取頭、二、尾，即係卜 Y、戈 I、日 A，合埋一齊就係 VFYIA。記住字首同字身各有配額，字首「糸」淨係俾兩碼，字身「戠」就俾足三碼，噉樣就啱晒五碼。想記實佢，你可以諗住婆婆織緊冷衫嗰陣，左手揸住條糸線 V F，右手一針一針織出個「戠」字 Y I A。

繼.en: Today we learn 繼, read gai3, meaning to continue or to carry on — you see it in 繼續 (to continue) and 繼母 (stepmother). Look at its shape: on the left sits 糸, and on the right is a piece called 㡭, so this is a left-right character. In Cangjie the left 糸 becomes the head, and a head is only allowed two codes — first and last — so from 糸's own full code VIF we take the first V (糸) and the last F (火), giving VF. The right 㡭 becomes the body, and a body may take three codes — head, second, last — so from 㡭's own full code VVII we take the head V (ㄑ), the second V (ㄑ), and the last I (戈), giving VVI. Put them together and the full code is VFVVI: 糸(V) 火(F) ㄑ(V) ㄑ(V) 戈(I). Memory hook: left side opens with 糸 then 火, then the right side runs two little ㄑ and closes with one 戈.
繼.zh: 今日我哋學「繼」字，讀做 gai3，意思係繼續、接住做落去，好似「繼續」同「繼母」入面咁用。你望下佢個樣，左邊係「糸」，右邊係一舊叫「㡭」嘅嘢，係一個左右結構嘅字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，左邊「糸」做字首，字首淨係取頭同尾兩碼，所以「糸」自己嘅碼係 VIF，取頭 V（糸）同尾 F（火），就得出 VF；右邊「㡭」做字身，字身可以取頭、二、尾三碼，「㡭」自己嘅碼係 VVII，取頭 V（ㄑ）、第二 V（ㄑ）同尾 I（戈），就得出 VVI。兩邊夾埋，全碼就係 VFVVI，即係糸（V）火（F）ㄑ（V）ㄑ（V）戈（I）。記住個口訣：左邊糸火開頭，右邊三隻手指跟住㇐兩個ㄑ再收一戈，「繼」就寫得出嚟喇。

續.en: Today we learn 續, read zuk6, meaning to continue, to carry on, to keep going — as in 繼續 and 持續. Look at the character: it splits into a left side, the silk radical 糸, and a right side, 賣. Cangjie takes the head first: 糸 can't be captured by a single key, so we take its head and tail, giving 女 (V) and 火 (F); then we take the body 賣, and since a body may take up to three codes, we use the head-second-tail method to pull out 土 (G), 囗 (W), and 金 (C). Put them together and you get VFGWC, five keys for one character. Remember it this way: silk on the left is 女火 (VF), and 賣 on the right is 土囗金 (GWC) — and just like that, you keep going.
續.zh: 我哋今日學「續」字，讀做 zuk6，意思係繼續、延續、接落去做，好似「繼續」同「持續」噉。你望住個字，佢分成左右兩橛：左邊係絞絲邊「糸」，右邊係「賣」。倉頡先拆字首「糸」，呢個部件唔係一個鍵搞得掂，所以要攞頭尾兩碼，就係「女」（V）同「火」（F）；跟住拆字身「賣」，字身可以攞到三碼，用頭、次、尾嘅方法，取「土」（G）、「囗」（W）、「金」（C）。噉樣合埋就係 VFGWC，五碼一個字。記住個口訣：左邊絞絲女火（VF），右邊賣字土囗金（GWC），續字就一氣呵成、接落去啦。

署.en: Today we meet 署, read cyu5, meaning a government office — you'll see it in 警署 ging2 cyu5, a police station, and 簽署 cim1 cyu5, to sign a document officially. Look at its shape: across the top sits a flat 罒, like a little net, and below it stands the character 者, so this splits into a 字首 on top and a 字身 underneath. The top 罒 is the 字首, and a 字首 takes only its first and last pieces, giving you 田 (W) and 中 (L); the bottom 者 is the 字身, which takes first, second and last — 十 (J), 大 (K) and 日 (A) — so the whole code reads WLJKA. The reason the top gives only two codes is that a 字首 is capped at two, leaving room for the 字身 below to carry the rest of the character. Picture a net on top (田中, WL) resting over 者 (十大日, JKA), and you'll always find the 署 where you go to report a case.
署.zh: 我哋今日學「署」呢個字，讀做 cyu5，意思係政府嘅辦公地方，好似「警署」ging2 cyu5 就係差人辦公嘅地方，「簽署」cim1 cyu5 就係喺文件上面正式簽名。你睇吓佢嘅結構：上面係一個扁扁嘅罒（好似個網咁），下面係「者」字，所以呢個字要分做字首同字身兩橛。上面嘅罒係字首，倉頡拆碼嘅時候取頭尾兩碼，就係田（W）同中（L）；下面嘅「者」做字身，取頭、次、尾三碼，即係十（J）、大（K）、日（A），所以全碼串埋就係 WLJKA。點解上面淨係取兩碼？因為佢係字首，字首最多取兩碼，剩低嘅碼數就留返畀字身，咁樣先夠位表達成個字。記住喇：上面一個網（田中 WL），下面一個者（十大日 JKA），我去警署報案就係去呢個「署」。

羅.en: Today we learn 羅, read lo4. It originally means a net for catching birds, and also refers to a fine silk gauze called 羅紗; it's also a very common surname. Look at it: on top sits a flat 罒, and underneath is the character 維, the two stacked together. That top head-piece 罒 isn't broken up fully — Cangjie takes only its first and last codes, the outer frame 囗 (W) then the inner 中 (L), giving WL for the head. The lower part 維 is the body, so instead of taking everything we use the head-second-tail rule: the first piece ㄑ (V), the second piece 小 (F), and the final piece 土 (G), spelling VFG, so the whole character is WLVFG. Memory hook: a net (罒) draped over a length of cord (維) — think 羅馬 (Rome) and 俄羅斯 (Russia), and someone whose surname is Law.
羅.zh: 今日我哋學「羅」呢個字，讀音係 lo4，本義係捕雀嘅網，亦都指輕薄嘅絲織品「羅紗」，同時都係好常見嘅姓氏。你望吓佢，上面係一個扁扁嘅「罒」，下面係「維」字，兩截疊埋一齊。上面呢個字首「罒」，你唔好拆到咁散，倉頡淨係取頭尾兩個碼——先係外框「囗」（W），再係入面嘅「中」（L），所以字首係 WL。落到字身「維」，因為佢已經係字身、唔使再攞晒全部，所以就用「頭二尾」嘅取碼法：攞頭嗰個「ㄑ」（V），跟住第二個「小」（F），最後尾嘅「土」（G），砌埋就係 VFG，全字合起嚟就係 WLVFG。記法可以咁諗：一張網（罒）罩住一條纜繩（維），「俄羅斯」同「羅馬」都係佢，佢姓羅。

美.en: Today we learn 美, read mei5, meaning beautiful or pretty, as in "this garden is beautiful." Look at the shape from top to bottom: on top sits the grass radical 艹, typed with T; in the middle there is 土, typed with G; and at the bottom stands a big 大, typed with K. Because 美 is treated as a whole-character shape — one solid block you cannot neatly break into separate head and body — Cangjie uses its special rule: take the head, the second piece, and the last piece, giving 艹土大, while skipping whatever sits in the middle. That gives you the full code TGK. Memory hook: read it straight down — grass, then earth, then big — T, G, K, and beauty grows on top of the ground.
美.zh: 今日我哋學「美」字，讀音係 mei5，即係美麗、靚嘅意思，好似「呢個花園好美」咁樣。你望住個字，最上面係草花頭「艹」，喺鍵盤取碼字母 T；跟住中間有個「土」，字母 G；最底係一個大大隻嘅「大」，字母 K。呢個字係一個「整體字」，即係話成個字連埋一齊、拆唔開好多截，所以倉頡有個特別規矩：只取頭、第二同埋尾，即係「艹土大」，中間嗰截就跳過唔取，所以完整碼就係 TGK。記憶鉤子：由頭到腳一路數落——草花頭、一撻土、一個大——TGK，草上種出一片美，好記啦！

義.en: Today we learn 義, read ji6, meaning righteousness or right conduct — the moral uprightness a person is supposed to live by. Look at the character: on top sits 羊, and underneath sits 我, two parts stacked together. 義 is a whole-character (整體字): it has too many strokes to split cleanly into a head and a body, so Cangjie takes it head-second-third-tail — you grab the most telling corners and let the crowded middle drop out. The top 羊 gives the first two codes, 艹 (T) then 土 (G); the bottom 我 gives the last three, 竹 (H), 手 (Q), 戈 (I), so the full code is TGHQI. Remember it this way: 羊 up top hands you 艹土, 我 down below hands you 竹手戈, and the middle is politely skipped.
義.zh: 今日我哋學「義」字，讀ji6，意思係正義、道義，做人講嘅嗰種正確操守。你望住個字，上面係一個「羊」，下面係一個「我」，兩件砌埋一齊。「義」係一個整體字，字形太多筆畫，冇辦法乾淨俐落咁分開字首字身，所以倉頡用「頭、二、三、尾」嘅取碼法，即係揀最有代表性嘅幾個角落，中間嗰堆就跳過唔理。上面個「羊」拆出頭兩碼，先係艹（T），再係土（G）；下面個「我」拆出後三碼，係竹（H）、手（Q）、戈（I），所以全碼就係 TGHQI。記住個口訣：羊喺頭畀你艹土，我喺尾畀你竹手戈，中間嗰橛乖乖跳過。

習.en: Today's character is 習, read zaap6, meaning to practice — its original picture is a bird flapping its wings. Look at how it stacks: the top is 羽 and the bottom is 白. We don't break 羽 stroke by stroke; Cangjie tells us to take just its head and tail, so from 羽 we get the head 尸 (S) and the tail 一 (M). Then we move to 白 and do the same head-and-tail: its head 竹 (H) and its tail 日 (A), giving us the full code SMHA. You'll meet this character in 學習 (hok6 zaap6, to study) and 習慣 (zaap6 gwaan3, habit), and the memory hook is simple: feathers flapping under the white sun as you practice — 尸一竹日, SMHA.
習.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「習」，讀作 zaap6，意思係練習，本義其實係雀仔拍翼嘅樣。你睇佢分成兩橛：上面係「羽」，下面係「白」。「羽」呢個部件唔係逐筆拆嘅，倉頡教我哋取頭尾就得，所以由「羽」度拎出頭嘅尸（S）同尾嘅一（M）；跟住落到「白」，同樣取頭尾，拎出頭嘅竹（H）同尾嘅日（A），砌埋一齊就係 SMHA。記住呢個字用喺「學習」（hok6 zaap6）同「習慣」（zaap6 gwaan3）度，記憶鈎就係：羽毛喺白日下拍翼練習——尸一竹日，SMHA。

翠.en: Today we learn 翠, read ceoi3 in Cantonese, meaning green or emerald, and also naming the kingfisher, that gorgeous little bird — you'll see it in the word 翡翠, jadeite. Look at the whole character: on top sits 羽 as the 字首, and beneath it sits 卒 as the 字身, one stacked over the other. The top piece 羽 is a complex shape, so Cangjie takes only its head and tail — head 尸(S) and tail 一(M) — giving the 字首 just SM. Then the 字身 卒 takes three codes, head/middle/tail: head 卜(Y), then 人(O), and tail 十(J), so the whole character builds up to SMYOJ. Remember it like this: a kingfisher (羽, SM) perched on 卒 (YOJ) — the full code SMYOJ, bright emerald green.
翠.zh: 今日我哋學「翠」字，粵音讀 ceoi3，意思係青綠色，又指翠鳥呢種好靚嘅雀仔，好似「翡翠」呢個詞噉。你望吓成個字，上面係「羽」字頭，下面係「卒」字身，一上一下咁疊住。先睇字首個「羽」，佢係一個複雜嘅形，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，頭係尸(S)，尾係一(M)，所以字首得 SM 兩個碼。跟住落到字身個「卒」，佢取頭、次、尾三碼：頭係卜(Y)，中間係人(O)，尾係十(J)，於是砌埋成個字就係 SMYOJ。你可以噉樣記：一隻翠鳥（羽 SM）停喺個「卒」度（YOJ），全字 SMYOJ，翠綠好搶眼。

老.en: Today we learn 老, read lou5, meaning old or aged — and by extension someone experienced, which is why it shows up in words like 老師 (si1, teacher) and 老婆 (po4, colloquial for wife). Look at the character: up top there's a cross-like shape, then a slanting stroke sweeping down across it, and tucked underneath a small curved piece. In Cangjie this is a whole-character (整體字), one that doesn't break into a tidy head-and-body pair, so instead we take the head, the second piece, and the tail, skipping the middle: the head is 十 (J), the second is ナ (K), and the tail is the little 匕 (P) at the bottom — giving JKP. The reason for skipping is that the shape is too compact to split cleanly, so Cangjie just samples head, next, and tail to capture its outline. Remember it this way: an old person's 十 (J) years bent their ナ (K) back into a 匕 (P) shape — J, K, P!
老.zh: 今日我哋學「老」呢個字，讀作 lou5，意思係年紀大、老咗，又或者形容有經驗嘅人，好似「老師」（si1，即係教你嘢嘅人）同「老婆」（po4，口語入面指老婆）都用到佢。你望住個字，會見到上面有個十字形，跟住斜斜落嚟嘅一撇一橫，最後底下藏住個彎彎嘅部件。倉頡入面呢個係一個「整體字」，唔會拆得好散，反而係取頭、取二、取尾，跳過中間嗰忽：頭係「十」（J），第二個係「ナ」（K），尾就係底下嗰個「匕」（P），所以碼就係 JKP。點解要跳過中間？因為整體字太緊湊，唔可以齊頭齊尾咁全部取晒，倉頡就用「頭、次、尾」三碼概括佢個形。記住呢句：老人家「十」（J）年前就「ナ」（K）咗腰，變成個「匕」（P），JKP 就係佢喇！

考.en: Today's character is 考, read haau2, meaning to examine or test — the same 考 you see in 考慮 haau2 leoi6, to think something over carefully, and in 考試 haau2 si3, a test or exam. Look at its shape: it doesn't fall neatly into a clean top and bottom that you could slice apart, so we treat it as a whole-character (整體字), which means we don't split it into a head and a body at all — instead we read straight through in writing order and take up to four pieces. Following the strokes, you take the head 十 which is J, then second 大 which is K, then third 卜 which is Y, and finally the last piece 尸 which is S, giving you JKYS. To remember it, picture sitting an exam and needing a big (大 K) cross (十 J) of a fortune-telling (卜 Y) reading pulled right out of the paper (尸 S) — head, second, third, last, straight through, and 考 is done.
考.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「考」，讀 haau2，意思係考核、測驗，好似「考慮」haau2 leoi6 咁樣去仔細諗清楚，又或者「考試」haau2 si3 呢個大家都熟悉嘅字眼。你睇下佢個樣，上面同下面唔容易齊齊整整咁一刀切開兩截，所以我哋當佢係一個「整體字」——整體字唔分字首字身，而係由頭到尾順住寫落嚟，最多取四個碼。你就照住筆順一路點：先取個頭「十」J，跟住第二個「大」K，第三個「卜」Y，最後取個尾「尸」S，砌埋一齊就係 JKYS。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗：考試前要一個「十」字「大」問「卜」卦問到條「尸」都攞出嚟，頭、二、三、尾順住行，考就砌好喇。

者.en: Today we meet 者, read ze2, meaning "the one who" or "that which" — the person who does something, as in 或者 (waak6 ze2, meaning or/perhaps) and 研究者 (jin4 gau3 ze2, a researcher). Look at the character: the top looks like a cross-shape with a slanting stroke, and underneath sits a 日 (sun) box. Cangjie reads it top to bottom, left to right: first the cross-piece 十 on the J key, then the slanting stroke ナ on the K key, and finally the 日 at the bottom on the A key, giving you the full code JKA. Why does it split this way? Because 者 is a whole character (整體字), so we don't divide it into head-part and body-part — we simply take three codes in stroke order from start to finish: head 十, next ナ, tail 日, and stop at three. Remember it like this: a cross holds up the top, a slant leans across, and the sun sits at the bottom — J, K, A spells the 者 in "reader."
者.zh: 今日我哋學「者」呢個字，讀做 ze2，意思係「嗰個人」或者「做嗰件事嘅人」，好似「或者」（waak6 ze2，即係 or、可能）同「研究者」（jin4 gau3 ze2，即係做研究嘅人）咁樣用。你望住個字，上面好似「土」加多一撇，下面有個「日」，倉頡就係順住由上到下、由左到右嘅次序去拆佢：先取頭嗰個十字形「十」，佢喺 J 鍵；跟住取條斜筆「ナ」，佢喺 K 鍵；最後取底下嗰個「日」，佢喺 A 鍵，所以成個碼就係 JKA。點解係咁拆呢？因為「者」係一個整體字，拆嘅時候唔分字首字身，只係順住筆勢由頭到尾攞三個碼——頭「十」、次「ナ」、尾「日」，啱啱夠三碼就停。記住個口訣：十字撐頭，斜筆一撇，日頭墊底，JKA 就係讀者嘅「者」。

而.en: Today's character is 而, read ji4, the little connecting word you already know from 而且 and 而家, meaning something like "and" or "and then." Look at the shape: it doesn't break cleanly into a left and right or a top and bottom, which makes it a whole character (整體字), so instead of the usual head-and-tail split we take four parts in a fixed order — head, second, third, tail. Following that rule, the flat top stroke is 一 on the M key, then the open box 冂 on the B key, then the first inner vertical 中 on the L key, and the last inner vertical 中 again on the L key, giving you the full code MBLL. Hold onto the phrase "一冂中中": one stroke on top, one box around it, and two little verticals standing side by side inside — and there's your 而.
而.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「而」，讀做 ji4，意思係「而且」、「而家」嗰個連接詞，用嚟串連兩件事。你望住個字形，佢係一個典型嘅整體字——冇明顯分成左右或者上下嘅字首字身，所以我哋唔可以照平時嘅頭尾拆法，而係要用整體字嘅特別規矩：取頭、二、三、尾四個部分。跟住呢個規矩，最頂嗰橫係「一」，喺 M 鍵；接住個框係「冂」，喺 B 鍵；再嚟裏面第一豎係「中」，喺 L 鍵；最後尾嗰豎又係「中」，一樣喺 L 鍵，所以全碼就係 MBLL。記住呢個口訣「一冂中中」，你就會諗起：一畫戴頂，一個框罩住，裏面兩支豎企齊齊，「而」就砌好喇。

聚.en: Today we're learning 聚, read zeoi6, meaning to assemble, to meet together, or to gather up, as in 聚集 (zeoi6 zaap6, to come together) and 聚會 (zeoi6 wui6, a gathering or party). Look at the character and you'll see it splits into a top and a bottom: the top is 尸 plus 又, and the bottom is the character 眾. Cangjie follows exactly that division — the top provides the 字首, giving 尸 (S) then 又 (E), while the lower 眾 is the 字身, which breaks down into three 人 shapes (O, O, O), so from start to finish you type SEOOO. Why three O's in a row? Because the 字身 眾 is literally built from three stacked 人, and a 字身 can take up to three codes, so all three 人 get typed out. Here's your hook: the top is 尸 and 又 side by side, and underneath three people crowd together — a crowd gathering is exactly what 聚 means, and tonight we're all gathering together.
聚.zh: 今日我哋學「聚」呢個字，讀做 zeoi6，意思係「聚集、相聚、聚攏埋一齊」，就好似「聚集」（zeoi6 zaap6，即係集合起嚟）同「聚會」（zeoi6 wui6，即係一班人相聚嘅場合）咁樣。你望住個字，會見到上面同下面兩大部分：上面係「尸」加「又」，下面係一個「眾」字。倉頡就係咁樣分嘅——上面取「尸」（S）同「又」（E）做字首，而下面嘅「眾」係字身，拆出三個「人」（O、O、O），所以由頭到尾打出嚟就係 SEOOO。點解會有三個 O 咁多？因為「眾」呢個字身係由三個「人」疊埋組成，字身唔止兩個碼，可以取盡到三個，於是三個「人」全部要打出嚟。記住呢個口訣：上面尸又一齊，下面三個人聚埋，人多就係「聚」，就好記喇——我哋今晚一齊聚會。

聯.en: Today's character is 聯, read lyun4, meaning to connect or join together — you'll meet it in 聯合 (lyun4 hap6, to unite or ally) and 聯盟 (lyun4 mang4, an alliance or coalition). Look at its build: on the left is the ear radical 耳, and on the right sits a busy, crowded body. Cangjie gives the radical and the body separate quotas, and here the left-side 耳 acts as the radical taking only head and tail — the 尸 (S) at the top and the 十 (J) at the bottom; then the body takes head, second and tail — 女 (V), then 戈 (I), then 廿 (T) at the end, giving you SJVIT. As a memory hook, picture an ear (尸十) pressed against the right side, where 女, 戈 and 廿 are all strung together — everything 'joined' into one. Try the sentence: 我哋要聯絡佢 — We need to contact him.
聯.zh: 今日學嘅字係「聯」，讀作 lyun4，意思係聯繫、連埋一齊，好似「聯合」（lyun4 hap6，即係聯手、結盟）同「聯盟」（lyun4 mang4，聯合起嚟嘅組織）咁樣。你望吓佢個結構，左邊係耳字部「耳」，右邊係一嚿好複雜嘅字身。倉頡拆字有個規矩：字首同字身各有配額，左邊嘅「耳」做字首，只可以取頭尾兩碼，即係頭嘅尸（S）同尾嘅十（J）；跟住嘅字身就取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係女（V），第二係戈（I），最尾係廿（T），合埋成 SJVIT。記住呢個字嘅時候，可以諗成一隻「耳」（尸十）貼住個右邊，右邊由女、戈、廿三個部件串連起嚟，就好似個個部件都「聯」埋一齊咁。造句練習：我哋要聯絡佢。

聲.en: Today we learn 聲, read as sing1 or seng1, meaning sound, voice, or tone — as in 聲音 sing1 jam1 (sound) or 大聲 daai6 seng1 (loudly). The character stacks into two parts: on top is 殸, and beneath it sits an 耳 (ear), and everything about it points back to sound and hearing. When Cangjie codes it, the top 殸 becomes the 字首 (leading part), and because it is a busy shape we take just its head and tail — 土 (G) first, then 水 (E); the bottom 耳 is the 字身 (body part), and it too gives head and tail — 尸 (S) at the head and 十 (J) at the tail. Put those four together and you get exactly GESJ. To remember it, picture speaking 大聲 out loud, then listening with that 耳 at the bottom — the ear is the piece that catches every sound.
聲.zh: 今日我哋學「聲」呢個字，讀音係 sing1 或者 seng1，意思係聲音、聲調，好似「聲音」sing1 jam1 咁樣，又或者「大聲」daai6 seng1 咁講。呢個字上下兩截：上面係「殸」，下面係一隻「耳」，全部意思都圍住聲音同耳仔嚟講。倉頡取碼嘅時候，上面嘅「殸」做字首，因為佢係複雜嘅字形，就取頭尾兩碼——先攞土（G），再攞水（E）；跟住下面嘅「耳」做字身，同樣取頭尾——頭係尸（S），尾係十（J），所以成個字砌埋就係 GESJ。你記住：字首取頭尾、字身都取頭尾，土水尸十，一路打落去就啱。想記嘅話，就諗住「大聲講嘢用把口，聽聲就要用耳」，下面隻耳仔就係關鍵。

職.en: Today we learn 職, read zik1, meaning duty, profession, or a job — the kind of thing you'd call your line of work. The character splits left and right: the head on the left is 耳, and the body on the right is 戠. Because 耳 is the head piece, Cangjie takes just first-and-last, giving you 尸 S and 十 J; the body 戠 is more crowded, and a body can take up to three codes, so we take head-second-last: 卜 Y, 戈 I, and 日 A, which all together spell SJYIA. Here's your hook: picture landing a good job — the 耳 (S J) is your ear listening to the boss, and the 戠 (Y I A) is the post you hold, just as in 職業 zik1 jip6 (occupation) and 職位 zik1 wai6 (position).
職.zh: 我哋今日學「職」呢個字，讀作 zik1，係職務、職業嘅意思，好似「份工」咁。呢個字分做左右兩邊：左邊字首係「耳」，右邊字身係「戠」。左邊嘅「耳」係一個部件，倉頡取頭同尾，所以攞到頭一個字形「尸」S、同埋尾嘅「十」J；右邊嘅「戠」比較複雜，字身可以攞到三碼，所以取頭、二、尾，即係「卜」Y、「戈」I、同埋「日」A，合埋成 SJYIA。你可以咁記：搵到份好工，個「耳」仔（S J）就聽住老闆講嘢，右邊嗰個「戠」（Y I A）就係你嘅崗位——例如「職業」zik1 jip6、「職位」zik1 wai6，都係講你喺邊個位置做嘢。

聽.en: This character is 聽, read teng1, ting3, or ting1, and it means to hear, to listen, and by extension to understand or to obey. Look at its structure: on the left there is an ear, 耳, and on the right sits the body. When Cangjie breaks it down, the left part 耳 gives only its head and tail — 尸 is S and 土 is G — so the left contributes SG; the body then takes its head, middle, and tail, with 十 as J, 田 as W, and 心 as P, giving the full code SGJWP. The reason the split falls this way is the quota rule: when a character divides into a lead part (字首) and a body (字身), the lead takes at most two codes, leaving the rest for the body. Here is your hook: your ears (SG) use the heart (P) to listen — hear it, take it to heart.
聽.zh: 呢個字係「聽」，讀 teng1、ting3 或者 ting1，意思係用耳仔去聽、去聆聽，引申仲有明白同埋服從嘅意思。你睇佢個結構：左邊係一隻「耳」，右邊係字身。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，字首「耳」淨係取頭尾兩碼——「尸」係 S、「土」係 G，所以字首就係 SG；然後字身就照頭、身、尾三碼嚟取，「十」係 J、「田」係 W、「心」係 P，合埋成 SGJWP。點解字首只取兩碼、字身取三碼呢？因為倉頡規定：當一個字分成字首同字身，字首最多取兩碼，剩返嘅碼數就留畀字身。記住呢句：耳仔（SG）用心（P）去聽——用耳去聽，記入心。

肉.en: Today we're learning 肉, read juk6, which means flesh or meat — the kind you eat, like beef or pork. Look at its shape: there's a box on the outside with two little 人 people packed inside it. This character is a whole-shape character (整體字) that can't be cleanly split into a head and body, so Cangjie uses a special rule: for a whole shape you take at most three codes — the first, the second, and the last — and skip whatever sits in the middle. So you start with the outer frame 冂, which is the O key; then the first 人 inside, which is the B key; the next 人 sits in the middle, so you skip it entirely; and finally the last 人, which is O again, giving you OBO. Remember it this way: one box, two people standing in a row inside — you grab the first and the last, let the middle one go, and you've built a piece of 肉.
肉.zh: 今日我哋學「肉」呢個字，讀做 juk6，意思就係我哋食嘅肉，好似牛肉、豬肉嘅肉。你望吓佢個樣，外面有一個框框，入面塞住兩個人字。呢個字係一個整體字，冇得清清楚楚分做字首同字身，所以倉頡有一條特別規則：整體字最多取頭、二、尾三個碼，中間嘅嘢就要跳過。你先寫外框嘅冂，個鍵係 O；再寫入面上面嗰個人字，個鍵係 B；跟住本來仲有一個人字，但佢喺中間，要跳過唔取；最後取埋尾嗰個人字，個鍵又係 O，所以成個碼就係 OBO。記住喇：一個框，入面兩個人排排企，你淨係捉頭尾兩個，中間嗰個放佢走，咁就砌成一舊「肉」喇。

肥.en: Today we learn 肥, read fei4, meaning fat or plump — and when we talk about soil it can mean fertile too. Look at it: on the left is the flesh-moon radical ⺼, and on the right is the character 巴, one part giving the body and one hinting at the sound, so it reads sensibly. When we split it, the head takes the left-hand flesh-moon ⺼, which lives on B; then the body is 巴, and because 巴 is a whole unit we take its first-and-last pieces — the top 日 on A and the bottom 山 on U — giving BAU. Here's your hook: flesh-moon B to start, then 巴's top 日 (A) and bottom 山 (U) — think of a 肥仔 you want to slim down!
肥.zh: 今日我哋學「肥」呢個字，讀作 fei4，即係肥胖、肥膩嘅意思，講食物又可以指肥沃。你望吓佢，左邊係肉月部⺼，右邊係一個「巴」字，一個係身體、一個係聲，好合理啦。拆字嘅時候，字首取左邊嘅肉月⺼，喺 B 鍵度；跟住字身係個「巴」字，佢係一個成件嘅字身，所以要用頭尾碼——頭係最上面嘅日 A，尾係最下面嘅山 U，合埋就係 BAU。記住個口訣：肉月⺼開頭 B，「巴」字頭日 A 尾山 U，你想減肥就記住「B 個肥仔」啦！

肯.en: Today's character is 「肯」, read hang2, meaning willing or to consent — as in 「佢唔肯食飯」, he refuses (is unwilling) to eat. Notice it's built top over bottom: the top is 止 and the bottom is ⺼, the flesh radical. When Cangjie splits this, the top 止 becomes the head part, but a head part can only give at most two codes, so we don't spell out all of 止 (whose own full code is YLM) — instead we take its first and last: the head 卜 is Y and the tail 一 is M, giving YM. Then the bottom ⺼ serves as the body, and since it's a whole unit we simply take B, so 「肯」 in full is YMB. Remember it this way: the top 止 lends only its first and last, 卜一 (YM), and the flesh radical below adds B — willingly, YMB!
肯.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「肯」，讀音係 hang2，解作「肯願意、答應」，好似「佢唔肯食飯」就係話佢唔願意食。你留意個字係上下兩橛砌成，上面係「止」，下面係「⺼」，即係肉字旁。倉頡拆字嘅時候，上面嘅「止」做字首，但係字首最多只可以取兩碼，所以我哋唔會將成個「止」（佢自己嘅碼係 YLM）拆晒，而係取佢嘅頭同尾——頭碼係「卜」Y，尾碼係「一」M，砌埋就係 YM。跟住落嚟下面嘅「⺼」做字身，佢係一個成體字，直接取「B」一碼就得，所以「肯」全碼就係 YMB。記住個口訣：上面「止」淨係借頭尾卜一（YM），下面肉字旁補返個 B，肯定就係 YMB！

育.en: Today we learn 育, read "juk6," meaning to produce, to give birth, to raise, to educate. Look at the character: on top there's a shape 𠫓, and underneath sits a 月. The character breaks into a head and a body: the head 𠫓 is a complex shape, and Cangjie has a rule that a complex head gives only its first and last codes, so we take the opening stroke 亠, which is Y, and its closing piece 厶, which is I; then we drop to the body 月 — the flesh-moon form we call ⺼ — which is a single B. Put the three together and you get Y, I, B, that is YIB. To remember it, picture the top holding its two ends Y and I, then a single 月 below — the head bookending, and one B nurturing a new character into being.
育.zh: 今日我哋學「育」字，讀「juk6」，即係生育、養育、教育嘅意思。你望住呢個字，上面係一個「𠫓」形，下面就係一個「月」形。呢個字分做字首同字身兩橛：字首「𠫓」係一個複雜嘅形，倉頡有個規矩，複雜嘅字首只取頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋喺度攞頭嗰筆「亠」，就係Y，再攞尾嗰個「厶」，就係I；跟住落到字身「月」，即係我哋叫「⺼」嗰個肉月旁，一碼就係B。三碼合埋就係Y、I、B，即係YIB。記住嘅時候，你可以諗成「頭尾夾住一個月」——上面攞頭尾Y、I，下面淨係一個B，養育出一個新嘅字。

能.en: Today we learn 能, read "nang4," meaning to be able or capable — the "can" in words like 可能 (can, possible) and 能夠 (to be able to). Look at it: on the left you have 厶 sitting on top of a 月 (here written as the ⺼ flesh radical), and on the right two little 匕 shapes side by side. When we split it, the 字首 (leading part) takes 厶 and 月: 厶 is I and 月 (⺼) is B, so the head fills its two codes and stops there; then the 字身 (body) is the pair of 匕 on the right, and since 匕 is P, the two of them give P and P, making the full code IBPP. Memory hook: left side 厶+月 (I, B), right side two daggers 匕 (P, P) — flesh on one side, two little knives on the other.
能.zh: 今日我哋學「能」呢個字，讀「nang4」，意思係「能夠」、「有能力做到」，好似「可能」、「能夠」咁樣，係好常用嘅字。你望住佢，會見到左手邊係「厶」加「月」（其實呢度嘅「月」寫成⺼肉字邊），右手邊就係兩隻並排嘅「匕」。拆碼嘅時候，字首取「厶月」兩件，「厶」係I、「月」（⺼）係B，字首兩碼取足就停，跟住輪到字身，字身係右邊兩隻匕，「匕」係P，兩隻就打P、P，所以全碼係IBPP。記住喇：左邊厶月（I、B），右邊兩把匕首（P、P）——「能力」就係一邊肉一邊兩把匕。

腦.en: Today we learn 腦, read nou5, meaning the brain inside your head. Notice the left side is ⺼ (the flesh radical), which lives on the B key and marks body parts — many body-related characters use it. The right side is built from two 巛 shapes stacked up carrying a 囟 underneath; 巛 sits on the V key and 囟 sits on the W key. The split works like this: the head ⺼ takes just one code, B, and the body takes its first 巛, its second 巛, and its final 囟 for three codes, giving BVVW altogether. To remember it, picture a lump of flesh (B) holding up two streams of water (V, V) flowing into a fontanelle (W) — that's your 電腦 and your 頭腦, as in 我個腦好攰。
腦.zh: 今日我哋學「腦」呢個字，讀音係 nou5，即係頭殼入面嘅腦袋。你留意佢左邊係「⺼」（肉字邊），呢個部件喺 B 鍵，代表身體器官，好多同身體有關嘅字都用佢。右邊嗰舊嘢係先由兩個「巛」疊住，再托住一個「囟」——「巛」喺 V 鍵，「囟」喺 W 鍵。拆法係咁樣：字首「⺼」只取一碼 B，字身就取頭嘅「巛」、次嘅「巛」同尾嘅「囟」共三碼，合埋就係 BVVW。記住呢個字，你可以諗成「一舊肉（B）頂住兩條川水（V、V）流入個囟門（W）」，就係你個電腦、你個頭腦嘞，好似「我個腦好攰。」。

腩.en: Today we learn 腩, read naam5, the Cantonese word for the fatty meat on a cow's belly — the stuff in 牛腩 (brisket) and 豬腩肉 (pork belly). Look at the character: on the left sits ⺼, the flesh-moon radical, and on the right stands the whole 南. The piece ⺼ is typed B, and because it is the 字首 (the leading part), we take just its one code, B. Then the right-hand 南 is the 字身 (body), and for a body we take head and tail: it opens with 十 typed J, then the enclosing 冂 typed B, and finally an inner 十 typed J, giving the body J B J. Put it all together and you get B, J, B, J — BJBJ. Here's your memory hook: two B's hugging two J's, flesh (⺼) meeting 南 — flesh beside 南 is 腩, just like that soft fatty layer on a cow's belly!
腩.zh: 今日我哋學「腩」字，讀naam5，喺廣東話入面即係牛腩、豬腩肉嗰啲肚腩上面肥美嘅肉。你望下呢個字，左邊係「⺼」（肉月旁），右邊係一個「南」字。「⺼」呢個部件喺倉頡度撳B，佢做字首，所以淨係取佢一個碼B。跟住右邊嘅「南」做字身，字身要拆頭同尾：起首係「十」撳J，再嚟中間包住嘅「冂」撳B，最後入面又有一個「十」撳J，所以字身取到JBJ三碼。合埋一齊就係B、J、B、J，即係BJBJ。記住呢個字好靚，兩粒B夾住兩粒J，左肉右南，肉貼住南就係「腩」，好似牛肚上面嗰嚿肥肉噉，睇到都想食牛腩喇！

臘.en: Today we learn 臘, read "laap6," which originally meant a year-end sacrifice and later came to mean cured, dried meat — as in 燒臘 (siu mei) and 臘腸 (Chinese sausage). Look at its shape: on the left is ⺼ (the flesh radical), and on the right sits a busy piece called 巤. In Cangjie we split off the 字首 first, and ⺼ is a single-code piece, giving you just B. Then the 字身 巤 follows the head-second-tail rule, and because it contains three repeated 女 shapes stacked below, you take VVV, so the whole code is BVVV. Here's your hook: one slab of meat (B) plus three 女 (VVV) makes fragrant cured meat — think of "我鍾意食臘腸," I like to eat Chinese sausage!
臘.zh: 我哋今日學「臘」呢個字，佢讀「laap6」，本來係指年尾祭祀嘅意思，後來又用嚟講風乾醃製嘅肉，好似「燒臘」、「臘腸」咁。你望下佢個樣，左邊係「⺼」（肉字旁），右邊係一個複雜嘅「巤」。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，先拆字首「⺼」，佢係一個一碼嘅部件，取B。跟住拆字身「巤」，佢下面重複咗三個「女」形，字身要取頭、次、尾三碼，就係VVV三個「女」，所以成個碼砌埋一齊就係BVVV。記住喇：一嚿肉（B）加三個女（VVV），臘肉香噴噴，你會諗起「我鍾意食臘腸」！

自.en: Today we meet 自, read zi6, which means "self" or "oneself," and can also mean "from," as in 嚟自, "to come from." Look at the shape: right at the top there's a single slanting stroke 丿, then underneath sits a boxed frame with lines that looks like an eye — in Cangjie this piece is called ⺫, on the B key — and the bottom portion we treat as 山 on the U key. 自 is an integral character (整體字), so instead of being split into a head and a body, it simply takes three codes across the whole shape: the first, the second, and the last, giving 丿⺫山, typed HBU. As a memory hook, picture a single stroke H perched on top, a little ⺫ box B in the middle, and a mountain 山 U holding it all up — three pieces stacked into the "self" you point to when you say "I did it myself."
自.zh: 今日我哋學「自」呢個字，讀音係 zi6，本身意思係「自己」、「自身」，亦都可以解「由……而來」，好似「嚟自」咁樣。你望住個字，會見到最上面有一撇 丿，跟住下面係一個好似「目」字咁嘅框連橫劃，喺倉頡入面呢一嚿叫做 ⺫，係 B 鍵，最後底下嘅部分我哋當成 山，係 U 鍵。「自」屬於整體字，即係話佢唔會拆做字首同字身兩截，而係一次過取頭、二、尾三個碼，所以就係 丿⺫山，全碼寫做 HBU。你記住喇：一撇 H 起頭，中間一個 ⺫ 框 B，落到底就一座 山 U，三劃砌埋就係講緊「我自己」嗰個「自」。

至.en: Today we meet 至, read zi3, meaning to reach or arrive, and also extremely or very — you see it in 甚至 sam6 zi3, meaning even or so much so that, and in 先至 sin1 zi3, meaning only then or not until. Look at the shape and it stacks into three pieces: a flat 一 on top, which is M; a small 厶 in the middle, which is I; and 土 at the bottom, which is G — so the full code is MIG. Why split it this way? 至 is a whole shape (整體字), one that can't be cleanly divided into a head part and a body part, so instead of hunting for a boundary we just take three codes from head, middle, and tail — head 一 (M), middle 厶 (I), tail 土 (G). Remember it top to bottom: 一 presses on top, 厶 sits in the middle, 土 rests at the base — MIG, flowing straight down.
至.zh: 今日我哋學「至」，讀做 zi3，意思係「到達、去到」，又可以解「極、非常」，好似「甚至」sam6 zi3 咁解「連……都」，或者「先至」sin1 zi3 咁解「至到嗰陣先」。你望下呢個字，佢由三嚿砌成：最頂係一橫「一」，撳 M；中間係個「厶」，撳 I；最底係塊「土」，撳 G，所以成個碼就係 MIG。點解係咁拆呢？因為「至」係一個整體字，冇得清清楚楚咁分開字首同字身，遇到呢種情況我哋唔理界線，直接取頭、中、尾三碼——頭係「一」M、中係「厶」I、尾係「土」G。記住呢句：「一」壓喺頭，「厶」夾喺中，「土」墊喺尾，由上到下 MIG 一氣呵成，就記得個字啦。

致.en: Today we learn 致, read zi3, meaning to send, to deliver or to present — the 致 in 導致, to cause or bring about. Look at the character: on the left is 至 and on the right is 攵, a left-right structure. In Cangjie the head is the left piece 至, whose own full code is MIG (一 M, 厶 I, 土 G), but as a head it may contribute only two codes, so we take its first and last — the 一 M and the 土 G; then the body is the right piece 攵, whose own full code is OK, and the body gives its first and last, the 厶 O and the 夂 K. Put them together and you get 一 M, 土 G, 厶 O, 夂 K, that is MGOK. Memory hook: 至 keeps just its head-and-tail (一土) and 攵 keeps 厶夂, and together they build the 致 in 致意.
致.zh: 今日我哋學「致」字，讀作 zi3，意思係送出、傳達，又或者係「導致」嘅「致」。你望下呢個字，左邊係「至」，右邊係「攵」，係一個左右結構嘅字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，字首就係左邊嘅「至」，佢自己嘅完整碼係 MIG（一 M、厶 I、土 G），但係做字首只可以出兩碼，所以我哋取佢嘅頭同尾，即係頭嘅一 M 同埋尾嘅土 G；跟住字身係右邊嘅「攵」，佢自己完整碼係 OK，字身取頭同尾就係厶 O 同夂 K。所以成個字砌埋一齊就係一 M、土 G、厶 O、夂 K，即係 MGOK。記住嘅竅門：「至」剩返頭尾（一土），「攵」剩返厶夂，就砌成「致意」嘅「致」喇。

與.en: Today's character is 與, read "jyu5," and it carries a rich set of meanings — "and," "with," or "to give" — as in 參與 (caam1 jyu5), meaning to join in or take part, and 參與者, a participant. Look at the shape and start from the very top: even though there's a horizontal stroke up there, Cangjie first takes the little grass-radical piece ⺾, which lives on the H key. Then comes the hard part — the middle of this character is a tangle too dense to break apart cleanly, so instead Cangjie uses the special X "difficult" key to stand in for that whole complicated centre. To finish, we take the tail: the 卜 shape on the Y key and the splayed 八 shape on the C key, giving you HXYC. Remember it as "grass on top, X for the impossible middle, then 卜 and 八 to close."
與.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「與」，讀「jyu5」，佢嘅意思好豐富，可以解「和、同」，好似「參與」（caam1 jyu5）就係加入、投入嘅意思，而「參與者」就係指參加嘅人。你睇個字，起手其實唔係頭上嗰橫，倉頡係先取最頂嗰個似草花頭嘅「⺾」，佢喺 H 鍵度。跟住嚟到最麻煩嘅地方：個字中間結構實在太複雜、太密，倉頡冇辦法乾淨咁拆開，於是索性用一個「難」字碼 X 嚟代替佢，X 就係專門用嚟頂住呢啲難拆位置嘅救兵。最後我哋收尾，取下面嘅「卜」（Y）同埋一撇一捺嘅「八」（C），合埋就係 HXYC；你記住「頭草花、中間太難用 X、尾卜八」，就唔會亂喇。

興.en: Today we're learning 興, which reads hing1 or hing3 and means to thrive, prosper, or flourish — it's the 興 in 興趣, interest. Take a good look at it: the middle is a tangle of crossing strokes, genuinely complex, so we don't try to spell every piece out.
