We start at the top with ⺕, keyed H; then, because the middle is too messy to break down cleanly, Cangjie uses a clever shortcut — the X 難 key stands in for that tangled middle, so you press X; finally we take the two pieces at the bottom, ⺼ keyed B and 八 keyed C, giving us HXBC. Remember it this way: hat on top (⺕, H), a middle so tangled it cries 'difficult' (X 難), and feet of ⺼ and 八 (BC) — when the middle is a mess, call for X.
興.zh: 今日我哋學「興」呢個字，佢讀 hing1 或者 hing3，意思係興旺、繁榮、興盛，好似「興趣」嘅興噉。你望下佢個樣，中間交叉重疊，其實幾複雜，所以拆碼嘅時候我哋唔會逐筆去砌。開頭我哋先取上面個「⺕」，撳 H；跟住個中間位太亂太複雜，砌唔到清楚，所以倉頡有個聰明嘅做法——用 X 難鍵頂替嗰堆亂碼，撳 X；到最尾我哋就取落腳嗰兩件，「⺼」撳 B，「八」撳 C，合埋就係 HXBC。記住個口訣：頭戴⺕（H），中間亂到要「難」（X），腳踩⺼八（BC）——複雜到中間要求救，就係「興」。

舉.en: Today's character is 舉, read geoi2, meaning to raise or lift up, and also to recommend, as in 選舉 (syun2 geoi2, to elect) and 舉行 (geoi2 hang4, to host). Take a look at the whole thing — it's a busy shape stacked from top to bottom, and there's no clean way to split it into a head and a body, so we treat it as a whole-form character. For whole-form characters Cangjie doesn't force a head/body break; instead it takes head, second, and tail — the very first piece, the second piece, and the very last piece. Here the head is 竹 (H), the second piece is 金 (C), and the tail is the 手 sitting at the bottom (Q), giving you HCQ. Remember the line "Raise your hand if you know the answer" — that 手 (Q) is your final key, anchoring the whole code HCQ.
舉.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「舉」，讀作 geoi2，意思係舉起、抬高，亦都可以解推薦，好似「選舉」（syun2 geoi2）同「舉行」（geoi2 hang4）咁。你望吓成個字，佢係一個好複雜、上下堆疊嘅字形，好難清楚咁分做字首同字身兩橛——呢種字我哋叫做整體字。遇到整體字，倉頡唔會硬拆做首尾兩部分，而係用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法取碼，即係揀最頭嗰個部件、第二個部件，同埋最尾嗰個部件。所以「舉」嘅字頭係「竹」（H），第二個部件係「金」（C），最尾係下面嗰隻「手」（Q），砌埋一齊就係 HCQ。記住呢句：「識答就舉手」——舉手嘅「手」（Q）就係最尾嗰個尾碼，幫你記住成組 HCQ。

舖.en: Today we meet 舖, read pou3, the word for a shop or store — the 舖 in 店舖 and 舖頭. Look at it: the left side is 舍 and the right side is 甫, and Cangjie splits it into a head part and a body part. The head 舍 is a busy shape, so it only gives its first and last pieces — 人 (O) and 口 (R) — making OR; then the body 甫 gives three pieces, head, second, and last: 戈 (I), 十 (J), and 月 (B), spelling IJB. Put them together and you get ORIJB, a full five keys. Remember it this way: 舍 opens with one 人 and one 口 (OR), 甫 follows with 戈-十-月 (IJB), and your shop swings its doors open.
舖.zh: 今日我哋學「舖」呢個字，讀 pou3，即係「店舖」、「舖頭」嗰個舖，意思就係做生意嘅鋪頭、商店。你睇吓佢，左邊係「舍」，右邊係「甫」，倉頡就分做字首同字身兩橛嚟拆。字首「舍」係一個較複雜嘅部件，所以只取頭尾兩碼——頭係「人」（O），尾係「口」（R），砌成 OR；跟住字身「甫」就用頭、二、尾三碼，取「戈」（I）、「十」（J）、「月」（B），連埋成 IJB。合埋就係 ORIJB，五碼齊全。記法係：左邊「舍」得頭尾一人一口（OR），右邊「甫」一戈一十一月（IJB），一間開咗門嘅舖頭就砌好嘞。

色.en: Today we learn 色, read sik1, which means colour or hue — you meet it in words like 綠色 luk6 sik1 (green) and 黑色 hak1 sik1 (black). Look at how it stacks up: there's a little ⺈ up top like a small blade, a 日 (sun) tucked in the middle, and a 山 (mountain) sitting at the bottom. Because this is a whole character whose pieces can't be neatly split into a separate head-part and body-part, we treat it as an integral shape and simply take the head, the second piece, and the tail: ⺈ is N, 日 is A, and 山 is U, giving you NAU. Picture the little cap ⺈ on the sun 日, and the sun resting on the mountain 山 — top to bottom, N-A-U — and say to yourself 我鍾意藍色 (I like the colour blue) to lock it in.
色.zh: 今日我哋學「色」呢個字，讀作 sik1，即係顏色、色彩嘅意思，好似「綠色」luk6 sik1 同「黑色」hak1 sik1咁。你望下佢嘅結構，上面有個好似刀嘅⺈，中間夾住個「日」，下面就係個「山」字。呢個字冚唪唥砌埋一齊、拆唔開清楚嘅字首字身，我哋當佢係整體字咁處理，所以就取頭、取二、取尾三個碼：頭係⺈按 N，第二個「日」按 A，尾就係「山」按 U，合埋就係 NAU。記住喇，⺈個帽戴喺個「日」頭，「日」又踩住個「山」，由上到下 N、A、U 三步就砌好個色，你可以講句「我鍾意藍色」嚟幫自己記住。

花.en: Today we learn 花, read faa1, meaning a flower or to blossom. Look at its shape: up top sits the grass radical 艹, and beneath it is the character 化. In Cangjie the head is that topmost grass radical 艹, whose key is T — the moment you see it you think of plants. What follows is the body 化, and a body doesn't get spelled out in full; you take only its head and tail, so the head 亻 gives O and the tail 匕 gives P, making the whole code T, O, P. Here's your hook: pop a grass hat T on the character 化, keep just its head O and tail P, and grass over 化 blooms into 花.
花.zh: 今日我哋學「花」呢個字，讀faa1，即係花朵、開花嘅意思。你睇吓佢嘅樣，上面有個草花頭「艹」，下面係「化」字。倉頡拆字，字首就係最上面嘅草花頭「艹」，佢嘅鍵係T，一睇就知同植物有關。跟住落嚟就係字身「化」，字身唔會逐部分全部拆晒，只係取頭尾兩碼——頭係「亻」，鍵係O，尾係「匕」，鍵係P，所以成個字係T、O、P。記住喇：頭頂戴住草帽T，個「化」字剩返頭尾O同P，草花配化就係花！

芳.en: Today we learn 芳, read fong1, meaning fragrant, sweet-smelling, and by extension beautiful or virtuous in character. Look at its shape: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath sits the whole character 方, like plants giving off their scent. When we split it, the character-head takes 艹 first, which lives on the T key; then the body 方 is coded with three parts — first, second, and last — so we take the head 卜 on Y, the middle 竹 on H, and the tail 尸 on S, giving us TYHS. To remember it, think of Kwai Fong (葵芳) station in Hong Kong, or the sentence 花園好芳香 — grass on top, 方 below, and out comes the fragrance.
芳.zh: 今日我哋學「芳」呢個字，讀做 fong1，意思係香、芬芳，亦都可以形容人品德美好。你睇下佢嘅結構，上面係草花頭「艹」，下面就係一個「方」字，好似形容花草嘅香味咁自然。拆字嘅時候，字首先取上面嘅艹，佢喺 T 鍵；跟住落嚟字身就係「方」，字身要取頭、二、尾三部分，所以取「方」嘅頭「卜」喺 Y 鍵、中間「一」形嘅「竹」喺 H 鍵、最後個尾「尸」喺 S 鍵，合埋就係 TYHS。想記住佢，你就諗下香港嘅「葵芳」站，或者一句「花園好芳香」，草花頭下面一個方，香味就出嚟喇。

苑.en: Today we meet 苑, read jyun2, meaning a pasture, park or garden — and sometimes a grand mansion, as in 花苑, a garden estate. Look at its build: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and below is the piece 夗, stacked one above the other. Because it splits top-and-bottom, the character head takes just that grass top 艹 on key T; then the lower body 夗 follows the first-second-last rule for a body, so we pick 乛 (N), 戈 (I), and skip to the final 凵 (U), giving TNIU altogether. Remember it this way: a grass hat on top (T), and beneath it a body held up by head, waist and feet (N, I, U) framing the garden.
苑.zh: 今日我哋學「苑」字，讀音係 jyun2，意思係花園、園林，又或者係大宅嘅意思，好似「花苑」咁樣。你望吓佢嘅結構：上面係草花頭「艹」，下面係一個「夗」字，係上下兩橛砌成嘅。因為係上下拆法，上面嘅字首就淨係取「艹」呢一橛，撳鍵 T；跟住落到下面嘅字身「夗」，字身要取頭、次、尾三碼，所以順住寫落去揀「乛」（N）、「戈」（I），再跳到最尾嘅「凵」（U），合埋就係 TNIU。記住呢個字：頭戴草帽（T），身有頭、腰、腳三點（N、I、U）撐起成個花園。

英.en: Today we learn 英, read jing1. It originally means petal or flower-leaf, can also mean brave or a hero, and very commonly stands for England or English. Look at the character: there's a grass radical on top and the piece 央 sitting underneath, so we split it by dealing with that top radical first. The top 艹 is the head, coded T, while the lower 央 is the body, and by the coding rule the body takes head-second-last: 中 L, 月 B, 大 K, giving the full code TLBK. Why does 央 split that way? Because as a body it's too complex to be taken whole, so we represent it by its first code plus the last two — L, B, K — rather than tracing every stroke. Remember it like this: hat of grass T, then the body LBK, and you can say '我識講英文' — I can speak English!
英.zh: 今日我哋學「英」字，讀做 jing1，本義係花瓣、花葉，又可以解勇敢、英雄，仲好常用嚟指英國、英文。你望住個字，上面有個草花頭，下面係「央」字，所以拆碼時要先睇上面呢個部首。上邊嘅「艹」係字首，取碼 T；下邊嘅「央」係字身，按取碼規則要拆頭、二、尾，就係「中」L、「月」B、「大」K，合埋成 TLBK。點解「央」要咁拆呢？因為佢做字身，形狀複雜到唔可以整個當一件，要用頭一碼加最尾兩碼嚟代表，所以係 L、B、K 而唔係逐筆拆。記住喇：頭戴草帽 T，身入 LBK，你就講到「我識講英文」啦！

茶.en: Today we learn 茶, read caa4 — the tea you sip at a Hong Kong café. Look at its shape: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath a person 人 stands over wood 木, as if someone is out among the tea trees picking leaves. When we break it down, the head is 艹, which gives us the key T; the body below has many strokes, and Cangjie has a rule that when a body is crowded you take only its first and last parts and drop the middle, so we grab 人 (O) and the final 木 (D), skipping what lies between — put together that spells TOD. Here's your memory hook: grass on top, a person standing on wood picking tea, T-O-D, time for a cup of tea.
茶.zh: 今日我哋學「茶」呢個字，讀作 caa4，即係你去茶餐廳飲嘅嗰杯嘢。你望下佢個樣，最上面有個草花頭「艹」，下面就係一個人「人」企喺樹木「木」之上，好似人喺茶樹之間採茶咁。拆碼嘅時候，字首係「艹」，我哋取佢個 T 鍵；跟住落嚟嘅字身筆畫多，倉頡有個規矩，就係取頭同尾兩部分，慳返中間，所以我哋只攞「人」（O）同最後嘅「木」（D），中間嗰啲就唔理佢，砌埋一齊就係 TOD。記住個口訣：草花頭上，一個人企喺木上面採茶，T-O-D，飲杯茶啦。

荃.en: Today we learn 荃, read cyun4, meaning an aromatic herb or a fine cloth — but the name you'll know best is 荃灣, Tsuen Wan out in the New Territories. Look at its shape: it stacks in two layers, with the grass radical 艹 sitting on top and the character 全 underneath. When we split it, the top comes first as the head, so 艹 is taken on its key T, and then we drop down to the body 全. A body in Cangjie takes at most three codes, so we read it first-second-last: 全 opens with 人 on key O, has 一 in the middle on key M, and ends with 土 on key G — put together that gives TOMG. Remember it this way: grass on top over a 全, T leads off and O, M, G finish — that's the 荃 in Tsuen Wan!
荃.zh: 今日我哋學「荃」呢個字，讀音係 cyun4，意思係一種香草，亦可以指幼細嘅布，不過對你嚟講，最熟悉嘅一定係「荃灣」呢個地名。你睇吓佢嘅樣，係上下兩層：上面係草花頭「艹」，下面係「全」字。拆碼嘅時候，上面嘅字首先取「艹」，佢個鍵係 T，跟住落到下面嘅字身「全」。字身喺倉頡入面最多取三碼，所以用頭、二、尾嘅方法：「全」開頭係「人」，個鍵係 O，中間係「一」，個鍵係 M，最尾係「土」，個鍵係 G，砌埋一齊就係 TOMG。記住呢個字嘅口訣：草花頭底下一個「全」，T 開路，O、M、G 收尾，就係荃灣個「荃」！

荷.en: Today we learn the character 荷, read ho4 or ho6, meaning a lotus or water lily, and also standing for Holland. Look at how it's built: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath is the whole character 何, like a lotus flower resting on the water plants above it. When we break it into codes, we first take the head 艹, which is T on your keyboard; then we work through the body 何, and since a body takes its head, its middle, and its tail, we pick the head 人 as O, then the middle 一 as M, and finally the tail 口 as R, giving us TOMR. Here's your memory hook: under the grass stands a person 何, with one stroke and a mouth beneath — that's the lotus blooming on the water.
荷.zh: 今日我哋學「荷」呢個字，讀作 ho4 或者 ho6，意思係荷花、水生嘅蓮，亦都可以指荷蘭。你望吓佢嘅結構：上面係草花頭「艹」，下面就係一個「何」字，好似荷花坐喺水草上面咁樣。拆碼嘅時候，我哋先取字首「艹」，佢喺鍵盤上係 T；跟住落嚟就要拆字身「何」，字身取碼要取頭、取尾，中間再夾一個，所以先取佢個頭「人」係 O，再取中間嘅「一」係 M，最後取尾嘅「口」係 R，合埋就係 TOMR。你可以咁樣記：草花頭下面企住一個「何」人，一橫一個口，荷花就開喺水面。

莉.en: Today we learn 莉, read lei6, which means the white jasmine flower — you'll often see it in girls' names like 薩莉 (Sally) and 瑪莉 (Mary). Look at its shape: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath sits 利, stacked one above the other. When we split it, the head 艹 is a single complete piece that takes just one code, T; then the body 利 gives up its head ⺮ as H, its second piece 木 as D, and its tail 弓 as N, so the whole thing spells THDN. The rule to remember is that the grass head takes one code, and the body below gives head, second, and tail — three positions. Picture the line 茉莉花好香, jasmine flowers smell nice, and let that fragrance lock in this T-headed character.
莉.zh: 今日我哋學「莉」呢個字，讀音係 lei6，意思係白色嘅茉莉花，好多女仔嘅名都會用到佢，好似「薩莉」（Sally）同「瑪莉」（Mary）咁。你望吓佢嘅樣，上面係草花頭「艹」，下面就係「利」，係一個上下疊埋嘅結構。拆碼嘅時候，字首「艹」係一個完整嘅部件，得一碼 T；跟住落嚟嘅字身「利」就取頭「⺮」係 H、第二筆「木」係 D、最後嘅「弓」係 N，合埋就係 THDN。你可以記住：草花頭下面攞頭、二、尾三個位，咁就啱晒；諗起「茉莉花好香」，個香味就幫你記住呢個 T 頭嘅字啦。

菜.en: Today we learn 菜, read coi3, meaning vegetables, a dish, or an item you order at a restaurant. Look at its shape: a grass radical sits on top, and below it is the character 采. The grass radical is called 艹 and lives on the T key — you'll meet it again and again in words about plants. The lower part, the body 采, has many strokes, but a body can contribute at most three codes, so instead of breaking it into every piece we use the first-last method, taking its opening 爫 (the B key) and its closing 木 (the D key), skipping whatever sits between. Put it together and the code is 艹T, 爫B, 木D. Remember it this way: grass on top, 采 below, and there's your plate of 菜 — as in Tung Choi Street, the vegetables you eat: I eat a lot of vegetables.
菜.zh: 今日我哋學「菜」呢個字，讀coi3，意思係蔬菜、餸菜，又或者係喺餐廳嗌嘅一道菜。你望下佢嘅樣：上面一個草花頭，下面係一個「采」字。草花頭我哋叫艹，喺鍵盤上面撳T，佢喺好多同植物有關嘅字都會見到。下面嘅字身「采」筆畫比較多，一個字身最多只可以取三碼，所以我哋唔會逐部分拆晒，而係用「頭尾取碼」嘅方法，攞佢最頭嘅爫（撳B）同最尾嘅木（撳D），中間就跳過。所以成個字合埋就係艹T、爫B、木D。記住喇：草花頭底下一個采，就係你日日食嘅「菜」，好似通菜街嘅通菜咁——我食好多菜。

華.en: Today's character is 華, read "waa4", which in the word 中華 refers to China, and can also mean flowery or illustrious, as in something splendid and radiant. Take a good look: on top sits the grass radical 艹, with some horizontal strokes in the middle, and a firm 十 planted at the bottom, giving the whole thing a balanced, upright feel. This is a whole-character shape, one that can't be cleanly divided into a head part and a body part, so we use the whole-character method and take four pieces — the head, the second, the third, and the last: first the grass radical 艹 (T), then 一 (M), then 廿 (T), and finally 十 (J), spelling TMTJ. Remember the rhythm of head-second-third-last, with grass blooming on top and a cross holding it steady below — 華 is the character where the flowers bloom brightest.
華.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「華」，讀「waa4」，喺「中華」入面就係指中國嘅意思，亦都可以解「華麗」嘅「華」，形容繁花似錦、光彩照人。你望吓個字，頂上係草花頭「艹」，落嚟中間有橫嘅一啲筆畫，底下企住個「十」，成個字睇落好對稱、好挺拔。呢個字係一個「整體字」，冇辦法清楚咁切開字首同字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅取碼法，攞頭、二、三、尾四個部件：先係草花頭「艹」（T），跟住係「一」（M），再嚟係「廿」（T），最後係「十」（J），砌成 TMTJ。記住呢個口訣——頭二三尾，草花開喺頂、十字撐喺底，「華」就係花開得最燦爛嘅一個字。

萬.en: Today we learn 萬, read maan6, meaning ten thousand or, by extension, countless and innumerable — you'll see it in 百萬 (baak3 maan6), a million, and 萬人 (maan6 jan4), ten thousand people or everyone. Look at its shape: on top sits the grass radical 艹, which is T, and below is a busy body made of 田 (W), 中 (L), and the bottom flesh piece ⺼ (B). Why does it split this way? The top 艹 is the prefix, and a prefix contributes only one code, T; the remaining body then takes first-second-last, so counting from the top we grab 田 (W) and 中 (L), then jump to the final piece ⺼ (B). Put it all together and you get TWLB — grass on top, and the field, the centre, and the flesh stacked below into one rich character, easy to recall the moment you picture a man with ten thousand dollars.
萬.zh: 我哋今日學「萬」呢個字，讀做 maan6，即係一萬嘅萬，亦都可以解「無數、好多」，例如「百萬」（baak3 maan6）就係一百個一萬，「萬人」（maan6 jan4）就係一萬人或者所有人。你望下佢個樣，上邊有個草花頭「艹」，係 T 掣；下邊個字身望落好複雜，係「田」（W 掣）、「中」（L 掣），再加底部嘅肉字邊「⺼」（B 掣）。點解會咁拆呢？因為上邊個艹係字首，字首淨係取一碼，就係 T；跟住落嚟嘅字身要取「頭、次、尾」三碼，所以由頭數起攞「田」W、「中」L，再跳到最尾嘅「⺼」B。合埋就係 TWLB，草花頭喺頂，底下田中肉三件砌成一個豐盛嘅「萬」，你有一萬蚊嗰陣就記得晒喇。

落.en: Today's character is 落, read lok6, as in 落雨 (to rain) or 落樓 (go downstairs) — it means to fall or drop, and can also mean the net amount left over. Look at its shape: on top sits 艹, the grass radical, which you type with T, and underneath is the block 洛. When Cangjie splits this, the top 艹 becomes the head and takes one code, T, while the whole 洛 below becomes the body; since a body takes at most three codes, we grab first-one and last-two — the three-dots-of-water 氵 with E, then 竹 with H, then the mouth 口 with R, giving TEHR. Picture grass up top and water trickling down past the bamboo and the mouth — everything falling downward, and that's 落.
落.zh: 今日學嘅字係「落」，讀 lok6，好似「落雨」、「落樓」咁，解跌落嚟、掉低嘅意思，亦都可以指淨落嘅數目。你望下佢個樣，上面係「艹」，即係草花頭，喺鍵盤度撳 T；下面就係「洛」。倉頡拆字，最上面嘅「艹」做字首取一碼 T，跟住成個「洛」做字身，字身最多取三碼，於是取頭一尾二——頭係三點水「氵」撳 E，然後係「竹」撳 H，最尾係個口「口」撳 R，砌埋一齊就係 TEHR。記住：草花頭喺天上，水喺下面流過竹同口，一路落落嚟，就係「落」喇。

葵.en: Today we learn 葵, read kwai4 — the 葵 in sunflower, and the same character you see in Hong Kong place names like 葵涌 (Kwai Chung) and 葵芳 (Kwai Fong). Look at its shape: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath rests the character 癸. When we break it down, the grass top comes first as the 字首, which is T. The lower 癸 is the 字身, and since it isn't a whole-piece character, we take three parts — head, middle, tail: the head is 弓 (N), the middle is 人 (O), and the tail is 大 (K). Put together the code is TNOK, starting with the grass hat T and then reading N, O, K down from top to bottom. Memory hook: a grass hat T sits on top, and below a bow 弓 (N) shoots toward a person 人 (O) and something big 大 (K) — that's your葵.
葵.zh: 今日我哋學「葵」呢個字，讀做 kwai4，即係向日葵嗰個「葵」，你成日聽到嘅「葵涌」、「葵芳」都係用呢個字。你望下佢個樣：上面係草花頭「艹」，下面坐住一個「癸」字。拆碼嘅時候，我哋先取草花頭做字首，就係 T。跟住落嚟嘅「癸」係字身，因為字身唔係整體字，我哋要拆頭、身、尾三部分：頭係「弓」，即係 N；中間取「人」，即係 O；最後尾取一個「大」，即係 K。所以四碼砌埋就係 TNOK，草花頭 T 開頭，之後 N、O、K 順住由上到下數落嚟。記住：頭戴草帽 T，下面一個弓（N）射向人（O）同大（K），你就唔會拆錯喇。

薈.en: Today we meet 薈, read "wai3" or "wui6", meaning luxuriant, flourishing, growing thick and abundant. Look at how it stacks: on top sits the grass radical 艹, the familiar plant head, which gives the code letter T. Underneath is the whole character 會 serving as the body, and here's the key rule — when a body is complex, Cangjie doesn't take every stroke but instead takes the first, the second, and the last piece, so from 會 we pull 人 (O) as first, 一 (M) as second, and 日 (A) as the last, giving us TOMA. To fix it in your mind, picture a clump of grass (T) with a meeting (會 = OMA) held beneath it — grass so lush it's positively 薈.
薈.zh: 今日我哋學「薈」呢個字，佢讀「wai3」或者「wui6」，意思係草木茂盛、繁多嘅樣。你睇佢分做上下兩橛：上面係草花頭「艹」，就係我哋熟悉嘅字首，取代碼字母 T。下面係個「會」字做字身。倉頡拆字身嘅時候，唔會逐筆全取，而係取頭、二再加最後一橛，所以「會」入面我哋揀「人」（O）做第一，「一」（M）做第二，最後再取底下嘅「日」（A），合埋成 TOMA。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成「一叢草（T）下面開會（會=OMA）」，草長得咁茂盛，真係好薈啊。

薩.en: Today's character is 「薩」, read saat3, and it doesn't really carry a meaning of its own — it's used mostly to transliterate foreign sounds, like the 「薩」 in 「菩薩」 (bodhisattva), or in names and foods such as 「披薩」 (pizza) and 「薩莉」 (Sally). Look at the character: on top sits the grass radical 「艹」, which is T, and it serves as the 字首; everything underneath is the 字身. In Cangjie a 字身 takes at most three codes, so we choose a representative first, second, and last piece: 「弓」 comes first and is N, 「中」 comes next and is L, and the final stroke 「一」 is M, giving the full code T, N, L, M. Memory hook: plant the grass first, then draw the 「弓」 bow, set the 「中」 in the middle, and finish with one 「一」 stroke — that's how this transliteration character grows.
薩.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「薩」，讀saat3，佢冇乜獨立意思，主要係用嚟音譯外來字，好似「菩薩」裏面嘅「薩」，又或者外國名同食物，例如「披薩」（pizza）同埋「薩莉」（Sally）。你望下呢個字，頂上有個草花頭「艹」，佢係T，做咗字首；淨低嗰大嚿就係字身，喺倉頡入面，字身最多取三碼，所以我哋要揀有代表性嘅頭、二、尾三筆。字身裏面第一個係「弓」，係N；第二個代表筆形係「中」，係L；最後一筆係「一」，係M，所以成個字砌埋就係T、N、L、M。記憶鉤：先種草，再拉「弓」、擺「中」間、收「一」筆，一棵菩薩草就咁樣長成。

藍.en: Today we learn 藍, read laam4 — the blue of blue color, originally the indigo plant, and also a surname. Look at it: on top sits the grass radical 艹, and underneath is the character 監. Because 藍 is a top-and-bottom shape, the grass on top serves as the 字首 and takes just one code, the T of 艹; the lower 監 is the 字身, and since a 字身 draws at most three codes, we take its head, second, and tail — head 尸 which is S, second 戈 which is I, and tail 廿 which is T, giving TSIT. Remember it this way: grass leads with one stroke, then split 監 into head 尸, second 戈, and tail 廿 — that's how 藍色 gets built in 天空係藍色嘅, the sky is blue.
藍.zh: 我哋今日學「藍」字，讀laam4，即係藍色嗰個藍，本身又指藍草，亦都可以做姓。你望吓佢，最上面係草花頭「艹」，下面就係個「監」字。因為「藍」係上下結構，上面嘅草花頭做字首，只取一碼，就係「艹」個T；跟住落嚟下面嘅「監」做字身，字身最多取三碼，所以要取頭、次、尾——頭係「尸」個S，次係「戈」個I，尾就係「廿」個T，合埋就係TSIT。記住個口訣：草花頭一劃領頭，下面拆頭尸、二戈、尾廿，「天空係藍色嘅」，藍色就係咁砌出嚟。

蘇.en: Today we meet 蘇, read sou1, which means to revive or come back to life, also names a kind of thyme, and shows up as the 蘇 in 蘇聯, the Soviet Union. Look at the character: a grass crown sits on top, and underneath a cluster of parts is packed together. When we split it, the head is 艹, keyed as T, and it gives just its one code first. Everything below counts as the body, and since a body takes at most three codes, we take its head piece 魚 as N, then 火 as F, and finally the tail piece 禾 as D, giving TNFD. The head quota was already spent on 艹, so the rest all falls into the body, and we pick head, middle, and tail until three codes are filled. Memory hook: grass hat T on top, then line up 魚 N, 火 F, 禾 D beneath — four codes make 蘇.
蘇.zh: 今日我哋學「蘇」呢個字，讀音係 sou1，本義係復甦、翻生，亦都可以指一種香草，仲成日用嚟音譯「蘇聯」個「蘇」。你望下呢個字，上面戴住個草花頭，下面就係一堆嘢逼埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，最上面嘅字首艹係「廿」T，先取佢一碼；跟住落嚟成個下半部分當做字身，入面有魚、火同禾三件嘢，字身最多取三碼，所以我哋取頭嗰件魚「弓」N、中間嘅火「火」F、再取埋最尾嘅禾「木」D，砌埋就係 TNFD。點解火同禾要一齊出現喺字身裏面呢？因為佢哋都係字身嘅組件，字首已經俾咗艹，其餘全部歸字身，順住頭、次、尾嘅次序揀夠三碼就收。記住呢個口訣：草花頭一頂帽 T，底下魚 N、火 F、禾 D 排隊，四碼成「蘇」。

蘭.en: Today we learn 蘭, read laan4, which names the orchid — a graceful, quietly elegant flower, and by extension the word can mean elegant or refined. Look at the whole shape: a grass radical 艹 sits on top like a little hat, and underneath is the character 闌. In Cangjie we take the top piece first as the 字首, and that grass radical 艹 is the key T. The 闌 underneath is the 字身, and a body like this is coded head-second-last: the head piece 日 gives A, the second piece 弓 gives N, and the last piece 田 gives W, so the whole code spells out TANW. Remember it as grass on top, then reach into that crowded body for its head and tail — 艹, 日, 弓, 田 — T, A, N, W, and the orchid blooms right on your keyboard.
蘭.zh: 我哋今日學「蘭」字，讀音係 laan4，意思係蘭花，一種好優雅、好清幽嘅花，所以又可以引申做「優雅」、「高潔」嘅意思。你望吓成個字嘅結構：上面戴住個草花頭「艹」，下面係一個「闌」字。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，先攞字首，就係頂上嘅「艹」，佢個鍵係 T。跟住落嚟嘅「闌」係字身，字身要照「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼方法拆——攞頭嗰個「日」係 A，攞第二個「弓」係 N，最後攞埋尾嗰個「田」係 W，所以成個碼砌埋就係 TANW。你可以咁樣記：草花頭下面一大堆嘢，抽頭抽尾——「艹日弓田」，TANW，蘭花就開喺你鍵盤上面喇。你亦可以喺「烏克蘭」同「荷蘭」呢啲地名度見到佢，例如「我媽鍾意種蘭花」。

處.en: Today we learn 處, which means a place or a locale, and can also mean a department. It reads cyu3, as in 休息處 (rest area), and also reads cyu2, as in 處理, meaning to handle or deal with something. Look at the character: on top sits 虍, the tiger's head, and underneath is 処. Cangjie splits it into two parts — the 字首 虍 gives just its head and tail, 卜 (Y) and 心 (P), while the 字身 処 takes three codes: head 竹 (H), second 水 (E), and tail 弓 (N). The split falls this way because this is a top-bottom character: the 字首 contributes two codes from head and tail, and the 字身 contributes three from head, second, and tail, giving the full code YPHEN. Here's your memory hook: a tiger (虍) settling into a spot (処) is a 處 — 卜心竹水弓.
處.zh: 我哋今日學「處」字，佢係「地方、場所」嘅意思，讀 cyu3，好似「休息處」；佢又可以讀 cyu2，好似「處理」，即係應付、料理事情。你望住個字，上面係「虍」（老虎頭），下面係「処」。倉頡拆碼分做兩部分：字首「虍」取頭尾兩碼，頭係卜（Y），尾係心（P）；字身「処」就取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係竹（H），第二碼係水（E），尾係弓（N）。點解係咁分？因為呢個字係上下結構，字首取頭尾夠兩碼，字身再取頭、二、尾三碼，合埋就係 YPHEN 五碼。記住喇：老虎（虍）坐喺一個地方（処），就係「處」——卜心竹水弓。

號.en: This character is 號, read hou6, meaning a mark, a sign, a symbol, or a number — as in 一號, the first day of the month or simply number one. Look at how it's built from a left and a right half: on the left is 号, and on the right is 虎. In Cangjie the left 号 acts as the 字首 and gives only its head and tail, which are 口 (R) at the top and 尸 (S) at the bottom; the right 虎 acts as the 字身 and gives three codes — head, second, and tail — namely 卜 (Y), then 匕 (P), then 山 (U), so the whole thing reads RSYPU. To remember it, picture a tiger (虎) shouting out a slogan (号) — put them together and you've got 號.
號.zh: 呢個字係「號」，讀 hou6，即係記號、符號、又或者數字編號嘅意思，例如「一號」就係初一或者第一個號碼。你睇下佢係左右兩邊砌成嘅：左邊係「号」，右邊係「虎」。倉頡入面，左邊嘅「号」做字首，只取頭同尾，即係開頭嘅口（R）同結尾嘅尸（S）；右邊嘅「虎」做字身，取頭、二、尾三個碼，就係開頭嘅卜（Y）、第二個匕（P）、最後嘅山（U），所以全碼砌埋就係 RSYPU。要記住呢個字，你可以諗成「一隻老虎（虎）叫緊個口號（号）」，一叫就係「號」啦。

蛋.en: Today we learn 蛋, read "daan2" or "daan6", the character for eggs — the kind of egg you eat, and also a word you'll see in insults like "bad egg". Look at the shape: on top sits 疋, and underneath sits 虫, a classic top-over-bottom build. The top part 疋 is the head, and from a head we take just the first two codes, 弓 N and 人 O. The bottom part 虫 is the body, and because 虫 is its own complete piece, we take head-first plus last-two, giving 中 L, 一 M, 戈 I, so the whole code is NOLMI. Here's the hook: two strokes on top for 疋 (NO), then three for the 虫 below (LMI head-and-tail), and your egg is done. You'll meet this same 蛋 in 魚蛋 (fish balls) and 蛋白質 (protein), and in a simple line like "I ate an egg."
蛋.zh: 今日我哋學「蛋」呢個字，讀「daan2」或者「daan6」，即係雞蛋嗰啲蛋，鬧人嘅時候都會用到，好似「壞蛋」咁。你望下呢個字，上面係「疋」，下面係「虫」，係典型嘅上下結構。上面嘅「疋」做字首，我哋取頭兩碼，即係「弓」N同「人」O。下面嘅「虫」做字身，虫係一個獨立可寫嘅部件，所以要取頭一碼加尾兩碼，即係「中」L、「一」M、「戈」I，合埋成為NOLMI。記住個訣竅：上面「疋」出兩下NO，下面條「虫」頭尾三下LMI，一隻蛋就打出嚟喇。你食「魚蛋」、講「蛋白質」，都係呢個「蛋」，好似「我食咗個蛋」咁自然。

行.en: Today we meet 行, a wonderfully flexible character read haang4 (行街, to shop around), hang4 (進行, to proceed), or hang6 (conduct), all meaning to go, walk, move, or circulate. Look at its shape: on the left sits 彳, and on the right sits 亍, and Cangjie splits it right down that middle. The left piece 彳 is the 字首, so we take its head and tail only, giving 竹 (H) and 人 (O). The right piece 亍 is the 字身, from which we take head, second, and tail, which come out as 一 (M), 一 (M), and 弓 (N). Put together the whole code is 竹人一一弓, HOMMN — the head keeps just two codes, the body earns three. Memory hook: a person (竹人) walking (一一) down a road that bends like a bow (弓) at the end — that's 行.
行.zh: 今日我哋學「行」呢個字，佢好百變，可以讀 haang4（行街）、hang4（進行）、hang6（品行），意思係走、去、移動、流通。你望下佢個樣，左邊係「彳」，右邊係「亍」，兩邊分開嚟砌。左邊嘅「彳」係字首，倉頡取佢嘅頭同尾，即係竹（H）同人（O）；右邊嘅「亍」係字身，取頭、二、尾，順住就係一（M）、一（M）、弓（N）。所以成個碼砌埋就係竹人一一弓，即 HOMMN，記住左邊淨取頭尾兩碼、右邊取到三碼咁樣分工。記憶鈎：一個人（竹人）行過兩條路（一一），最後彎入弓——就係「行」。

術.en: Today we learn 術, read seot6, meaning art, skill, or method — you meet it in everyday words like 技術 gei6 seot6 (technique) and 藝術 ngai6 seot6 (art). Look closely: the outer 行 wraps around and hugs the small 术 sitting in the middle. Because it's a left-right embracing shape, we take the character-head first, pulling 彳 (H) and 人 (O) from the left side of 行, giving us HO; then the character-body is the inner 术, from which we take the first-two-and-last rule to grab 戈 (I), 金 (C) and 弓 (N), spelling ICN, so the whole code is HOICN. Picture it like this: 行 opens its arms and gives you 彳人 (HO) first, then squeezes 戈金弓 (ICN) in the middle — think of the sentence 佢學緊魔術, he's learning magic tricks, and the shape will stick.
術.zh: 今日我哋學「術」呢個字，讀音係 seot6，解作技藝、方法或者本領，好似「技術」gei6 seot6同「藝術」ngai6 seot6咁常用。你望真啲個字：外面係「行」字被中間夾住，左右分開包住裏面嘅「术」。因為係左右夾抱嘅結構，我哋先拆字首，取「行」左邊嘅彳（H）同人（O），所以字首係 HO；跟住字身係中間嗰個「术」，我哋照取頭二尾嘅規矩，拎戈（I）、金（C）同弓（N），砌成 ICN，全字合埋就係 HOICN。記住個口訣：「行」字張開手，先攞彳人（HO），再夾住中間戈金弓（ICN），「佢學緊魔術」你就記得晒喇。

街.en: Today's character is 街, read gaai1, meaning a street, road, or thoroughfare — you'll see it in words like 大街 (daai6 gaai1), a main street, and 街市 (gaai1 si5), the wet market where you go to buy your groceries. Look at its shape: the character 行 is split open into a left half and a right half, with 圭 and 亍 tucked inside the middle. In Cangjie, the left part of 行 acts as the 字首, and from it we take just the head and tail codes — 竹 (H) and 人 (O); everything in the centre, the 圭 and the 亍, becomes the 字身, giving us 土 (G), 土 (G), and 弓 (N). The split falls this way because the 字首 and 字身 each have their own coding quota: the left of 行 contributes only its head-and-tail 竹 人, while the inner 圭 亍 fills out the body as 土 土 弓, so the full code reads HOGGN. Remember it like this: 竹 and 人 frame two 土 and one 弓, and you've walked right out onto the 街.
街.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「街」，讀音係 gaai1，意思就係街道、馬路，好似「大街」（daai6 gaai1）或者「街市」（gaai1 si5）咁樣，即係你去買餸嗰個地方。你留意下個字嘅結構：左右兩邊嘅「行」字被拆開，中間夾住一個「圭」同「亍」。倉頡入面，「行」字嘅左邊做字首，取頭尾兩個碼，就係竹（H）同人（O）；而中間嗰嚿「圭」同「亍」就一齊做字身，取土（G）、土（G）、弓（N）三個碼。點解要咁拆呢？因為字首同字身各有自己嘅取碼配額，字首行字左邊只取頭尾竹人，字身就順住寫落去攞晒中間嘅土土弓，所以成個碼就係 HOGGN。記住個口訣：竹人夾住兩個土同一個弓，你就行返出條「街」喇。

衣.en: Today we learn 衣, read ji1, meaning clothes or clothing — as in 衣服 ji1 fuk6, the garments you wear on your body. Look at its shape: a dot and a stroke up top, then a tangle of strokes below, like a robe draped over your body. When we take the code, 衣 is a whole character, so instead of breaking out every stroke we use the head-second-tail method: the head is the top 亠 on Y, the second piece is 竹 on H, and the tail is 女 on V, while the middle is simply skipped — giving us YHV. Why skip like this? Because a whole character is too dense to split cleanly into a head part and a body part, so Cangjie takes only the first, second, and last shapes to stand in for it. Remember it this way: a garment drapes from the top (Y) down to the tail (V), and whatever's in the middle you let go — just hold onto the two ends.
衣.zh: 我哋今日學「衣」呢個字，讀 ji1，即係衫、衣服嘅意思，好似「衣服」ji1 fuk6 就係身上着嘅嘢。你望吓佢個樣，上面一點一橫，下面一堆筆畫，睇落好似一件披喺身上嘅衫。拆碼嘅時候，「衣」係一個整體字，我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法：頭係上面嘅「亠」Y，第二個係「竹」H，尾就係最後嘅「女」V，中間嗰啲部分就直接跳過唔理，所以成個碼就係 YHV。點解要咁跳？因為整體字太密，冇明顯嘅字首字身可以分開，倉頡就只取頭、次、尾三個位嚟代表佢。你可以咁記：一件衫從上（Y）披到落尾（V），中間隨佢去，記住頭尾就夠。

表.en: Today we learn 表, read "biu2" in Cantonese, meaning to show, express, or display — you meet it in words like 代表 (representative) and 表示 (to indicate). Because this character is tangled and packed with strokes, Cangjie treats it as a whole-form character, and whole-form characters don't get coded piece by piece — we simply take the head, the next mark, and the tail. Look at the top and you'll find 手, taken as Q; the next clear code is the single horizontal stroke 一, taken as M; and the foot of the character is 女, taken as V, while everything crammed in the middle is skipped. That gives us 手 (Q), 一 (M), 女 (V), spelling QMV. Here's your hook: head 手, waist 一, foot 女 — skip the middle — and picture the 手 (hand) leading the way as you glance at the watch, the 手表, on your wrist.
表.zh: 今日我哋學「表」呢個字，粵音讀「biu2」，意思係表示、表達、顯示出嚟，好似「代表」、「表示」呢啲詞都用到佢。呢個字筆畫多、結構糾纏，所以倉頡當佢係一個「整體字」嚟拆——整體字唔使逐忽對應，我哋只係取頭、次、尾三個位就夠。你睇個字最頂係「手」，取Q做字頭；跟住第二個明顯嘅碼係一橫「一」，取M；最後個字腳係「女」，取V，中間嗰啲部件我哋一律跳過。所以個碼就係手(Q)、一(M)、女(V)，QMV。記住個口訣：頭手、腰一、腳女，中間唔理，你戴住個「手表」睇時間，就記得個「手」字排頭喇。

被.zh: 今日我哋學「被」呢個字，讀音係 bei6 或者 pei5，一係做被動語態嘅記號，即係英文嘅「by」，好似「被捕」咁；一係解作蓋喺身上嘅被鋪。你望下佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係衣字旁「衤」，右邊係「皮」字。左邊嘅衤就係字首，取佢一個碼 L 就夠。右邊「皮」字做字身，字身最多取三個碼，所以我哋用「取頭、取次、取尾」嘅辦法揀出佢嘅代表筆形：頭係木 D，第二個係竹 H，最尾係又 E，合埋就係 LDHE。記住呢個口訣：一件衫遮住張被——衤先行，皮就頭、二、尾。

製.en: Today we learn 製, read zai3, meaning to make, to manufacture, to produce something. Look at its build: the top is 制 and the bottom is 衣, stacked one above the other. The top 制 is the prefix, so by the first-last rule it gives just its head 竹 (H) and its tail 乙 (N); the bottom 衣 is the body, so it takes first-second-last — 卜 (Y), 竹 (H) and 女 (V) — giving the full code HNYHV. Remember it this way: on top you make (制), underneath is clothing (衣), and what you produce is 製!
製.zh: 今日我哋學「製」呢個字，讀做 zai3，意思係製作、製造，即係整嘢出嚟。你睇佢嘅結構，上面係一個「制」字，下面係一個「衣」字，兩部分疊埋一齊。上邊「制」係字首，跟住取頭尾嘅法則，只攞頭嗰個「⺮」（H）同尾嗰個「乙」（N）；下邊「衣」係字身，取頭二尾三碼，就係「卜」（Y）、「竹」（H）同「女」（V），所以成個碼順住打落去就係 HNYHV。你記住：上面制衫、下面着衣，做出嚟嘅就係「製」！

西.en: Today we learn 西, read sai1, meaning west or western, the direction opposite of east. Look at its shape: a flat stroke across the top, a splayed 八-like pair opening in the middle, and an outer box 囗 wrapping around it — together they form 西. This is a 整體字, a whole character, so instead of breaking out every single stroke we just take three representative pieces from head, middle, and tail: the head is the horizontal 一 on M, the middle is 八 on C, and the tail is the enclosing box 囗 on W, with the extra strokes in between simply skipped — giving the code MCW. Picture the line "the sun sets in the west," and let it sink from M down through C into the W box, and MCW will stay with you.
西.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「西」，讀作 sai1，即係方向入面嘅西邊、西方，同「東」相對。你睇下佢個形：上面一橫、中間好似「八」咁向兩邊分開、外面再包住一個「囗」框，全個字砌埋一齊就係「西」。呢個係倉頡入面嘅整體字，我哋唔會逐筆逐筆拆到盡，而係取頭、中、尾三個代表位——頭係一橫 M（一），中間係 C（八），尾係外框 W（囗），中間多餘嗰啲筆畫直接跳過唔理，所以碼就係 MCW。你可以諗住「太陽喺西邊落」呢句，記住由 M 到 C 到 W，就好似太陽由高處慢慢落入西邊個框入面咁。

要.en: Today we learn 要, read jiu3, meaning necessary or essential — you'll meet it constantly in words like 重要 (zung6 jiu3, important) and 需要 (seoi1 jiu3, to need). Look at the whole character: there's a 田 sitting up top and a 女 holding the bottom, forming one tidy, self-contained block, which makes it a whole-character shape (整體字). For shapes like this, Cangjie has a rule — take the head, the second piece, and the last, and skip whatever sits in the middle — so we keep only 一=M, 田=W, and 女=V, letting the rest go untouched. Type them straight down the character, top to bottom: M, W, V. As a hook, picture one line pressing on a field with a woman steadying it below — 一, 田, 女, and you've got it.
要.zh: 今日我哋學「要」呢個字，讀 jiu3，意思係「需要」、「必要」，好似「重要」（zung6 jiu3）同「需要」（seoi1 jiu3）咁樣，喺日常好常見。你望吓成個字，上面有個 田，下面有個 女，字形好完整，佢屬於「整體字」，即係唔會拆到好散。倉頡拆呢類字有一條規矩：取頭、二、尾，即係取開頭同埋最後嘅碼，跳過中間唔要，所以我哋只揀 一=M、田=W、女=V 三個部件，中間嗰啲就唔理。記住嘅時候，你可以諗成「一橫壓住個 田，個 女 撐喺底」，M、W、V 順住由上到下打落去，練幾次就記得住喇。

見.en: Today we learn 見, read gin3, meaning to see or to perceive — using your eyes to observe and notice something. Look at it: on top sits the 「⺫」 eye radical, which you type with B; beneath it comes the 「凵」 shape on U; then a slanting 「竹」 stroke on H; and finally a 「人」 person-stroke on U, giving you BUHU. Why does it split this way? Because 見 is a whole-form character with no clean division into head and body, so we use the whole-form method and take pieces in writing order — head B, second U, third H, and tail U — landing on exactly four codes. Remember the hook: the eye (B) looks down (U), a stroke (H) reveals a person (U), and you've seen it!
見.zh: 今日我哋學「見」呢個字，讀gin3，就係「見到」、「睇見」嘅意思，表示用眼睛去觀察、察覺。你望住佢：上面係一個「⺫」字部，喺倉頡度打B鍵；跟住下面係「凵」形，打U鍵；再嚟係一撇「竹」，打H鍵；最後一捺係「人」字，打U鍵，合埋就係BUHU。點解會咁樣拆？因為「見」係一個整體字，冇辦法清楚分成字首同字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅取碼方法，順住寫字嘅次序取頭B、二U、三H、尾U，啱啱四碼。記住佢嘅口訣：眼(B)望落去(U)，撇(H)出一個人(U)，睇見你喇！

規.en: Today's character is 規, read "kwai1", meaning rules, regulations, customs, or law — you see it in words like 規則 kwai1 zak1 (rule) and 規定 kwai1 ding6 (to stipulate). Look at the shape: on the left sits 夫, on the right sits 見, and Cangjie breaks it along that left-right divide. The 夫 head is only allowed two codes, so you take 扌 (Q) and 人 (O), giving QO. The 見 body is the last part, so it gives head-second-tail: ⺼ (B), 山 (U), and 山 (U) again, spelling BUU. Two for the head, head-second-tail for the body — that's the standard left-right split, and it lands you on QOBUU. Memory hook: 夫 looks and QO — then he sees BUU rules to follow.
規.zh: 今日學嘅字係「規」，讀「kwai1」，意思係規則、規矩、法度嘅意思，例如「規則」kwai1 zak1 同「規定」kwai1 ding6 都用到佢。你望下個字，左邊係「夫」，右邊係「見」，倉頡就係跟住呢個左右結構嚟拆。左邊嘅字首「夫」只取兩碼，就係「扌」（Q）同「人」（O），所以字首得QO兩個碼；右邊嘅字身「見」就取頭、二、尾三碼，順住就係「⺼」（B）、「山」（U）、「山」（U），砌埋成BUU。字首取二、字身取頭二尾，正正就係倉頡分左右嘅標準做法，所以全碼係QOBUU。記住個口訣：夫望見（QO見到 BUU），要跟規矩就記實呢個字！

視.zh: 今日我哋學「視」呢個字，讀做 si6，意思係「望、觀察、審視」，好似「電視」din6 si6 或者「視為」si6 wai4 咁樣用。你望吓佢，其實係由左邊嘅「示（礻）」同右邊嘅「見」砌埋一齊嘅，倉頡就照住呢個左右結構嚟拆。左邊做字首，「礻」嘅寫法係一點「丶」（I）加一個「小」（F），所以字首取 IF；右邊做字身「見」，因為係字身要取「頭、二、尾」三碼，我哋就攞頭嘅「⺼」（B）、跟住兩個「山」（U、U），砌成 BUU。合埋就係 IFBUU 五碼。記住呢個口訣：左邊示（IF）望向右邊見（BUU），一望就係「視」。

親.en: Today we learn 親, read can1 and sometimes can3, meaning relatives, parents, or something intimate and dear, as in 父親 (father) and 親愛 (beloved). Look at it: it splits left and right, where the left is the head 亲 and the right is the body 見. For the head 亲 we take first and last, so 亠 (Y) at the top and 木 (D) at the bottom, giving us just YD on the left; then the body 見 takes head, second, and tail — three pieces: ⺡ (B), 山 (U), and 儿 (U) — which together spell YDBUU. Why does the left get only two codes while the right gets three? Because in Cangjie the character head can give at most two codes, while the body is allowed up to three, so the split falls right there to keep everything clear. Remember it this way: 亠木 opens on the left, then 見 gives you head, mountain, and legs — YDBUU.
親.zh: 今日我哋學「親」呢個字，讀 can1，有時亦讀 can3，解作親人、父母，或者親密嘅意思，好似「父親」同「親愛」咁樣。你望下佢，左右兩邊分開嚟砌：左邊係字首「亲」，右邊係字身「見」。字首「亲」我哋取頭尾，頭係「亠」（Y），尾係「木」（D），所以左邊得 YD 兩碼；右邊字身「見」就取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係「⺡」（B），跟住「山」（U），最後「儿」都係（U），砌埋就係 YDBUU。點解左邊淨係兩碼、右邊要三碼呢？因為倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，字身就可以取到三碼，咁樣先夠拆得清楚。記住呢句：亠木先開頭，見字頭尾山儿收——YDBUU，一講就記得住。

覺.en: Today we learn 覺, read gok3 or gaau3, meaning to wake up from sleep or to feel and be conscious of something, as in the sentence 我覺得好攰, "I feel very tired," describing a feeling inside you. The character stacks into a top part, which is the 字首, and the 見 underneath, which is the 字身. For the top 字首 you take just the head and tail: the head is the bamboo ⺮ (H) and the tail is the cover 冖 (B), giving you HB. Then the 字身 見 takes three codes — head is the flesh radical ⺼ (B), the second is 凵 (U), and the tail is 山 (U) — spelling BUU, so the whole code is HBBUU. Notice the neat pattern of two B's and two U's, like the pieces stacking symmetrically top and bottom, and it sticks in your memory.
覺.zh: 今日我哋學「覺」字，讀作 gok3 或 gaau3，係「瞓醒」、「感覺」嘅意思，好似「我覺得好攰」入面咁樣，講你心入面嘅感受。呢個字上下兩截，上面嗰截係字首，下面個「見」係字身。字首上半你要取頭尾兩碼：頭係竹⺮（H），尾係禿寶蓋冖（B），所以字首兩碼就係 HB；字身「見」就取三碼——頭係月字旁⺼（B），第二碼係凵（U），尾係山（U），砌埋就係 BUU。全部連埋一齊打，就係 HBBUU。記住呢個字有兩個 B 兩個 U，好似上面兩件、下面兩件對稱咁排，一睇就記得晒。

觀.en: Today's character is 觀, read gun1 (also gun3), meaning to see, observe, or view — the act of looking closely and taking notice. Look at its shape: on the left sits 雚 and on the right sits 見, a classic left-right build. When we split it, the 字首 (leading part) 雚 may only take its head and tail, so we grab the top 艹 (T) and the 土 (G) below it, letting the middle pieces drop away. The 字身 (body) 見 then takes head, second, and tail — written in order as ⺼ (B), 凵 (U), 山 (U) — so the whole thing spells TGBUU. Remember it this way: 艹土 opens the door, and 見 trails off with a double U at the end.
觀.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「觀」，讀 gun1，粵語又有 gun3 音，意思係「觀看」、「觀察」，即係去睇、去留意嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係「雚」，右邊係「見」，係一個典型嘅左右結構字。拆碼嘅時候，字首「雚」只可以取頭尾，所以我哋攞最頂嘅「艹」（T）同下面嘅「土」（G），中間嘅部分就跳過唔理。字身「見」就取頭、二、尾三碼，順住寫落去係「⺼」（B）、「凵」（U）、「山」（U），所以全字砌成 TGBUU。記住呢個口訣：「艹土」開頭，「見」字身尾拖住兩個 U，你就唔會拆錯喇！

角.en: Today we meet 角, read gok3, meaning a horn like an animal's horn, and also an angle or a corner — the point where things meet. Look at its shape: there's a little 「⺈」 on top, a 「⺼」 in the middle, and a stroke that closes it off at the bottom. This is a 整體字, a whole shape that doesn't break apart cleanly, so instead of forcing a split we take head-second-tail: first the top 「⺈」, typed N, then the second piece 「⺼」, typed B, and finally the bottom closing stroke read as 土, typed G, giving NBG. The reason the tail becomes 土 is that when a whole shape is closed this way, that final vertical stroke is claimed by the 土 code, so G rounds it off. Picture it: 「⺈」 caps the 「⺼」 flesh and a stroke drives down into the 土 earth — NBG, and the horn is drawn.
角.zh: 我哋今日學「角」呢個字，讀作 gok3，係「牛角」嘅角、又或者「牆角」嘅角，指尖尖嘅角、角落頭嘅意思。你望下佢個形：上面有個「⺈」，中間係「⺼」，下面收埋一橫加一豎。呢個字係一個唔容易乾淨拆開嘅「整體字」，所以我哋唔硬拆，而係用「取頭二尾」嘅辦法，先攞頭嗰撇「⺈」，打 N；再攞第二件「⺼」，打 B；最後攞底部收尾嗰筆一豎，當佢係「土」，打 G，合埋就係 NBG。點解尾要當「土」呢？因為整體字取尾嗰陣，會將最尾嘅一豎歸入「土」呢個碼位，所以就用 G 作結。記住一個畫面：「⺈ 蓋住⺼肉，一豎插落土」，NBG，一角就成形喇。

解.en: Today we learn 解, a character with several meanings — read gaai2 it means to loosen, unfasten or untie, read gaai3 it means to explain or interpret, and there's an old reading haai6 naming a hexagram. Look at its shape: on the left is 角, and on the right 刀 and 牛 sit together, so it's a left-right character. When Cangjie breaks it up, it takes the left part 角 first as the head unit, and since such a busy head unit only gets a head and a tail, we take ⺈ (N) at the top and ⺼ (B) at the bottom; the right body then gives three codes — 尸 (S) at the head, 竹 (H) in the middle, and 手 (Q) at the tail — spelling NBSHQ. Remember it this way: a horn on the left, then a knife slowly loosening things on the right, finishing with a hand (Q).
解.zh: 今日我哋學「解」呢個字，佢有好多意思，可以讀 gaai2 解開、鬆開、拆開，又可以讀 gaai3 解釋嘅意思，仲有一個古老讀音 haai6，係卦名。你睇吓佢個樣，左邊係「角」，右邊係「刀」同埋「牛」砌埋一齊，係一個左右結構嘅字。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，先取左邊字首「角」，因為字首連身複雜嘅字只可以取頭同尾兩碼，所以攞頭嘅⺈（N）同尾嘅⺼（B）；跟住右邊字身要取三碼，攞頭嘅尸（S）、中間嘅竹（H），最後尾嘅手（Q），合埋就係 NBSHQ。記住呢個字：左邊一隻角，右邊攞把刀慢慢解開，用個手（Q）收尾就得。

言.en: 你可以留意例句「佢一言都冇講。」，講嘅正正就係一個字都冇出過口。
言.zh: 今日我哋學「言」呢個字，讀作 jin4，即係言語、說話嘅意思，好似「語言」jyu5 jin4 或者「方言」fong1 jin4 咁樣。你望吓佢個樣：上面一點，跟住兩橫，再落到底係個口字，成個字堆得好齊整。呢個字係一個「整體字」，冇辦法乾淨咁分成字首同字身，所以我哋唔用普通嘅切法，而係用整體字嘅「頭、二、三、尾」規則嚟拆碼。頭嗰點係卜 Y，第二筆一橫係一 M，第三筆又係一橫都係一 M，最尾嗰個口字係口 R，四碼合埋就係 YMMR。記住個口訣：一點兩橫一個口，講嘢就要用把口，咁你就唔會撈亂喇。

訂.en: Today we look at 訂, which reads ding3 and means to draw up an agreement or to arrange — think of booking a plane ticket or concluding a contract. See how the left side is the 言 speech radical and the right side is 丁. The character splits into a head and a body: the head 言 contributes its first and last shapes, 卜 (Y) on top and 口 (R) below, while the body 丁 gives its first and last shapes, 一 (M) and the hook 亅 (N), making the full code YRMN. Here is your memory hook — you must speak (言) and settle things (丁) before you can book anything, so 訂 stays fixed in your mind.
訂.zh: 今日我哋學「訂」呢個字，佢讀 ding3，意思係訂立、安排，好似訂機票、訂立合約噉。你望下佢，左邊係個「言」字部，右邊係個「丁」字。呢個字分做字首同字身兩部分：字首就係「言」，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，即係最頂嘅卜（Y）同埋下面嘅口（R）；字身就係「丁」，同樣取頭尾，即係上面嘅一（M）同埋一鈎亅（N），所以全碼就係 YRMN。記住個口訣：講嘢（言）要傾掂（丁），先至可以訂立，噉你就唔會忘記個字點砌喇。

計.en: Today's character is 計, read gai3, and it means to plan, to plot, or a scheme — the very word you'd reach for when you want to 計數 (work out a sum) or 設計 (design something). It's built from two parts: the 言 radical on the left, which becomes the 字首 (the leading part), and 十 on the right, which is the 字身 (the body). Because 言 is a fuller shape, Cangjie takes only its head and tail — the top piece 卜 (Y) and the bottom piece 口 (R) — while the body 十 gives its own single code 十 (J). Put them in typing order and you get YRJ: head-and-tail of 言 first, then 十 at the end. Remember it as 'speak (Y, R), then ten (J)' — you speak your plan, then seal it with a ten.
計.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「計」，讀 gai3，意思係計劃、盤算、計謀嘅意思，好似你想「計數」或者「設計」嗰陣就用到佢。呢個字左邊係「言」字部，右邊係「十」，我哋分做字首同字身兩橛。字首係「言」，倉頡見到「言」呢種比較複雜嘅部件，就取佢嘅頭同尾兩碼，即係頭嗰粒「卜」（Y），加埋尾嗰粒「口」（R）；跟住字身「十」就取自己一碼「十」（J）。所以「計」全碼就係 YRJ——言取頭尾卜口，再加十。記住呢個口訣：講「言」（Y、R）先，最後拍落「十」（J），咁就砌成一句「計」啦。

訊.en: Today we're learning 訊, which reads seon3 and means to inquire, to ask, or to examine — you'll meet it in words like 資訊 (zi1 seon3, information) and 訊息 (seon3 sik1, a message or text message). Look at the shape: the left side is 言, the speech radical, and the right side is the 訊 element, so you can already sense it's about words and asking. When we split it, the left 言 acts as the head, and in Cangjie a head takes its opening and closing pieces, so we grab the top 亠 (Y) and the bottom 口 (R); then the right side serves as the body, giving us 乙 (N) and 十 (J), which together spell YRNJ. A simple hook: the 言 on the left hands you its head-and-tail (亠, 口), and the right body hands you 乙 and 十 — think of it whenever you get a short text message (短訊).
訊.zh: 今日我哋學「訊」呢個字，讀音係 seon3，意思係查問、詢問，好似「資訊」（zi1 seon3，information）同「訊息」（seon3 sik1，message、短訊）咁樣。你望吓佢，左邊係「言」，右邊係另一個部件，一睇就知同講嘢、問嘢有關。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「言」做字首，倉頡取碼取頭同尾，所以攞頭嗰個「亠」，個碼係 Y，再攞尾嗰個「口」，個碼係 R；跟住右邊做字身，攞到「乙」係 N，同埋「十」係 J，四個碼合埋就係 YRNJ。記住呢個口訣：左邊言字攞頭尾（亠口），右邊字身攞乙十，你收到「短訊」嗰陣就會諗起佢喇。

記.en: lear, we'll study 記, read gei3, meaning to record or to keep something in mind — just like when you remember a fact. The character splits into two sides: the 字首 on the left is 言, and the 字身 on the right is 己. When Cangjie breaks it apart, the 字首 言 only takes head and tail — the head is ⺊ (Y) and the tail is 口 (R); then the body 己 also takes head and tail — the head is 丂 (S) and the tail is 乚 (U). Put them together and the full code is YRSU. Memory hook: words you speak (言) are kept inside yourself (己), so 記 means to remember — two codes per side, nice and tidy.
記.zh: 今日我哋學「記」呢個字，讀「gei3」，意思係記錄、記住喺心入面，就好似你記得一件事咁。呢個字分做左右兩邊：左邊嘅字首係「言」，右邊嘅字身係「己」。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首「言」淨係取頭尾兩碼，個頭係「⺊」（Y鍵），個尾係「口」（R鍵）；字身「己」都係取頭尾，個頭係「丂」（S鍵），個尾係「乚」（U鍵）。所以成個字砌埋就係 YRSU。記憶法：講嘢（言）記喺自己（己）心度，就係「記」，唔會亂咁多碼，一邊兩碼就啱晒。

設.en: Today we learn 設, read cit3, meaning to build, establish, display, and also to suppose or assume. Look at how it stands on the page: on the left is 言, on the right is 殳. The left piece 言 is the head, and it hands you two codes, YR. The right piece 殳 is the body, and because it has more than one part inside it, we follow the body rule that takes head, second, and tail — so it gives 竹 H, then 乙 N, and finally 又 E. Put them together and you get YRHNE. To remember it, picture words (言) plus a hand (又) coming together to set something new up — you're designing, 設計, from scratch.
設.zh: 今日我哋學「設」呢個字，讀作 cit3，意思係建立、設立、擺設，仲可以做假設嘅意思。你望下佢由左右兩橛砌成：左邊係「言」，右邊係「殳」。左邊「言」係字首，佢取兩個碼 YR。右邊「殳」係字身，因為佢唔止一橛，所以用倉頡嘅取碼規矩——字身取頭、次、尾三個碼，即係頭「竹」H、跟住「乙」N、最後「又」E。合埋成 YRHNE。記住嘅時候，你可以諗成：講嘢（言）加上一隻手（又）去砌一樣新嘢——「設計」出嚟。

評.en: Today we learn 評, read ping4, meaning to appraise, criticize, or evaluate — to weigh something and pass judgment on it. Look at it: the left side is the speech radical 言, and the right side is 平, so a word about speaking to assess something fits the meaning nicely. The 字首 on the left, 言, contributes only head and tail: the head is 卜 (Y) and the tail is 口 (R), giving YR. The 字身 on the right, 平, contributes head, second, and tail — 一 (M), 火 (F), and 十 (J) — because Cangjie lets a 字首 take at most two codes while a 字身 may take up to three, so 言 fills its quota as YR and 平 spreads out as MFJ, joining to make YRMFJ. Memory hook: use your 言 words to 評 an ordinary 平 person.
評.zh: 今日我哋學「評」呢個字，讀 ping4，意思係評價、批評、評估，即係對啲嘢作出判斷同衡量。你望吓佢，左邊係「言」字旁，右邊係「平」，一開口就係講嘢評論嘅意思，好夾字義。左邊嘅字首「言」，倉頡淨係取頭尾兩碼，個頭係「卜」（Y），個尾係「口」（R），所以係 YR；右邊嘅字身「平」，就取頭、二、尾三碼，分別係「一」（M）、「火」（F）同「十」（J）。點解係咁分？因為倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼、字身最多取三碼，「言」做字首夠曬額度就係 YR，「平」做字身就攤開成 MFJ，合埋就係 YRMFJ。記住呢句：「言」講一句話，去「評」一評個「平」凡人。

試.en: Today we learn 試, read si3, meaning to test or to try — as in 你試下呢件衫, you try on this shirt. The character has 言 on the left and 式 on the right, and Cangjie breaks it apart piece by piece. The head 言 takes only its first and last shapes, 卜Y and 口R, while the body 式 takes head-second-last, giving 戈I, 匕P and 一M — together YRIPM. Why does 言 give only two but 式 give three? In a left-right character the head is limited to first-last (two codes) and the body is allowed three, a fixed quota. Memory hook: speak half of 言 (卜口), then set down one 式 (戈匕一), and you have 試.
試.zh: 我哋今日學「試」，讀 si3，即係試驗、嘗試嘅意思，好似「你試下呢件衫」咁。呢個字左邊係「言」，右邊係「式」，倉頡就係咁一部分一部分咁拆。字首「言」取頭尾兩碼，頭係卜Y，尾係口R；跟住字身「式」，取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係戈I，第二個係匕P，最後係一M，合埋就係 YRIPM。你會問點解「言」淨係取兩個而「式」取三個？因為喺左右結構入面，字首只攞頭尾兩碼，字身先攞得三碼，呢個係固定嘅配額。記住口訣：講「言」講一半（卜口），再擺一個「式」樣（戈匕一），就係「試」。

話.en: Today we learn 話, read waa6 or waa2, meaning speech, talk, language or dialect — you see it everywhere in words like 說話 (to speak) and 嘅話 (as said). Look at it: on the left is the 言 speech radical, and on the right is 舌, the tongue — put talking and the tongue together and you get speech. Cangjie breaks it into five codes: the 字首 is 言, but a 字首 takes at most two codes, so it gives only its head 卜 (Y) and its tail 口 (R); then the 字身 is 舌, which gives its head 竹 (H), its second piece 十 (J), and its tail 口 (R), making the full code 卜口竹十口, YRHJR. Remember it this way: the mouth on the left opens to speak (卜口), the tongue on the right moves to shape the words (竹十口) — no tongue, no talk, so you'll never split it wrong.
話.zh: 我哋今日學「話」字，讀 waa6 或者 waa2，意思係說話、言語、方言，好似「說話」、「嘅話」咁常見。你望吓佢，左邊係「言」字部，右邊係「舌」字，兩橛砌埋一齊就係講嘢嘅意思。倉頡拆佢做五碼：字首係「言」，佢唔會全部拆晒，只取頭嘅卜（Y）同埋尾嘅口（R），因為字首最多得兩碼；跟住字身係「舌」，取頭嘅竹（H）、中間嘅十（J），再取尾嘅口（R），所以成個碼就係卜口竹十口，即係 YRHJR。你記住：左邊「言」開口講（卜口），右邊「舌」尖動起（竹十口），有舌先有話，咁就唔會拆錯喇。

該.en: Today we learn 該, read "goi1", meaning should, ought to, or need to. Look at it: on the left sits the 言 speech radical, and on the right stands the character 亥. In Cangjie the split follows a firm rule for how many codes each part gives: the radical 言 as the 字首 takes only its head and tail, so you get the top dot 卜 (Y) and the mouth 口 (R) at its bottom; then the body 亥, a piece on its own, gives head, second and tail, meaning the top 亠 (Y), the middle 女 (V), and the final 人 (O), which together spell YRYVO. Why does 亥 give three codes? Because as the 字身 it is allowed up to three, so beyond head and tail it also takes one middle stroke. Remember it as: speech head-and-tail (卜口), then 亥 head-middle-tail (亠女人) — and picture 你唔該我, "you should thank me."
該.zh: 今日我哋學「該」呢個字，讀「goi1」，係「應該」、「應份」嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係個「言」字部，右邊係個「亥」字。倉頡拆呢個字要記住取碼嘅規矩：字首「言」我哋淨係取頭同尾，頭係一點「卜」（Y），尾係下面個「口」（R）；跟住字身「亥」係一個獨立部件，取頭、次、尾三碼，頭係上面個「亠」（Y），次係中間嘅「女」（V），尾係最後個「人」（O），合埋就係 YRYVO。點解「亥」要取三碼呢？因為佢做字身，而字身通常可以取到三碼，所以除咗頭同尾，仲要夾多一個中間嘅碼。記個口訣：言頭尾（卜口），亥頭次尾（亠女人），「你唔該我」，就記得晒喇！

認.en: Today we're learning 認, read jing6, which means to recognise, to know, or to understand — as in 認為 jing6 wai4, meaning "in my opinion," and 認識 jing6 sik1, meaning to know or be familiar with someone or something. Look at the character and you'll see the speech radical 言 on the left and 忍 on the right, and that's exactly where we split it into head and body. The head 言 takes its first and last codes, Y and R, giving YR; the body 忍 takes head, second, and tail, so 尸 is S, 戈 is I, and 匕 is P, together making SIP. Why does the body get three codes here? Because when a character splits into two parts and the head takes only two, the body takes three, so the full code comes out as YRSIP. Here's your hook: before you speak (言), you must 忍 — hold back — until you truly recognise things clearly.
認.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「認」，讀做 jing6，即係認得、認識嘅意思，例如「認為」jing6 wai4 就係我覺得、我認為咁解，「認識」jing6 sik1 就係識得、熟悉個人或者件事。你望下呢個字，左邊係個「言」字部，右邊係個「忍」字，我哋就係咁樣分做字首同字身。字首「言」係倉頡碼 Y 同 R，取頭尾兩碼，所以係 YR；字身「忍」就要取頭、二、尾三碼，「尸」係 S、「戈」係 I、「匕」係 P，合埋就係 SIP。點解字身要取到三碼呢？因為字首淨係取兩碼，倉頡規定分成兩份嘅字，字身要補多一碼，所以連埋成個字就係 YRSIP。記住呢句：講嘢（言）之前要「忍」住，先至認得清楚！

語.en: Today we learn 語, read jyu5, meaning language or words — it's the very 語 in 粵語, the Cantonese language you speak every day. Look at its shape: on the left is 言, the speech radical, and on the right sits 吾, which fits nicely with a character all about speaking and saying. When we split it, the left-hand 言 is the head and gives just one code, Y; then the whole right side 吾 becomes the body, and a body takes at most three codes by head-middle-tail, so we grab head 口 as R, tail 口 as R, and the two horizontal strokes 一 and 一 in between fill the middle as M and M — head plus body gives us YRMMR. That's why the rhyme goes: head 言 gives Y, body 吾 takes head-two-tail, 口一一口. Remember 言 leads, two flat 一 strokes sit sandwiched in the middle, and a 口 tops and tails it — say 我識講粵語 and you've already got 語.
語.zh: 今日我哋學「語」呢個字，讀 jyu5，喺「語言」入面就係語言、言語嘅意思，你日日講嘅「粵語」個「語」就係佢。你望吓佢個樣，左邊係「言」，右邊係「吾」，好符合佢講嘢、講說話嘅意思。拆碼嘅時候，左邊「言」係字首，淨係取一碼 Y；跟住成個右邊「吾」做字身，字身最多取三碼，我哋要取頭、取中、取尾，於是頭取「口」R、尾取「口」R，中間見到兩橫「一」「一」，就取 M、M 填夠三碼，加埋字首一共 YRMMR。所以個口訣係字首言 Y，字身吾取頭二尾——口一一口，記住言字打頭、兩橫夾喺中間、口口一頭一尾，「語」就記得穩陣喇。你識講「我識講粵語」，就已經識咗「語」點解。

說.en: Today's character is 說, read syut3, as in 說話 (to speak) or 小說 (a novel) — it means to speak, say, or talk. Look at it: on the left sits the 言 speech radical, and on the right is 兌. In Cangjie the head part 言 only contributes its first and last codes, 卜 (Y) and 口 (R), giving YR for the head. The body 兌 is then coded by taking head-second-last: 金 (C), 口 (R), and 山 (U), which is CRU, so the whole character reads 卜口金口山, or YRCRU. Here's your hook: to speak you need to open your mouth — and sure enough 說 hides two 口 (two R's), one in each half.
說.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「說」，讀 syut3，好似「說話」、「小說」入面咁，即係講嘢、講說話嘅意思。你望吓佢：左邊係「言」字部，右邊係「兌」字。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首「言」只攞頭同尾兩碼，即係 卜（Y）同 口（R），所以字首得 YR。跟住字身「兌」係一個獨立字，就用「取頭、二、尾」嘅方法揀三碼：頭係金（C），二係口（R），尾係山（U），合埋 CRU；成隻字就係 卜口金口山，即 YRCRU。記住呢個口訣：「言」頭尾（YR），「兌」頭二尾（CRU），講嘢自然一開口就有兩個口（兩個 R）。

課.en: Today's character is 課, read fo3 — the 課 in homework and lessons, meaning a course or a piece of classwork. Look at it: the left side is the 言 speech radical, and the right side is 果 (fruit), speech on the left and a result on the right. Cangjie splits it by the usual left-right rule: the left 言 is the prefix, so it takes only first and last, giving 卜 (Y) and 口 (R); the right 果 is the body, again first and last, giving 田 (W) and 木 (D). Put together the four codes are YRWD — 卜口田木. Memory hook: first you speak (言), then you get a result (果) — that's your 課.
課.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「課」，讀做 fo3，即係功課、課堂嗰個「課」，意思就係一堂堂嘅學習。你望吓佢，左邊係「言」字部，右邊係「果」字，一個講嘢一個結果，砌埋一齊。倉頡砌呢個字要跟左右分家嘅規矩：左邊「言」係字首，只可以取頭尾，所以攞頭嘅卜（Y）同尾嘅口（R）；右邊「果」係字身，同樣取頭尾，攞頭嘅田（W）同尾嘅木（D）。四碼合埋就係 YRWD，卜口田木。記住一句：講咗（言）先有結果（果），你就記得呢個「課」啦。

調.en: Today we learn 調, read "diu6" as in 調查 (to investigate), meaning to transfer, move or change — it also reads "tiu4" for tuning, like adjusting sound. Look at its build: on the left is the radical 言 (speech), and on the right sits the character 周. The radical 言 isn't broken stroke by stroke in Cangjie; instead it's taken as a fixed pair, giving Y and R, so you start with YR. Then for the body 周, which as a body can give up to three codes, you take its head ⺆ as B, its middle 土 as G, and its final 口 as R — put it all together and you get YRBGR. Remember it this way: first you speak the 言 (YR), then you box up a 周 (head B, second G, tail R), and you've tuned it in perfectly.
調.zh: 我哋今日學「調」，佢讀「diu6」，好似「調查」咁，指移動、更換，又或者讀「tiu4」，即係調校、調音。你睇睇佢個結構：左邊係「言」字部首，右邊係一個「周」字。「言」呢個字首，喺倉頡入面唔係逐筆拆，而係一次過取YR兩碼，所以我哋起手就打Y同R。跟住輪到字身「周」，字身最多取三碼，我哋就取佢個頭「⺆」係B、中間個「土」係G、最尾個「口」係R，合埋就係YRBGR。記住喇：先講句「言」（YR），再框住一個「周」（頭B、二G、尾R），你就調得掂喇！

請.en: The character 請 reads "cing2" and means to ask, to request, or to invite — you can use it politely just like "please." Let's see how it's built: on the left is the head 言, and on the right is the body 青. The head 言 doesn't take just one code — because it's the leading part we give it two codes, taking the top 言 shape as Y and the 口 beneath it as R, so the head is YR. Then the body 青 follows, and since a body can't take too many codes, the rule is head-second-tail: we take 手 (Q) as the head, 一 (M) as the second, and the final ⺼ (B) as the tail, giving QMB. Put it all together and you get YRQMB — remember it as "speaking (言 YR) brings the green (青 QMB)," and you've got 請.
請.zh: 「請」呢個字讀「cing2」，即係「請求」、「邀請」嘅意思，禮貌上都可以當「please」咁用。我哋睇下佢點砌出嚟：左邊係字首「言」，右邊係字身「青」。字首「言」我哋唔止取一碼，而係取頭尾兩碼——上面嗰個「言」字頭係Y，下面個「口」係R，所以字首就係YR兩碼。跟住輪到字身「青」，字身唔可以取太多碼，倉頡規則係取頭、二、尾三碼，所以我哋攞「手」（Q）做頭、「一」（M）做第二，再攞最尾嗰個「⺼」（B）做尾，砌埋就係QMB。全字合埋就係YRQMB，記住口訣：講嘢（言YR）帶青（QMB）就係「請」。

論.en: Today we meet 論, read "leon6," meaning to debate or discuss — you see it in 無論 (mou4 leon6, meaning no matter what) and 討論 (tou2 leon6, meaning to talk something over). Look at its shape: on the left sits the speech radical 訁, and on the right sits 侖, so Cangjie splits it left-to-right along that natural seam. The head 訁 takes only its first and last pieces, the top 卜 (Y) and the 口 (R) below it; then the body 侖 supplies 人 (O), 一 (M), and 月 (B), giving you YROMB. The key idea is that a character head never spells out every stroke inside it — it takes just the top and bottom to stand in for the whole, which is why 訁 yields only 卜口 while the body gets to give more. Remember it like this: 訁 opens its mouth to speak (卜口), then 侖 follows with 人一月 — let's discuss it together and it'll stick.
論.zh: 今日我哋學「論」呢個字，讀「leon6」，即係辯論、討論嘅意思，好似「無論」（mou4 leon6，即係唔理點樣）同「討論」（tou2 leon6，即係傾傾偈研究一件事）咁用。你望下佢個樣，左邊係言字部「訁」，右邊係「侖」，倉頡就係跟住呢個左右嘅結構嚟拆。字首係「訁」，佢只取頭尾兩碼，就係最上面嘅「卜」（Y）同下面嘅「口」（R）；跟住字身「侖」就取「人」（O）、「一」（M）、「月」（B）呢三個部件，合埋就係 YROMB。要記住嘅係，字首唔會攞盡佢入面每一筆，只取頭尾嚟代表，所以「訁」淨係得卜口兩碼，而字身就可以取多啲。記住呢個心法：「訁」開口講嘢卜口，「侖」就人一月接落去，你哋一齊討論下就記得嘞。

諗.en: Today's character is 諗, read nam2, a very common Cantonese word meaning to think or ponder — as in 我諗緊食咩好, "I'm thinking about what to eat." On the left sits the 言 radical, and on the right is 念. In Cangjie, 言 as the 字首 doesn't get spelled out stroke by stroke; instead you take its head and tail — head 卜 (Y) and tail 口 (R). Then 念 serves as the 字身 and gives 人 (O), 戈 (I), and 心 (P), so the whole code reads YROIP. The reason 言 yields only two codes is that a 字首 has a limited quota, and head-plus-tail is enough to stand in for it. Here's your hook: 言 opens the mouth to speak, and 念 keeps it on the heart — speak from the heart, and you'll always remember how to type 諗.
諗.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「諗」，讀做 nam2，喺廣東話入面好常用，即係「思考、想」嘅意思，好似「我諗緊食咩好」就係話你正喺度思量。呢個字左邊係「言」字部，右邊係「念」字。倉頡入面，「言」做字首唔會逐筆全取，而係取頭同尾——頭係卜（Y），尾係口（R）；跟住「念」做字身，取人（O）、戈（I）、心（P），連埋一齊就係 YROIP。點解「言」淨係取頭尾兩碼呢？因為佢做字首有配額限制，取頭取尾就夠代表佢，唔使填滿。記住呢個口訣：「言」開口講，「念」放心頭，你就一世唔會忘記「諗」點打。

講.en: Today's character is 講, read gong2, meaning to explain, discuss, or talk — as in 嚟講 and 講嘢, talking. Look at it: the 言 speech radical sits on the left and 冓 on the right, so this is a clear left-right split where the left is the head and the right is the body. From the head 言 we take just its first and last pieces: the top 卜 (Y) and the bottom 口 (R). From the body 冓 we're allowed up to three pieces, so using head-second-tail we grab 廿 (T), another 廿 (T), and the tail ⺼ (B), giving the full code YRTTB. Here's your hook: to talk you need a 口, then two stacked 廿 with a ⺼ underneath — say 你講嘢慢啲啦, speak a bit slower please.
講.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「講」，讀做 gong2，即係解釋、傾偈、講嘢嘅意思，好似「嚟講」同「講嘢」噉。你睇睇佢，左邊係個「言」字部，右邊係「冓」，好明顯係一個左右分開嘅字，所以我哋左邊取字首、右邊取字身。左邊嘅「言」做字首，取頭同尾兩件：先取頂上嘅「卜」（Y），再取底下嘅「口」（R）；右邊嘅「冓」做字身，字身可以取到三件，用頭、次、尾嘅辦法，摸到「廿」（T）、再一個「廿」（T）、同埋尾嘅「⺼」（B）。連埋一齊就係 YRTTB。記住喇：講嘢用個「口」（言字部），右邊兩個廿疊住，收個⺼字尾，「你講嘢慢啲啦」就係噉。

證.en: Today we learn 證, read zing3, meaning proof or evidence — to testify or verify. Look at its structure: on the left is the 言 speech radical, and on the right is 登. The character takes five codes, split into a lead part and a body part. The lead is the left-side 言, from which we take its first and last pieces, 言 Y and 口 R, giving YR. The body is the right-side 登, and because it has many strokes we take its first, second, and last pieces — 弓 N, then 人 O, then 廿 T — spelling NOT, so the whole character is YRNOT. Here's your memory hook: your words (言) need to be registered as proof, so YR plus NOT gives you 證.
證.zh: 今日我哋學「證」字，讀做 zing3，即係證明、證據嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅結構：左邊係「言」字部，右邊係「登」字。呢個字打五個碼，分做字首同字身兩部分。字首係左邊嘅「言」，取頭尾兩碼 Y（言）同 R（口），所以係 YR。字身係右邊嘅「登」字，因為佢筆畫多，我哋取頭、二、尾三碼，即係頭一個「弓」N、第二個「人」O、最後一個「廿」T，合埋就係 NOT。成個字連埋就係 YRNOT。記住嘅竅妙：講嘢（言）要有憑據先可以登記入冊，YR 加 NOT 就係「證」。

識.en: Today's character is 識, read sik1, meaning to recognize, understand, or know how to do something — as in 我識講廣東話, "I know how to speak Cantonese." It splits into a left-hand 字首, the piece 言, and a right-hand 字身, the piece 戠, and we code each part in turn. The 字首 言 is a busy shape, and a 字首 is allowed at most two codes, so we use head-and-tail: the top 卜 (Y) and the bottom 口 (R), giving YR. Then the 字身 戠 is also busy, so it gets its full three codes by head, second, and tail — the top 卜 (Y), the next piece 戈 (I), and the last piece 日 (A) — which builds up to YRYIA. Remember it this way: to speak (言) is to know (戠), so YR opens the mouth and YIA closes it.
識.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「識」，讀作 sik1，即係認得、明白、識得某樣嘢嘅意思，好似「我識講廣東話」咁樣。呢個字分開做左邊嘅字首「言」同右邊嘅字身「戠」，我哋一段一段拆嚟睇。字首「言」係一個複雜嘅部件，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，所以我哋用「頭尾」法，攞頭嘅「卜」（Y）同尾嘅「口」（R），得出 YR。跟住字身「戠」都係複雜部件，可以取到三碼，用「頭、次、尾」三個位，攞頭嘅「卜」（Y）、次嘅「戈」（I）、尾嘅「日」（A），砌埋成 YRYIA。記住個口訣：講嘢（言）要識得（戠），一開口一收口，YR 打頭，YIA 收尾。

譚.en: Today we learn 譚, read taam4, a common Hong Kong surname — as in 譚老師好好人, "Teacher Tam is a very nice person" — and it can also mean to talk or converse. Notice this is a left-right character: on the left is the 言 speech radical, on the right is 覃, and Cangjie follows that left-to-right order. The left 言 is the 字首 (lead), and we take only its first and last codes — 言 on its own is coded YMMR, so as the lead we keep 言 Y and 口 R. The right side 覃 is the 字身 (body), which takes first-second-last: 覃 on its own is MWAJ, so we take 一 M, 田 W, and the final 十 J, giving the whole character YRMWJ. Remember it this way: speech 言 stands on the left, and 覃 hands you 一 M, 田 W, 十 J top to bottom — that's how you build the surname Tam.
譚.zh: 今日我哋學「譚」字，讀音係 taam4，係一個常見嘅姓氏，好似「譚老師好好人」入面嘅譚老師咁；佢本身都有講嘢、傾談嘅意思。你留意呢個字係左右結構，左邊係「言」字旁，右邊係「覃」字，倉頡就順住呢個左右次序落手。左邊嘅「言」屬字首，我哋只取佢頭尾兩碼——「言」自己嘅完整碼係 YMMR，字首取頭同二，即係言 Y 同口 R；跟住右邊嘅「覃」係字身，取頭、二、尾三碼，「覃」自己嘅碼係 MWAJ，所以我哋取一 M、田 W，同埋尾嘅十 J。合埋就係 YRMWJ。記住呢個字：左邊有講嘢嘅「言」，右邊個「覃」由上到下畀你一 M、田 W、十 J，姓譚嘅譚就係咁砌出嚟。

警.en: Today we learn 警, read ging2, meaning to guard or be on the alert, as in 警告 ging2 gou3 (to caution or warn) and 警署 ging2 cyu5 (a police station). Look at the character and you'll see it splits top and bottom: the top is 敬 and the bottom is 言. In Cangjie, the top 敬 acts as the head part, so we take its first and last pieces — the grass radical 艹 on key T, then the little crossing strokes 乂 on key K; the bottom 言 acts as the body, from which we take its head 亠 on Y, the horizontal 一 on M, and the final mouth 口 on R. That gives you the full code TKYMR — head takes first-and-last, body takes head-middle-tail, which fills the quota nicely. Remember it this way: grass on top with a little cross (艹乂), then speech below spoken clearly (亠一口), and when the police speak up, that's 警 — as in 警察好快就到, the police arrived very quickly.
警.zh: 今日我哋學「警」呢個字，讀作 ging2，意思係守衛、戒備，好似「警告」ging2 gou3（提醒人小心）同「警署」ging2 cyu5（差人辦公嘅地方）咁。你望下呢個字，其實係上下兩橛：上邊係「敬」，下邊係「言」。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，上邊「敬」做字首，我哋喺佢入面取頭同尾——頭係草花頭「艹」，撳 T，尾係一撇一捺嘅「乂」，撳 K；下邊「言」做字身，就取頭一橫「亠」撳 Y、中間嘅「一」撳 M、同埋最尾嘅「口」撳 R。所以成個字打出嚟就係 TKYMR，字首取頭尾、字身取頭中尾，啱啱好夠碼。記住呢個口訣：草花頭配把交叉刀（艹乂），下面言字講清楚（亠一口），差人講嘢就係「警」，例如「警察好快就到。」

議.en: Today's character is 議, read ji5, meaning to consult, talk over, or discuss — it shows up in words like 建議 (gin3 ji5, to suggest) and 會議 (wui6 ji5, a meeting). Look at the left side: it's the 言 speech radical, which appears in loads of characters about talking — and of course discussing something means opening your mouth to speak. When Cangjie splits this character, the left 言 is the 字首 and gives its head and tail, so 言 (Y) plus 口 (R); then the right-hand 義 is the 字身, which is allowed three codes, so it takes head 艹 (T), middle 土 (G), and tail 戈 (I), giving you YRTGI. Why does the left take only two while the right takes three? Because the 字首 and 字身 have separate quotas — the leading part caps at two codes, and only the body part may stretch to three. Memory hook: on the left you open your mouth to speak (言, 口), and on the right you read top to bottom, 艹, 土, 戈.
議.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「議」，讀做 ji5，意思係商量、討論，好似「建議」（gin3 ji5）同「會議」（wui6 ji5）咁。你望下佢嘅左邊，係一個「言」字部——凡係同講嘢有關嘅字，好多都帶住呢個部件，商議梗係要開口講嘢喇。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，左邊嘅「言」係字首，取頭尾兩碼——頭係「言」（Y），尾係「口」（R）；跟住右邊嘅「義」係字身，字身可以取到三碼，所以取頭「艹」（T）、中間「土」（G）、同尾「戈」（I），合埋就係 YRTGI。點解左邊淨係取兩碼、右邊卻取三碼呢？因為字首同字身各有配額，字首最多兩碼，字身先至可以去到三碼。記住喇：左邊開口講（言、口），右邊由上到下係艹、土、戈，講講下就記到。

護.en: Today we learn 護, read wu6, meaning to protect, guard, or shelter — the same 護 in 保護 (to safeguard) and 守護 (to guard over). Notice the character splits left and right: the speech radical 訁 on the left is the head, and the tall stack on the right is the body. From the head 訁 we take just first and last, which are 卜 Y and 口 R, so you begin with Y, R. The body is a cluster of more than two pieces, so it follows the first-middle-last rule: first is the grass top 艹 T, the middle is 隹 O, and the last is 又 E, giving T, O, E. Put it together and you get YRTOE — picture words (訁) standing watch over a whole bundle of things, keeping them safe, and the code will stay with you.
護.zh: 我哋今日學「護」呢個字，讀作 wu6，意思係保護、守護，好似「保護」同「守護」噉，去照顧同守衞啲人或者嘢。你留意個字分做左右兩橛：左邊嘅「訁」（言字旁）係字首，右邊嗰大橛就係字身。字首「訁」我哋取頭尾兩碼，頭係卜Y，尾係口R，所以先打 Y、R。跟住字身係一個超過兩件砌埋一齊嘅組合，就要取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係草花頭艹T，第二件係隹O，最尾係又E，順住落嚟就係 T、O、E。成個字砌埋就係 YRTOE——記住「護」就係一把說話（訁）罩住一大堆嘢，日夜守護緊，你就唔會撈亂。

讀.en: Today we learn 讀, read as duk6, meaning to read or to study — as in 讀書 duk6 syu1, to read a book or attend school, while a person who reads is a 讀者 duk6 ze2, a reader. The character has the speech radical 訁 on the left and 賣 on the right, so Cangjie splits it along that left-right seam. The head 訁 gives just two codes, its top and bottom: first the 卜 shape which is Y, then the 口 shape which is R. The body 賣, being the character-body, follows the first-middle-last rule and gives three: 士 which is G, 囗 which is W, and 八 which is C. Put them together and you type Y, R, G, W, C. Remember it this way: a mouth opens up (Y R) to speak, and what it reads aloud is 賣 (G W C) — speak it out and you have 讀.
讀.zh: 今日我哋學「讀」呢個字，佢讀作 duk6，意思係閱讀、學習，好似「讀書」duk6 syu1 咁樣，就係睇書、求學嘅意思，而讀某本書嘅人就叫「讀者」duk6 ze2。呢個字左邊係言字部「訁」，右邊係「賣」，倉頡就跟住呢個左右結構嚟拆。字首「訁」取頭尾兩碼，先寫個「卜」係 Y，再寫個「口」係 R；到咗字身「賣」，因為佢係字身，就跟頭、次、尾嘅規則，取頭「士」G、中間「囗」W、同埋最尾「八」C。所以成個字連埋就係 Y、R、G、W、C 五碼。記住呢句：一個人一開口 Y R 講嘢，就係讀出「賣」G W C 呢個字，講出嚟就係「讀」喇。

變.en: Today we learn 變, read bin3, meaning to change, transform, or alter, as in 變成 (bin3 sing4, to turn into something) or 改變 (goi2 bin3, to change or reform). The character looks busy, but it splits neatly in two: the top is the 字首, a big cluster called 䜌, from which we take only its head and tail — 女 (V) and 火 (F). The bottom is the 字身, the piece 夂, and again we take just head and tail — 人 (O) and 乂 (K). Why head and tail only? Because these parts are stroke-heavy, and Cangjie caps each of 字首 and 字身 at a maximum of two codes, so instead of tracing every stroke we grab the most telling opening and closing shapes. Put them in order and you get VFOK — 女, 火, 人, 乂 — so remember: woman over fire on top, person with a slash below, and when the cold snaps in, everything 變!
變.zh: 今日我哋學「變」呢個字，讀作 bin3，意思係改變、變化、轉變，好似「變成」（bin3 sing4，轉變成另一樣嘢）或者「改變」（goi2 bin3，去更改）咁樣。呢個字睇落好複雜，其實拆開嚟就簡單啲：上半部分係字首，係一大嚿嘅䜌，我哋只取佢嘅頭同尾，即係「女」（V）同「火」（F）；下半部分係字身，係個夂，同樣取頭尾，即係「人」（O）同「乂」（K）。點解要咁樣分頭尾呢？因為呢啲部件筆畫多，倉頡有配額限制，字首同字身都係最多取頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋唔會逐筆去拆，而係揀最有代表性嘅開頭同結尾。合埋就係 VFOK，即係女火人乂。記住個口訣：上面女配火，下面人配乂，天氣一凍就會「變」啦！

豐.en: Today's character is 「豐」, read fung1, meaning abundant, lush, or bountiful — the picture of plenty, as in 「今年收成好豐富」, this year's harvest is abundant. It has many strokes, but don't worry, because it's a whole-character (整體字): instead of splitting it into a head part and a body part with their own quotas, we simply take head, second, third, and tail as we read down the shape. Trace it top to bottom: at the very top is 「凵」 (U), then 「十」 (J), then 「一」 (M), then 「口」 (R), and finally the 「豆」 at the bottom, which Cangjie represents with 「廿」 (T) — giving the full code UJMRT. Remember: for a whole-character we don't cut it into front-and-back halves, we just pick head, second, third, and last — and «豐» is packed with pieces just like it's packed with abundance, so read straight down and you won't lose your place.
豐.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「豐」，讀作 fung1，意思係豐富、豐盛、好多好足夠嘅樣，好似「今年收成好豐富」咁講。呢個字筆畫多，但唔使驚，因為佢係「整體字」，我哋唔會拆做字首字身兩截去計配額，而係跟住頭、二、三、尾嘅辦法，順住個字由上到下、逐格咁揀碼。你順住睇落去：最上係「凵」（U），跟住係「十」（J），再嚟係「一」（M），之後係「口」（R），最尾係下面個「豆」字，喺倉頡入面用「廿」（T）代表，所以成個字係 UJMRT。記住：整體字唔講前後兩截，只係揀頭、第二、第三同最尾——「豐」字碼多料足，就好似豐收咁「多」，你順住由上數落嚟就唔會亂。

象.en: Today we're learning 象, read zoeng6, which is that big animal the elephant, and it can also mean ivory, an image, or a figure. This character is tall and stacked, layer upon layer, so it looks busy — that's exactly why Cangjie treats it as a whole character (整體字) rather than splitting it into a head and a body. The rule for a whole character is special: you don't take every single piece, you take the head, the tail, and one or two telling shapes from the middle, skipping the rest — so 象 gives just four codes: the head piece 乙 (N), then 日 (A), then 勹 (P), and finally the tail piece 人 (O), spelling NAPO. Picture an elephant walking from head N, through body A and P, out to tail O — you simply stroll past its big middle without stopping.
象.zh: 今日我哋學「象」呢個字，讀音係 zoeng6，即係大象嗰隻動物，亦都可以解「象牙」、「形象」或者「圖象」嘅意思。呢個字生得高高瘦瘦，一疊疊咁砌上去，睇落好複雜，所以喺倉頡入面當佢做一個「整體字」嚟拆。拆整體字有個特別規矩：唔使成個字每一件都取，而係取頭、取尾、再喺中間揀有代表性嘅碼，跳過剩低嘅部分——所以「象」淨係取四碼，頭嗰件係「乙」（N），第二件係「日」（A），第三件係「勹」（P），最後尾件係「人」（O），砌埋就係 NAPO。你可以記住：一隻大象由頭N、身A、身P、行到尾O，中間肥肥嘅身軀就跳過唔理啦！

豪.en: Today we're learning 豪, read hou4, which means brave, heroic, or grand in spirit — you'll meet it in words like 自豪 (zi6 hou4, proud of one's own achievements) and 富豪 (fu3 hou4, a wealthy tycoon). Look closely and you'll see this character stacks several pieces from top to bottom: first the little lid 亠 on top, which lives on Y; then 口, the mouth shape, on R; then the small cover 冖 in the middle-lower area, on B; and finally 人, the person, sitting at the bottom on O. Because 豪 is a dense, many-stroke character, Cangjie treats it as a whole character and takes head, second, third, and tail — Y, R, B, O — deliberately skipping whatever sits in the middle, which is how we arrive at the full code YRBO. To remember it, just read the character straight down like a little tower: 亠 Y, 口 R, 冖 B, 人 O, four pieces top to bottom in the order you see them.
豪.zh: 今日我哋學「豪」呢個字，讀音係 hou4，意思係英雄、豪爽、有氣派，好似「自豪」（zi6 hou4，即係為自己嘅成就而驕傲）同「富豪」（fu3 hou4，即係好有錢嘅大人物）呢啲詞都會用到佢。你細心望吓呢個字，佢由上到下堆疊咗好多嘅部件，第一嗺係頂上嘅「亠」，喺 Y 度；跟住係「口」，喺 R 度；再落嚟係中間偏下嘅「冖」（禿寶蓋），喺 B 度；最後底部係「人」，喺 O 度。因為「豪」係一個筆畫多又疊得密嘅字，倉頡當佢係一個整體字嚟拆，規矩係取頭、取第二、取第三、再取尾，中間嗰啲就跳過唔取，所以最後嘅碼係 YRBO。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以由頭望到尾：亠 Y、口 R、冖 B、人 O，四粒由上而下順住落嚟，好易記。

豬.en: Today we learn 豬, read zyu1 — the pig you eat as pork. Look at it: it splits left-and-right, with 豕 on the left and 者 on the right, so we treat the left as the head and the right as the body. From the head 豕 we take only its first two shapes, 一 (M) then 人 (O), giving MO. The body 者 is a busy piece, so we use the head-second-last rule, taking its first 十 (J), its next 大 (K), and its last 日 (A) to make JKA, so the whole character is MOJKA. Remember it this way: the left 豕 gives MO and the right 者 gives JKA, and together they fatten up into one plump pig.
豬.zh: 今日我哋學「豬」呢個字，讀做 zyu1，即係我哋成日食嘅豬肉嗰隻豬。你望下，佢係左右兩邊嘅字：左邊係「豕」，右邊係「者」，所以我哋要拆做字首同字身兩橛。字首「豕」我哋淨係取頭兩個碼，一「一」M、二「人」O，得出 MO。字身「者」係一個複雜嘅部件，所以我哋用「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼法，取頭「十」J、次「大」K、尾「日」A，砌埋就係 JKA，全字連埋就係 MOJKA。記住喇：左邊個「豕」畀 MO，右邊個「者」畀 JKA，一隻好肥嘅豬就係咁砌出嚟。

負.en: Today we learn 負, read fu6, meaning a load or burden and, as a verb, to carry or bear something — in 負責 (fu6 zaak3) it means to take responsibility, to be in charge, and in 負面 (fu6 min2) it means the negative side of things. Look at the character: on top sits a little 「⺈」 shape, and underneath sits the whole 「貝」 component. In Cangjie we break this into two parts, a 字首 (the top ⺈) and a 字身 (the bottom 貝). The 字首 isn't an all-in-one 整體字, so we take head and tail: its head is 弓 (N) and its tail is ⺼ (B), giving NB; the 字身 貝 follows the head-second-tail rule for a connected body, with head 山 (U) and tail 金 (C), giving UC, so the full code is NBUC. Remember it this way: 弓⺼ up top does the carrying, 山金 down below takes the weight — one figure shouldering a burden is 負.
負.zh: 今日我哋學「負」，讀 fu6，意思係負擔、背負、承擔嘅意思，好似「負責」（fu6 zaak3）就係要承擔責任、話事嘅意思，「負面」（fu6 min2）就係負嗰一面、唔好嗰一面。你望住個字，上面係一個「⺈」形，下面就係一個「貝」字。倉頡入面呢個字拆做兩橛：字首係上面嗰個「⺈」，字身係下面嗰個「貝」。字首唔係整體字，所以照拆頭尾，「⺈」個頭係「弓」（N），個尾係「⺼」（B），所以字首取 NB；字身「貝」就照連體字嘅頭、二、尾三碼規矩嚟拆，個頭係「山」（U），最尾係「金」（C），所以字身取 UC，合埋就係 NBUC。記住喇：頂上「弓⺼」揹住，底下「山金」墊住——一個人揹住重擔，就係「負」。

貢.en: Today we're learning 貢, read gung3, meaning to offer tribute or the tribute itself — as in the word 貢獻, to contribute or dedicate. Look at the shape: the top is 工 and the bottom is 貝, stacked one above the other. The top 工 is the prefix and takes first-and-last, so you type 一 (M) then ⺼ (B); the bottom 貝 is the body and takes first-second-last, giving 凵 (U) then 八 (C, the C family). Put them in that order and the full code is MBUC. Just remember 工 on top and 貝 below, with the 貝 closing on 凵 and 八, and you'll type it right every time.
貢.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「貢」，讀gung3，意思係進貢、貢品，就好似「貢獻」呢個詞噉，指付出同奉獻。你望吓個字，上邊係「工」字，下邊係個「貝」字，噉樣疊埋一齊。上邊「工」做字首，取頭尾兩碼，即係頭嘅一（M）同尾嘅⺼（B）；下邊「貝」做字身，取頭、二同尾三碼，即係頭嘅凵（U）同尾嘅八（C，即係金家嗰個八）。所以成個字砌出嚟就係MBUC。你記住上「工」下「貝」，記住個「貝」尾收埋喺凵同八度，就唔會撳錯喇。

責.en: Today we're learning 責, read zaak3, which means one's responsibility or duty — the burden a person has to shoulder. Look at how it's built: the top is the 主 shape sitting above, and the bottom is a 貝 shell. Cangjie splits it top and bottom, so the top becomes the 字首 (lead) and the bottom becomes the 字身 (body). Because the top part is the 字首, we're only allowed to take its head and tail — the opening 手 is Q and the 一 is M, giving us QM. The bottom 貝 is the 字身, so it can take head, second, and tail: the head ⺼ is B, the second piece 凵 is U, and the tail 金 is C, so the whole code is QMBUC. To remember it, picture the top 主 taking charge while the bottom shoulders the duty — QM leads, BUC carries the load — just like 責任 (responsibility) or 負責, as in "this matter is his responsibility."
責.zh: 今日我哋學「責」呢個字，讀做 zaak3，意思係責任、職責，即係一個人要孭起嘅本分。你望下佢嘅結構：上面係「責」字頭嗰個「主」，下面係一隻「貝」字。倉頡拆字上下分開，上面做字首，下面做字身。上面嗰橛因為係字首，我哋只可以取頭尾兩碼——起筆嗰個「手」係 Q，跟住個「一」係 M，所以字首得 QM。下面隻「貝」做字身，可以取頭、二、尾三碼：頭係「⺼」B，第二個「凵」U，最尾嗰個「金」C，合埋就係 QMBUC。記住呢個字時，你可以諗成「上面主管，下面孭起責任」，Q M 領住頭，B U C 孭埋尾，成個字就係一份要擔起嘅責任。你可以喺「負責」同「責任」呢啲詞入面見到佢，好似「呢件事係佢負責」噉。

貴.en: Today's character is 貴, read "gwai3", meaning expensive, costly or valuable — as in "呢件衫好貴。", this shirt is very expensive. The shape stacks top over bottom: the top is the head, the bottom is the body, so we split it there. The head gives just two codes — 中 is L and 一 is M — while the body 貝 is treated as one piece and takes first, second and last: 中 becomes 中 no wait, its ⺼ is B, the 凵 is U, and the 金 at the bottom is C, giving LMBUC. The split works this way because a head contributes its first two codes (中, 一), and the body then supplies three (⺼, 凵, 金), adding up to a full five. Memory hook: top says "中一", bottom is 貝 grabbed head-middle-tail — LMBUC, and something this valuable is worth typing in full!
貴.zh: 今日學嘅字係「貴」，讀「gwai3」，即係話貴、值錢、珍貴嘅意思，好似「呢件衫好貴。」咁。呢個字上下兩部分，上面係字首，下面係字身，我哋分開嚟拆。字首取兩碼：「中」係 L，「一」係 M；字身係「貝」字，取頭尾三碼——起首嘅「⺼」係 B，中間嘅「凵」係 U，最尾嘅「金」係 C，所以全碼就係 LMBUC。點解咁拆呢？因為字首只取頭兩碼（中一），而字身作為一個部件取頭、二、尾三碼（⺼、凵、金），加埋啱啱五碼。記住個口訣：上面「中一」，下面「貝」字頭中尾摞晒——LMBUC，貴嘢緊要摞得齊！

買.en: Today we learn 買, read "maai5" — the buy in 買嘢 (to shop) and 買杯奶茶 (buy a cup of milk tea); it means to get something with money, and can also mean to win someone over. Look at its shape: a flat 罒 sits on top, with 貝 resting underneath. In Cangjie the top 罒 is the head, and a head takes at most two codes, so we pull the first 田 (W) and the last 中 (L); then the 貝 below is the body, which gives us 月-like ⺼ (B), 凵 (U), and 八 (C), spelling out WLBUC. Why only two pieces up top? Because the head has a quota — 田 and 中 already stand in for the outer edges of that boxy 罒, so we skip the middle. Remember it this way: field-and-middle boxed on top, and a little shell opening its door to collect the coins below — and you'll recall how to type "I want to buy a cup of milk tea."
買.zh: 今日我哋學「買」呢個字，讀「maai5」，就係「買嘢」、「買杯奶茶」嗰個買，意思係用錢換返嚟，有時亦解作用好處去打動人。你望吓佢個樣：上邊有個扁扁嘅「罒」，下邊坐住個「貝」字。倉頡拆字，上邊「罒」做字首，字首最多取兩碼，所以我哋攞頭「田」（W）同尾「中」（L）；跟住落到下邊個「貝」做字身，順住寫出「⺼」（B）、「凵」（U）同「八」（C），砌埋一齊就係 WLBUC。點解上邊淨係取兩件？因為字首有配額限制，田同中已經夠代表個「罒」嘅頭尾，中間唔使再取。記住一句：上面田中一格罒，下面貝仔開門收錢，你就會記得「我想買杯奶茶」點打喇。

資.en: Today we learn 資, read zi1, meaning property, wealth, or capital — the same 資 you see in words like 資料 (material, data) and 資訊 (information). Look at its shape: 次 sits on top and 貝 sits underneath, and Cangjie splits it neatly along that top-and-bottom join. The head, 次, gives just two codes — 厶 is I and 人 is O — because a head takes only its first and last pieces, so you type I, O. Then the body 貝 takes three codes, head, second and tail: ⺼ is B, 凵 is U, 八 is C, giving the full code IOBUC. Remember the quota — head two, body three — and it's clear why 次 yields only two keys while 貝 yields three. Memory hook: gathering 資 (capital) needs a team, two hands up top and three below, five keys to fund it fully.
資.zh: 今日我哋學「資」呢個字，讀作 zi1，意思係財產、資本、資源，好似「資料」同「資訊」入面用到嘅一樣。你望吓佢個樣，上面係「次」，下面係「貝」，倉頡就順住呢個上下結構嚟拆。上面嘅字首「次」，我哋取頭同尾兩個碼——「厶」係 I，「人」係 O，所以先打 I、O；跟住落到字身「貝」，字身要取頭、次、尾三個碼，「⺼」係 B、「凵」係 U、「八」係 C，於是拼埋成 IOBUC。記住字首只取兩碼、字身取三碼呢個規矩，你就會明點解「次」得兩粒、「貝」有三粒。記憶鈎：搵「資」料要搭夠人手，上面兩個、下面三個，五碼齊備先夠本。

質.en: Today we learn 質, read "zat1," meaning matter, material, or substance — you'll see it in words like 物質 (mat6 zat1, matter) and 質素 (zat1 sou3, quality). The character sits in a top-and-bottom arrangement: 斦 up top and 貝 underneath, so we split it into a head and a body. The head 斦 takes just its first and last shapes, giving 竹 (H) and 中 (L); the body 貝 is a complex form, so it takes head, second, and tail — 月 (B), 凵 (U), and 金 (C). Put them together and you get the five-code HLBUC, where the head gives two codes and the body gives three, which is the standard quota. A memory hook: the two 斤-like pieces up top hand you 竹 中, and the 貝 below unfolds into 月 凵 金 as you write it downward — top to bottom, outside to inside.
質.zh: 今日我哋學「質」呢個字，讀「zat1」，指物質、材料、質地嘅意思，好似「物質」（mat6 zat1）同「質素」（zat1 sou3）咁樣用。呢個字上邊係「斦」，下邊係「貝」，係一個典型嘅上下結構，我哋就要拆做字首同字身兩橛。字首「斦」取頭同尾，就係「竹」（H）同「中」（L）；字身「貝」係複雜字形，取頭、二、尾三碼，即係「月」（B）、「凵」（U）、「金」（C）。連埋一齊就係 HLBUC 五碼，你留意字首只攞頭尾兩碼，字身就攞到頭二尾三碼，呢個係倉頡拆字嘅基本配額。記住呢個字上面兩把「斤」變出竹中，下面個「貝」慢慢寫成月凵金，順住由上到下、由外到內咁打，就好易記喇。

走.en: Today we learn 走, read zau2, which basically means to walk or go on foot, and can also mean to run or to leave — as in 我哋走喇, meaning we're leaving now. Look at the character: on top sits a 土 shape, and below it there's something that looks like a person in motion. This is a whole-character, and a whole-character isn't chopped into a fixed head-piece and body-piece — instead you just read its shapes in order from top to bottom: first the head 土 (G), then the middle 卜 (Y), and last the 人 (O), giving you the code GYO. Memory hook: picture a person (人) standing on the earth (土) with a step-mark (卜) between them, ready to set off walking — GYO, and off they go.
走.zh: 今日我哋學「走」呢個字，讀作 zau2，本義係行路、行走，亦都可以解作跑、離開，好似「我哋走喇」就係話「我哋而家走喇」。你望住個字，上半係一個「土」字，下面就好似有個人喺度郁動咁。呢個字係一個整體字，整體字唔會硬生生斬成字首同字身，而係由頭到尾順住次序取碼：先取頭嘅「土」（G），跟住取中間嗰粒「卜」（Y），最後取埋個「人」（O），所以碼就係 GYO。記憶鈎：「土」上一「卜」一「人」，一個人企喺土地上面，正正準備起步走，GYO 一路行過去。

起.en: : Today we are learning 起, read hei2, the 起 in 起身 (get up) and 起立 (stand up), carrying the idea of rising, going up, or beginning. The character splits into two parts: on the left the 字首 is 走, and on the right the 字身 is 己. The 字首 走 does not get spelled out stroke by stroke — Cangjie uses a head-and-tail rule for the 字首, taking only two codes, so 走 gives us the head 土 (G) and the tail 人 (O). Then the 字身 己 contributes 口 (R) and 山 (U), building the full code GORU. Picture the sentence 我朝早六點起身 — at six the day begins, like a 人 (person) standing up above the 土 (ground), and the code will stick with you.
起.zh: 今日我哋學「起」呢個字，讀作 hei2，即係「起身」、「起立」嗰個「起」，有升起、開始嘅意思。呢個字分做兩橛：左邊嘅字首係「走」，右邊嘅字身係「己」。字首「走」唔會逐筆逐筆咁拆晒，倉頡有個「頭尾」規則，字首只取頭同尾兩個碼，所以「走」取到嘅係頭嘅土(G)同尾嘅人(O)。跟住去到字身「己」，佢畀出口(R)同山(U)，就拼成完整嘅碼 GORU。你想想「我朝早六點起身」，六點鐘天光開始，好似「土」上面有個「人」慢慢企起身咁，就記得住喇！

超.en: Today we learn 超, read ciu1, meaning to leap over, to exceed, to surpass someone — as in 超過 ciu1 gwo3, to outstrip, and 超級 ciu1 kap1, super or ultra. Look at the character: on the left sits 走, on the right sits 召, and Cangjie follows exactly this structure when it splits. The 字首 is 走, but a 字首 can give at most two codes, so we use the head-tail method: take the head 土 G and the tail 人 O, ignoring what lies between. Then the 字身 is 召, which is allowed up to three codes, so we use head-second-tail: the head 尸 S, the second piece 口 H, and the tail 口 R, giving GOSHR all together. Here's your hook: you run over (GO), someone calls you in (SHR), and just like that you've leapt over — 超 — everyone else.
超.zh: 今日我哋學「超」呢個字，讀做 ciu1，意思係跨越、超過、勝過人哋，好似「超過」ciu1 gwo3 同「超級」ciu1 kap1 咁。你望住個字，左邊係「走」，右邊係「召」，倉頡就係順住呢個結構嚟拆嘅。字首係「走」，但係一個字首最多只可以取兩個碼，所以我哋用「頭尾」法，取頭嘅「土」G 同埋尾嘅「人」O，中間嘅筆畫就唔理佢。跟住字身係「召」，字身可以取到三個碼，所以用「頭、二、尾」法，取頭嘅「尸」S、第二嘅「口」H、再取尾嘅「口」R，合埋就係 GOSHR。記住喇：走過去（GO），叫一聲召你入嚟（SHR），你就「超」過咗人哋喇！

越.en: Today we learn 越, read jyut6, meaning to exceed or go beyond — and in the pattern 越嚟越… it carries the sense of "more and more." Look at its build: 走 sits on the left and 戉 on the right, so Cangjie splits it into a head and a body along that seam. The 走 head doesn't give all its pieces; as a head it yields just its first and last codes, 土 which is G and 人 which is O, so the head is GO. The 戉 body follows the same head-and-tail habit, taking its head 戈 as I and its tail ㄑ as V, so the whole character lines up as GOIV. Remember it this way: the 土人 stride ahead in 走, while 戈 and one stroke close off 戉 — and the sentence 佢跑得越嚟越快 (he runs faster and faster) locks in both sound and shape.
越.zh: 今日我哋學「越」呢個字，讀音係 jyut6，意思係「超越、超過」，喺「越嚟越……」呢種講法入面就係「越發、更加」嘅意思。你望下佢嘅結構，左邊係「走」，右邊係「戉」，倉頡就跟住呢個左右分法嚟拆。字首「走」我哋唔會成個攞晒，只取頭尾兩碼：「土」係 G，「人」係 O，所以字首得 GO 兩碼。字身「戉」都係跟頭尾規矩，取頭「戈」係 I，取尾「ㄑ」係 V，於是成個字砌埋就係 GOIV。你可以咁記：「土人」行喺前頭（走），「戈」同一劃收尾（戉），一句「佢跑得越嚟越快」就幫你記實個音同個字。

路.en: Today we learn 路, read lou6, meaning a road, a path, or a journey. Look at it: on the left is the 足 foot radical, and on the right is 各, and together they make the road you walk every day. Here is how Cangjie breaks it down: the 足 head does not take its full code but only its head-and-tail pieces — first the 口 (R) at the top, then the 一 (M) at the bottom; then the 各 on the right is the body, giving its head, second, and tail pieces, which are 竹 (H), 水 (E), and 口 (R), so the whole code is RMHER. Why does 足 give only two pieces? Because sitting on the left as the head it takes just its first and last, skipping the strokes in the middle. Remember it by the two 口 bookends: one 口 opens at 足, and another 口 closes at 各 — a road with a mouth at each end is 路.
路.zh: 我哋今日學「路」呢個字，讀作 lou6，即係道路、路徑，又或者係旅途嘅意思。你望吓佢，左邊係個「足」字部，右邊係個「各」字，砌埋一齊就係我哋日日行嘅路。倉頡拆法係咁樣：「足」字首唔取足碼，而係取佢嘅頭尾——先攞頭嘅口（R），再攞尾嘅一（M）；跟住右邊「各」字係字身，取頭、次、尾三碼，即係竹（H）、水（E）、口（R），所以成個碼就係 RMHER。點解「足」淨係攞頭尾兩碼？因為佢喺左邊做字首，字首只取頭尾兩碼，中間嘅筆畫就跳過唔要嘞。記住呢個口字頭尾包夾嘅樣：「路上」有個口，行到「一路」尾又有個口，兩頭都有口，就係「路」嘞。

身.en: Today we learn 身, read san1, meaning body or trunk — it's also the 身 in the hull of a ship. When you look at it, the middle feels crowded and hard to break into clean strokes, and that's exactly what Cangjie calls 難, "hard." So we use a clever trick: take one slanting stroke 丿 at the top and another 丿 at the bottom, and 丿 lives on the H key, while the tangled middle that won't split is covered by the X 難 key. Put them in order and you get H, then X, then H — HXH. The hook: a stroke opens, the 難 key sits in the middle, a stroke closes — H wraps around X to make 身.
身.zh: 今日我哋學「身」呢個字，讀作 san1，意思係身體、軀幹，好似船身嘅「身」都係用呢個字。你望住佢，會覺得中間好複雜，唔容易一筆一劃咁清楚拆開，呢種正正就係倉頡話嘅「難」字。所以我哋用一個聰明嘅辦法：頭同尾各取一撇「丿」，撇喺鍵盤上係 H 鍵，而中間嗰嚿拆唔到嘅部分，就用 X 難鍵頂住，於是成個字砌埋就係 H、X、H，即係 HXH。記住喇：一撇開頭，難鍵坐中間，再一撇收尾，H 夾住 X，就係「身」。

車.en: Look at this character: 車, read "ce1" — it's the cart or car you ride in every day.
