This is a whole-form character, meaning its parts are tangled together into one solid shape with no clean top-bottom or left-right seam, so instead of the usual head-body split we take three codes: head, second, and tail. Let your eyes travel down it — at the top there's a cross, 十=J; in the middle sits a field, 田=W; and at the bottom another cross, 十=J — reading top to bottom gives you JWJ. The memory hook is easy: two crosses hugging a field, J, W, J, and your cart is built, the very same 車 you see in 轉車 (transfer) and 停車場 (car park).
車.zh: 睇下呢個字：車，讀「ce1」，就係我哋日日搭嘅車、汽車嗰個車。呢個字係一個整體字，即係佢成個結構糾纏埋一齊，冇一個清楚嘅上下或者左右分界，所以就唔用普通嘅字首字身拆法，改為取頭、二、尾三個碼。你嘅眼睛望落去，最頂係一個十字（十=J），中間係一個田字（田=W），最底又係一個十字（十=J），咁樣由上到下順住抽出嚟就係 JWJ。記住嘅口訣好簡單：兩個十字夾住一個田，J、W、J，一部車就整好嘞，好似「轉車」同「停車場」都係用呢個字。

軍.en: Today we learn 軍, read gwan1, meaning army or soldier. Take a look at this character: on top sits a little cover 冖, like a hat resting over things, and underneath it is a whole 車 (cart). To split it, you first grab the head 冖, which lives on the B key; then the body is 車, and because 車 is one solid piece that can't be broken down further, you take its head-second-tail — the first stroke, the second stroke, and the last stroke — which written out are 十 J, 田 W, and 十 J. Put it all together and the full code is BJWJ. Here's your hook: one little hat (B) sitting over a cart (JWJ) — that's 軍, the army loading up and rolling out!
軍.zh: 今日我哋學「軍」字，讀作 gwan1，即係軍隊、軍人嘅意思。你望下呢個字：上面有一個好似帽子咁蓋落嚟嘅「冖」，下面就係一部「車」。拆字嘅時候，先取字首「冖」，佢喺 B 掣；跟住個字身係「車」，因為佢係一個獨立部件，唔可以再細拆，所以要用「取頭二尾」嘅方法——即係取佢第一筆、第二筆同最尾一筆——寫出嚟就係「十」J、「田」W、「十」J。合埋成個碼就係 BJWJ 呀。記住喇：一頂帽仔（B）罩住一部車（JWJ），咁就係「軍」——軍隊坐車出發啦！

軒.en: Today we learn 軒, read hin1, which originally meant a carriage and by extension something high, wide, or open — like a balcony or veranda. Look at how it splits into two halves: 車 on the left and 干 on the right. The left piece 車 is the prefix, and Cangjie takes its head and tail, both of which are 十, so you type J then J. The right piece 干 is the body, giving you 一 as M and 十 as J, so the full code is JJMJ — picture the carriage 車 pulling the 干 alongside it. Your memory hook: think of Hennessy Road in Causeway Bay — 軒尼詩道 — where that same 軒 leads the way.
軒.zh: 今日我哋學「軒」呢個字，讀音係 hin1，本來指馬車，引申有高、闊、寬敞嘅意思，例如陽台、露台。你睇下佢分做兩橛：左邊係「車」，右邊係「干」。左邊嘅「車」係字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，頭同尾都係「十」，所以打兩個 J（J、J）。右邊嘅「干」係字身，取「一」M 同埋「十」J。四碼合埋就係 JJMJ，睇住「車」搭「干」，就係一架高高哋嘅馬車喺度行。記住「軒尼詩」，你住喺銅鑼灣軒尼詩道嗰個「軒」就係佢喇。

較.en: Today's character is 較, read "gaau3", meaning to compare or comparatively, more — you see it in 比較 (to compare) and 較大 (comparatively large), and in the sentence 今日較凍, meaning today is comparatively cold. Look at how it divides left and right: the left side 車 is the head, and the right side 交 is the body. For the head 車 we don't spell out every stroke — Cangjie's head-and-tail rule tells us to take only the first and last pieces, which give 十 (J) and 十 (J), so the left is JJ. The body 交 takes its first piece and its last two: the 卜 (Y) on top, the 金 (C) in the middle, and the 乂 (K) at the end, spelling YCK. Put them in order and you get JJYCK — just remember "車gives two 十, 交gives 卜金乂" and you'll never scramble it.
較.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「較」，讀「gaau3」，意思係比較、相對咁樣，好似「比較」、「較大」噉用，例句「今日較凍」就係話今日相對咁凍。你睇下佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係「車」字做字首，右邊係「交」字做字身。字首「車」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，倉頡有頭尾規則，所以只取頭同尾，攞到十（J）同十（J），噉左邊就係 JJ 兩個十。字身「交」就攞頭一尾二，即係頂上嘅卜（Y）、中間嘅金（C）、最後嘅乂（K），砌埋成 YCK。成個字順住打就係 JJYCK，記住口訣「車頭尾兩個十，交身卜金乂」，你就唔會撈亂喇。

輝.en: Today we learn 輝, read fai1, meaning brightness, luster, radiant brilliance. Look at the shape: the left side is 光 and the right side is 軍, so this is a left-right compound that splits into a head and a body. The head is the left piece 光, and Cangjie takes its first two shapes — first 火 (F) on top, then 山 (U) below — giving us FU. The body is the right piece 軍; since it is already the body and has more than two shapes, we take the head plus the last two shapes: the head 月 (B), then the final two 十 (J) and 十 (J), giving BJJ, so the whole code is 火 F, 山 U, 月 B, 十 J, 十 J — FUBJJ. Memory hook: put 光 (light) beside 軍, and the light shines out everywhere — that brilliance is 輝.
輝.zh: 今日我哋學「輝」字，讀做 fai1，意思係光芒、燦爛、光輝奪目嘅意思。你望下呢個字，左邊係「光」，右邊係「軍」，係一個左右分開嘅合體字，所以要拆做字首同字身兩橛。字首係左邊嘅「光」，倉頡取碼取頭兩個字形：先係上面嘅火 F，再係下面嘅山 U，合埋就係 FU。字身係右邊嘅「軍」，因為佢已經係字身，字形多過兩個，就取頭同埋尾兩個：頭係月 B，尾就數埋最後兩個十 J、十 J，所以字身係 BJJ。成隻字砌埋就係火 F、山 U、月 B、十 J、十 J，即係 FUBJJ。記住喇：「光」字加「軍」，光芒普照，就係光輝嘅「輝」啦。

輯.en: Today we learn 輯, read cap1, which originally means to gather up or collect, and by extension to edit or compile — you see it in words like 編輯 (pin1 cap1, to edit) and 專輯 (zyun1 cap1, an album). Look at it: on the left sits 車, and on the right sits 咠, so this is a left-right character. The left piece 車 acts as the head, and for a head Cangjie takes first and last only — first is 十 J, last is again 十 J, giving you 十J 十J. The right piece 咠 is the body, and because a body may take up to three codes it uses first-middle-last: first 口 R, middle 尸 S, last 十 J, so the whole thing is JJRSJ. Memory hook: a 車 (car) carrying 咠, with a cross-shaped 十 at both its front and back, driving straight to the editing room — 我睇緊呢輯劇, I am watching this series.
輯.zh: 今日我哋學「輯」呢個字，讀 cap1，本義係收集、聚集，引申做編輯、編纂嘅意思，好似「編輯」（pin1 cap1）同「專輯」（zyun1 cap1）都用到佢。你望下佢，左邊係個「車」字，右邊係個「咠」字，係一個左右結構嘅字。左邊嘅「車」做字首，倉頡取頭尾兩碼，頭係「十」J，尾都係「十」J，所以字首拆出十J十J；右邊嘅「咠」做字身，因為係字身可以取到三碼，就用頭二尾嘅方法，頭係「口」R，中間係「尸」S，尾係「十」J。合埋一齊就係 JJRSJ。記憶鉤：一架「車」載住個「咠」，車頭車尾都係十字，一路載去編輯部——「我睇緊呢輯劇。」

輸.en: Today we learn 輸, read syu1, meaning to transport, carry or haul. Look at its shape: on the left sits 車 (cart), and on the right sits 俞. In Cangjie the left 車 is the head part, so instead of spelling out every stroke we take only its first and last 十 十 (J and J); the right 俞 is the body part, taken in order as 人 (O), 一 (M) and 弓 (N), giving the full code JJOMN. Why only two J from 車? Because as the head part it fills its quota with just the first and last pieces, and the strokes in between are skipped — that is the head-part rule at work. Memory hook: two 十 grip the cart, 人一弓 loads it up, and off it goes to transport — JJOMN.
輸.zh: 今日我哋學「輸」呢個字，粵音讀 syu1，解運送、運載嘅意思。你睇下佢係左右結構：左邊係「車」字，右邊係「俞」字。倉頡取碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「車」係字首，我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，只係取頭同尾兩個「十」（J、J）；右邊嘅「俞」係字身，順住取「人」（O）、「一」（M）同「弓」（N），所以成個碼就係 JJOMN。點解「車」得兩個 J 呢？因為佢做字首，取頭尾兩碼就夠，中間嗰啲筆畫唔使理，呢個就係字首嘅取碼原則。記住呢個口訣：兩個「十」揸實架車，「人一弓」裝落去就開得車，一齊「運輸」——JJOMN。

轉.en: Today we learn 轉, read zyun3 or zyun2, meaning to shift, move, or turn — as in "Turn left here and you'll arrive." Notice it splits into a left and right side: 車 on the left is the 字首, and 專 on the right is the 字身. The 字首 takes head and tail, and 車 breaks into two 十 shapes, both keyed J, so you start with J J; then the 字身 專 takes head, second, and tail — its head is another 十 (J), followed by two 戈 strokes keyed I and I, giving J I I. Put together, that's JJJII. Memory hook: three 十 lead the charge, then two 戈 tails — J J J I I, and 轉車 rolls right along!
轉.zh: 今日我哋學「轉」字，讀作 zyun3 或者 zyun2，意思係轉動、移動、轉方向，好似「呢度向左轉就到。」咁講。你睇下佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係「車」做字首，右邊係「專」做字身。字首取頭尾，「車」拆出兩個「十」，全部係 J，所以先打 JJ；跟住字身「專」取頭、次、尾三碼，頭一個又係「十」J，再落到「戈」形嘅兩筆 I 同 I，砌埋成 JII。合埋就係 JJJII。記住個口訣：三個「十」排頭陣，尾巴兩支「戈」，J J J I I 一氣呵成，「轉車」轉得順！

辣.en: Today we're learning 辣, read laat6, the peppery, pungent heat you feel when food is spicy. Look at it: on the left sits 辛, and on the right is 束 stacked into a single block. Cangjie allows the first part at most two codes, so from 辛 we take only its top and the piece just below — 卜 as Y and 十 as J; then from the body 束 we take the tail, pulling out 木 as D plus the vertical 中 that runs through it as L, giving us YJDL all together. A little hook: think of the 辛 of hardship bundled up with a fiery 束, and you get 辣 — as in 麻辣 (hot and numbing) or 酸辣粉 (hot and sour noodles), and 呢碟菜好辣, this dish is very spicy.
辣.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「辣」，讀音係 laat6，即係你食嘢時嗰種辛辣、火辣辣嘅感覺。你睇下佢，左邊係一個「辛」字，右邊係一個「束」字疊埋一齊。倉頡有個規矩：字首最多取兩碼，所以「辛」我哋淨係取佢個頭同埋跟住嘅部分——上面個「卜」係 Y，下面個「十」係 J；到咗字身「束」，我哋就取尾，攞出「木」係 D，加埋中間穿過嘅一竪「中」係 L，砌起嚟就係 YJDL。你可以記住：辛苦嘅辛，加上一束火辣辣嘅感覺，就係「辣」——「呢碟菜好辣」，麻辣、酸辣粉都用得着佢。

辦.en: Today we're learning 辦, read baan6, meaning to manage, to handle, to take care of something — as in 舉辦 (geoi2 baan6), to hold an event, or 冇辦法 (mou5 baan6 faat3), there's no way to do it. Look at the whole shape: it's really two 辛 pieces with a little 力 wedged between them, spread out left-centre-right. Cangjie divides it into a head and a body: the left 辛 is the head, and a head takes just first-last, so we grab 卜 (Y) at the top and 十 (J) at the bottom, giving YJ; then the entire right side becomes the body, which takes first-second-last — 大 (K) for the head, 尸 (S) for the second, and 十 (J) for the tail, spelling KSJ. Put them together and 辦 is exactly YJKSJ, five codes in all. Here's your hook: the left 辛 hands you YJ, the big right side hands you KSJ, and a character with two 辛 hugging the middle always splits right down that seam — 呢件事我幫你辦好, I'll handle this for you.
辦.zh: 今日我哋學「辦」呢個字，讀做 baan6，意思係辦理、處理、搞掂一件事，好似「舉辦」（geoi2 baan6）就係舉行一個活動，「冇辦法」（mou5 baan6 faat3）就係無得搞。你望吓成個字，其實係兩個「辛」中間夾住一個「力」字部件，左中右三橛咁擺開。倉頡分做字首同字身兩橛：左邊嗰個「辛」係字首，取頭尾兩碼，頭係「卜」（Y），尾係「十」（J），所以字首係 YJ；跟住成個右邊當做字身，取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係「大」（K），第二個係「尸」（S），尾係「十」（J），砌埋就係 KSJ。所以「辦」全碼就係 YJKSJ 五碼。記住喇：左邊「辛」畀你 YJ 兩碼，右邊一大橛畀你 KSJ 三碼，兩「辛」夾住嘅字就係咁拆——「呢件事我幫你辦好」。

近.en: Today we learn 近, read gan6 or sometimes kan5, meaning near, close, to approach, or intimate — you'll meet it in everyday words like 附近 (fu6 gan6, nearby) and 最近 (zeoi3 gan6, recently). Look at the character: it splits into two parts, the wrapping 辶 (the walking radical) on the outside and 斤 tucked inside. In Cangjie, 辶 is the 字首 and takes just one code, Y; then 斤 is the 字身, and a 字身 takes head, second, and tail, so we grab head 竹 (H), second 一 (M), and tail 中 (L), giving the full code YHML. Here's your memory hook: walk your way over (Y) until you draw close to 斤 (H-M-L), and you've arrived at 近.
近.zh: 今日我哋學「近」字，讀音係 gan6，或者又讀 kan5，解「近」、「接近」或者「親近」嘅意思，好似「附近」（fu6 gan6）同「最近」（zeoi3 gan6）咁常用。你望下呢個字，佢分做兩部分：一個係包住嘅走之底「辶」，另一個係入面嘅「斤」。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，「辶」係字首，好乾脆淨取一碼 Y；跟住「斤」做字身，就要取頭、次、尾三碼——頭係「竹」H，次係「一」M，尾係「中」L，所以成隻字砌埋就係 YHML。你記住個口訣：走之行過去（Y），去到近處嘅斤（HML），咁就到咗「近」啦。

透.en: Today we're learning 透, read tau3, meaning to penetrate or pass through — you'll see it in 透過 (by means of, via) and 透露 (to leak out, to reveal). Look at the shape: on the left there's the walking radical 辶, and on the right sits the character 秀. For any character built on the 辵 group, we always take 辶 as the head, which lives on the Y key, so the first code is Y. The body 秀 comes next, but a body can only give up to three codes, so we use the head-second-tail method: the head 禾 is H, the second piece 木 is D, and the tail 尸 is S, giving you YHDS. Remember it this way: the walking road carries 秀 across, picking up 禾, 木, 尸 as it passes through.
透.zh: 我哋今日學嘅係「透」字，讀做 tau3，意思係穿過、透入，例如「透過」就係憑住、經由嘅意思，而「透露」就係漏出、揭露。你睇下呢個字，左邊有個走之底，右邊係個「秀」字。凡係辵部嘅字，我哋一律攞個走之底 辶 做字首，佢喺 Y 鍵度，所以第一碼一定係 Y。跟住字身係「秀」，但係一個字身最多只可以取三碼，於是我哋用「頭、次、尾」嘅取碼法：頭係禾 H，次係木 D，尾係尸 S，拼埋一齊就係 YHDS。記住呢句：「走之帶住秀，禾木尸行過」，個走之底一路帶你穿透過去，就唔會撳錯喇。

這.en: Today we learn 這, read ze3, meaning "this" or "here" — you'll see it in words like 這個 (ze3 go3, "this one") and 這些 (ze2 se1, "some of these"). Notice the walking radical 辶 running along the bottom; whenever a character sits on 辶, Cangjie uses a special order — you don't type 辶 first, you first reach inside for the head of what it wraps. Here the inner part is 言, whose head is the single dot 卜 taken as Y, then you type the 辶 itself, also Y, and only after the radical do you fill in the 字身, which is 一 (M) and 口 (R), giving the full code YYMR. So the rhythm is dot, walk, then the body: 卜, 辶, 一, 口 — Y, Y, M, R. Remember it as "peek inside first, then walk, then finish the body."
這.zh: 今日我哋學「這」呢個字，佢讀 ze3，即係「呢個」嘅意思，例如「這個」ze3 go3、「這些」ze2 se1。你睇下佢個底係一個「辶」，即係行走部，凡係有「辶」嘅字，倉頡有個特別規矩：唔係先打「辶」，而係先打入面嗰嚿嘢嘅頭。呢度入面係「言」，「言」個頭係一點「卜」，所以第一碼取 Y；跟住至打「辶」本身，佢都係 Y；打完部首之後先返返去打字身，字身係「一」M 同「口」R，所以成個碼砌埋就係 YYMR。記住個口訣：「辶」字係『先取入面個頭，再行路，最後補返身』——「這」就係卜、辶、一、口，Y、Y、M、R。

通.en: Today we learn 通, read tung1, meaning to pass through, to go through, and by extension things that are common or that communicate, as in 溝通. Notice it is built from two big parts: the walking radical 辶 sitting at the lower left, which maps to Y in Cangjie and is taken first as the head of the character; the remaining 甬 on the upper right is then the body. A body is not spelled out stroke by stroke — it follows the first-second-last rule, so we take the top hook 乛 (N), then the middle 戈 (I), then the closing piece 乀 at the bottom, ⺒ (B), giving YNIB. Why split here? Because 辶 is the enclosing radical and must always be written and typed first as the head, leaving 甬 to supply its three body codes. Remember it like this: walk first (Y), then 甬 gives head-second-last N, I, B — and the line 呢條路唔通㗎, 'this road doesn't go through', keeps 通 in your mind.
通.zh: 我哋今日學「通」呢個字，讀做 tung1，解作通過、通行，又或者係「共通」、「溝通」嘅意思。你留意佢由兩大部分砌成：左下邊嗰個行走部首「辶」，喺倉頡入面對應 Y 字母，我哋就攞佢做字首，最先打；剩低右上邊嗰個「甬」就係字身。字身唔會逐筆全取，而係跟「頭、二、尾」嘅規則，所以先攞頂上嘅橫折「乛」（N），再攞中間嘅「戈」（I），最後攞底部收尾嘅「⺒」（B），合埋就係 YNIB。點解要咁樣拆？因為「辶」係包住外面嘅部首，一定要先寫先打做字首，入面嘅「甬」再照字身取碼規則抽三個碼。記住個口訣：行走先行（Y），入面「甬」字取頭二尾 N、I、B，一句「呢條路唔通㗎」就幫你記住個「通」字啦。

造.en: Today we learn 造, read zou6, meaning to construct, build, or make — as in 創造 (cong3 zou6), to create or bring something new into being, and 造成 (zou6 sing4), to bring about or cause a result. Look at the character in two parts: the walking radical 辶 tucked at the lower left, and the body 告 sitting above it. That 辶 belongs to the 辵 family, and Cangjie takes just one code from it, 卜 (Y); it has a special habit — even though it sits on the left, its Y is placed last, at the end of the code. The body 告 is then read head-second-tail: the head 竹 (H), the second piece 土 (G), and the tail 口 (R), giving HGR, with the trailing Y added after, so the full code is YHGR. Remember it this way: first spell out 告 as 竹土口 (HGR), then let the 辶 walk (Y) up to the very end — and 造 is built.
造.zh: 今日我哋學「造」呢個字，讀 zou6，意思係建造、製作、製造，例如「創造」cong3 zou6 就係創作、帶嚟一啲新嘢，「造成」zou6 sing4 就係引致某個結果。你睇個字分兩大部分：左下角行走嘅「辶」部，同埋上面嘅字身「告」。「辶」呢個部首係辵部，倉頡入面淨係取一碼「卜」（Y），而且佢有個特別規矩——雖然佢喺左邊，但係要殿後放，所以Y排喺最尾。字身「告」就照「頭、次、尾」拆法取碼：頭係「竹」（H），次係「土」（G），尾係「口」（R），合埋就係 HGR，前面再加上殿後嘅Y，全碼就係 YHGR。記住個口訣：先寫「告」訴你——竹土口 HGR，再由「辶」（Y）行到最尾，就砌成「造」喇。

連.en: Today we learn 連, read lin4, meaning to join, to connect, or continuous — you see it in words like 連結 (to link) and 連接 (to connect). Look at its shape: a 車 wrapped by the walking radical 辶, and the meaning fits — like a cart travelling along, joined and continuous. When we break it down, 辶 comes first as the 字首, but because it's an enclosing radical it gives only its first code, Y; then the inner 車 is the 字身 and takes first-second-last, which is J, W, J, so the whole code is YJWJ. Why does 車 give just three? Because we read straight from its own code JWJ — first J, second W, last J, nothing extra. Remember the hook: the enclosing 辶 gives one Y, and 車 walks its first-second-last JWJ — travelling joined together makes 連.
連.zh: 今日我哋學「連」字，讀音係 lin4，意思係連接、連續，好似連結、連接呢啲詞咁。你睇下佢個樣，係一個「車」畀「辶」呢個行走部包住，字義就好似一部車一路行、一路連住去咁。拆碼嘅時候，「辶」做字首，但佢係個包圍嘅部件，所以淨係取頭嗰一個 Y；跟住入面嘅「車」做字身，行足頭、二、尾三碼，即係 J、W、J，砌埋一齊就係 YJWJ。點解「車」得三碼呢？因為佢淨係本身嘅碼 JWJ 讀出嚟，頭係 J、第二個 W、尾又係 J，冇多冇少。記住個口訣：辶字首得一個 Y，車行頭二尾 JWJ，連住行就係「連」。

進.en: Today's character is 「進」, read zeon3, meaning to advance, to make progress, or to enter — you'll meet it in words like 「進行」 (zeon3 hang4, to be in progress) and 「促進」 (cuk1 zeon3, to enhance). Look at the shape: the right part 「隹」 sits on top of the walking radical 「辶」, giving that sense of stepping forward. When we split it, the 辶 acts as the 字首, and because it's a single whole piece it takes just one code, Y. Then the 字身 「隹」 follows, and since the body only gets its head and tail, we take the head 「亻」 (O) and the tail 「土」 (G), giving us YOG. Remember it this way: 辶 carries 隹, walking from 亻 down to 土 — Y-O-G steps you forward.
進.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「進」，讀作 zeon3，意思係前進、進步、進入，好似「進行」（zeon3 hang4）同「促進」（cuk1 zeon3）咁常見。你望下呢個字，右邊個「隹」由個「辶」托住，一步一步向前行，就係進步嘅感覺。拆碼嘅時候，個走之底「辶」做字首，佢係一個成件嘅部件，得一碼 Y，唔使再拆。跟住輪到字身「隹」，字身取頭尾兩碼，頭係「亻」(O)，尾係「土」(G)，砌埋一齊就係 YOG。記住個口訣：辶托住隹，由亻行到土，一步步 Y-O-G 就前進喇。

遊.en: Today we learn 遊, read jau4, meaning to wander, roam or travel — you meet it in words like 旅遊 (a trip) and 遊戲 (a game). Look at the shape: the right side looks like 方 stacked with 子, and tucked under the left is the walking radical. To type it, the walking radical 辶 acts as the 字首 and gives Y first; then the 字身 is broken into three, because a 字身 takes at most its first, one middle, and its last piece, so we get 卜 (Y), then 尸 (S), then 木 (D) at the end, spelling YYSD. Memory hook: start walking with Y, then just roam along Y, S, D — four steps and you've arrived!
遊.zh: 我哋今日學「遊」字，讀做 jau4，即係漫遊、周圍行、旅行嘅意思，好似「旅遊」同「遊戲」噉。你望吓佢個形，右邊係一個好似「方」加「子」嘅部分，左下角就係走之底。拆碼嘅時候，走之底 辶 做字首，取 Y；跟住字身分三嚿嚟拆，因為字身最多取頭、尾兩碼，中間至多夾一碼，所以就係頭取 卜（Y）、二取 尸（S）、尾取 木（D），砌埋一齊就係 YYSD。記住個口訣：走之底行先（Y），再一路 Y、S、D 遊落去，四步就到！

運.en: Today we learn 運, read wan6, which can mean luck or fortune, and also to ship or transport. Look at its structure: the outer piece 辶 means walking or movement, and it wraps around 軍 inside. When we split it, 辶 is the head and gives us the Y key; then 軍 inside is the body, but we don't take the whole thing — instead we follow Cangjie's rule of taking head, second, and tail, which gives us ⺼ as B, then 十 as J, and one more 十 as J at the very end, so the whole code is YBJJ. Picture an army (軍) travelling down the road, carrying your fortune along with it — Y leading the way, then B, J, J following behind. Try it with 運動 (wan6 dung6, sports or exercise) and 命運 (ming6 wan6, destiny), as in 佢好鍾意運動 — he likes doing sports.
運.zh: 我哋今日學「運」呢個字，讀做 wan6，佢可以解「運氣」、「命運」，又可以解「運送」、「搬運」。你望下佢嘅結構：外面有個「辶」，就係行走嘅意思，包住入面嘅「軍」。拆字嘅時候，「辶」係字首，攞佢個 Y 鍵；跟住入面嘅「軍」係字身，我哋唔會整個攞晒，而係跟倉頡嘅取碼規矩攞頭、二、尾三部分，即係上面嘅「⺼」B、再嚟個「十」J、最尾又一個「十」J，所以成個字就砌成 YBJJ。記住呢個畫面：一個人揸住「軍隊」喺路上「行走運送」，Y 帶住 B、J、J 一路行，好運就嚟喇！你可以諗埋「運動」（wan6 dung6）同「命運」（ming6 wan6），例如「佢好鍾意運動。」

過.en: Today we learn 過, read "gwo3", meaning to pass, to pass through, or to go across — you meet it in words like 不過 (but, however) and 透過 (by means of, via). Look at the character: on the left is the walking radical 辶, and on the right sits the body 咼. When we split it, the head 辶 gives just its one key Y, and then we move to the body 咼; because 咼 is the body, it takes at most three codes, so instead of writing every stroke we grab the first 冂 (B), the last 冂 (B), and the closing 口 (R), building YBBR. Here's your hook: you walk 辶 (Y) through two gates 冂冂 (BB) and reach a mouth 口 (R) — pass through both gates and you've "passed over"!
過.zh: 今日我哋學「過」呢個字，讀「gwo3」，意思係經過、通過、走過去，好似「不過」、「透過」都用到佢。你望下個字，左邊有一個行走部首辶，右邊係「咼」呢個字身。拆碼嘅時候，字首辶淨係取佢頭嗰個碼Y，跟住就到字身「咼」；因為「咼」係字身，最多取三個碼，所以我哋唔係逐筆拆晒，而係取頭嗰個冂（B），再取尾嗰個冂（B）同最後嘅口（R），砌成 YBBR。記住個口訣：走辶（Y）行過兩重門冂冂（BB），最後見到個口（R）——「過」咗兩道門就到目的地喇！

道.en: Today we learn 道, read dou6, which originally means a road or path (as in street, roadway) and later extends to mean a method or a way of doing things. Look at its shape: the walking radical at the lower left, 辶, is the "movement" foot that suggests travelling along a road, and in Cangjie it is taken as Y, always placed first as the head. Once the head is taken, the remaining part is the body 首, and following the rule we take its top and bottom pieces — 廿 on top as T, the 竹 shape in the middle as H, and 山 at the bottom as U — giving the full code YTHU. Why split it this way? Because 辶 is a wrapping radical, custom writes the head Y first, then works through the enclosed 首, taking body pieces top to bottom: 廿, 竹, 山. Remember it as a journey: the walking foot sets off first, then 廿, 竹, 山 lead you down the road — YTHU walks the whole path from top to bottom.
道.zh: 今日我哋學「道」呢個字，讀音係 dou6，本來解「路」，例如街道、道路，後來又引申做「方法」、「道理」。你睇下佢個形，係一個帶住行走部首嘅字：左下角嗰個「辶」係走之底，代表行路郁動，佢喺倉頡度取 Y，一定擺喺最頭做字首。字首取咗之後，剩返嘅部分係「首」呢個字身，我哋照倉頡規矩取佢嘅頭同尾——最上面嘅「廿」取 T，中間嗰個「竹」形取 H，最底嘅「山」取 U，所以成個碼砌埋就係 YTHU。點解要咁拆？因為「辶」係一個包住其他嘢嘅部首，慣例先寫字首 Y，再拆入面個「首」字，字身就順住由上到下取廿、竹、山。記住個口訣：行走之底行先，跟住廿、竹、山一路落——YTHU 就係一條由頭行到落嘅路。

達.en: Today we learn 達, read daat6, which means to arrive at or reach, and can also mean intelligent or well-versed. Notice it's a walking-radical character, and it often pairs up in words like 達到, to reach or achieve. To break it down, we first take the 字首: the walking piece 辶 at the lower left gives the key Y, so the code opens with Y. The remaining 字身 is 羍, and since a 字身 takes at most three codes, we use the head-second-tail method: the head 土 gives G, the next piece 廿 gives T, and the tail 手 gives Q, spelling out YGTQ. Remember it like a journey: walk in with 辶 (Y), then count from top to bottom through 土 (G), 廿 (T), 手 (Q), and you'll have reached your destination.
達.zh: 今日我哋學「達」呢個字，讀daat6，意思係「到達、抵達」，亦都可以解「聰明、通達」。你睇佢，係一個行走部嘅字，成日同「到」一齊用，好似「達到」咁。拆碼嘅時候，我哋先睇字首：左下嗰個行走嘅部件係「辶」，取碼字母Y，所以第一個碼就係Y。之後嘅字身係「羍」，字身最多只可以取三個碼，我哋用「頭、次、尾」嘅方法：頭係「土」取G，次係「廿」取T，尾係「手」取Q，砌埋一齊就係YGTQ。記住個口訣：先行走辶（Y），跟住土（G）廿（T）手（Q）由頭數到尾，就「達到」目的地喇。

遠.en: Today's character is 遠, read jyun5, meaning distant or far, as in 永遠 (wing5 jyun5, forever) and 遠方 (jyun5 fong1, the far distance). Look at the bottom-left of the character: that's the 辵 radical 辶, which suggests walking or movement, and in Cangjie it's a special 字首 that gives just one code, 卜 Y, placed at the end rather than the front. The rest is the 字身 袁, from which we take head-second-tail: 土 G, 口 R, and 女 V, so the whole thing builds up as YGRV. Here's your memory hook: the walking radical 辶 walks all the way to the back, so 袁 lines up first as GRV and the Y comes running after — no matter how far you go, that Y is always chasing behind you.
遠.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「遠」，讀做 jyun5，意思係「遠」，好似「永遠」（wing5 jyun5，即係 forever）同「遠方」（jyun5 fong1，即係遠處）咁樣用。你睇下呢個字，左下角有個「辶」，呢個係辵部，行走嘅意思；佢喺倉頡入面係一個特別嘅字首，淨係取一碼「卜」Y，而且係擺喺最後，唔係擺頭。剩返嘅字身係「袁」，我哋拆頭、二、尾三碼——「土」G、「口」R、「女」V，所以成個字砌埋就係 YGRV。記住個竅門：行嘅部首「辶」Y要行到最後先出現，前面袁字先行企定 GRV，行得幾遠都要有個 Y 喺後面追住你。

選.en: Today we learn 選, read syun2, which means to choose or select, as in 選擇 syun2 zaak6 (to choose) and 選舉 syun2 geoi2 (to elect, an election). Look at its shape: there's a walking radical 辶 wrapping the bottom-left, and tucked inside it sits the component 巽 — and when you write it by hand, you draw the inside first and the sweeping 辶 last. Cangjie follows exactly that logic: even though 辶 sits on the outer edge, it acts as the body (字身) and gets typed last, so we take the enclosed 巽 first — 口 (R), then 凵 (U), then 金 (C) at the base — and only then add 辶 (Y), giving YRUC. The memory hook: pick the inside first and let the slow-walking 辶 trail behind, just like the sentence says — pick whichever you like, take your time choosing.
選.zh: 今日我哋學「選」呢個字，讀音係 syun2，即係揀、挑選嘅意思，好似「選擇」syun2 zaak6同「選舉」syun2 geoi2咁樣，講揀邊個、揀邊樣。你睇下佢個形，右下角有一條行走辶嘅部首（Y），入面包住一個「巽」字，寫嘅時候係先寫入面、後寫外面嗰條辶。倉頡打法都跟住呢個道理：雖然辶喺個字最外圍，但佢做字身，要留到最後先打，所以我哋先拆入面嘅巽——由頭嘅口（R）、跟住個凵（U）、再到底部個金（C），最後先補返條辶（Y），砌埋一齊就係 YRUC。記住口訣：「入面巽先行，辶尾行得慢」，因為選嘢要慢慢揀嘛，就好似句「你揀邊個都得，慢慢選」咁！

邊.en: This character is 邊, read bin1, and it means the edge, margin or side of something — the same 邊 in 旁邊 pong4 bin1 (the side, an adjacent place), and in 邊個 bin1 go3, where you literally ask "which one?" It belongs to the 辶 family, and 辶 (the Y key) follows a special rule: even though it wraps around the outside, you do NOT type it first — you tuck it in at the very end and read the inner part 臱 first. For that inner block we take head, second and tail: the head is 竹 (H), the second code is 凵 (U), and the tail is 尸 (S). Only after those three do we add the 辶 head (Y), giving the full code YHUS. Remember it as: read the inside 臱 first — H, U, S — then walk the 辶 in last.
邊.zh: 呢個字係「邊」，讀 bin1，意思係邊緣、旁邊，就好似「旁邊 pong4 bin1」嗰個位，又或者問人「邊個 bin1 go3」即係問「邊一個」。呢個字係走之邊「辶」嘅字，倉頡有個特別規矩：包住嘅「辶」（H 隔離嗰個 Y 掣）唔係一開始就打，而係最後至補上去，所以我哋要先睇入面嗰嚿「臱」。入面呢嚿，我哋照「頭、二、尾」嘅方法拆：頭係「竹」（H），第二個碼取「凵」（U），尾係「尸」（S）。拆完裡面三個碼，最後先補返「辶」個頭（Y），砌埋一齊就係 YHUS。記住呢個口訣：入面臱字 H、U、S，走之最後補個頭。

邨.en: Today's character is 邨, read cyun1, meaning a village or hamlet — in Hong Kong you'll see it most often in the names of housing estates, like 杏花邨 (hang6 faa1 cyun1, Heng Fa Chuen) or 工業邨 (gung1 jip6 cyun1, an Industrial Estate). Notice it's built from 屯 on the left plus 阝 on the right, and the full Cangjie code is PUNL. The head 屯 isn't spelled stroke by stroke; instead it takes just its first and last shapes — 匕 (P) at the front and 屮 (U) at the end — while the body 阝 gives 弓 (N) and 丨 (L). Put in order that gives you 匕 (P), 屮 (U), 弓 (N), 丨 (L), exactly four codes. Remember it this way: the left 屯 is bracketed by 匕 and 屮, the right 阝 is 弓 then 丨 — the very 邨 in 我住喺呢個邨, "I live in this estate."
邨.zh: 今日學嘅字係「邨」，讀音係 cyun1，即係鄉村、村落嘅意思，喺香港最常見喺屋邨嘅名，好似「杏花邨」（hang6 faa1 cyun1）、「工業邨」（gung1 jip6 cyun1）咁。你望下呢個字係左邊「屯」加右邊「阝」砌成，倉頡完整碼係 PUNL。左邊個字首「屯」唔係逐劃拆晒，而係取頭尾兩碼——頭係「匕」（P），尾係「屮」（U）；右邊個字身「阝」就取「弓」（N）同「丨」（L）。所以整個字排落嚟就係匕（P）、屮（U）、弓（N）、丨（L），啱啱四碼。記住喇：左邊屯頭尾夾住匕屮，右邊阝就係弓丨，「我住喺呢個邨」個邨就係咁砌出嚟。

郎.en: This character is 郎, read long4, meaning a young man or a gentleman, and sometimes a husband — it's the 郎 in 新郎, a bridegroom. Look at how it splits into two sides: 良 on the left and 阝 on the right. When Cangjie breaks it down, the head 良 gives only two codes — first the opening dot 丶 (the I key), then the 厶 inside it (also the I key) — and the body 阝 gives 弓 (the N key) and 丨 (the L key), so the whole code is IINL. Why does 良 give just two? Because as the head part, a component is capped at two codes, so we take its first shape 丶 and its last shape 厶 and stop. Remember it like this: a dot, then a 厶, then 弓 pulling a vertical stroke — 丶厶弓丨, IINL.
郎.zh: 呢個字係「郎」，讀 long4，指年輕嘅男子或者男君子，有時仲解做丈夫，好似「新郎」個「郎」咁。你望吓佢分開兩邊：左邊係「良」，右邊係「阝」。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，字首「良」淨係取頭尾兩碼，先取起筆嗰點「丶」（I 鍵），再取入面嘅「厶」（都係 I 鍵）；跟住字身「阝」取「弓」（N 鍵）同「丨」（L 鍵），合埋就係 IINL。點解「良」只出兩碼呢？因為佢係字首，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，所以取頭嗰「丶」同尾嗰「厶」就夠。記住呢句：「一點一個厶，弓拉一豎」，你就記得 IINL 啦。

部.en: Today's character is 部, read bou6, meaning a part, division, or section — as in 部份, a portion of a whole. Look at how it stands: the left side is the 字首 (head part) and the right 阝 is the 字身 (body part). Cangjie limits a complex 字首 to just its head and tail codes, so from the left we take the head 卜 (Y) and the tail 口 (R), skipping whatever sits between them. Then the right-hand 阝 as the 字身 gives us 弓 (N) and 中 (L), so the whole thing spells out YRNL. Remember it this way: on the left, 卜 and 口 mark the top and bottom, and on the right, 阝 breaks into 弓 and 中 — practise it with 呢部電話好靚, this phone is very nice.
部.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「部」，讀做 bou6，即係「部份」、「部分」嘅意思，指一個整體入面嘅一部分。你睇下佢分左右兩邊：左邊係字首，右邊個「阝」係字身。倉頡有個規矩，一個複雜嘅字首最多取頭同尾兩碼，所以左邊我哋取頭嘅「卜」（Y）同埋尾嘅「口」（R），中間嘅部分就唔理佢。跟住右邊個「阝」係字身，取「弓」（N）同「中」（L），咁樣砌埋一齊就係 YRNL。記住呢個口訣：左邊卜口一頭一尾，右邊阝分弓中，「呢部電話好靚」就係最好嘅練習。

都.en: Today we learn 都, read "dou1", a very common word meaning "all, the whole" as in "we are all very happy", and it can also mean "metropolis, capital". Look at it: it's a left-right pair, with 者 on the left and 阝 on the right. The 者 on the left is the head, and Cangjie takes the first and last pieces of a head, so from 者 you take the top 十 (J) and the bottom 日 (A). The right side 阝 is the body, which gives 弓 (N) and 中 (L), so the full code is JANL. Remember it this way: 者 gives head-and-tail 十, 日, then 阝 fills in 弓, 中 — together they make 都!
都.zh: 我哋今日學「都」呢個字，讀「dou1」，好常用，可以解「全部、都係」，好似「我哋都好開心」咁，亦都可以解「都市、首都」。你望吓佢，係左右兩邊夾埋嘅：左邊係「者」，右邊係「阝」。左邊嘅「者」係字首，倉頡拆字首取頭同尾，所以喺「者」入面取到頭嘅「十」（J）同尾嘅「日」（A）。右邊嘅「阝」係字身，拆到「弓」（N）同「中」（L），連埋一齊就係 JANL。記住呢個口訣：「者」頭尾取十、日，「阝」補弓、中，一齊夾成「都」！

配.en: Today's character is 配, read pui3, meaning to match, to pair, or to blend things together. Look at how it divides into two sides: the left is 酉 and the right is 己. The left 酉 acts as the head (字首), and because it's a busy shape, Cangjie takes just its first and last pieces — the top horizontal 一 (M) and the 田 (W) below it. The right side 己 is the body (字身), and reading down through it you take 匚 (S) then 凵 (U), so the whole character is 一, 田, 匚, 凵, spelling MWSU. Remember it this way: when you pour the wine (酉), you match it (配) to your own (己) taste — and it'll always be a good pairing!
配.zh: 今日學嘅字係「配」，讀 pui3，意思係配對、相襯、又或者調配。你睇吓佢分開兩邊：左邊係「酉」，右邊係「己」。左邊「酉」做字首，因為佢係一個複雜嘅部件，倉頡規矩係取頭同尾兩碼，頭碼取上面嗰橫「一」（M），尾碼取下面嗰個「田」（W）。右邊「己」做字身，順住寫落去取「匚」（S）同埋「凵」（U）。所以成個字砌埋就係 一、田、匚、凵，即係 MWSU。你記住：飲酒（酉）要識得配（配）返自己（己）杯口味，就唔會撞味喇！

酒.en: This character is 酒, read "zau2", the word for alcohol — the wine, beer or spirits you drink. Notice it's built from two big parts: on the left the three-drops-of-water 氵, which you type with E, and on the right the body 酉. Because 氵 on the left is the 字首 (lead), it gives just one code, E; the 酉 body on the right then follows the head-second-tail rule of Cangjie, so you pick its head 一 as M, its middle 金 as C, and its tail 田 as W — putting it all together gives you E, M, C, W. Picture it like this: pour the three drops of water 氵 first, set down the 酉 wine jar next, and you've poured yourself a cup of 酒.
酒.zh: 呢個字係「酒」，讀「zau2」，即係我哋飲嘅酒，例如啤酒、紅酒嗰啲含酒精嘅飲品。你留意佢由兩大部分砌成：左邊係三點水「氵」，喺鍵盤上打E；右邊係「酉」呢個字身。因為左邊嘅「氵」係字首，只取一碼E就夠；而右邊嘅「酉」係字身，就照倉頡「頭、二、尾」嘅規則抽三個碼，抽到頭嘅「一」係M、中間嘅「金」係C、尾嘅「田」係W，所以成隻字合埋就係E、M、C、W。記住呢個畫面：先倒三點水「氵」落去，再擺個裝酒嘅「酉」樽，斟起一杯酒就係「酒」喇。

酸.en: Today we learn 酸, read syun1, meaning sour or tart — the taste of a lemon that makes you squint — and it also covers acid in chemistry and that stiff, achy feeling in a tired body. Look at how it's built: it's a left-right character, with 酉 on the left and 夋 on the right. In Cangjie the left part 酉 is the head and the right part 夋 is the body, and neither takes its whole code — each gives only a few pieces. So the head 酉 takes its first and last, M (一) and W (田), while the body 夋 takes its first, second, and last, I (戈), C (金), and E (水), giving you MWICE all together. Remember it this way: left 酉 first-last MW, right 夋 first-second-last ICE — and the sour taste is complete.
酸.zh: 今日我哋學「酸」呢個字，讀作 syun1，即係酸味嘅酸，好似檸檬嗰種令你眯埋眼嘅味道，亦都可以指化學上嘅酸，或者身體攰到「腰酸背痛」嗰種痠軟。你睇下佢嘅結構，係左右兩邊夾埋嘅：左邊係「酉」，右邊係「夋」。倉頡分「酉」做字首、「夋」做字身，字首同字身都各自淨係取幾碼，唔會成個字全取，所以字首「酉」取頭尾兩碼M（一）同W（田），而字身「夋」取頭、二同尾三碼I（戈）、C（金）、E（水），合埋就係 MWICE。記住呢個口訣：左邊酉頭尾MW，右邊夋頭二尾ICE，酸味就砌成喇。

醫.en: Today we learn 醫, read ji1, meaning medicine or to heal — it's the 醫 in 醫院 ji1 jyun2 (hospital) and 醫生 ji1 sang1 (doctor). Look at how it stacks: the top is 殹 and the bottom is 酉. The top is the head, and instead of writing out all of 殹, you take its first-and-last plus the piece hugged in the middle — first the right-opening box 匚 (S), then the arrow 矢 tucked inside (E), then 殳 on the right (M). The bottom 酉 is the body and gives its head-second-last, MCW: M to start, the gold shape 金 (C) for second, and W for the last. Put it together and you get SEMCW. Memory hook: the box holds an arrow with 殳 on top (SEM), the wine jar lines up MCW below — and when you say "我要睇醫生," you'll have it.
醫.zh: 今日我哋學「醫」呢個字，讀ji1，即係醫治、醫生嘅意思，好似「醫院」ji1 jyun2、「醫生」ji1 sang1 咁樣用。你望吓佢嘅結構，係上下砌成嘅：上面係「殹」，下面係「酉」。上半部分係字首，我哋唔會將成個「殹」拆晒出嚟，而係取佢嘅頭尾加中間夾住嘅嘢——先打個開口向右嘅方框「匚」（S鍵），再打入面夾住嘅箭矢「矢」（E鍵），跟住打右邊嘅「殳」（M鍵）。落到下半部分嘅字身「酉」，就取頭、二、尾三碼，即係MCW：M起頭、金「金」（C鍵）做第二、尾碼再係M後嘅W。合埋一齊就係SEMCW。記住一句：上面框住支箭再加殳（SEM），下面個酒埕排MCW，「我要睇醫生」你就記得晒喇。

里.en: Today we're learning 里, read lei5. It originally means a unit of distance — the kind you see in 公里, a kilometer — and it can also mean a village or a lane. Look at its shape: it stacks into two parts, top and bottom. On top sits 田, whose key is W, and underneath sits 土, whose key is G. This is a tidy whole character, so we simply read it top to bottom, taking 田 W first and then 土 G — just two codes, giving WG. Here's your hook: plant one field 田 (W) on top of the earth 土 (G), and you've built a 里, the same character you meet in 公里 (kilometer) and 荷里活 (Hollywood).
里.zh: 今日我哋學「里」呢個字，讀音係 lei5，本來係一個長度單位（好似「公里」咁），亦都可以解作村莊或者巷弄。你望下佢個樣，其實係上下兩截疊埋一齊：上面係「田」，個鍵係 W，下面係「土」，個鍵係 G。呢個字係一個結構清晰嘅整體字，我哋順住由上而下嘅次序去拆，就係先打「田」W、再打「土」G，兩碼就搞掂，寫成 WG，簡簡單單。記住呢個口訣：一塊「田」W 種喺一片「土」G 上面，就成咗一個「里」啦！我哋見過「公里」（kilometer）同埋「荷里活」（Hollywood）都用到佢。

重.en: means heavy or weighty, and it can also mean double or to repeat. It has several readings depending on the sense: cung4, cung5, or zung6. Look at how the shape is built from top to bottom: the little slanting mark at the top is 竹 (H), then the crossing horizontal-and-vertical stroke is 十 (J), the boxed belly in the middle is 田 (W), and the base it sits on is 土 (G), giving you the full code HJWG. Why this particular split? Because 重 is a whole-shape character (整體字) with no clean division into a head and a body, so Cangjie applies its rule for such characters: take the first, second, third, and last pieces — 竹, 十, 田, 土 — and simply skip whatever sits in the middle. Remember the pieces stacking downward, 竹-十-田-土, layer upon layer piling up heavier and heavier — a fitting picture for a character that means heavy!
重.zh: 今日我哋學「重」字，佢有幾個讀音，可以讀 cung4，又可以讀 cung5，仲可以讀 zung6，意思係「重」、有份量，又可以解「重複」嘅意思。你睇下佢一筆一筆點砌出嚟：最頂似撇嘅一點係竹（H），跟住有橫直交叉嘅十（J），中間肚位係田（W），最底墊住嘅係土（G），所以成個碼就係 HJWG。點解會咁樣拆呢？因為「重」係一個整體字，冇一個清楚嘅字首字身界線，遇到呢種情況倉頡有一條規矩：取頭、二、三、尾四碼，即係竹、十、田、土，中間嘅部分就跳過唔理。你記住「竹十田土」由上到下讀落嚟，就好似一層層疊起嚟，越疊越重，正好切合「重」呢個字咁沉！

野.en: This character is 野, read "je5", meaning open country, field, or wilderness — the wide-open land outside the city, as in 田野 (tin4 je5), fields and open land, or 吉野家 (gat1 je5 gaa1), the Japanese fast-food chain Yoshinoya. It splits left and right: the left part 里 is the 字首 and the right part 予 is the 字身. From 里 you take its top 田 (W) and its bottom 土 (G), giving the first two codes; from the body 予 you take head, then, and tail — the head 弓 (N), the second piece 戈 (I), and the tail 弓 (N) — so the full code is WGNIN. Notice the body follows head-second-tail, which is why 戈 in the middle is the only inside piece that gets picked. Remember it this way: field over earth on the left, and a 弓 hugging a 戈 hugging a 弓 on the right — that's the wild open 野.
野.zh: 呢個字係「野」，讀「je5」，意思係郊外、原野、荒野嗰種空曠地方，好似「田野」（tin4 je5）就係田地同開闊嘅土地，而「吉野家」（gat1 je5 gaa1）就係嗰間日式快餐店啦。呢個字分做左右兩部分：左邊嘅「里」做字首，右邊嘅「予」做字身。字首取「里」上面嘅田（W）同下面嘅土（G），加埋就係頭兩碼；字身「予」就取頭、次、尾三碼，即係頭嗰個弓（N）、中間嘅戈（I）、同最尾嗰個弓（N），所以全碼係 WGNIN。留意字身取碼係「頭一、次一、尾一」，所以「予」中間唯一取到嘅係戈。記住喇：左邊田土疊起，右邊弓戈弓夾住，就係郊野嘅「野」。

量.en: Today's character is 量, read loeng4 or loeng6, meaning to measure, quantity, or capacity — you'll meet it in 力量 (lik6 loeng6, strength) and 量度 (loeng4 dok6, to measure). Look at it: it's a tall stack of horizontal strokes and little boxes, and it looks crowded, but Cangjie treats it as a whole-character rather than breaking every piece apart. For a whole-character we take head, second, third, and tail — four codes only — and skip whatever sits in the middle, so we read down the tower: 日 (A) at the top, then the stroke 一 (M), then we jump past the middle to 田 (W) below, and finish with 土 (G) at the very bottom, giving AMWG. Your memory hook: top to bottom it's sun, line, field, earth, and you gently step over the middle — just like the doctor measures your blood pressure, one clean read is all you need.
量.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「量」，讀作 loeng4 或者 loeng6，意思係量度、數量、容量，好似「力量」（lik6 loeng6）同「量度」（loeng4 dok6）咁。你望吓呢個字，佢係一個上下疊得好高嘅字，由好多橫線同框框砌成，睇落好複雜。因為佢係整體字，倉頡就唔會逐部件拆晒，而係用「頭、二、三、尾」四碼嘅法則，跳過中間唔取，所以我哋順住寫落去，最上面攞「日」（A），跟住一橫「一」（M），中間跳過，再攞下面嘅「田」（W），最後攞埋個「土」（G），合埋就係 AMWG。記住呢個口訣：由頭到尾，日、一、田、土，中間嗰截我哋輕輕跳過就得——就好似醫生幫我量血壓，快靚正咁量一次就夠。

金.en: Today we learn 金, read gam1, meaning gold, metals in general, or by extension money. Look at its shape: a pointed roof on top, then a horizontal line holding up two little dots below — the whole thing is neatly symmetrical and solid, like a bar of metal sitting steady on the ground. What makes this character special is that it is itself a radical — 金 is its own radical, so you don't break it into pieces at all; you just press the single key C on your keyboard and the full code is simply C, one letter. Here's your memory hook: something as precious as gold needs only one key — C is for gold, quick and clean! When you ride the MTR and see the station 金鐘 (gam1 zung1, Admiralty), or read 金融 (gam1 jung4, finance) in the news, that first character is always just a press of C.
金.zh: 今日我哋學「金」呢個字，讀作 gam1，意思係黃金、金屬，又或者引申做金錢。你望下佢個樣，上邊似個尖頂，下邊一橫托住兩點，成個字結構好對稱、好穩陣，好似一舊金放喺度咁。呢個字特別之處，就係佢本身已經係一個部首——「金」係部首本字，所以你唔使拆件，直接喺鍵盤上面撳 C 呢個掣就打得出，全碼就係 C 一個字母咁簡單。你可以咁記：黃金咁矜貴嘅嘢，一個掣就搞掂，C 就係金！平時你去搭地鐵見到「金鐘」（gam1 zung1）呢個站名，或者睇新聞見到「金融」（gam1 jung4）兩個字，第一個字都係撳 C 就得。

銀.en: Today we look at 銀, read ngan4, meaning silver — the metal, element 47 on the table, symbol Ag — and by extension money, cash, and wealth. Look at it and you'll see it splits neatly into a left and a right: the 金 on the left and 艮 on the right. In Cangjie the head 金 gives us the code C; then the body 艮 is a fuller shape, so instead of spelling out every stroke we take just its head and tail — the top piece 日 gives A and the bottom piece 女 gives V, so 艮 becomes AV, and the whole character is CAV. Why head-tail here? Because a body takes at most three codes, and for a shape like 艮 the first piece plus the last piece is enough to pin it down without cramming in the middle. Here's your hook: the silver-metal side is C, the 艮 body is 日-女, AV — put them together, CAV, and off you go, 我去銀行入錢, to the bank to deposit money.
銀.zh: 我哋今日睇「銀」呢個字，讀做 ngan4，即係白銀嗰隻金屬，元素表第47號，代號 Ag，同時又可以指錢財、現金。你一眼睇落去，就會見到佢分開左右兩橛：左邊係「金」，右邊係「艮」。倉頡拆字，字首「金」取碼 C；跟住字身「艮」係一個較複雑嘅形，所以我哋唔會逐畫拆晒，而係取佢嘅頭尾兩碼——頭係「日」取 A，尾係「女」取 V，所以「艮」拆成 AV，全個字就係 CAV。點解字身要頭尾咁取？因為一個字身最多都係取三碼，「艮」呢類形取頭一碼加尾一碼就夠，唔使夾硬拆中間。記住呢句：金字旁一個 C，「艮」就日女 AV，砌埋一齊 CAV，去銀行入錢啦——我去銀行入錢。

銅.en: Today we learn 銅, read tung4 — it's the metal copper, element 29 with the symbol Cu, and it shows up in alloys like 青銅 (bronze). Look at the character: on the left sits 金 and on the right sits 同, so its meaning as a metal comes through clearly. When we split it, the left 金 is the 字首, and because it's a radical here it gives just one code, C; then the right side 同 becomes the 字身, which takes head, second, and tail — so we take the head ⺼ (B), the second piece 一 (M), and the tail 口 (R), giving CBMR all together. Remember it this way: the metal 金 stands beside 同, and you spell down the right piece top to bottom — C, then ⺼, 一, 口 — like reading the copper glow of an old Causeway Bay sign.
銅.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「銅」，讀音tung4，就係我哋日常講嘅金屬「銅」，元素表上面排第廿九位，符號Cu，好多合金好似青銅都靠佢。你望吓個字，左邊係「金」，右邊係「同」，一睇就知同金屬有關。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「金」係字首，佢係一個部首，淨係取一碼C；跟住右邊嘅「同」做字身，字身要取頭、二、尾三個部分，所以先取個頭⺼（B），再取入面第二個部分一（M），最後取尾嘅口（R），合埋就係CBMR。你可以咁記：金字旁邊有個同，青銅嘅色好似銅鑼灣個舊招牌咁閃，C同、⺼一口，一路砌落去就啱嘞。

鋪.en: This character is 鋪, read pou1, pou2, or pou3, and it carries a rich range of meanings — to spread out or pave, and also a shop or store, or even a bed you sleep on. Look at it: the left side is the 金 radical and the right side is 甫, so we follow this left-right structure when we break it apart. The 金 on the left is the head and gives us C; the 甫 on the right is the body, and since a body takes at most three codes, we pick its first two pieces and its last piece — 戈 I, 十 J, and 月 B — giving CIJB. The reason we take first-two-and-last is exactly this: when a body has more than three parts, Cangjie uses the head-next-tail method. Remember it this way: 金, 戈, 十, 月 — one very big shop!
鋪.zh: 呢個字係「鋪」，讀 pou1、pou2 或者 pou3，意思好豐富，可以指鋪開、鋪路，又可以指鋪頭、店鋪，甚至指瞓覺嘅床鋪。你望下佢，左邊係「金」字部，右邊係一個「甫」字，所以拆嘅時候就順住呢個左右結構嚟拆。左邊「金」係字首，取 C；右邊「甫」係字身，一個字身最多取三碼，所以我哋要喺「甫」入面揀頭兩個同最尾一個部件，即係戈 I、十 J，同埋月 B，砌埋一齊就係 CIJB。之所以係揀頭二尾三，正正因為字身部件多過三個嗰陣，倉頡就用「頭、次、尾」呢個取碼法。記住呢個口訣：金字戈十月，一間好大嘅鋪頭！

錄.en: Today we learn 錄, read luk6, meaning to copy, write down, or record — the character you see in words like 記錄 (to record) and 錄音 (to record sound). Look at its shape: on the left is the 金 metal radical, and on the right is 彔, a clean left-right character. When Cangjie splits left from right, the left 金 acts as the 字首 and gives just one code, C; the right 彔 acts as the 字身 and takes three codes — first, second, and last — reading top to bottom to pick up 彐 as V, 乙 as N, and the bottom 氺 as E, so the full code is CVNE. To remember it, picture a metal recorder: your left hand holds the gold C, and your right hand sweeps down V, N, E to capture the sound.
錄.zh: 今日我哋學「錄」呢個字，讀 luk6，即係抄寫、記低、記錄嘅意思，好似「記錄」、「錄音」咁用。你望吓佢個結構：左邊係「金」字旁，右邊係「彔」，一個典型嘅左右字。倉頡分左右嘅時候，左邊「金」做字首，只取一碼 C；右邊「彔」做字身，就要取頭、次、尾三碼，順住由上到下嘅筆順分別攞到「彐」V、「乙」N、同最底嘅「氺」E，所以全碼砌埋就係 CVNE。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗成「金屬彔音機」——左手攞住金 C，右手由上掃落去 V、N、E，就記低咗把聲。

錦.en: Today we learn 錦, read gam2, meaning a beautifully woven, patterned silk fabric — brocade. Look at how it splits into two parts: on the left is 金, and on the right is 帛. The left piece 金 is the 字首, and a 字首 like this takes just one code, which is C. The right piece 帛 is the 字身, and a 字身 can take up to three codes, so we use head-second-tail: the head is 竹 H, then 日 A, and the final tail is the ⺼ underneath, which is B, giving HAB. Put them in typing order and you get C, H, A, B — that is CHAB. Remember it this way: one lump of 金 C on the left, then 帛 broken into bamboo-sun-flesh HAB — that is how the brocade shirt is woven.
錦.zh: 今日我哋學「錦」呢個字，讀做 gam2，意思係織得好靚、有花紋嘅絲織品，好似錦緞、錦繡咁。你望下佢由兩大部分砌成：左邊係「金」，右邊係「帛」。左邊「金」係字首，只取一碼，就係 C。右邊「帛」係字身，字身可以取到三碼，我哋用「取頭二尾」嘅方法：頭係「竹」H，接住個「日」A，最後個尾係下面嘅「⺼」B，砌埋一齊就係 HAB。所以成個字順住打就係 C、H、A、B，即係 CHAB。記住個口訣：左邊一嚿金 C，右邊「帛」拆做竹日肉 HAB，錦衫就係咁織成㗎。

鍋.en: Today we're learning 鍋, read wo1, meaning a cooking-pot or saucepan — the same 鍋 you see in 火鍋, hotpot. Look at its shape: it's a left-right character, with 金 on the left and 咼 on the right. When we type it, we start with the head part 金 — because 金 is a whole-piece (整體字) unit, we take only its single code, which is C. Then for the body part 咼, which is not a whole-piece unit, we take head-second-tail, three codes: the head is ⺼ (B), the second is again ⺼ (B), and the tail is 口 (R), giving us BBR. Put it all together and you get C, B, B, R — CBBR. Here's your memory hook: the metal radical 金 gives one code C, and on the right the 咼 has two ⺼ pieces hugging a 口 — and that's your cooking pot!
鍋.zh: 今日我哋學「鍋」呢個字，讀音係 wo1，意思就係煮嘢食用嘅鑊、煲，好似「火鍋」個鍋噉。你望吓佢個樣，係左右結構，左邊係「金」，右邊係「咼」。打字嘅時候，我哋先睇字首「金」——「金」係一個整體字，所以我哋淨係攞佢一碼，就係 C。跟住到字身「咼」，佢唔係整體字，所以要取頭、二、尾三碼：頭係「⺼」（B），第二個又係「⺼」（B），最後個尾就係「口」（R），砌埋一齊就係 BBR。成個字連埋就係 C、B、B、R——CBBR。記住喇：金字旁一碼 C，右邊咼字兩個⺼夾住個口，噉就係一個煮嘢食嘅鍋啦！

鍾.en: Today we're learning 鍾, read zung1. It originally meant a cup, goblet or wine vessel, and nowadays you'll most often meet it as a surname, or in the word 鍾意, which means to like something. Look at its shape: on the left sits the 金 metal radical, and on the right stands the character 重, so Cangjie follows that left-to-right order when breaking it apart. The left 金 is the prefix, and although a prefix may take up to two codes, here it contributes only its one code C before handing over to the body on the right. That right-hand 重 is the body, and a body takes first-second-last, so reading down through it we grab the first piece 竹 H, then the second piece 十 J, then the last piece 土 G, giving CHJG. Remember it this way: gold leads with one code C, and 重 fills in with 竹十土 — that's the 鍾 in 我好鍾意食蛋糕, 'I really like eating cake.'
鍾.zh: 今日我哋學「鍾」呢個字，讀音係 zung1，本來解杯、盞或者酒器，而家最常見係做姓氏，好似「鍾意」噉樣用嘅時候，就係喜歡嘅意思。你望吓佢嘅結構，左邊係「金」字部，右邊係一個「重」字，倉頡拆碼就順住呢個左右嘅次序嚟做。左邊嘅「金」係一個字首，字首最多只可以取兩碼，但係金部喺呢度只取一碼，就係 C，之後就交畀右邊嘅字身。右邊個「重」係字身，字身要取頭、次、尾三碼，所以我哋順住寫落嚟，先攞頭嘅「竹」H，再攞次嘅「十」J，最後攞尾嘅「土」G，合埋成 CHJG。記住呢個口訣：金字帶頭一碼，重字補上竹十土，「我好鍾意食蛋糕」嘅鍾就係噉打出嚟。

鐵.en: Today's character is 鐵, read tit3, meaning iron — the metal, element 26 on the periodic table — and by extension anything strong, solid, or firm. Take a look: on the left is the 金 metal radical, and on the right is a cluster of strokes packed together. Cangjie usually splits a character into a head part (字首) and a body part (字身), and each part gives at most three codes. Here 金 is the head, and because its full code would run past three keys, we take only its head-and-tail: 金 (C) and 十 (J), giving CJ; the body on the right then contributes 戈 (I) and its final piece 土 (G), so the whole code is CJIG. Remember it like this: the metal on the left takes just its two ends (CJ), and the right side finishes with 戈 and 土 (IG) — that's your 鐵, the character you use in 高鐵 (gou1 tit3, high-speed rail) and 拿鐵 (naa4 tit3, latte).
鐵.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「鐵」，讀音同「鐵」（tit3）一樣，就係金屬入面嘅鐵，元素表第二十六號，仲可以形容一樣嘢好堅硬、好穩固。你望下佢，左邊係「金」字部，右邊係一堆筆畫砌埋一齊。倉頡有個規矩：一隻字通常分做字首同字身，字首同字身各自最多取三個碼。左邊嘅「金」係字首，因為個碼會多過三個，所以就取頭尾兩碼，即係頭嘅「金」（C）同尾嘅「十」（J），變成CJ；右邊嘅字身就取「戈」（I）同最後嘅「土」（G），合埋成CJIG。記住呢個口訣：金字打頭尾（CJ），戈土收尾（IG），鐵就砌好喇。你平時搭嘅「高鐵」（gou1 tit3）、飲嘅「拿鐵」（naa4 tit3）都用到呢個字。

鑼.en: Today we learn 鑼, read lo4, meaning a gong — that round metal disc in Chinese percussion that goes "clang" when you strike it. Look at how it splits into a left and a right part: the left is 金, the head, which gives you its key C; the right is 羅, the body. Cangjie caps a character at five codes and divides the quota between head and body, so once the head 金 has taken its one code C, the body 羅 can't spell out every piece — it takes only head, second, and tail, which are 囗 as W, 中 as L, and 土 as G. Put together the whole code is CWLG, so remember it as the 鑼 in 銅鑼灣, Causeway Bay, and the 鑼 that someone beats over there.
鑼.zh: 今日我哋學「鑼」呢個字，讀做 lo4，意思係銅鑼，即係中國打擊樂器嗰種一敲就「噹」一聲嘅圓盤。你睇佢由左右兩橛砌成：左邊係「金」，做字首，取佢個鍵 C；右邊係「羅」做字身。倉頡有個規矩，一個字最多拆五碼，字首同字身各有配額，字首「金」佔一碼齊晒，於是「羅」呢個字身就唔可以逐部件全取，只能夠取頭、二、尾三個碼——頭「囗」係 W，第二個「中」係 L，最尾「土」係 G。所以成個字砌埋就係 CWLG，記住「銅鑼灣」個鑼、佢喺度打鑼嗰個鑼就得喇。

長.en: Today we're learning 長, which reads "coeng4" and means long or length, and by extension to excel at something or to be a leader. Take a good look at its shape: it's a single-body character (整體字) that flows together and can't be cleanly split into a head part and a body part, so instead we use the special rule for such characters — take the head, the second piece, and the tail, for three codes in all. The head is 尸, which you type with S; the second piece is the single horizontal stroke 一, typed with M; and the tail is 𧘇, typed with V, giving you SMV. Because there's no natural break to divide it, we simply sweep from top to bottom — 尸 on top, one stroke in the middle, a trailing tail below — head, second, tail, S, M, V. Think of Cheung Sha Wan (長沙灣) or Cheung Chau (長洲), and when you write that 長 you'll reach for SMV.
長.zh: 今日我哋學「長」呢個字，佢讀「coeng4」，即係長短嘅「長」，可以指長度，又可以引申做擅長、首領。你望吓佢個樣，係一個連埋一齊、拆唔開嘅整體字，冇辦法好清楚咁分做字首同字身，所以我哋用整體字嘅取碼法：取頭、取次、取尾，總共三碼。個頭係「尸」，喺鍵盤上面撳 S；跟住第二個部件係一橫「一」，撳 M；最後個尾係「𧘇」，撳 V，合埋就係 SMV。記住個口訣：一個尸字頭、中間一橫、下面拖住條尾巴，就好似頭髮咁「頭、中、尾」順住落嚟，長長哋一條。你可以諗吓「長沙灣」（Cheung Sha Wan）同埋「長洲」（Cheung Chau）呢兩個地方，寫嗰個「長」字嘅時候就係打 SMV。

門.en: Today we meet the character 門, read mun4, which means a gate, a door, or an entrance — the very doorway you pass through when you leave or enter a home. Take a good look at it: it's symmetrical, with two panels standing on either side, so the shape itself looks like a pair of doors, which makes it easy to recognise. In Cangjie, 門 is a whole character (整體字), meaning it isn't split into a head part and a body part; instead you simply take one piece from its head and one from its tail — the head is 日 on the A key, and the tail is 弓 on the N key, giving you AN. The reason it's just these two codes is that whole characters don't follow the usual splitting quotas; they only grab the head and the tail and ignore everything in between, so you never have to worry about the inner strokes of 門. Remember it this way: 日 opens the door and 弓 closes it — AN is a doorway, the same one you find in words like 屯門 (Tuen Mun) and 專門店 (a specialty store).
門.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「門」，讀做 mun4，意思就係一道門、大門或者出入口，好似你出街入屋都要經過嘅嗰道門。你望吓個字，兩邊對稱，好似真係有兩扇門板咁企喺度，係一個好形象嘅字。喺倉頡入面，「門」係一個整體字，成個字唔會拆做字首同字身兩截，而係直接由個字嘅頭同尾各取一個部件：頭取「日」（喺 A 鍵），尾取「弓」（喺 N 鍵），所以整個碼就係 AN。點解係頭尾兩碼咁少呢？因為整體字唔跟一般拆字嘅配額規矩，佢淨係捉頭、捉尾兩個位，中間嘅嘢一律唔理，所以你唔使去諗個「門」入面其他筆畫應該點打。記住呢句口訣：日字開頭、弓字收尾，AN 就係一道門，好似「屯門」同「專門店」都用得着。

開.en: Today we're learning 開, read hoi1, meaning to open, to begin, to start. Look at its outer frame: it's the character 門, a gate, and there's something living inside the gate, so we split this character into two parts. When Cangjie takes the 門 frame, it doesn't grab every stroke — it takes the head and the tail, first the 日 (A) on top, then the 弓 (N) below, and those two form the head part. Then for the piece inside, we again take head and tail: 一 (M) first, then 廿 (T), giving us the full code ANMT. Here's your hook: the gate frame is 日弓, the belly inside is 一廿 — swing the gate 開 and you get ANMT!
開.zh: 今日我哋學「開」呢個字，讀做 hoi1，即係「打開」、「開始」嘅意思。你望下佢個外框，係一個「門」字，門入面又有嘢，所以呢個字要分開兩部分嚟拆。倉頡拆「門」呢個框嘅時候，唔會逐筆攞晒，而係取頭尾兩件——先攞頂上嘅日（A），再攞底下嘅弓（N），呢個就係字首。跟住入面嗰嚿嘢，都係取頭尾——先一（M），後廿（T），合埋成 ANMT。記住一句口訣：門框係「日弓」，肚裏面係「一廿」，門一打「開」就係 ANMT！

間.en: This character is 間, read gaan1, meaning an interval or space between things, and also the measure word for houses and shops, as in "this house." Look closely and you'll see the 門 gate wrapping around an inner 日 sun — the whole thing is a gate enclosing something inside. Because the outer 門 is the 字首, we don't spell it out stroke by stroke; instead we take its head 日 (A) and its tail 弓 (N), giving AN for the leading part; then the enclosed 日 (A) is the 字身, and a 字身 like this takes just one code, so it adds A. Put the three pieces together and the code is ANA, that is 日 弓 日. Remember it this way: look through the gate and you meet the head 日 first, the tail 弓 next, and finally the 日 sitting inside — 日 弓 日, one clean sweep.
間.zh: 呢個字係「間」，讀gaan1，意思係中間、空間，又或者係量度屋、鋪嘅單位，好似「呢間屋」咁講。你望真啲，會見到個「門」字圍住入面一個「日」，成隻字係一個門包住一樣嘢嘅結構。因為外面嘅「門」係字首，我哋唔會逐筆拆佢，而係取佢個頭嘅日（A），再取佢個尾嘅弓（N），所以字首就係AN；跟住入面被包住嘅日（A）係字身，字身只取一碼，於是就係A。三個部件砌埋一齊，個碼就係ANA，即係日弓日。記住喇：門口望入去，先見頭日、後見尾弓，最後見到門裏面嗰個日，日弓日一氣呵成。

閣.en: Today's character is 閣, read gok3, meaning a chamber or pavilion, and also the government "cabinet" as in 內閣. Look at its shape: an outer 門 frame wraps around whatever sits inside, like a big doorway. That 門 frame is treated as one whole unit at the front, so you take it complete as A without breaking it apart; then the inner 各 is coded by its own pieces, split head-second-last into three parts — first 夂 giving N, then 竹 giving H, and finally the 口 shape, from which you take the head as E and the tail as R. Put them together and you get the five-code sequence ANHER. Picture it this way: one door (A) framing a 各 inside (NHER), and when the door swings open you find yourself in the attic — 閣樓.
閣.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「閣」，讀做 gok3，解作樓閣、亭閣，又或者政府嘅「內閣」。你望吓佢個樣，外面係一個「門」字框，將裏面嘅嘢包住，好似一道大門。呢個門字框係一個整體字首，我哋成個攞落嚟做 A，唔使拆開佢；跟住輪到框裏面嘅「各」字，佢就要拆成頭二尾三塊——先係「夂」字取 N，再係「竹」字取 H，最尾嘅「口」字，因為要取頭同尾，所以頭一個「口」取 E，尾嗰個「口」取 R。合埋一齊就係 ANHER 五碼喇。記住呢個畫面：一道門（A）框住入面一個各（NHER），門一開就見到「閣樓」。

關.en: Today we learn 關, read gwaan1, which can mean a frontier pass, to close, or a relation — as in 關係 gwaan1 hai6, a connection between things, or 關於 gwaan1 jyu1, meaning about or concerning something. Look at its shape: the whole character sits inside a 門 gate, so we begin by breaking down that 門 radical. The 門 gate is a big enclosing frame, and when we split it we don't count every stroke — we take just first and last, which are 門 A and 乙 N, so the frame gives us A, N. Then we step inside the frame to the inner body and take first-second-last: 女 V, 戈 I, and 廿 T, giving the full code ANVIT. Remember it this way: draw the gate first (A, N), then tidy up the three things inside (V, I, T) — and don't forget to close the door.
關.zh: 我哋今日學「關」字，讀作 gwaan1，佢可以解作關口、關閉、又或者關係，好似「關係」gwaan1 hai6 咁講兩件事有連繫，又或者「關於」gwaan1 jyu1 咁講同某件事有關。你望下佢個樣，成個字包喺一個「門」入面，所以我哋先由呢個「門」字部開始拆。「門」係一個大框，拆碼嗰陣我哋唔會逐筆數盡，只係取頭尾兩個位——頭係「門」A，尾係「乙」N，於是門框先打 A、N。跟住入到門框裏面嘅字身，取頭、二、尾三個位：頭係「女」V，第二個係「戈」I，最後係「廿」T，合埋就係 ANVIT。記住呢個心法：先框住個門（A、N），再入去執中間三件嘢（V、I、T），關門就記得晒喇。

阿.en: Today we're learning 阿, read "aa3", a friendly prefix you put before someone's name — you already know it from 阿媽 (mom) and 阿爸 (dad). Look at how it's built: the left side is 阝 and the right side is 可, so we split it into a 字首 and a 字身. The 字首 阝 gives you two codes, first 弓 (N) then 中 (L), so NL. The 字身 可 then takes three codes — the head 一 (M), the second 弓 (N), and the tail 口 (R) — giving you the full code NLMNR. Remember it this way: the left 阝 is NL, then 可 hands over its head, middle, and tail, and you've typed the 阿 of 阿媽.
阿.zh: 我哋今日學「阿」呢個字，讀「aa3」，係擺喺人名前面嘅稱呼，好似「阿媽」、「阿爸」咁樣，好親切。你望下佢嘅結構，左邊係「阝」，右邊係「可」，所以我哋分做字首同字身兩部分。字首「阝」拆做兩個碼，先係「弓」（N），再係「中」（L），合埋就係 NL。字身「可」就要取三個碼——頭係「一」（M），第二係「弓」（N），尾係「口」（R），所以全字連埋就係 NLMNR。記住個口訣：左邊嘅「阝」係 NL，右邊嘅「可」頭中尾各取一，就砌成「阿媽」個「阿」啦。

限.en: Today's character is 限, read haan6, meaning a boundary or a limit — you'll see it in words like 限制 haan6 zai3 (limitation) and 無限 mou4 haan6 (infinity). Look at how it divides into two sides: the 字首 on the left is the ear-shaped 阝, and the 字身 on the right is 艮. Cantonese Cangjie doesn't spell 阝 stroke by stroke; instead it takes its head and tail, which are 弓 N and 中 L, so the 字首 gives you N and L. The 字身 艮 follows the same head-tail rule, taking 日 A at the head and 女 V at the tail, giving you A and V. Put the two sides together and 限 is typed NLAV — remember it as a boundary held on the left by 阝 (弓中, N-L) and blocked on the right by 艮 (日女, A-V), four keys that draw the line.
限.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「限」，讀音係 haan6，即係界線、限度嘅意思，好似「限制」haan6 zai3、「無限」mou4 haan6 咁樣用。你睇下呢個字分做兩邊：左邊嘅字首係耳仔旁「阝」，右邊嘅字身係「艮」。字首「阝」倉頡唔係逐筆咁拆，而係取頭尾兩碼，頭係弓 N、尾係中 L，所以字首就係 N、L 兩個碼；跟住字身「艮」同樣係取頭尾，頭係日 A、尾係女 V，所以字身就係 A、V。合埋一齊，成個「限」字就係打 NLAV。你可以咁記：一道界線由左邊嘅「阝」框住，右邊嘅「艮」擋住，弓中先開路、日女再收尾，四碼一氣呵成，就係「呢度限速好慢」嗰種「限」。

院.en: Today we learn 院, read "jyun2", meaning courtyard or school — it shows up in words like 醫院 (hospital) and 學院 (college). Look at it: on the left is the 阝 ear-radical, and on the right sits 完, so we split it into a head and a body. The 阝 head is one connected shape, and for such shapes Cangjie takes first and last — the opening stroke reads as 弓 (N) and the final as 中 (L), giving NL for the head. The 完 body then takes at most three codes using head-second-tail: the head is 十 (J), the second is 一 (M), and the tail is 山 (U), so the body is JMU. Put together it types NLJMU — remember it as "an 阝 next to a complete 完 courtyard," and the pieces fall right into place.
院.zh: 今日我哋學「院」呢個字，讀「jyun2」，係「courtyard」、「school」嘅意思，好似「醫院」、「學院」都用到佢。你望吓，佢左邊係個阝（耳仔邊），右邊係「完」，我哋要拆成字首同字身兩橛。字首個阝係一件相連嘅嘢，倉頡拆連體字係取頭尾，開頭望到係弓（N），最後收筆係中（L），所以字首係 NL。跟住右邊「完」做字身，一件字身最多取三碼，用頭、二、尾嘅辦法：頭係十（J），第二係一（M），最尾係山（U），合埋就係 JMU。成個字順住打落去就係 NLJMU，你可以記住「阝旁一間醫院，入面『完』得好齊全」，咁就唔會撈亂。

陣.en: Today we learn 陣, read "zan6", which originally means a row or file of troops — the battle formation soldiers line up in. Look at how it splits into two sides: on the left is 阝, and on the right is 車. The 阝 is the 字首 (leading part), and it hands over two codes, 弓 (N) and 中 (L); then 車 is the 字身 (body), and a body gives its head, second, and tail — three codes — so you take 十 (J) as the head, 田 (W) as the second, and 十 (J) again as the tail, giving you NLJWJ. Why here? Because in a lead-plus-body character the 字首 always gives two codes and the 字身 gives head-second-tail as three, landing neatly at five codes. Memory hook: left side 阝 is NL, right side 車 wraps 田 between two 十 — wait a moment (等我一陣) and it clicks.
陣.zh: 今日我哋學「陣」呢個字，讀「zan6」，本來係指一列一列嘅軍隊，即係打仗排開嘅陣勢。你睇佢由左右兩部分砌成：左邊係「阝」，右邊係「車」。個「阝」係字首，我哋唔可以淨拆一碼，要取「弓」（N）同「中」（L）兩碼；跟住個「車」係字身，字身取頭、二、尾三碼，所以攞「十」（J）做頭、「田」（W）做第二碼、再「十」（J）做尾，合埋成 NLJWJ。點解係咁分？因為一個字首字身結構，字首交兩碼、字身交頭二尾三碼，啱啱夠五碼收工。記住個口訣：左邊阝仔 NL，右邊車仔一頭一尾夾住個田，等我一陣先！

除.en: Today we learn 除, read ceoi4, meaning to remove or eliminate, and also "except for," as in 除非 (only if). Look at it: on the left is the little ear-shape 阝, and on the right is 余. In Cangjie the 阝 piece is not taken as one whole unit—it splits into 弓 (N) and 中 (L), so you type N then L for the left side. The 余 body then contributes only three codes, following the head-middle-tail rule for a body: the head 人 (O), then M standing in for the middle stroke, and the tail 木 (D), giving the full code NLOMD. Remember it as the ear on the left, 弓中 (NL), plus 人一木 (OMD) on the right—just like "除咗你, 冇人嚟": except you, no one came.
除.zh: 我哋今日學「除」呢個字，讀作 ceoi4，意思係「除去」、「除咗……之外」，好似「除非」咁。你望下佢，左邊係個耳仔形嘅「阝」，右邊係「余」。喺倉頡入面，「阝」呢個部件並唔係一個整體碼，而係拆成「弓」同「中」兩件，所以先打 N 再打 L；跟住右邊嘅字身「余」就只揀三件——頭嘅「人」O、中間嘅「二」其實喺碼度取一橫「一」M、最後個尾係「木」D，合埋就係 NLOMD。字身通常只取頭、中間同尾三碼，所以「余」就精簡到 O、M、D 咁三件。記住：左邊耳仔「弓中」（NL），右邊「人一木」（OMD），「除咗你，冇人嚟」就記得晒喇。

陳.en: Today we learn 陳, read "can4" in Cantonese, meaning to state or display, and also a very common surname, as in 陳先生, Mr. Chan. Look at the character: on the left is the ear-shaped piece 阝, and on the right is the character 東, so the whole thing is a left-right pair joined together. When we break it up, the left 阝 is the head, and Cangjie's rule says a head takes at most two codes, so from 阝 we take the first shape 弓 (N) and the last shape 丨 (L) and stop there; then the right side 東 is the body, from which we take the first shape 木 (D) and the last shape 田 (W), giving us NLDW. Remember it like this: left ear gives 弓丨, right body gives 木田 — say it as "Mr. Chan came home" and the pieces will stick.
陳.zh: 今日我哋學「陳」呢個字，粵音讀「can4」，可以解作陳述、陳列，亦都係好常見嘅姓氏，例如「陳先生」。你望住個字，左邊係「阝」（即係耳仔邊），右邊係「東」字，成個字係左右兩橋砌埋一齊。拆碼嘅時候，左邊嘅「阝」係字首，倉頡有規矩：字首最多取兩碼，所以我哋喺「阝」度取頭「弓」（N）同埋尾「丨」（L）就夠；跟住右邊嘅「東」係字身，我哋喺佢入面取頭「木」（D）同尾「田」（W），砌埋就係 NLDW。記住喇：左耳「弓丨」，右身「木田」，一齊讀成「陳先生」，就記得晒喇。

陸.en: Today we learn 陸, read luk6, meaning land or continent, and it can also mean the 'army' in 'land forces.' Look at the left side — that 阝 shape isn't one code in Cangjie; it splits into two pieces, 弓 (N) and 丨 (L), so the head takes those two codes, NL. Now the body on the right is built top to bottom: you take the top 土 (G), then the 八 (C) in the middle, then the bottom 土 (G) — three codes in all, because the body is allowed up to three, and here they fall neatly as head, middle, and tail. Put it together and you get NLGCG. Remember it this way: the left ear splits into 弓丨, and the right side counts 土八土 from top to bottom — 'we walk on land.'
陸.zh: 今日我哋學「陸」呢個字，讀作 luk6，意思係陸地、大陸，亦都可以解軍隊嘅「陸軍」。你睇睇佢左邊有個「阝」，呢個部件喺倉頡入面唔係一個碼，而係拆做兩橛：「弓」（N）同「丨」（L），所以字首就攞呢兩個碼 NL。跟住睇右邊嘅字身，佢由上到下砌成，先攞頭嗰個「土」（G），再攞中間嘅「八」（C），最後攞落底嘅「土」（G），字身合共三個碼；字身最多攞三碼，啱啱就係頭、中、尾各一件，所以係 G、C、G。全個字連埋就係 NLGCG。記住個口訣：左邊阝拆弓丨，右邊土八土由上數到落——「我哋喺陸地行」。

際.en: This character is 際, read zai3, meaning a border, a boundary, or the juncture where two things meet. It splits into two parts: the left side is the 字首 (lead) 阝, and the right side is the 字身 (body) 祭. The 阝 part is coded head-tail, taking the head 弓 (N) and the tail 中 (L, which is the vertical stroke 丨); the 祭 body uses head-2nd-last, taking the head ⺼ 月 (B), then 人 (O), then the final 火 (F), giving the full code NLBOF. Why does 阝 give only two codes? Because as the lead it has few strokes, and Cangjie caps a 字首 at two, so you keep just the head and tail — while the busier body 祭 gets three codes through head-2nd-last. Remember it like this: left ear 弓 guarding with 中, and on the right 月, 人, 火 cooking up 祭 — that's 際, as in 國際 (international) and 實際 (reality).
際.zh: 呢個字係「際」，讀 zai3，意思係邊界、界線，又或者係兩樣嘢交接嗰個時刻。你睇佢分兩部分：左邊嘅字首係阝，右邊嘅字身係祭。阝呢個部件喺倉頡入面拆做頭尾兩碼，取頭嘅弓（N）同尾嘅中（L，即係一條豎筆丨）；字身祭就用「頭、二、尾」嘅取碼法，攞頭嘅月（B，即⺼）、跟住嘅人（O）、同最尾嘅火（F），所以合埋成 NLBOF。點解阝淨係取兩碼？因為佢係字首、筆畫少，倉頡規定字首最多取兩碼，所以只揀頭尾；而祭係字身筆畫多，就用三碼嘅頭二尾嚟捉。記住佢：左耳仔弓、中把關，右邊月、人、火煮緊祭，就係「際」喇。你可以諗「國際」同「實際」呢兩個詞，好似「呢間國際學校好好。」咁用。

隨.en: Today we meet the character 隨, read ceoi4, which means to follow, to listen to or obey, and also carries the sense of "subsequently" or "then" — you see it in words like 隨時 (ceoi4 si4), meaning at any time or whenever you need. Look at the shape: on the left there's the little ear form 阝, and on the right sits a cluster of pieces. The head 阝 splits in Cangjie into two parts — 弓 (N) and 中 (L) — so the head gives us NL. Then the body is taken by the head-plus-last-two rule, giving 卜 (Y), 大 (K) and 月 (B), and putting it all together the full code is NLYKB. Here's your memory hook: the left ear 阝 always leads with NL, and the body follows right behind with YKB — the follower 隨 quietly stepping in line after its leader.
隨.zh: 今日我哋學「隨」呢個字，讀做 ceoi4，意思係跟隨、聽從，又可以解「隨後」、「跟住」，好似「隨時」（ceoi4 si4）咁樣，就係話幾時都得、隨時都可以。你望住呢個字，左邊有個耳仔形嘅阝，右邊係一堆有腳嘅部件。我哋先睇字首阝，佢喺倉頡入面拆做兩個部件——弓（N）加中（L），所以字首就攞 NL 兩碼。跟住輪到字身，字身就用頭同二尾嘅取碼法，攞到卜（Y）、大（K）、月（B），三碼合埋，全字就係 NLYKB。記住呢個訣竅：左耳阝永遠先出 NL，右邊個身再取頭二尾 YKB，就好似「跟住」個個影，一步步跟落嚟咁。

隻.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「隻」字，讀做 zek3，佢係量詞，你講「一隻手」、「呢隻貓」嗰陣就用到佢。你望住個字，上面係「隹」，下面係「又」，倉頡就係跟住呢個上下嘅結構去拆。上面嘅「隹」係字首，字首最多取兩碼，所以我哋喺佢入面取頭嘅「亻」（O）同埋「土」（G），淨低嘅唔再取；下面嘅「又」係字身，字身取尾一碼，就係「又」自己嘅 E，所以成個碼砌埋就係 OGE。你記住個口訣：一個「亻」、一撇「土」、再加一個「又」，OGE，就係一隻一隻咁數嘅「隻」喇。

集.en: Today's character is 集, read zaap6, meaning to assemble or collect things together, as in 收集 sau1 zaap6 (to gather) and 聚集 zeoi6 zaap6 (to assemble). Look at its shape: on top sits 隹 and underneath is 木 — a bird resting on a tree, and when many birds gather you get the idea of collecting. The Cangjie code is OGD: the top part 隹 has too many strokes to take whole, so we take its head and tail, giving 人 O as the head and 土 G as the tail, and then the bottom 木 D becomes the final code. Remember it like this: a bird made of 人 O and 土 G perches on a 木 D — that builds 集, OGD.
集.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「集」，讀做 zaap6，意思係聚埋一齊、收集，例如「收集」sau1 zaap6 同「聚集」zeoi6 zaap6。你睇下佢嘅樣：上面係「隹」，下面係「木」，一隻雀停喺樹上面，好多雀停埋一齊就係聚集嘅意思。倉頡編碼係 OGD，上面嘅「隹」筆畫太多，唔可以全部取出嚟，所以要取頭尾——頭係「人」O，尾係「土」G，下面嘅「木」D 就作為最後嘅尾碼。記住個口訣：一隻雀（人 O、土 G）停喺木（D）上面，就砌成咗「集」OGD。

雜.en: Today we learn 雜, read zaap6, the word for things mixed or blended together — as in 複雜 (complicated) or 牛雜 (stewed mixed beef offal). Look at the character and you'll see it splits left and right: the left side 杂 is the head, and the right side 隹 is the body. Cangjie takes the head 杂 by its first and last shapes — the little dot on top is 卜 on the Y key, and the 木 below it is the D key, giving YD. Then the body 隹 follows the usual head-and-tail rule for a body: its head is 人, the O key, and its tail is 土, the G key, so the whole code comes together as YDOG. To remember it, picture the dot-and-wood on the left holding up a busy little bird on the right, all crowded together — that jumble is exactly the 'mixed' feeling of 雜.
雜.zh: 今日我哋學「雜」字，讀作 zaap6，即係「混雜」、「複雜」嗰個意思，講嘅係好多嘢溝埋一齊。你望住個字，會發現佢分做左右兩邊：左邊係字首「杂」，右邊係字身「隹」。倉頡幫字首「杂」拆出頭尾兩個碼——上面嗰一點係「卜」，個 Y 鍵，下面個「木」就係 D 鍵，所以字首取 YD。到咗右邊字身「隹」，就照字身取頭尾嘅規矩嚟做：頭係「人」，個 O 鍵，尾係「土」，個 G 鍵，於是砌埋成 YDOG。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗住左邊嘅一點加木撐住，右邊嘅隹鳥由人到土，好似好多嘢雜亂咁夾埋一齊——正好就係「複雜」同「牛雜」嗰種溝雜嘅感覺喇。

雞.en: This character is 雞, read gai1, the everyday word for chickens or domestic fowl. Notice it divides into a left part and a right part: 奚 on the left is the 字首, and 隹 on the right is the 字身. In Cangjie a compound like this normally takes head and tail from each side, so from 奚 you take its head 爫 on the B key and its tail 大 on the K key, then from 隹 you take its head 人 on the O key and its tail 土 on the G key, giving you BKOG. To remember it, picture a chicken (爫, those claws) as big (大) as a person (人) standing on the ground (土) — B, K, O, G in a row.
雞.zh: 呢個字係「雞」，讀 gai1，即係我哋日日見到嘅雞、家禽。你睇下佢分做左右兩橛：左邊嘅「奚」係字首，右邊嘅「隹」係字身。倉頡有個規矩，複合字嘅字首通常取頭尾兩碼，所以「奚」我哋取佢個頭「爫」，係 B 鍵，再取個尾「大」，係 K 鍵；字身「隹」同樣取頭尾，個頭係「人」，係 O 鍵，個尾係「土」，係 G 鍵，砌埋一齊就係 BKOG。記住嘅時候可以諗成：一隻雞（爫爪）大到（大）一個人（人）企喺塊地（土）上面，B、K、O、G 順住嚟。

離.en: Today we learn 離, read "lei4", meaning to leave, depart, or separate — it's the word you use when you check out of a hotel (離開), and it also lives inside 距離, distance. Look at the whole character: the left side is 离 and the right side is 隹, and Cangjie splits it exactly there, into a head and a body. The head 离 is a busy shape, so we take just its first and last pieces — 卜 (Y) at the top and 月 (B) at the bottom; the body 隹 also gives its first and last, 人 (O) and 土 (G). String them together in reading order and you get 卜月人土, which is YBOG. Hold onto the sentence 我唔想離開你 — "I don't want to leave you" — and remember the head gives you 卜月 and the body gives you 人土, four keys straight down.
離.zh: 今日我哋學「離」呢個字，讀「lei4」，係離開、分開嘅意思，你去酒店退房都叫「離開」（check out），仲有「距離」都用佢。你望吓成個字，左邊係「离」，右邊係「隹」，倉頡就係咁分做字首同字身兩橛。字首「离」筆畫多，倉頡拆碼取頭尾兩碼，頭係「卜」（Y），尾係「月」（B）；字身「隹」都係取頭尾，頭係「人」（O），尾係「土」（G）。所以成個碼順住打落去就係卜月人土，即係 YBOG。記住呢句：「我唔想離開你」，一講到離開就記得個字首係卜月、字身係人土，四粒鍵順住打就得。

難.en: Today we learn 難, read naan4, meaning difficult, arduous, hard — something that takes real effort and doesn't come easily. Look at it: the left part is the head 𦰩 and the right part is the body 隹, and we break each one down on its own. In Cangjie both head and body take their first-and-last shapes, so from the head 𦰩 we keep the first piece 廿 on the T key and the last piece 人 on the O key, and from the body 隹 we keep the first piece 人 on the O key and the last piece 土 on the G key, giving TOOG. Notice the two O keys in a row — that happens because the tail of the head and the head of the body both happen to be 人, so just type both. Picture 呢題好難做, this question is hard to do: with two 人 squeezed in the middle, 難 (T, O, O, G) really is a tough one!
難.zh: 今日我哋學「難」呢個字，讀音係 naan4，意思就係「困難、艱難」，做起上嚟好辛苦、好唔容易嘅意思。你睇下佢，左邊嘅字首係「𦰩」，右邊嘅字身係「隹」，兩邊各自要拆碼。倉頡拆字，字首同字身都係取「頭同尾」，所以字首「𦰩」我哋只取頭嘅「廿」，鍵位係 T，同尾嘅「人」，鍵位係 O，字身「隹」就取頭嘅「人」，鍵位又係 O，同尾嘅「土」，鍵位係 G，合埋一齊就係 TOOG。你會發現連續打咗兩個 O，正正就係字首個尾同字身個頭啱啱都係「人」，唔使驚，照打就啱。記住呢句「呢題好難做」，難字四碼 T、O、O、G，兩個人夾喺中間，就好似做嘢做到夾硬咁難！

雲.en: Today's character is 雲, read wan4 — it means clouds, and it can also name Yunnan province. Look at its build: the top is the 雨 (rain) radical, and the bottom is 云, stacked one above the other. For the top head 雨, we take first and last only — the head 一 (M) and the last piece 月 (B) — giving MB. For the bottom body 云, we take head, second, and last — head 一 (M), second 一 (M), and last 戈 (I) — giving MMI; put together, the whole code is MBMMI. Here's your memory hook: 雨 (rain, MB) falls from the sky and becomes 云 (MMI) — rain over cloud makes 雲.
雲.zh: 今日學嘅字係「雲」，讀 wan4，就係天上飄嘅雲，亦都可以指雲南省。你睇下佢嘅結構：上面係個「雨」字頭，下面係個「云」，兩部分上下疊住。上面嘅字首「雨」，我哋用頭尾兩碼——先取頭「一」（M），再取尾「月」（B），所以字首係 MB。下面嘅字身「云」，就取頭、次、尾三碼——頭「一」（M）、次「一」（M）、尾「戈」（I），砌成 MMI；合埋就係 MBMMI。記住個小竅妙：天上落「雨」（MB），落完就變一片「云」（MMI），雨同云疊埋就係「雲」。

電.en: Today we learn 電, read "din6", meaning electricity or lightning. Notice it stacks into two parts: on top sits the rain radical 雨, and beneath it is 电. Because the character splits into a top and a bottom, Cangjie treats it as 字首 (head part) and 字身 (body part), each getting two codes: the 字首 雨 gives its head, the flat stroke 一 which is M, and its tail ⺼ which is B; the 字身 电 gives its head 田 which is W and its tail 山 which is U, so the full code is MBWU. The reason each part gives only two codes is that when a character clearly divides into upper and lower halves, Cangjie shares the code slots between them rather than piling them all onto the top. Picture it like this: rain falls from the sky (M, B), then lightning follows (W, U) — rain then electricity gives you 電. Try it in 電腦 (computer) and 電影 (movie).
電.zh: 我哋今日學「電」呢個字，讀「din6」，就係電力、閃電嘅意思。你留意佢上下兩截：上面係個「雨」字頭，下面係個「电」，合埋一齊就成個「電」。倉頡拆佢嘅時候，因為佢係上下結構，所以分做字首同字身兩部分：字首「雨」取頭尾兩碼，起筆嗰橫「一」係M，收筆嗰個「⺼」係B；字身「电」同樣取頭尾兩碼，頭係「田」W，尾係「山」U，合埋就係 MBWU。點解字首字身各取兩碼？因為當一個字明顯分成上下兩橛時，倉頡就每橛各分一半嘅碼位，唔會全部塞晒喺上面。記住呢個畫面：天上落雨（M、B），閃電（W、U）跟住落嚟，一雨一電，就係「電」喇。你可以用嚟砌「電腦」同「電影」。

需.en: Today we learn 需, read seoi1, meaning to need, to require, or must — as in 需要 (seoi1 jiu3), "to need." The character stacks into two parts. On top sits the "rain" radical 雨, which we don't spell stroke by stroke; instead we take just its head and tail, so the top horizontal 一 is M and the inner shape ⺜ is B, giving MB for the head. The body underneath is 而, and because a Cangjie body takes at most three codes, we grab head, middle, and tail: the opening 一 is M, the ⺆ shape is B, and the final vertical 丨 is L, making MBL. Put it together and the whole thing is MBMBL — think of it as rain on top and a need down below, and remember: when you need something in the rain, you type MB then MBL.
需.zh: 今日我哋學「需」呢個字，讀做 seoi1，意思係需要、必須，好似「需要」（seoi1 jiu3）咁樣。呢個字上下兩截：上面係個「雨」字頭，我哋唔會逐筆咁拆，係取頭尾兩碼——最頂嗰橫「一」係 M，跟住個雨字內部嘅形取 ⺜ 係 B，所以字首「雨」就係 MB。落到下面嘅字身「而」，倉頡有個規矩，字身最多取三碼，於是取頭、二、尾：開頭一橫「一」係 M，中間個 ⺆ 係 B，最後嗰豎「丨」係 L，合埋 MBL。成個字連埋就係 MBMBL。記住個口訣：頭上落雨（MB），身要記住（MBL），落雨要帶遮，帶遮就係需要！

露.en: Today's character 露 reads lou6, and it means dew, or by extension "to expose, to reveal"; you see it in 露天 (lou6 tin1), meaning outdoors or in the open, and in 透露 (tau3 lou6), meaning to leak or divulge something. The character stacks in two halves: the top is 雨 (rain) serving as the 字首, and the bottom is the whole character 路 (road) serving as the 字身. The 字首 雨 follows the head-tail rule, so you take its head 一 (M) and its tail 月 (B), giving MB; the 字身 路 is a complete standalone character, so it takes three codes — head 口 (R), second 一 (M), and tail 口 (R) — giving RMR. Put them together and you get MBRMR. Picture it this way: rain (雨) falling from the sky onto the road (路) below leaves dew — in the morning there is dew on the grass.
露.zh: 今日學嘅「露」讀 lou6，意思係露水，又可以解「露出、暴露」，例如「露天」（lou6 tin1）就係喺戶外冇遮冚嘅意思，「透露」（tau3 lou6）就係漏咗出嚟、講咗出嚟。呢個字上下兩截，上面係「雨」字頭做字首，下面係「路」字做字身。字首「雨」照倉頡取頭尾嘅規矩，拆頭「一」（M）同尾「月」（B），所以字首係 MB；字身「路」係一個獨立完整嘅字，就拆頭、二、尾三碼——頭「口」（R）、次「一」（M）、尾「口」（R），即係 RMR。合埋一齊就係 MBRMR。記住個畫面：天上「雨」水滴落嚟，沾濕咗腳下嘅「路」，就係「露」啦——朝早草上有露水。

青.en: Today we learn 青, read cing1 (sometimes ceng1), meaning blue or green, and also "young." Look at the shape: the top piece looks like 手 (hand), there's a single horizontal stroke 一 in the middle, and a ⺼ sits at the bottom, and together they make 青. In Cangjie this is a whole-character (整體字) — it can't be cleanly split into a head part and a body part, so instead of forcing a split we follow the take-head, take-second, take-tail rule: the head 手 gives Q, the middle stroke 一 gives M, and the tail ⺼ gives B, so the full code is QMB. Just read it top to bottom — 手, 一, ⺼, that is Q, M, B — and 青 falls right into place.
青.zh: 我哋今日學「青」呢個字，佢讀 cing1，有時又讀 ceng1，解藍色、綠色，又可以解年輕嘅「青」。你望住個字：上面好似「手」嘅樣，中間一橫，下底有個「⺼」，砌埋一齊就係「青」。喺倉頡入面，呢個字係「整體字」，一個字唔可以清清楚楚咁劈開做字首同字身，所以我哋唔硬拆，而係跟住取碼規矩「取頭、取二、取尾」：頭部係「手」，撳 Q；第二部分係中間嗰一橫「一」，撳 M；最尾嗰個「⺼」，撳 B，合埋就係 QMB。記住呢個順序：由手 Q 開始，落到一 M，最後埋尾 B，「手、一、⺼」由上到下讀落嚟，「青」就砌好喇。

非.en: Today's character is 非, read fei1, meaning "not" or "non-" — a negative that also carries the sense of opposing, as in 非常 (fei1 soeng4, meaning very or extraordinary) and 非洲 (fei1 zau1, Africa). Look at the shape: a tall vertical line runs down the middle, and on each side three short horizontal strokes reach outward, making the whole thing symmetrical, like two rows lined up. This is a whole character with no clear head-and-body division, so we follow Cangjie's ordering rule, taking pieces left to right and top to bottom: first the left vertical, coded as 中 (L) then 一 (M), and then the three strokes on the right, each read as 卜 (Y), giving three Y's in a row for the full code LMYYY. Here's your hook: one central pole standing in the middle, then three little 卜 on the right — that's 非.
非.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「非」，讀音係 fei1，意思係「唔係」、「不」，帶有否定同埋反對嘅意味，好似「非常」（fei1 soeng4，即係好、極之）同埋「非洲」（fei1 zau1）。你望住個字，會見到中間有一條長長嘅直線貫穿上下，兩邊各有三橫伸出去，成個字左右對稱，好似兩排嘢排開咁。呢個字係一個整體字，冇分明顯嘅字首同字身，所以我哋要跟返倉頡嘅取碼規矩，由左至右、由上至下咁攞：先攞左邊嗰豎，取「中」（L）同「一」（M），再攞右邊嗰三橫，每一橫都當「卜」（Y），所以連續打三個 Y，合埋成 LMYYY。記住個口訣：一條中軸企喺中間，右邊三下「卜卜卜」，就係「非」喇。

面.en: This character is 面, read min6, the very word for the face on your head — and it also stretches to mean a surface, a plane, or one side of something. Look at its shape: an outer frame wraps around a busy middle, and the whole thing hangs together as one inseparable block, which is why we treat it as a 整體字, a whole character. For a whole character we ignore the usual head-and-body quotas and instead take the head, the second piece, the third piece, and the tail — exactly four codes drawn straight from the character. So as you write it out you press 一 M, then 囗 W, then 卜 Y, then 中 L, giving MWYL. Remember it this way: one framed face, four spots — head, second, third, tail — 一囗卜中, and there's your face.
面.zh: 呢個字係「面」，讀 min6，即係你塊面嗰個「面」，亦都可以指表面、平面、或者一件嘢嘅其中一邊。你睇下佢個樣：外面好似一個框咁包住，入面塞滿咗筆畫，成個字連埋一齊、拆唔開，所以佢屬於「整體字」。碰到整體字，我哋唔理字首字身嘅配額，直接用「取頭二三尾」嘅辦法：由開頭數起，攞第一、第二、第三個部件，再加最尾嗰個，剛好四碼。所以喺鍵盤上，你順住寫落去撳「一」M、「囗」W、「卜」Y、「中」L，砌成 MWYL。記住喇：一個框住嘅面，頭二三尾四個位，一囗卜中就係你塊面。

韓.en: Today we learn 韓, read hon4, which means a fence or an enclosure, is also a surname, and above all is the 韓 in 韓國, Korea. Look at the character: the left side is a head-piece called 𠦝, and the right side is a body called 韋, so we split it into head and body and read each side in turn. The head 𠦝 takes first-and-last, and since both its ends are the shape 十 (J), you type J twice; the body 韋 takes head-second-tail, which gives 木 (D), then 一 (M), then 手 (Q), so the whole code is JJDMQ. The reason the head gets two codes while the body gets three is the Cangjie quota rule: when a character divides into a head-piece and a body, the head may take at most two parts and the body at most three, which is exactly why 𠦝 gives JJ and 韋 gives DMQ. Memory hook: two crossed 十 posts hold up the fence, and 木-一-手 finish it off — that's the 韓 of Korea.
韓.zh: 今日我哋學「韓」呢個字，讀音係 hon4，可以解作籬笆、圍欄，亦都係一個姓氏，更加係我哋成日講嘅「韓國」嘅韓。你睇下呢個字，左邊係一組叫「𠦝」嘅字首，右邊係一個叫「韋」嘅字身，所以要分頭同身兩邊嚟拆。字首「𠦝」取頭尾兩碼，頭係「十」（J），尾都係「十」（J），所以連續打兩個 J；字身「韋」就取頭、二、尾三碼，頭係「木」（D），第二係「一」（M），尾係「手」（Q），合埋成 JJDMQ。之所以字首得兩碼、字身得三碼，係因為倉頡拆字有分工，一個字分開字首字身嗰陣，字首最多攞兩碼，字身最多攞三碼，正正符合「𠦝」取 JJ、「韋」取 DMQ。記住口訣：兩個十字撐起門欄，木一手接住，就係「韓國」嘅韓。

音.en: Today we're learning 音, read jam1, meaning sound, tone or pronunciation — you'll meet it in words like 聲音 sing1 jam1 for sound or voice, and 音樂 jam1 ngok6 for music. Look at the character: the top is 立 and the bottom is 日, so Cangjie splits it cleanly into two — the top becomes the 字首 and the bottom becomes the 字身. For the top 立 we don't spell out every stroke; instead we take the head and tail, so the opening dot 卜 gives Y and the horizontal 廿 gives T. Then the whole 日 underneath serves as the 字身 and gives A, so putting it together we type Y, T, A — YTA. Here's your hook: stand up (立) and make a sound, top head-and-tail Y T over the sun 日 A, and you've built 音.
音.zh: 今日我哋學「音」呢個字，讀做 jam1，即係聲音、音調嘅意思，好似「聲音」sing1 jam1 或者「音樂」jam1 ngok6 都用到佢。你望住個字，上面係「立」，下面係「日」，倉頡就係咁樣一分為二：上面做字首，下面做字身。字首「立」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，而係取頭尾兩碼——起筆嗰點「卜」係 Y，中間嗰橫「廿」係 T；跟住下面成個「日」做字身，取 A。所以砌埋一齊就係 Y、T、A，即係 YTA。記住喇：立正嗰刻先出聲——上面立字頭尾 Y T，下面日 A，咁就砌到個「音」啦。

響.en: Today we learn 響, read hoeng2, meaning to make a sound or to sound off — think of the sentence 個電話響咗, meaning the phone rang. Look at the character and you'll see it's built from two stacked halves: the top is 鄉 and the bottom is 音. In Cangjie the top 鄉 is treated as the head, so it only gives its first and last pieces — 女 (V) and 丨 (L); then the bottom 音 becomes the body, and since a body may take up to three codes, we take head-second-tail, which are 卜 (Y), 廿 (T), and 日 (A). Put it all together and you get VLYTA — just remember 'top gives two, bottom gives three' and you'll never drop a code.
響.zh: 今日我哋學「響」呢個字，讀音係 hoeng2，意思係發出聲音、作響，好似「個電話響咗」咁樣。你望下呢個字，其實係上下兩橛砌埋一齊：上面係「鄉」，下面係「音」。倉頡拆呢個字嘅時候，將上面嘅「鄉」當字首，只取頭尾兩個碼——「女」（V）同「丨」（L）；跟住落到下面嘅「音」做字身，因為字身可以取到三個碼，就取頭、二、尾，即係「卜」（Y）、「廿」（T）同「日」（A）。所以成個碼砌返出嚟就係 VLYTA，記住「上鄉取兩、下音取三」，你就唔會漏碼喇。

項.en: Today's character is 項, read hong6. It originally means the nape or back of the neck, and later grew to mean an item or a sum, as in 項目 (an item or project) and 款項 (funds). Look at it: the left side is 工 and the right side is 頁, and Cangjie splits it along this natural left-right divide. The 工 on the left is the head, and Cangjie takes its first and last codes — both are the horizontal stroke 一, keyed as M — so you type M twice. The 頁 on the right is the body, and a body can give up to three codes taken head-to-tail: the top stroke 一 (M), then 月 (B) and 金 (C) closing it off, so 頁 contributes M, B, and C. Put it all together and you get MMBC. Remember it as two flat strokes MM to open from 工, then BC as the tail of 頁 — as in 呢項工作好重要, counting the tasks one 項 at a time.
項.zh: 我哋今日學嘅字係「項」，讀做 hong6，本來解頸後面嗰個位，即係頸項，後來又引申做「一項」嘅意思，好似項目、款項噉。你望下佢，左邊係「工」，右邊係「頁」，倉頡就係跟住呢個左右結構嚟拆。左邊嘅「工」做字首，倉頡取頭同尾兩個碼，即係頭嗰橫同尾嗰橫，兩個都係「一」，鍵位係 M，所以連續打兩個 M。右邊嘅「頁」做字身，字身最多取三個碼，用頭尾法：頭係上面嗰橫做「一」M，尾就取「月」B 同「金」C 收尾，所以「頁」呢部分貢獻咗 M、B、C。合埋一齊就係 MMBC。記住嘅方法係：工字兩橫 MM 開頭，頁字尾巴 BC 收，「呢項工作好重要」，一項一項噉數落去。

順.en: Today we learn 順, read seon6, meaning to obey or go along with, as in 順利 — things flowing smoothly without a hitch. Look at it: 川 sits on the left and 頁 on the right, two parts joined together. The left part 川 is the 字首, and Cangjie takes its head and tail, both of which are the vertical stroke 丨 — and that shape 丨 lives on the L key, so you press L twice; the right part 頁 is the 字身, and again we take head and tail, the head being another vertical 丨 (one more L) and the tail being 金, which sits on the C key. Put the four together and you get LLLC. Remember it as a stream of three L's flowing in a line, sealed off at the end by a single C — smooth all the way down.
順.zh: 今日我哋學「順」呢個字，讀 seon6，意思係順從、跟隨，好似「順利」咁，事情一路暢通冇阻礙。你望吓佢，左邊係「川」，右邊係「頁」，兩件砌埋一齊。左邊「川」做字首，倉頡取頭尾兩筆，都係一豎「丨」，而「丨」呢個形喺 L 鍵，所以連續打兩個 L；右邊「頁」做字身，同樣取頭尾，頭係一豎「丨」，即係再多一個 L，尾就係「金」形，喺 C 鍵。四件砌埋就係 LLLC。記住呢個字尾巴一個 C 收住，前面三個 L 排隊，好似流水順住條路咁順利流落去。

須.en: Today we learn 須, read seoi1, meaning "must, need to, have to" — you'll see it in 必須 (bit1 seoi1), "to have to," and 無須 (mou4 seoi1), "need not." Look at the whole character: on the left are the three slanting strokes of 彡, and on the right sits 頁. Cangjie splits it into a head and a body: the head is 彡, and because a head takes at most two codes — its first and last piece — we grab only the top 丿 (H) and the bottom 丿 (H), skipping the middle stroke. The body is 頁, which is allowed up to three codes, so we take its parts in writing order: the 一 on top (M), then the ⺼ (B), then the 金 at the bottom (C), giving HHMBC. Remember it this way: two slashes from 彡, then 一, moon-flesh, and gold from 頁 — H-H-M-B-C.
須.zh: 今日我哋學「須」字，讀作 seoi1，解「必須、需要、一定要」嘅意思，好似「必須」（bit1 seoi1）就係「一定要」，「無須」（mou4 seoi1）就係「唔使、唔一定」。你望吓成個字，左邊係三撇嘅「彡」，右邊係個「頁」字。倉頡拆法要分字首同字身：字首係「彡」，佢有幾撇，但字首最多只取頭同尾兩碼，所以我哋淨係攞頭一撇丿（H）同尾一撇丿（H），中間嗰撇就唔理啦。跟住字身係「頁」，可以取到三碼，就順住寫落去攞頭嘅一（M）、然後中間個⺼（B），最後個金（C），砌埋成 HHMBC。記住一個口訣：「彡取兩撇，頁取一⺼金」，你就唔會拆錯喇。

預.en: Today we learn 預, read "jyu6", the same 預 in words like "prepare" and "in advance" — it means to arrange something ahead of time. Look at it: on the left sits 予, and on the right stands the big 頁, and the two parts join together. The head part 予 gives up only its first and last codes, so we take 弓N and 乙N — that's why the head is 弓N 乙N. The body 頁 then gets three codes, first-middle-last: 一M, ⺼B, and 金C, giving 一M ⺼B 金C. A head only ever spares first-and-last while a body may take up to three, so the whole character lines up as 弓N 乙N 一M ⺼B 金C — NNMBC. Memory hook: two bows-and-hooks "give" you a page, prepared in advance for whatever comes.
預.zh: 今日我哋學「預」呢個字，讀「jyu6」，同「預備」、「預先」嗰個預一樣，意思係事先安排好、預備定。你望吓佢，左邊係「予」，右邊係大大隻嘅「頁」，兩部分砌埋一齊。左邊嘅字首「予」我哋淨係要頭尾兩碼，頭係弓N、尾係乙N，所以字首就係弓N乙N；右邊嘅字身「頁」就取頭、中、尾三碼，頭係一M、中間係月B、尾係金C，合埋就係一M月B金C。字首慳住只取頭尾，字身可以取到三碼，所以成個字砌起嚟就係弓N乙N一M月B金C，即係 NNMBC。記住喇：兩個弓乙開頭「予」你，一頁書就係為咗「預」備你未來嘅事。

領.en: This character is 領, read ling5, and it means the neck or the collar of a garment, and by extension to lead or to guide — a 領袖 is the person out in front. Look at it: the left side is 令 and the right side is 頁, and we split it into a head part and a body part. The head 令 is a compound face, so we take its first and last pieces, 人 which is O and 戈 which is I; the body 頁 follows the first-second-last rule, taking its top two pieces first — the 一 which is M and the 月 which is B — then its very last piece, the 金 which is C, so the whole code reads OIMBC. Remember it this way: 令 (人, 戈) leads the way and 頁 (一, 月, 金) brings up the rear — one heads the line, one holds the tail.
領.zh: 呢個字係「領」，讀 ling5，講嘅係頸、衣領，又可以解帶領、引導，好似「領袖」就係帶頭嗰個人。你望吓佢，左邊係「令」，右邊係「頁」，我哋要分做字首同字身兩橛嚟拆。字首「令」係複體字，取頭尾兩碼，頭係「人」O，尾係「戈」I；字身「頁」就跟頭二尾一嘅規矩，先攞頭兩件——最上嘅「一」M、跟住嘅「月」B，再攞最尾嘅「金」C，所以成個碼砌埋就係 OIMBC。記住喇：先寫「令」（人戈）帶頭，再落「頁」（一月金）殿後，一個帶隊、一個押尾，好易記。

頭.en: Today we learn 頭, read tau4, meaning head or top, and also chief, first, or boss. Look at it: it splits left and right, with 豆 on the left and 頁 on the right. When we take the code, the head part 豆 isn't spelled out fully — as a 字首 it gives just its first and last pieces, 一 (M) and 廿 (T); then the body 頁, being a complex shape, is allowed three codes, so we take its head, second, and last pieces, 一 (M), ⺼ (B), and 八 (C). Together that makes MTMBC, five keys in all. Here's your hook: 豆 opens with M and T, 頁 finishes with M, B, C — and your head is complete.
頭.zh: 今日我哋學「頭」呢個字，讀作 tau4，意思係頭、頂端，又可以指首領、老闆。你望下佢，係一個左右結構嘅字：左邊係「豆」，右邊係「頁」。拆碼嘅時候，字首嘅「豆」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，只係取頭尾兩個部件，就係「一」M 同「廿」T；跟住字身嘅「頁」係一個複雜部件，字身可以攞到三碼，所以取頭、二、尾三部分，就係「一」M、「⺼」B、「八」C。合埋一齊就係 MTMBC 五碼。記住呢個口訣：豆頭有廿，頁腳分肉八，頭嘅碼就砌得出嚟喇。

題.en: Today we learn 題, read tai4. It originally meant forehead, but nowadays it usually means a title, headline, or theme — you meet it in words like 問題 man6 tai4, a question or problem, and 主題 zyu2 tai4, a theme. Look at its shape: on the left is 是, and on the right is 頁, and we split it right down that seam. The 是 on the left is the head, and a head like this gives only its first and last parts — first is 日 A, last is 人 O, so the head is AO.
