The 頁 on the right is the body, and a body gives head, second, and tail — head 一 M, second 月 B, tail 金 C, giving MBC. Put them together and you get AOMBC, two codes for the head plus three for the body, exactly five. Remember it as 日人 (AO) then 一月金 (MBC) — 呢條數學題好難, this maths problem is hard.
題.zh: 今日我哋學「題」呢個字，讀音係 tai4，本來解額頭，而家最常見嘅意思係題目、標題、主題，好似「問題」man6 tai4 同「主題」zyu2 tai4 咁樣。你望下佢個結構，左邊係「是」字，右邊係「頁」字，兩件分開拆。左邊「是」係字首，我哋淨取頭尾兩碼——頭係「日」A，尾係「人」O，所以字首得 AO；右邊「頁」係字身，取頭、次、尾三碼，頭係「一」M，次係「月」B，尾係「金」C，砌埋就係 MBC。合起來全個字就係 AOMBC，字首兩碼加字身三碼，啱啱好五碼。記住個口訣：日人（AO）一月金（MBC），「呢條數學題好難」，慢慢就會記得住喇。

類.en: Today we learn 類, read leoi6, meaning a class, kind or category — you see it in 人類 jan4 leoi6, mankind, and 類似 leoi6 ci5, similar. This character splits left and right: the left part 米 plus 大 is the head unit, and from a head unit we take only its first and last codes — 米 opens with 小 F, then comes 大 K. The right part 頁 is the body, and from a body we take head, second and tail — the head is 一 M, the second piece is ⺼ B, and the tail is 金 C, giving you FKMBC in all. The reason the head gets just two codes while the body gets three is Cangjie's rule for a two-part character: the head is capped at two, the body at three, so FK on the left and MBC on the right fit perfectly. Remember the line 呢類書好好睇 — sorting books into kinds is exactly what 類 is about.
類.zh: 今日我哋學「類」呢個字，讀作 leoi6，意思係種類、類別，好似「人類」jan4 leoi6 或者「類似」leoi6 ci5 咁樣。呢個字左右兩邊分開，左邊係「米」加「大」，屬於字首，我哋淨係取頭尾兩個碼——「米」個頭係「小」F，接住係「大」K；右邊個「頁」係字身，取頭、二、尾三個碼，頭係「一」M，第二個係「⺼」B，最尾係「金」C，合埋就係 FKMBC。點解字首得兩碼、字身得三碼呢？因為倉頡個規矩就係一個字分開兩橛嗰陣，字首最多取兩碼，字身最多取三碼，所以左邊 FK、右邊 MBC 啱啱好。記住一句：「呢類書好好睇」，睇書分門別類，就係「類」喇。

風.en: Today we learn 風, read fung1, the wind that blows — and by extension it also means atmosphere or style. Look at the character: there's a frame wrapping the outside, and hiding inside is a 虫 (insect) — hold that picture in mind. This is a whole character (整體字) that we don't cleanly break into two halves, so we use the head-second-tail method: first the outer frame gives us ⺆=H and 弓=N, and then we go inside to the 虫 and take its head, second, and tail — ⺆=H, 中=L, 戈=I — giving the full code HNHLI. Notice ⺆ shows up twice here, once as the big outer frame and once as the little frame inside the 虫, so you press H both times. Memory hook: a big wind blows in, a little bug shelters inside the frame — the risk (風險, fung1 him2) is high, but you must still have style (風格, fung1 gaak3)!
風.zh: 今日我哋學「風」，讀 fung1，就係吹嘅風，亦都指風氣、氣派嘅意思。你望住個字，外面有個框圍住，入面藏住一隻「虫」——記住呢個組合。呢個字係整體字，唔可以隨便斬做兩截，所以要用「頭二三尾」嘅取碼辦法：外框先取撇頭，就係⺆=H同埋弓=N；跟住入到裏面嘅虫，再取佢嘅頭、二、尾——⺆=H、中=L、戈=I，合埋一齊就係 HNHLI。你會見到⺆呢個框出現咗兩次，一次係大框，一次係虫入面嗰個細框，兩次都撳 H。記憶鉤：一陣大風吹入嚟，框裏面藏住一條蟲仔，風險（fung1 him2）好大，但風格（fung1 gaak3）都要有！

食.en: Today we learn 食, read "sik6", meaning to eat, a meal, or food — a word right at the heart of your daily life. Take a look at its shape: there's a 人 sitting on top like a little roof, with a cluster of strokes packed underneath. Because 食 is a whole character (整體字), Cangjie doesn't chop up every piece; instead it grabs four positions — head, second, third, tail — which are 人 on key O, 戈 on key I, 日 on key A, and 女 on key V, giving the full code OIAV, while the middle strokes are simply skipped. Hold onto the words 食咗 (sik6 zo2, to have eaten) and 食物 (sik6 mat6, food) and this character will feel familiar fast. Memory hook: a 人 wearing a little hat, eating all the way down to the 女 at the bottom — 人戈日女, OIAV.
食.zh: 今日我哋學「食」呢個字，讀「sik6」，就係食嘢、食飯、食物嘅意思，好貼近你日常生活。你望吓佢個樣，上面有個「人」字撐住成頂帽咁，下面砌埋一堆嘢，睇落有啲複雜。因為「食」係一個整體字，倉頡唔會逐格拆晒，而係用「頭、二、三、尾」四個位嚟取碼——最頂係「人」，撳 O；跟住上邊一點嘅「戈」，撳 I；再落嚟中間係「日」，撳 A；最後底部個「女」，撳 V，所以完整碼係 OIAV，中間嗰啲筆畫就跳過唔理。你記住「食咗」（sik6 zo2，即係食完）同埋「食物」（sik6 mat6）呢兩個詞，就好易上手。記憶鉤：一個「人」戴住帽仔，一路食到落個「女」度，人戈日女，OIAV。

飯.en: Look at this character: 飯, read faan6, meaning cooked rice, a meal, or food in general — a word you meet every single day. It splits into two sides: the left is the food radical 食, and the right is 反. When Cangjie handles the left 食 as the head, it takes the first and last pieces — the first is 人 (O) and the last is 戈 (I); the right side 反, taken as the body, also gives first and last — the first is 竹 (H) and the last is 水 (E), so the whole thing builds into OIHE. Why first-and-last on each side? Because 飯 is a left-right compound, and the head and body each surrender two codes, their opening and closing pieces, filling out exactly four. Remember it this way: 人戈 for the food side, 竹水 for the 反 side — a person holding a spear while water pours down, the picture of a hearty meal.
飯.zh: 睇下呢個字：飯，讀faan6，即係煮熟嘅飯、餐飯、食物嘅意思，係我哋日日都見到嘅字。呢個字分做兩邊：左邊係食字旁（飠），右邊係反。倉頡處理左邊嘅食嗰陣，做字首，取頭尾兩個部件——頭係人（O），尾係戈（I）；右邊嘅反做字身，都係取頭尾——頭係竹（H），尾係水（E），所以成個字砌埋就係OIHE。點解要咁樣頭尾各取？因為飯係一個左右合體嘅字，字首同字身各自攞頭同尾兩碼，湊夠四碼就啱晒。記住喇：食飯（人戈）、反手（竹水），人戈竹水，即係話搵嘢食嘅時候，人揸住戈、水灑落嚟，就係食飯嘅畫面。

飲.en: Today we meet 飲, read jam2 — the drink of 飲水 and 飲品, meaning to swallow a beverage down. Look at it: on the left is the food radical 飠, and on the right is 欠, one giving the food meaning and the other hinting at the sound. When we break it into code, the head is the left-side 飠, which is a busy shape, and since Cangjie takes at most two codes from a head, we take only its first two pieces — 人 (O) and 戈 (I). Then the body is the right-side 欠, and for a body we use the first-last method, taking the opening 弓 (N) and the closing 人 (O), giving us OINO in full. Remember it this way: the left 飠 gives only its first two strokes OI, while the right 欠 gives one head and one tail NO — a person (O) at the start and a person (O) at the end, framing your drink.
飲.zh: 今日我哋學「飲」呢個字，讀作 jam2，即係「飲嘢」、「飲水」嘅飲，意思係將飲料吞落肚。你望吓佢，左邊係食字旁「飠」，右邊係「欠」，一個表示同飲食有關，一個帶出讀音。拆碼嘅時候，字首係左邊嘅「飠」，佢好複雜，倉頡最多喺字首取兩碼，所以我哋淨係取佢頭兩個部件——人（O）同戈（I）；跟住字身係右邊嘅「欠」，字身用首尾取碼嘅方法，取頭嘅弓（N）同尾嘅人（O），合埋成 OINO。你可以記住：左飠只取頭兩筆 OI，右欠一頭一尾 NO，飲水嘅時候正正係一人（O）喺頭一人（O）喺尾。

餃.en: Today we learn 餃, read "gaau2" — the stuffed dumplings you love to eat, a filling wrapped in a pasta skin. Notice it splits into two sides: on the left is 飠 (the food radical), and on the right is 交. The left-hand 字首 飠 has many strokes, so Cangjie takes just its head and tail — head 人(O) and tail 戈(I); the right-hand 字身 交 then gives its head 亠(Y), then 金(C), and its tail 大(K), so the whole code strings together as OIYCK. Remember it this way: the food radical yields only two codes, while 交 is read top to bottom as 亠, 金, 大 — and "I want to eat shrimp dumplings" is ready to type.
餃.zh: 今日我哋學「餃」呢個字，讀「gaau2」，就係我哋成日食嘅餃子，包住餡料嘅麵皮點心。你睇下佢分做兩邊：左邊係「飠」（食字邊），右邊係「交」。左邊嘅字首「飠」筆畫多，倉頡取頭尾兩碼——頭係人(O)，尾係戈(I)；右邊嘅字身「交」就取頭亠(Y)，中間金(C)，尾大(K)，所以成個碼砌埋就係 OIYCK。記住喇：食字邊只取兩碼，右邊「交」由上到下亠、金、大逐格取，「我想食蝦餃」就搞掂晒。

餐.en: Today we're learning 餐, read caan1, which means to eat or dine — it's the word for a meal, like the meal you sit down to enjoy. This character looks busy and complicated, but don't worry, because it's treated as a whole-character (整體字), so we don't break every single piece apart; instead we grab the head, a couple of key shapes, and the tail. Look at the top: there's ⺊, which is Y; then on the upper right the 又 shape, which is E; below that the 人 shape, which is O; and finally at the very bottom the ㄑ shape, which is V — giving you the full code YEOIV. Since it's a whole-character, we follow the rule of taking the head Y, the second E, the third O, then jumping straight to the tail V, skipping the middle pieces like the 厶 (I) that sit in between. Here's your memory hook: eat this 餐 meal from the top ⺊ down to the tail ㄑ, and just skip whatever's stuck in the middle!
餐.zh: 今日我哋學「餐」呢個字，讀作 caan1，意思係食飯、一餐嘅嘢食，就好似你去食晏、食一餐飯咁。呢個字筆畫多，睇落好複雜，但你唔使緊張，因為佢係一個「整體字」，我哋唔會逐個部件拆晒佢，只係取頭尾同前面幾個關鍵形。你睇，最上面係「⺊」，撳 Y；跟住喺右上角係「又」字形，撳 E；再落嚟係「人」字形，撳 O；最後喺底部取「ㄑ」呢個尾形，撳 V，所以成個碼就係 YEOIV。因為係整體字，中間嗰啲部件（好似「厶」I）我哋照規矩取頭 Y、二 E、三 O、再跳去攞尾 V，中間唔會逐個攞晒。記住喇：一「餐」飯要由頭 ⺊ 食到尾 ㄑ，中間嗰啲就跳過佢啦！

館.en: Today's character is 館, read gun2, meaning a public building — the kind of place in 咖啡館 (gaa3 fe1 gun2, a café) or 博物館 (bok3 mat6 gun2, a museum). It splits left and right: the food radical 飠 is the head on the left, and 官 is the body on the right. In Cangjie a head takes at most two codes, so from the food radical you take only its first two pieces — 人 (O) and 戈 (I); then you move to the body 官 and take 十 (J), 口 (R), 口 (R) in order. Put together it's OIJRR — remember the food radical gives just two, and the 官 on the right counts down after it. A hook: two sips (人, 戈), then an official (官) inside the building with two open mouths (口口) below him.
館.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「館」，讀做 gun2，指嘅係公共建築物，好似「咖啡館」（gaa3 fe1 gun2）或者「博物館」（bok3 mat6 gun2）咁。呢個字左右兩邊分開，左邊係食字旁「飠」做字首，右邊係「官」做字身。倉頡拆字，字首最多取兩碼，所以食字旁只揀頭兩個部件——「人」（O）同「戈」（I）；跟住到右邊嘅字身「官」，順住次序取「十」（J）、「口」（R）、「口」（R）。合埋就係 OIJRR，記住食字旁只出頭兩粒，右邊個「官」慢慢數落去就得。你不妨記住：飲咗兩杯（人、戈），去館裏面搵一個官，官下面兩張口（口口）。

首.en: Today we meet 首, read "sau2". At heart it means "head", and from there it stretches to "first, leader, chief", and it's also the word you use to count poems and songs. Look at its shape: it's one dense block with no clean seam to split a 字首 from a 字身, which makes it a 整體字, a whole character. For a whole character Cangjie's rule is head-2-3-tail — take the first two pieces, skip the middle, then grab the very last — so following the writing order we collect four pieces: the top 廿 (T), then 竹 (H), then 月 (B), and finally 山 (U), giving THBU. The reason we skip the middle is precisely that a whole character can't take every stroke, so this head-2-3-tail method picks four representatives. To remember it, read "廿竹月山" straight down the block and just leap over the middle — the same 首 that starts 首先 (sau2 sin1) and 首次 (sau2 ci3).
首.zh: 今日我哋學「首」呢個字，讀「sau2」，本身係「頭」嘅意思，引申做「第一、領導、首領」，數詩嘅時候一首歌、一首詩都係用佢。你望下佢個樣，成隻字係一大嚿疊埋一齊，冇一條清楚嘅界線可以劃開字首同字身，所以佢係一隻「整體字」。遇到整體字，倉頡嘅規矩就係取頭二三尾——即係頭嗰兩件、跳過中間、再攞埋最尾嗰件，所以我哋順住寫嘅次序攞四件：最上面嘅廿（T），跟住嘅竹（H），再嚟嘅月（B），同埋最尾嘅山（U），砌成 THBU。點解要跳過中間？因為整體字唔可以攞齊所有部件，就用「頭二三尾」呢個取碼法揀出四件代表。記住佢嘅時候，你可以想成「廿竹月山」由頂讀到底，中間嗰橛跳過就得，例如「首先」sau2 sin1、「首次」sau2 ci3 都係佢起頭。

香.en: Today we learn 香, read hoeng1, meaning fragrant or sweet-smelling, and it can also mean the sticks of incense you burn when praying. Look at its shape: a grain-like top sitting over the character 日 (sun) at the bottom. This is a whole-character (整體字) — it has no clean head/body seam to break it apart, so we use the whole-character method: take the head, the second piece, and the tail. The head is the grain radical ⽲, keyed H; the second piece is 木 (tree), keyed D; and the tail is 日 (sun), keyed A — giving you HDA. You'll see it in 香港 hoeng1 gong2 (Hong Kong) and 香港人 hoeng1 gong2 jan4 (Hong Kong people); remember the sentence 呢啲花好香, these flowers smell good — and picture grain (H), tree (D), sun (A) counted top to bottom so you never slip.
香.zh: 今日我哋學「香」，讀做 hoeng1，意思係香噴噴、有陣好聞嘅氣味，又可以指供神拜佛嗰啲香枝。你睇下佢個樣，上面似禾，下面係個「日」字。呢個字係一個「整體字」，即係佢冇一個清楚嘅字首字身界線畀你劈開，所以就用「整體字」嘅取碼方法：取個頭、取第二件、再取個尾。個頭係「禾」嘅嗰個⽲字頭，撳 H；第二件係「木」，撳 D；最尾係「日」，撳 A，合埋就係 HDA。你熟嘅詞有香港 hoeng1 gong2、香港人 hoeng1 gong2 jan4；記住呢句：呢啲花好香。想住禾（H）、木（D）、日（A）順住由上到下數落嚟，就唔會撳錯。

馬.en: Today we learn 馬, read maa5, the horse you already know so well, and it can also be a surname. Look at its shape: it's like a horse standing up, with four little dots of fire at the bottom serving as its four hooves. This is a 整體字, a whole-character written in one flowing stroke that doesn't break cleanly apart, so instead of splitting it we simply take four codes straight through: the head 尸 (S), the second piece 手 (Q), the third piece 尸 again (S), and the final four dots which are 火 (F, standing for the 灬 underneath). That gives you the whole code SQSF — head S, second Q, third S, tail F. Just picture a horse standing on its little fire-hooves, and 馬 is yours!
馬.zh: 我哋今日學「馬」，讀做 maa5，即係你成日聽開嘅嗰隻馬，亦都可以做姓氏。你睇吓佢嘅樣，好似一隻馬企喺度，下面仲有四點火腳做四隻蹄咁。呢個字係一個「整體字」，一筆過寫落去唔容易分開，所以我哋唔理咁多，直接由頭到尾攞四個碼：頭係「尸」（S），第二個係「手」（Q），第三個又係「尸」（S），最尾嗰四點就係「火」（F，代表底下嘅灬）。所以成個字係 SQSF——記住頭S、二Q、三S、尾F，一隻馬企喺火腳上面，就係「馬」喇！

體.en: Today we learn 體, read tai2, as in 身體 (body) — it means body, or a group, class, or unit. This character splits left and right: the 骨 part on the left is the head (字首), and 豊 on the right is the body (字身). For the head 骨 we don't spell out every stroke; we take just first and last, and both happen to be B — the ⺼ shape (B) — so the head gives us BB. The body 豊 has many strokes, but a 字身 caps at three codes, so we take its head 廿 (T), its second piece 田 (W), and its last piece 廿 (T), giving the full code BBTWT. Memory hook: the left 骨 lays down a double B, then 豊 rounds it off with T, W, T — one whole body, five keys.
體.zh: 今日我哋學「體」呢個字，讀做 tai2，就好似「身體」嘅「體」，指身體、又或者一個團體、單位。呢個字係左右兩部分：左邊係「骨」字部做字首，右邊係「豊」字做字身。字首「骨」我哋唔會逐筆拆晒，係取頭尾兩碼——頭係⺼（B），尾都係一個 B，所以字首就係 BB。字身「豊」筆畫多，倉頡規定字身最多取三碼，於是就取頭嘅廿（T）、第二個嘅田（W），同埋最尾嘅廿（T），合埋成 BBTWT。記住嘅竅門：左邊「骨」畀你兩個 B 打底，右邊「豊」再補上 T、W、T，一體成形！

高.en: Today we learn 高, read gou1, meaning high, tall, lofty or elevated — the word you'd use in a sentence like 佢生得好高, "he is very tall." Look at its shape: it stacks up from top to bottom, starting with the little lid 亠 on top, then a mouth 口, then an enclosing frame 冂, and finally another mouth 口 at the bottom. Because 高 is a whole-form character with no clean way to split it into a head part and a body part, we don't carve it left-right or top-bottom; instead we simply follow the writing order and take the head, the second, the third, and the tail. That gives us 亠 as Y, the second piece 口 as R, the frame 冂 as B, and the last 口 as R, spelling YRBR. Remember it as a little hat, a mouth, a box, and one more mouth — read top to bottom, Y-R-B-R is 高.
高.zh: 我哋今日學「高」呢個字，讀作 gou1，意思係高、高聳、崇高，好似「佢生得好高」入面咁形容一個人好高。你望下佢個樣，係一層層由上而下疊起嚟嘅：最頂係「亠」，跟住有個「口」，再落嚟係個框框「冂」，最底又有個「口」。因為「高」係一個整體字，冇一個清楚嘅字首字身可以拆，所以我哋唔理左右上下，只係順住個寫字次序，取頭、取二、取三、再取尾，即係「亠」係 Y、第二個「口」係 R、「冂」係 B、最尾嗰個「口」又係 R，砌埋一齊就係 YRBR。你可以記住：一頂帽（亠）、一把口（口）、一個框（冂）、再一把口（口），由頭數到尾，Y、R、B、R 就係「高」。

魚.en: Today we learn 魚, read jyu4, which means the fish that swims in the sea, and it can also be a surname. Look at its shape: on top sits a little ⺈ (typed N), in the middle a neat square 田 (typed W), and underneath the four-dot base 灬 (typed F), stacked together into the picture of a fish. Why just these three parts? Because 魚 is a whole-character shape with no clear left-right or top-bottom division, so instead of the head/body split we take head, middle, and tail — the top ⺈, the central 田, and the bottom 灬 — giving exactly three codes, NWF. Remember it as a fish drawn top to bottom: the head (⺈), the body (田), and the splash of its tail (灬) — N, W, F.
魚.zh: 今日我哋學「魚」呢個字，讀 jyu4，就係海入面游嚟游去嗰種魚，亦都可以做姓氏。你望下佢個樣，上面係一個小小嘅⺈（打 N），中間係一個四四方方嘅田（打 W），下面係四點底嗰個灬（打 F），三嚿疊埋一齊就砌成一條魚嘅樣。點解淨係取呢三碼呢？因為「魚」係一個整體字，冇明顯嘅左右或者上下分家，所以我哋唔搞字首字身嗰套，而係用「頭、二、尾」嘅方法，順住由上到下攞頭嗰嚿⺈、中間嗰嚿田、同埋尾嗰嚿灬，啱啱好三碼 NWF。記住：一條魚嘅頭（⺈）、身（田）、同尾巴嘅水花（灬），由上游到落，就係 N、W、F。

鮨.en: Today we learn 鮨, read zi1, which means seasoned rice mixed with fish or vegetables — exactly the sushi rice you see at a Japanese restaurant. Look at the character: on the left is 魚 (fish) and on the right is 旨, so you can guess right away it has something to do with fish. In Cangjie we split it into a head and a body. The head 魚 does not get spelled out fully; we take only its first and last shapes — first 弓 for N, last 火 for F, because those four dots at the bottom of 魚 count as 火 in Cangjie. The body 旨 likewise gives first and last — 匕 for P and 日 for A — so the full code is NFPA. Here's your memory hook: fish (NF) meets a tasty intention (PA), and together they make a plate of 鮨.
鮨.zh: 今日我哋學「鮨」呢個字，讀作 zi1，係指用魚或者菜同飯撈埋一齊嘅食物，即係我哋去日本料理見到嗰種壽司飯。你望下呢個字，左邊係「魚」，右邊係「旨」，一睇就知同魚有關。倉頡拆呢個字要分字首同字身：字首係「魚」，我哋唔會逐劃拆晒，只係取頭尾兩碼——頭係「弓」，撳 N；尾係「火」，撳 F，因為魚字底部嗰四點喺倉頡入面就當「火」。跟住字身係「旨」，同樣取頭尾——頭係「匕」，撳 P；尾係「日」，撳 A，砌埋一齊就係 NFPA。記住個口訣：魚（NF）搭埋旨（PA），一條魚配一個好味嘅心思，就成一碟鮨。

鮮.en: Today we learn 鮮, read sin1 like in 新鮮 (fresh); it means fresh, new, or delicious, and sometimes rare or few. Look at its shape: on the left is a fish 魚, and on the right is a sheep 羊 — two tasty things joined together, which is exactly why the character means delicious. When Cangjie breaks it up, the left 魚 is the head and we take only its first and last pieces — first 乙 (N), last 火 (F); the right 羊 is the body and likewise takes first-last — first 廿 (T), last 手 (Q). Put them in order and you get N, F, T, Q, which is NFTQ. Remember it this way: one fish plus one sheep, fish gives 乙火 and sheep gives 廿手, and out comes the fresh flavour.
鮮.zh: 今日我哋學「鮮」呢個字，讀 sin1，好似「新鮮」咁；佢原本嘅意思係「新鮮」、「美味」，有時亦解「稀少」。你望吓佢嘅結構，左邊係一條「魚」，右邊係一隻「羊」，兩樣好味嘅嘢合埋一齊，難怪解做鮮美。倉頡拆字嗰陣，左邊嘅「魚」係字首，我哋淨係取佢嘅頭尾兩碼——頭係「乙」（N），尾係「火」（F）；右邊嘅「羊」係字身，同樣取頭尾——頭係「廿」（T），尾係「手」（Q）。所以成個字砌落去就係 N、F、T、Q，即係 NFTQ。記住呢句：一條魚配一隻羊，魚取乙火、羊取廿手，鮮味就出嚟嘞。

鴻.en: Today's character is 「鴻」, read hung4, which originally names a large species of wild swan and by extension means vast or grand — you'll see it in words like 「鴻圖」 (a variant of 宏圖, grand plans) and 「鴻運」 (a variant of 紅運, great fortune). Look at the whole character and you'll see it's built from 「江」 on the left and 「鳥」 on the right joined together. When Cangjie breaks it up, the head 「江」 gives its first and last pieces: the three-drop water 「氵」, keyed E, and the single horizontal stroke 「一」, keyed M; then the body 「鳥」 gives its first and last pieces too, 「竹」 keyed H and 「火」 keyed F. Put them in order and you get E, M, H, F — EMHF. To remember it, picture a great bird taking flight beside the water: 「氵一竹火」, a swan rising over the river.
鴻.zh: 今日我哋學嘅字係「鴻」，讀做 hung4，本義係一種好大隻嘅野天鵝，引申開嚟又有「宏大、廣闊」嘅意思，好似「鴻圖」（即係宏圖）、「鴻運」（即係紅運）咁。你望吓成個字，其實係由左邊嘅「江」同右邊嘅「鳥」拼埋一齊。倉頡拆字嘅時候，字首就取「江」嘅頭尾兩碼，開頭係三點水「氵」，個掣係 E，尾就係一橫「一」，個掣係 M；字身就取「鳥」嘅頭尾兩碼，頭係「竹」，個掣係 H，尾係「火」，個掣係 F。所以成個字砌埋就係 E、M、H、F，即係 EMHF。記住呢個字嘅時候，你可以諗：水邊有隻大鳥飛過，「氵一竹火」，一隻鴻雁展翅高飛。

鵝.en: Today we're learning 鵝, read "ngo4" in Cantonese — the goose, that big long-necked bird. Look at its shape: on the left sits 我 (me), and on the right sits 鳥 (bird), and the two halves together make a goose. In Cangjie the 字首 (lead part) 我 gives only its head and tail — head is 竹 H and tail is 戈 I; then the 字身 (body part) 鳥 is a full, complex piece, so it takes three codes — head 竹 H, second code 日 A, and tail 火 F, giving the whole code HIHAF. Remember the rhythm here: the lead part contributes two codes and the body part three, which is the standard way a left-right character splits, so just think "我 then 鳥". Picture a plate of 燒鵝 (roast goose) or a 天鵝 (swan), and you'll remember that the bird half runs all the way down to that final fire, F.
鵝.zh: 今日我哋學「鵝」呢個字，粵音讀「ngo4」，就係嗰隻大隻又長頸嘅家禽——鵝。你睇下佢個結構，左邊係個「我」字，右邊係個「鳥」字，兩件砌埋一齊就成隻鵝。喺倉頡入面，字首「我」我哋只取頭尾兩碼——頭係「竹」H，尾係「戈」I；跟住字身「鳥」係一件複雜嘅字，可以取足三碼——頭係「竹」H，第二碼取「日」A，尾係「火」F，所以全碼就係 HIHAF。記住呢個節奏：字首取兩碼、字身取三碼，係倉頡拆字嘅基本規矩，你唸「我-鳥」就啱晒。你可以記住「燒鵝」同「天鵝」呢兩個詞，一想起碟燒鵝，就記得個「鳥」字要取到尾嗰個火 F 啦！

麗.en: Today we learn 麗, read lai6, meaning beautiful, magnificent, or elegant — you see it in 美麗 (mei5 lai6, beautiful) and 瑪麗 (maa5 lai6, the name Mary). Look at the shape: up top there are two horizontal bars sitting side by side, and underneath sit two ⺼ pieces followed by a 匕, which looks busy but breaks apart very tidily. The top serves as the 字首 and gives only its head and tail, and since both are the stroke 一 which is M, you get M then M; the bottom serves as the 字身, which is allowed three codes taken as head, second, and tail — the first ⺼ is B, the second ⺼ is B, and the final 匕 is P, so the full code is MMBBP. The reason the top gives two and the bottom gives three is the standard quota: once a character splits into 字首 and 字身, the 字首 takes head-tail while the 字身 takes head, second, and tail. Remember it as two bars up top, MM, and the bottom "month month spoon," BBP — say that and this elegant character falls into place.
麗.zh: 今日我哋學「麗」字，讀做 lai6，解「美麗」、「漂亮」嘅意思，好似「美麗」（mei5 lai6）、「瑪麗」（maa5 lai6，即係 Mary）咁。你望下呢個字，上面係兩橫排住嘅結構，下面係兩個「⺼」加埋一個「匕」，睇落好複雜，但拆起上嚟好有規律。上半部分做字首，我哋取頭尾兩碼，兩個「一」都係 M，所以係 M、M；下半部分做字身，字身可以取到三碼，就係取頭、二、尾——頭一個「⺼」係 B，第二個「⺼」又係 B，最尾嘅「匕」係 P，合埋就係 MMBBP。點解字首得兩碼、字身有三碼呢？因為倉頡拆字有配額：一個字分開字首字身之後，字首取少啲、字身取多啲，字首取頭尾兩碼，字身就取頭二尾三碼。記住口訣：上面兩橫 MM，下面「月月匕」BBP，一句就砌返個靚靚嘅「麗」字。

麥.en: Today's character is 麥, read mak6 — it means wheat, barley or oats, the grain you find in words like 麥當勞 (McDonald's) and 丹麥 (Denmark). Look at it: the top half is really the character 來, and the bottom half is 夊, a little trailing foot. When you break it up, the top 來 acts as the 字首, and a 字首 takes just its head and tail, so you get 十 (J) and 人 (O); then the bottom 夊 is the 字身, giving 乙 (N) and 夊 (I), for the full code JONI. Remember it this way: the 來 on top hands you 十 and 人, and the little foot below hands you 乙 and 夊 — just picture a bowl of oatmeal to lock it in.
麥.zh: 今日學嘅字係「麥」，讀做 mak6，即係麥、大麥、燕麥嗰啲穀物，例如「麥當勞」同「丹麥」都係用呢個字。你望吓佢，上半其實係一個「來」字，下半就係一隻腳嘅「夊」。拆碼嘅時候，上半嘅「來」做字首，字首取頭尾兩碼，所以就攞「十」（J）同埋「人」（O）；跟住落到下半嘅「夊」做字身，就淨係取「乙」（N）同「夊」（I），合埋成 JONI。記住個口訣：上面「來」畀你十人，下面一隻腳畀你乙夊，食碗麥皮就記得晒喇。

麵.en: Today we learn 麵, read min6, meaning flour, dough, or noodles — the same character in 麵包 min6 baau1, bread, and in a steaming bowl of 車仔麵 ce1 zai2 min6, cart noodle. The character breaks into two parts: the 字首 on the left is 麥, and the 字身 on the right is 面. Because 麥 is a full, complex radical serving as the head part, it only lends its head and tail: head 十 J and tail 乙 N. The body 面 then follows the normal rule of head, second, and tail, giving head 一 M, second 田 W, and tail 中 L, so the whole code spells out JNMWL. The thing to hold onto is why the head part gives only two codes while the body gives three — the 字首 quota is head-and-tail, the 字身 quota reaches for a third piece. As a memory hook, picture a bowl of noodles with a stalk of 麥 on the left and a 面 on the right: J N to open, M W L to close, and you have min6.
麵.zh: 今日我哋學「麵」呢個字，讀作 min6，即係麵粉、麵團同麵條嘅意思，好似你成日食嘅「麵包」min6 baau1，或者一碗熱辣辣嘅「車仔麵」ce1 zai2 min6。呢個字分做兩橛：左邊嘅字首係「麥」，右邊嘅字身係「面」。字首「麥」係複雜嘅字，所以取頭尾兩碼——頭係「十」J，尾係「乙」N；跟住字身「面」照倉頡取碼規則，取頭一、次一、尾一，即係頭「一」M、第二嘅「田」W、尾「中」L，所以成個字砌埋就係 JNMWL。你要記住嘅重點係：字首因為係一橛完整嘅偏旁，淨係借頭同尾兩碼；而字身就影全身，可以取到三碼。記住嘅竅門——一碗麵，左邊嘟一把「麥」，右邊擺個「面」，J N 開頭、M W L 收尾，一齊入口就啱晒！

麻.en: Today's character is 麻, read maa4, the plant we call hemp, jute or flax, and also the sesame we cook with. Look at its shape: there's a 广 roof on top, and tucked underneath is 林, two trees standing side by side. When we break it into code, the head 广 is easy — it simply gives its own key I; then the body 林 isn't taken stroke by stroke but by head and tail, so we take the leading 十 as J and the trailing 金 twice, each C, giving us the full code IJCC. Why only these few pieces from the body? Because a body takes at most three codes, and reading 林 head-then-tail yields exactly 十金金, three pieces that fit the quota. Remember it this way: the 广 shelters the roof, and beneath it 林 splits into 十金金 — say that and the shape will never tangle you up.
麻.zh: 今日學嘅字係「麻」，讀 maa4，即係大麻、亞麻嗰種植物，又或者係我哋煮嘢食用嘅芝麻。你睇下佢個樣，上面有個廣字頭「广」，下面藏住兩棵木疊埋一齊嘅「林」。拆碼嗰陣，字首「广」好簡單，就攞佢個碼 I；到咗字身「林」呢個部分，倉頡唔係逐筆全取，而係取頭同取尾——攞頭嗰粒「十」係 J，再攞尾嗰兩個「金」，兩次都係 C，所以合埋成 IJCC。點解字身淨係揀到呢幾粒？因為字身最多只取三粒碼，「林」順住取頭二尾，就攞到「十金金」三粒，啱啱好。記住個口訣：广頂住個屋簷，下面林拆做十金金，你就唔會再撈亂喇。

黃.en: Today we learn 黃, read wong4, meaning the colour yellow, and it also works as a surname, as in 黃大仙. Look at the whole shape: it's a 整體字, a whole-character, meaning it doesn't break cleanly into a head and a body, so we simply read it top to bottom, first piece to last. The top piece is 廿, on the T key; then the horizontal 一 in the middle, on the M key; below that the 田, on the W key; and finally the 八 at the bottom, on the C key, giving you TMWC. Just stack them from the top down — 廿, 一, 田, 八 — layer by layer, and the whole yellow 黃 comes together.
黃.zh: 今日我哋學「黃」字，讀音係 wong4，意思係黃色，亦都可以做姓氏，好似「黃大仙」咁。你望下成個字，佢係一個「整體字」，即係話冇明顯分成字首同字身兩橛，我哋只需要順住由上到下、由頭到尾嘅次序拆佢就得。開頭係「廿」，撳 T 鍵；跟住係中間嗰橫「一」，撳 M 鍵；再落嚟係中間嗰個「田」，撳 W 鍵；最後係底部嘅「八」，撳 C 鍵，合埋就係 TMWC。記住由上數落嚟：廿、一、田、八，一層一層咁疊起，就砌出成個黃色嘅「黃」喇。

黑.en: Today's character is 黑, read hak1 (sometimes haak1), meaning black or dark, and by extension evil or sinister, as in a black-hearted person. Look at it: up top sits a 田, then a horizontal band in the middle, and four dots of fire underneath — everything piling up into a deep, shadowy mass. 黑 is a whole-character shape (整體字) that can't be cleanly cut into a head and a body, so Cangjie falls back on its general rule: take the head, take the second piece, and take the last. The head is 田, which is W; the second piece is the 土 in the middle, which is G; and the last piece is the four fire dots 灬, which is F — giving you WGF. Picture a field, a patch of earth, and four flames scorching it black beneath, and the three steps W, G, F will stay with you.
黑.zh: 今日學嘅字係「黑」，讀作 hak1（有時讀 haak1），意思係黑色、幽暗，引申開去仲可以指邪惡、陰險，好似「黑心」咁。你望住呢個字，會見到上面一個「田」字，中間夾住一橫，底下四點火，砌埋一齊就係一團好深好暗嘅感覺。「黑」係一個整體字，唔可以清清楚楚咁劈開字首字身，所以倉頡就用取碼嘅通則：頭一個碼、次一個碼，加埋尾一個碼。頭係「田」，撳 W；第二個係中間嗰個「土」，撳 G；尾係底下四點火「灬」，撳 F，合埋就係 WGF。記住呢個畫面：一塊田、一撻泥土、底下四點火慢慢焗到成塊地變黑，你就記得 W、G、F 呢三步。

點.en: Today we're learning 點, read dim2. It originally means a dot or a drop — like a speck of ink landing on paper, a single 'point' — and from there it grew to mean a point, a spot, or a degree, and in Cantonese it turns up in questions like 點樣 (how) and 點解 (why). Look at the shape: it's stacked top over bottom, with 黑 on top and 占 underneath, the four little fire-dots at the base hinting nicely at 'dots' and 'sparks.' When Cangjie breaks it up, the head 黑 gives its first and last pieces — 田 W at the front and 火 F at the end — while the body 占 also takes first and last, 卜 Y and 口 R, so the whole code is 田火卜口, WFYR. Here's your hook: the black field-and-fire on top, the divining stroke-and-mouth below — four keys, WFYR, and you've got 點.
點.zh: 今日我哋學「點」呢個字，讀做 dim2，本來意思係一點、一滴，好似墨水滴落張紙咁樣一「點」，後來又引申做「點」，即係一個位、一個程度，甚至喺廣東話入面問「點樣」、「點解」嘅時候都用到佢。你望吓個字，佢係上下結構：上面係「黑」，下面係「占」，四粒火點喺個「黑」字底下，一睇就知同「點、火星」有關。倉頡拆碼嘅時候，字首「黑」取頭尾兩碼——頭係田 W，尾係火 F；字身「占」都係取頭尾——頭係卜 Y，尾係口 R，所以整個字砌埋就係田火卜口 WFYR。記住呢個口訣：黑色嘅田火，占卦嘅卜口，四個碼一齊落，就係「點」喇。

齊.en: Today we learn 齊, read cai4, meaning even, uniform, or all of the same height with nothing sticking out longer or shorter. Look at this character — it's genuinely complex, a dense stack of strokes crowded together, and breaking it cleanly into pieces would be awkward. Cangjie has a special trick for characters that are this hard to decompose: you take the opening part, then finish with the 難 ("difficult") key. So 齊 begins with a 卜 shape, which lives on the Y key, and instead of struggling to split the rest, you simply press the 難 key on X, giving you YX. The memory hook: if a character looks too tangled to take apart, it's often just "first code plus X" — as in 一齊 (jat1 cai4) and 整齊 (zing2 cai4), everything lined up neat and even.
齊.zh: 今日我哋學「齊」，讀 cai4，意思係整齊、齊全、一樣咁高，冇長短之分。你望吓呢個字，佢結構好繁複，成堆筆畫疊埋一齊，要逐粒拆出嚟其實好難。倉頡遇到呢種複雜到唔容易拆嘅字，有一個特別辦法：先取字嘅開頭部分，然後用「難」鍵嚟收尾。所以「齊」開頭係一個「卜」形，喺 Y 鍵；跟住我哋唔再逐部分拆落去，而係直接撳「難」鍵，佢喺 X 鍵度，於是整個字就係 YX。記住：一望就覺得難拆嘅字，好多時就係「頭一碼加 X」，好似「一齊」（jat1 cai4）、「整齊」（zing2 cai4）咁，撳落去成排企得齊齊整整。

龍.en: Today we learn 龍, read lung4, the mighty dragon of legend. It looks complicated, but we still split it into left and right: the left block is the 字首 and the right block is the 字身. A 字首 takes only head and tail, so from the left we pick the first piece 卜 (Y) and the last piece 月 (B); a 字身 may take three, using head-second-tail, so from the right we pick 卜 (Y), 匚 (S), and 心 (P). Put together that gives YBYSP. You will see this character in 九龍 (Kowloon) and 九龍城 (Kowloon City), right here in Hong Kong. Remember it as: left side 卜月, right side 卜匚心 — keep the two halves apart and the code falls into place.
龍.zh: 今日我哋學「龍」呢個字，讀 lung4，即係傳說入面嗰隻威武嘅龍。呢個字睇落好複雜，但係我哋照樣拆做左右兩邊：左邊嗰嚿係字首，右邊嗰嚿係字身。字首取頭尾兩碼，所以我哋喺左邊揀到頭嗰個卜（Y）同尾嗰個月（B）；字身可以取三碼，用頭、二、尾嘅方法，喺右邊揀到卜（Y）、匚（S）同心（P）。合埋就係 YBYSP。你睇「九龍」、「九龍城」都有呢個字，就喺我哋香港㗎。記住口訣：左邊卜月，右邊卜匚心，中間隔開就唔會亂喇。

𡃉.en: Today we're learning 𡃉, read gaa3, a very common Cantonese sentence-final particle — you tack it onto the end of a sentence, like in 係咁樣做𡃉 ("It's done this way"). Notice the 口 mouth radical on the left; a lot of these little spoken particles carry a 口 because they're sounds you say out loud. When we break it up, the head is that left-hand 口 R, and the right-hand piece 奌 is the body; the body is coded by its first, middle, and last shapes, so we take 大 K, then 口 R, then 火 F, giving RKRF all together. Why only three codes for the body? Because Cangjie caps a body at three codes, so when there's more inside we keep only the first, middle, and last as stand-ins and skip whatever sits between. Remember it as mouth first, then big-mouth-fire after — you open your 口 to say 𡃉, and that mouth radical is your anchor.
𡃉.zh: 今日我哋學嘅係「𡃉」，讀音係 gaa3，係廣東話一個好常見嘅句末語氣詞，好似「係咁樣做𡃉」噉樣，擺喺句尾用嚟收尾。你留意佢左邊有個「口」字部，好多語氣詞都有個口字部，因為佢哋係講嘢嘅音。拆碼嘅時候，字首就係左邊個口 R，跟住右邊嘅「奌」就係字身；字身要用「頭、次、尾」三碼嚟取，所以我哋攞頭嘅大 K、次嘅口 R、同埋尾嘅火 F，合埋一齊就係 RKRF。點解字身只攞三個碼呢？因為倉頡規定字身最多取三碼，唔夠位嘅就只揀頭、次、尾三個代表，所以「奌」中間嗰啲細節就跳過咗。記住口喺前、大口火喺後，一講「𡃉」就開口，個口字部就係你嘅記認。

⺌.en: Look at this shape: ⺌, the 小 top — it's the variant of 小 that sits above other characters. It lives on the F key together with its parent radical 火, and you can spot it perched on top of characters like 光 and 當.
⺌.zh: 你睇下呢個形：⺌，就係「小字頭」，即係「小」字擺喺個字頂嗰個變體。佢屬於 F 掣，同「火」係同一個掣，你可以喺「光」同「當」呢兩個字嘅頂部搵到佢。

⺮.en: Look at this shape — ⺮, the bamboo top. It's the variant form of the parent radical 竹, standing for things made of bamboo, and it lives on the H key. You can spot it sitting on top of characters like 等 and 筆.
⺮.zh: 你睇下呢個形——⺮，就係竹字頭，代表用竹造嘅嘢，係「竹」呢個部首嘅變形。佢喺H掣度，好似「等」同「筆」嘅頂部咁，一寫就見到兩片竹葉。

⺼.en: Take a look at this variant shape ⺼ — it's the flesh form of 肉, the piece you see in characters about body parts. It lives on the B key under the parent radical 月, and you can spot it on the left side of a character like 腦.
⺼.zh: 睇下呢個變體形 ⺼，佢係「肉」字嘅變形，即係肉字旁，通常出現喺同身體部位有關嘅字入面。佢屬於 B 掣，母部首係「月」，好似「腦」呢個字左邊嗰嚿就係喇。

ナ.en: Look at this shape: ナ. It looks like the left-hand strokes — a slash crossing a horizontal line. It lives on the K key as a variant of the parent radical 大, and you can spot it in characters like 左, 友, and 有.
ナ.zh: 你睇吓「ナ」呢個形，佢好似人嘅左手邊，一撇加一橫咁樣。呢個形收喺K掣度，係「大」字嘅變形，你可以喺「左」、「友」、「有」呢啲字入面搵到佢。

ㄑ.en: Look at this shape: ㄑ, a single stroke that twists and bends like a wriggling line. It's a variant of the parent radical 女 (woman), and it lives on the V key.
ㄑ.zh: 睇下呢個形狀：ㄑ，好似一劃扭嚟扭去嘅扭紋筆咁。佢係女字部嘅一個變體形，收喺鍵盤嘅 V 掣度。

七.en: Look at this shape: 七, the bend you see at the bottom of the character 七 that sweeps across and hooks upward — that's why we call it the 七 bend. It's a variant on the 心 radical, which lives on the P key, and you can spot it on the left side of the character 切.
七.zh: 你望下呢個形：七，就好似「七」字下面嗰一劃打橫再向上彎起，所以叫做「七字彎」。佢係心部（P鍵）嘅一個變形，你可以喺「切」字左邊搵到佢。

丨.en: Look at this shape: 丨, a single vertical stroke running straight down from top to bottom. It lives on the L key as one of the faces of the 中 radical, and you can spot it in the upright stroke on the left side of 引.
丨.zh: 睇下呢個形：丨，一條由上到下嘅豎筆，簡簡單單一劃。佢喺 L 掣度，係中字碼嘅其中一個樣，你可以喺「引」字左邊嗰條直豎搵到佢。

丶.en: Look at this shape: 丶. It's just a single dot, like a light tap of the brush on the paper. This is one of the variant faces on the I key, which belongs to the 戈 radical, and you can spot it inside characters like 太 and 凡.
丶.zh: 你睇下呢個形：丶，就係一點，好似寫字時輕輕篤落去嘅一點咁。呢個係戈字母 I 鍵嘅其中一個變體，你可以喺「太」同「凡」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

丷.en: Look at this shape: 丷, two little strokes splaying outward like the character 八 flipped upside-down. It lives on the C key as a variant of the parent radical 金, and you can spot it sitting on top of the character 兌.
丷.zh: 你睇下呢個形：丷，就好似個「八」字反轉咗咁，兩點向外撇開。佢住喺C鍵度，係金字部嘅一個變體，你可以喺「兌」字上面搵到佢。

丿.en: Look at this shape: 丿, a single stroke slanting down toward the lower left. It belongs to the 竹 radical and lives on the H key, and you can spot it inside characters like 少 and 乎.
丿.zh: 你留意下呢個形：丿，就係向左下方斜落去嘅一撇。佢屬於竹字母，喺H掣度，好似「少」同「乎」呢兩個字裏面都搵到佢。

乂.en: Look at this shape: 乂, two strokes that fork open and cross each other, like an open crossing point. It's a variant of the parent radical 大, and it lives on the K key — you can spot it inside characters like 文 and 父.
乂.zh: 睇下呢個字形：乂，兩筆開叉噉交叉埋一齊，好似一個交叉點噉。佢係「大」呢個字母嘅其中一個變體，擺喺 K 鍵度，你可以喺「文」同「父」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

乙.en: Look at this shape: 乙, like a stroke that runs flat and then hooks back up at the end. It lives on the N key as a variant under the parent radical 弓, and you can spot it inside characters like 九 and 氣.
乙.zh: 你望下呢個形：乙，就好似一個打橫拉出去、尾嗰度勾返起嘅鈎。佢屬於 N 掣，係「弓」呢個字根之下嘅一個變體，你可以喺「九」同「氣」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

亅.en: Look at this shape: 亅, a straight vertical stroke that hooks up at the bottom — the straight hook. It lives on the N key as one of the variant faces of the parent radical 弓, and you can spot it in characters like 打 and 丁.
亅.zh: 你睇下呢個形：亅，係一條打直、尾端向上鈎起嘅鈎。佢屬於 N 鍵，係「弓」呢個字根嘅其中一個變體，你可以喺「打」字同「丁」字裏面搵到佢。

亠.en: Look at this shape: 亠, like a little lid sitting on top of a character — one horizontal stroke with a dot above it. It belongs to the 卜 radical on the Y key, and you can spot it perched on top of both 交 and 市.
亠.zh: 睇下呢個形：亠，好似一頂帽咁擺喺個字嘅頭頂，一橫下面加一點。佢屬於卜（Y）呢個掣，你可以喺「交」同「市」呢兩個字嘅上面搵到佢。

亻.en: Look at this shape: 亻, a person standing on the left side of the character, just two lean strokes. It's a variant of the parent radical 人, and it lives on the O key — you'll spot it on the left of characters like 你, 佢, and 係.
亻.zh: 你留意下呢個形狀：亻，係一個人企喺字嘅左邊，兩劃瘦瘦哋。佢係「人」字嘅變體，收喺 O 鍵度，好似「你」、「佢」、「係」呢啲字，左邊都係佢。

入.en: Look at this shape: 入, which means 'enter' — it's like the character 人 with its two legs swapped. It lives on the O key as a variant of the parent radical 人, and you can anchor it with the character 內.
入.zh: 睇下呢個形：入，意思係「入去」，好似「人」字兩隻腳掉轉咁樣。佢屬於 O 鍵，係「人」呢個字根嘅一個變體，你可以用「內」呢個字嚟記住佢。

八.en: Look at this shape: 八 — two strokes splitting apart, as if something is being divided down the middle. It lives on the C key as a variant of the parent radical 金, and you can anchor it with the characters 分 and 公.
八.zh: 睇下呢個字形「八」，佢係兩筆向兩邊分開嘅樣，好似有樣嘢俾人由中間分開咁。呢個字形擺喺 C 鍵度，係金字部嘅其中一個副形，你可以用「分」同「公」呢兩個字嚟記實佢。

冂.en: Look at this variant shape: 冂, a frame that opens downward, like a little roof covering what's underneath. It lives on the B key as a variant of the 月 radical, and you can spot it inside both 內 and 周.
冂.zh: 睇下呢個變形樣：冂，係一個開口向下嘅框，好似一頂帽咁遮住個頭。佢屬於B掣，係月字部嘅變形，你喺「內」同「周」呢兩個字度都揾到佢。

冖.en: Look at this shape: 冖, a flat cover that sits on top and shades whatever is underneath, like a lid. It's a variant of the 月 radical and lives on the B key, and you can spot it in 學 and 愛.
冖.zh: 你睇下呢個形：冖，係一個平平嘅冚頭蓋，好似蓋喺上面咁遮住下面嘅嘢。佢係月字母嘅一個變形，收喺 B 鍵度，你可以喺「學」同「愛」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

凵.en: Look at this shape: 凵, like a little box that opens upward, its mouth facing the sky. It's a variant of the parent radical 山, and it lives on the U key — you can spot it inside characters like 出 and 凶.
凵.zh: 睇下呢個形：凵，好似一個向上開口嘅盒仔，張開口向住天。佢係山字嘅一個變形，收喺U掣入面，你可以喺「出」同「凶」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

勹.en: Look at this shape: 勹 — it's like a hook curving down from the top, wrapping around whatever sits inside, which is why we call it a wrapping hook. It's a variant on the P key under the parent radical 心, and you can spot it in the characters 勿 and 句.
勹.zh: 睇下呢個形：勹，好似一個由上向下彎落嚟嘅鈎，將入面嘅嘢包住，所以叫做「包住嘅框」。佢係心部P鍵嘅一個變形，你可以喺「勿」同「句」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

匕.en: Look at this shape: 匕, curved like a spoon. It's a variant that lives on the P key, under the parent radical 心, and you can spot it inside characters like 化 and 老.
匕.zh: 睇下呢個形：匕，好似一隻匙羹咁，係心字部（P鍵）嘅一個變化形。你可以喺「化」同「老」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

匚.en: Look at this shape: 匚, like a box that opens toward the right — closed on three sides with a gap on the right. It's a variant on the S key, belonging to the 尸 radical, and you can spot it inside 區 and 匹.
匚.zh: 睇下呢個形：匚，好似一個開口向右嘅箱，三邊圍住、右邊留返個缺口。佢係 S 鍵嘅其中一個變體，屬於「尸」呢個字根，你可以喺「區」同「匹」呢兩個字裏面搵到佢。

厂.en: Look at this shape: 厂, a cliff overhang — a flat top that juts out and slopes down, like a ledge of rock hanging over your head. It's one of the variant faces on the M key, belonging to the parent radical 一, and you can spot it sitting on top of characters like 石, 原 and 厚.
厂.zh: 你睇下呢個形：厂，好似一個山崖嘅頂，一橫由上面斜斜咁伸出嚟，好似一塊懸空嘅崖石咁。佢係一（M）嘅其中一個變形，你喺「石」字上面就見到佢，「原」同「厚」字都係用呢個崖頭起頭。

厶.en: Look at this shape: 厶, a little coiled tail, like a loop tucked into a corner — you'll spot it in both 私 and 去. It's a variant face living on the I key under the parent radical 戈, so just anchor it to that coil in 私 and 去.
厶.zh: 睇下呢個形：厶，就好似一個打咗個圈嘅小尾巴，你可以喺「私」同「去」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。呢個係「戈」字部（I 鍵）嘅一個變體，記住私、去嗰個圈就得㗎喇。

又.en: Look at this shape 又 — it looks like a right hand reaching out, and it lives on the E key as one of its variant forms, even though that key's main radical is 水 (water). You can spot this hand tucked inside characters like 友 and 受.
又.zh: 睇下呢個字形「又」，佢好似一隻伸出嚟嘅右手，係喺 E 掣入面嘅其中一個變化形，而 E 掣本身嘅正主係「水」。你可以喺「友」同「受」呢兩個字度見到佢，嗰隻手嘅形態就藏喺入面。

囗.en: Look at this shape: 囗, a fully sealed box with four sides closed, like a wall that pens everything inside. It lives on the W key as a variant of the 田 radical, and you can spot it inside characters like 回, 因, and 國.
囗.zh: 睇下呢個形：囗，一個四邊圍實嘅框，好似一道圍牆將入面嘅嘢圍住咁。佢屬於 W 掣，係田字部嘅其中一個變形，你可以喺「回」、「因」、「國」呢啲字入面搵到佢。

士.en: Look at this shape: 士, meaning scholar — it looks like 土 but with the long stroke on top and the shorter stroke below. It's a variant of the 土 radical and lives on the G key, and you can spot it inside a character like 志.
士.zh: 睇下呢個形：士，即係學者嘅意思，佢好似個土字，不過上面嗰橫寫得長啲、下面嗰橫短啲。佢係土字部嘅一個變形，收喺 G 鍵度，好似「志」呢個字裏面就有佢喇。

宀.en: Look at this shape: 宀, the roof radical — picture the top of a house giving you shelter overhead. It lives on the J key as a variant under the parent radical 十, and you can spot it sitting right on top of the character 家, covering the whole house below.
宀.zh: 望下呢個形：宀，就係我哋成日講嘅寶蓋頭，好似一間屋嘅屋頂咁，有瓦遮頭。佢屬於十字母（即係 J 鍵），係「十」呢個部首之下嘅一個變體，你可以喺「家」呢個字入面見到佢喺最上面遮住成間屋。

小.en: Look at this shape: 小, which carries the meaning of smallness. It's one of the variant forms on the F key, belonging to the parent radical 火, and you can spot it inside characters like 少 and 尖.
小.zh: 望下呢個字形：小，佢代表「細小」嘅意思。呢個係 F 鍵嘅其中一個變體，母字根係火，你可以喺「少」同「尖」呢兩個字入面搵到佢。

屮.en: Look at this shape: 屮, like a young sprout just pushing up out of the ground. It's a variant of the 山 radical and lives on the U key — you'll find it inside the character 出.
屮.zh: 睇下呢個形：屮，好似一棵剛剛冒出嚟嘅嫩芽，向上生長。佢係山字母嘅其中一個變形，收喺 U 鍵度，你可以喺「出」呢個字入面搵到佢。

广.en: Look at this shape 广: it's like a lean-to roof slanting over the top and left side, and it usually signals shops and places, which is why you'll spot it in 店, 度, and 廣. This face lives on the I key as a variant of its parent radical 戈, so reach for it when you're typing a place-word like 店.
广.zh: 睇下呢個字形「广」，佢好似一個斜頂嘅屋簷，蓋住上邊同左邊，通常代表舖頭同地方，好似「店」、「度」、「廣」呢啲字入面都見到佢。「广」係屬於 I 掣，係「戈」部嘅一個變形，你打「店」呢個地方嘅時候就會用到佢。

忄.en: Look at this shape: 忄. It's the standing heart — the form 心 takes when it stands on the left side of a character, and it carries the sense of feelings, which you can see anchoring characters like 快 and 情. It lives on the P key, part of the same family as its parent radical 心.
忄.zh: 睇下呢個形：忄。佢係「豎心邊」，即係「心」字擺喺左邊嗰陣變出嚟嘅樣，代表感情，你喺「快」同「情」呢兩個字入面都見到佢企喺左手邊。呢個形收喺 P 掣度，同「心」字係一家人。

扌.en: Look at this shape: 扌, the raised-hand radical, standing for actions done with the hand — you'll see it on the left of 打 and 接. It's a variant of the parent radical 手, and it lives on the Q key.
扌.zh: 你望下呢個形：扌，就係提手旁，代表用手做嘅動作，好似「打」同「接」入面左邊嗰部分。佢係「手」字嘅變形，收埋喺 Q 掣度。

曰.en: Look at this shape: 曰, a flattened version of 日 that means 'to say'. It belongs to the 日 radical family and lives on the A key — you'll spot it inside characters like 書, 最, and 會.
曰.zh: 你望下呢個字形：曰，係一個扁扁哋嘅日字，解「講」嘅意思。佢屬於日字部，收喺 A 掣度，好似「書」、「最」、「會」呢啲字入面都搵得到佢。

氵.en: Look at this shape: 氵, three little drops of water standing for wet things. It's a variant of the water radical 水 and lives on the E key — you'll spot it on the left side of characters like 港, 海 and 湯.
氵.zh: 你望下呢個形——氵，三點水，即係三滴水，代表濕嘅嘢。佢係「水」字嘅變身，收喺 E 鍵度，好似「港」、「海」、「湯」呢啲同水有關嘅字，個左邊嗰三點就係佢喇。

氺.en: Look at this shape: 氺. It's the water radical 水 squashed flat — the upright water pressed down into a wider form, so it still lives on the E key with the rest of the water family. You can spot it inside the character 求.
氺.zh: 睇下呢個形狀：氺。佢係「水」字被壓扁咗嘅樣，本來直立嘅水，而家攤平咗，所以佢一樣屬於 E 鍵嘅水部大家族。你可以喺「求」字裏面搵到佢。

灬.en: Look at this shape: 灬, four little dots sitting along the bottom like flames licking upward — it means heat and cooking. It's a variant of the 火 radical and lives on the F key, and you can spot it underneath characters like 熱 and 點.
灬.zh: 睇下呢個樣：灬，四粒點排喺底部，好似火燒緊嘢咁，代表熱同煮食。佢係火字的變體，收喺 F 掣度，你可以喺「熱」同「點」呢兩個字下面搵到佢。

爫.en: Look at this shape: 爫, a claw — a hand reaching down from above. It lives on the B key as one of the variant faces of the parent radical 月, and you can spot it sitting on top of characters like 愛 and 受.
爫.zh: 望下呢個形：爫，係「爪」字頭，即係一隻手由上面向下抓落嚟。佢屬於B鍵，係「月」字嘅其中一個變形，你可以喺「愛」同「受」呢兩個字嘅上面搵到佢。

疒.en: Look at this variant shape: 疒, the sickbed frame — picture a person lying down on a bed to rest while ill, which is why it stands for sickness. It lives on the K key as one of the faces of the parent radical 大, and you can spot it in both 病 and 痛.
疒.zh: 睇下呢個變體：疒，就係「病字框」，好似一個人瞓咗喺床度養病噉，所以佢代表疾病嘅意思。佢住喺 K 掣，係大字部嘅其中一個變體，你喺「病」同「痛」呢兩個字入面都搵得到佢。

艹.en: Look at this shape: 艹, the grass top you often see sitting on top of characters — it means plants and greenery. It lives on the T key as one of the faces of the parent radical 廿, and you'll spot it crowning characters like 花, 茶, and 菜.
艹.zh: 你睇下呢個字形：艹，就係我哋成日見到嘅「草花頭」，代表花草植物嘅意思。佢屬於 T 鍵，係「廿」呢個部首嘅其中一個樣，你喺「花」、「茶」、「菜」呢啲字嘅頂部都會搵到佢。

衤.en: This shape is 衤, the clothing radical — it means clothes or garments, and it lives on the L key as one of the variant faces under the parent radical 中. You can spot it on the left side of characters like 初 and 被.
衤.zh: 呢個字面係「衤」，即係衫字旁，代表衣服嘅意思，佢屬於 L 掣，係「中」呢個部首之下嘅其中一個變體。你睇下「初」同「被」呢兩個字，左邊嗰個部分就係「衤」喇。

辶.en: Look at the shape 辶 — it's the walking road, the piece that carries a sense of motion or travelling along a path underneath a character. It lives on the Y key and belongs to the 卜 radical, and you can see it sitting at the bottom of 過.
辶.zh: 你睇下 辶 呢個形，佢係「行路底」，代表移動、行走嘅意思，好似一條路托住上面嘅字咁。佢屬於卜部，收喺 Y 鍵度，好似「過」呢個字下面嗰個部件就係佢喇。

𠆢.en: Look at this shape: 𠆢, a pointed little roof that shelters whatever sits beneath it — that's why it's called the person roof, one of the faces of the radical 人, and it lives on the O key. You can spot it perched on top of characters like 今, 會 and 食, and whenever you see it, you press O.
𠆢.zh: 你睇吓呢個形：𠆢，好似一個尖尖嘅屋頂遮住下面嘅嘢，所以叫「人字頭」，佢係「人」呢個字嘅其中一副面孔，住喺 O 掣度。你可以喺「今」、「會」、「食」呢啲字嘅頂部搵到佢，每次見到就撳 O。

A.en:
Let's look at this shape together: 日. It began life as a pictograph of the sun — long ago it was a circle with a dot in the middle, marking the sun's bright core. Over thousands of years the circle squared off into a rectangle, and that dot straightened into the middle stroke you see today. On its own it reads jat6 — the 日 in 日頭 and 星期日, meaning day.

As a component, 日 almost always signals time and light. Picture the sun rising, its light spreading, the hours slipping by — that's why so many time-and-light words carry it hidden inside: 時, 早, 明, 晚, each one holding a 日.

On the keyboard, the sun radical lives on the A key. The A key sits at the far left of the home row — the middle row — right where your left little finger rests naturally. The Side-frame 尸 you learned in an earlier lesson lives on the S key, which sits immediately to the right of A, so the two are next-door neighbours.

Now let's walk through what it builds. 嘅 is RAIU — the mouth 口 you met before opens on the R key, then comes our sun today, A. 的 is HAPI, with that A in the middle again giving you the sun. 香 is HDA, where the final A is the 日 sitting at the bottom. One more thing to preview: 日 has a variant face called 曰, a flattened 日 that means 'say', which you'll meet in 書, 最 and 會 — the same A key, hiding behind this squatter shape.
A.zh:
我哋一齊睇下呢個形：日。佢本來係太陽嘅象形字——古時候係一個圓圈，中間一點，代表太陽個核心。經過幾千年慢慢寫方咗，圓變成長方形，中間嗰點就變咗中間一橫，最後就成為今日你見到嘅日。佢自己一個字讀 jat6，就係「日頭」、「星期日」嗰個日。

做部件嘅時候，日通常同時間、同光有關。你想像下太陽升起、日光普照，同時間流逝，所以好多同時間、光線有關嘅字都有佢：時、早、明、晚，全部都藏住一個日。

喺鍵盤上面，日呢個部件擺喺 A 掣。A 掣坐喺中排（home row）最左邊嗰個位置，係你左手尾指自然搭落去嘅地方。你之前學過嘅尸字框，就係擺喺 S 掣，佢啱啱好坐喺 A 掣右手邊，兩個做鄰居。

我哋睇下佢砌出嚟嘅字。「嘅」係 RAIU——你先前學過嘅口字擺喺 R 掣做開頭，跟住就係我哋今日呢個日 A。「的」係 HAPI，中間嗰個 A 又係日。「香」係 HDA，最尾嗰個 A 就係下面嗰個日字。另外要提你一樣：日有個變樣叫曰，係扁身嘅日字，解「講」，你會喺書、最、會呢啲字入面見到佢——同一個 A 掣，收埋喺呢個扁扁嘅樣後面。

B.en:
Today we're looking at 月, the character for the moon. Look at its shape: it's a pictograph of a crescent moon, that graceful curved sliver you see in the night sky. As a building block, this piece leads a double life, and it's worth fixing both in your mind. Its first life is about months and time, as in the character 期. Its second life is cleverer — it's a disguised form of 肉, meaning 'flesh,' written as ⺼, which is why so many characters about parts of the body carry a 月: 腦 (brain), 肚 (belly), 腳 (foot). So next time you spot a 月 in a character, you can guess whether it's talking about a piece of the body.

Now let's find it on the keyboard. The moon lives on the B key. The B key sits on the bottom row, fourth from the left of the six keys there. This is one of your very first keys, so take your time and get a feel for where it lives. When you press it, remember: hitting B calls down that crescent moon from the sky.

Let's see what the B key builds. Start with 有, coded KB — that final B is exactly the 月 sitting underneath. Next look at 同, coded BMR, where B comes first because the opening hook of that outer frame is taken as the moon. And finally the more elaborate 龍, coded YBYSP, which tucks a B right in the middle.

One last thing to preview: the very same B key hides behind several other shapes too. There's ⺼, the flesh form we just met, for body parts like 腦 and 有. There's 爫, a claw — a hand pressing down from above — seen in 愛 and 受. There's 冖, a bare cover laid over the top, in 學 and 愛. And there's 冂, a frame open at the bottom, in 內 and 周. None of these look like a moon, yet they all answer to the B key.
B.zh:
我哋今日睇嘅係「月」呢個字，月牙嘅象形字。你望吓佢個形，就係天上面嗰彎新月，一勾一彎，好靚。作為一個部件，佢有兩個身份，值得你記清楚。第一個身份係講月份同時間，好似「期」字咁；第二個身份就巧妙啲喇——佢係「肉」字嘅變形，寫成⺼咁樣，所以好多同身體部位有關嘅字都帶住個「月」，好似腦、肚、腳。下次你見到一個字有「月」，就可以估吓佢係咪講緊身體嘅一部分。

喺鍵盤度搵佢啦。月字係喺 B 掣。B 掣坐喺鍵盤最底嗰一行，由左數起第四個位。呢個係你頭幾個學嘅掣之一，所以慢慢嚟，摸熟佢喺邊。你打嗰陣就記住：撳 B，就係召喚天上嗰彎月亮。

我哋睇吓 B 掣砌到啲乜嘢字。先睇「有」，佢個碼係 KB，最後嗰個 B 正正就係下面嗰個「月」。跟住睇「同」字，碼係 BMR，你見到 B 排喺頭，因為「同」外面個框開頭嗰勾就係用月嚟取碼。最後睇個比較複雜嘅「龍」字，碼係 YBYSP，中間都藏住咗一個 B。

最後同你預告吓：同一個 B 掣，其實仲會躲喺幾個唔同嘅樣裏面。⺼就係頭先講嘅肉字旁，講身體部位，好似「腦」同「有」；仲有爫，係爪字頭，即係一隻手由上面按落嚟，好似「愛」同「受」；再有冖，一笪冚頭嘅蓋，好似「學」同「愛」;最後仲有冂，一個開口向下嘅框,好似「內」同「周」。呢啲樣睇落唔似月，但佢哋通通都收埋喺 B 掣度。

C.en:
Let's look at this shape together: 金. This is 金, one of the five elements, and it stands for metal. In Chinese, a great many characters about metals and money carry this component — think of 錢, 鐘, 銀. Notice how each of those has 金 sitting on the left side. So whenever a meaning touches on metal or money, this 金 should come to mind.

Now find it on the keyboard. 金 lives on the C key. The C key sits on the very bottom row, second from the left along that row. This is one of your first keys, so there are no learned neighbours to lean on yet — just fix the position in your hand: bottom row, second from the left, and pressing it gives you 金.

Now let's see what the C key builds. Take 港 first; its code is ETCU, and you can spot the C tucked in the middle. Then look at 小, coded simply NC — the last key of that pair is our C. And there's 鋪, coded CIJB, which opens with C because its left side is exactly that 金 component, fitting its meaning of metal and money.

One last thing: the C key also hides other faces. Besides 金, it hosts the 八 shape — the two strokes that split apart, which you see opening 分 and 公. It also holds 丷, which is 八 turned upside down, like the two little strokes on top of 兌. The same C key quietly carries all these shapes, and you'll come to recognise them in time.
C.zh:
我哋一齊睇下呢個字形：金。呢個係五行之一嘅「金」，代表金屬。喺中文入面，好多同金屬、錢銀有關嘅字，都會用到呢個部件——好似錢、鐘、銀呢啲字，你留意下佢哋左邊，都係「金」字旁。所以每次你見到同金屬或者錢銀有關嘅意思，個腦入面就要諗起呢個「金」。

而家喺鍵盤度搵下佢啦。「金」係放喺 C 掣。C 掣坐喺鍵盤最底嗰一行，由左邊數過嚟係第二個位。呢個係你頭嗰幾個學嘅掣之一，所以你唔使記邊個鄰居，淨係要記住個位——最底行、左邊算起第二個，撳落去就係「金」。

跟住我哋睇下 C 掣可以砌到啲乜嘢字。先睇「港」，佢嘅碼係 ETCU，你見到 C 就藏喺中間。再睇「小」，個碼係 NC，好簡單，最尾一個掣就係我哋嘅 C。仲有「鋪」，個碼係 CIJB，呢個字一開頭就係 C，因為佢左邊正正就係「金」字旁，同錢銀金屬有關，啱晒。

最後同你講聲，C 掣仲收埋咗第二個樣。除咗「金」之外，佢仲住埋「八」形——即係分開兩邊嗰兩筆，你喺「分」同「公」開頭嗰兩筆就見到。仲有「八」倒轉嚟寫嘅「丷」，好似「兌」上面嗰兩點噉。同一個 C 掣，收埋咗呢幾個唔同嘅樣，你慢慢就會認得晒。

D.en:
Today we're looking at the shape 木, Wood — the wood of the five elements. Take a good look at it: the vertical stroke running down the middle is the trunk of a tree, and the horizontal stroke with the two lines slanting off each side are its branches. The whole character is a picture of a tree standing there. Any character to do with trees, or with things built out of wood, often carries this 木 inside it — think of 樹 (tree), 橋 (bridge), and 樓 (a storeyed building), all words you see around you every day.

On the keyboard, 木 lives on the D key. Rest your hands in the normal typing position, on the middle row — we call it the home row. Counting from the left, the D key is the third one along, sitting right where your left middle finger naturally falls. This is one of the very first keys you're learning, so take it slowly: feel where the finger sits, and know that pressing it plants a tree.

Now let's see how the D key joins with other parts to build characters. Start with 地, coded GPD — see that D at the very end? That's the 木 part sitting inside the character. Next, 香, coded HDA, where 木 hides in the middle as the second key. And finally 新, a slightly longer code, YDHML, with 木 in the second position.

Did you notice something? The same D key shows up at the start, in the middle, and at the end across these three characters. The position changes, but what it stands for never does — it's always 木, that same tree. You don't need to memorise where it lands; just spot the 木 shape inside a character, and you'll know to reach for the D key.
D.zh:
我哋今日睇嘅字係「木」，Wood，五行入面嘅木。你望吓佢個樣，其實好易記——中間一直落嘅係樹幹，橫嗰筆同兩邊斜落嘅係樹枝。成個字就係一棵樹企喺度嘅象形。凡係同樹木、同用木整出嚟嘅嘢有關嘅字，好多都收埋咗個「木」，好似「樹」、「橋」、「樓」呢啲你日常見到嘅字。

喺鍵盤上面，「木」放喺 D 掣。你隻手放喺打字嘅基本位置，即係中間嗰行——我哋叫佢做 home row。由左邊數起，D 掣係第三個掣，就喺你左手中指自然㩒落去嗰個位。呢個係你頭幾個學嘅倉頡掣之一，所以慢慢嚟，記住個手指擺喺邊，記住㩒落去就係一棵「木」。

跟住我哋睇吓 D 掣點樣同其他部件砌成字。先睇「地」，個碼係 GPD——你見到最尾嗰個 D，就係「木」呢個部件坐喺個字入面。再睇「香」，個碼係 HDA，「木」就藏喺中間，做咗第二個掣。最後睇「新」，個碼長少少，係 YDHML，「木」喺呢度排第二位。

你留意到冇？同一個 D 掣，喺三個唔同嘅字入面，有時排頭、有時排中、有時排尾，位置雖然唔同，但佢代表嘅始終都係「木」呢一棵樹。你唔使死記個位置，只要見到字入面有「木」呢個形，就知道要㩒 D 掣。

E.en:
Today we're learning 水, water — one of the five elements. Look at the character: a main current running down the middle, with droplets splashing off on either side, just like a flowing river. But in everyday characters it rarely shows up in its full form. Instead it loves to disguise itself as 氵, the three little drops. Anything to do with being wet tends to carry it: 港 as in harbour, 海 the sea, 湯 soup, 酒 wine — all of them wear those three drops.

This water radical sits on the very top row of your keyboard, third from the left. Do you remember the keys we've already met? 田 Enclosure lives right next door on its left — that's the W key — and 口 Mouth sits right next door on its right, the R key. So water is squeezed neatly between them on the E key. Rest your finger on E: W on the left, R on the right, and water in the middle.

Let's walk through the characters it builds. Take 港, coded ETCU — you can see the E right at the front, and that's the three drops 氵 on the left, joined by the other parts to complete the character. Now look at 及, coded NHE. Here the E isn't water at all — it's disguised as 又, a right hand, tucked at the end of the character. And 餐, coded YEOIV, hides an E in its middle too.

As for disguises, this E key hides several faces. The three drops 氵 are the most common, standing beside all things wet — 港, 海, 湯. Sometimes water gets squashed flat into 氺, like the shape underneath 求. And the most surprising one of all is 又, a right hand, as in 友 and 受 — that hand boards the very same E key.
E.zh:
今日我哋學嘅係「水」，五行入面嘅其中一個。你睇下個「水」字，中間一條主流，兩邊有水花濺開，就好似河水嘅樣。但係喺日常字入面，佢好少會用足個完整嘅樣出現，反而最鍾意化身做三點水 氵。凡係同濕有關嘅嘢，多數都會見到佢：港口嘅港、大海嘅海、煲湯嘅湯、飲酒嘅酒，全部都掛住呢三滴水。

呢個「水」放喺鍵盤最上面嗰一行，由左數起第三個位。你仲記唔記得之前學過嘅字？「田」字（Enclosure）住喺佢隔籬左手邊，就係 W 掣；而「口」字（Mouth）就喺佢右手邊，即係 R 掣。所以呢個「水」字，就係夾喺兩者中間嘅 E 掣。你將手指擺喺 E 掣度，左邊 W、右邊 R，中間就係水。

我哋一齊睇下佢砌乜嘢字。「港」字，個碼係 ETCU——你見到頭一個 E，正正就係左邊嗰三點水 氵，之後配埋其他部件砌成成隻字。再睇「及」字，個碼係 NHE，呢度個 E 就唔係水，而係化身做「又」，即係一隻右手，收埋喺個字嘅尾度。仲有「餐」字，個碼係 YEOIV，中間都藏住呢個 E。

講到變身，呢個 E 掣其實收埋咗好幾個唔同嘅樣。頭先講嘅三點水 氵，係最常見嗰個，濕嘅嘢都靠佢，好似港、海、湯咁。有時佢會壓扁咗變成 氺，好似「求」字下面嗰個樣。而最估佢唔到嘅，就係「又」——一隻右手，好似「友」同「受」咁，原來都係住喺呢個 E 掣度。

F.en:
Today we meet 火, fire — one of the five elements. Look at its original shape: a cluster of flames leaping upward. But in a great many characters, fire doesn't keep that full flaming look. Instead it turns into four little dots along the bottom of a character, written 灬. Picture those four dots as four small flames burning underneath. So whenever a character has to do with heat or cooking, you'll often find this fire tucked away below.

On the keyboard, fire lives on the F key. Your left index finger already rests right there on F, so it's one of the most natural keys to reach. F sits on the middle row — the home row where a typist's hands rest — fourth from the left. Remember Wood from an earlier lesson? Wood is on the D key, right next door to F on its left. And right next door on F's other side sits Earth, on the G key. Wood, fire, and earth are three neighbours in a row, all under one hand.

Let's see fire build some characters. Take 係, read hai6, whose full code is OHVF — notice the F right at the end, fire closing it off. The character 喺, read hai2, with the mouth radical, is ROHF: it opens with R for mouth and again ends in F for fire. And 為, read wai4, is coded IKNF, where those four dots along the bottom are exactly 灬, typed with F. Type enough and you'll find that whenever four flame-dots appear at a character's foot, your finger drops onto F by itself.

Finally, let me show you the other faces the F key hides. Besides the four flames 灬 — as in 熱 and 點 — it also carries the small shape 小, meaning smallness, seen in 少 and 尖. And it holds ⺌, the 小 form that perches on top of a character, as in 光 and 當. One single F key, and this many disguises behind it.
F.zh:
今日我哋學嘅係「火」，五行入面嘅火。你睇下佢原本個樣：一團火焰咁，向上升。不過喺好多字入面，佢唔會保持成團火嘅樣，反而化身做字底嗰四點——寫做 灬。你想像嗰四點就係四束細細嘅火苗，喺個字下面燒緊。所以凡係同熱、同煮嘢有關嘅字，好多時底下都藏住呢個火。

喺鍵盤上面，火住喺 F 掣。你隻左手食指本身就擺喺 F 度，係最順手嘅一個位。F 喺中間嗰行——即係打字員擺手嗰行——由左數過去第四個。仲記唔記得之前學過嘅木？木喺 D 掣，就喺 F 嘅左手邊隔離。而火嘅右手邊隔離就係土，喺 G 掣。木、火、土三兄弟排埋一齊，你一隻手就摸得晒。

我哋睇下火點樣砌字。「係」呢個字，讀 hai6，全碼係 OHVF——你留意最尾嗰個 F，就係火收尾。「喺」呢個口字邊嘅字，讀 hai2，係 ROHF，開頭個 R 係口，最尾又係 F 火。仲有「為」字，讀 wai4，碼係 IKNF，底下嗰四點正正就係灬，用 F 打出嚟。你打得多就會發覺，好多字尾一見到四點火，你隻手就自動㩒 F。

最後同你講吓 F 掣藏起嘅其他面孔。除咗四點火 灬——好似「熱」同「點」咁——佢仲藏住細小嘅「小」，出現喺「少」同「尖」呢啲字度。仲有「小」字頭 ⺌，即係企喺字頂嗰個小，好似「光」同「當」咁。同一個 F 掣，背後原來收埋咁多副面孔。

G.en:
Look at this shape: 土. Three strokes forming a cross with a bar across the bottom, just like soil piled up on the ground. It's one of the Five Elements — metal, wood, water, fire, earth — and it stands for the ground, for soil. Characters that have to do with ground and places very often hide this 土 inside them.

Find it on the keyboard: the earth radical 土 lives on the G key. G sits on the home row — the middle row — in the fifth position, right at the centre of the row. Your fingers naturally rest on this row when you type, so G is one of the easiest keys to reach.

Now see what it builds. The character 地 (ground) is typed GPD — 土 comes first because the earth radical is on the left side, then the pieces on the right follow. The character 街 (street) is typed HOGGN, and you'll spot two G's in a row in the middle — that's two 土 stacked together. And 廳 (hall) is typed ISGP, with the 土 tucked inside the big hall.

There's one variant face to remember: 士 (si6, scholar). It looks like 土, but the top stroke is the long one and the bottom stroke is the short one — long on top means scholar. This 士 also lives here on G. The character 志 begins this way, a scholar's heart.
G.zh:
睇下呢個字形：土。三劃寫成一個十字加一橫喺底，就好似泥土疊喺地面上面。呢個字係五行之一——金木水火土——代表大地、泥土。凡係同地面、地方有關嘅字，好多時都藏住呢個土。

喺鍵盤上面搵佢：土呢個部首放喺 G 掣。G 坐喺 home row，即係中間嗰行，第五個位，啱啱好喺行嘅中間。你隻手指打字嗰陣自然停喺呢行，所以 G 係最容易搵到嘅其中一個掣。

睇下佢砌到啲乜。地 呢個字打 GPD——土開頭，因為左邊就係個土字邊，跟住係右邊嘅部件。街 呢個字打 HOGGN，你會見到中間連續兩個 G，正正就係兩個土疊埋一齊。仲有 廳 打 ISGP，個土收埋喺個大廳裏面。

有一個變面你要記住：士（si6，學者）。佢同土好似，不過係上面嗰橫長、下面嗰橫短——上長下短就係士。呢個士都住喺 G 呢度。志 就係咁開頭嘅，一個讀書人嘅心。

H.en:
Look at today's shape: 竹. In Cangjie, the 竹 key stands for the leftward slant stroke 丿 from the stroke class. When you write 少, that last tail you drag out to the lower left is exactly this slant. So you can think of the 竹 key as the 'sweep down and to the left' motion — one of the most basic strokes there is.

Find it on the keyboard: 竹 lives on the H key, sitting in position six of the home (middle) row. Right to its left is the 土 Earth key you learned earlier, which is G; right to its right is the 十 Cross key you also learned, which is J. So G, H, J in a row gives you Earth, then 竹, then Cross — your finger just walks along the middle row and there it is.

Besides being the slant stroke, the 竹 key wears another very common face: the bamboo top ⺮. Things made of bamboo often have this cap sitting over them — words like 筆, 等, and 箱 all have ⺮ on top, and every one of them begins with the H key.

Let's walk through a few example characters. 係 breaks down as OHVF, and you can see the H 竹 tucked in the middle. 的 is HAPI, opening straight away with H 竹. 香 is even simpler, coded HDA, again leading with H 竹. Remember the two faces: ⺮ is the bamboo top, hiding inside 等 and 筆; while 丿 is the plain slant stroke, hiding inside 少 and 乎 — the same H key lurking behind these different shapes.
H.zh:
睇吓今日呢個形：竹。喺倉頡入面，竹掣代表嘅係筆畫類入面撇出去嘅斜筆 丿。你寫「少」嘅時候，最後拖出去嗰一筆，就正正係呢個斜筆。所以你可以將竹掣諗成「向左下撇一撇」嘅動作，係一種好基本嘅筆畫。

喺鍵盤度搵佢：竹係 H 掣，坐喺中排（home row）第六位。佢左手邊就係你早前學過嘅土掣，即係 G；佢右手邊就係你學過嘅十掣，即係 J。所以由 G 到 H 到 J，就係土、竹、十三個掣排埋一齊，你隻手指喺中排慢慢行過去就搵到。

除咗做斜筆，竹掣仲有一個好常見嘅身份，就係竹字頭 ⺮。凡係用竹造嘅嘢，好多時個頂就蓋住呢個竹字頭，好似「筆」、「等」、「箱」呢啲字，個頭都係 ⺮，全部都用 H 掣起手。

我哋睇吓幾個例字點砌。「係」呢個字拆做 OHVF，你會見到 H 竹夾喺中間。「的」呢個字係 HAPI，一開頭就係 H 竹。「香」就更加簡單，拆做 HDA，同樣係 H 竹行先。記住個變面：⺮ 係竹字頭，收埋喺「等」、「筆」入面；而 丿 就係一撇，收埋喺「少」、「乎」呢啲字入面——同一個 H 掣，可以躲喺呢啲唔同嘅樣貌後面。

I.en:
Today we're looking at a very small shape — a single dot. The radical is 戈, but in Cangjie this key stands for the dot stroke 丶. Think of the little dot at the bottom of 太, or the dot inside 凡 — that's it. It's tiny, but a great many characters lean on it to finish or to begin, so it's a part you'll bump into again and again as you type.

On the keyboard this is the letter I, sitting in the top row, the eighth of ten positions. Reach a finger up and feel for it — it's over toward the right side of the top row, not quite the last one, second from the end. Since this is one of your very first keys, you don't have any learned neighbours yet, so just hold onto the position — top row, eighth spot — and the others will connect to it over time.

Now let's see how it builds characters. Take 嘅, that everyday spoken-Cantonese word you use all the time — its code is RAIU, and there's the I helping out inside. Then 餐 has the code YEOIV, again with an I tucked in the middle. And 廳 has the code ISGP, where the I steps out right at the front. You don't need to memorise all of these yet, but you'll notice I really does turn up everywhere.

Finally, let me show you the other faces hiding behind the I key. Besides the dot 丶 (as in 太 and 凡), it also stands for 厶 — the little coil you see in 私 and 去 — and for the lean-to roof 广, the slanted roof over shops and places like 店, 度, and 廣. So one and the same I key is sometimes a dot, sometimes a coil, sometimes a lean-to roof, and you'll learn to recognise them all in time.
I.zh:
我哋今日睇嘅係一個好細嘅形——一點，個部首係「戈」，喺倉頡入面就代表一點 丶。你諗吓「太」字下面嗰一點，或者「凡」字入面嗰點，就係佢喇。細細粒，但係好多字都靠佢收尾或者起頭，係你打字嘅時候經常撞到嘅一個部件。

喺鍵盤上面，呢個鍵係字母 I，坐喺最頂行，由左數起第八個位。你伸隻手指上去摸吓，佢喺頂行右邊嗰邊，唔算最尾，尾二先啱。因為呢個係你頭幾個學嘅鍵，暫時未有已經識咗嘅鄰居，你就記住個位——頂行第八個——慢慢佢會同其他鍵連埋一齊。

跟住睇吓佢點樣砌字。「嘅」呢個口語字你日日都用，佢嘅碼係 RAIU，你見到個 I 就喺入面幫手。「餐」字碼係 YEOIV，同樣有個 I 藏喺中間。仲有「廳」字，碼係 ISGP，個 I 一開頭就出場。你唔使即刻背晒，但你會發現 I 呢個鍵真係周圍都見到。

最後同你講吓 I 鍵背後仲收埋咗幾個唔同嘅樣。除咗一點 丶（好似「太」同「凡」嗰點），佢仲代表「厶」——即係「私」同「去」入面嗰個打圈嘅部件；仲有斜頂屋「广」——舖頭、地方嗰種斜頂，好似「店」、「度」、「廣」。所以同一個 I 鍵，有時係一點，有時係個圈，有時係間斜頂屋，你慢慢就會認得晒。

J.en:
Look at the shape: 十. Two strokes crossing — one horizontal, one vertical — meeting right in the middle to make a cross. This is the 'cross' shape from the stroke class, the idea of two lines crossing each other. It's a very simple little cross, and you see it every day: the number ten, 十, is exactly this shape. Cangjie borrows that crossing idea as its symbol.

On the keyboard, this cross shape lives on the J key. The J key sits on the home row — the middle row your fingers rest on — in position seven of nine. Remember the 大 Fork shape you learned a few lessons back? That one is on the K key. Find K again, and the key immediately to its left is J — the two are next-door neighbours. With your hand resting on the middle row, it's right there under your finger.

Let's see what it builds. The first character is 個, coded OWJR — you can spot J tucked in the middle, doing the crossing strokes. Then 麵, coded JNMWL, which opens with J for the cross at the top. And 家, coded JMSO, which also starts with J.

Why does 家 begin with J? Because the J key hides another face: 宀, the roof radical. This is the shelter shape — the top of a house. So words that have a roof over them lean on this key: 家, 安, 定 — all of them sheltered under a roof. The very same J key is waiting behind all those little rooftops.
J.zh:
睇吓個形：十。兩筆相交，一橫一豎，喺正中間交叉埋一齊——呢個就係筆畫類嘅「交」，「交叉」嘅交。好簡單嘅一個十字形，你日日都見到，數目字入面嘅「十」正正就係佢。倉頡就用呢個交叉嘅意思嚟做代表。

喺鍵盤上面，呢個「交」形擺喺 J 掣。J 掣坐喺 home row，即係中間嗰一行，喺九個位入面排第七。你仲記得早幾課學過嘅 大 Fork 嗎？佢就喺 K 掣。而家你摷返 K 掣出嚟，你隔籬左邊嗰粒就係 J 掣喇——兩個係鄰居。手指擺喺中間行，一撳就搵到。

我哋睇吓佢砌得出啲乜。第一個字係「個」，碼係 OWJR——你見到 J 匿喺中間，做緊「田」下面嗰豎同橫交叉嗰部分。跟住「麵」字，碼係 JNMWL，一開頭就係 J，係「麥」字上面嗰交叉。最後「家」字，碼係 JMSO，同樣係 J 打頭。

點解「家」會用 J 開頭呢？因為 J 掣仲有一個變面：宀，寶蓋頭。呢個就係有瓦遮頭嘅意思——一間屋嘅頂。所以有屋頂遮住嘅字都會用到佢：家、安、定，全部都係有瓦遮頭。同一粒 J 掣，就係匿喺呢啲屋簷底下面。

K.en:
In this lesson we look at the character 大, but don't just think of it as the 大 meaning 'big', because in the stroke class it stands for the 'fork' — an open, crossing stroke. Picture two slanting strokes crossing each other, like the character 乂: one going down to the left, one going down to the right, meeting in the middle. This crossing shape is the base you see under 文, and the top of 左, written as ナ. And besides the fork, one very special shape also lives here: the sickness frame 疒. Look at it and you can imagine a person lying on a bed, unwell — which is why characters like 病 (sick) and 痛 (pain) use it.

To find it on the keyboard, it sits on the middle row (the home row), the eighth position counting from the left. Remember the 中 Vertical key (L) you learned earlier? It sits right next to K, immediately to its right. So once you find L, just step one key to the left and you're on K. This is the sixth key in our teaching order.

Let's walk through what it builds. The character 有 has the code KB — that first K is our ナ from today (the left-hand strokes you'll meet in 左, 友, 有), followed by B. Now look at 為, coded IKNF: you'll spot K tucked in the middle, again standing for that fork stroke. And the everyday Cantonese word 咗 is coded RKM, with our K sitting right in the centre.

One last preview: the same K key hides behind several different faces. Sometimes it's the open crossing 乂, as in 文 and 父; sometimes it's the left-hand strokes ナ, as in 左, 友, and 有; and sometimes it becomes the sickbed frame 疒 — a person lying on a bed — as in 病 and 痛. Little by little you'll get used to it, and the moment you see these shapes, your hand will reach for K on its own.
K.zh:
呢一課我哋睇「大」呢個字，但係唔好淨係諗住「大細」嘅大，因為喺筆畫類入面，佢代表嘅其實係「叉」——一種開叉、交叉嘅筆。你想像兩劃斜斜咁交叉埋一齊，就好似個「乂」字咁，一劃向左下、一劃向右下，喺中間交會。呢個交叉嘅形，就係「文」字下面嗰個底，亦都係「左」字上面嗰個頭 ナ。除咗開叉，仲有一個好特別嘅形都住喺呢度，就係病字框 疒——你望落去，就好似一個人瞓咗喺張床度，病咗咁，所以「病」、「痛」呢啲字都用到佢。

喺鍵盤度搵佢，佢喺中間嗰一行（home row），由左數起第八個位。你記唔記得之前學過嘅「中」（Vertical，L鍵）？佢就喺 K 嘅右手邊，緊貼住 K。所以你揾到 L 嘅時候，向左行一格就係 K 喇。呢個係我哋教到第六個鍵。

我哋一齊睇下佢砌得出啲乜。「有」呢個字，碼係 KB——頭嗰個 K 就係我哋今課嘅 ナ（就係「左」、「友」、「有」個頭嗰種左手邊筆畫），跟住個 B。再睇「為」，碼係 IKNF，你會見到 K 匿喺中間，佢喺呢度都係代表嗰個叉嘅筆。仲有廣東話成日用嘅「咗」字，碼係 RKM，中間又係我哋嘅 K。

最後同你預告一下：同一個 K 鍵，其實收埋咗幾副唔同嘅面孔。有時佢係開叉嘅交筆 乂，好似「文」、「父」咁；有時佢係左手邊嗰組筆畫 ナ，好似「左」、「友」、「有」；有時佢又變成病字框 疒——人瞓喺床——好似「病」、「痛」。慢慢你就會習慣，見到呢啲形，隻手就自然㩒落 K 度。

L.en:
Look at this shape: a single straight stroke 丨, drawn top to bottom in one motion. This is the 'vertical' radical — a line that stands up straight. You already met the horizontal 一; now here is its upright cousin. It's about as simple as a shape can get: one stroke, drawn downward. You can spot it inside the character 引 — those two vertical lines on the right are exactly this stroke.

On the keyboard this lives on the L key. Find the middle row — the home row, where your fingers rest naturally — and slide all the way to the right, to the ninth and last position. Your right little finger reaches over to it. There are no learned neighbours to lean on yet, so just fix it in mind: middle row, far right, the letter L.

Now watch it build. Take 麵, coded JNMWL — that final L is the vertical stroke closing it off on the right. Then 新, coded YDHML, again finishing with an L for its upright stroke. And 樓, coded DLWV, where the L sits in second place instead. You'll notice L often shows up to supply that one straight downward line.

One more thing to know: the same L key also hides another face — the clothing radical 衤. This is the form that appears in characters about clothes and cloth. You'll see it in 初 and in 被, where that clothing side is typed with L. So remember, two faces live behind L: the vertical stroke 丨, and the clothing radical 衤.
L.zh:
睇下呢個形：一支直筆 丨，由上到下，直落一畫。呢個係「縱」——即係垂直嘅意思。你之前學過橫嘅一，而家呢個就係直嘅一。最簡單嘅形，得一畫，由上寫落嚟。你可以喺「引」呢個字入面搵到佢，右邊嗰兩豎就係佢喇。

呢個鍵喺鍵盤上叫做 L 鍵。佢坐喺中間嗰行——即係你手指自然擺放嗰行——最右邊，第九個位。你右手尾指伸過去就摸到佢喇。而家仲未學到佢隔籬啲鍵，所以你淨係記住：中間行、最右邊、L 呢個字母。

睇下佢點樣砌字。「麵」呢個字，碼係 JNMWL，最尾嗰個 L 就係右邊嗰一豎。「新」字碼係 YDHML，又係尾筆用 L 收一豎。「樓」字碼係 DLWV，呢次個 L 排喺第二位。你會發現，好多時 L 就係幫你補返嗰一直筆。

仲有一樣嘢要話你知：同一個 L 鍵，仲收埋另一個樣——衫字旁 衤。呢個係衣服嘅部首，凡係同衫褲衣物有關嘅字，好多都用到佢。譬如「初」字同「被」字，個衣字旁就係㩒 L。所以記住，L 背後匿埋咗兩個面：一豎 丨，同埋衫字旁 衤。

M.en:
Let's start with the simplest shape in all of Chinese: 一. Look at it — it's one flat stroke, drawn just once, left to right. This is the plainest form there is, the stroke we call the 'horizontal' (橫). In Cangjie it belongs to the stroke class, standing in for every flat horizontal line. It's easy to remember, because it really is nothing more than a single line.

Now find it on your keyboard. This horizontal stroke lives on the letter M, down on the very bottom row, in the sixth and last position counting from the left. Since this is the first key you're learning, there aren't any already-learned neighbours keeping it company yet, but you'll get comfortable soon enough — whenever you think of a flat horizontal stroke, you press M.

Look at what it builds. Take 下: the horizontal sits on top with something hanging below, and its code is MY, starting with our horizontal M. Now look at 同, coded BMR, where the horizontal M is tucked into the middle. Even a busier character like 麵, coded JNMWL, still hides an M inside it. This flat stroke turns up as a helper in all kinds of characters.

This M key also hides a second face: the cliff overhang 厂. Picture it as a stone ledge sheltering whatever sits underneath. In 石, 原, and 厚, the parts seem to be born under that cliff — so when you type those characters, the cliff overhang 厂 is pressed with M too. One key, two faces: the flat 一 and the sheltering cliff 厂.
M.zh:
我哋由最簡單嘅一個形開始：一。你望吓佢——就係一筆打橫，由左至右，一嘢過畫出嚟。呢個係中文入面最簡單嘅形，就係「橫」呢一畫。喺倉頡入面，佢屬於「筆畫類」，代表所有打橫嘅一筆。記住個形好易，因為佢真係得一條線咋。

嚟啦，喺鍵盤度搵佢。呢個橫畫喺英文字母 M 度，喺鍵盤最底一行，由左數過去第六個、亦即係最後一個位。因為呢個係你學嘅第一個鍵，暫時仲未有隔籬啲已學過嘅鍵陪住佢，但你慢慢會熟嘅——一諗起打橫，就撳 M。

睇吓佢砌到啲乜。「下」呢個字，個橫喺頂，下面有嘢墜住，碼係 MY，開頭就係我哋嘅橫 M。再睇「同」字，碼係 BMR，中間都收埋咗個橫 M 落去。就算複雜過少少嘅「麵」字，碼係 JNMWL，你一樣搵到個 M 收喺入面。呢個橫畫喺好多字度都幫緊手。

呢個 M 鍵仲收埋咗第二個面：崖頭 厂。你可以諗成一塊崖石嘅簷篷，遮住底下嘅嘢。喺「石」、「原」、「厚」呢幾個字入面，個嘢都好似喺崖底出世咁——所以打呢啲字嘅時候，個崖頭 厂 一樣係撳 M。同一個鍵，兩個面：打橫嘅一，同埋崖頭嘅厂。

N.en:
Look at today's radical: 弓, the Hook. In Cangjie it belongs to the stroke class, and it stands for strokes that end with a hook. Notice how, when you write certain characters, the last stroke flicks or curls — like the flick that ends 九 and 氣, or the tail that hangs under 打 and 丁 and hooks back up. All of these hooked strokes gather onto this one key.

Find it on the keyboard: the Hook lives on the letter N, sitting on the bottom row, the fifth of six positions. The 月 Moon key (B), which you learned earlier, sits immediately to its left, and the 一 Horizontal key (M), also learned earlier, sits immediately to its right. So you can locate it from two familiar friends — 弓 is tucked right between them, just to the right of centre.

Look at what it builds. Take 小: its code is NC, and that opening hook is our Hook, N. Take 麵: its code is JNMWL, and you'll spot the Hook N sitting in the second position. Take 街: its code is HOGGN, where the Hook N comes right at the very end to finish it off — exactly that flicking hook.

This key hides two faces. The first is 乙, the flat hook, which you see in 九 and 氣. The second is 亅, the straight hook, the tail hanging under 打 and 丁. Flat or upright, whenever a stroke ends in a hook, you press the same key: N.
N.zh:
睇下今日呢個部首：弓，鈎。喺倉頡入面，佢係筆畫類其中一個，代表帶鈎嘅筆。你留意下寫字嗰陣，有啲筆去到最後會飛一飛、勾一勾——好似 九 同 氣 收尾嗰下彈出去，又好似 打 同 丁 落到底嗰筆勾返上嚟。呢啲有鈎嘅筆，全部歸埋喺弓呢個鍵。

喺鍵盤度搵佢：弓喺英文字母 N 度，坐喺最底一行，由左數起第五個位。你之前學過嘅月（B 鍵）就喺佢左手邊隔籬，而一（M 鍵）就喺佢右手邊隔籬。所以你搵佢嘅時候，可以由熟悉嘅月同一嗰度定位——弓就夾喺中間偏右嗰邊。

睇下佢砌到啲乜。小 呢個字，碼係 NC，起首嗰一鈎就係我哋嘅弓 N。麵 呢個字碼係 JNMWL，你會見到弓 N 排喺第二個。街 呢個字碼係 HOGGN，弓 N 走到最尾收尾——正正就係嗰種飛出去嘅鈎。

弓呢個鍵藏住兩張面。第一張係乙，打橫嘅鈎，你喺 九 同 氣 度見到嘅就係佢。第二張係 亅，打直嘅鈎，掛喺 打 同 丁 底下嗰條尾就係佢。橫又好、直又好，只要係帶鈎嗰筆，你都撳同一個 N 鍵。

O.en:
Today we're learning the shape 人, which means 'person'. Look at it — one stroke leaning left, one leaning right, like a figure standing with its legs apart. 人 is one of the most basic characters in Chinese, and because so many words are about people, a great many characters open with it. Fix its picture in your mind: a person standing upright.

On the keyboard, 人 lives on the top row, the ninth of ten positions, almost all the way over to the right. We call it the O key. Do you remember the 戈 Dot from an earlier lesson, the I key? It sits right next to O, immediately to its left. So if you're hunting for the O key, just step one place to the right from I.

The 人 shape wears several faces. The most common is 亻, a person standing at the left edge — 你, 佢 and 係 all begin with it. Take 係: its code is OHVF, and that first O is exactly that left-standing 亻. The character 個 works the same way, coded OWJR, with O again as the 亻 on the left. 餐 is a little different — here the person is tucked inside, and the code is YEOIV, with the O hiding in the third spot.

Beyond 亻, the O key also hides a second face: 入, meaning 'enter'. It's really 人 with the legs swapped over, and you'll meet it inside 內. And there's a third face — the person roof 𠆢, the little cap that sits over 今, 會 and 食. One O key, all these disguises, and soon you'll spot each of them at a glance.
O.zh:
今日我哋學嘅係「人」呢個字形。你睇下佢——一撇一捺，好似一個人企喺度，張開對腳。人係最基本嘅字之一，喺中文入面，好多同人有關嘅字都由佢開頭。你要記住佢嘅樣：一個企定定嘅人。

喺鍵盤上面，人字排喺最頂嗰行，第九個位，即係差唔多去到右邊嘅盡頭。我哋叫佢做 O 掣。你仲記唔記得上一堂學嘅戈 Dot、即係 I 掣呀？佢就喺 O 掣嘅左手邊，緊貼住。所以你搵 O 掣嘅時候，可以由 I 掣向右行一格。

人呢個字形識變好多副面孔。最常見嘅係企喺左邊嘅 亻——你、佢、係 全部都由佢開頭。我哋睇下「係」字，佢嘅碼係 OHVF，你見到頭一個 O 就係左邊嗰個亻。「個」字都一樣，碼係 OWJR，第一個 O 都係亻。「餐」字就唔同啲，人字收埋喺中間，碼係 YEOIV，個 O 匿咗喺第三個位。

除咗亻之外，O 掣仲收埋咗第二副面孔——「入」字。入去嘅入，其實就係人字兩隻腳掉轉咗，你會喺「內」字度見到佢。仲有第三副：人字頭 𠆢，即係頂喺 今、會、食 上面嗰個蓋。同一個 O 掣，藏住咁多個樣，慢慢你就會一眼認得出。

P.en:
Look at this shape: 心. This is the character for the heart — the physical organ, and also the seat of our feelings. In Cangjie it belongs to the body class, because the heart is part of us and is where our emotions live. Have you noticed? So many characters about feelings carry this marker in one form or another.

This shape lives on the P key. The P key sits at the far right end of the top row, in the tenth and last position. Remember the 人 Person radical you learned earlier? It's on the O key, sitting immediately to the left of P — so just find O and step one key to the right, and you've got P.

Let's see how the P key builds characters. The first is 號, coded RSYPU, where you'll spot P near the end. Next is 廳, coded ISGP, with P again in the final position. And there's 的, coded HAPI, where P is tucked into the middle. Type these a few times and the position will settle into your fingers.

The P key also hides behind several other faces. The most important is the standing heart 忄 — the upright form of 心 that means feelings, seen on the left of characters like 快 and 情. Beyond that, there's 匕, a spoon shape (as in 化 and 老), 勹, a wrapping hook (as in 勿 and 句), and 七, the 七 bend (as in 切). All these bent, curving strokes board together at the P key.
P.zh:
睇下呢個字形：心。呢個係「心」字，代表心臟、感情。喺倉頡入面佢屬於人身類，因為心係我哋身體嘅一部分，亦都係我哋感情嘅所在。你留意到冇？好多同心情有關嘅字，都會用到呢個記號。

呢個字擺喺 P 掣。P 掣坐喺鍵盤最頂一行嘅最右邊，係第十個、亦即係最後一個位。你之前學過嘅「人」字喺 O 掣，就正正喺 P 掣嘅左手邊，所以你只要搵到 O，再向右行一格，就搵到 P 喇。

我哋睇下 P 掣點樣砌字。第一個係「號」，碼係 RSYPU，你見到 P 排喺後尾。跟住係「廳」字，碼係 ISGP，P 又係喺最尾嗰個位。仲有「的」字，碼係 HAPI，呢度個 P 就夾喺中間。慢慢砌多幾次，你就會對佢個位置越嚟越熟。

P 掣仲收埋幾個唔同嘅樣。最重要嘅一個係豎心邊 忄——即係企起身嘅心，代表感情，好似「快」同「情」呢啲字嘅左邊就係佢。除此之外，匕呢個匙羹形（好似「化」「老」）、勹呢個包住嘅框（好似「勿」「句」），同埋七字嗰個彎（好似「切」），呢啲彎彎曲曲嘅筆畫都一齊住埋喺 P 掣度。

Q.en:
Today we're looking at the radical 手, which means "hand." Look at the shape: 手 — it's your own hand. In Cangjie it stands for all the characters that have to do with actions. The most common face it wears is the raised-hand form 扌, which you can spot on the left side of 打 and 接 — those three strokes are a hand busy doing something. So remember this: when a hand is doing something, think Q.

Now let's find it on the keyboard. The 手 radical lives on the Q key, which sits on the top row, the very first of the ten positions there. It's easy to find because it's in the far top-left corner. You've already learned 田, the Enclosure radical, on the W key — and W sits immediately to the right of Q, so if you find 田, just step one key left and you're on the hand.

Now let's see what the Q key builds. Take 牛: its code is HQ, so you type H and then Q, and two strokes finish it. Then 年, coded OQ, again ending on Q. And 我 is coded HQI — H, then Q, then I. Notice how Q keeps turning up in the middle or as a key piece of these characters.

One last thing — a preview of its variant face. Besides the plain 手, this radical also appears as the raised-hand form 扌, the marker of actions that you see in 打 and 接. The same Q key is hiding behind both of those shapes.
Q.zh:
我哋今日睇嘅係「手」呢個部首。你望下個字形：手，即係我哋隻手。喺Cangjie入面，佢代表所有同動作有關嘅字。最常見嘅樣就係提手旁「扌」，你喺「打」同「接」呢啲字入面都見到——左邊嗰三劃就係一隻手喺度做嘢。所以你記住：見到隻手喺度做嘢，就諗Q。

跟住去搵佢喺鍵盤邊度。手呢個部首放喺Q掣度，即係最頂一行、由左邊數起第一個位。佢好易搵，因為就喺鍵盤最左上角。你之前學過嘅「田」（Enclosure）喺W掣，就緊貼喺Q掣右手邊，所以你只要搵到田，向左行一格就係手喇。

而家睇下Q掣砌到啲乜。「牛」呢個字，個碼係HQ，即係先打H再打Q，兩劃就搞掂。跟住「年」，個碼係OQ，你見到又係用Q收尾。至於「我」，個碼係HQI，即係H加Q加I三個掣——你留意到Q喺呢啲字入面好多時都做緊個中間或者關鍵嘅角色。

最後提你一提個變體樣。手呢個部首除咗正正一個「手」字之外，仲會化身做提手旁「扌」，即係代表動作嗰個記號，你喺「打」同「接」都見到佢。同一個Q掣，就係收埋喺呢兩個唔同嘅樣後面。

R.en:
Look at the shape 口: a little square, hollow in the middle — like a mouth held open. This radical belongs to the body class, and it means speech, an opening, the act of talking. Best of all, it's the great friend of written Cantonese! Every time you write 嘅, 唔, 啲, 咗 or 嘢, there's a mouth sitting inside. So from now on, when you see a 口 tucked on the left of a character, you can usually guess it's a spoken-language word.

Now find it on your keyboard. The 口 radical lives on the R key, up on the top row, the fourth position from the left. The R key is one of the very first keys you're meeting, so rest a finger on it and fix the spot in your mind — spoken Cantonese is so common that your fingers will soon reach it without thinking.

Let's take apart a few characters together. First 嘅, coded RAIU: that opening R is the mouth on the left. Then 號, coded RSYPU, which also begins with R, its mouth leading the way. But 個 works a little differently — its code is OWJR, with the R falling all the way to the end. That's because in 個 the mouth sits down in the lower-right corner, not at the start, so R comes last.

The R key has no variant faces to worry about — a mouth is just a mouth, nice and simple. Just remember this: R is 口, and it's the handiest key you have for typing everyday Cantonese.
R.zh:
你睇吓「口」呢個字：一個四方形，中間空咗，就好似一張開咗嘅嘴。呢個部首屬於人身類，講嘅係開口、講嘢嘅意思。最緊要嘅係——佢係我哋廣東話口語字嘅老朋友！你平時寫嘅「嘅」、「唔」、「啲」、「咗」、「嘢」，全部都有一把口喺度。所以以後見到個字左邊有個口字旁，你多數可以估到，佢係一個「講出嚟嘅字」。

嚟喺你嘅鍵盤上面搵佢啦。「口」擺喺 R 掣度，喺最頂嗰行，由左數起第四個位。R 掣係你最早學嘅其中一個掣，你可以將手指輕輕搭喺上面，記住呢個位——因為口語字實在太常用，你嘅手指好快就會熟到唔使諗。

我哋一齊拆吓幾個字。先睇「嘅」，佢嘅碼係 RAIU：開頭嗰個 R 就係左邊嗰把口。再睇「號」，碼係 RSYPU，同樣係由 R 開頭，左邊個口帶頭。跟住「個」就有啲唔同喇，佢嘅碼係 OWJR，把口 R 走咗去最尾——因為喺「個」入面，口係喺個字嘅右下角，唔係開頭，所以 R 就排到後面。

呢個 R 掣冇其他變化字形，一個口就係一個口，好易記。你只要記住：R 就係「口」,係你打廣東話口語字最好使嘅一個掣。

S.en:
Today we look at the S key, which carries the radical 尸. It belongs to the shape class, and we call it the 'side-frame' — a frame that opens to one side. Look at the shape of 尸: it's like a person lying down, a horizontal line with a stroke leaning down. You'll often find it sitting on top of characters, like the head of 屋 and 尾, where the whole upper part is a 尸.

Finding it on the keyboard is easy. The S key sits on the home row — the middle row where your fingers naturally rest — and it's the second of the nine letters there. Remember the Wood radical 木 you learned earlier, on the D key? The D key sits right next to S, immediately to its right, so from S you just move one step rightward to reach 木. The two fingers are close neighbours.

Now let's see how S builds characters. Take 號, coded RSYPU — you can see the S sitting as the second part. Then 記, coded YRSU, where S turns up again in the middle. And 廳, coded ISGP, also hides an S inside. You'll notice the 尸 radical often tucks itself into just one piece of a character; you don't need a whole visible 尸 to reach for the S key.

Finally, let me show you the other face of S. Besides 尸, the S key also holds 匚 — a box that opens to the right. Look at 區 and 匹: that outer shell framing them is the 匚, and it too is typed with the S key. So one single S can be either a reclining person or a box opening rightward.
S.zh:
我哋今日睇嘅係 S 掣，佢代表嘅字根係「尸」，屬於字形類，我哋叫佢做「側」——即係側邊嘅框。你望下「尸」呢個形，好似一個人瞓低咗咁，一橫一撇搭埋。佢通常係一啲字嘅頭部，例如「屋」同「尾」呢類字，個頂就係一個 尸 字。

喺鍵盤度搵佢好易。S 掣坐喺 home row，即係中間嗰行手指自然擺放嘅位置，係九個字母入面嘅第二個。你仲記得之前學過嘅「木」字，喺 D 掣度嘛？D 掣就緊貼喺 S 掣嘅右手邊，所以你只要由 S 向右行一格就到 木 喇，兩隻手指好近。

我哋而家睇下 S 點樣砌字。「號」呢個字碼係 RSYPU，你見到第二碼就係我哋今日嘅 S。「記」字碼係 YRSU，S 又一次出現喺中間。而「廳」字碼係 ISGP，同樣藏住咗個 S 喺入面。你會發現 尸 呢個字根成日匿埋喺字嘅一部分，唔一定要成個尸字先用得 S。

最後同你講埋 S 嘅另一個面貌。除咗 尸，S 掣仲收埋咗「匚」——即係一個開口向右嘅箱。你睇「區」同「匹」呢兩個字，外殼嗰個框框就係 匚，都係撳 S 掣打出嚟。所以同一粒 S，可以係瞓低嘅人，又可以係向右開口嘅箱。

T.en:
Today we're learning a key from the shape class, and its radical is 廿. Look at its form: two strokes standing side by side, like two posts lined up together — that's why it belongs to 'parallel', the idea of things placed beside each other. The character 廿 on its own is read jaa6 and means 'twenty'. But for your typing, the most important role of 廿 is that it transforms into the grass top 艹 — the mark you find on plants, on all those characters to do with flowers, tea leaves, and vegetables, each wearing this little 艹 cap on its head.

Now find it on the keyboard. 廿 lives on the T key, sitting on the top row, fifth from the left of ten. Remember the Mouth radical 口 from an earlier lesson, on the R key? It sits immediately to the left of T. And the Dot-and-post 卜 on the Y key sits immediately to its right. So R, T, and Y run in a row together, and you can walk over from the familiar Mouth key to land on T.

Let's see what it builds. Take 茶: right on top it wears the grass cap 艹, with the body beneath, and the whole code is TOD — the moment you see it start with T, you know it's wearing that 艹 hat. The character 港 is less obvious; its code is ETCU, with T tucked into the middle as one of the parts. And 站 has the code YTYR, where you'll spot T appearing again inside.

Hold on to one thing: the same T key hides behind different faces. The most common one is the grass top 艹 — the flower-tea-vegetable characters, with those two parallel strokes across the top, are all typed by pressing the T key.
T.zh:
今日我哋學嘅係字形類嘅一個掣，個部首係 廿。你望吓佢個樣：兩劃並排企喺度，好似兩支柱一齊排開，所以佢屬於「並」——並排嘅意思。廿 呢個字本身讀 jaa6，即係「二十」咁解。不過對你學打字嚟講，廿 最重要嘅身份係佢會變身做草花頭 艹——就係植物嘅記號，好多同花草、茶葉、蔬菜有關嘅字，個頭頂都戴住呢個 艹。

去鍵盤搵佢啦。廿 喺 T 掣度，坐喺最頂嗰行，由左數起第五個位。你仲記得之前學過嘅口部（R 掣）嘛？佢就喺 T 掣嘅左手邊。而 卜（Y 掣）就喺 T 掣嘅右手邊。所以 R、T、Y 三個掣打橫排喺一齊，你可以由熟悉嘅口部行過去搵到 T。

睇吓佢砌乜嘢字。「茶」呢個字，頭頂就係草花頭 艹，跟住下面係字身，成個碼係 TOD——你一睇個 T 起頭就知，佢戴住 艹 呢頂帽。「港」字就無咁明顯，佢個碼係 ETCU，個 T 收埋喺中間做其中一個部件。至於「站」字，個碼係 YTYR，你見到 T 又出現喺入面。

記住一件事：同一個 T 掣，會匿喺唔同嘅樣後面。最常見嘅就係草花頭 艹——花、茶、菜呢類植物字，個頭頂嗰兩筆並排嘅記號，全部都係撳 T 掣打出嚟。

U.en:
Look at today's shape: 山. It's a picture character, drawing three mountain peaks — tall in the middle, shorter on the sides — just like a ridgeline you might see gazing out over the hills of a country park.
